title: IMPACT OF SATELLITE RE-ENTRIES AND ROCKET LAUNCHES ON THE EARTH ATMOSPHERE EARTH OBSERVATION MONITORING ARCHITECTURE CONCEPT STUDY - EXPRO PLUS
description: The European Earth Observation (EO) Ecosystem is a cross-cutting vision for the future of Space Earth Observation, addressing future opportunities, challenges as well as trends and drivers which potentially impact the EO Ecosystem in the time horizon 2050+.Embedded in this framework, the activity "Impact of satellite re-entries and rocket launches on the Earth Atmosphere - Earth Observation monitoring architecture concept study" will help to prepare the foundation to understand how space debris impacts the atmospheric composition and climate system. Therefore, the study scope is to assess which observation capacities are already in place (e.g. on current / planned EO missions -or atmospheric models, databases) and illustrate their fit-for-purpose. Suggest based on the findings a future impact and monitoring Earth Observation architecture concept as well as make recommendations for future scientific / technical studies and for programmatic decisions.

title: REFERENCE PROGRAMMABLE OSCILLATOR CHIP FOR TELECOM APPLICATIONS (ARTES AT 5C.541) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The activity objective is to design, manufacturing and test a high-performance programmable reference oscillator basedon microelectromechanical (MEMS) resonator operating in the 10 - 500 MHz range to serve as a reference oscillator or to attend directly as local oscillator the lower frequency range for telecom application.Targeted Improvements: - Enabling a European or Canadian source of a MEMS oscillator chip suitable for system on chip (SoC) integration.- Size, weight and power reduction by several orders of magnitude versus current technology of quartz OCXO.- Increase of fractional-N frequency generation by a factor of more than5.Description:Current telecom satellite payload equipment used mainly quartz-based oscillators for clock generation reference signals, used for track-and-hold amplifiers and digital-to-analogue (DAC) and analogue-to-digital (ADC) blocks in direct conversion (zero-IF or homodyne) frequency converters; for I-Q demodulator blocks in fully digital beamforming networks; and in double conversion super heterodyne frequency converters local oscillators (LOs) at different carrier frequencies. However, European sources of quartz-based oscillatorsare becoming more limited, and these solutions are expensive, with a form factor and power consumption that becomes challenging when incorporating into highly integrated payloads. Current state-of-art oscillators based on microelectromechanical(MEMS) resonators display competitive phase noise and frequency stability performance compared to quartz-based solutions, but thereare no European or Canadian sources of such products. Important advantages of such MEMS resonators compared to quartz-based oscillatorcan be seen, where MEMS achieves performance in between the Temperature Controlled Crystal Oscillator (TCXO) and Oven ControlledCrystal Oscillators (OCXOs) but with the advantage of their extremely small form factor, low power consumption and integration capability with Silicon process. One more important aspect is that the MEMS fundamentalmode frequency can be much higher than that of aQuartz crystal, whereas cost reduction is expected at lower frequencies and better performance at higher frequencies.This activity will design, manufacture of an engineering model oscillator chip based on European microelectromechanical technology in the 10 and500 MHz frequency range. The performance shall be suitable for a range of application scenarios in telecom payloads. The engineering model chip shall be built and tested in a critical environment, including thermal test

title: VERY LARGE AND MODULAR SOLAR ARRAYS FOR IN-ORBIT ROBOTIC ASSEMBLY - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop and manufacture a robotic testbed to demonstrate the modular solar arrays robotic assembly, and validate the functionality in a laboratory environment, validating solar array modules design, and mechanical/electrical interfaces.Description: The activity aim is to develop a very large and modular solar array that is suitable to power very large space structures and thatcan be assembled in orbit. The design of the solar array and process of manufacturing on-ground shall be developed to target the modularity but with emphasis in covering a very large area, as well as allowing in-orbit integration. These can be achieved by exploiting existing technologies or proposing novel concepts. Concentrated Photovoltaics can be also considered, particularly for large structures targeting Deep Space missions. The assembly of solar panels within in-orbit large space structures requires careful analysisof the panels mechanical and electrical interactions and interfaces, to enable the use of robots for interlinking and assembling the necessary infrastructure. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition and design of modular solar arrays and themechanical and electrical interfaces interconnecting them, suitable for building large area space structures. Targeting to obtain solar arrays 2 or 4 times bigger than current state-of-the-art. - Development and manufacturing of a robotic testbed to demonstrate the modular solar arrays robotic assembly. - Prototyping of electrical and mechanical interfaces between panels and with the robotic systems. - Initial proof of concept demonstration, verify functionality in a laboratory environment, validating solar array modules design, and mechanical/electrical interfaces.

title: ULTRA LOW POWER CONSUMPTION MICROCONTROLLER FOR DEEP SPACE HIBERNATION SYSTEMS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop an ultra-low power, Mixed Signal Microcontroller (MCU) for hibernation control for Avionics units.Description: Planetary and deep space missions necessitate a hibernation controller that can operate reliably at low power for extended periods, even under extreme temperature variations. This controller is essential for managing the wake-up and shut-down processes of avionics during planetary nights and deep space travel, ensuring the spacecraft's survival and functionality throughout the mission. Recent advancements in semiconductor technology and manufacturing have significantly reduced the power consumption of digital logic andprocessors, while also expanding their operating temperature range to include cryogenic levels. These developments are particularlyrelevant for ensuring the reliable operation of Mixed Signal Microcontrollers (MCUs) across a wide temperature spectrum at ultra-low power levels. MCUs, commonly used as primary processing units in control applications and on-board computers, can be equipped withsmall dedicated circuits to enter hibernation mode and wake up periodically for operational tasks or in response to sensor alarms. This results in power consumption as low as 10 nA. An MCU with such capabilities would be ideal for the hibernation controller in avionics subsystems, offering significant advantages over discrete solutions with limited functionality and higher power consumption. Theactivity includes a survey of available space-grade MCUs to identify a suitable candidate for managing the hibernation and control of the start-up and shut-down processes of avionics electronics. The final selection is based on a thorough analysis and environmental testing of the identified MCU. Integrating a small, ultra-low power, reliable clock and monitoring alarm circuit are used to upgrade the selected MCU to serve as a hibernation controller for planetary and deep space missions. The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Use case determination - Analysis, thermal environmental testing and selection of space grade MCUs for hibernation controller functions - Evaluation of the MCU technology for the implementation of an ultra-low power clock and monitoring alarm circuit - Design of the ultra low-power hibernation clock and monitoring alarm function - Incorporation of the hibernation clock and monitoring alarm into the MCU - Manufacturing of the hibernation MCU (h-MCU) - Thermal environmental testing of the h-MCU - Evaluation of MCU and hibernation functions - Demonstration of an h-MCU module for incorporation into space avionic systems.ProcurementPolicy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: RAYLEIGH GUIDE STAR FOR ADAPTIVE OPTICS IN OPTICAL COMMUNICATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.075) EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to evaluate the use of a Rayleigh guide star as a reference beacon for adaptive opticspre-and post-compensation for optical communication through the atmosphere.Targeted Improvements:75% reduction in cost and complexity with respect to the use of a Sodium guide star laserDescription:The use of a Rayleigh guide star as a reference beacon for optical pre-and post-compensation over the current Sodium laser solution would allow for a considerable decrease in both the cost and complexity of the laser system required for adaptive optics in optical links through the atmosphere.The Rayleigh guide star shall be evaluated for its suitability and be compared to existing solutions, to demonstrate the potential improvements. An evaluation of the sub-system, the choice of equipment and the operational implementation shall be addressed for use on optical communication links through the atmosphere. The activity will perform a numerical study comparing the main possible beacons to be used as reference for pre- and post-compensation in Adaptive Optics (AO) in the context of optical communications, using as a reference the 3 main solutions: Sodium Guide Star, Beacon from the satellite and Rayleigh Guide Star. A selection of suitable equipment solutions will need to be chosen and the impact of the beacon method on the global architecture/cost, ease of operation/complexity/laser safety of backscattered light evaluated. Upon a positive solution being proposed, integration and tests will be conducted in a laboratory environment, and then on-sky tests will be conducted.

title: SCALABLE PHOTOVOLTAIC TECHNOLOGIES FOR TELECOMMUNICATION CONSTELLATIONS MASS PRODUCTION (ARTES AT 4F.183) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test innovative III-V solar cell s processes and associated disruptive photovoltaic assembly technologies aiming to reduce the complexity, manufacturing and assembly time to meet the high demand of telecommunication satellites constellations. III-V solar cells will be developed and tested using thedeveloped processes along with flexible Photovoltaic Assembly (PVA) mini modules.Targeted Improvements: - Enabling a European source of III-IV solar cells and PVAs for satcom constellations by - At least a factor of 2 reduction of the epitaxial growth time- Enabling substrate reuse in the fabrication - Enabling a standardised and flexible PVA mini module for mass production of solar arrays.Description: In the space telecommunications sector, the shift from GEO satellites to LEO constellations requires advanced solar technologies that offer a balance of high performance, scalable manufacturing and proven reliability across diverse LEO mission profiles. Within this evolving landscape,III-V multi-junction cells remain the benchmark in terms of efficiency and performance, but complexity, manufacturing and assembly time must be significantly improved to meet the growing demand for constellations. In order to achieve this goal,innovative processes must be developed to increase the production capacity. Development efforts should not focus solely on solar cell technology but must also extend to the photovoltaics assembly (PVA) level, enabling the realisation of standardised modular and scalable PVA solutions tailored to constellation needs.This activity will focus on III-V solar cells and their associated PVA technologies. It will study and develop solutions to two main primary factors currently limiting the scalability of III-V solar cells:- Reducing epitaxial growth time at least by a factor of 2 by increasing the growth rate of III-V materials while maintaining high opto-electronic properties. For doing so, new and disruptive epitaxial growth processes must be developed.- Enabling substrate reuse in the fabrication through the implementation of innovative Epitaxial Lift-Off (ELO) processes either chemical or mechanical based. The ELO process provides a dual benefit, as it supports the production of flexible, ultra-thin solar cells (e.g. 30um thick) and contributes to reduce the use of critical materials in the substrate (e.g. Germanium recycling). A combination of a mechanical and chemical lift-off approaches will be studied and developed to optimise the overall ELO process.The resulting developed III-V based solar cells will be manufactured and tested. They will serve as a critical building block for the development of a flexible PVA blanket. Interconnection and encapsulation technologies will be developed and tested. Finally, a standardised and flexible PVA mini-module, designed to function as a plug-and-playbuilding block for mass production of solar arrays, will be developed and testedProcurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: CIMR COMPANION MISSION CONCEPT DEFINITION SYSTEM STUDY - EXPRO PLUS
description: Mission Concept Study (pre-Phase 0) to explore potential mission concept for a companion satellite to CIMR the context of the exploration step for a potential Mission of Opportunity. A Mission of Opportunity (MoO) is defined as an Earth Observation Research Mission in cooperation with a Space Agency outside ESA Member/Cooperating/Associated States. The turbulent fluxes between the ocean and atmosphere are fundamental to understanding and quantifying the exchange of heat, moisture, momentum and gas between the ocean and the atmosphere. They directly impact atmospheric and oceanic variability, thereby modifying weather and climate, including precipitation patterns, terrestrial water availability, floods and droughts, and extreme events such as terrestrial and marine heatwaves. A key challenge to address is the fact that satellite-derived estimates of ocean-atmosphere fluxes are derived from multi-mission satellite data that are not co-located or contemporaneous in space and time leading to large sampling errors and uncertainties. Today, there is no satellite system designed to measure ocean fluxes from space. The Copernicus Imaging Microwave Radiometer (CIMR) isplanned for launch in 2029 and will provide measurements of sea ice parameters sea surface temperature, ocean vector winds and salinity, based on 1.4, 6.9, 10.65, 18.9 and 36.5GHz channels over a 1900 km swath. Since this mission uses a mesh reflector, it cannotinclude frequencies above Ka-band effectively ruling out lower troposphere air temperature and humidity sounding channels that are required to compute collocated and contemporaneous ocean and atmosphere flux estimates. This procurement will investigate and analyse different system concepts (including platform and instrument) targeting a medium size companion mission for CIMR that would provide higher frequency (e.g. 50-184GHz) channel capability. Together with the CIMR mission, these data would be used to retrieve lower troposphere air temperature and humidity profiles. This study will run in parallel and interact with the CIMR Companion Mission Concept Definition Science Study, subject of a parallel ITT. The output of the study will be a dossier of different mission concepts(including potential pre-development activities, technological roadmap, schedule, and estimated cost elements) that can be used is support to its potential approval to initiate a subsequent Phase 0.

title: SP-SW-02 INITIAL SPACE WEATHER SERVICE OPERATIONS
description: This activity will constitute the establishment and operation of the initial EU Space Weather service including interfacing with end users and provision of the service.The scope of the service shall cover all relevant space weather phenomena and their potential impact on spacecraft and space surveillance and tracking (SST) including in-situ radiation and plasma environments, variations in upper atmospheric density potentially leading to increased thermospheric drag and ionospheric conditions leading to possible communication disturbances.The aim of the service shall be to reduce vulnerabilities of European operators within the domain to negative impacts of space weather, reducing the duration of any resulting service disruption, and supporting the operational activities of SST services. The service shall provide the users with timely and reliable space weather bulletins and alerts based on near real-time monitoring, nowcast and forecast of space weather conditions and their potential impacts on spacecraft along with information to support post-event-analysis. It will include a helpdesk with both technical and domain specific support available to service users when needed, both during and outside normal working hours.

title: NOVEL METROLOGY SYSTEM FOR VERY LARGE DEPLOYABLE OR SEGMENTED ULTRASTABLE TELESCOPE EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a real-time in-orbit optomechanical metrology system enabling very large segmented or distributed aperture telescopes and their in-orbit active correction and control.Description: In 2040, progress in astro architecture and in-orbit manufacturing and integration could enable the affordable construction of very large telescopes based on either filled apertures with a large number of segments or sparse sub apertures with large numbers of distributed mirrors. These very large telescopes have the power to unlock revolutionary leaps in both Astrophysics and Earth observation thanks to their extreme resolution and collecting power. This activity targets future missions in those domains. This activity focuses on the metrology system at the core of the opto-mechanical architecture of those very large telescopes. For such telescopes to function properly, all main elements of the optical system (primary mirror segments of distributed sub apertures, M2 and other mirrors, focal plane instruments entrance interfaces) need to be extremely accurately located over large distances in order to control and correct their position via an active correction loop. Several technological solutions for sensors have been envisaged (laser truss, interferometric sensors, videogrammetry...) but their technological maturity, space implementation and organisation in a coherent metrology system interfacing with a correction loop needs to be developed. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Review of current state-of-the-art metrology systems for large telescopes and requirements of active correction chains. - For both segmented and distributed aperture cases, study of novel metrology sensors for space applications and metrology system for ultra large telescopes allowing to control the optomechanical structures and components within the range of an active correction chain. This metrology system shall allow for combination of different technological bricks in order to address the different ranges necessary to accurately sense the position and orientation of the different optomechanical key elements. - Development of a breadboard and related data processing and software demonstrating the adequacy of such a metrology system in terms of accuracy and range. - Roadmap for the development of a full-scale metrology system based on the concept solution found.

title: PHASED ARRAYS EXPLOITING GRATING LOBESFOR SCATTEROMETER INSTRUMENTS EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop a representative demonstrator of a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array with a reduced number of control points, by exploiting grating lobes.Description: For Earth Observation applications there are instruments, like Scatterometers, requiring a limited number of beams M pointing in fixed directions. A promising antenna architecture is based on an array antenna organized in interleaved subarrays (number of subarrays equal to the number of target beams M). Each subarray is having the periodic cell split in M sub-apertures. One of the M sub-apertures is occupied by a radiating element, the other M-1 slots are kept emptyto be used by the other M-1 interleaved subarrays. The dimension of the periodic cell is larger than one wavelength in order to create grating lobes exactly in the directions where the desired beams of the Scatterometer instrument are targeted. The array factor associated to the M phase centres of the M subarrays, when fed with identical phase value, creates a beam pointing at the boresight direction with radiative nulls positions coinciding with the grating lobes positions. Accordingly, when feeding the M inputs with thesame phase value a main beam in the boresight direction can be generated and the M-1 grating lobes can be cancelled by the radiative nulls. When feeding the M inputs with a linear phase in order to point the main beam exactly at one of the M possible targeted angles, the radiative nulls permit to cancel all the subarray pattern beams except the desired one. The M beams can be generated one atthe time, or simultaneously by adding a small beamforming MxM network. Possible values for M could be 3 or 5. To be noted also thatthecorresponding beams can be placed in the same azimuthal plane or not. This beamforming solution permits to reduce by a factor Mthe number of controls (phase shifters, direction couplers, amplifiers). As a consequence, a significant reduction in the cost and complexity of the entire instrument can be achieved. Reducing by a factor 3-5 the number of passive and active components in a Scatterometer instrument based on a phased array. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Instrument identification and requirements refinement. - Technology trade-off and down-selection. - Identification/optimization of most promising architectures. - Preliminary design of a baseline architecture and back-up architecture - Detailed design of a baseline architecture - Define preliminary manufacturing technique and prototype. - Definition of test and verification plan - Breadboard manufacturing and test - Results analysis and evaluation.

title: STRUCTURAL ULTRA-COMPACT FLAT BATTERIES BASED ON HIGH SPECIFIC ENERGY MATERIALS EXPRO+
description: To develop ultra-compact and structurally integrated flat batteries using materials with high specific energy.Description: Structural flat batteries that enhance spacecraft performance while reducing launch costs and system complexity show high potential in thepresent satellite market. This activity aims to develop ultra-compact, structurally integrated flat batteries using materials with high specific energy, for space applications with the intent of optimizing energy storage efficiency, while reducing weight and volume. The activity aims at exploring advanced materials, processes, and innovative designs to enhance performance and integration within spacecraft structures. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Literature review on Advanced Materials and structural batteries: Investigate and identify materials with high specific energy, that are/could be suitable for space applications. This includes studying their properties, performance, and compatibility with spacecraft structures and environment. - Innovative Design and Integration: Develop innovative designs that allow for integration of flat batteries within spacecraft structures. This involves optimizing the battery's shape, size, and placement to ensure efficient energy storage and minimal impact on the spacecraft's overall weight and volume. - Process Development: Explore advanced manufacturing processes to produce flat batteries. This includes techniques such as 3D printing, layering, and other methods that can enhance the battery's performance and integration. The capability of the supply chain shall be key to ensure industry competitiveness, by improving its affordability and industrialization and to reduce totaltime required to source materials, manufacture and deliver the battery. Furthermore, European independence in procurement and finalcosts should be taken into account. - Performance Enhancement: Conduct experiments and simulations to enhance the battery's performance. This should include testing the batteries under various conditions to ensure they meet the required standards for space applications. - Integration Testing: Perform integration tests to ensure the batteries work seamlessly within the spacecraft structures. This should include testing the batteries' compatibility with other systems and components.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. description: The aim of this activity is to establish a robust and validated greenhouse gas emissions baseline for the European space sector in support of ESA's broader decarbonisation roadmap. The work includes defining the sector scope and system boundaries, developing a harmonised accounting methodology, collecting and consolidating data from relevant stakeholders, quantifying emissions for a referenceyear, validating results, and preparing outputs that can directly inform future decarbonisation actions, target-setting, and strategic decision-making across the sector.

title: SOFTWARE UPDATES SMS, MATERIAL AND LORENTZ - EXPRO+
description: The ESA Antenna Laboratory operates several unique antenna and RF material measurement facilities, including the Sub-mmWave Scanner(SMS), LORENTZ cryogenic near-field scanner, and CATR Material Characterisation Facility. These facilities support antenna and RF characterisation activities covering a frequency range extending from microwave to sub-millimetre-wave frequencies and are routinely used in support of ESA programmes, technology developments, industrial activities and research campaigns.Operation ofthese facilities relies on dedicated custom-developed software that interfaces with motion control systems, network analysers and auxiliary equipment to perform automated measurements, collect measurement data and generate outputs suitable for post-processing andanalysis. Overthe past decade, this software has evolved through multiple development and maintenance activities, supporting successive laboratory upgrades and increasingly demanding measurement campaigns. The software currently comprises three principal application domains: SMS scanner control software. LORENTZ scanner control software. CATR Material Characterisation control software.In addition, a growing set of shared software components has been introduced to provide common functionality across facilities, including hardware abstraction, configuration management, measurement orchestration, data management and graphical user interfaces. Historically, software development activities were executed through a number of independent projects. Consequently, different facilities evolved at different rates and software versions diverged over time. Recent maintenance activities have established a common software management approach based on GitLab repositories, issue tracking mechanisms and shared software components, improving traceability and maintainability of the software assets. The LORENTZ and CATR applications now share a modern architecture built around common software libraries and hardware abstraction layers. The SMS software remains operational but is based on anearlier architecture and represents the principal remaining source of technical debt within the software suite. Long-term sustainability of the Antenna Laboratory software therefore requires continued maintenance, harmonisation and progressive migration towards acommon software framework.The software environment further depends on several third-party components, including software drivers and interfaces fromKeysight, ACS Motion Control, Trio Motion Technology and other equipment suppliers. Maintaining compatibility withcommercial operating systems, hardware drivers and measurement instruments is therefore an essential part of maintaining the operational capability of the Antenna Laboratory. As several ESA facilities depend on the availability, reliability and traceability of measurement data,particular attention must be given to configuration control, software version management, measurement file compatibility and preservation of laboratory know-how. The software shall therefore be maintained as an operational laboratory asset rather than as a standalone development project.- Objective(s) of the ActivityThe objective of the activity is to ensure the continuous operation, maintenance, evolution and long-term sustainability of the Antenna Laboratory software systems, while preserving compatibility with existing facilities, measurement workflows and historical measurement data.

title: HIGH-SPEED QUANTUM RANDOM NUMBER GENERATOR FOR SATELLITE PAYLOADS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3H.005) EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a free-space communication link with optical key distribution (OKD) functionality.TargetedImprovements:Improvement of the key distribution rate by at least a factor of 100 with respect to QKD, alternatively, the reduction of the aperture sizes of both terminals(for the same key rate as QKD). Provision of the security assessment for OKD.Description: In the vast majority of cases, the security of communication systems is only ensured at their digital layers, leaving the lowest physical layer open toeavesdropping and interference. The primary concern in space scenarios is passive attacks, where the adversary is often able to capture an even largerportion of the signal than the legitimate receiver(s). At the same time, feasible physical layer security (PLS) solutions must meet the stringent SWaP (size,weight, and power) requirements of space missions and should be easily integrated with data transmission, even in the case of the simplest intensitymodulation/direct detection (IM/DD) links.Optical Key Distribution (OKD) is a promising solution for secure communication. It allows authenticated parties to establish a secure cryptographic key,by exploiting the high directionality of optical beams. By using optical noise, OKD is cost-effective and suitable for free-space communications, such asinter-satellite and satellite-to-ground links. The technique distributes a secure key that can be used for encryption protocols like AES, SSL/TLS, or as aone-time pad. It avoids the complexities and high costs of quantum key distribution (QKD) systems while providing adequate security for free-spacescenarios. OKD keys are quantum-safe, assuming the adversary's detection capability is limited by shot noise.The activity aims to investigate and develop a cost-effective solution for the physical layer security of optical satellite communication links, namely OpticalKey Distribution (OKD), which allows authenticated parties to establish a secure key, by monitoring the presence of an eavesdropper along the satelliteto-ground line-of-sight, while avoiding the complexity and resulting significant costs of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) systems. The activity will establishsecurity assumption for OKD and provide the security assessment of the proposed OKD system. The outcome of thiswork shall be evaluated by a security expert with competencies in the protection of communication links.

title: RESILIENT COMMUNICATION SYSTEM IN NON-GEOSTATIONARY HIGH-ALTITUDE INCLINED ELLIPTICAL ORBITS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 3A.230) - EXPRO+ (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: The objective of this activity is to define the system requirements and the preliminary concept of a resilient communication systemoperating in non-geostationary high-altitude ellipticalorbits.TargetedImprovements: Enabling the development of high altitude inclined elliptical orbits satellite communications systems in ESA Member States for providing resilient communications.Description: Satcom satellites typically fly in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), Medium Earth Orbit (MEO), or Geostationary Orbit (GEO). However, high-altitude elliptical orbits (HEO) offer special features ofinterest to resilient and secure satcom systems. This includes in particular coverage of Europe and polar regions thanks to the large orbital inclination. Furthermore, the HEO platform isexpected to share design and development similarities with existing GEO platforms, enabling faster development and deployment.Such a HEO system can enable the rapid provision of resilient and secure satellite communications for governmental use, ensuring secure service continuity andoperational resiliencethat satisfy the short-term secure communication needs. It will consist of several satellites placed in different orbits. This approach will provide an initial layer of protection againstjamming, as a single jammer would be unable to disrupt more than one satellite. Further robustness of the system shall be provided based on anti-jamming capabilities to be investigatedin the activity.In this activity, the different governmental and commercial use cases will be investigated, and mission and user requirements will be derived.The activity will study and compare multiple orbits of interest, and define concepts of mission, system, satellite, payload, and user terminal required to achieve the desired services.System requirements will be derived. In addition to anti jamming capability, the study shall analyse and trade-off various techniques for the system to stay resilient to other kinetic andnon-kinetic impairments. System development and deployment plan, business and cost analysis and related technology roadmap shall be defined. The defined use cases and theirrelated performance shall be confirmed by means of a comprehensive mission/system simulator.A key result of the analysis will be the confirmation of the possibility to develop and rapidly deploy the satellites for the envisioned HEO system, leveraging the experience of the Europeanindustry acquired in the development of platforms and payloads for GEO orbit

title: CONSOLIDATION PHASE OF IRIS LOW LEO PRE-OPERATIONAL AND DE-RISK ACTIVITIES- EXPRO+
description: IRIS Low LEO Pre-Operational and De-Risk Activities components are part of theElement 3 of the ESA Programme and are intended to provide pre-operational servicevalidation and in-orbit demonstration opportunities. These aim at enabling rapid andrecurrent cycles, in alignment with ESA Ministerial Council cycles, from service-orientedconcepts to orbit and establishing a structured pathway for the maturation and de-risking ofsystem concepts and services prior to their integration into the EU IRIS system.The Procurement Plan outlines the proposed procurement framework, describes theupcoming preparatory actions and provides indicative timelines forprocurement activitiesfor IRIS Low LEO Pre-Operational and De-Risk Activities components as part of theElement 3 of the ESA Programme, in alignment with applicable ESA and EU objectives.Procurement activities will also be conducted by the European Commission in the EU IRIS2programme; these are not described within the scope of this document. In pursuit of acoordinated approach with the European Commission, coordination mechanisms betweenthe EU IRIS2 programme and ESA Programme are described in this document.Not covered by the scope of the ESA Programme are any subsequent activities to transitionthe pre-operational developments in these components of the ESA Programme towardstheir operational deployment in the EU IRIS2 programme (e.g. system integration, serviceentry intooperation, or follow-on development).In the short-term, the focus is on defining and establishing the framework required to executethe first ESA Ministerial Council cycle. This includes the consolidation of the services ofinterest for the European Commission and the initiation of the first procurement actions,aimed at enabling timely contract signature as early as Q3 2026.In the medium-term, corresponding to an ESA Ministerial Council cycle, the procurementstrategy is proposed in two-phases: A "Consolidation phase"followed by an "Implementationphase"The Consolidation phase targets a level comparable to maturation activities associated withPhase A/B1. The Implementation phase targets a level comparable to maturation activitiesassociated with Phase B2/C/D, while remaining strictly limited up to pre-operationalobjectives.A first Invitation to Tender "ITT1" will be issued for the Consolidation phase. A secondInvitation to Tender "ITT2" (not limited to those participating in ITT1) will be issued for theImplementation phase.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: EO PLATFORM INTEROPERABLE BUILDING BLOCK EVOLUTION FRAMEWORK - COORDINATION
description: Cloud-based platforms have proven to be an essential cornerstone for a paradigm shift in Earth Observation (EO), suitable to allow science and application initiatives to efficiently manage the huge volume of data availability in a "bring-the-user-to-the-data" paradigm. This paradigm has been demonstrated to be a critical enabler of innovation and acceleration, which in the European context needs to leverage a fragmented cloud and platform ecosystem, developed with a multitude of industrial and public investments at European and National level. The overall objective of the proposed contractual framework is to evolve and develop the generic standards and interoperable Building Blocks (BBs) allowing to consolidate and harmonise a federated EO cloud and platform offering that can support common utilisation scenarios of the EO Science, RD, and applications community. These BBs shall allow tailoring to specific community environments at national, European, or international collaboration level that serve FAIR (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) and Open Science principles to preserve RD project results for future use and to share data, code, and project results to large communities on cloud-based environments. Institutional and Industrial operational stakeholders shall be incentivised to contribute to a common opensource base. The framework shall support all ESA EO-related programmatic activities and promote the Member States' strategic view to international bodies, mainly OGC, CEOS and GEO. This tender will select a prime contractor for the overall contract management and technical coordination, with a contract commitment for a 3-year period with an optional 2-year extension. Subcontractors to implement the work streams will be selected in open competition via the ESA Best Practice (BP) Approach.

title: DIRECT-TO-DEVICE MULTIBAND ACTIVE ANTENNA IN FREQUENCY RANGE 1 (FR 1) (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5B.259) - EXPRO+
description: Direct-to-Device (D2D) for unmodified handsets, Machine-to-Machine (M2M) and Internet of Things (IoT) communications are rapidly becoming a key focus area for the satellite sector. Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations with active antennas are well suited for a broad range of these services with low latency. UHF-, L- and S-Band are envisaged for D2D systems in FR 1. The multifrequency and generic aspect of future D2D payloads is only viable if the active antenna critical RF building blocks (multi-band Transmit / Receive radiating element, filtering and amplification stages) are available to meet the challenging multiband requirements. This activity will develop and test generic and multi-band building blocks of a FR 1 Transmit / Receive active antenna for LEO constellations. A modular active array scaled EM (as a minimum a 4x4 tile including Transmit / Receive radiating elements, filtering and amplification stages) shall be manufactured and tested for critical functions in a relevant environment.

title: NAVISP-EL1-124-OPTIMISATION OF PVT ENGINES FOR LEO MEASUREMENT DIVERSITY - EXPRO+
description: This activity focuses on designing and optimizing Position, Velocity, and Time (PVT) engines specifically for LEO-based PNT systems. It aims to exploit the unique measurement diversity offered by LEO satellites, such as multipath whitening, Doppler utilization, and rapid LOS/NLOS transitions. Two approaches will be developed and compared: a conventional Kalman filter-based design and an AI/ML-based design to handle unexpected LEO measurement behaviours. The study will include state-of-the-art review, algorithm development, and benchmarking against traditional MEO GNSS-based engines. Field measurement campaigns will validate performance and inform a roadmap for commercialization. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity

title: HIGH-ENERGY SOLID-STATE BATTERY CELL FOR SATCOM APPLICATION (ARTES AT 4F.173) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop, manufacture and test a high-energy, solid-state battery cell with a specific energy over 300 Wh/kg and a minimum capacity of 4-5 Ah.Targeted Improvements:- Enabling high energy low volume battery for high ratio aspect satellite.- Increase specific energy at cell level by at least 35%- Increase cell intrinsic safety.Description: Batteries are a key component of the power sub-system of telecommunication satellites and have a significant impact in the platform design. The size and mass of satellite batteries is driven by the current achievable specific and volumetric energy parameters and operational depth of discharge (DoD). Solid state battery is considered as next generation battery technology due to significant improvement compared to conventional Li ion technology: more energy, more power, increased safety and higher production rates. Other concepts, like a new application of composite materials to create a multi-functional composite panel that can store electrical charge, could also be very relevant for flat satellites applications.This activity will conduct a thorough state-of-the-art assessment on solid state battery technologies in Europe and world-wide. A battery cell breadboard with a capacity of at least 4 Ah, and a specific energy of 300 Wh/kg will be designed, developed, manufactured and tested. The test campaign will include cycling at 100% Depth of Discharge to validate their cyclability, accelerated life tests and safety tests. Finally, a manufacturing upscale assessment will be performed to assess the feasibility for mass production.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of qualityand quantity) of non-primes (incl. title: OPTIMISATION OF THE SPECTRUM UTILISATION LEVERAGING EXISTING SPACE- AND GROUND-BASED RF MONITORING SYSTEMS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 3A.223) EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective:The objective of this activity is to identify, develop, and demonstrate at least five use cases where the active use of RF monitoring improves spectrum utilisation.Targeted Improvements:Spectrum utilisation efficiency increase of at least 20%. Enhanced spectrum sharing of at least 10%.Description:Despite advancements in RF spectrum monitoring technologies, there is a notable lack of practical examples demonstrating how such monitoring systems can be effectively used to optimise spectrum usage and sharing.While the technology has progressed, particularly in terms of monitoring capabilities and data collection, hardly any real-world examples showcasehow these systems can be leveraged to actively improve spectrum efficiency.This activity aims to identify, developand demonstrate, in collaboration with both space- and ground-based RF monitoring providers, several use cases in which the active use of RF spectrum monitoring can significantly improve spectrum utilisation. This activity will leverage upon several dynamic spectrum sharing activities which have been completed, but put them into a realistic context, using actual RF measurements instead of simulations.These scenarios will focus on how leveraging measurements obtained from RF monitoring systems can result in optimised spectrum utilisation. This involves the development of a representative environment where existing space- and ground-based RF spectrum monitoring systems and the optimisation of spectrum usage scenarios are demonstrated. As part of the demonstration, the bidder shallderive the improvement factor achieved due to the active use of RF spectrum monitoring systems. The findings shall be derived into a set of guidelines for the optimisation of spectrum utilisation using RF monitoring systems, to address issues like dynamic spectrum sharing, interference management and cross-border spectrum coordination, as well as the identification of capability gaps and future developments.

title: DIRECT COOLING SYSTEM FOR HIGH PERFORMANCE, HIGH POWER (300W CLASS) TELECOM SIGNAL PROCESSING COMPONENTS (ARTES AT 4D.087) - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE (1-12828)
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop and test an active two-phase cooling system capable to remove in the order of 300Watts from a single electronic component (e.g. switch/router Integrated Circuit).Targeted Improvements:Increase by at least a factor of 5 the maximum thermal dissipation of signal processing components that can be supported on a spacecraft.Description: Modern satellite telecommunications systems are moving towards on board regenerative payloads, capable of routing high throughput real time traffic across the system. As a result, satellite technology providers and integrators have started considering powerful digital integrated circuits, often developed for the terrestrial market, with extremely high powerconsumption and dissipation(in the range of several hundreds of Watts), creating an unprecedented thermal bottleneck at component level (factor 6 to 10 increase ofthermal dissipation with respect to heritage space grade devices). In order to able to dissipate the large amount of power witha very high heat flux density, new technics such as microchannel cooling, direct spray cooling or jet impingement cooling, alreadyutilised in terrestrial applications, will need to be studied, traded-off and developed. The design of the integrated circuits willneed as well to consider thermal aspects (e.g. internal thermal gradients). The availability of a high performing component thermalmanagement solutionwill as well benefit other highly dissipative elements of the payload and platform, such as Power Field Effect Transistors (FET) commonly used in many equipment and RF amplifiers.This activity will start with a comprehensive state-of-the-art technology survey with corresponding trade-offs to select a preferred technical solution and implementation architectures to supportthe use of high dissipation components in the next generation of spacecraft platform and payloads. A representative breadboard of the selected technology(ies) will be designed, built and tested to evaluate the performance of the cooling system. Finally, the activity will identify key remaining risks in the technology and the necessary developmentactivities that would be required to generate the corresponding space suitable commercial solution.

title: URBAN DEVELOPMENT, LIVEABILITY AND ADAPTATION - EXPRO+
description: The Urban Development, Liveability and Adaptation RD activity comprises three projects to develop, together with key end-users, Earth Observation-integrated solutions addressing key urban challenges: 1) World Informal Settlements will develop regional to global EO-based methodology to identify, characterise and monitor evolution of informal settlements, providing consistent and scalable statistics and socio-economic indicators; 2) Urban Liveability and Adaptation will develop EO-based indicators to assess urban liveability by integrating data on land use, built-up density, urban form, and key climatic, environmental and social-economic factors, to inform and support urban planning and adaptation strategies; 3) EO for sustainable mobility will develop EO based methodology to perform mobility patterns analysis in relation to urban structure and population distribution, in support of urban sustainable mobility planning.

title: S3-CL-06 SECURE AUTONOMOUS DISPOSAL INTERFACE SAFETY MODULE - REISSUED
description: The increase in small satellite missions has intensified the need for compliance to international space debris de-orbiting requirements. To meet these requirements CubeSat-class missions frequently rely on their primary On-Board Computer (OBC) and Electrical Power Subsystem (EPS) to activate disposal mechanisms, however deployment and late-mission failures; such as battery degradation, bus freeze, or cyber compromise; can prevent successful disposal execution.This activity addresses this gap through the development of the Secure Autonomous Disposal Interface and Safety Module: a standardised, independent Disposal Trigger Module (DTM) compatible withCubeSat buses from 1U to 16U across a variety of disposal mechanisms. The DTM shall implement two autonomy levels of increasing complexity and prove resilient to spacecraft failures and cyberattacks. The project targets bring the technology to TRL6.

title: COMBINED COMMUNICATIONS AND PNT USER TERMINAL DEVELOPMENT - EXPRO PLUS
description: The LightShip mission envisions deploying passenger spacecraft in Low Mars Orbit equipped with a User Terminal (UT) to access communications and position, navigation and timing (PNT) services. Developing a combined communications and PNT terminal would reduce size and mass, benefiting both spacecraft and overall mission efficiency, while also offering applicability to future deep space and lunar missions. The objective is to design a modular hardware architecture adaptable to various mission profiles, including transfer, orbital, lander, and surface operations. The software will include generic components alongside a customizable navigation engine, with a focus on real-time reduced dynamic solutions for demanding scenarios such as Mars transfer and orbiting. The activity will alsovalidate navigation techniques combining one-way and two-way measurements to improve accuracy and timing. Ground Support Equipment will be developed to test system performance under simulated Mars conditions, supporting hardware and software design, manufacturing,testing, and future flight model development.

title: COMMON AND REDUCED INTERFACES FOR MID-SIZE SATELLITE INDUSTRIALISATION (M-IND) - EXPRO+
description: A Mid-size satellite INDustrialisation (M-IND) consultation to European mid-size satellite (100 to 500 kg) integrators was organized in March 2025. Two key recommendations are relevant to this activity are: the need for reducing the number of interfaces in mid-size satellites in order to enable compatibility, multi-source and interoperability of platform equipment and payloads; the timeliness in the delivery of Earth Observation (EO) data to ground needs to improve when using LEO constellations with high revisit.This activity aims at the reduction and commonalisation of mostly, but not only electrical interfaces. It is deemed very important to base it on a to be agreed avionics high-level reference architecture that can meet high level system requirements (e.g. mid-size platforms compatible with EO payloads suitable for LEO constellations, timely delivery of data to ground). The activity includes a consultation to M-IND European integrators and key equipment suppliers via a Survey and the organisation of mini-Workshops in order tofind as much consensus as possible regarding the selection of a reduced and common set of Interfaces. A number of deliveries in thestudy are public (i.e. not proprietary) so that they can be used in future equipment and EO payload adaptations to the common interfaces to be selected in this activity.

title: NOVAMOON PHASES B/C/D/E/F
description: Approved at CM25 under Component 3: Future PNT Demonstrators of the FutureNAV Programme, NovaMoon is a lunar-based local differential, selenodetic/geodetic and timing station that will enhance Moonlight and LunaNet lunar PNT services and support lunar scientificexperimentation. This activity comprises Phases B/C/D/E/F of NovaMoon and is organized in three incremental builds, the development of which would allow to reach the full NovaMoon configuration (meeting all NovaMoon mission objectives) with NovaMoon Build3 aimed to fly on Argonaut2. NovaMoon Intermediate Builds1 and 2 will be designed to be as lander independent as possible (providing maximum flexibility in terms of lander opportunities). NovaMoon aims to demonstrate the following main objectives:1. Reference localPNT differential station (< 1 metre accuracy in real time),2. International Advanced "geodetic" Lunar Reference Station (< 10 cm accuracy),3. International "Lunar Time-reference" Laboratory ( ns-level).

title: OPENING THE BLACK BOX: SELF-EXPLAINABLE AI FOR EARTH OBSERVATION - EXPRO+
description: The wide adoption of AI in Earth Observation (EO) has been hindered in some cases by the lack of the transparency and explainability of the underlying decision makings process of AI algorithms and the limited explainability and trustworthiness of the proposed model outcomes and predictions. The objective of this activity is to provide a significant methodological improvement in the field of AI explainability for EO, as well as its application to downstream applications in the field of Rapid mapping of disasters and Climate Change. Another key output of the activity shall be the development of a state-of-the-art open-source AI model aimed to help end users/stakeholders with fast, accurate and trustworthy AI model outputs. The model itself and its outputs shall be inherently interpretable and self-explainable, e.g. at the same time as predicting, the model will generate text output to help understand the rational and/or reasoning. This activity shall be applied to at least two downstream use cases (Rapid mapping of disasters and Climate Change) provided by end-users engaged in the activity. These use-cases shall have high impact in the field and end-users' activity.

The model itself and its outputs shall be inherently interpretable and self-explainable, e.g. at the same time as predicting, the model will generate text output to help understand the rational and/or reasoning. This activity shall be applied to at least two downstream use cases (Rapid mapping of disasters and Climate Change) provided by end-users engaged in the activity. These use-cases shall have high impact in the field and end-users' activity.

title: MINIATURIZATION OF NITROGEN-VACANCY CENTER-BASED MAGNETOMETERS - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a space proven NV-Centred Diamond magnetometer with reduced SWaP. Description: Magnetic field measurements from low Earth orbit are important for understanding Earth's magnetosphere, monitoring of space weather, and studying geophysical processes. These measurements provide insights into solar-terrestrial interactions and help mitigate risks to both orbital infrastructure and terrestrial systems. NV -centres magnetometers are recent developments that have been successfully implemented on the ISS. Next to their scientific interest, one of their applications lays in using the magnetic field for AOCS purposes in space. Using a magnetic map, the full attitude of the spacecraft can be followed. This has been demonstrated during the first Ariane launch where one of these systems could follow the first minutes of the trajectory of the rocket. There is now the need to further develop such system to allow them to be utilized for navigation of spacecrafts or on other bodies (which have a magnetic field) with a specific focus on reduction of size and mass of the instrument to be integrated to AOCS system. The development shall be focused on miniaturisation and reduction of resources and on increasing the resolution of the magnetometers to pT. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Consolidation of technical requirements given application in miniature quantum devices and preliminary design.- Detailed design of the magnetometer. - Manufacturing, integration and functional verification. - Test campaign, outcomes and development plan to qualification. Deliverables: Breadboard, Reports

title: NEW RF TECHNOLOGIES FOR MM-LEVEL ACCURACY METROLOGY - EXPRO PLUS (RE-ISSUE - 1-11776)
description: Spaceborne two-way links in Ku-band or above have since long shown their value in providing extremelyaccurate ranging such as Two-Way Time and Frequency Transfer by Satellite (TWTFTS) and the microwavelinks supporting ACES or GRACE. So far, their benefits have been bounded to timing and gravimetry becauseof the very few satellites equipped.Many more scientific applications (e.g. geodesy) could use such capabilities if available with a continuousworldwide coverage and from multiple satellites. However, the feasibilityof adapting these technologies to a wide coverage involving many satellites still needs to be demonstrated because of the multiple low TRLtechnological challenges such as highly-accurate multi-beam fixed user terminal, multiple access techniques,links calibration, payload complexity and power consumption.The purpose of this activity is to investigate and demonstrate the technological feasibility of introducing two-way RF metrology with mm-level ranging accuracy in a multiple access system architecture in particular inEHF bands (e.g. 44/47 GHz or 66/71 GHz).This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Assessment of the state-of-the-art (e.g. RFmetrology and TWTFTS, benchmark with optical technologies,etc.),- Feasibility and preliminary performance analysis of different architectures of the RF links for various usecases (Gateway-to-Gateway, Gateway-to-User and User-to-User) to identify the most promising ones,including trade-off for the most adequate frequencies vs. L-band and optical links,- Development of a early breadboard /proof-of-concept of the end-to-end RF link, involving technologies(non-space qualified) representative of the critical functions atpayload and user terminal level,- Characterization of the achieved performances for the different scenarios and working points (rangingaccuracy, calibration, multiple access, etc.).Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: E3CS-048 - DEVELOPMENT OF GLOW-BENCH: GLOVEBOX OPTICAL WORK-BENCH
description: The proposed concept involves procuring a modular unit starting with an Optical Bench. Thisbench will feature payload interfaces compatible with the ISS's Microgravity Science Glovebox,ensuring seamless transfer of existing legacy payloads. The unit will be designed with a minimumworking volume of 450L, providing essential resources such as water cooling, mounting area,power, data, and gas/venting interfaces. A standard top bench interface will allow for the accommodation of various kits totransform theunit, enabling a broad range of applications:- glovebox kits for biological/chemical containment- shielding kits for precise optical measurements- kits for accommodating portable COTS (Commercial Off-The-Shelf) systems, such as Pointof-Care (PoC) devices, microscopes, etc.This modular approach aims to enhance ESA's research capabilities and strategically positionthe agencywithin the evolving LEO commercial landscape.

title: GT1I-800GA AI APPLICATION SUITE FOR GROUND SEGMENT OPERATIONS
description: The development of a suite of AI applications for accurate and reliable prognostics and health management ofspacecraft represents a significant advancement and opportunity in space technology. AI systems, leveragingmachine learning algorithms and data from various sensors, enhance the capability to monitor the health andperformance of spacecraft in real-time, predicting potential failures before they occur and ensuring optimaloperation. However, current AI tools are often separate and specialised, leading to inefficiency. There is aneed for a seamless, unified suite with shared features like explainability, data handling, and consistentinterfaces. This will make AI easier to use and adopt across teams. Many new technologies and approachesare in active development. Especially, use of federated learning and continual learning lead to reducedcomputation demands and enable more powerful AI techniques, suchas prediction remaining useful lifetimeof components. Additionally, whilst traditional AI/ML approaches have been proven valuable solutions to detectanomalies during routine operations, they degrade fail in accuracy, generalization and interpretability whennovel conditions are encountered or manoeuvres are performed. AI-enhanced modelling and simulation toolssuch as Digital Twins, which integrate Operational simulators, which emulate OBC and run OBSW with AImodels to enhance the fidelity of the simulations and are provide credible representativeness of the behaviourof spacecraft under various conditions. This allows for more personalized/tailoredmodelling which will enhancethe accuracy of prognostics and health management capabilities. They can model novel conditions andconsider the effect of manoeuvres and procedures in the spacecraft behaviour. In this light, this activity aimsalso at leveraging AI-enhanced modelling and simulation tools to detect and assess normal and abnormalconditions, by comparing the expected behaviour ofhigh-fidelity and representative simulations with acquiredmonitoring data.

AI systems, leveragingmachine learning algorithms and data from various sensors, enhance the capability to monitor the health andperformance of spacecraft in real-time, predicting potential failures before they occur and ensuring optimaloperation. However, current AI tools are often separate and specialised, leading to inefficiency. There is aneed for a seamless, unified suite with shared features like explainability, data handling, and consistentinterfaces. This will make AI easier to use and adopt across teams. Many new technologies and approachesare in active development. Especially, use of federated learning and continual learning lead to reducedcomputation demands and enable more powerful AI techniques, suchas prediction remaining useful lifetimeof components. Additionally, whilst traditional AI/ML approaches have been proven valuable solutions to detectanomalies during routine operations, they degrade fail in accuracy, generalization and interpretability whennovel conditions are encountered or manoeuvres are performed. AI-enhanced modelling and simulation toolssuch as Digital Twins, which integrate Operational simulators, which emulate OBC and run OBSW with AImodels to enhance the fidelity of the simulations and are provide credible representativeness of the behaviourof spacecraft under various conditions. This allows for more personalized/tailoredmodelling which will enhancethe accuracy of prognostics and health management capabilities. They can model novel conditions andconsider the effect of manoeuvres and procedures in the spacecraft behaviour. In this light, this activity aimsalso at leveraging AI-enhanced modelling and simulation tools to detect and assess normal and abnormalconditions, by comparing the expected behaviour ofhigh-fidelity and representative simulations with acquiredmonitoring data.

title: WATER-VAPOUR ELECTRIC PROPULSION SYSTEM (HALL EFFECT THRUSTER OR GRIDDED ION ENGINE) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: Develop and test a compact, integrated, low-power, water-vapour Electric Propulsion System for all on-station manoeuvres, including EOL disposal, on LEO micro-smallsats constellations.Description: Water propulsion systems are being developed for various applications. The main advantages of water electric propulsion are safe storability and cost reductions compared to Xenon or Krypton propellants. Water is freely available on Earth and can be found in solid state in various places in the solar system. Using water as a propellant does not require high-pressure storage. Handling is inherently safe. The concept of water propulsion extends beyond immediate applications in LEO satellites and is potentially useful in future exploration missions employing a simple form of In-Situ Resource Utilisation (ISRU). Several types of water Electric Propulsion are commercially available or under development, with the most mature being water-vapor Resistojets. These are simple thrusters but mainly employed on low delta-V missions or as RCS systems due to their limited performance (high thrust but low ISP). Water-fed Microwave Electric Thrusters (METs) and Water Electrolysis Propulsion (WEP) systems are under development but today remain at low maturity. Water electrolysis is also used in conventional chemical thrusters and various developments are ongoing in Europe to mature them including past and ongoing ESA-funded RD activities. This activity targets prototyping and performance verification of a water-vapor Hall Effect Thrusters (HET) or Gridded Ion Engines (GIE) electric propulsion system that incorporates thruster head, fluidics, and electronics. Water-vapor HETs and GIEs do not need an electrolyzer onboard the spacecraft, which signifies less mass, volume, and complexity penalties. The target performance include: - Thrust: up to 10mN - Power: up to 600W - Life: compatible with LEO micro-smallsats constellations. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements Definition - Design Definition and Justification - Breadboard Prototype and Testing including performance characterisation and endurance test.

title: COST-COMPETITIVE SOLAR CELL DEVELOPMENT - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop a cost-competitive solar cell either III-V-based or silicon-based for LEO satellite constellations.Description:The satellite industry is undergoing a major shift from traditional geostationary (GEO) platforms to large-scale lowEarth orbit (LEO) constellations. In this new landscape, solar cell requirements are increasingly driven by the needfor scalability, cost competitiveness, and radiation hardness tailored to the LEO environment. III-V multi-junctionsolar cells remain the benchmark for efficiency and space reliability, but their high cost and manufacturingcomplexity limit their suitability for mass production. In contrast, silicon-based solar cells, widely used in terrestrialsolar arrays, offer a more scalable and cost-efficient option, though they are not optimized for the spaceenvironment and typically have lower radiation resistance. Future development of III-V cells should focus onreducing complexity and cost. For silicon technologies, the priority is improving tolerance to radiation-induceddegradation, which is generally more severe than in III-V cells.Within this activity, it is foreseen to develop one solar cell technology that can support the LEO constellations inview of cost competitiveness and production capability. Technology options for this activity are either III-V-basedor silicon-based, with the following specific objectives: Option 1 - III-V-based technology development, to reduce production costs by up to 50% and doublemanufacturing throughput to meet large-scale deployment needs: there is substantial potential to reduce costsand increase manufacturing throughput by optimizing existing processes or implementing new ones. Potentialstrategies include increasing epitaxial growth rates, integrating terrestrial PV techniques (e.g., screen-printingfor contactmetallization), and replacing photolithography steps with more cost-effective alternatives.For this option, the activity encompasses the following tasks:o Develop an optimized manufacturing route for III-V solar cells, incorporating both improvements tocurrentprocesses and introduction of new techniques.o Fabricate solar cell samples using the newly developed manufacturing process.o Conduct an engineering test campaign to evaluate and validate the electrical and mechanicalperformance of the produced cells.This development stream complements developments performed in the following activity: T703-900EP - HighEfficient Cost-Effective Solar Cells. Option 2 - Silicon-based technology development, with the aim to achieve 21% efficiency at beginning-of-life(BOL) and 18% at end-of-life (EOL) and to improve reliability in the LEO space environment. The developmentactivity will focus on both design innovation and process optimization, aiming to enhance radiation toleranceand thermal cycling robustness while achieving the required beginning-of-life (BOL) and end-of-life (EOL)efficiency targets. For this option, the activity encompasses the following tasks:o Implement cell design optimizations already identified for existing silicon solar cell concepts toimprove radiation resistance to meet the 21% BOL and 18% EOL efficiency targets.o Investigate alternative metallization methods, anti-reflective coatings (ARCs), and interconnectiontechniques to improve thermal cycling robustness.o Explore compatibility of silicon structures with potential self-annealing properties to mitigate radiationinduceddegradation with industrial manufacturing framework.o Validate the final solar cell design through an engineering test campaign.This development stream complements developments performed in the following activity: Spin-indevelopment of terrestrial solar cell technology for constellation applications (ARTES AT 4F.175).

title: NAVISP-EL1-126-APPROXIMATE COMPUTING FOR LOW-POWER GNSS SIGNAL PROCESSING - EXPRO+
description: General DescriptionThis activity explores the application of Approximate Computing (AxC) techniques to GNSS signal processing for reducing power consumption while maintaining acceptable accuracy. It focuses on implementing AxC in acquisition, tracking, and PVT stages of GNSS receivers. The study will identify suitable AxC methods, develop a prototype receiver supporting both exact and approximate modes, and evaluate performance in terms of power efficiency, accuracy, and correlation degradation. Test campaigns will use live and replayed GNSS data from various environments to validate the concept. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity

title: H2.2/2022/005 - S5P-FRM4DOAS CENTRAL PROCESSING
description: MAX-DOAS spectrometers are ground-based remote sensing instruments operating in the UV-visible spectral range and widely used for air quality observations.Through dedicated ESA activities, MAX-DOAS has been incorporated into the Fiducial Reference Measurements (FRM) framework, with the aim of harmonising instrumentation and data processing. This has led to the definition of best practices for instrument operation and the development of a prototype centralised processing system capable of delivering near-real-time data. This system was successfully demonstrated in the FRM4DOAS project.For routine satellite validation, such as for Sentinel-5 Precursor, timely and operational access to high-quality FRM datasets from ground-based MAX-DOAS instruments is essential.Building on the achievements of FRM4DOAS, this activity aims to establish an operational service for the centralised processing of the MAX-DOAS network, ensuring consistent and timely delivery of reference-quality data.

title: QUANTUM-ENABLED PNT DEMONSTRATOR PHASES 0/A/B1
description: This activity aims to prepare a future in-orbit demonstrator of novel Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) concepts based on quantum technologies. The study will investigate the integration of quantum inertial sensors, advanced timing techniques, including optical clocks, and hybrid navigation architectures combining quantum and classical sensors.Emphasis will be placed on system resilience, autonomy and GNSS-independent navigation including applications in Earth orbit and beyond. The activity will include system-level definition, performance assessment and critical pre-developments, including sensor fusion and onboard processing techniques.The objective is to mature concepts and associated key technologies up to TRL 5/6 and deliver a credible mission concept for a future PNT demonstrator.

title: D-BAND TRANSCEIVER MODULE FOR 6G SATELLITE SYSTEMS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5C.542) - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, build, test an integrated D-band transceiver module for high data rate satcom applications.TargetedImprovements: - Enabling D-band satellite links with higher than 10Gbit/sec- Increasing the transmission capacities by a factor of 4.- Smaller footprint and weight than Ka, V-band ISL or even optical ISL.- Less risk for interference as spectrum not completely allocated.- More resilient compared to Optical ISL (e.g. pointing misalignment or thermal effects).Description: The current state of satellite communication technologies, particularly in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations, relies on existing RF and microwave frequencies, which oftenstruggle to meet the growing demand for higher bandwidth and faster data rates. Withthe advent of 5G and the transition towards 6G, current systems face significantchallenges in scaling data throughput and maintaining efficient communication, especially beyond the atmosphere. This challenge is exacerbated by the limitations of traditionalfrequency bands and the complexity of integrating both passive and active elements within semiconductor-based antenna arrays.The introduction of sub-Terahertz frequencies, specifically in the D-Band range of 110 to 170 GHz, can offer a solution to these issues. These higher frequency bands providesignificantly larger bandwidths, allowing for faster data rates, lower power consumption, and smaller,more efficient hardware. However, fully utilizing the D-band spectrumrequires innovative concept to integrate both active components, such as amplifiers and receivers, and passive components, such as filters, with advanced semiconductor-basedantenna arrays.This project will address these challenges by developing two D-Band transceiver module engineering models, using the latest advancements in MMIC (Monolithic MicrowaveIntegrated Circuit) chipset technologies and packaging techniques, enabling future 6G NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) phased-array applications. It will focus on the integrationof both active (e.g. amplifiers, receivers) and passiveelements (e.g. filters) with semiconductor-based antenna arrays. This integration is crucial for power efficiency, reducingpower losses, and ensuring scalable solutions that can be applied across satellite constellations. In addition to addressing integration challenges, the proposed activity willexplore advanced multiplexing techniques, such as Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM), which can significantly increase communication capacity without requiring additionalfrequency bandwidth. This novel approach promises to optimize system performance and unlock greater scalability for satellite communication systems in the 6G era. Theproject will first focus onbreadboarding critical components like the high-power amplifier, receiver, filtering functions and antenna. Subsequently, two engineering modeltransceiver modules with critical functions will be manufactured and tested. A point-to-point link demonstrator will becreated for testing, ensuring that the system meets at leastone specific 6G use case such as Joint Communication and Sensing (JCAS), Multi-orbit Inter-satellite Link (ISL), or Extreme Capacity Backhaul (xHaul).

title: ESA TECHNOLOGY BROKER NETHERLANDS 2026-2028 (RE-ISSUE)
description: The primary objective of this activity is to create added value for European industry by solving their technology needs using spacetechnology and to solve the needs of the European Space industry using terrestrial innovations. This shall include the following main activities: contribute to building an ecosystem fuelling technical innovation and business growth between space and terrestrial industries; generating collaborative, commercial activities between non-space entities and the space industry; develop relationships and interface with space technology developers within the Netherlands; perform an Opportunity Analysis of markets within the Netherlands that have high potential for either using space technology or contributing innovations to the space industry; subsequently engage these non-space industries leading to the creation of Technology Needs and candidate innovations for spin-in; promotion, event organisation, and participation; create a digital presence, promote news stories, and provide content to the ESA Commercialisation Network Website; coordinate collaborate with other members of the ESA Commercialisation Network within the Netherlands as well as with ESA Technology Brokers in other Participating States. In detail the following indicative goals have been defined to be completed over the duration of the contract: support at least 6 Successful Business Support Cases (SBSC). A sufficient pipeline of opportunities to support meeting the above objective shall also be developed with the following as anticipated performance indicators: 60 Introductions brokered between economic operators in the space and non-space industries; 30 Facilitations achieved. Additionally, the bidder is expected to capture 30 Technology Descriptions or Technology Needs and to respond to all Technology Needs posed by other ESA Technology Brokers within the requested time frame.
