title: COMPACT, EXTREME LOW FREQUENCY AND LOW NOISE ELECTRIC FIELD PROBE DEVELOPMENT EXPRO PLUS
description: ObjectivesTo develop a low frequency and low noise, 3 axis electric field probe, enabling direct ongroundverification by test fornext generation in-situ space plasma sensing missions and for missions with EMC sensitive payload integrated inside the spacecraft structure.DescriptionBackground and Context:Missions that are studying space plasma with wave instruments are imposing low frequency and low-level electric field requirements on the spacecraft in order to limit the unwanted radiated emission that could disturbthe instrument performance. In addition, other increasingly challenging and sensitive payloads also require more stringent control ofelectric fields at lower frequencies. Therefore, the on-ground verification of the electric field requirements driven by the payloads has paramount importance i.e. to confirm the presence of unintentional electric field interference originated from the spacecraftthat can jeopardize the instrument performance. Current electric field probes do not cover the needs of compact probing of low frequency and low noise radiated electric fields in which 3 axes and phase information is needed, in particular to characterise emissions close to units or even inside the spacecraft. By improving both the frequency range and thesensitivity, compact electric field probes could be utilised for improved verification and new applications that were not feasible before.Justification:The commercially available electric field probes are not suitable to capture the low frequencies and the low amplitudes, that are required for upcoming missions of Plasma Observatory, M-Matisse and New ATHENA or required by already flying missions like JUICE and Solar Orbiter.Description:The goal of the activity is to develop a triaxial field probe together with its conditioning unit with start frequency of 0.1 Hz or lower and sensitivity of 0.5 mV/m or lower up-to 200 kHz.An additional constraint for the field probe development is the size. The newly developed field probe shall allow to place minimum of 16 identical field probes around the unit under test at a distance closer than 0.25 m without interfering with each other.Moreover, the field probe needs to produce the field data along eachprincipal axes that can be processed with typical laboratory equipment like spectrum analyser, EMI receiver, digital oscilloscope, data acquisition unit, etc.Task list:- Identification of technology concepts and market research for state-of-the-art field probes in terms of frequency range, sensitivity and dynamic range- Evaluation of weak points of the existing field probes and identification of the critical components needed for the required improvements- Bread boarding of 3 axis sensor (e.g. optimize the type, sizeand shape of sensor) together with its conditioning unit (e.g. design a low noise read out chain including low noise amplifier) also considering constraints like size and cost- Validation tests and reportsDeliverables:- Documentation of the research- The bread board of the improved field probe together with its conditioning unit- Test reports and calibration data

title: TRIM FLAP DEVELOPMENT FOR MARTIAN LANDERS - EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop a trim flap system for lift modulated entry at Mars for lander missions.Description: During the entry sequence, the next European Mars lander will need to fly a lifting entry trajectory, meaning that the aerodynamic angle of attack will benon-zero. To achieve this, there have been two techniques employed so far in Mars missions offsetting the centre of gravity (CoG) position radially or utilising a trim flap to offset the centre of pressure (CoP) position of the vehicle. The CoG offset is usually achieved by ballast mass ejection, which for the Mars Entry, Descent and Landing (MEDaL) mission has been estimated to weigh on the order of 115 kg. While the ballast ejection system is simpler than a trim flap, the mass gains with the latter could be significant.The system can offer up to an order of magnitude reduction in the mass penalty to perform the L/D modulation. A European-developed trim flap can draw on the heritage of the control flap of the IXV (Intermediate eXperimental Vehicle) and Space Rider vehicles. Thisactivity aims to perform early design, simulation, analysis and breadboard testing of a trim flap system. It includes the development of trim flap hardware, including the Thermal Protection System (TPS), the flap structure and the deployment mechanism. The deployment and retraction mechanism are de-risked through breadboarding and the aerothermodynamic characteristics of the flap are established. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Mechanical, thermal and electric design of the entire trim flap mechanism. - Derive the AEDB (Aerodynamic Data Base) and the ATDB (Aerothermal Data Base) for the aeroshell and simulate the modulation dynamics. -Design and manufacturing of a breadboard of the flap mechanisms at full scale plus any additional testing at component level or reduced/coupon scale needed to achieve confidence in the mechanism performance. - Perform instrumented ambient deployment tests in a laboratory environment on the breadboard developed to verify function. - Perform plasma wind tunnel testing on the mechanism or a representative subset of the mechanism.Deliverables: Breadboard, Report

title: ARRAY OF RYDBERG SENSORS FOR MULTI-BAND PNT SYSTEM - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To define and assess the application potential of using array of Rydberg receivers for PNT applications.Description: Rydberg sensors are usually baselined on warm-cell vapour. A finer frequency bandwidth can be achieved with Laser cooled atom Rydbergreceiver, which in the domain of multi-layer multi-band PNT could substantially ameliorate an array of receivers. The objective of this activity is to demonstrate the multi-layer multi-band PNT benefit of using an array configuration of Rydberg sensors. The use ofcold atom is seen as a secondary objective, in case the warm-cell vapour will not be sufficient for an array configuration. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirement analysis, including review of cold atom Rydberg performance and definition of use cases. - Trade-off between cold atom and warm vapour cell and selection of use case for Rydberg sensors array - Breadboarding of an array of Rydberg sensors and performance testing - Establishment of a roadmap for the development of an Engineering Model of an array configuration of Rydberg Receivers.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: HIGH EFFICIENCY HPA WITH IMPROVED LINEARITY FOR HIGH FIDELITY RANGING SIGNALS EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: To define and assess the feasibility of a digitally controlled, highly efficient and compact High-Power Amplifiers in L-band / C-band for PNT applications.Description: With the increased demand for navigation services, the number of signal componentstransmitted by a GNSS satellite has increased. Since constant envelope multiplexing schemes are not suitable (or inefficient) with ahigh number of signal components, modern GNSS systems generate signals with high PAPR (Peak to average Power Ratio). DC power efficiency is critical for high power amplifiers (HPA) transmitting signals with high PAPR. In the last decades several HPA architectureshave been investigated to solve this limitation. Among those, the category of polar transmitters such as Envelope Tracking (ET) andEnvelope Elimination and Restoration (EER) stand out for high efficiency and excellent thermal management of the transistors. Conversely, they showed major challenges such as high complexity and difficult implementation with wideband signals. Given the narrowbandnature of Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals, polar transmitters are a good candidate for PNT applications. The challenge of analogue envelope reconstruction can be overcome by a digital modulator, leveraging recent advances in digital technologies. Atthe same time, evolution of PNT services is moving beyond L-band, targeting C-band or other frequency bands with larger bandwidths,where there is no example of dedicated HPAs for navigation. This activity will investigate amplifier design solutions to address high PAPR narrow band, as well as medium PAPR broadband signal configurations. The amplifiers will include digital predistortion, to achieve high-quality PNT signal performance, and compact designs to target advanced payload architectures. The selected designs willbe demonstrated through the development and testing of elegant breadboards (EBB) This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of the operational scenarios and end-to-end user requirements associated. - Literature review, oriented at the latest developments in ET and polar transmitters in general, in analogue and in digital domain, as well as in broadband HPA solutions - Trade-off and down-selection of the most promising technologies based on the survey and preliminary high-level studies - Breadboards detailed design, and analysis and preparation of manufacturing plan and test plan - Breadboards manufacturing and test - Critical analysis of the results obtained and future roadmap.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). Among those, the category of polar transmitters such as Envelope Tracking (ET) andEnvelope Elimination and Restoration (EER) stand out for high efficiency and excellent thermal management of the transistors. Conversely, they showed major challenges such as high complexity and difficult implementation with wideband signals. Given the narrowbandnature of Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) signals, polar transmitters are a good candidate for PNT applications. The challenge of analogue envelope reconstruction can be overcome by a digital modulator, leveraging recent advances in digital technologies. Atthe same time, evolution of PNT services is moving beyond L-band, targeting C-band or other frequency bands with larger bandwidths,where there is no example of dedicated HPAs for navigation. This activity will investigate amplifier design solutions to address high PAPR narrow band, as well as medium PAPR broadband signal configurations. The amplifiers will include digital predistortion, to achieve high-quality PNT signal performance, and compact designs to target advanced payload architectures. The selected designs willbe demonstrated through the development and testing of elegant breadboards (EBB) This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of the operational scenarios and end-to-end user requirements associated. - Literature review, oriented at the latest developments in ET and polar transmitters in general, in analogue and in digital domain, as well as in broadband HPA solutions - Trade-off and down-selection of the most promising technologies based on the survey and preliminary high-level studies - Breadboards detailed design, and analysis and preparation of manufacturing plan and test plan - Breadboards manufacturing and test - Critical analysis of the results obtained and future roadmap.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: INNOVATIVE CERAMIC MANUFACTURING FOR SPACE APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop and optimise additive manufacturing techniques for ceramic components, as well as developing post-processing,improving crack detection and establishing a robust European supply chain.Description:Ceramics play a crucial role in spacecraftfor their unique properties, namely high thermal stability/resistance, low density and high strength. Ceramics like silicon carbide(SiC) and silicon nitride (Si3N4) are employed in structural components, delivering high stiffness with relatively low mass. They are vital for optical applications for a stable and accurate placement of sensors and mirrors. They are also used for thermal protectionsystems, microwave and radio-frequency equipment. Recently, additive manufacturing (AM) has further expanded the applications ofceramics in spacecraft, enabling the production of unprecedented complex shapes. Overall, ceramics are becoming indispensable for modern spacecraft.Nevertheless, ESA recognises the need to enhance several key aspects of the ceramic manufacturing chainto supportindustrialisation and establish a robust supply. Despite the advancements in AM, specific challengespersist, particularly when attempting to achieve thin walls, improving surface finish or enabling more intricatelattice geometries with high reliability and precision. The feasibility of assembling larger structures from smallerceramic parts is a way to overcome AM equipment size and processlimitations. In parallel, there is a need toimprove data for crack analysis and damage tolerance, coupled with the development of viableNon-Destructive Testing (NDT) solutions for crack detection. Downstream operations are critical, including precisionmachining formounting interfaces, coatings and polishing. Additionally, exploration of alternatives to SiC and Si3N4 may yield new opportunities. The use of ceramics poses challenges for spacecraft demisability, which can limit their suitability for satellites in large constellations adhering to the zero-debris charter. This constraint must be considered early in the design phase and accounted for in mission architecture.The aim of this activity is to further develop AM processes for ceramics. It can be expected that this will involve the use of novel materials, achieving higher geometric complexity, improved surface finish, larger part size and/or thinner walls.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Trade-off potential use cases (e.g. parts, AM processes and materials) whichwould allow further developingceramic manufacturing technologies for space applications.- Select the most promising application and develop the corresponding AM processes, progressing towards arepresentative part prototype. This will likely involve complementary steps such as surface treatments, joining, coating, polishing and NDT.- Develop numerical simulation tools to support design formanufacturing, for example by predictingdeformation and crack formation during fabrication or sintering.- Manufacture and test the prototype under relevant conditions.- Define end-of-life strategies.Deliverables: Breadboard, Prototype part, Report

It will also demonstrate key components and functions via small-scale laboratory proof-of-concept setups. title: MODULAR PHOTOVOLTAIC ASSEMBLY TECHNOLOGY FOR STANDARDISED MANUFACTURING EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop modular photovoltaic assembly technologies that can be used in different solar array configurations enabling reduction of the manufacturing costs.Description: The new mega constellation landscape requires an increase in the production capacity of solar arrays which are suitable for this new scenario. For doing so, it is necessary to have a versatile concept of modular Photovoltaic Assembly (PVA) which can be used on both semi or fully automated processes and with the main goal of reducing the cost and increasing the production throughput. The modularity of the PVA is aimed to allow the combination of the developed modules (series/parallel connection) in order to meet the power needs of the specific application and depending on the particular characteristicsof the power architecture. The main benefit of following this modular approach lies on the fact that the same PVA units can be usedfor different mission profiles and also by different solar array suppliers with no capacity to produce their own PVA. This activityencompasses the following tasks: - Definition of a specification of PVA module compatible with a low-cost solar cell - Development of technology building blocks derived from the previously defined specification - Description of manufacturing processes - Breadboarding and preliminary testing of components making up the modular PVA concept

title: ELECTROMAGNETICALLY QUIET SKIES - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a tool for the prediction of satellites' unintended electromagnetic radiation on the ground telescopes and todevelop concepts to minimise the electromagnetic footprint of satellites.Description: The proliferation of an increasing number of satellites is making it harder for astronomers to execute their observations. Satellite unintended electromagnetic emissions generated by operating electronic equipment and as byproduct (spurious or out-of-band radiation) of intentional radio-frequency (RF) transmissions are being measured by astronomical observatories, also with increasingly sensitive detectors. This is potentially interfering with astronomical observations at their protected electromagnetic bands and is being exacerbated by the trends of satellite constellations flying at lower altitudes. The long-term objective is to protect radio astronomy, to preserve dark and quiet skies, whileallowing a sustainable future in space. Contributing to this, the activity seeks for the methods to predict and minimise the growing electromagnetic footprint caused by spacecraft. This activity is structured around two main tasks. The first is to define and create a base computational tool to predict the potential impact of satellites' unintended electromagnetic emissions on telescopes and other RF-sensitive sensors. This tool is aimed to be designed with a sufficiently generic framework to allow seamless integration into existing space debris simulation tools. The second task aims to develop technical measures for reducing the unintended emissions generated by electronic equipment and resulting from RF transmissions. In this component, the activity explores techniques to increase the electromagnetic and radio-frequency compatibility and improve the RF spurious performance, such as advanced shielding, filtering, noise-suppression strategies, adherence to stricter spectral masks, power and frequency control. Performance criteria and measurement techniques are also to be proposed to verify the reduced electromagnetic footprint. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Survey of satellite emission data. - Development and prototyping of software to calculate the impact of satellite unintended emissions on observatories, with testing and benchmark measurements for verification. - Research and trade-off analysis of techniques for reducing unintended electromagnetic emissions. - Conceptual design of feasible and effective mitigation measures, with investigation supporting proof-of-concept and proposed performance criteria Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access to it and can provide update to the community of users.

title: M-IND - INDUSTRIALISATION OF MID-SIZE PLATFORMS FOR LEO CONSTELLATIONS (SAR OPTICAL)
description: Multiple studies on "Industrialisation of mid-size platforms for LEO constellations in Earth Observation". This activity is part of the "vertical axis" of the M-IND (Mid-size satellite INDustrialisation) initiative and it is intended for mid-size satellite integrators in order to support the scaling-up of the production of European mid-size satellite (100-500 kg) for Earth Observation applications with LEO constellations. It complements the "horizontal axis" of M-IND, where separate technology activities, mostly fundedunder GSTP, will support Equipment suppliers to modernise and industrialise Equipment for sub-systems in mid-size satellites.This activity will focus on the definition and establishment of credible industrialisation roadmaps covering production ramp-up of full mid-size satellites for Earth Observation, including supply chain strategies covering interchangeability and interoperability of sub-system from multiple suppliers, modular platform architectures including modernisation of capabilities like for example low latency communication via Intersatellite Links (ISL), suitability for several types of Earth Observation payloads, and sustainability aspectsfor zero debris mitigation at end of mission life and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). The envisaged solutions and roadmaps shall enable cost-efficient, resilient and high-rate manufacturing aligned with future institutional and commercial mission needs in the EarthObservation domain.

This activity is part of the "vertical axis" of the M-IND (Mid-size satellite INDustrialisation) initiative and it is intended for mid-size satellite integrators in order to support the scaling-up of the production of European mid-size satellite (100-500 kg) for Earth Observation applications with LEO constellations. It complements the "horizontal axis" of M-IND, where separate technology activities, mostly fundedunder GSTP, will support Equipment suppliers to modernise and industrialise Equipment for sub-systems in mid-size satellites.This activity will focus on the definition and establishment of credible industrialisation roadmaps covering production ramp-up of full mid-size satellites for Earth Observation, including supply chain strategies covering interchangeability and interoperability of sub-system from multiple suppliers, modular platform architectures including modernisation of capabilities like for example low latency communication via Intersatellite Links (ISL), suitability for several types of Earth Observation payloads, and sustainability aspectsfor zero debris mitigation at end of mission life and Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). The envisaged solutions and roadmaps shall enable cost-efficient, resilient and high-rate manufacturing aligned with future institutional and commercial mission needs in the EarthObservation domain.

title: IRIDE SERVICE SEGMENT
description: Scope of IRIDE Service Segment is to implement an operational service portfolio providing geospatial products and to set up the digital tools and the operational scenarios for the provision of the services to IRIDE Users (with a focus on Institutional sector), byalso taking care of designing and developing suitable exploitation solutions and interfaces with User Operational Systems for the use of IRIDE Services outputs. Main Service Thematic Domains to be addressed by the Service Segment have been identified by previous work carried out within National User Forum and related working groups at Institutional level. They are: Coastal and Marine Monitoring; Air Quality; Ground Motion; Land Cover\Land Use; Hydro\Meteo\Climate; Water Management; Emergency Response; Security. These Service Thematic Domains will drive the design, implementation and delivery of dedicated Service Segment elements, named Service Value Chains, relying on a common infrastructure, the IRIDE Marketplace, where enabling blocks of the SVCs will be provided, such as data catalogues, marketplace for accessing the services, etc. Although the provided services will be based on satellite data processing, they will also identify and integrate other data sources necessary for the compliance with the information need of the User. IRIDE Service Value Chains will be designed with user driven approach and therefore IRIDE data will be used in a wider input data set. Impact assessment activities will be also designed and carried on, in order to evaluate the utility, benefits and impact of provided services. Moreover, activities related to liaison with on-going relevant initiatives primarily in Italy and in Europe will be included, for non-duplication and for building IRIDE in a wider context. Last but not least, fundamental activity for the success of IRIDE Service Segment, will be devoted to User uptake of the services and to the analysis of sustainable operational scenarios, to be implemented after the end of the Programme. The work will be organised according to three cycles of similar activities, one year each. The precursor cycle will design, develop and deliver Services that are based on existing data sets. The following ones will integrate IRIDE data, enabling new services, new processors and an enlargement of the User Community.

title: ON-BOARD 5G SPACE USER EQUIPMENT FOR LEO SATELLITES (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5A.092) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop, and demonstrate an on-board 5G space User Equipment (UE) for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites.Targeted Improvements:Provide a standardised method - leveraging 5G NTN developments - for broadband connectivity via data relay to LEO satellites.Description: The future 5G New Radio Non-Terrestrial Networks (5G NR NTN) will offer continuous and ubiquitous coverage targeting terrestrial user equipment.Through the New Space paradigm, a new group of users emerges in the form of LEO satellites such as CubeSats.The future 5G NTN networks (LEO/MEO/GEO) can be leveraged to provide standardised broadband connectivity services also to these space users for LEO. The gNodeBcan be either on the ground or in space. The activitywill- design and develop an on-board 5G space user equipment (UE) breadboard featuring the capabilities standardised in NTN.- identify a suitable mission for CubeSat with the developed breadboard embedded.- test and evaluate the connectivity performance level of the developed technology using a leased 5G NR NTN link.- implement and collect time-of-arrival measurements from NTN downlink signals used for communication.

title: IMPLEMENTATION AND ENGINEERING MODEL TESTING OF IP BLOCKS FOR IMAGE SENSOR OUTPUTS FASTER THAN 1 GBIT/S
description: Objectives:To have a fully European IP block to be used by European Image Sensor designers heavily dependent onnon-European sources. The objective of this activity is to design and validate high throughput serial outputsfor image sensors for dual use applications.Description:The future of infrared and visible sensors (larger formats, smaller pixels, fast frame rates) is tightly linkedtothe ability to read them out fast, but European detector manufacturers have not yet developed thecapability to adopt newer and faster communication protocols.In applications like Earth Observation, there is trend in image sensors towards more pixels and faster framerates, with analogue to digital conversion performed on chip. Transfer of information from the detector diecan become challenging using parallelized transfer standards, either limiting the frame rate or increasingthe complexity of the electrical interface.JESD204 interface standard is an ideal solution, offering a higherspeedserial interface with reduced pin-counts compared to the options currently used.In this activity, a JESD204-enabling circuitry for the Read-Out Integrated Circuits (ROICs) of image sensorsshall be implemented in the selected technology node and verified to be used in future detector designs.The IP blocks shall be radiation hard and compatible with a European foundry. The design shall bedemonstrated and verified, with the IP blocks becoming available for the European detector designcommunity.Parallel developments targeting most relevant technologies for infrared CMOS ROICs manufactured inEurope shall be implemented. It is anticipated that this leap-forward in interface speed and simplicity shallbe adopted by all European detector manufacturers using the relevant technology nodes and so shallbecome the dominant output interface in European space missions using digital output infrared sensors.This activity shall encompass the following tasks:- Study the latest JESD204 standard and future needs of the detector market in line with the developmentschedule of this activity- Derivation of requirements, IP Blocks architecture and identification of configurable parameters- Design of the IP blocks including test circuitry- Manufacture engineering model devices- Design and manufacture of the EGSE to assess the devices- Electrical and radiation test andcharacterization of the devices- Debugging and realization of the prototype- Support detector companies to implement and interface with the IP block.

title: INTEGRATED CONTROL OF MULTI-ACTUATED LAUNCHER STAGES - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To design and implement control methodologies for multi-actuated launcher stages, targeting applications that can only be achieved by controlling multiple actuators in an integrated fashion.Description: Current launcher GNC design processes rely on anarchitectural simplification under which engine throttling and thrust vector control (TVC) are managed independently. With the new generation of reusable launchers, new GNC challenges are arising, rendering the aforementioned separation impractical if not unfeasible. These challenges are related to much tighter dynamical attitude/trajectory couplings (especially during re-entry, descent and landing) and to interactions between actuators including aerodynamic surfaces and thrusters (required for control during ballistic and exo-atmospheric phases). Linked to the development of reusable launchers, clustered engine configurations are frequently used because very advantageous in terms of versatility and reliability, but only when all the actuators and their interactions are jointly addressed in the GNC design. In the scope of the activity is therefore to investigate the improvements that can be achieved by the newgeneration of multi-actuated vehicles including clustered, gimballed engines, grid or planar fins and thrusters. This investigationshall cover topics from control design and allocation up to architectural design and adaptive configuration management. A special focus shall be placed on applications that can only be enabled via an integrated system-level multi-actuated approach. Examples of these applications are the following: - Aerodynamic load relief during launch using uniform and differential throttling, TVC and fin deflections; - Precise retro-propulsive landing; - Optimal allocation of thrusters, differential throttling, TVC and fin deflections;- Exo-atmospheric maneuvers, such as stage flip-over and detumbling. This activity will entail the following tasks: - Define requirements and scenarios that are illustrative of multi-actuator launcher GNC, including the applications above as a minimum; - Investigate what types of models, design techniques and algorithms are more suitable for this problem; - Perform a preliminary prototyping of different candidate control architectures and functions, following the traditional and integrated approach; - Execute a trade-off analysis between the various architectures and functions; - Design, implement and verify the control algorithms based on the trade-off analysis, including on a representative processor; - Establish way forward for the deployment of the developed methodologies, including required sensing capabilities.

title: LUNAR NIGHT PCDU - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop and implement a "hibernation mode" function for PCDUs reducing the current sunk from the battery and implement a "low power consumption mode".Description: Power control and distribution unit (PCDU) is always connected to a battery and energy sources (e.g. solar panel) in order to keep the power bus available at all conditions. Because of this, there is always a non-negligible PCDU internal consumption from the batteries. However, there are some very specific cases where the power should be reduced to a minimum in a controlled manner (e.g. to survive long lunar nights with a limited energy stored on the batteries). This activityaims to develop a PCDU hibernation mode, so that the PCDU can enter into an extremely low consumption mode (e.g. below 7.5mA) in a reliable manner and can come back to nominal operations after a command is sent or via a watchdog signal. In addition to the hibernation mode, this activity develops a "low power consumption control" mode, where the loads to be supplied during low energy consumption mode are to be identified and supplied according to the needs and the energy available (e.g. heaters for lunar night survival). Implementation of hibernation mode for PCDUs is targeted to include the aspects such as i.e. wake-up mechanism, watchdogs, low stand-by consumption technologies. Meanwhile, "low power consumption mode" entails the development of control algorithms and low consumption hardware to provide power to dedicated loads according to the energy available. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Consolidation of the preliminary requirements of the low power consumption and hibernation modes taking into account future exploration missions needs. - Trade-off potential designs (best topologies, control logic, switching devices...) and select a baseline. - Design of the baseline, including the design analysis - Prototype manufacturing - Testing of the prototype - Analyze test results, identify deviations and implement corrections if any on the prototype.Deliverables: Breadboard, ReportProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: T811-900GS OPTIMIZATION OF LASER INTENSITY ON SPACE DEBRIS VIA COHERENT BEAM COMBINATION (EXPRO+)
description: Recently, strategies have been explored to perturb space debris orbits using high-power ground-based lasersystems. This method, known as laser momentum transfer, can also be used for deep-space opticalcommunications. Multi-beam architectures have been designed and implemented to obtain the required powerlevels that would be unachievable with a single laser source or that would be limited by atmospheric turbulenceeffects. In a recent study on laser momentum transfer, 40 kW-class lasers based on multiple beams have beenproposed to alter the orbits of space debris and prevent collisions with active satellites.One challenge is delivering the generated power to the selected target while minimizing losses caused by laserpropagation and ensuring efficient momentum transfer for collision avoidance manoeuvres. Adaptive opticssystems have been considered but there are still several challenges due to the limited maturity of thistechnology. For example, retrieving tip-tilt information to compensate for atmospheric turbulence still dependson sunlight reflected from debris, which is a limiting factor in operational terms. Additionally, today's deformablemirror technology is not mature enough for the power levels needed for this application. While research is stillongoing, Coherent Beam Combining (CBC) techniques could offer a valid alternative to mitigate atmosphericeffects. Description: Recently, strategies have been explored to perturb space debris orbits using high-power ground-based lasersystems. This method, known as laser momentum transfer, can also be used for deep-space opticalcommunications. Multi-beam architectures have been designed and implemented to obtain the required powerlevels that would be unachievable with a single laser source or that would be limited by atmospheric turbulenceeffects. In a recent study on laser momentum transfer, 40 kW-class lasers based on multiple beams have beenproposed to alter the orbits of space debris and prevent collisions with active satellites.One challenge is delivering the generated power to the selected target while minimizing losses caused by laserpropagation and ensuring efficient momentum transfer for collision avoidance manoeuvres. Adaptive opticssystems have been considered but there are still several challenges due to the limited maturity of thistechnology. For example, retrieving tip-tilt information to compensate for atmospheric turbulence still dependson sunlight reflected from debris, which is a limiting factor in operational terms. Additionally, today's deformablemirror technology is not mature enough for the power levels needed for this application. While research is stillongoing, Coherent Beam Combining (CBC) techniques could offer a valid alternative to mitigate atmosphericeffects. This approach has the potential to correct the negative impact of atmospheric turbulence in systemsinvolving multiple beams.This activity aims at investigating CBC techniques to concentrate the highest possible intensity on the target,dynamically adjusting the phase of each beam, and achieving an optimal relationship between the phases ofthe multiple beams.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators. title: ESCA - SPANISH COMPONENT OF THE ATLANTIC CONSTELLATION
description: The purpose of this procurement, carried out in open competition, is the development (up and until final acceptance) of the SpanishComponent of the Atlantic Constellation composed by: a ready to be flown and qualified for operation' Flight Segment, composed by small earth observation satellites with a minimum set of 4 payloads ( i.e. multispectral optical payload, GNSS/R, AIS/VDES and IoT, with the possibility for the tenderers to propose additional payloads as an option to improve the future exploitation of the constellation) and Ground Segment (FOS, PDGS and Marketplace plus all the required ancillaries). Launch and operations of the constellation are explicitly excluded from the scope and objectives of this procurement, while compatibility with several European launchers, accommodation and orbit injection analysis as well as operations preparations up to Final Acceptance Review shall be considered for the proposal preparation. Subject to good quality of received proposal(s), a contract might be placed with a Spanish Prime Contractor.Therefore, the present ITT is addressed to Spanish economic operators having their registered office in Spain and acting as Prime Contractors. ESA shall consider for evaluation only proposals from Spanish entities at Prime Contractor level. In addition, specific industrial policy measures will be implemented to maximise the involvement of Spanish economic operators. The resulting Contract will encompass two (2) contractual Phases as follows: Phase 1 devoted to development and delivery of the first satellite and the associated Ground Segment up to their Final Acceptance Review and Phase 2 devoted to development and delivery of the additional recurring satellites and the associated delta Ground Segment activities up to Final Acceptance Review of the entire constellation. The Agency will reserve the right not to proceed with Phase 2. The procurement will be carried out on the basis of ESA's regulations [in particular, the ESA Procurement Regulations (ESA/REG/001, rev. 5) and the General Clauses and Conditions for ESA Contracts (ESA/REG/002, rev. 3)].

title: FLAPPING WING TECHNOLOGY FOR MARS - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop a flapping wing technology that is able to perform autonomously in-situ measurements near the Mars surface.DescriptionThe aim of this activity is to design and test a concept insect based flapping technologies performing in situ measurements near Mars surface atmosphere and related geology, optimized for Mars atmospheric flight. In this activity, insect-based light weight such as a bumblebee and hummingbird-sized concepts, with a wingspan up to 30 cm are designed, prototyped and tested in a relevant environment. When compared to conventional helicopter or fixed wing concepts, flapping wing on Mars could demonstrate superior performance in terms of energy efficiency, maneuverability, structural robustness and adaptability to external disturbances.The objective is to focus on the propulsive technologies and assess the flight range and payload capability.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Analysis of the requirements and identification of the needs in terms expected performance- Preliminary assessment of the thermal, structural and aerodynamic design quantifying and characterizing the critical elements- Design of a breadboard model in a relevant ground-based facility- Prototyping and aerodynamic testing taking into account suitable scaling parameters- Evaluation of test results and creation of a development roadmap for technology maturation. Develop design guidelines for future applications

title: ERS-EO SPACE RESILIENCE NODES USER NEEDS STUDIES EXPRO+
description: As part of the European Resilience from Space - Earth Observation (ERS-EO) Programme Element 2, this tender covers the studies on User Needs for Space Resilience Nodes (SRN), up to 300k each with duration of approximately 5 months per Study. These Studies area first step towards establishing new SRNs within Participating States, leveraging on ESA's emerging SRN Reference Framework. SpaceResilience Nodes are defined as an unclassified user segment comprising digital, physical, and human components, which together enable rapid access to a suite of space-enabled solutions for Public Protection and Disaster Relief. The Studies aim to understand the needs of Public Protection and Disaster Relief stakeholders in Participating States, so as to tailor the SRN Reference Framework to the national context, and pave the way towards SRN deployment therein. The Agency intends to select up to six (6) distinct studies, to be implemented through separate contracts placed by ESA, each covering a different country/region. The following list of countries/region to be covered by the studies is indicative, the final list will be confirmed in the published tender: 1. Arctic region SRN; 2. Austrian SRN; 3. Belgian SRN; 4. Danish SRN5; 5. Hungarian SRN; 6. Luxembourgish SRN (which will include a focus on the international humanitarian sector). The key tasks and outputs of the studies are expected to include:(1) Identify and understand key Node stakeholders (Mapping of Stakeholders, coordination structures, crisis plans, relevant policies and legal frameworks; identify which stakeholders are to be Node users)(2) Facilitate understanding by key Node stakeholders of SRN concept and Reference Framework, and how it can support them (engagement and outreach; mapping of stakeholders expectations' from and potential roles in the SRN)(3) Define Node high-level mission requirements and architecture based on ESA SRN Reference Framework (identifying priority use cases; analyse baseline capabilities; identify legacy systems and national initiatives or assets to be integrated with/leveraged by the Node; assess pooling and sharing needs; identify security and resilience requirements)(4) Recommend an organisational model and Node deployment timeline(5) Provide input to SRN User Needs Harmonisation Study

description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design and demonstrate the beaconless inter-satellite pointing and acquisition of Laser Communication Terminals (LCT) at deep-space distances. title: ETHERNET CONNECTIVITY FOR MID-SIZE SATELLITES EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To evaluate options standardisation around Ethernet, including connectors and software protocols - and to identify enablers for utilisation of Ethernet in mid-size satellites.Description: Mid- and small-size satellite providers increasingly rely on COTS technologies to meet stringent market cost requirements. The use of COTS FPGAs has enabled space-specific command, control, and data interfaces, while COTS processors are increasingly adopted in data handling equipment. These processors typically provide terrestrial electrical interfaces such as Ethernet. Interest in Ethernet for on-board data handling is growing, driven by the availability of new devices and the ability of later Ethernet versions to support very high data rates (up to 100 Gbit/s). Ethernet up to 100 Mbps has already been used successfully in ESA programmes, including human spaceflight, and several initiatives have explored its usein critical applications. However, Ethernet adoption in space raises new challenges: -No standardised or widely accepted flight connector exists for Ethernet (1GbE, 10GbE and above). -Ethernet introduces additional layers in the protocol stack (e.g., UDP/TCP at the transport layer and IP at the network layer). Further work is needed to determine how best to implement and optimise application-layer protocols on top of these. -Many data handling system elements (e.g., payload front-ends) rely on FPGAs, and integrating Ethernet IPs requires additional considerations. This activity addresses the technology gap for end-to-end interoperable 1GbE and higher Ethernet in mid-size satellites and identify elements for standardisation to enhance equipment reusability and strengthen European competitiveness. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Assess Ethernet flight connector options for 1GbE, 10GbE, and higher rates, considering ESA mission heritage and available connectors. - Assess suitable software application protocols for use with Ethernet and standard stacks, ensuring implementation feasibility in FPGAs, qualified RTOS, and Linux. -Study the availability of EEE components implementing Ethernet building blocks (processors, transceivers, switches, etc.) and derive a roadmap for adoption. -Manufacture, test, and validate Ethernet implementations across different microelectronics options (e.g., processors, FPGAs), identifying performance, integration, and qualification considerations. - Deliver a breadboard setup implementing selected flight connector candidates, software protocols, and EEE/microelectronics components identified above Software shall be delivered under an ESA SoftwareCommunity Licence, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access it and can provide update to the community of users.Deliverables: Breadboard, Report

title: SUSTAINABLE AND ADAPTIVE AGRICULTURE SOLUTIONS - EXPRO+
description: The Sustainable and Adaptive Agriculture Solutions activity comprises four coordinated projects advancing Earth Observation (EO) enabled methods to address emerging agricultural challenges. (1) Crop Yield Estimation and Forecasting at Parcel Level will develop EO and AI enhanced approaches for yield forecasting and anomaly detection (24 months). (2) Next Generation Thermal Products for Crop Health and Water Use Monitoring will deliver harmonized thermal infrared products generating actionable information for agriculturalproduction (48 months). (3) WorldCultivate will establish a policy ready EO capability providing indicators that link crop performance and land suitability to support land use planning and food sovereignty (36 months). (4) WorldIrrigation will develop a global EOsolution for monitoring irrigation occurrence, water consumption, productivity, and withdrawal (36 months).

title: ADHA SOFTWARE ARCHITECTURE - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a complete Software product portfolio of building blocks facilitating the integration of ADHA platforms in Mid-size LEO satellite platforms.Description: The Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA) has been developed as a set of hardware components with standardized communication interfaces. Previous work has focused on the hardware aspects, but the current situation highlights the need for a robust software stack to support ADHA in space missions, in particular mid-sized LEO satellites. The main concern is to ensure that enough software components are ready for use in flight and developed using modern, modular techniques to enhance compatibility and performance. This activity aims to provide a modular software stack that can be utilized across different ADHA-based computers, including On-Board Computers (OBCs) and Instrument Control Units (ICUs) from various vendors. By leveraging different European processors, FPGA, and other COTS processors commonly used in commercial satellites, the software stack is aimed at offering flexibility and interoperability. The added value includes improved mission reliability, reduced development time, and cost savings through standardized software components. The configuration and deployment of the software will be integrated into a model-based software development and code generation tools such as TASTE using Space Creator, facilitating streamlined development and deployment processes. Future activities may involve further refinement of the software stack, extending compatibility to additional processors, and continuous improvement based on user feedback and mission requirements. This activity encompasses the following tasks: -Assessing the feasibility of a modular software stack for different ADHA-based computers. - Developing the software stack to support multiple European processors. - Integrating the software stack into a software MBSE toolset (e.g. TASTE). - Testing and validatingthe software stack across different hardware configurations. - Documenting the development process and results. Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence, allowing access and updates by individuals or entities within ESA Member States.

title: NON-BODY SOLID WASTE COMPACTION AND INHIBITION
description: Objective: To develop a breadboard demonstrating single-step waste inhibition and compaction and characterize cross-linked biodegradable materials compatible for this process.Description: Re-supply and waste management are critical components of crewed space exploration. The current waste management approach exposes the crew to (bio)safety risks during the temporary storage period and is unpractical in longer space missions. Generic waste compaction/inhibition technologies of mixed waste materials in space have been generally studied. However, despite promising results on the volume reduction performance, the physical characteristics of the product obtained allow for limited transformation of re-usable resources. To address this, the activity aims to develop a breadboard demonstrating single-step waste inhibition and compaction and characterize cross-linked biodegradable materials compatible for this process. Lastly, there is a benefit in defining new packaging materials, which are biodegradable in the conditions of identified recycling systems and withstand the proposed compaction and inhibition process. The activity includes the following tasks: - Review single-step waste inhibition/compaction methods compatible with resource recovery (e.g. water) and developed biodegradable materials - Trade-off and selection of integrated waste inhibition and compaction processes and compliant packaging/padding materials. - Design and assembly of a breadboard system for single-step waste inhibition and compaction - Test to validate selected single-step waste inhibition and compaction technological modifications and biodegradability of treated packaging material - Developed cross-linking agents to enhance the barrier properties of biodegradable packaging materials, while maintaining biodegradability and process compatibility - Test to validate biodegradability and intended use of developed packaging. - Define a roadmap for technology maturation for integration into an operational system.Deliverables: Breadboard, Report

title: S3-SW-14 SPACE WEATHER CENTRE FOR SPAIN INITIAL ESTABLISHMENT AND CORE CAPABILITY DEVELOPMENTS: PART 1
description: Space Weather Centre for Spain Initial Establishment and Core Capability Developments: Part 1This activity will constitute the initial establishment and operation of a Space Weather Centre for affected stakeholders along with underpinning tools, capabilities and procedures required in order to deliver tailored high quality services to end users. Key user groups are expected to include operators of energy transmission systems, satellite operators, the aviation sector, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) and others. The Centre shall operate in close cooperation with ESA's Space weather Service Network with the aim to establish a node that facilitates collaborative actions with network participants while moving progressively towards a structure with a clear operational dimension ableto support the development and delivery of tailored space weather capabilities and services. Particularly the centre will focus on translating complex space weather information from multiple sources into streamlined, actionable information. A colocation of the development and operations teams shall be foreseen with the aim to streamline the R2O process, support team building and to encouragedirect feedback to research, optimising the use of facilities in ESAC.Part 1 shall include: Systematic mapping of end users and establishment of key contact points with users and stakeholders Establishment of a proactive engagement strategy and actions with the identified end users to ensure full understanding of end user needs and operational requirements Development of necessary IT infrastructure, tools and service operation procedures in order to operate the space weather front desk, initially on an 8/5 basis, with on-call support during periods of elevated space weather activity. OoProcedures shall be developed with a view to transitioning into full 24/7 support at the start of a future Part 2 of this activity. Operation of the space weather front desk from KO+3 months for at least 6 months prior to the start of Part 2 handover Development of a space weather dashboard capabilities targeting end users and building on well demonstrated and tested space weather assets, constituting a layer for translating complex technical concepts into an easy-to-use tool for end users. Training for end users including exercises and simulations based on realistic use casesDevelopment of a roadmap for the operational Centre including priority R2O needs and the inclusion of a space weather testbed facility to be used for regional event simulations and training, bringing together stakeholders including end users, operators and domain experts with a focus on optimising the R2O2R pipeline. Support for data and product provision from existing assetsas part of the service provision shall be foreseen where it does not duplicate activities already funded via the Space Safety Programme's pre operational space weather service activities. Operationalisation of certain key models and tools along with their re-deployment within the Centre may be foreseen subject to the necessary licensing agreements with the asset owner. A handover to Part 2of the activity shall be foreseen.

title: USER MANAGEMENT SERVICE (UM-SER)
description: The User Management Service contract will encompass a comprehensive suite of offeringsdesigned to support and enhance user interactions and experience for ESA and Third PartyEO Missions.This service contract aims at integrating the User Communication and Information Portaltogether with the User Management functions, covered in the past by separate contracts,whereby ensuring autonomy to Industry in designing and using communication tools asadditional instrument to reach and stimulate a dynamic and variegated user community.The Information Portal is expected to provide seamless access to relevant content and data,Graphical and Editorial Servicesshall deliver visually engaging and professionally curatedmaterials, and finally User Experience Benchmarking Services enable performancecomparisons and insights. A dedicated User Help Desk completes the suite assisting userswith inquiries and technical support, ensuring prompt and effective resolution of issues.User Management Services will implement personalized access to tools, resources, andaccount features through the management of authorisation and authentication services withprovision of a secured User Area. The User Management service will foster a user-centricapproach that prioritizes accessibility, support, and continuous improvement driven by userfeedback.The User Management Service contract shall include the following services: Operations, maintenance and evolutions of the web services for data discoveryaccess and retrieval of Earth Observation products and information (composed byEarth Online, eoPortal, Swarm Data Handbook, EarthCARE Data Handbook, 3DVisuals and Quality Reports Advanced Search platforms). Content Management and Creation, including editorial and graphical services. Operations, maintenance and evolutions of an identity access management infrastructure with federated identity access configurations. Support to user community via a unique and integrated user help desk which serves as the single point of contact for answering to user enquiries and complaints, facilitating data access requests, monitoring and ensuring user satisfaction, and providing communications about system unavailability. The user help desk function will also provide AI powered chatbots and virtual support assistants being powered by a comprehensive and well-maintained and updated knowledgebase. Management of data access requests, assign authorisation to users for accessing restrained data, in agreement to applicable terms and condition (including quota management). Management of a large set of user profiles, including asecure and personalised self managementarea to access and manage account information, access settings and transaction history tracking support requests. By centralizing these functions, the userarea enhances convenience, engagement, and control, allowing users to efficiently interact with the system and AI powered virtual assistant while ensuring their dataand preferences are protected. User experience benchmarking services for systematic analysing and monitoring of user and stakeholder feedback (surveys and behaviour analytics) and monitor performance to help identifying strengths, weaknesses, and areas for improvement

title: PHASE 0/A SYSTEM STUDIES OF THE WIVERN MISSION
description: Wivern - short for wind velocity radar nephoscope - is the only mission in the world that would measure wind in clouds, and deliverprofiles of rain, snow and ice water. Carrying a dual-polarisation, conically scanning 94 GHz Doppler radar, the mission would benefit the prediction of high-impact weather and hazard warnings for weather forecast models and contribute to the climate record of cloud and precipitation profiling. The procurement in subject includes the Phase 0 system studies and Phase A system studies which will be performed through a phased contract. Subject to reception of good quality proposals, it is intended to place two parallel contracts. Phase 0: the Phase 0 system study will cover all elements of the mission architecture: space segment (platforms and instruments), ground segments, operations and exploitation concepts. These studies will be based on the Agency's Statement of Work (SoW) and the Mission Assumptions and preliminary Technical Requirements (MATER). Risk retirement activities will also be identified and initiated within the frame of the study, to raise TRL of critical technologies. The expected duration of the Phase 0 system studies is 14 months from kick-off to final approval of all deliverables. The results of the Phase 0 will be used as input for the down selection of two EE-11 missions out of four to progress to phase A. If the mission is selected the second phase of the contract will be initiated, otherwise the contract will be terminated. Phase A: The Phase A system study will address all elements of the mission architecture, namely space segment (platform and payload), ground segment, mission operations and exploitation. The Phase A system study will be based on the Statement of Work (SoW) applicable from the beginning of the contract and the System Requirements Document (SRD) established by ESA and consolidated at the end of the phase 0. Relevant technology pre-developments will be initiated within the frame of the study, to raise TRL of critical technologies, with the aim to reach TRL 4 by the end of phase A, and with a final goal to reach TRL 5 by the end of phase B1. The expected duration of the Phase A system studies is 14 months from kick-off to final approval of all deliverables. The results of the Phase A will be used as input for the down selection of one EE-11 mission out of the remaining two to progress to phase B1. It is expected that Phase B1 will be placed as a rider to the Phase 0/A contract of the EE-11 mission selected for implementation.

title: COPERNICUS SPACE COMPONENT - COPERNICUS MISSION PLANNING SERVICE
description: The objective of this activity is to ensure the continuation of the current Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 Mission Planning (MP) operations and maintenance for 31 months, up to mid-2029. The new Copernicus Mission Planning Service will cover the following activities: Sentinel-1 Mission Planning Function maintenance, Sentinel-2 Mission Planning Function maintenance, Station Resources Allocation (SRA) maintenance and operations, routine Mission Planning operations (including Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellites observation and downlink planning, planning of operational acquisition resources including X-Band services, planning of Sentinel-1 Collaborative Stations, operations of interfaces with Flight Operations Segment), emergency planning operations including those in support to the Copernicus Emergency Service and to the International Charter Space and Major Disasters-Set-up, and maintenance and operations of an interface point (MPIP) providing access to MP-related information to authorized entities (e.g., S-3/S-5P/CO2M MP services, FOS, acquisition services, etc.). An optional extension will be included to gradually integrate the Mission Planning operations for the Copernicus Expansion Missions (CRISTAL, ROSE-L, LSTM, CIMR, and CHIME) in line with their respective launch dates. This activity is funded under EU Copernicus Programme and will be open exclusively to economic operators and organisations (including subcontractors) established in a European Union Member State or a State participating in the Copernicus Component of the European Union Space Programme. The Invitation to Tender (ITT) package (Cover Letter, Special Conditions of Tender, Draft Contract, Letter of Invitation, and requirements documentation including the Statement of Work) will be available on ESA Star Publication website (https://esastar-publication.sso.esa.int/), the ESA tendering website. Any Tenderer which is not yet registered with ESA as a potential supplier must complete theonline questionnaire in esa-star: https://esastar-emr.sso.esa.int/. Further information on the registration process can be found onthe Doing Business with ESA portal: https://doing-business.sso.esa.int/. Please, note that esa-star allows two levels of entity registration: "Light" and "Valid Full". This allows new users wishing to do business with ESA to carry out their registration in two steps. While "Light" registration will grant access to all esa-star services up to and including proposal submission, the award of ESAcontracts requires "Valid Full" status. The issue of the Invitation to Tender is foreseen in Q2 2026. ESA intends to place one (1) contract as a result of this procurement.

title: ADHA MASS-MEMORY MODULES AND UNIT INTEGRATION EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective:To develop a complete ADHA solid-state mass-memory with compatible modules, usable either standalone orwith other ADHA-compatible hardware in ADHA units for Earth observation, exploration, science, andnavigation missions.Description:The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) is a collaboration between ESA, European satellite primesand data handling equipment suppliers. It includes the definition of an architecture for data handling unitsbased on standard module functions. A standard module procurementflow has been defined, as well as astandardized backplane connector and electrical interfaces. This allows independent developmentofinteroperable modules that can be connected in ADHA units.This activity aims to develop ADHA solid-state mass-memory (MM) modules, based on ADHA-compatiblehardware modules. The development will follow the standard requirements for the development of ADHAmodules.The mass-memory module design will be fully compliant to the ADHA generic specification for mass-memorymodules. The developmentwill include the development of the mass-memory software (including support forfile-based operations, and CFDP Class-1 and Class-2). The developed ADHA mass memory module willsupport high-speed data reception and transfers, featuring a scalable architecture to meet the demands offuture ESA missions in earth observation, science, exploration, and navigation, as well as commercialmissions. Utilizing state-of-the-art processing, memory storage and interconnect technologies, this new massmemoryshall offer superior integration, data storage volume and processing performance compared toprevious generations. These advancements will also enable the implementation of sophisticated functionssuch as artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms for on-board data processing.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Detailed module requirements analysis, based on the existing ADHA specification documents, including theADHA generic mass-memory module specification.- ADHA mass memory module architectural design and trade-off of key components.- Engineering model (EM) design, including electrical, mechanical, thermal, FPGA design and software.- Engineering model (EM) manufacturing and EGSE procurement.- Engineering model (EM) validation campaign, including integration in anADHA unit rack.- Data-handling and storage demonstration, including performance benchmarks.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: ACTIVE ANTENNA FOR DIRECT SATELLITE-TO-DEVICE 5G/6G COMMUNICATIONS IN FREQUENCY RANGE 1 (FR 1) (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5B.253) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of this activity is to design, develop and test a demonstrator of a Tx and Rx active antenna based on tiles for direct satellite-to-device 5G/6G communications in FR1.Targeted Improvements:Increase the antenna apertures up to 400% with respect tothe platform size while being highly storable and assessing simplification of the beamforming implementation.Description: The direct connectivity between satellites and standard mobile terrestrial user equipment such as smartphones, represents an essential feature of future non-terrestrial networks.Due to the RF characteristics of handheld devices, high antenna gains, and therefore large antenna apertures, are required on board the satellite. However, increasing the size of the array often leads to high complexity dueto the increasing number of phase shifters and/or digital signal processing units.This activity will develop and test a demonstratorof a Tx and Rx active antenna based on tiles for direct satellite-to-device 5G/6G communications in the FR1 L/S-band frequency band. A narrowband beamforming concept will be developed that allows to increase the size of the array while minimising its complexitybydividing the array into subarrays of groups of elements. The array is thus divided into multiple tiles that are deployed in orbit thanks to the same dedicated mechanism. This method reduces the number of weights to steer the beam at group level, thereby minimising complexity. Additionally, this has the advantage to split the beam forming network into two levels: subarray and array level, which simplifies the implementation compared to the fully analogue or digital beamforming approaches. Recent advances in the areas oflightweight material and RF/digital IC in ESA Member States would also naturally support the concept.The activity will design, manufacture, and validate in a laboratory environment a phased array active antenna full -scale engineering model (approximately 4m diameter) based on tiles with a fixed size, operating in L-/S-Band (FR 1). The activity shall seek synergies with the ARTES deliverables aswell as with ongoing direct satellite-to-device antenna projects within ESA Member States that are already being built-up. The activity will be implemented with a phased approach. In Phase 1, the bidder shall demonstrate the technology's feasibility through analysis and testing on a two-tiles scaled-down breadboard (TRL 4). In Phase 2, a reduced scale engineering model (TRL 5), based on afour-tile subarray with a deployable mechanism, shall be manufactured and tested. In Phase 3, a full-scale engineering model (TRL 6), including the full deployable mechanism and the thermal concept, shall be manufactured and tested. title: REAL-TIME OPTIMAL POWERED DESCENT GUIDANCE CONTROL FOR MARS PRECISION LANDERS EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop propellant-optimal real-time guidance control algorithms for Mars propulsive landing phases, including hazard avoidance and maneuvers for pinpoint and/or soft landing.Description: Optimal propulsive descent guidance (PDG) is a critical technology for ensuring Mars safe and precise landings. Current propulsive landing systems face challenges in terms of real-time guidance control that can optimize propellant consumption while achieving accurate and soft landing, especially in hazardous terrain. Traditional methods like gravity turns offer low-cost solutions but may lack the precision needed for autonomous precision landing. This activity aims to address these challenges by developing real-time guidance control algorithms that optimize propellant usage and ensure safe landings in hazardous terrains. The algorithms will consider hazard avoidance and other maneuvers (e.g. backshell avoidance, site selection), providing a robust solution for pinpoint and soft landings. The added value includes improved landing accuracy, enhanced safety, and efficient propellant usage; all which are crucial for future Mars precision landing missions. The goal is also to enable better trade-offs and consolidation of Mars exploration roadmaps and studies while providing sizing and limits of performance at systems level. The present technology development entails creating optimal PDG algorithms for the propulsive landing phase exploiting state-of-the-art techniques like nonlinear model predictive control and/or convexification techniques. Such methods allow finding optimal landing trajectories autonomously and in real-time. These algorithms will be designed to optimize numerical efficiency and robustness while keeping fallback options in case of infeasibility. The performance will be evaluated via high-fidelity dynamical simulations, while portability to flight processors will be assessed through profiling of the developed guidance control algorithms. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Consolidation of the proofs-of-concept and review the state-of-the-art of real-time PDG. - Definition of requirements, operational scenarios, use-cases, and preliminary validation and verification (VV) plan. - Detailed development of guidance control algorithms with focus on real-time capability, performance, and optimization for embeddability. - VV campaign of the proposed solutions and algorithms. - Assessment of computational performance on a space-graded processor through profiling. - Study synthesis, and recommendations for a technology roadmap to increase TRL.

title: GT1C-810SD DATA FUSION FOR COLLISION AVOIDANCE AND SPACE TRAFFIC COORDINATION (EXPRO+)
description: Timely and efficient planning, coordination and execution of collision avoidance manoeuvres requires accurateand consistent knowledge on the orbits. The Zero Debris targets on orbit accuracies are only achievable whenincreasing the data volume and mixing different data sources.Surveillance systems may produce conflicting information due to different model assumptions, which cannotbe merged with classical data fusion approaches. This is an adverse condition for space traffic coordination,especially when multiple parties rely on different data sources. The harmonisation of the data sources,estimation of biases between systems, identification of deterioration of specific sources, characterisation ofcombined uncertainties are mandatory requirements to achieve the accuracy levels. Typically, data fusion isperformed on different product levels, e.g. raw measurements or derived products.

title: END-TO-END DEMONSTRATOR FOR 6G CANDIDATE WAVEFORMS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.041) EXPRO+
description: The objective of this activity is to implement in hardware and evaluate the performance of at least two candidate waveforms for 6G,including the orthogonal time-frequencyspace (OTFS) waveform.Targeted Improvements:Enabling technologies paving the way of satellite communications into the 6G marketDescription: In parallel to the deployment of 5G networks across the globe, the Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) Release 17 has recently addressed the integration between terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks. In future releases, the 3GPP will transition from enhancements and extensions of 5G to the new 6G standard. Several waveforms aregood candidates for being included in 6G, and consensus has not been yet achieved within the community. However, most waveforms currently envisaged are based on orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM), mainly due to the legacy technology developments from both 4G and 5G. Orthogonal time-frequency-space (OTFS) waveform is a particularly popular candidate, as it is being thoroughlyinvestigated by academia. This activity shall develop an end-to-end software demonstrator for the physical layer of at least two candidate waveforms for 6G, one of which shall be OTFS. For all the considered waveforms, reduced-complexity transmitter and receiver algorithms shall be designed, implemented, and tested in the software demonstrator for bidirectional links over representative satellite channels. Both single user and multi-user cases shall be assessed, to ensure the capability of the considered waveforms to multiplex different users, and to address any issue that such capability may create at the physical layer. To demonstrate the hardware implementation of the designed transmitter and receiver for both waveforms, the designs shall be exported in hardware targeting space-grade field programmable gate array (FPGA) technology. The benefits of using the considered waveforms for joint communications and sensing purposes shall also be demonstrated, in line with the high-level requirements of 6G. title: STRATEGIC ADVOCACY FACILITY
description: The Strategic Advocacy Facility is a strategic Action Readiness instrument within ESA's Earth Action framework that enables the translation of EO innovation, science and applications into sustained operational uptake and impact, particularly within the impact finance ecosystem of International Financial Institutions, climate and environmental funds, and developing-country stakeholders. The Facility combines programme-level impact measurement and evidence generation, strategic partnership engagement, institutional advisorysupport, country-level uptake assessment, strategic intelligence, advocacy and communication within a single integrated framework. Building on the legacy and assets of the Global Development Assistance (GDA) programme, it establishes a common Theory of Change, monitoring and evaluation system, stakeholder engagement architecture and learning framework for Earth Action, while creating feedbackloops between implementation, partnerships, communication, programme governance and future RD investments. Through interconnected task setup, the Facility acts as a cross-cutting enabler that strengthens EO adoption, supports partner alignment, captures and communicates evidence of impact, and ensures that Earth Action activities can be scaled, mainstreamed and translated into long-term societal, environmental and development outcomes.

title: 54 MBAUD SOFTWARE DEFINED DEMODULATOR ON LOW-END PROCESSOR OR GRAPHICS PROCESSING UNIT (ARTES AT 7B.090)
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop and test a 54 Mbaud DVB-S2 and 5G NR demodulator on a low-end Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) or Central Processing Unit (CPU).Targeted Improvements: Enabling a 54 Mbaud software defined radio for low end platforms not existing today in ESA Member States.Description: Previous projects have demonstrated that carriers of equivalent bandwidth can be demodulated in software on x86 server-level CPUs. Also, by using high-performance GPUs and parallel processing, bandwidths of hundreds of MHz or even many GHz could be demodulated. To date, a low-cost GPU or CPU-based demodulation solution with typical consumer terminal performance have not been developed. Such technology would allow field-upgradable terminals that can enable the deployment of new waveforms without expensive hardware swaps in the middle of the life of the system.This activity will develop and test a software-based demodulator running in a consumer GPU as found in a games console or a PC graphics card or a low-end CPU (Intel Core i3 or equivalent), with a throughput equivalent to a TV receiver or a consumer satellite broadband terminal. Superior demodulation algorithms than those in common open-source Software Defined Radio (SDR) toolkits will be studied and further developed and implemented.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 shall implement and test a DVB-S2/S2X demodulator on one of the hardware platforms described above. The DVB-S2/X demodulator software will be tested against a hardware modulator or dedicated test equipment in the relevant environment to ensure the baud rate is met and fully compliant with as a minimum theDVB-S2 specification. Phase 1 deliverable will be a DVB-S2/S2X demodulator on a low-end CPU or GPU platform. Budget is up to 700 kEuro.- Phase 2 shall implement and test in the relevant environment 5G-NR waveform or other proprietary waveform development on the hardware platform delivered by Phase 1.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).
