title: RETURNABLE TESTBED FOR IN-ORBIT MANUFACTURING PROCESSES FOR LARGE STRUCTURES O TELECOM SATELLITES (ARTES AT 3E.027) - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to develop and characterize an additive manufacturing process to enable in-orbit manufacturing of large structural parts for satcom applications (e.g. large reflector, large solar array, large radiator structure). An in-orbit test-bed will be designed, manufactured and operated. Test-samples and complex demonstrators will be produced in order to evaluate the developed end-to-end in-orbit manufacturing process.Targeted Improvements: Enabling large in-orbit manufactured satcom hardware (e.g. large reflector, large solar array, radiator structure) not possible today.Description: Recent studies have explored the possibility of making large structures in orbit for future satcom applications, revealing new opportunities for applications, services andmarkets.The use of in-orbit additive manufacturing could eliminate the constraints of the launch vehicle fairings and the complexity of the deployment mechanisms, which are currently required for large deployables (e.g. very large reflectors, radiators and booms) relative to the platform size. However, the effects of microgravity, thermal, vacuum, and radiation on the additive manufacturing process in space are not well known, especially when assessing the structural, thermophysical and thermoelastic properties of the fabricated parts.This activity will characterize, through the production of test samples, the space environmental effects on the additive manufacturing processes required for future in-orbit manufacturing of large structural parts for satcom applications. An onboard testbed, using well established additive manufacturing processes and space qualified materials, will bedeveloped, manufactured andvalidated. The testbed shall accommodate visual and in situ measurements of the manufacturing process (e.g. temperature, molecular/particulate contamination induced by the process, etc) as well as allowing for the retrieval of the produced specimens for post-analysis on Earth. The testbed will also be used to producecomplex demonstrators (e.g. reflectors, booms and radiators or representative parts thereof). All in-orbit produced parts will be returned to Earth for post-analysis.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach. The first phase of the activity will develop, manufacture and achieve flight readiness of the testbed. The testbed performance will be validated on ground with reference test samples being produced and characterised. Phase 1 output will comprise of:Flight ready in-orbit manufacturing testbed, characterised end-to-end manufacturing process and reference test samples. The second phase will launch and operate the test bed to investigate the end-to-end additive manufacturing process in the space environment. Phase 2 will produce test samples in-orbit for process and material characterisation that are collected and returned for on ground analysis and comparison.The test results will be fed into Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) models to optimise in-orbit manufacturing parameters and processes for the production ofthe complex demonstrators.

title: SERVER IN SPACE MODULE FOR COMMUNICATION PAYLOADS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5A.098) - EXPRO+ (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture, and test a Server in Space (SiS) module for regenerative processors in satellite communication systems, enablingefficienton-board data processing and offering advanced autonomy applications andemergency management services.TargetedImprovements: Enabling application layer processing on-board for Servers in Space to offer advanced autonomy applications and emergency management services.Description: It is expected that satellites will have a larger percentage of regenerative processing, which opens the door to application layer processing on-board of satellites. The mainchallenge to be addressed is the availability of a Server in Space (SiS) with application layer processing, with technical challenges to be addressed in terms of powerconsumption, radiation hardening of ground-based data centre technology, and maturity of application layersoftware for embedded devices. Additionally, aspects of modularityand scalability for larger space datacentres shall be considered. Recent advancements of cloud providers in embedded processors, as well as technical developments inefficient FPGAs and computational memories, allow to link this concept to 5G/6G Non-Terrestrial-Networks (NTN) and Direct-to-Device (D2D) connectivity, enabling thesatellite to act as a server in space. By integrating the application layer on the satellite, cloud services, currently only provided on ground, could be made available to users innatural disaster situations or with special requirements that cannot use the regular network, e.g. very stringent latency needs like Internet-of-Things (IoT) or autonomousdriving.This activity will design and develop a cloud computing module, integrate it with the regenerative processor, and test it to ensure its efficiency and reliability inthe relevantenvironment. Focus shall be on the interfaces between the payload and components in the module, including also technologies used on ground, due to the high data ratesrequired. A fully functional Server in Space (SiS) module engineering module, capable of efficient on-board data processing and data storage, shall be designed, developedand tested. The SiS module shall demonstrateits capability to be integrated in future satcom digital processors and to be scaled to large data centres in space.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: UNLOCKING FPUTS AT SCALE THROUGH INTERFACE STANDARDISATION ( ARTES FP 1A.137) - EXPRO+
description: This activity will evaluate the technical and commercial feasibility of developing a standardised and interoperable set of Flat Panel User Terminal (UT) building blocks and internal interfaces, able to be reused in end user equipment designed for deployment across a broad range of market sectors and network types.The objective is to support the creation of a scalable, industrialised and costcompetitive ecosystem for flat panel user terminals in the ESA Member States by enabling economies of scale through open architectures and harmonised specifications.The activity will also identify standardised FPA terminal profiles (classes'), defining their RFperformance characteristics and associated validation and certification methodologies, to facilitate objective performance assessment and enable fair and interoperable competition among vendors.

title: QUANTUM COMPUTING ALGORITHMS DEVELOPMENT FOR SPACE APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop and assess quantum computing algorithms, methods and related tools for solving specific spacerelated computational challenges with higher performance and reliability than the state of the art achieved with the classical technologies.Description:Quantum computing technologies are progressing rapidly, with early-stage commercial and academicplatforms offering capabilities relevant to space applications. As one of the strategic sectors expected to benefit from quantum advantage, the space domain offers complex, high-impact challenges that can guide algorithm development and platform requirements. Lessons learned from these applications will be transferable to other sectors, enabling a broader quantum technology ecosystem. This activity aims to ensure European industry is quantum-ready and positioned to lead in the global race for space-enabled quantum technologies. It supports European strategic autonomy by fostering sovereign capabilities in quantum algorithm development, hybrid integration, and secure processing architectures tailored to ESA or national mission needs. The initiative also strengthens Europe's industrial competitiveness by enabling use-case-driven innovation and demonstrating technical leadership in both terrestrial and space environments. This activity aimsto encourage the usage of quantum computing potentials to address the challenges in space missions and technologies. It is expectedto extensively use the precision and fast calculations to solve in the most innovative ways challenges related to, mission planningbooks, AI integration, cryptography, and onboard processing, optimisation algorithm for power batteries, among others. Technology focus areas can include but are not limited to quantum-enhanced simulation for propulsion, materials, thermal, power, satellite station keeping, radiation and orbital dynamics, optimization of tools for mission planning, routing, scheduling, debris avoidance and predictive maintenance, quantum Machine Learning (QML) for Earth Observation, anomaly detection, and FDIR, design of quantumnativepre-measurement processing flows, leveraging intrinsic quantum dynamics to condition mission-criticaldata within the quantum domainpriorto readout or classical interface, digital twin powered by quantumcomputing.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Development and benchmarking of quantum algorithms tailored to space-relevant challengesconsidering gate-based, annealing or hybridquantum computing methods- Ground-based demonstrators for performance validation on quantum computers and/or classical high performance computers- Development of a software tool or product enabling the exploitation of the quantum algorithm for oneor more specific space related use cases- Analysis of the expected performance scaling with future generations of quantum computersThe tasks shall include clearly defined use cases and assess how quantum approachesincluding hybridmethods and error mitigation techniquesperformunder realistic computational loads and spaceenvironments, compared to classical baselines.Deliverables: Software, Report

title: JOINT IMPLEMENTATION OF SAT-3 AND COGNITIVE CLOUD COMPUTING IN SPACE (EOCOGNITIVELAB)
description: EOCognitiveLab brings together the evolution of the sat mission series and ESA's work on Cognitive Cloud Computing in Space for Earth Observation (3CS4EO). The activity is intended to demonstrate the added values unlocked by AI-enabled, cooperative Earth Observation capabilities across multiple heterogeneous?satellites?(including, event-based acquisition replanning, coordinated acquisitions), onboard processing and inter-satellite-link information exchange,?for selected end-to-end Earth Observation use cases, and to establish an in-orbit laboratory for autonomous, distributed and software-defined Earth Observation missions.? The mission will be based on a cooperative two-satellite space segment, equipped with onboard computing capabilities, supported by ground processing, and an exploitation platform enabling data distribution and community access. In addition, EOCognitiveLab will leverage open inter-satellite-link interfaces and be designed to support future expansion through the federation of additional Earth Observation missions.? As an in-orbit laboratory, EOCognitiveLab will provide an open and expandable environment for additional in-orbit experimentation forESA Members, Associated and Cooperating States EO community. Target experimentation areas include cooperative sensing, distributed processing, novel mission-orchestration approaches, onboard federated learning and fine-tuning, and other AI techniques relevant to distributed Earth Observation systems.? The proposed?activity will be implemented through a Mission Consolidation Phase followed, subject to a successful Gate Review, by a Mission Implementation Phase covering detailed design, development, integration, verification, launch, LEOP, commissioning and in-orbit verification up to the In-Orbit Commissioning Review.

title: ESEC-2 FLIGHT OPERATIONS SERVICE CONTRACT
description: The subject of this procurement proposal is the procurement of "Operations Engineering Services in support in ESEC/Redu" covering operational services for the preparation and execution of the mission operations entrusted to the Directorate of Operations located in ESEC, including the relevant Galileo Hosting Agreements. ESA/ESEC is the ESA European Space Security and Education Centre located in Belgium and is one of the ESA sites in Europe. The main core business in Mission Operations relevant to this procurement are: Control dedicated Satellites and Ground Segment (so called "Small Satellite missions") Perform its In-Orbit activities. Host and operate some ground segment elements in support to the EU Space Programme within a secured environment - mainly Galileo and EGNOS The Operational services, within the scope specified above, will be therefore divided in two main WPs: WP-1 Small Satellites Operations: A number of Small Satellites (such as the PROBA ones) are or will be controlled from ESEC with the help of a dedicated ground segment. In the current set-up and number of missions, up to six passes per satellite daily are supported in automatic mode for TM reception and commanding, which may be extended in the future when new missions will be operated from ESEC. The mission products are made available at ESEC and ready for distribution. title: MODULAR FRAMEWORK FOR ENHANCED PERCEPTION AND DECISION-MAKING - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a software module based on visual agents to integrate and combine visual inputsprocessing and decision-making capabilities.Description:The use of artificial intelligence for computer vision tasks has been extensively explored and applied over the lastdecade, resulting in a myriad of industrial applications. However, these approaches have predominantly relied on traditional CNN-based systems, which are often rigid, task-specific, and lack decision-making capabilities. Recent advancements, such as multimodal large language models, visual transformers, and agentic workflows, have demonstrated the potential for more flexible and adaptable solutions, that can also combine both visual input processing and decision making. This activity aims to develop a software module that will:- Define and implement a software layer (execution layer) to support the inference of visual agents and enable easy integration of new agents.- Design and implement an agentic workflow to execute various computer vision tasks (i.e.: object localization,image segmentation) on top of the defined execution layer.- Integrate decision-making capabilities into the agent implementation, leveraging the output of the vision tasks.For instance, planning and scheduling tasks or specific instruction to be executed, considering the output ofthe computer vison task processed by the agent.- Identify and deploy the solution on space-representative hardware.The software solution will integrate visual perception with decision-making capabilities that surpasses currentfunctionalities provided by traditional convolutional neural network (CNN). Unlike traditional CNNs, the agentic software developed in this activity will utilize multimodal inputs that may include various types of sensors outputs,(e.g. optical, radar, time series, astextual instructions), enabling agents to perform diverse tasks. The softwaredeveloped in this activity can impact multiple application domains, like Earth Observation missions. Additionally,the solution will enable onboard capabilities to be presented as functions or services that can be adapted based on evolving ground requirements. Therefore, at the system level (flight-ground), this solution will influence current interaction paradigms, allowing the ground segment to define new goals for a satellite dynamically. This is a key technology for the Space Domain Awareness (SDA) and for tracking activities on Earth, supporting disasters monitoring, civil protection, border control, and security applications.The activity shall encompass the following tasks:- Review and analyse traditional AI algorithms applied to computer vision tasks in space and identify new trendsusing multimodal transformers, visual transformers, and agentic workflows.- Identify use cases where the visual agent framework will be applied. At least two different use cases shall beproposed to demonstrate the framework's flexibility to adapt to different situations and covering both the visualtaskand reasoning task to be implemented by agents.- Design and develop the visual agent framework, including the final selection of onboard space hardware and the design specifications necessary for deploying the algorithm on it.- Integrate the framework into the different use cases and deploy it onto the selected hardware.- Verify and validate the framework, including performance assessment to evaluate the framework's efficiency, adaptability, and robustness compared with traditional algorithms.

title: S2P S2-VS-06 VISDOMS-S PHASE A/B1
description: The procurement covers the VISDOMS-S Mission Phase A/B1. Based on the previous Space Based Optical Monitoring (SBOM) feasibility study, a mission concept using a small satellite and existing imager shall be further elaborated in a short Phase A. Suitable small platform candidates shall be further investigated in terms of its capacity and compliance towards the observational needs, the deorbiting requirements, and its capability to host the identified optical imager. The preliminary technical, engineering and quality assurance requirements for the Delta-Class mission shall be reviewed, agreed and consolidated as part of the Preliminary Requirements Review. The development approach shall be further elaborated with the objective to enable the establishment of the implementation and procurement plan. System optimisations based on previous flight experience that may lead to an improvement of the mission performance and its robustness by enhancing the existing equipment and optical imager may be considered for further elaboration during Phase B1.The Phase B1 industrial system study shall produce a preliminary design of the space and ground segment that shall include all elements for the mission definition, the spacecraft and the optical imager and the ground segment. The satellite design shall be matured, and a detailed accommodation study of the optical imager shall be performed. The design of the optical imager and potential modifications that may be required shall be addressed including the detector selection, readout electronics and the control and data processing unit. The technical requirements specifications of all major units shall be established, and the system requirements shall be consolidated and verified as far as possible by analysis. The study shall produce the necessary documentation for the System Requirements Review and confirm that the review objectives are achieved.

title: NAVISP EL1-134 ALL-WEATHER LASER COMMUNICATION LINKS FOR OPTICAL PNT SYSTEMS - EXPRO+
description: EL1-134 - This activity will investigate innovative techniques to enable continuous optical timing and ranging links under all weather conditions, addressing a key challenge for operational optical PNT (Positioning, Navigation, and Timing) systems. Optical satellite-to-ground links, such as those planned for ESA's OpSTAR mission, are vulnerable to atmospheric effects, particularly cloud cover, which can degrade or completely interrupt communications with an Optical Ground Station (OGS). The study will assess and experimentally demonstrate atmospheric transmission enhancement techniques designed to improve link availability under adverse weather conditions. It will evaluate whether these approaches can maintain accurate and reliable timing and ranging measurements between laser terminals representative of future operational optical PNT systems.

title: MODULAR ROBUST WAVEFORM FOR END-TO-END COMMUNICATIONS - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a proof-of-concept of a modular robust waveform for E2E communications that offers further protection for the missions, in a modular approach in accordance with the mission security needs.Description:Intentional RF interference is a threat to space missions, as it can disrupt the radio links between satellite and ground/users. There are waveform techniques that can counter or mitigate the impact of that interference but they need to be designed specifically against reference threats. This activity is aimed at developing a modular robust waveform for end-to-end (E2E) communications offering further protection for the missions, by designing the waveform aspects as well as the receiver operations. It will consider typical RF threats and tune the waveform against the most common ones, so that space missions do not have to develop new solutions for their case. The design of the modular robust waveform can include cryptographically robust spread sequences that can be used to drive a frequency hopping scheme, or a direct Sequence spread spectrum modulation, coupled with Adaptive Coding and Modulation (ACM). The adaptation algorithm of the ACM can cover both the typical Modulation and Coding schemes as well as the Transmission Security (TRANSEC) functions (e.g. Direct Sequence Spread Spectrum and Frequency Hopping), providing flexible level of protection based on the link conditions. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Consolidation of the most common RF interference signals and attacks method - Investigation of state of theart signal techniques to counter RF interference and development of a SWAT analysis to select the optimum measures for the consolidated attacks options. - Detailed design of the waveform blocks to counter the identified common RF interference threats. Particular emphasis shall be devoted to the Add-on modularity so that each block can be added as plug-in. - Development of a Proof of Concept simulator including signal generator/receiver of the waveform and assessment of the E2E performance of the proposed Waveform. - Investigation of the regulatory constraints from the Radio Frequency Compatibility with specific focus on the impact of wideband signals on ITU frequency bands allocation. The software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access to it and can provide update to the community of users.Deliverables: Report, Software

title: LOW-COST, HIGH-ISP, INTEGRATED AIR-BREATHING ELECTRIC PROPULSION SYSTEM FOR HIGH ASPECT RATIO VLEO SMALL SATELLITES - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop, manufacture and test a low-cost, integrated high-Isp air-breathing electric propulsion systemsuitable for drag compensation of High-Aspect Ratio (HAR) small satellites operating in VLEO.Description:Sustainable operations in Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO, below 250 km altitude) are currently constrained bythe propellant mass required to continuously compensate for aerodynamic drag. Air-Breathing ElectricPropulsion (ABEP) offers a potential solution by replacing conventional on-board propellant with atmosphericparticles collected through a suitably designed intake and delivered to Electric Propulsion thrusters for thrustgeneration and drag compensation.Previous ESA and non-ESA studies, supported by early-stage technology development activities, have demonstrated the feasibility of the ABEP concept and its strong potential to enable a range of applications, inparticular Telecommunications (D2D / D2H) and high-resolution Earth Observation missions. To reduce the propulsion effort required to counteract aerodynamic drag and prevent orbital decay, VLEO platforms typically adopt slender spacecraft configurations with optimised drag area, typically based on a High-Aspect Ratio (HAR) topology. This activity specifically addresses ABEP systems designed for such drag-areaoptimisedsmall satellites. The ABEP systems will be capable of operating across varying atmospheric densityand composition regimes, accounting for diurnal and seasonal variability, and across altitudes below 250km.Lifetime assessment is required, including appropriate material selection to withstand high-velocity particleimpacts and Atomic Oxygen (ATOX) exposure.The feasibility of integrated ABEP systems for this class of small satellites has already been demonstrated upto TRL 3. This activity aims to mature the technologyat system level through the design, manufacture, andtesting of a fully integrated ABEP system capable of providing continuous dragcompensation for HAR smallsatellites operating in VLEO. The expected outcome is a validated ABEP system at TRL 4, including intake,thruster, fluidics and Power Processing Unit (PPU). Successful completion of the activity will provide a compact and efficient drag-compensation solution to support sustained VLEO operations and address emerging market needs for future VLEO constellations.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidation of the ABEP system requirements for a High-Aspect Ratio small satellite.- Design, manufacturing, assembly and integration of a fully integrated ABEP system (including PPU,thruster, intake, fluidics).- Perform a functional verification test and performance mapping at system level in VLEO-representativetest conditions.- Define the thrust control laws for drag compensation based on the results achieved in the test campaign.- Perform a short endurance (250h) test that showcases performance stability and lack of early-life failuremechanisms.

Description: Objective:To develop, manufacture and test a low-cost, integrated high-Isp air-breathing electric propulsion systemsuitable for drag compensation of High-Aspect Ratio (HAR) small satellites operating in VLEO.Description:Sustainable operations in Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO, below 250 km altitude) are currently constrained bythe propellant mass required to continuously compensate for aerodynamic drag. Air-Breathing ElectricPropulsion (ABEP) offers a potential solution by replacing conventional on-board propellant with atmosphericparticles collected through a suitably designed intake and delivered to Electric Propulsion thrusters for thrustgeneration and drag compensation.Previous ESA and non-ESA studies, supported by early-stage technology development activities, have demonstrated the feasibility of the ABEP concept and its strong potential to enable a range of applications, inparticular Telecommunications (D2D / D2H) and high-resolution Earth Observation missions. To reduce the propulsion effort required to counteract aerodynamic drag and prevent orbital decay, VLEO platforms typically adopt slender spacecraft configurations with optimised drag area, typically based on a High-Aspect Ratio (HAR) topology. This activity specifically addresses ABEP systems designed for such drag-areaoptimisedsmall satellites. The ABEP systems will be capable of operating across varying atmospheric densityand composition regimes, accounting for diurnal and seasonal variability, and across altitudes below 250km.Lifetime assessment is required, including appropriate material selection to withstand high-velocity particleimpacts and Atomic Oxygen (ATOX) exposure.The feasibility of integrated ABEP systems for this class of small satellites has already been demonstrated upto TRL 3. This activity aims to mature the technologyat system level through the design, manufacture, andtesting of a fully integrated ABEP system capable of providing continuous dragcompensation for HAR smallsatellites operating in VLEO. The expected outcome is a validated ABEP system at TRL 4, including intake,thruster, fluidics and Power Processing Unit (PPU). Successful completion of the activity will provide a compact and efficient drag-compensation solution to support sustained VLEO operations and address emerging market needs for future VLEO constellations.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidation of the ABEP system requirements for a High-Aspect Ratio small satellite.- Design, manufacturing, assembly and integration of a fully integrated ABEP system (including PPU,thruster, intake, fluidics).- Perform a functional verification test and performance mapping at system level in VLEO-representativetest conditions.- Define the thrust control laws for drag compensation based on the results achieved in the test campaign.- Perform a short endurance (250h) test that showcases performance stability and lack of early-life failuremechanisms.

title: STEPPING STONE MISSION DEFINITION STUDY
description: Stepping Stone Missions are a new class of user driven Earth Observation missions designed to address gaps in the current EO ecosystem by delivering quality certified data and services tailored to environmental policy needs at European and global level. They build on and complement existing reference missions and infrastructures, while targeting observation domains and sampling requirements not adequately covered today. A key characteristic is their service oriented and commercially minded nature: missions are conceived from the outset to enable operational services, foster downstream applications, and evolve into scalable, privately operated constellations once their performance and utility have been demonstrated in orbit. The Stepping Stones activity focuses on conducting mission definition studies that mature candidate concepts up to a consolidated system baseline. This includes the parallel development of the space and ground segments, the definition of user oriented services, and the establishment of a robust business case demonstrating long term viability. The studies also encompass assessment of technical feasibility, verification and validation approaches, and readiness with respect to user needs, policy alignment, and commercial exploitation. Overall, the objective is to de risk and validate the end to end concepttechnical, service, and marketup to System Requirements Review level.

title: UHF IOT ANTENNA FOR MEDIUM EARTH ORBIT SMALLSATS (ARTES AT 5E.034) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, develop and test an engineering model of a UHF antenna suitable for operating from MEO-based smallsats.Targeted Improvements: 10-dB gain increase compared to current state-of-the-art UHF antennas.Description: UHF antennas have been already developed for Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) smallsats/nanosats. Moving from LEO to Medium-Earth-Orbit (MEO) enables a reduction of the number of required satellites in the constellation to provide global coverage. title: HIGHLY INTEGRATED TRANSMIT AND RECEIVE DIRECT RADIATING ANTENNA ARRAY BASED ON MM-WAVE SILICON TECHNOLOGIES AND PACKAGING (ARTES AT 5B.241) RE-ISSUE (1-12262) EXPRO+
description: The objective of the activity is to develop a highly integrated, scalable Ku or Ka-band TX/RX direct radiating array, for versatileconnectivity missions in low earth orbit. Critical breadboarding will be carried out, levering the advances in Mm-wave silicon technologies and advanced packaging techniques to achieve a high degree of integration. Targeted Improvements: Enabling highly integrated combined transmit and receive active antenna with a large number of elements, for low earth orbit applications, not existing today. Description: Mm-wave silicon technologies together with advanced packaging and printed circuit board technologies are the key enablers of high-volume active antennas today. To achieve the equivalent isotropic radiated power (EIRP) required by LEO constellationsatellites, power levels of up to 20dBm are needed in 2000+ element class arrays. At the same time, noise figure levels approaching1dB at Ka band can significantly improve the performance of next generation arrays. Multibeam beamforming operation can be obtainedby several beamforming strategies that have only been possible thanks to the recent advancements in silicon technologies. To allow affordable high-volume manufacturing of reliable arrays, packaging and PCB integration are of equal importance as the semiconductor technology itself and they all need to be considered in co-design. This activity will develop in a first step a scalable Ku- or Ka-band direct array transmit and receive architecture taking into account aspects including beamforming, low noise and high-efficiency power amplification, filtering, control, switching, interconnections, PCB routing and thermal control. Mm-wave silicon technologies and packaging techniques will be reviewed, and a technology baseline will be selected for all critical antenna elements. Thermal management and spacecraft accommodation will be taken into account to maximise integration. In a second step a sub-array breadboard with radiating elements will be designed manufactured and tested. The breadboard shall be sufficient to evaluate the functionality of the direct radiating architecture and to test the RF and thermal management concept.

title: SECURITY AWARE POSITION, VELOCITY AND TIME INTEGRITY CONCEPT - EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesTo develop an integrity concept leveraging Position, Velocity and Time (PVT) assurance solutions for safety critical applications.DescriptionSafety critical applications rely on integrity concepts based on protection levels and alerting schemes to bound the position error in nominal and failure scenarios under a given integrity risk. This allows estimating the worst-case user position systematically taking into account potential feared events. Similar integrity concepts and list of feared events can be developed considering the potential presence of intentional GNSS signal impairments.The Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) providers are implementing mechanism in order to protect the users from security threats such as spoofing. For instance, Galileo will provide both navigation message authentication (NMA) and ranging authentication (Commercial Service Authentication [CAS]). Therefore, the user integrity concepts will have to be expanded to define the impact of intentional interference, to specify the related feared events, and to consider the barriers provided by PVT assurance solutions.This activity aims at exploring technological enablers, algorithms and concepts for future positioning integrity concepts, which would enable safe and secure operations even in the presence of potential intentional impairments. It will investigate the contribution to the overall safety and trustworthiness provided by GNSS-based PVT assurance. Moreover, attention will be given to demonstrating that the overall target integrity can be achieved by different positioning solutions and PVT assurance techniques.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- State-of-the-art survey of integrity concepts for PVT, of PVT assurance services, and of anti-spoofing techniques,- Development of innovative security-aware concepts,- Performance assessment of the integrity concepts,- Roadmap for standardization.DeliverablesReport, Software

title: EO PNRR IRIDE PROJECT ENGINEERING SUPPORT TO IT-PNRR EO ACTIVITIES
description: According to the "Arrangement for ESA's Assistance to the Italian National Project concerning Earth Observation and Space Transportation", ESA/LEG/525 Paris, 22 December 2021, ESA will provide technical assistance to the Presidency of Council of Ministries of theItalian Republic for the swift implementation of the Italian "Piano Nazionale di Ripresa e Resilienza" (hereinafter also IT PNRR), in the domain of Earth Observation and Space Transportation.In providing the technical assistance, ESA will manage the technical and contractual aspects of the project and will be responsible for the procurements related to the Arrangement. This contractual activity is relevant to the Component of the PNRR devoted to Space Activities for Earth Observation (hereinafter called EO PNRR IRIDE Project), which covers the realization of an End-to-End System composed by the Upstream Segment, the Downstream Segment and the Services Segment to provide the geospatial-based services at National and European level, according to the needs expressed by the Italian National Authorities with the objective to provide services to the Public Administration and to private Customers.- The Upstream will be based on a Satellite Constellation(s). The payloads will be a combination of SARs and optical, panchromatic, hyperspectral andinfrared Imagers- The Downstream is composed by the Flight Operation Segment, the Payload Data Ground Segment, the "marketplace" (which is a digital market which combines demand and supply using innovative developments in geospatial processing, cloud computing, artificial intelligence and fusion of different sources of data) and the Cyber Italy (which is a Digital Twin of Italy)- The Services will be a combination of services to public administrations and commercial services. The following 8 services for public administrations have been currently identified: Coastal service and maritime-coastal monitoring, Air Quality Service, Ground Motion Service,Monitor service coverage and land use (Land Cover/Use), Hydrometeorological Service, Water Resources Service, Emergency service, Security service.This procurement addresses the provision of specialized engineering support for the implementation of the upstream, downstream and services elements of the EO PNRR IRIDE Project. The following types of support will be addressed:- Provision of specialized consultancy or execution of technical tasks (e.g. one-shot mission analysis for inclusion of a new constellation, review of Technical Notes addressing specialized topics, etc.)- Execution of technical reviews or status checks, to support the assessment ofthe status of implementation activitiesThe Agency shall submit engineering support requests as they materialize along the project lifetime. The activity will last 4 years.In view of the overarching objective of the Italian PNRR to strengthen growth potential, job creation and economic, social and institutional resilience of Italy, thereby enhancing, in accordance with the objectives of the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility, the economic, social and territorial cohesion and convergence within the Union, the present ITTis addressed to economic operators registered in Italy. Consequently, the Agency shall consider for evaluation all proposals from such economic operators.Industry awarded with this contract is excluded from any other contractual activity in the frame of the EO PNRR IRIDE Project.

description: The objective of this activity is to design, develop and deploy the next version of the S3TOC (V3), including hardware, software and communications network.The S3TOC V3 shall be a full redesign of the system following a top-down approach. The new design should reuse the current S3TOC hardware to the maximum extent possible. Regarding software, it may reuse parts of the current system, which shall be modified as needed, considering that third-party IPRs should be avoided.It is important to note that the S3TOC is currently an operational system and that it shall remain operational through the execution of this work. This means that the deployment of the S3TOC V3 shall be planned considering minimal or, whenever possible, no interruption to the services provided by the S3TOC, and coordinated with the S3TOC operations team.

title: ONBOARDING AND OPERATIONS COORDINATION SERVICES FOR EO SCIENCE MISSIONS
description: The "Onboarding and Operations Coordination Services" for EO Science Missions consist of engineering services to be delivered by a Service Provider possessing a diversified expertise in the EO domain including suitable engineering expertise for EO mission and data management systems as well as sound experience in the coordination of integration, testing, validation and operational activities.In addition, specific expertise will be initially needed to include heritage missions in the new approach and concept.A strong underlying competence of the Service Provider in key EO data generation and management functionalities (such as data processing, data flows and data exchange interfaces), and related security aspects is also required. Familiarity with the specificities of the applicable EO Science mission's portfolio is expected.The Onboarding and Operations Coordination Services will be deployed and operated based on a SecDevOps approach to ensure coherence between the operated services and their evolutions and to guarantee a common governance in all the phases of the framework lifecycle.It is worth highlighting that, in general terms, the Onboarding and Operations Coordination Services are not conceived to carry out specific developments nor to perform themselves EOF operational activities, ratherto coordinate specific operational services (e.g. in the domain of data processing, data access, data acquisition, data archive).Under ESA authority, the selected Service Provider will be responsible for:1. Maintenance and Evolution of the EOF-EOS Reference Architecture2. Onboarding of new missions3. End-to-end Operations coordination

title: ADVANCED COATINGS AND MATERIALS FOR LOW EARTH ORBIT SATELLITES FOR DARK AND QUIET SKIES EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop advanced coatings and materials for Dark and Quiet Skies (DQS) with optimised reflectance/scattering, scalable production, and durability in (V)LEO environments.Description: The expansion of satellite mega constellations in (Very) Low Earth Orbit ((V)LEO) for Telecommunications or Earth Observation applications poses growing challenges for astronomy, particularly due to increased satellite brightness and stray light. Key contributors to this issue are large external spacecraft surfacessuch as solar arrays, radiators, multilayer insulation (MLI), optical instruments, and structural componentsthat reflect sunlight and increaseoptical interference. Traditionally, spacecraft materials have been optimized for thermal, mechanical, or electrical properties, with limited consideration for optical performance in the visible range. This activity aims to identify high-risk materials and applications that conflict with Dark and Quiet Skies (DQS) guidelines, especially where qualified low-impact alternatives are lacking. Based on this evaluation, the focus will shift to developing new coatings or materials that reduce optical interference while preserving existing performance standards. Scalability and compatibility with complex satellite designs is to be considered. Two specific applications are aimed to be addressed: 1. A high-risk material or application identified during the initial assessment (e.g., solar cells, MLI, thrusters). 2. Large deployable radiators, whose surfaces contribute significantly to spacecraft brightness. Here, innovative microstructured surfaces will be designed to reflect sunlight at controlled angles away from Earth and be coated to match the optical performance of existing OSR or SSM materials. This activity involves the development, testing, and characterization of new materials with a focus on critical optical properties such as Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function (BRDF), Total IntegratedScatter (TIS), and total hemispherical reflectance, in addition to standard performance metrics. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of current materials and available alternatives - Development of DQS mitigation strategies - Selection of twodetailed application cases - Definition of requirements and material/coating design - Sample manufacturing - Testing of new materials for both cases including mechanical stress and micrometeoroid impact assessments

title: COPERNICUS SENTINEL-3 NEXT GENERATION OPTICAL PHASE A/B1
description: Sentinel-3 NGO Phase 0 system studies which were initiated in 2021 allowed to perform high level trade-offs, explore the perimeter of the preliminary set of mission requirements stemming from the EC and the Sentinel-3 NGO Ad Hoc Expert Group (AHEG), and to identify complexity/cost drivers and critical technologies.Following those Phase 0 activities, the subject of the current procurement proposal is the Phase A/B1 of Sentinel-3 NGO, designed to provide enhanced-performance continuity to the existing Sentinel-3 mission, in-line with the evolving user needsSentinel-3 NGO will carry two instruments: the Advanced Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (AOLCI)and the Advanced Sea and Land Surface Temperature Radiometer (ASLSTR).The main improvements compared to the legacy Sentinel-3 (optical) mission and considered as key design drivers are:-Improved spatial sampling distance (SSD) by a factor of 2 for AOLCI to bring it to 150 m and bring the SSD to 500 m for all bands of ASLSTR-Increased number of spectral bands for AOLCI. New bands have been added based on recommendations to improve the retrieval of diatoms, coccolithophores, cyanobacteria and support atmospheric correction-Increased number of spectral bands potentially also for ASLSTR, aimed at supporting observational needs of Sea Surface Temperature and to improve sensitivity of daytime aerosol retrievals

title: DEVELOPMENT OF ULTRA-HIGH ENERGY DENSITY BATTERY CELLS (500 WH/KG) EXPRO+
description: To develop ultra-high energy density battery cells with specific energy of 500 Wh / kg (e.g. Lithium sulphur, Lithium-metal anode etc).Description: Deep space missions demand energy storage solutions that significantly outperform current state-of-the-art technologies in terms of specific energy density, reliability and resilience under extreme environmental conditions. As missions move beyond the Earth orbit toward the Moon, Mars and beyond, spacecraft must operate autonomously for extended periods without the possibility of recharge or maintenance. This requires batteries with ultra-high energy density, that can maximize the mission duration and system efficiency, whilst minimizing the mass of the units. These batteries must also withstand vacuum, a high temperature range and radiation conditions. The development of high specific energy battery cells is an asset to reduce the mass and volume of the battery units. This activity focusses on defining an ultra-high energy density battery cell chemistry. Upon selected chemistry it develops abreadboard of a battery. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Technology survey and selection: Review and assess emerging battery chemistries and architectures with the highest potential for space applications. Select the most promising candidates forfurther development. - Material and cell development: Develop and optimize materials and electrochemical cells that meet the defined requirements, including electrodes, novel electrolytes, and the design of ultra-high energy density cell formats. - Prototype designand assembly: Design, manufacture and assemble a cell or battery prototype. Emphasis should be placed on minimizing the final mass,while enhancing safety and durability. - Performance testing and validation: Perform environmental and performance testing, including thermal cycling, vacuum exposure, vibration, life-tests and radiation tolerance, to validate the operational readiness of the developed cells. - Roadmap and industrialization strategy: Develop a roadmap for technology maturation and space qualification. Outlinean industrialization and scale up strategy, including potential partnerships with European industry to secure long term supply capabilities.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses.

title: NAVISP EL1-132 DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF FLEXIBLE ELORAN/GNSS SIGNAL SIMULATOR- EXPRO+
description: The increasing dependence on GNSS for positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) services has highlighted vulnerabilities to jamming,spoofing, interference and space-weather effects. eLORAN is emerging as a resilient terrestrial complement to GNSS, but its adoptionrequires advanced tools capable of realistically testing and validating hybrid GNSS/eLORAN solutions. This activity will develop and validate a flexible, modular and future-proof eLORAN/GNSS signal simulator, synchronised with commercial GNSS simulators and supported by dedicated Receiver Analysis and Validation Tools. The simulator will provide high-fidelity signal generation, propagation modelling, multi-chain and multi-time-reference capabilities, and record-and-replay functions, enabling realistic end-to-end validation of resilient PNT solutions across timing, maritime and other application domains.

description: InSPoC-4 is the latest initiative of the In-Space Proof Of Concept (InSPoC) venture, with a dedicated focus on Advanced In-Space Logistics. Its core objective is to scale the in-space transportation ecosystem into a dynamic, efficient logistics network, much like the multimodal systems we use on Earth to ship parcels across continents. This InSPoC-4 System study will: 1.Analyse and flow the in-space logistics customers needs to define a Use Case Catalogue and refine the overall In-Space Logistics CONOPS; 2.Perform a system modelling of the In-Space Logistics Ecosystem and Cluster Space Cargo in Cargo Classes;3.Analyse Space Cargo Transfer CONOPS and identify required technologies for handling operations;4.Perform a detailed analysis on selected Use Cases with customer to:a.Refine Operational Concept;b.Provide ISTV Preliminary Definition;c.Identify Critical Technologies;d.Define roadmap toward ground and in-orbit demonstrations ;

It will survey typical CNIs and define use cases involving GNSS-based timing and positioning. The test bench willinject signal impairments, including jamming and spoofing, and measure performance impacts. Additional outputs include a machine-learning training database for interference detection, independent FTA/FMECA analyses, and a searchable Lessons Learned database. title: IN-ORBIT RECONFIGURABLE SOLAR ARRAY - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To design a solar array concept allowing for in-orbit reconfiguration of strings length and section size and to optimisethe solar array power output for EOL best possible performance.Description: Solar cell voltage and current are a function of operating temperature and degradation level. String lengths and section sizes are optimised for EOL best performance. However, this means that for most of the time the solar array is not exploiting its full performance capability. If string lengths and section sizes were reconfigurable, the power output at each time of the mission could be maximised. This concept could provide various benefits, such as flexible adaptation in case of unforeseen events (e.g. solar flares, micrometeorite impacts, etc.), mission extension in GEO and potential use of cells with less performance in GEO radiation environment. These benefits can be of interest for Telecom applications, where very large solar arrays are typically required to compensate for the degradation over the entire mission. This activity targets innovative photovoltaic assembly concepts that allows for reconfiguring string lengths and section size to optimise performance in dependence of operating conditions during the mission (e.g. temperature, irradiation level). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of a solar array / photovoltaic assembly concept allowing for reconfiguration of string lengths and section sizes. - Prototyping of interconnection concepts. - Initial proof of concept demonstration.

title: HIGH-THRUST, MODERATE-ISP, 6DOF ELECTRIC PROPULSION SYSTEM FOR CUBESATS - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop a 6 DOF electric propulsion system for close-proximity operations and formation flyingof future CubeSats.DescriptionPropulsion capabilities are crucial to enhance utilisation perspectives of future CubeSats. Sixdegrees of freedom (6DOF) propulsion is an enabling technology to perform close-proximityoperations and formation flying. 6DOF propulsion systems are already available in a form of podsof micro cold gas thrusters or micro resistojets, both having limited Isp, e.g. between 50 and 100seconds.This activity aims at initiating the development of a disruptive, moderate Isp (>100s), 6DoF electricpropulsion system capable to deliverrelatively high thrust and to comply with the needs of higherdelta-V missions. The system shall be designed to include propellant storage and distribution, powerprocessing units (PPUs) and a pod of electric propulsion thrusters.Preliminary propulsion system requirements are:- 6DoF manoeuvring capability, e.g. obtainable with a pod of 6 (tbc) thrusters- Delta-V >50 m/s.- Thrust levels sufficient to guarantee agility and fast response, e.g. >1mN- Mass and power consumption compatible with a 6 to 12U CubeSats- "Readyto fire" configuration- Use of inert or low-reactivity propellant.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- System requirements definition- System design definition and justification- Breadboard manufacturing and testing, including performance characterisation andendurance test of 200 hours on a single thruster- Generation of development plan for follow-up qualification.

title: EO FOR ESSENTIAL BIODIVERSITY VARIABLES GBF INDICATORS - EXPRO+
description: In partnership with GEO BON and the European Biodiversity Observation Coordination Centre (EBOCC), this activity will study how Essential Biodiversity Variables (EBVs) enabled by satellite remote sensing can be integrated in the monitoring framework of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KM-GBF) adopted at COP 15 of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) in December 2022.The objective is to develop state-of-the-art EO solutions to produce EBVs in terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecosystems addressing different EBV classes (e.g., ecosystem structure and function, community composition, species population). The project aims to support the integration of EBVs, enabled by satellite remote sensing, into the GBF monitoring framework and its indicators. The activity will leverage existing EBV initiatives conducted by European and international partners, including GEO BON, EUROPABON, the European Knowledge Centre for Biodiversity (KCBD), the European Biodiversity Partnership (Biodiversa+) and the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF).

title: MATERIALS FOR SUSTAINABLE ATMOSPHERIC RE-ENTRY - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To characterise spacecraft materials that minimise atmospheric impacts during re-entry.Description:ESA's Green Agendaand Ecodesign Policy require that the environmental impacts of all space missions andprogrammes are assessed and reduced across their full life cycle. Launch and spacecraft re-entry effects onthe atmosphere are known gaps to fulfil these requirements. This results in significant uncertainty andsystematic exclusion of such effects when developing materials on the basis of sustainable performance.Previous and ongoing Discovery activities, Insights into the Chemistry of Atmospheric Re-entry of JunkedSpacecraft (ICARUS) and Impacts of space Debris ablation on Earth's Atmospheric System (IDEAS), havehighlighted the potential importance of ablation products in the atmosphere while established initial modellingapproaches and experimental validation capabilities.The proposed activity addresses this critical knowledge gap by developing a consolidated experimental andmodelling framework to characterise emissionsfrom spacecraft re-entry and integrate these into atmosphericand design assessment tools. This will enable the incorporation of atmospheric impacts into Life CycleAssessment (LCA) and support both Ecodesign and Design-for-Demise (D4D) decision making. Such aframework would be the first worldwide.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Identify representative launcher and spacecraftdemise-critical materials as well as Space Debris Particles(SPSs)- Propose material characterization factors (e.g. Ozon Depletionmetrics, radiative forcing proxies) andassociated quantification methodology- Refine methods to allow observation and characterization of particles generated during the vaporizationphase of selected materials- Demonstrate validation tests under realistic atmospheric re-entry conditions (e.g. Thermal, pressure andflow conditions) measuring and linking ablation fluxes to downstream chemical compositions- Parametrization and modelling of datasets for integration into re-entry and atmospheric chemistryclimatemodels-Define uncertainty and applicability ranges for model use- Formulate recommendations for standardised testing procedures to support the continuous developmentand population of material datasets.Procurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SME RD organisations, preferably in cooperation. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: LOW-IMPACT VELOCITY TOOLS FOR VERIFICATION AND VALIDATION OF CLOSE PROXIMITY OPERATIONS STRATEGIES EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a comprehensive set of rigorously tested tools that ensures monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance for close proximity operations.Description: Past activities related to Close Proximity Operations (CPO) highlighted the need ofdeveloping low impact velocity tools that can verify and validate that the servicer spacecraft (SC) maintains a collision risk probability of less than given threshold (e.g 10^-4) with the client SC during CPO. For missions involving multiple SC in close formation, the design of manoeuvres to avoid collisions with catalogue objects not belonging to the formation requires to take into account all SC of the formation, e.g. an avoidance manoeuvre performed by one SC of the formation shall not trigger an inner-formation collision risk but rather minimise disturbance to the formation while ensuring the required risk reduction. This activity aims at developing a comprehensive set of tools (e.g. DRAMA like tool, prototype software for formation flying) that ensure monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance during close proximity operations (including formation flying). This activity encompasses the followingtasks: - Develop and refine software tools that model the trajectory of both the target and servicer. - Develop algorithms that identify safe trajectories for close approaches and include collision avoidance features. - Develop tools that perform uncertainty propagation to estimate the likelihood of a collision between the servicer and client. - Identify sensor systems capable of providing design and operational level data about the relative positions, velocities, and orientations of both the servicer and the target. - Conduct virtual testing within the developed tools to simulate close approach and rendezvous operations in various scenarios. - Develop mathematical models of constraints and requirements and prototype a software solution suitable for realistic scenarios.

Description: Objective: To develop a comprehensive set of rigorously tested tools that ensures monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance for close proximity operations.Description: Past activities related to Close Proximity Operations (CPO) highlighted the need ofdeveloping low impact velocity tools that can verify and validate that the servicer spacecraft (SC) maintains a collision risk probability of less than given threshold (e.g 10^-4) with the client SC during CPO. For missions involving multiple SC in close formation, the design of manoeuvres to avoid collisions with catalogue objects not belonging to the formation requires to take into account all SC of the formation, e.g. an avoidance manoeuvre performed by one SC of the formation shall not trigger an inner-formation collision risk but rather minimise disturbance to the formation while ensuring the required risk reduction. This activity aims at developing a comprehensive set of tools (e.g. DRAMA like tool, prototype software for formation flying) that ensure monitoring, risk assessment, and collision avoidance during close proximity operations (including formation flying). This activity encompasses the followingtasks: - Develop and refine software tools that model the trajectory of both the target and servicer. - Develop algorithms that identify safe trajectories for close approaches and include collision avoidance features. - Develop tools that perform uncertainty propagation to estimate the likelihood of a collision between the servicer and client. - Identify sensor systems capable of providing design and operational level data about the relative positions, velocities, and orientations of both the servicer and the target. - Conduct virtual testing within the developed tools to simulate close approach and rendezvous operations in various scenarios. - Develop mathematical models of constraints and requirements and prototype a software solution suitable for realistic scenarios.

title: ERS-EO PROOF OF CONCEPT TO SUPPORT ENHANCED PROTECTION OF CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE
description: ERS-EO Proof of Concept on Critical Infrastructure ManagementThe ERS-EO Element 1 Critical Infrastructure Monitoring Prof of Concept is intended to demonstrate the step improvement for enhanced monitoring and management of critical infrastructure resulting from the effective combination of diverse EO and non-EO capabilities representative of the future Earth Observation Governmental Service (EOGS) capacity. In particular, the customization and fusion of these capabilities will generate significant improvements in tasking response, persistent data collection, information delivery latency, expanded information content andflexibility and adaptability in response to dynamic situations. In this context, the Critical Infrastructure Monitoring PoC will:Stimulate innovative combinations of public and private EO systems to support improved and more flexible tasking, response latency, persistence and cross-operator cueing;Develop customized workflows connecting satellite operators, non-EO data providers, analytics tool developers and critical infrastructure operators to ensure enhanced capability to detect, characterize, respond to and mitigateemergent threats and anomalies;Verify the improvements achievable over current state of the art with respect to emerging threat detection and mitigation action execution for critical infrastructure operators under realistic operating conditions;With respect to gaps in current capabilities, elaborate technical approaches for their resolution, verify their impact under representative operational environments and conditionsand elaborate a road map for eventual transfer to full operations based on exclusively European technology. The contract will integrate existing EO and non-EO capabilities as well as capabilities at an advanced stage of development into a pre-operational network providing a range of analysis support information. The procurement will be structured into three periods as follows:Step[BJ1] 1:requirements consolidation and initial operating capability specification, implementation and testing.Step 2 initial capability demonstrations under realistic operating conditions covering extended routine threat mitigation, timely detection, characterization and response elaboration for emerging threats and anomaly/event response situationsStep 3: extended capability demonstration under fully representative conditions as agreed in the milestone review concluding Step 2 activities All underlying Information and Communication Technology (ICT) functions will be provided by the ERS-EO Element 1 Testbed.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF AN ELECTRO-DYNAMIC SHIELD SYSTEM FOR PLANETARY MISSIONS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop an Electro-Dynamic-Shield system to mitigate systems degradation for missions to the Moon, Mars and planetarybodies including a significant dusty environment.Description: Exploration systems in contact with planetary surfaces covered in regolith such as the Moon and Mars are subject to local dust displacement and accumulation on critical surfaces affecting system performance as for instance thermal balance, power generation efficiency and optical transmission and system lifetime. A number of mitigation strategies have been put forward and tested mostly on ground with a very limited demonstration in space. The Electro-Dynamic Shield (EDS) technology is a method used to mitigate the accumulation of dust on surfaces, particularly in space environments. This technology employs electric fields to repel dust particles, preventing them from settling on critical surfaces such as solar panels, sensors, and other equipment. This technology has been studied for more than twenty years outside of Europe for the mitigation of dust deposition on terrestrial and space system and it has been recently demonstrated on the Moon. In Europe, most of the studies performed so far have been on laboratory scale. Among others, an experimental EDS was successfully implemented on a number of samples including optical glass and Kapton sheets and demonstrated very high dust removal efficiency in a vacuum environment including UV, showing good potential for targeted system feasibility studies. Based on this success, the feasibility of implementing such technology on actual space hardware by breadboarding and testing critical functionalities can be addressed. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define the requirements for the implementation of an EDS system into relevant spacecraft structures and materials of interest with a priority towards solar arrays (with possible applicability to optical surface and other materials) and define the requirements from the target system towards EDS. - Assess the required modifications of standard designs to accommodate an EDS system, establish a list of technological gaps, define specific tests and a test plan to address the technological gaps. - Design and manufacture relevant breadboards to demonstrate EDS operational efficiency on targeted system. - Perform test for critical functionalities,including in representative laboratory environments (dusty vacuum and in presence of UV). - Based on the tests outcomes and future missions needs provide a technical roadmap with a cost outline.

title: TGO-MEX BISTATIC UHF RADAR STUDY - EXPRO+
description: Both TGO and MEX spacecraft are equipped with UHF radios, used for relaying data to and from landers. In certain geometries, UHF signals broadcasted from MEX are reflected from the martian surface before being received at TGO. In these cases, the received signal properties depend on the properties of the surface, in particular on the ice content of the surface and shallow (1m) subsurface.

title: HYDRON RESILIENCE: SECURITY ASPECTS OF NETWORKS INTEROPERABILITY (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.240) EXPRO+
description: Objective:The objective of this study is to assess the feasibility of applying Common Criteria framework (or equivalent) to guarantee compatible security mechanisms with HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network).Targeted Improvements:To achieve security interoperability of HydRON with other networks with a clear protection profile definition in line with international standards.Description:Multiple constellations are expected to be developed in the coming years, addressing different applications, like navigation, Earth Observation and communications as well as defence. Each constellation will be optimized for the target application, in terms of technologies, coverage, but also security functions. The challenge, but also the opportunity is to make use of all the possible infrastructure to enhance coverage and resilience of these systems by the integration of optical communication security features like Low Probability to be detected or interfered (LPD/LPI).However, different users will have different protection profiles and thereforesecurity targets will differ between networks. The Common Criteria for Information Technology Security Evaluation (referred to as Common Criteria) is an international standard (ISO/IEC 15408) used to specify security functional and assurance requirements, to guarantee implementation and verification of the security features and it can be used as a baseline for the security analysis of different networks and interoperability of security levels.This activity shall define a set of protection profiles for different target users and identify the security targets for different networks. Taking HydRON as a baseline for communications, the activity shall consider additional, selected national or EC networks interconnected by optical links in space or with optical ground stations and ground networks.For such security interoperability, the activity will define the required security functions (confidentiality, integrity, availability, authentication, non-repudiation...) and achievable levels of assurance by the different space networks. For the sected networks, an analysis of the impact shall be performed for each of these security functions, including a preliminary assessment of vulnerabilities by different potential threat actors and its impact on the system. The feasibility of applying Common Criterialframework or similar framework for these networks shall be assessed. Additionally, the achievable level of protection by the different networks shall be provided as a draft catalogue, to be presented to potential users. The activity shall define initial access scenarios for Ministries of Defence (MODs) and Civil Security Entities to utilise the upcoming HydRON installation to conduct dedicated, potentially classified testingvalidating defencegrade security, resilience behaviours, and interoperability in realistic operational scenarios and providing inputs to preliminary vulnerability assessment analysing operational impacts of potential attacks.

title: WIDEBAND HIGHLY LINEAR AND EFFICIENT POWER AMPLIFIER MODULE ARCHITECTURE FOR 5G ACTIVE ANTENNA APPLICATION (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5C.543) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, develop and test wideband power amplifier module architectures that exhibithigh linearity and efficiency for active antenna covering asignificant portion of the Frequency Range 1 (FR1). The amplifier architectures must be capable of handling high crest factors, which are characteristic of the multi-carrierwaveforms proposed in 5G New Radio. The module should include the complete power amplifier chipset with housing and interfaces to beamforming network and phasedarray with flexible dynamic power control.TargetedImprovements: Enabling wideband power amplifiers (700 2700 MHz), with at least 30% Power Added Efficiency (PAE).Description: The waveform and modulation schemes used in 5G New Radio (NR) aim to provide spectral efficiency, high data throughput, and resilience required for terrestrial 5Gcommunications. Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) offers good spectral efficiency whilst providing resilience to selective fading, however such multi-carriertechniques introduce a high Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR), which has a major impact on the efficiency of the RF Power Amplifiers (PA) as thelinear operation requireslarge output back-off. Conventional satellite power amplifier architectures without efficiency enhancement techniques can impact the power added efficiency (PAE) of thepower amplifier front-end, due to the required Output Back-Off (OBO)toachieve the desired linearity. For the OFDM waveform the amplifiers are typically operated at 6 to 8 dBOBO to achieve the desired linearity, Noise Power Ratio (NPR), and Error Vector Magnitude (EVM). This represents a major hurdle in the application of 5G NR foron-boardamplifiers with high PAPR.This activity will investigate novel PA architectures that can operate over a significant portion of the FR 1 band (i.e. from 700 to 2700 MHz), with a PAE greater than 30% andmeeting the linearity requirements. Several highlinearity and efficiency RF power amplifiers technologies and architectures will need to be investigated for the benefit of theefficiency enhancement techniques and shall be evaluated, simulated, and demonstrated at the Engineering Model level. At least two potential architectures with optimumtechnology shall be selected, designed, developed and tested to demonstrate the RF performance improvements with OFDM waveforms and their application to active antennaarrays for 5G payloads. Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: AI-POWERED AUTONOMOUS SATELLITES FOR THREAT DETECTION AND MITIGATION (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 3D.038) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective is to develop and validate an AI-powered autonomous satellite system capable of real-time threat detectionand mitigation targeting LEO constellations. This will reducereliance on ground-based monitoring and improve resilience in satellite operations.TargetedImprovements: - 50% improvement in real-time threat detection latency / delay over ground-based solutions.-60% reduction in response time using AI-initiated autonomous countermeasures.- Development of a simulator for cyber, RF and physical attacks, enabling validation of AI-based countermeasure/mitigation solutionsintroducing a novel capability in ESA MS.Description: Current satellite security solutions depend on ground-based infrastructure for threat detection and mitigation, introducing latency and operational risks. Traditional security mechanismsare static, rely on predefined protocols, and lack adaptability, making them ineffective against sophisticated, evolving threat scenarios.This activity will develop an AI-powered Autonomous Satellite Systemfor real-time cyber threat detection and mitigation. By leveraging AI-driven intrusion detection and automatedresponse mechanisms,the system will enable LEO satellites to autonomously identify, analyse, and counter cyber threats without reliance on ground intervention.Edge computing will facilitate real-time adaptive security policies, ensuring rapid response to attacks while significantlyimproving system resilience.To evaluate the concept, the activity will develop a reference cybersecurity architecture, incorporating an AI-powered intrusion detection engine, automated countermeasure execution,and simulation frameworks for cyberattack modellingand mitigation testing. The system will be deployed and validated using a FlatSat testbed, an attack simulator to model, test, andrefine simulated cyber-attack scenarios, and a simulator for the Inter-satellite link to validate real-time threat mitigation in context of satellite constellation. The simulator environmentshall be capable to analyse and validate AI-driven mitigation strategies across multiple simulated orbital assets in a constellation. Furthermore, the attack simulator model shall analyseand benchmark threat mitigation techniques for additional RF and/or physical threat scenarios.The expected outputs include a functional FlatSat testbed, an AI-driven intrusion detection engine for autonomous response to cyber and signal interference threats, and a simulationenvironment to model, test, and refine specific attack scenarios.

title: L4 ENCELADUS ICY SURFACE MODEL DEVELOPMENT - EXPRO+
description: Develop an Enceladus Icy Surface model to support the de-risking of lander architectureand landing approach surface sample collectionDescription.In preparation for the L4 mission to Enceladus, the knowledge of the physical compositionand mechanical strength properties of the icy surface is of high importance to ensure asuccessful landing and sample collection.However current understanding of the Enceladus surface environment is limited.This activity shall include at a minimum the following tasks:- Review of an internal ESA Enceladus Icy surface model- Review of plume/environment models either from ongoing TDE activity (ESA AO/1-12241/25/NL/CRS/my) or other state-of-art models, which would include snow depositionmaps and temperature maps.- Create/update Enceladus Icy Surface model.- Monte-carlo simulations of the parameter space of the surface models a (e.g. location,precipitation rates, temperature ranges, thermal inertia)The Enceladus Icy surface model shall be able to predict the local surface conditions tosupport the landing and guide the design of sample collection mechanisms.E.g. the model shall account for the surface deposition rate from the plumes, sintering ofthe snow column, depending e.g. on the local subsurface temperature gradients. Themodel shall be able to estimatethe snow strength as a function of latitude and longitude values around the south pole. Additionally snow buildup and sintering around local topology variations (e.g. crevasses and boulders) shall be assessed.

title: INTEGRATED MULTIPLEXER FOR HYBRID SATCOM/TERRESTRIAL 6G USER TERMINALS IN FREQUENCY RANGE 3 (FR3) (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7A.081) EXPRO+
description: The objective of the activity is to design, build, and test a wideband multiplexer breadboard supporting 6G Non-Terrestrial-Networks (NTN) in FR3.Targeted Improvements:Enabling building block for hybrid terrestrial/Satcom 6G services.Description: In the frame of 6G developments, the network infrastructure will evolve towards a higher level of integration between the terrestrial network (TN) and the non-terrestrial network (NTN), with unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) satellites playing a significant role in extending coverage and offloading traffic.Frequency Range 3 (FR3) spanning from 7 GHz to 24 GHz, has emerged as a new development area for 6G communications. The spectrum potentially allocated to mobile service on a primary basis includes 7.145 8.5, 10 13.25, 14.3 15.35, 17.7 19.7, and 21.2 23.6 GHz, accumulating in an aggregate bandwidth of approximately 9 GHz. For such systems, a multiband and highly integrated multiplexer would be a key component to enable multiple RF (Radio Frequency) chains to share a common antenna aperture for terminals communicating with both TN/NTN. This feature is particularly attractive in the implementation of hybrid User Terminals for 6G, where up to five bands need to be separated.This activity will develop a wideband multiplexer breadboard using advanced RF filtering and packaging techniques, enabling hybrid terrestrial/satcom 6G NTN services within the same antenna aperture. A review of multiplexing techniques suitable for wideband operation (covering as a minimum the 7 - 24 GHz frequency range) will be carried out with emphasis on filter and multiplexing techniques compatible with monolithic circuit integration,multimode single filter, Air-Filled Substrate Integrated Waveguide, or metamaterials.The activity will trade off and select at least one application scenario (e.g. direct-to-device (D2D), UAVs-supported satellite backhauls) and will produce the detailed design ofa breadboard (5 channels minimum) based on the selected application scenario.Finally, the multiplexer breadboard will be manufactured and tested. The activity shall seek synergies with ongoing flat-panel antenna developments and studies which are outside the scope of this activity. Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSIs isrequested.
