title: HIGH ISOLATION SINGLE APERTURE TRANSMIT-RECEIVE KA-BAND FLAT PANEL ANTENNA TO ENABLE FULL-DUPLEX OPERATION - EXPRO+
description: Objective: Enabling full duplex operation for Ka-band satcom terminals based on single Tx/Rx radiating aperture flat panel antennasby providing high isolation between the transmit and receive ports.Description: Satcom terminals at Ku or Ka based on single Tx/Rx aperture typically provide half duplex services, which reduces the available data rate. To enable full-duplex operation, high isolation between the Tx and Rx chains has to be implemented. While significant advancements in satcom terminal technologiesparticularly flat panel antennas with single aperture for transmit and receivehave been made outside Europe, the availability of such technologies in Europe remains limited. The activity focuses on the on the definition and implementation of development of a flat panel antenna operating in the SATCOM Ka band based on a single transmit and receive shared aperture, providing sufficient isolation between the Tx and Rx ports to enable full-duplex operation. The transmit and receive chains function at different frequencies. Therefore, a radiating aperture supporting both frequency bands will have to be designed. The isolation between the Tx and Rx ports will have to be provided at antenna element and/or feeding line level. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Consolidation of the requirements, - Trade-off analysis among several solutions and identification of the most promising antenna configuration, - Design and detailed analysis, - Manufacture and testing of a representative simplified antenna Breadboard

title: EARTH UPPER ATMOSPHERE FORECAST TOOL FOR MISSION DESIGN AND OPERATIONS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a software for VLEO atmospheric environment models that could reduce mission design margins and risks of satellite loss by non-compensated atmospheric drag effects at low altitudes.Description: Atmospheric density increase during geomagnetically active periods is a well know phenomenon. However, the increase of atmospheric density is not well-constrained and predictableand becomes particularly troublesome for the early phases of spacecraft commissioning that rely on a very low altitude (e.g. 200 to300 km) initial orbit. To date, for general spacecraft design purposes, the ESA Space Environment Information System (SPENVIS) includes various Earth atmosphere and wind models, some of which also consider geomagnetic activity. Several upper-atmosphere co-exist butthere are no comprehensive model or database of atmospheric and thermospheric parameters allowing to capture intra- (local time, seasonal, solar and magnetospheric inputs-driven) and inter-model variabilities, in order to derive better informed engineering margins. In such context, the proposed activity aims to fill that gap by developing a software allowing to interrogate models and definevariability envelopes based on major variability drivers (e.g. solar events, seasonal effects etc.) useful for design and exploitationphases. Software outputs shall feed the existing Space Weather modelling network with relevant products. In addition, the activity will establish a method to build model-based, time-dependent, 3D atmospheric parameter snapshots in order to produce a database of relevant parameters (at least species densities, temperatures as a function of altitude), including variabilities over different timescales relevant to mission design and planning (e.g. daily to seasonal) as a function of local time and latitude. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Review the existing state of the art models of the upper atmosphere, including preferably couplingeffects between the thermosphere / ionosphere system and solar inputs, as well as state of the art (e.g. ML based) methods allowingto capture atmospheric variability and temporal evolution as a function of external forcing (e.g. solar activity). - Define LEO/VLEO user and software requirements definition, including interfacing with relevant Space Weather tools and databases, and the capability toevolve as updated models and data become available. - Concept design, and a preliminary architecture design. - Develop and test critical functions to validate the approach. - Consolidate the design, full implementation and testing of the software. - Validatethe software by using independent data where possible and inter-models comparisons.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: HIGH CADENCE AUTONOMOUS SPACE-PLANES: FAST-TRACK TO ORBIT - EXPRO+
description: To consolidate next generation re-usable spaceplane configurations through a multidisciplinary analysis and optimization architecture.Description: Various configurations of reusable transportation systems have been investigated and are presently being deployed,mainly based on classical launcher architectures, based on liquid rocket engines and cylindrical layouts. Next generation vehicle architectures being investigated exploit the ascent and descent through the atmosphere as lift generating spaceplanes. The flight vehicle architecture should target full reusability and make use of the atmosphere to cross it back-and-forth in an efficient, fast, reliable and safe way similar to airplanes nowadays. To achieve a design capable of fulfilling all those requirements, a review of paststudies shall identify space planes configuration with a sufficient aerodynamic efficiency (L/D>4) to optimize ascent and gliding descent for reusability. At least two types of space-planes configurations are aimed to be analysed based upon advanced propulsion techniques, i.e. detonation and airbreathing based propulsion and assessed in sufficient detail. The multi-disciplinary design analysis and optimization (MDAO) architecture for co-design of aero-thermal-mechanical-propulsion-GNC system of hypervelocity flight vehicles) should take advantage of latest advances in parallel computing and AI techniques, and be able to link both highly specialized sub-system COTS software as well as newly developed simplified performance models to allow both detailed and fast iterations and trade-offs. This will be supported by experimental wind tunnel testing (WTT) campaign for validation and calibration. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Aeroshape review and optimization through MDAO with exploitation first of computational fluid dynamicsand engineering tools, and then injecting WTT results; - System conceptual design and mechanical justification with Finite ElementMethod (FEM) and Treed Meta-Model (TMM) models of respectively airframe and TPS - Aeroshape characterization through (cold) trisonic wind tunnel testing with ad-hoc models for the critical mission phases (take-off/ascent phase, fly-back and down-range landing) - Aeroshape aerodynamic database synthesis - Mission and trajectory analysis - Flight mechanics performances assessment - GNC needs definition and identification of system-level impacts - Definition of a development roadmap: conceptual definition of testing effort forin-flight verification and validation in supersonic, transonic and subsonic regime.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: EOGB JUL 25 / JUN 26 - EARTH OBSERVATION GRAPHIC BUREAU SERVICES AT ESRIN
description: The ESA Earth Observation Programme Directorate (EOP) carries out a range of promotional activities that are specifically targeted to support its dialogue with its science and user communities and to increase awareness and utilisation of Earth Observation data within the wider society. This user community includes thousands of Earth Observation scientists and application developers worldwide,a large number of national, regional and international public sector user organisations, many specialised value-adding service companies and their clients, as well as universities and schools. Alongside this target, as above-mentioned, also the general public hasbecome an important audience, e.g. there is a wide interest in space for earth/space for climate topics across EO programmes.The responsibilities of EOP related to projects that use data from ESA Earth Observation missions include: Collecting, synthesizing, reporting, and presenting the results achieved in the ESA EO programs for different audiences, from scientific communities to the general public interface, along with the members of the application and research community. Promoting achievements and ongoing work related to Earth Observation at international, European, and National level, in particular via dedicated workshops and conferences, each of which requires totes, exhibition panels, posters, flyers, foldable programmes, etc.The Earth Observation Directorate also provides a regular flow of specialized Earth Observation promotional, graphical materials and relevant communication activities to the ESA Corporate Communications Department. These materials are subsequently re-used and integrated within ESA's corporate communication campaigns and channels, which are specifically targeted towards the press, social media and for the general public. The Earth Observation Directorate therefore needs to generate a significant volume of EO- specific, high-quality graphics, promotion, multi-mediaand web materials/contents, varying from simple graphics and animations to complex website, multimedia publications, and videos, upto augmented and virtual reality experiences. Communication content primarily derives from EO Missions, and from EO science and application RD projects carried out under ESA EO programs.The collection, maintenance and promotion of these results and informationsets require regular generation and integration of high-quality communication products with scientific and technical material. For the generation of these materials ESA must be capable of incorporating a range of attributes, including design, content, and layout for a variety of media, and addressing different audience levels and categories. The Contractor shall provide a Graphic Bureau service that includes: A Routine Graphic Design service satisfying requests for the development of standard multimedia material (e.g.posters, totems, desk banners, roll-ups, cover pages, key visuals, badges, web/social media graphics), supporting the conversion ofscientific and technical raw material into attractive graphical outreach material, in support to exhibits, conferences, workshops, symposia and for any other promotion and communication opportunity. This service shall include a electronic library allowing users to reuse past approved productions in self-service mode.Support to Special projects and related approval workflows for the work types requiring a dedicated effort evaluation (e.g. videos, 3D animation, augmented reality, interactive PDFs, brochures). These work types are less frequent may have very variable effort. Therefore it is not considered feasible to define a standard fee, instead a custom price will have to be defined for each single request and approved via an automated workflow.

title: ECODESIGN HARNESS FOR SPACE APPLICATIONS -EXPRO+
description: Objective: To design and assess the life cycle of an optimised harness including cables, connectors, and back-shell components, allmanufactured using eco-friendly processes and alternative materials.Description: Spacecraft harnesses are essential for power distribution, data transmission, and signal integrity within satellites and other spacecraft systems. However, conventional harness designs rely on materials and manufacturing techniques that have a significant environmental impact, such as PTFE (Polytetrafluoroethylene)-based insulation, gold and nickel plating, and energy-intensive production processes. The ecodesign harness initiative focuses on the development of a sustainable harness architecture, incorporating alternative materials and environmentally optimised production methods. This includes innovative approaches to conductors, insulation, jacket, connectors, accessories, tie bases, assembly processes and integration, all tailored for space qualification. This activity aims to minimise environmental impact while maintaining space-grade reliability and performance, contributing to the broader vision of sustainable space through responsible material selection, reduced emissions, and improved end-of-life strategies. A comprehensive life cycle assessment (LCA) will be performed to comparethe environmental impacts of the optimised harness against conventional designs, from raw material extraction through to end-of-life,including phases such as manufacturing, integration, launch, and decommissioning. title: GNC SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE FOR PARAFOIL FLIGHT WIND KNOWLEDGE FUSION EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a robust, adaptive guidance framework for parafoil-based recovery systems based on the fusion of wind data from both ground-based measurements and onboard sensors.Description: Parafoil-based recovery systems offer a lightweight, low-cost, and reusable solution for space re-entry and payload delivery. They require advanced GNC strategies to achieve precise and reliable landings in highly dynamic atmospheric conditions. Their aerodynamic controllability and passive deployment make them suitable for various missions. However, achieving precise landings in real-world conditions remains challenging due to atmospheric variability, especially wind, which introduces uncertainty in trajectory prediction and landing dispersion. Accurate and timely wind knowledge is therefore not just a helpful input, but a critical enabler of parafoil performance and reliability. Current GNC systems often treat wind as a disturbance, relying on conservative margins or reactive filtering. This limits system performance, increases landing footprints, and misses opportunities for optimization. Crucially, there is a gap in the systematic use of wind dataforecasted, sensed, or inferredin guidance and navigation design. This activity addresses that gap with a GNC architecture that treats wind knowledge asa core element, integrated by design into both preflight planning and onboard adaptation. By continuously adjusting to atmospheric variations, this approach aims to enhance landing accuracy and improve system robustness to weather conditions. This activity explores wind-aware GNC through two synergistic layers: (1) ground-based wind profiling and forecasting for mission planning, and (2) onboard sensing and virtual estimation to refine wind knowledge in-flight. By fusing this data into navigation filters and adaptive guidance laws, the system dynamically adjusts trajectories, reduces dispersion, and exploits beneficial wind structures. This leads to more accurate and resilient landings. The output will be a modular GNC software prototype, validated in Monte Carlo simulations, and designed for future TRL scaling. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define GNC architecture, wind data levels, simulation environment, and test interfaces. - Develop wind estimation (onboard sensors, virtual sensing), integrate with navigation filters. - Design adaptive guidance using wind input, implement real-time trajectory updates. - Integrate full GNC stack, simulate full missions, and evaluate robustness to wind variability in a representative simulation environment.

title: N2O SATELLITE OBSERVATION REQUIREMENTS - EXPRO PLUS
description: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is an important greenhouse gas that also contributes to stratospheric ozone depletion. This study aims at characterising the needs for space-based observations of atmospheric N2O, starting from a user and science perspective. Knowledge gaps are identified related to the N2O production and life cycle, its impact on stratospheric ozone, and its role in the Earth's radiation balance that can be addressed with the help of satellite observations, with a focus on information that can be provided from satellite observations. The study explores the space of requirements that satellite observations of atmospheric N2O (Level-2) and measurements of radiances at the top of the atmosphere (Level-1) would have to meet in order to contribute to addressing these knowledge gaps.

title: WAVEFORM SIMULATOR FOR POLARIMETRIC RADAR ALTIMETERS EXPRO+
description: Data of the ground-based dual-frequency fully polarized Ku- and Ka-band radar "KuKa" from the MOSAiC Arctic expedition and Antarctic sea ice measurements in the Weddell Sea suggest a clear relationship between cross-polarized radar echo waveforms and snow depth. However, cross-polarized radar altimetry echo waveforms models and simulators that describe this effect are not available. Furthermore, a mature analytical framework to describe these observations with a physical model is not available. Such a tool is required to explore how sensitive cross-polarized echo waveforms are to different snow properties and instrument and geometry parameters.For the simulation of the cross-polarized echo waveforms, the Snow Microwave Radiative Transfer model (SMRT) offers a promising candidate. The SMRT is a framework in active community development and includes different electromagnetic theories, representations of snow microstructure, and other modules at various calculations steps that can be combined. In recent years, also the "nadir_altimetry" solver was added to the SMRT framework to allow for co-polarized radar altimeter waveform generation.The objective of this activity is to develop, implement and validate a cross-polarized radar altimeter waveform model inside the framework of the SMRT and to analyse the polarisation sensitivity in dependence of different instrument, geometry and scene parameters.To achieve this, the Contractor shall implement multi-scattering functionalities into the altimeter solver of SMRT. Further, the Contractor shall implement waveform simulations of ground- and airborne-based radar altimeters. After implementation and validation with real data, the Contractor shall use SMRT to perform simulations of representative scenarios of ground-based, airborne-based and satellite-based instruments in dependence of different snowpack parameters.

title: SECONDARY HEAT EXCHANGER FOR COMBUSTION CHAMBER COOLING OF ROCKET ENGINES - EXPRO+
description: The objective of this activity is to develop a cooling approach for steady state rocket engines to enable the use of more cost-effective materials. This should be achieved with the use of secondary heat exchange.Currently only two cooling approaches are used forrocket motor chamber design. Direct regenerative cooling with the propellants or much simpler radiative cooling. Regenerative cooling recovers energy lost in the radiative approach and offers both higher performance and, wider material options which is possible due to the lower operating temperature.Regenerative cooling is almost never limited by the sensible enthalpy, the temperature rise of the cooling propellants. It is typically limited by local effects in the cooling channel design. These effects come down to two factors the local geometry and the local vapor pressure of the coolant. The geometry is naturally constrained by the need for a rocketchamber shape.In the absence of local geometric options then the local vapor pressure can only be improved for a given propellant by driving up the local static pressure. This rules out many in-space applications where gas pressurized feed systems are the norm, the static pressure is too low. The power for high pressure pumps to regeneratively cool current spacecraft engines would require pumps more than 1.5 kWs. An alternative approach is to design a heat exchanger to transfer the heat from the wall of the combustion chamber to propellant indirectly. This has the advantage of allowing the design of specified cooling rates independent of the geometryor propellant feed conditions. Either end of the exchanger can be designed to operate at specified temperatures. This simplifies the material selection of the chamber and the transfer of energy to the propellant.A fixed temperature exchanger would have none of the limiting factors of a classical regeneratively cooled chamber. It could also simplify start up transient for many larger engine cycles. The more benign operating conditions would also allow for greater reusability; thermal gradients could be more tightly managed and more robust materials could be used, eliminating issues such as plasticity and deformations of the cooling channels. As statedearlier local conditions drive the failure in regenerative engines these are compounded when the engine flow conditions are dynamicwhen throttling. Lander engines tend to require deep throttle rates. Secondary heat exchangers operate outside these constraints and would maintain thermal integrity of deeper throttling designs. Similarly higher performance engine architectures such as aerospikes are inhibited from adoption due to the thermal complexity ofimplementing them compared to classical designs. Various ideas have been considered; however liquid metals are only one potential solution. Active pumping of a secondary coolant would also be feasible.This activity shall focus on the concept of secondary heat exchange design for high performance engine design and demonstrate a secondary heat exchanger unit by firing a representative breadboard. This would allow a greater exploitation of the propellant sensibleenthalpy than current regenerative approaches. In addition, secondary heat exchange would allow low pressure drop designs and enable actively cooled design applications where currently radiative cooling is mandated. Finally secondary heat exchange would allow theenergy to be exploited in other systems if required: repressurization, power recovery, etc. The activity encompasses the following tasks: Analysis of the state of the art of secondary heat exchanger options for combustion chamber applications. Develop and manufacture a breadboard of a secondary heat exchanger for combustion chamber. Demonstrate a secondary heat exchanger for combustion chamber design by firing a representative breadboard with heat exchanger or an appropriatesimulator. Validate the design tools toimplement such a chamber.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation offinancial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: DISTRIBUTED ARRAY END-TO-END PAYLOAD SYSTEM ARCHITECTURES FOR PNT - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop innovative end-to-end payload system architectures, techniques and algorithms enabling large distributed arrays for PNT based on high-gain beamforming.Description: Large arrays of antennas and distributed arrays of antennas are being considered for the generation of very high-gain beamforming. In this case, the main objective is to achieve a high received power by the ground user receivers, such that high data rates can be supported per user. Large and distributed arrays can be considered for PNT, both for Earth and Spaced Service Volume users and applications. One clear expected advantage would be to achieve much larger received power on the user receivers than with current GNSS systems. This can be of interest in particular in harsh propagation conditions, including the presence of interference and jamming, or to reach very far-away space users/assets. The objective of this activity is to design techniques and algorithms to enable large distributed array satellite and payload (PL) system architectures/configurations for PNT. The focus will be on the generation of very high-gain beamforming, while ensuring the transmission of high-accuracy signals-in-space, even when wide-band signals are used. Both the transmission in L-band (reference) and alternative bands (e.g., S and Cbands) will be addressed. Additionally, the activity will investigate innovative ideas for the exploitation of the large distributedarray architecture for PNT purposes, leveraging concepts and operational modes exploited in other space applications like SyntheticAperture Radar (SAR) systems. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition and design of innovative techniques and algorithms in the areas identified above; - Implementation of the required tools/software enabling the assessment of the proposed techniques and algorithms; - Assessment/test of the different techniques and algorithms in simulated conditions; - Identification of themost promising techniques/algorithms based on the results obtained; - Definition of the proposed the way-forward to further matureeach of the promising techniques/algorithms identified.Deliverables: Report, SoftwareProcurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. title: METHODOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK AND ORGANISATIONAL SUPPORT FOR ESA STRATEGIC INITIATIVES AND STRATEGY 2040 IMPLEMENTATION
description: ESA has established Strategy 2040 as the guiding framework for the long-term evolution of the Agency. Strategy 2040 defines a clearset of overarching goals to: protect our planet and climate, explore and discover, strengthen European autonomy and resilience, boost growth and competitiveness, and inspire Europe. These goals guide the preparation of ESA programmes and underpin Council Ministerial (CM) cycles, which occur on a 3-year basis, ensuring that future investments respond to societal needs, scientific ambition, andindustrial priorities. Within ESA, the Strategy Department is responsible for the strategic development of ESA and for coordinatingthe CM cycle at Agency level. In this role, it ensures coherence between long-term strategic objectives, programme preparation, andevolving Member States priorities, while promoting cross-directorate alignment and strategic direction.In this context, ESA is seekingto strengthen the implementation of Strategy 2040 through targeted innovation and action that support the alignment and evolution of ESA programmes, including through the preparation of new activities. To support this effort, ESA has established the new StrategicInitiatives activity, a collaborative framework and structured process to accelerate the rollout of new, high-potential initiatives.

title: PROPAGATION MODELS FOR THE CLUTTER LOSS IN FREQUENCY SHARING ANALYSIS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop propagation models and improve their applicability for clutter loss on terrestrial and Earth-space paths to frequency sharing methods used by ESA and European frequency managers.Description: The development of terrestrial 5G systems has ledto the developments and updates of propagation models for what regards the effect of clutter on interference with space services andwith other Earth stations. The initial development done in ITU-R SG3 and in past TDE activities (ref. no. T507-601EF) focused in frequency bands used by passive EO missions, and by Earth stations for Space exploration and EO data downlink. These models are used for radio regulation frequency sharing analyses to determine the compatibility of services using radio spectrum. The frequency sharing analyses have specific needs, stemming from the considered system configuration (e.g. use of active antennas, coverage area etc.)On the other hand, clutter models can be relatively complex, as they depend on several system and stochastic parameters (e.g. frequency, elevation angle, height of the ground transmitter, characteristics of the clutter environment etc.). Therefore there is the needto improve clutter propagation models and to define their usage in to frequency sharing methods. To address this, this activity improves clutter loss models and defines the methods and the requirements for their use by frequency management engineers in system simulations to assess the compatibility of different radio services of the radio regulations and to perform the respective studies. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - State-of-the-art review and development plan, - Clutter model improvement and implementation, - Design and Implementation of system simulation for test-cases for sharing analyses, - Execution and analysis of test cases- Inputs for radio regulations and Conclusions Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access to it and can provide update to the community of users.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: ENHANCEMENT OF THE PHASE SPACE DENSITY OF LASER COOLED NEUTRAL STRONTIUM ATOMIC SYSTEMS - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop a system enhancement in the cold atom production rate, and reduction of the thermodynamic temperature, of atomic Strontium (Sr), using novel Magneto Optical Trap (MOT) laser cooling techniques and technologies. DescriptionThe availability of an efficient and simplified system to generate a laser cooled Sr sample, in large atom numbers at low temperature, is a key driver and project enabler for both laboratory systems and field deployable systems and those for space deployment. Laser cooled atoms are an essential resource for ultra-high stability Optical Atomic Frequency Standard (OAFS) and specifically for Sr, using the quantum forbiddenelectronic transition at 698nm. These optical systems have demonstrated performance metrics (fractional frequency stability) which are orders of magnitude superior to their laser cooled RF counterparts. This opens up experimental possibilities that cannot be realised with RF systems. An Atom Interferometer, using clouds of laser cooled Sr atoms has also been proposed, and demonstrated, in a laboratory environment. Such an instrument can measure gravitational waves, in a frequency band not possible by LISA or the ground-based systems (LIGO, VIRGO etc).This activity shall serve as a development approach for both of above mentioned applications for future space implementations. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Analysis of system performance requirements and parameters leading to an OAFS and mater wave interferometry (MWI) implemented with neutral Sr - Theoretical analysis of neutral Sr atomic system and implementation of system modelling tools to explore the implementation possibilities- Develop several viable design options leading to a PDR- Trade off the design options based primarily on flux enhancement and thermodynamic temperature reduction anddesign simplification; leading to CDR - Develop manufacturing, integration and test plan to verify the performance of a breadboardunit - Roadmap the development of the Sr MOT system for specific mission scenariosProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restrictedto non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: IMPLEMENTATION OF AN ESERO (EUROPEAN SPACE EDUCATION RESOURCE OFFICE) IN LITHUANIA
description: The European Space Education Resource Office (ESERO) is ESA's main project in the field of formal and non-formal early childhood, primary and secondary education. Under the coordination and steering of ESA and the national space agencies and offices, and with the support of national institutions and organizations active in the field of formal and non-formal education, the project aims at enabling capacity building in the school level teacher and educator communities and at designing and promoting the use of didactic resources and activities that make use of space as a context for the teaching and learning of STEM-related disciplines.National ESERO offices are established to implement activities across their hosting country. They are staffed by national education experts able to work in strong synergy and partnership with the national education authorities, stakeholders and networks, as well as the national space sector - an approach that has already proven to be effective and successful across 22 ESA Member States. In July 2026 a new ESERO will be established in an ESA Associate Member State - Latvia. Other countries have also now expressed interest in hosting an ESERO.

title: DYNAMICALLY ADAPTIVE SYSTEM ARCHITECTURAL MODEL FOR CONNECTIVITY GAP AREAS IN 4G AND 5G TERRESTRIAL NETWORKS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.048) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of this activity is to design, implement and evaluate different types of satellite system architectural models aimed at dynamically focusing available resources on coverage gaps in terrestrial 4G and 5G networks.Targeted Improvements:Achieving national regulator coverage and service objectives for direct-to-device services and enabling twice as efficient satellite resourcespooling over the service area.Description: Today there are coverage gaps of the terrestrial telecommunication system despite initiatives from non-European industries to provide supplementary coverage from space. Concentrating satellite connectivity exclusively on coverage gap areas (including low service areas) rather than aiming for satellite connectivity over a broad coverage has the potential to maximize the efficiency of the satellite system. It could offer an increased throughput which translates in reduced deployment costs per bit and higher quality of service for end users. Moreover, this approach could enable flexible resources allocation based on the population density as well as step up and step down of terrestrial connectivity services.This activity will design,implement and evaluate satellite system architectural models addressing non-uniform spatiotemporal traffic patterns in particular of handheld services. First, the activity will develop a high-resolution spatiotemporal traffic model, which shall consider available datasets and trend analyses of service requirements of Mobile Network Operators (MNOs) and their representative organisations, along with actual and target service coverage obligation set by National Regulation Administrations (NRAs) for terrestrial network gaps. The outputs of this model will be used to define coverage gaps from existing and planned terrestrial networks and space networks. The activity will then study and implement in a software prototype Distributed Satellite System (DSS) concepts for Frequency Range 1 (FR1) considering different orbits, multi-connectivity techniques (e.g. beam overlapping, coordinated multi-point etc) and infrastructure configurations (e.g. fractionated, swarm and federated concepts). System sizing optimizing the satellite resources will be carried out of at least 3 selected DSS concepts and the performance will be evaluated by simulation. The activity shall identify the most promising DSS concept and development roadmap considering complexity and system performance and the ability to accommodateopportunities beyond direct to device services. title: EMBEDDING AT SCALE - EXPRO+
description: Generating embeddings for large-scale EO datasets involves significant engineering considerations: data must be efficiently pre-processed, batched, and passed through embedding models, often in HPC and other distributed systems capable to handle millions or billions of inputs. In EO, data formats, data projections, data storage and data retrieval are critical, requiring optimized techniques and tools to maintain performance and scale embedding generation to regional and global scale. In addition, ensuring generated embeddings are usable for a wide range of downstream applications and are coherently updated when new EO data is acquired are other key challenges. Several efforts in the past, such as work performed with MajorTOM in the ESA -lab, showed how these challenges can be an important limitation for scaling embeddings and AI models and ultimately fully utilize the vast amount of Earth Observation data acquired by ESA and non-ESA missions. The objective of this activity is to develop technologies, methods and tools required to establish a system capable of generating, retrieving and utilizing embeddings at regional and global scale from multimodal EO data (e.g., Sentinel missions at different product levels, VHR data, SAR data...). The activity final aim is to unlock new large-scale capabilitiesnd support the generation and utilization of embeddings of massive EO datasets for downstream application, with the final goal to democratize access to EO data, making it more usable and accessible for users with limited computational resources.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF SERIALIZER AND DESERIALIZER IP CORE FOR ULTRA DEEP SUB MICRON TECHNOLOGIES
description: To develop a Serializer and Deserializer IP Core, without any access restriction for European Industry, to provide a low power HighSpeed Serial Link up to 56GbpsDescription: Most of the required functionalities for the future space components such as processors, accelerators, routers, analog/digital converters will be developed within the GSTP activity GTE3-101ED "Ultra Deep Sub-Micron - Foundation and Platform Technology".The High Speed Serial Link (HSSL) is one of the key functionalities required for the next generation of space components that could not be included in the GTE3-101ED. Due to the importance to provide this functionality in a timely manner, this dedicated activityhas been defined with the aim to develop a Serializer and Deserializer (SERDES) IP Core to enableHSSL to at least 32Gbps and up to 56Gbps.This IP Core will support the different HSSL protocols used in space like SpaceFibre, Ethernet, PCIe, JESD204. Specifically the HSSL IP Core will be compliant to the newer PCIe 5.0 and Ethernet802.3cd link operation. TheHSSL IP Core will support power efficient operation both for short range as well as long range applications (two optimized implementations might be considered). The outcome of this activity shall be made available whenever required with concomitant activities, and in particular the GTE3- 101ED and shall be made accessible for future developments ofEuropean space products.The activity encompasses the following tasks :- Identify the space component requiring SERDES IP Core and targeted UDSM technology and foundry- Determine the HSSL requirement specifications and suitable commercial SERDES IP Core design- Perform Radiation test of selected HSSL in the targeted UDSM technology- Design radiation harden HSSL IP Core with improvedperformances- Validate the HSSL IP Core functionalities and performances on test vehicles, including radiation hardened operation- Demonstrate compliant operation on optimised and corrected design- Perform functional ESCC testing, characterization, andevaluation- Make the HSSL IP Core available and support the integration into the activity GTE3-101ED- Package the HSSL IP Core for use into future developments Deliverables include SERDES IP Core, Simulation model files, samples of the test chips and documentation as per applicable Standard for IC development, tailoredas required for the development of reusable IP.

title: COTS PYROTECHNICS INITIATOR, SQUIB AND DETONATOR BREADBOARD
description: Objective:To develop a space-qualified pyrotechnic initiator based on a COTS and to demonstrate its integrationwithin the associated subsystems required for the qualification of the squib and detonator configurations.Description:This activity addresses the development of space-compatible pyrotechnic devices, through the adaptationof a Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) initiator. Its objective is to transform an existing COTS initiatorinto a connectorized initiator suitable for space applications, including both launchers and spacecraft. Thework focuses on design adaptation, system integration, and functional demonstration under spacerelevantenvironmental and interface constraints, with the goal of reducing technical risk and increasingthe technology's maturity toward future space qualification and flight adoption.Given the criticality of this activity qualification, requirements for satellites and launchers will be furtherconsolidated with satellites and Launcher primesThe following tasks shall be executed:- Assess the requirements for Launchers and Spacecraft- COTS Initiator Assessment and Selection- Design Adaptation a Space Initiator- Develop the Squib Assembly (Initiator + Booster) - [Squibs are used on launchers and satellitesbecause of pyro-valve applications.]- Develop thedetonator Assembly (Initiator + Detonator cap)- Perform environmental and interface verification testing- Perform functional demonstration and Validation.Deliverables: Breadboard, reports

title: LARGE AREA AVALANCHE PHOTODIODE ARRAY FOR HIGH SIGNAL SWIR APPLICATIONS EXPRO PLUS (RE-ISSUE)
description: Objective: To develop prototype Avalanche Photodiode (APD) structures in an Mercury-Cadmium-Telluride (MCT) detection layer for high flux Earth Observation applications.Description: Hybrid infrared detectors, using a silicon Readout Integrated Circuit (ROIC) andMercury-Cadmium-Telluride (MCT) detection layer, are the gold standard for high performance optical systems in space. Recent demonstrations of Avalanche Photodiode (APD) technology in MCT layers opens up the possibility of signal magnification at the pixel level which reduces the effective readout noise. This can unlock performance improvements through an enhanced Signal-to-Noise ratio (SNR),or allow operation at equivalent SNR but with faster frame rates (reducing ground sampling distances, or allowing higher operating temperatures). Prototype APD structures in MCT material shall be designed and manufactured, and coupled to a high performance readout circuit suited for Earth Observation applications. Detailed electro-optic characterisation shall be performed, to compare to equivalent detectors manufactured with a standard MCT technology. The advantage/disadvantages of the technology shall be assessed for a range of EO applications. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Expected performance simulation for an Earth Observation ROIC operated with an APD detection layer - Design and manufacture of test samples with APD designs - Characterisation of device performance - Critical assessment of test results, including comparison to performance simulation and design expectations.

title: COMPETITIVE FRAME CONTRACT FOR GROUND SEGMENT ENGINEERING, MISSION OPERATIONS AND ENGINEERING SUPPORT SERVICES TO SPACE TRAFFIC (GOFX)
description: The subject of this procurement proposal is the Competitive Frame Contract for Ground Segment Engineering, Mission Operations and Engineering Support Services to Space Traffic (GOFX). This frame contract succeeds the current GOF9 frame contract following its termination at the end of 2026 and service provision will start in January 2027. The frame contract covers the procurement of industrialservices and deliverables at ESOC in the following domains: (1) Mission Operations Services including mission operations preparation and mission operations security, (2) Ground Operations Services including support to pre-launch activities in the areas of system configuration, integration and operations preparation, (3) Mission Operations IT and Operational Control Centre Services including the transformation and continuous evolution of the operational computer, communications, and control centre infrastructure as well the operational facilities, (4) Space Communication Engineering Services including development and evolution of R/F and optical systems as well as ground station (backend) systems and interoperable communications architectures, (5) System Application Engineering Services including mission data systems development and maintenance, end-to-end ground segment system engineering, and cybersecurity engineering , and (6) Engineering Support Services to Space Traffic including provisioning of products and services in the area of space debris. OPS depends on these industrial services for successful provision of mission operations and ground segment engineering support to institutional missions and third parties. The frame contract will be procured together with a set of initial work packages for each of the six domains.

title: DEPLOYABLE REFLECTOR FOR CUBE- AND SMALLSATS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To design, manufacture and test a 1m deployable offset fed reflector antenna for small/cube satellites suitable formissions up to Ka-band.Description:A strong need for deployable Ka-band high gain antennas for cubesat and small satellites for various applications (TTC, payload data downlink, black hole observation VLBI (very long baseline interferometry), rain/precipitation observation and more) has been identified, hence, the importance to develop this technology to further maturity, which is currently notavailable in Europe.The antenna to be developed is 1m (scalable up to 3m) diameter deployable reflector antenna in an offsetconfiguration (reduction of aperture blockage) suitable for missions up to Ka-band. An engineering model including the reflector, the boom and the feed will be manufactured and tested demonstrating the critical functions of the element in a relevant environment. The testing will include, as a minimum, surface accuracy measurement after deployment, deployment test in representative environment (TVAC), vibration tests, thermal cycling, RF performance tests, passive intermodulation (PIM) tests at sample level.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Preliminary design (including de-risking activities of new, modified or unmodified (re-used) modules with lower TRL and/or higher risk)- Detailed design (including de-risking activities of unmodified (re-used) modules with lower TRL and/or higher risk).- Antenna manufacture and integration.- Test campaign and development roadmap.

title: E4EX-022 LASER COMPONENT OF A DOPPLER LIDAR FOR MARTIAN WINDS - EXPRO+
description: This activity is to perform trade-offs and a risk-reduction design study for the laser component of a Doppler LIDAR for measuring, from a spacecraft in Mars orbit (via laser light scattered by atmospheric particles) the winds in the martian atmosphere. The main driver for this search is Signal-to-Noise Ratio of the returned signal and the consequent needs in terms of total optical output power (in the order of tens of mJ per pulse for each wavelength), shared between 1064 nm and 532 nm from the transmitting laser. Secondly, such a laser must be compact and designed for long-duration, high-duty cycle operation. The activity shall target TRL 3.

title: GNC TECHNOLOGIES FOR PRECISE LANDING OF LAUNCHER STAGE AND BOOSTER - EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop the GNC architecture and algorithms required to enable precise landing of launcher stages / booster with highthrust-to-weight ratio via accurate hover-slam maneuvering.Description: Recent developments in reusable launch systems have demonstrated the operational and economic advantages of recovering and reusing first-stage boosters and upper stages. However, the current state-of-the-art is limited to a small number of operators, and many of the underlying technologies, including GNC for precision propulsive landing of high thrust-to-weight ratio vehicles, remain at low TRL, in particular in Europe. Achieving pinpoint landing ischallenging due to restrictive throttling constraints and to tight dynamical couplings where there is no room for error: the required Thrust Vector Control (TVC) deflections are large and so is the drift they induce, the controllability offered by fins is limiteddue to the low velocities, and the vehicle is operating under uncertain conditions stemming from interactions such as plume impingement and ground effect. This activity will tackle these challenges by advancing GNC technologies for propulsive stages descent, trajectory shaping, terminal landing maneuvers and autonomous control. The following key enabling GNC functions will be developed as part of the study: - Descent Guidance Algorithms - Navigation filters based on multiple sensors fusion (e.g. altimeters, multiple IMUs,multiple GNSS antennas and receivers, strain gauges) - Control strategies and multiple-actuation architectures (TVC, fins, thrusters) - Autonomy functions (real-time decision-making, contingency handling, failure detection) The aims at investigating candidate GNCarchitectures and algorithms suitable for landing scenarios, considering as a minimum boosters and upper stages landing. This is critical to enable cost-effective and robust European solutions for reusable launchers in future missions. This activity encompassesthe following tasks: - Identify representative mission scenarios for vertical propulsive landing (hover-slam manoeuvre) - Define mission and system-level requirements for each scenario and vehicle - Develop modular GNC architectures - Model environmental dynamics (gravity, aerodynamics, wind) and vehicle dynamics (multi-body kinematics, flexible structures, sloshing) - Integrate GNC algorithms in a high-fidelity 6-DOF simulation framework - Perform trade studies on actuators and sensors, including sensitivity and robustness analysis - Validation and verification campaign of the selected GNC architectures and algorithms, including an evaluation of performance - Study synthesis and recommendations for a technology roadmap to increase TRL

title: T709-903GA SELF-HEALING ARCHITECTURES FOR CYBER RESILIENT GROUND SEGMENT SYSTEMS (EXPRO+)
description: Today, mission ground segment systems face increasingly sophisticated and fast-movingcyber threats that can evade static or rule-based detection tools and overwhelm traditionalrecovery procedures. As attacks grow more pervasive, dynamic and subtle, currentapproaches, such as rule-based or ticket driven responses struggle to react at the requiredspeed, resulting in prolonged attacker dwelltime and potential disruption of critical missionoperations, if an attack is detected at all.Real-time automated responses or self-healing' mechanisms, such as fall-back tosecure/minimum configurations, runtime policy/rule change, trusted state reconstitution, orrapid tear-down and re-deploy of compromised systems, can reduce the time required tocontain threats. The aim is to reduce attacker dwell time and maintain service continuityduring otherwise high impact incidents. This activity addresses that gap by developing anddemonstrating a proof-of-concept autonomous self-healing architecture tailored to thecritical mission operations ground segment. It will provide an adaptive resilience mechanismaddressing detection, isolation and recovery with an emphasis on service continuity. Moderntechnologies and techniques are to be explored including:- declarative infrastructure as code for cloud-agnostic redundancy and recovery automation- decoupled micro-service isolation and zero-trust architectures- secure root of trust and immutable system configuration restoration- failure prediction- adaptive response mechanisms leveraging machine learning.The proof-of-concept demonstrator will be integrated into a multi-mission, cloud nativeground segment scenario, leveraging existing (Cyber) Security Operations Centres((C)SOC) monitoring and diagnostic capabilities to ensure operational relevance. It willdemonstrate end to enddetection, isolation, and recovery in the context of missionmonitoring and control systems operating in the loop.

title: MULTI-LAYER/BAND PROPAGATION MODELS FOR GNSS EVOLUTIONS EXPRO PLUS - RE-ISSUE
description: To develop a consistent set of propagation models for multi-layer/multi-frequency GNSS that will allow to carry out user performance assessments related to RF signal propagation.Description:In the recent years, there has been an increasing interest on investigating new technologies that can be used to backup or complement existing GNSS for increased reliability and performance. Among others, these initiatives include the use of satellites in other orbits (beyond traditionally used MEO) and new bands below and above current Radio Navigation Satellite Service (RNSS) allocations. The benefits for the user segment are promising (e.g. indoor penetration with longer wavelengths, higher decorrelation due to faster satellite dynamics...) but require preliminary analysis for correct system design. Among other aspects, the modelling of the signal propagation conditions is an essential part of the final user ranging error.The definition of such a model is particularly challenging due to the different range of frequencies, different dynamics andforeseen GNSS signal evolution bandwidths. In addition, the use of new frequency bands for navigation, which were traditionally dedicated to other types of services, requires an update on the characterization of propagation effects, focusing on synchronization aspects. A clear example of this is the use of millimeter wave signals which could potentially bring several benefits to Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) users (terminal size, synergies with other systems...) but also impose some challenges such as higher propagation losses and sensitivity to obstacles. A better understanding of these new bands is essential for future system designs. While individual models for classical PNT bands and users exist with a high level of maturity, a framework to combine them in a consistent manner is missing, which limits the reliability on the estimated benefits of a multi-layer/frequency GNSS system. The activityencompasses the following tasks: - Providing a consistent software framework for the assessment of propagation effects in future GNSS including new frequency bands, beyond the current RNSS allocations and multiple types of orbit (from VLEO to GEO) in support of Signal in Space Performance assessments for PNT users.- Covering atmospheric losses using consolidated and standardised models- Covering multipath propagation and its impact on Time of Arrival estimation using a combined physicalstatistical approach for a more realistic characterisation of the local environment.- Providing interfaces to advanced hardware simulators for injection of channelrealizations for hardware receiver testing.- Submission of models to ITU-R for standardization.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: RECONFIGURABLE INTELLIGENT SURFACE OVER-THE-AIR TECHNOLOGY VALIDATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.040) EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to develop and implement over-the-air satellite system demonstrators that validate Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface technology developments in realistic conditionsTargeted Improvements:Enabling a variety of integrated terrestrial/satellite 5G/6G use-cases currently not feasible with low-gain user antennas.Description: Integrated terrestrial and satellite networks are considered a promising concept for supporting service demands in 5G and 6G communications. However, there are some fundamental issues to be tackled for seamless integration of terrestrial and satellite networks, especially in the case of mobile users operating in complex environments with low directive antennas. For the satellite link, received signals degrade severely upon arrival at the users due to the long-distance propagation, rain fading effects and blockage by obstacles. Moreover, due to spectrum sharing in the integrated terrestrial-satellite network, the interference mitigation problem between the two systems should be considered jointly to enhance the spectrum efficiency. Recently, reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) technology has drawn much attention due to its capability to enable reconfiguration of the radio propagation environment. This technology is based on large planar surfaces, comprising many passive reflecting elements able to induce a controllable amplitude and/or phase change to the incident signal. By strategically installing RIS (e.g., on building facades or roofs), system capacity, coverage, and/or energy usage can be improved cost-effectively. Standardisation bodies, such as 3GPP or ETSI, are in fact now discussing RIS deployments from the operational and regulatory perspectives. Many developments focused on RIS technology already take place as part of industrial, academic and European Commission activities. These developments have not been demonstrated in an endto-end or system context including both terrestrial and satellite networks, which is paramount for attracting the interest of key stakeholders such as satellite and mobile network operators. To fill this gap, this activity shall develop and implement several over-the-air satellite system demonstrators, validating the outcome of various RIS technology developments in various integrated terrestrial-satellite architectures. As a minimum, the activity shall quantify the benefits of RIS in the following realistic scenarios, with low-gain user antenna: 1) Improved link budged thanks to the enhanced signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at the receiver through the RIS-concatenated channel.2) Enhanced satellite user performance by employing RIS to mitigate inter-system interference in the integrated terrestrial-satellite system.Additional demonstrations can be added as soon as technology developments mature following an agile approach. The activity shall assess all relevant RIS developments and propose convincing demonstrations. The activity shall seek synergies with the ARTES deliverables and testbeds as well as by ongoing RIS projects and provide inputs to the 3GPP relevant standardisation working groups.Procurement Policy:C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: AURION ADVANCING UNDERSTANDING THROUGH RESEARCH AND INDUSTRY-ORIENTED CO-DESIGN OF NEW MISSIONS - EXPRO PLUS
description: AURION aims to establish a structured pre-Phase-0 co-design environment in which scientific ambition and industrial feasibility aredeveloped concurrently to define credible, innovative Earth Observation mission concepts.The activity targets mission concepts at SRL =3 that have not previously been assessed within ESA, and enables their maturation through joint science-industry system-level design, including early assessment of technical feasibility, cost drivers, and programmatic viability.AURION studies are characterised by:Joint science-industry leadership (mandatory co-design) Concurrent SRL and TRL maturationFocus on novel mission concepts, not incremental extensions Early integration of industrial feasibilityExplicit treatment of technical, cost, and programmatic riskSelected consortia shall perform integrated science-engineering co-design studies covering:Definition of measurement concept and observing principleExploration of mission architectures (orbit, geometry, constellation vs monolithic)Elaboration ofpreliminary Level-1 and Level-2 mission requirementsIdentification and maturation pathway of critical enabling technologies (TRL13+) Development of end-to-end data chain, including calibration and processing Preliminary cost and risk assessmentActivities shall remain strictly within pre-Phase-0, shall not converge prematurely to a single industrial solution, and shall maintain architectural optionality through structured trade-space exploration.

title: NAVISP-EL1-127-CROSS-DOMAIN NONLINEAR STATE ESTIMATION FOR AUTONOMOUS SYSTEMS USING UNSCENTED KALMAN FILTERING- EXPRO PLUS
description: This activity aims to develop a modular Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF)-based state estimation framework for autonomous systems operating in GNSS-challenged environments. It will enable robust multi-sensor fusion using GNSS, IMU, LiDAR, and vision data without relying on linearization, improving accuracy over traditional EKF approaches. The framework will incorporate adaptive noise modeling andadvanced unscented transformations for resilience under sensor degradation and dynamic conditions. A prototype will be designed, tested in hardware-in-the-loop setups, and validated through field trials on ground vehicles or UAVs. Comparative benchmarks against EKF and other filters will be performed, and a roadmap for integration into autonomy stacks will be delivered. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity

title: DEVELOPMENT OF LOW-BARRIER DIODES AND MIXERS FOR PASSIVE SUB-THZ RADIOMETER ARRAYS - EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop low barrier Schottky diodes and mixers for passive remote sensing of the Earth's atmosphere, with a local oscillator power requirement less than 25% compared to a traditional GaAs mixer.Description: Traditional Gallium Arsenide mixers such as the one used for MetOp-SG Micro Wave Imager (MWI) and Micro Wave Sounder (MWS) and Ice Cloud Imager (ICI) instruments need few milliwatts of local oscillator (LO) power to reach optimal conversion efficiency and noise figure. For single pixel instruments, this is well achievable with current local oscillator technology. For extended arrays of heterodyne receivers, this would mean to increase the local oscillator power requirements by one or two orders of magnitude. Therefore, the need for low LO power mixers is key to develop extended arrays of heterodyne receivers. This can be achieved by implementing a direct current (DC) biasing circuit together with GaAs mixer technology. This increases the complexity of the mixer circuit. An alternative solution is to implement low-barrier mixers using alternative semiconductor technology to reduce the barrier-height of the Schottky contact and similarly the pump power level, without the need for external DC biasing. The objective of this activity is to develop low-barrier diodes and mixers at EarthObservation applicable frequencies in the millimetre-wave and sub-THz regions of the spectrum. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Review of the current state-of-the-art in terms of low-barrier Schottky technology available (InGaAs, SiGe,...). - Design, manufacture and test a low-barrier diode and mixer operating in the 166-664 GHz range - Perform analysis of the performance, lessons learned and propose roadmap for future developments.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: DEVELOPMENT OF A EUROPEAN SOURCED ALLOY POWDER FOR ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING PROPULSION APPLICATIONS EXPRO+
description: To design a novel alloy for propulsion systems in next generation launch vehicles, while promoting European technological sovereignty and supply chain resilience.Description: Propulsion remains a critical element of launch vehicle development, driving the pursuit for higher thrust enabled by operation at elevated temperatures. This requires balancing performance goals and manufacturing constraints. Thrust chamber design is heavily influenced by the intrinsic limitations of the available materials. These are required to maintain their strength under severe thermo-mechanical conditions, while being able to dissipate surplus heat. Advances in materialsand manufacture broaden the design possibilities and unlock performance/competitiveness. Thrust chamber requirements have motivatedthe use of alloys in Cu, Ni, Ti and stainless steel. A need to incorporate integral cooling channels has also led to significant investment in additive manufacturing (AM), enabling ambitious designs, in some cases by combining multiple materials like copper and Inconel. A breakthrough has been made with the invention of GRCop-42, a high conductivity and strength alloy, suited for AM. While its composition is public, making parts in this alloy involves intricate and costly processes that are difficult to control. Selected companies have developed technologies to optimise production and performance, often protected as trade secrets or through patents. There are no European alternatives which could offer equivalent performance. Some engine developers have been exploring the use of copper-chrome-zirconium alloys, which can be more readily sourced in Europe, but the properties cannot compete with GRCop-42. ESA has identified a clear need to develop new and cheaper copper-based European alloys tailored for thrust chambers to sustain future launch vehicles. This is especially relevant given that many new players are preparing new platforms. A new alloy would be an enabling technology for all. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define generic future propulsion requirements, including: (a) Performance (higher strength and conductivity), (b) Manufacturability (compatible with AM, as well as general fabrication and repair methods), (c) Supply chain (produced from elements readily available in Europe) and (d) Competitiveness: Production cost and industrialisation feasibility. - Alloy design, possibly enabled by artificial intelligence to factor various requirements. - Manufacture and test coupons from experimental powder formulations. - Outline a plan for industrialisation in subsequent programs.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: T709-801GD DLT-BASED ACCESS MANAGEMENT FOR THE (CO-)OPERATION OF SHARED SPACE ASSETS (EXPRO+)
description: There is an increasing trend towards collaboration among space agencies and a rapidly growingnumber of commercial space actors. This raises the scenario and challenge of how different partiescan cooperatively operate shared space assets through distributed access control mechanisms.The standard approach to manage access to a shared asset, e.g., hosted payloads, where one ofthe collaborating parties assumes full authority over the asset, while the other parties strictly rely onthis authority, may be too rigid for manyemerging use cases. Modern concepts such as launch rideshares, ground segments and platforms as a service models, or even token-based economiccommercialisation of space missions require a more fully collaborative approach.Thus, in the pursuit towards true collaboration and along trends such as web3 and Blockchain, thisactivity shall aim to demonstrate fully distributed identity and accessmanagement. DecentralisedLedger Technologies (DLT) shall be leveraged to support associated operations concepts andmanage credentials and policies for individual actors interacting with the space assets. DLTsolutions differ in key aspects regarding cybersecurity, performance and scalability thus a specificemphasis shall be placed on measuring overheads in terms of data, network traffic and computingpower in the constrained environment of space systems. DLT applications shall be identified andtested in support of:- managing credentials and access to collaborating space assets in a distributed manner- public key certificates including revocationand enforcement (e.g., revoke access of a specificoperator)- distributed identity establishment (e.g., how parties trust each othersendorsement of actors)- cryptographic key management and root of trust aspects (e.g., securely managing keys via trustedhardware and use of merkle-tree hashs and proof of inclusion concepts)

title: T409-801GD LAUNCH CAMPAIGN PREPARATION AND OPERATIONS INTELLIGENT ASSISTANCE (EXPRO+)
description: Given the huge amounts and heterogeneity among the data collected during a launch campaign,the task of correlating information anddetecting unexpected behaviours is too complex for a humanoperator to handle. This becomes more evident when the data is stored indistributed machines,different formats (textual, graphs, TM, etc) and needs to be carefully investigated during critical andtime pressing operations like launches.An Intelligent Assistant is a software agent that can perform tasks or services for an end-user; itsrange of capabilities is wide and can be tailored to the user needs, ranging from fetching andcorrelating information across a variety of vast heterogeneous data sources, providing a humanlike interaction with the systems to automating tasks or training newcomers, avoiding the loss ofknow-how due to staff rotations. The key technology employed is Artificial Intelligence (AI). Morespecifically, an Intelligent Assistant consists mainly of a knowledge base and a communicationlayer. The first contains the knowledge from the field of expertise, an aggregated suitably preprocessed version of the available data sources (e.g. a Knowledge Graph), along with reasoningmethods. The communication layer provides a human-like interaction, employing Natural LanguageProcessing methods forsemantic parsing of human requests or documents, extracting intent,providing question and answering functionality, etc.The technology has the potential to completely transform the nature of accessing, correlating,sharing information and identifying key insights in data. Its benefits have been demonstrated indiverse industrial domains. To address space concepts, a domain-specific assistantis needed.However, the employment of such technology within the space sector is still in its infancy.

title: ADVANCED TECHNIQUES FOR MOMENTUM MANAGEMENT WITH THRUSTER ORIENTATION MECHANISMS - EXPRO PLUS
description: To improve the spacecraft momentum management with autonomous and optimal control of thrustorientation, enabling Reaction Wheel capacity reduction.DescriptionModern Telecom/GEO Satellites employ electric propulsion thrusters for both Orbit Raising phaseand Station Keeping. Gimbaled electric Thrusters via thruster orientation mechanisms (2 or 3 degree of freedom) are typically used both for orbital manoeuvres (e.g. North-South Position in Station Keeping) and concurrently management of the on-board momentum by unloading the reaction wheels. Conventional unloading strategies are often executed via controlled operations (e.g. sequence of programmed TOM angles along the orbit to ensure proper Thrust vectororientation). AOCS estimates the on board S/C momentum and controls the TOM angles in closed loop to limit the angular momentum storage due to both the thrust misalignment with respect to the S/C centre of gravity and the environmental disturbance torques, while satisfying multiple constraints such as TOM allowed angular range, TOM activation cycles, consumption, wheel capacity and collocation (if any). Large wheels are typically employed for this reason, thus increasing S/C overall mass.The activity consists of investigating advanced on-board optimization methods to control the TOM angles in optimal way and efficiently manage the on-board momentum, such to increase the onboardautonomy (less dependency on ground, autonomous generation of TOM angle profiles), minimize the maximum required wheel capacity while satisfying mechanisms constraints such as maximum number of activation cycles and minimising consumption.The activity is dedicated to GEO Telecom missions, taking into account their specifics in terms ofsensor and actuator architecture, as well as AOCS design drivers and mission/operations constraints. Gain on Reaction Wheel offloading need is expected to be in the range of 30%, on top on operational cost decrease thanks to autonomous TOM guidance during EOR.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Existing application cases selection including performance requirements, sensors and actuators selection, AOCS subsystem /modes design, mission and system constraints for thrust control optimisation- Optimisation methods survey selection of the most promising one- Design analysis applied to the selected use cases - Implementation in simulator, including multi-body dynamics modelling- Validation test campaign- Assessment of autonomy, performance and mass gain vs heritage design and implementation way forward.

title: LONG-LIFE, SUB-KW HALL EFFECT THRUSTER FOR MICRO/SMALL SATELLITES IN GEO AND LEO - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a sub-kW Hall Effect Thruster with total impulse capability in excess of 2MNs.Hall Effect Thrusters (HET) have become the leading choice for propulsion systems in GEO comsats and LEO constellations due to their high specific impulse (Isp),significant thrust-to-power ratio, and proven reliability. They are used for tasks like orbit insertion, changing or raising orbits, momentum unloading, station keeping, repositioning, collision avoidance, and deorbiting at the end of mission. Micro and small GEOcomsats and LEO constellations typically use sub-kW Hall Effect thrusters. European sub-kW Hall Effect thrusters that use Xenon arecurrently being qualified for a total impulse capability of 1 MNs. Future micro and small GEO comsats will require higher total impulse capabilities (more than 2MNs) for GTO-GEO orbit raising and 15 years of station keeping in GEO. Future LEO constellations may also need higher total impulse capabilities if the satellite's operational life will be extended to 7 or 9 years. Today there are noEuropean Hall Effect thrusters capable of such high total impulse capability. The objective of this activity is to develop and testa European sub-kW HET with a significantly increased total impulse capability compared to currently available HETs. The thruster shall operate over a power range of 500 to 1000 W, provide a total impulse of at least 2 MNs and use Xenon as propellant. The new thruster shall be cost competitive with a design for manufacture. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements Specification definition - Preliminary design definition and justification - Manufacture of breadboard(s), performance characterisation and endurance testing (duration sufficient to demonstrate total impulse capability (possibly in combination with modelling) - Modelling of life-limiting factors to support demonstration of total impulse capability - Generate roadmap to complete qualification and achieve flight readiness status.

title: T709-904GA TOWARDS A STREAMLINED DEVELOPMENT APPROACH IN SIMULATORS (EXPRO+)
description: SIMULUS is a framework for the development of space assets, developed by ESA, andavailable to ESA Member States under the ESA Software Community Licence. It is widelyused by European industry to develop spacecraft simulators, both in ESA contracts as wellas commercially. It is predominantly used for the development of operational simulators, thatsupport the training of operators for most ESA missions, but over the years, in particularsince it became available as ESA Software Community Licence, it has gained traction inother areas, e.g. onboard software validation facilities.With new players joining the sector (e.g. New Space) as well as increasing demand oncurrent industrial partners, a common feedback/request is to streamline the 15+ year olddevelopment process currentlyin place, as it is based on outdated/heavy/rigid developmentprocesses (e.g. Waterfall) while the sector is moving toward to more flexible/agiledevelopment approach, as it adapts to a wider family of missions, from cubesats to thetraditional ESA satellites.In today's space context, to support European industry to be more competitive, a simpler,more modern process is required, that not onlyreduce costs but also enables the scaling ofdevelopment of more simulators by industry. In such context, the proposed activity aims tosimplify the development process and the tools that support it, by revisiting the currentapproach in close collaboration withindustry. It is expected to reduce the number of manualsteps required to setup the simulator, the number of tools involved and reducing thedependency on costly 3rd party software.

title: ROBUST FDIR ARCHITECTURE FOR FUTURE CLOSE-PROXIMITY MISSIONS - EXPRO PLUS
description: To design and develop Fault, Detection, Isolation and Recovery (FDIR) architectures tailored for future close-proximity operations (CPO) missions.Description: The development of CPO missions, including formation flying and rendezvous with cooperative/non-cooperative targets, is rapidly increasing. These missions contribute to Zero Debris Policy (ZDP) by acting as Active Debris Removal (ADR)/In-Orbit Servicing (IOS) missions. As having two satellites operating at close range raises the risk of collision, it is crucial todesign robust architectures that minimize debris risks. One approach to achieve system robustness while maintaining autonomy is theimplementation of FDIR. FDIR is crucial in CPO missions and more complex than in traditional missions,it enables relative position detection and autonomous sequencing to reduce collision risk and handles failure detection and collision avoidance manoeuvres. A tailored FDIR system capable of supporting CPO tasks does not exist yet. To ensure mission safety, dedicated FDIR solutions must be designed to address the unique challenges of CPO. Implementing tailored FDIR systems will bridge the gap between classic missions and CPO tasks. This activity is crucial to meet ZDP constraints, contributing to FDIR, CPO, and Space Debris Mitigation Requirement (SDMR) body of knowledge by developing standardized FDIR for CPO missions. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Specify all identified CPO space missions use cases to define a complete FDIR strategy, requirements and architecture. - Prepare a FDIR development plan, including process, tasks, tools, verification and validation, for each use case. - Develop a FDIR strategy for each use case including safe/survival modes definition, modes transitions, FDIR requirements, dedicated redundancy strategies and a list of critical monitors. - Develop detailed simulations and models of selected CPO uses-cases to validate various FDIR architectures and create scenarios that include potential debris generation and collision risks. Use simulations to evaluate performance, robustness, and efficiency of those different FDIR strategies and provide recommendations for FDIR implementation and complexity reduction.
