title: DUST MODEL FOR THE OUTER SOLAR SYSTEM EXPRO+
description: Develop a dust model prototype and integrate it into an engineering tool to evaluate thedust impacting on spacecraft in the Outer Solar System.DescriptionMicrometeoroids pose a relevant risk to spacecraft on interplanetary missions. In several recent interplanetary projects the risk by impacting particles dominate the risk budget in terms of planetary protection and in some cases overall reliability. Recent ESA mission concepts target destinations in the Outer Solar System (e.g. Voyage 2050, Ice Giants) where there is currently a limited understanding of the dust environment. There are scientific models in the US with limited applicability. However, there are noengineering tools available to be applied in the spacecraft development process. The ESA activity Enhanced Interplanetary Meteoroid Environment Model IMEM2 (Contract No. 114513) was developed to describe the meteoroid environment up to about 6 AU. At higher Sun distances the dust sources need to be revised, as e.g. Kuiper Belt Objects, new physical effects modeled, as e.g. collisions of objects, and also the propagation timescales extended to achieve a steady state distribution. The model output will be in aformat that it can be interfaced with impact risk assessment tools as ESABASE2/Debris to provide the risk for a 3D spacecraft design. Similar to sporadic dust there are also meteoroid streams and interplanetary dust that are modelled with IMEX model. The need to update these models shall be assessed and arespective development plan prepared in the scope of this activity. Note that there is anongoing acticity to model the local dust environment inside the Saturnsystem, mainly to target the risk for the large solar arraysflown here. However, the risk for the same arrays during transit in interplanetary space (beyond 6 AU) is not addressed. This activity shall encompass:- literature review and data study to identify relevant dust sources and populations,scientific dust models and data sources to be exploited in the activity- definition and implementation of sources, populations and physics to be consideredinthe activity- large scale simulation of dust distribution in the Solar System- comparison of the model with observational dataand other models- assess need to update stream and interstellar dust models (IMEX) and preparerespective development plan.Procurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SMEs RD Entities. title: SECURE RECONFIGURABLE SOFTWARE DEFINED SATELLITES - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To design, develop, implement, test and verify secure reconfigurable technologies needed to support softwaredefined satellites.Description:Europe's first commercial satellite capable of being completely reprogrammed while in space are already incommercial use. Such satellites offer unprecedented mission reconfiguration capacity and capabilities(including but not limited to beams reshaping and redirection). In addition, in-flight re-programmabilitycapabilities that will enable avionic platforms to support many missions are also considered. The availability ofsystem-on-chip, powerful micro-controllers and reprogrammable Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)enables a high-level of flexibility while improving the performance of avionic systems.However, all these software defined capabilities and flexibility require to be managed and implemented in asecure way, to ensure that cannot be exploitedby potential attackers to compromise the confidentiality,integrity or availability of the provided services, of the software defined capabilities and of the platform itself.Security measures, including access controls, cryptographic based authentication, software authenticityprotection using digital signatures or other suitable technology, secure booting based on root of trust, user /operator / management segregation, and other, must be implemented.This activity is divided in phases and encompasses the following tasks:Phase 1 (budget: 500 k, duration: 8 months):- Asses the state of the art of software defined satellites technologies and architectures.- Security assessment of the risks of using these technologies and architectures, identification and assessmentof securitytechnologies that can be used to mitigate these risks; identification of suitable products (software /hardware) implementing thesesecurity technologies.- Design a complete secure reconfigurable software defined satellite using the identified security technologiesto address the security risks.- Proof-of-concept development of selected functionalities, demonstration and testing.Phase 2 (budget: 1,500 k, duration: 16 months):- Develop the technologies that will be used for securing the configuration and authenticity of software definedsatellites.- Implement an end-to-end secure reconfigurable software defined satellite.- Test, verify and demonstrate end-to-end secure reconfigurable software defined satellite.

The availability ofsystem-on-chip, powerful micro-controllers and reprogrammable Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)enables a high-level of flexibility while improving the performance of avionic systems.However, all these software defined capabilities and flexibility require to be managed and implemented in asecure way, to ensure that cannot be exploitedby potential attackers to compromise the confidentiality,integrity or availability of the provided services, of the software defined capabilities and of the platform itself.Security measures, including access controls, cryptographic based authentication, software authenticityprotection using digital signatures or other suitable technology, secure booting based on root of trust, user /operator / management segregation, and other, must be implemented.This activity is divided in phases and encompasses the following tasks:Phase 1 (budget: 500 k, duration: 8 months):- Asses the state of the art of software defined satellites technologies and architectures.- Security assessment of the risks of using these technologies and architectures, identification and assessmentof securitytechnologies that can be used to mitigate these risks; identification of suitable products (software /hardware) implementing thesesecurity technologies.- Design a complete secure reconfigurable software defined satellite using the identified security technologiesto address the security risks.- Proof-of-concept development of selected functionalities, demonstration and testing.Phase 2 (budget: 1,500 k, duration: 16 months):- Develop the technologies that will be used for securing the configuration and authenticity of software definedsatellites.- Implement an end-to-end secure reconfigurable software defined satellite.- Test, verify and demonstrate end-to-end secure reconfigurable software defined satellite.

title: GLOBAL RADIATION BELT MODEL IMPROVEMENT BY RADIATION MONITOR DATA - EXPRO+
description: In-orbit radiation instrument data is available from a range of European missions. In this activity, radiation monitor data shall be analysed to understand how the updated flux maps affect different reconstructions of the complete Van Allen belts through both analytical mapping/interpolation and physics-based modelling. The various existing European pre-developments and prototype models shall be evaluated and used in this process where found suitable. Different established means (Singular Value Decomposition, Neural Networks, etc.) to convert the instrument counts to environmental fluxes in an optimal and transparent way shall be assessed. A prototype database will be a reference database, version controlled and with community open access.The following tasks are foreseen in the activity: In preparation of a new European global radiation belt model, evaluate the latest methodologies available on data merging issues. Make comparisons to predictions from existing models and analyse the differences. Analyse the quality of the calibration and simulation metadata gained from relevant missions and process it into usable quantities: particle fluxes, spectra, doses, etc. Derive the radiation response functions of the suitable instruments. Build a coherent multi-cycle set of data that can be transformed into time-dependent flux maps of the radiation belts by applying crosscalibration. The data on Solar Particle Events shallbe consideredbased on occurrence. A detailed development plan for a global end model system and related software shall be prepared. The software versions resulting from this activity shall be distributed under an ESA Software Community Licence, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access to it and can provide updates to the community of users. Nevertheless, thecontractor shall own all intellectual property rights on the software resulting from this activity and may therefore additionally distribute it, in its own discretion, under any other license (e.g. without the territorial restriction of the ESA Software Community Licence). NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: HIGH PERFORMANCE INSULATING MATERIALS FOR L4 ENCELADUS LANDER - EXPRO+
description: To assess the potential use of alternative insulating materials (e.g. aerogel) to improve the thermal performance of classical MLI,and sustaining the extreme environments applicable to L4 Enceladus Lander.Current thermal insulation solutions for Solar System missions are mainly based onconductive and radiative insulation (e.g. JUICE Nomex reinforced MLI), or includeconvective insulation function, not assessed for L4 Enceladus Lander environments (e.g.ExoMars Upilex foam). Due to the L4 Lander extreme environment on Enceladus (lowtemperatures, potential interaction with plumes, snow and/or ice and challenging landingconditions), the use of classical MLI technology, even with an efficient, reinforced designsuch as the one used in JUICE, is probably insufficient to achieve the required thermalinsulation and reduce the use of electrical heating. Heaters use is to be minimized (with atarget of 0 W), as the electrical power consumption is directly linked to the mass andlifetime span of the Lander on Enceladus surface. In addition, the selected thermal controltechnologies shall ensure nominal performance while keeping physical integrity (stringentmechanical loads during landing) and fulfilling mass, EMC, planetary protection and otherrequirements of the mission.Potential technologies such as Aerogel have been identified in similar missions such asMars Pathfinder ("(...). The WEB is a thermal isolating composite structure with cocuredthermal control surfaces and an ultralightweight hydrophobic solid silica aerogel whichminimizes conduction and radiation. This design provides excellent thermal insulation atlow gas pressures and meets the structural requirements for spacecraftlaunch loads andfor a 60 g impact landing at Mars without damage to the insulation or structure. (...)",https://www.jstor.org/stable/44725574). The use of these technologies or alternative onesneeds being assessed for L4 Enceladus Lander. The activity encompasses the followingtasks:Requirements consolidation and assessment of state of the art- Design of breadboard and associated test bench- Manufacture of breadboard, test bench- Execution of tests and exploitation of results- Conclusions elaboration and roadmap for further development towards a flight applicationThe outcomes of this activity are extendable to other planetary missions.

title: ESTRACK FRONT-END CONTRACTS
description: A new engineering, sustaining and third-level maintenance approach for the ESTRACK network is covered by this ITT proposed in whichthe end-to-end responsibility for the ground station installations is taken over - upon successful phase-in - by prime contractors. The contractual scope includes sustaining activities, predictive maintenance of the various subsystems, system and subsystem retests, spares and repair procurement and third-level support to the Maintenance and Operations (MO) teams. The ESTRACK network consists of two categories of antennas: The four 35m Deep Space Antennas (Category 1) and the smaller non-Deep Space Antennas (Category 2). The equipment and technical expertise required for Deep Space antennas differ substantially from those needed for smaller antenna systems.The Deep Space Antennas can further be subdivided in two groups, the first-generation Deep Space antennas in NNO-1, CEB-1, MLG-1 and the latest 2nd generation Deep Space antenna NNO-3. Hence the following Lots are defined for this procurement:Lot 1 - for NNO-1, CEB-1 and MLG-1 - Category 1 antennasLot 2 - for NNO-3 - Category 1 antennaLot 3 - for KIR-1, KRU-1 and NNO-2 - Category 2 antennas

title: DETERMINISTIC ETHERNET SPACE TIME-SENSITIVE NETWORKING SOFT IP CORE - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop a technology independent soft IP (Intellectual Property) core that complies with the aerospace profile of TSN(Time Sensitive Networking).Description:TSN (Time-Sensitive Networking) and TTE (Time Triggered Ethernet) are the two technologies that allow to deliver determinism and quality of service on top of standard Ethernet networks. Since TTE can be considered relatively closed technology (i.e. proprietary solution, patents pending on the technology), since a few years TSN is emerging as a potential successor of that technology. TSN is IEEE supported set of standards that implements wide range of quality of services (i.e. reliability, determinism, mixed criticality traffic, redundancy, time synchronization) on top of the standard Ethernet protocols. TSN benefits from Ethernet Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) tools/ecosystem, it is free of patents and is being introduced step-by step in industrial applications (automotive/industrial) and aerospace domain (IEEE P802.1DP - TSN for Aerospace Onboard Ethernet Communications). Although TSN is very successful in the automotive/industrial sector, in space applications TSNis still being considered as low TRL technology. Many current and future Exploration and Space Transportationmissions are considering Ethernet-based networks for the data-handling communication bus. Having thistechnology available for future ESA missions is seen as a key driver for future missions. The aim of this activity Is to develop an IP core that contains the core functionalities of Time-Sensitive Networking needed for space applications. Although the set of TSN standards is very wide, there are several on-going activities aiming attailoring of TSN for space applications. Having an TSN IP tailored to space applications could be considered asa key enabler of this technology in future ESA and national missions.The following technical aspects shall be considered:- Development of End-system IP Core. Switch IP core is out of scope of this activity- One or two Ethernet ports shall be supported.- Host integration: AXI4 lite for registers and IP configuration, and AXI4 stream for packet data- The IP shall support 10/100/1000Mbps speeds. 10Gbps is considered optional.- Compatible and configurable with various PHY interfaces (i.e. MII/GMII/RGMIII).- To be developed as technology independent VHDL.- To be implemented and validated in 2 FPGA/ASIC technologies (preferable NG-Ultra/Ultra300 andMicrochip Polarfire).This activity encompasses the following tasks:- TSN IP core requirements identification and development of the high-level architecture of the TSN soft IP core.- Prototype development and integration into a representative Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) based network platform.- Verification and validation targeting high speed use cases- TSN soft IP core release and related documentation.Deliverables: Prototype, Report, SoftwareApplication/Need Date: Exploration and Space Transportation missions. Mission Classification: alpha, beta,gamma, delta

title: ERS-EO IOD-A - LOW LUMINANCE / NIGHT VISION
description: In order to de-risk and accelerate the implementation phase of EOGS, the IOD/IOV activities will focus on short-term achievements delivered through targeted in-orbit experiments. These experiments are intended to provide early proof of concept and in-orbit validation, with demonstrable results available ahead of the next Ministerial Conference in 2028.The scope and objectives of the IOD/IOV activities are aimed at strengthening European autonomy, including enhancing the industrialisation of solutions already under development, and supporting pre-operational validation and technology demonstration.The technologies to be developed for EOGS space missions will be selected in consultation with the European Commission and Participating States, and in accordance with the main findingsof the EOGS studies. The technologies which are being considered are:- Secure inter-satellite links and IRIS interoperability;- Data management, on-board processing and dynamic satellite tasking to reduce latency;- Enhanced security features demonstrating resilience to the considered threats;- Serialisation and synergies (re-use) across the ERS fleet;- Increased agility and imaging capacity over crisis area;- Low-cost high-performance SAR and optical payloads with extended imaging capabilities; and- Platforms optimised for batch launches on European launchers and compatible with applicable clean space policies.Drawing on these findings, together with further consultation with industry through the Request for Information (RFI) released in July 2025 which received a substantial number of responses four main themes have been identified for the IOD/IOV activities.The In-Orbit Demonstration/Validation(IOD/IOV) activities are therefore organised into the following four themes:A. IOD-A: Low Luminance / Night VisionB. IOD-B: DynamicSatellite TaskingC. IOD-C: Reduced information age (i.e. data latency from acquisition to product delivery)D. IOD-D: Satellite Super AgilityThese correspond to areas where a further consolidation is needed (hence the relevance of conducting an IOD) before a feature of very high interest and relevance to the ERS-EO programme objective could be declared operational and included in the nominal configuration of the system.

These experiments are intended to provide early proof of concept and in-orbit validation, with demonstrable results available ahead of the next Ministerial Conference in 2028.The scope and objectives of the IOD/IOV activities are aimed at strengthening European autonomy, including enhancing the industrialisation of solutions already under development, and supporting pre-operational validation and technology demonstration.The technologies to be developed for EOGS space missions will be selected in consultation with the European Commission and Participating States, and in accordance with the main findingsof the EOGS studies. The technologies which are being considered are:- Secure inter-satellite links and IRIS interoperability;- Data management, on-board processing and dynamic satellite tasking to reduce latency;- Enhanced security features demonstrating resilience to the considered threats;- Serialisation and synergies (re-use) across the ERS fleet;- Increased agility and imaging capacity over crisis area;- Low-cost high-performance SAR and optical payloads with extended imaging capabilities; and- Platforms optimised for batch launches on European launchers and compatible with applicable clean space policies.Drawing on these findings, together with further consultation with industry through the Request for Information (RFI) released in July 2025 which received a substantial number of responses four main themes have been identified for the IOD/IOV activities.The In-Orbit Demonstration/Validation(IOD/IOV) activities are therefore organised into the following four themes:A. IOD-A: Low Luminance / Night VisionB. IOD-B: DynamicSatellite TaskingC. IOD-C: Reduced information age (i.e. data latency from acquisition to product delivery)D. IOD-D: Satellite Super AgilityThese correspond to areas where a further consolidation is needed (hence the relevance of conducting an IOD) before a feature of very high interest and relevance to the ERS-EO programme objective could be declared operational and included in the nominal configuration of the system.

title: MEASUREMENT AND MODELLING OF THE ATTITUDE OF METOP AND SENTINEL 1 TO PREPARE FOR ERASE PHASE A - EXPRO+
description: Summary Description The proposed activity is will support the preparation for the ERASE Phase A. ERASE aims to prepare the removalof large, non-cooperative and unprepared objects in low Earth orbit, initially considering Metop and Sentinel-1 targets (starting with METOP-A and S1B, both being decommissioned), thereby supporting ESA's Space Safety Programme and the transition towards a circular economy in space. This activity will establish and demonstrate ground-based laser-ranging measurement, modelling and analysis capabilities to characterise the attitude state and tumbling behaviour of non-cooperative, unprepared targets, with initial focus on Metop and Sentinel-1 targets. The output is essential and urgent for the ERASE Phase A study. Without this information available at the start of Phase A, there is a risk that the technical feasibility of the mission is incorrectly assessed. The target spin rate is adesign driver for the servicer delta-V and operations timeline, the relative navigation subsystem, and the robotic capture sizing and loads. The spin-axis orientation drives the safe approach direction and the capture strategy. In addition, the probability of very low spin-rate cases must be understood, as such cases may lead to long durations in unfavourable attitude conditions for target power generation, thermal control and ground contact. The challenge is that the targets are not prepared with cooperative markers or laser retro-reflectors that would facilitate attitude reconstruction. The attitude state must therefore be reconstructed from non-cooperative laser-ranging observables, making use of time-of-flight/range measurements, return-signal characteristics, pass geometry, target geometry, known or estimated surface properties, and attitude-dynamics modelling. Where beneficial, the laser-ranging data maybe complemented by passive optical or radar observations.The activity will assess the feasibility, achievable accuracy and uncertainty of attitude determination and dynamics-based propagation from ground. It will characterise and propagate target dynamics, in particular spin rate and spin-axis orientation, and will provide statistically meaningful uncertainty envelopes for ERASE Phase A design trade-offs. The activity will also prepare the capability to perform repeated attitude characterisation campaigns in support of ERASE. The attitude state of non-cooperative targets may evolve over time due to environmental torques and target-specific dynamics; therefore, measurements may be required not only during the present feasibility phase, but also before launch, to confirm that the target conditions remain within the design assumptions, and potentially at intermediate points during mission preparation. A dedicated task will assess the applicability of the developed measurement and modelling methods to a broader range of large, unprepared, non-cooperative low Earth orbit targets beyond Metop and Sentinel-1, identifying the key target properties, observation conditions and limitations that determine feasibility.

title: 5G AUTOMOTIVE ANTENNA PROTOTYPE AND DEMONSTRATION (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7C.084)
description: The objective is to design and demonstrate a new class of low-profile and conformal antennas, providing seamless connectivity for 5G services on vehicles.Targeted Improvements:Enabling technology Satellite antennas compatible with the constrains of the automotive markets (in terms of aesthetics, aerodynamics and safety), whilst providing seamless connectivity, are currently not available.Description:The automotive sector is a crucial target group for future 5G systems, as the new standards pursues the goal of integrating mobile communications into vehicles. However, antennas providing seamless connectivity on board of vehicles are not available today, due to many technological and commercial challenges that shall not be addressed in isolation. Antennas for satellite-connected cars can be designed for various frequency bands (e.g., L-, S-, Ku- and/or Ka-Band), require compatibility with terrestrial and other satellite services (e.g., satellite radio and navigation) and must satisfy requirements of the automotive market.This activitywill design a class of low-profile and conformal antennas, following a holistic approach where all main stakeholders (i.e., antennatechnology provider, car manufacturer, satellite/terrestrial operator) are involved in the antenna design. This includes aspect such as:- Selection of at least one use-case and system definition: frequency bands (e.g. S-, Ku-, Ka-Band) satellite type and orbits(e.g. LEO, MEO, GEO and/or HEO) Optimisation of the system architecture, aiming to the automotive antenna simplification.- Selection of a vehicle class and associated environmental and safety constrains Co-design of the antenna/vehicle chassis, where the satellite terminal antenna aperture isembedded in the chassis frame, roof and/or other conformal structure, to guarantee a suitable aperture size and orientation, whilst minimising the impact on the vehicle design and aesthetics.- End-to-end demonstration of the prototype system with two or more vehicles, validating the target use-case(s).

title: HIGH TEMPERATURE METALIZED PET (POLYESTER) FILM CAPACITORS EXPRO PLUS (RE-ISSUE)
description: To develop metalized Polyester (PET) film capacitors based on Surface Mounting Device (SMD) that can withstand assembly high-temperature stress due to the lead-free transitionDescriptionCurrently, metallized PET film capacitors are mainly used in space for filtering purposes and power electronics. They have low dielectric losses, stable characteristics, and cover power constraints with lower capacitance values than other capacitor families.Unfortunately, owing to the current lead-free transition, there are no capacitors of this family that are able to withstand the high temperatures, around 240 degrees Celsius, induced by the lead-free soldering. These capacitors are not available either in the automotive qualified domain.Capacitors with high capacitance values are only available in through-hole packages and cannot withstand the high temperature stress induced by the lead-free transition. Thus, there is a need to develop an innovative solution of metallized polyester film capacitors, in SMD package in order to ease the integration, and with improved internal design to withstand inherent high-temperature leadfree soldering.This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Literature review and market survey - Technology and process review for the selection of promising solutions - Development and manufacturing of high-temperature metallized PET film capacitors. - Electrical characterization and reliability assessment of the capacitors, including thermal cycling, mechanical testing and assembly verification. - Identification of limitations, improvements and roadmap for future space qualificationProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: ROSE-L COMPANION SATELLITE INSTRUMENT CONCEPT STUDY - EXPRO PLUS (RE-ISSUE)
description: The goal of the ROSE L Companion Satellite Instrument Concept Study is to investigate a variety of instrument concepts suitable forimplementing a bistatic companion satellite to ROSE L. This includes examining different instrument options and configurations thatcould enable a more compact SAR instrument design, even if this leads to reduced performance across certain Level 1 parameters.Thestudy aims to build an understanding of the multi-dimensional trade space between various SAR instrument concepts, their parametervariations, and the resulting impact on Level 1 performance. This analysis will support the tailoring of the instrument design to meet a specific set of Level 1 requirements while also informing the scientific community about how sensitive these performance parameters are to overall instrument complexity. Ultimately, the study will used as an input to define an optimal set of mission requirements and identifying a suitable instrument concept for a bistatic ROSE L companion satellite.

title: TALLINN HELSINKI OPTICAL RELAY (THOR) TESTBED (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.092) - REQUESTED
description: The objective of the activity is to define and develop a free space optical communication testbed suitable for testing a cross-atmospheric optical connectivity in the horizontal link between Tallinn and Helsinki. Targeted Improvements: To create a terrestrial testbed capability allowing for demonstration and long-term communication testing. The testbed will provide information on the long-distance atmospheric channel and the stability of the optical links in fixed and mobile configuration. The testbed facility will support new technology developments for optical and quantum satellite communication. Description: Most of satellite constellations developed these days include intersatellite links. However, the adaptation of cross-atmospheric links remains to be progressing slowly. One of the challenges is the limited availability of outdoor, free-space testbeds. The proposed testbed facility will enable testing over the long-distance, cross-atmospheric channel created between two stations located in Tallinn and Helsinki. The testbed will allow for fixed-points free-space optical connection, demonstrating and validating a continuous datalink between interoperable terminals and transceivers aligned with satellite optical communication standards. The testbed should allow to collect and analyse information on the atmospheric channel over multiple seasons. It should monitor weather conditions and investigate beam dissipation dynamics and various mitigation strategies. The spatially dynamic optical links will also be demonstrated to test and validate a free-space optical datalink between moving terminals. The testbed should foresee and facilitate testing of quantum-encrypted free-space optical communication capabilities. The preparation to demonstrate data-relay with a satellite link is planned to be included in the activity.

title: AEROTHERMODYNAMIC CHARACTERIZATION OF GAS-SURFACE INTERACTIONS FOR HYPERSONIC UPPER STAGE RECOVERY VEHICLES - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To model the hypersonic flow around critical points of the re-entry of a upper stage vehicle, accounting for the catalytic properties of a Si-O-C ceramics, and for the chemical modifications of the surface exposed to the air.Description: There is a renewed interest in the implementation of reusable vehicles for in-orbit operation. A critical aspect in the lifetime of a space vehicle is to improve the durability of the thermal protection structures, to limit the replacement of the thermal shield. Ultra-high temperature ceramics (UHTC) materials, based on the Si-O-C compounds with dedicated coatings (boride, molybdenum etc.) demonstrated to be a good choice, due to their capability to resist and survive above 1500 K. To fully evaluate the response of any material in suchextreme operating conditions, it is also imperative to determine the catalysis in high temperature gas, strongly affecting the surface heat flux. Moreover, the interaction of the material coatings with dissociated gases such as oxygen and nitrogen, induces variations on the material properties. The technology to be developed is to model accurately the complex physical processes at the gas surface interface during ascent and descent, in which different coatings are experimental tested validating the predictive capabilitiesof the numerical models. The model will include advanced kinetics, using a hybrid state-to-state -Multi-Temperature (StS-MT) derived from the StS, where the vibrational degrees of freedom are described by the vibrational temperature, while electronic excited states are treated as independent species, in order to estimate the radiative properties. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Development of a chemical model of air interacting with the Si-O-C ceramic material, in dissociation regime; - Development of a hybrid StS-MT kinetic model - Develop a database for thermodynamic properties and of transport cross sections for air including Si-O-C species - Implementation of kinetics and transport in a numerical tool for hypersonic flows for the reliable simulation, flat plate/coupons - Model chemical gas surface interaction, chemical stability, roughness, thickness, stability of coatings, catalyst by experimental plasma testing of different samples, thermal optical properties, emission spectroscopy - Numerical modelling and testing thermal bounding of the silica based substrate bounding with the coating, testing of the attachment devices - Evaluation of differentceramics suitable for the orbital entry conditions.

title: STANDARDISED FUNCTIONAL POWER CONTROL MODULES FOR CONSTELLATIONS SATELLITES (ARTES AT 4F.182) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, build and test standardised functional power modules resulting in a Commercial-off-the-Shelf-based Power Conditioning and Distribution Unit (PCDU) consisting of the solar array regulator, the controller module, the battery management module, the power distribution module and the deployment module, for telecomsconstellations applications.Techniques and technologies to improve the power efficiency will be studied and implemented as well as health monitoring capabilities as needed to comply with Zero Debris requirements.Targeted Improvements: - Power module manufacturing time reduction by 80% andreduction of risk of production delay- PCDU efficiency improvement of up to 15% thanks to solar regulator efficiency improvement by10 percentage points and 50% improvement of the power distribution module.Description: Typical space power units are designed andbuilt to comply with project-specific specifications. As a consequence, manufacturers implement different solutions, which are notcompatible nor interoperable. Therefore, a specific power unit can only be built by a specific manufacturer. When large number of units have to be built this often poses a supply chain challenge. APA is an advanced power architecture standard developed with EuropeanPrimes with the potential to overcome supply chain bottlenecks. It aims at standardising the electrical and mechanical interfaceofmodular power distribution units and hence unit production can easily be spread among multiple suppliers.This activity will identify opportunities for standardisation of power control modules for constellations satellites taking the APA and other available standards as a starting point. title: NAVISP-EL1-131-CHIP SCALE OPTICAL ATOMIC CLOCK FOR PNT APPLICATIONS EXPRO+
description: Development of a compact optical atomic clock module (physics package) for PNT applications. The activity will design, manufacture,and test an Engineering Model (EM) of a chip-scale optical clock exploiting an atomic optical transition to achieve 10 improved stability (target timing drift 10-30 ns/day) versus existing microwave clocks. The clock will provide a stabilized optical frequencyoutput in a low-power (< 5 W), compact device. Tasks include detailed thermo-mechanical design for robust operation in harsh environments, definition of low-power control electronics requirements and autonomous operation algorithms, assembly of the optical clock physics package, and development of Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) to control and test the EM. The EM will undergo performance verification in ambient and thermal conditions to demonstrate its stability, targeting TRL 4-5 and paving the way for future space-qualified ultra-stable timing solutions for navigation and timing systems.

title: FULLY RETRACTABLE SOLAR ARRAYS FOR MISSIONS TO SATURN EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesTo develop a solar array design for use in deep space missions to Saturn.DescriptionFor an orbiting satellite to pass safely through the rings of Saturn, the solar array needs tobe retractable. In order to minimize target area, the array should alsobe fully flexible. Fullyretractable and flexible arrays are currently being developed for telecommunicationmissions, which may form the starting point of this development. With a high specificpower, such arrays lend themselves for use in exploration missions.Recent feasibility studies have demonstrated that missions to Saturn, fully powered bysolar arrays, are indeed feasible. However, the total area needed would be between 150 -200 m2. This places demanding requirements on the solar array design. Apart from highspecific power (W/kg) and low areal mass (kg/m2), other important parameters include theeigenfrequencies in stowed and deployed configurations, as well as the ability to retractand to re-deploy, to protect the array from damage, should the satellite pass through thedust rings of Saturn.The activity therefore encompasses the following tasks:Design of a solar array with a cell area of 100 m2.- Development of deployment mechanisms to allow array retraction.- Assessment of areal mass, using latest LILT solar cell technology, potentially modified with reduced thickness.- Assessment of eigenfrequencies for arrays of up to 100 m2 area.- Demonstration ofmultiple retractions and re-deployments of the solar array by means oftest at low temperature of a representative design mock-up.- Identification of development needs.- Preparation of a roadmap.

title: INVESTIGATION OF GAS-SURFACE INTERACTIONS ON RE-USABLE UPPER STAGE LAUNCHERS - EXPRO+
description: Objectives: To develop affordable, re-usable aerodynamic shapes involving the re-entry of upper stages of launchers. Description: The use of ceramics and metallic materials on aerodynamic shapes for reusable systems technology allows for affordable and sustainable operations involving the re-entry of upper stages of launchers. This study aims at designing and prototyping the shapes with an appropriate material combination that can survive the mechanical stresses induced in the initial ascent and can subsequently survive the extreme heating and mechanically shear environment of re-entry. Also it conducts ground based experimental tests for a relevant flight profile and advances the numerical prediction of gas surface interactions. This activity is building upon a previous TDE activity on the recovery of upper stage launchers (T418-703MP) as well as the Space Rider Programme.This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition, of the descent system requirements and the trade space to be examined for materials with suitable coatings and aerodynamic shapes: - Performance analysis conducted to define the pressure and shear environment with emphasis on re-usability. - Numerical modeling and prediction of the surface catalysis for multiple flights. - Design and prototype the aerodynamic shape system for a typical upper stage recovery of small and large European launchers like Ariane next and/or VEGA-E using numerical investigations as a basis. - Perform plasma testing in relevant pressure and shear environments, supported by rebuilding and extrapolation to flight. - Evaluation of test results. - Development of a roadmap for technology maturation and guidelines for future applications. Provision for inputs for a possible future handbook.

title: ON CHIP INTEGRATED POWER CONVERTER FOR ADVANCED FIELD PROGRAMMABLE GATE ARRAYS (ARTES AT 5C.440) (RE-ISSUE)
description: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test an on-chip integrated power converter for high performance Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) applications to reduce size and footprint. Targeted Improvements: 50% reduction in FPGA application footprint, fourfold increase in reliability and 20% increase in efficiency. Description: Currently external power supplies are used to power FPGAs in space applications. This limits the performance of the FPGAs, due to unwanted resonances created by an inductive-capacitive interface, which amplifies any current spikes or perturbations. Integrating the power converter into the same package as the FPGA has the potential to overcome the above limitations, allowing for higher FPGA performance and a significant reduction of the interface pin count, as well as improving the reliability. Taking benefit from progress achieved for terrestrial applications, where the power supply is integrated in the microcontroller or FPGA, this activity will further develop the technology for space applications. A concept trade-off will be carried out to select the best integration option, either in a single- or multi-die technology, together with passive component integration. An integrated power converter breadboard will be designed, manufactured and tested in a laboratory environment.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). For additional information please go to EMITS news "Industrial Policy measures for non-primes, SMEs and RD entities in ESA programmes".

title: WORLD AGENTIC ENGINE - WAE
description: Europe has built world leading Earth Observation (EO) infrastructures, but today's exploitation paradigm remains fragmented and focused on data pipelines rather than integrated intelligence. As a result, transforming EO data into actionable insights is slow, difficult to scale, and poorly aligned with the needs of non space industries. Meanwhile, global digital leaders are advancing rapidly with geospatial foundation models, world models and agentic AI systems that reason across heterogeneous data. Without a comparable European capability, much of the value generated from European EO assets risks being externalised.To address this, the proposed activity aims to prototype a World Agentic Engine (WAE), an agentic, AI driven capability able to orchestrate models, data, and servicesusing a shared semantic layer. Built around multi mission geospatial embeddings, GFMs, and world models, it will support reasoning,prediction, scenario exploration, and cross domain decision making. Rather than duplicating data, the WAE will interface with existing infrastructures and integrate both institutional and commercial actors. A key objective is to develop and to validate the economic model of the World Agentic Engine, which will federate institutional and commercial players within a European-centric ecosystem. A primary pilot will support FAO and national forest monitoring systems, showcasing AI driven reporting and climate finance applications. Additional pilots will explore domains where agentic EO intelligence delivers operational impact. By doing so,the WAE aims to demonstrate Earth Intelligence, moving from isolated applications to an integrated, scalable, sovereign European ecosystem.

title: RF PERFORMANCE DEMONSTRATION OF AN IN-ORBIT ASSEMBLED LARGE REFLECTOR ANTENNA EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop a reduced breadboard demonstrating the assembly of shaped panels with electrical connectivity between them with the goal to assemble a large reflector antenna and validate the RF performance on ground.Description: Despite the evolution of the antenna technologies and the development of new antenna architectures, reflector antennas remain as a reliable solution when large antennas are required. In order to comply with the requirements of the future missions, reflector antennas larger than the fairing diameter of the launchers are required. Large deployable antennas based on mesh technology with different deployment mechanisms have been considered allowing the implementation of antennas in the order of 10m. New manufacturing techniques based on in-orbit assembly have been proposed in order to achieve reflector diameters in the order of 25m or larger, which it would be an enabler for new applications, for example, in telecommunications, earth observation and exploration applications. The technology based on robotic arms required for the mechanical connection of flat panels has already been demonstrated on ground. However, in order to use this structure as an antenna, the assembly of shaped panels forming a parabola and ensuring the electrical connection between them must be realized. In this activity, the technology for the connection of shaped panels with the aim of assembling a large reflector antenna shall be demonstrated, including the electrical connectivity between them. A feed shall be considered for the illumination of a reducedprototype. The RF performance of such an antenna shall be demonstrated through radiation pattern measurements and gain characterization. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements consolidation and architecture trade-off - Preliminary design and breadboarding - Detailed design and analysis - Manufacturing and integration - Testing - Conclusions and technology development roadmapDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

title: ALLOY DEVELOPMENT FOR HIGH PRESSURE AND OXYGEN RICH ENVIRONMENT PROPULSION EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop new European alloys for high-pressure, oxygen-rich propulsion applications, enhancing performance, manufacturability and supply chain resilience for next-generation launch vehicles.Description: Propulsion remains a key driver in launch vehicle performance, particularly as the sector pursues higher thrust capabilities through operation at elevated temperatures. Applications such as high-thrust engines, oxygen-rich pre-burners (used in staged combustion), gas generators, and high-pressure liquid oxygen (LOx) turbopumps must operate under extreme thermal and mechanical loads in highly reactive environments. At present, Europe lacks a material solution capable of meeting these demands. ESA teams, across several directorates have jointly identified this as a critical capability gap. While progress has been made in non-member states countries, Europe currently lacks materials capable of operating reliably in oxygen-rich and high-pressure environments. The development of tailored European alloy systems would directly support ongoing launcher developments, both from established industry and emerging companies working on micro, small and medium launch vehicles. These materials would serve as a strategic enabler across the sector, particularly for reusable platforms. The activity aimsto develop novel high-performance alloys suitable for use in oxygen-rich and high-pressure environments. These alloys must offer high thermal conductivity, mechanical strength at elevated temperatures, and compatibility with additive manufacturing (AM). Candidatematerial families include refractory alloys, superalloys, and oxide-dispersion-strengthened (ODS) alloys. Computational tools, including artificial intelligence (AI), will guide the design process to optimise performance and manufacturability while ensuring alignment with European supply chain capabilities. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define propulsion application requirements (temperature, duration, material compatibility, structural loads). - Conduct state-of-the-art assessment across candidate alloy families. - Use AI to support design of new alloy compositions meeting propulsion and AM requirements. - Produce experimental powder batches for selected alloy formulations. - Manufacture and test printed coupons in representative operational environments. -Evaluate manufacturability, including welding compatibility and potential for repair. - Perform preliminary life cycle analysis and assess European sourcing of raw elements. - Outline a roadmap for further maturation in subsequent projects.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: SURVEY AND FEASIBILITY STUDY OF OPTICAL TECHNOLOGIES FOR THE L4 ENCELADUS LANDER EXPRO PLUS
description: ObjectivesTo perform a survey study and experimental tests of optical technologies to demonstrate the suitability of this technology for ranging and surface characterization in the frame of the L4-Enceladus mission.DescriptionOptical technologies (such as LIDAR systems) have proven their efficiency for ranging and hazard detection for terrestrial and space applications.This activity therefore aims performing a survey and feasibility study as well as experimental tests to demonstrate the suitability of optical technologies deployed onboard the ESA L4-Enceladus lander to secure the landing with the following goals:- primary task: altimeter for thelander (max altitude of 20 - 100 km TBC), with capabilities of analyzing snow surface properties at close range (10 - 100m TBC) to support the lander site selection regarding mechanical surface stability- secondary task: mapping of surface topology (e.g. surfaceinclination, obstacles such crevasses and boulders) The activity shall contain as a minimum the following tasks:1) Review of L4 needs and requirements vs existing optical technologies and devices. In particular, review existing LIDAR technologies/solutions and recent developments for Moon/Mars environments.2) Procure or build and as needed adapt suitable Optical instruments to be used as a prototype.3) Conduct performance/reliability tests in analogous to Enceladus ice and snow surfaces.Conduct test campaigns focused on snow/ice surfaces addressing the primary objectives.4) Derive a technology development roadmap for instruments adaptations to fulfill mission needs. Determine requirements for Enceladus use-case with a focus on reliability testing in relevant Enceladus Lander environment to further raise the TRL.

title: ERS-EO ALPSTAR FEDERATED LAYER DEFINITION AND PRELIMINARY IMPLEMENTATION (ACTIVITY 2B)
description: Activity 2B addresses Phase B of the Alpstar Federation Layer, aiming to consolidate requirements, architecture, and prototype validation for a federated, multi stakeholder space system. Building on the MRD 2.0, this phase will define and specify all functional, technical, and security requirements of the Federation Layer, including secure interfaces with commercial service providers and Alpstar Nodes via unidirectional "diode" connections.The activity encompasses the full design of the Alpstar system architecture and the development and demonstration of a User Ground Segment prototype. Comprehensive specifications will be produced for all major Federation Layer components, ensuring interoperability, security, and scalability across federated participants.The procurement also includes the acquisition of a minimum of three months of satellite data, necessary to support validation and testing of the Ground Segment prototype under operationally representative conditions.A key deliverable of this phase is a User Ground Segment prototype featuring:A role based user interface, enabling differentiated access and operational views.An initial implementation of the Digital Governance Agent (DGA), enforcing a first set of provisional federation rules and acting as the central mission management and planning capability.The Alpstar Federated Layer shall integrate the following core functionalities:Digital Governance Agent (DGA)for federation rule enforcement and central mission managementSecure Data Pooling Service for controlled dissemination of observation resultsFederated Ledger to record and audit transactionsStandardised APIs interfacing with Nodes (FOS and PDGS)Federated Data Lake hosted in a cloud environmentVirtual Constellation Management for coordinated asset utilisationFederated CatalogueCross federation taskingNATO FMN / Joint ISR tasking interfaces routed to AlpstarRole based user interfaceFederation dashboard for operational and governance oversightWith a target duration of 12 months, the expected outcomes of Activity 2B include:Complete specifications of the Federation LayerDefinition of the Federation Layer architectureRough Order of Magnitude (ROM)cost estimate for implementationIdentification of the industrial consortiumDevelopment plan and integrated scheduleDemonstration of the User Ground Segment prototypeThis phase will provide the technical, architectural, and organisational foundations required to progress Alpstar toward a fully operational, secure, and governed federated space capability.

title: BULGARIA AWARENESS RAISING AND EDUCATION STUDY - EXPRO PLUS
description: The primary objective is to increase awareness of the dependencies on and benefits of space within the general population of Bulgaria. The secondary objective is to increase the interest in pursuing space as a career amongst children and young adults and to promote the wider uptake of space based services in the wider Bulgarian ecosystem. Awareness raising and education activities are fundamental not only to prepare the future workforce, but also to help building generations of future citizens who are suitably informed about the benefits of space to both themselves and society as a whole. The interest generated by Europe's achievements in space can act as motivation for the education and the benefit of the younger generation - from early age to early professional levels - as well as to encourage those in non-space industries to be aware of the possible space based solutions available to them.While the ITT is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, the present ITT is addressed only to legal entities of Bulgaria registered in ESA-STAR, as prime tenderer.

title: ENCELADUS TERRAIN AND TOPOGRAPHY DATA PROCESSING AND ANALYSIS
description: The landing on Enceladus, one of Saturn's moons, as part of the Science L4 mission, presents significant challenges. This is due tothe unique cryovolcanic environment and our limited understanding of Enceladus's surface compared to other planetary and lunar bodies. Although the Cassini and Voyager missions have gathered extensive scientific data using their cameras and sensors, the data related to Enceladus has only been partially processed and primarily for scientific purposes. Therefore, the goal of this activity is tocollect and process all available scientific data and information about Enceladus'senvironment. This shall specifically support the planning and robust design of the L4 orbiter and lander

title: IOD/IOV SERVICE (HORIZON EUROPE) - IHE1-4 CUBESAT PROJECT 2024
description: One of the main objectives of the Space Strategy for Europe is to foster a globally competitive and innovative European space sector in particular by improving support to technological maturation, for sub-systems, equipment and technologies, including in-orbit demonstration and validation activities, to reduce time to market. To ensure the European Union non-dependence and competitiveness in technologies, there is a clear need for a regular, sustainable, cost-effective and responsive In-Orbit Demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) service in the European Union. Space flight heritage in real conditions and environment is often required to de-risk innovations such as new technologies, products, concepts, architectures, and operations techniques, are they for unique or recurrent, institutional or commercial missions. On 31 March 2023, the European Commission issued a call for expression of interest for IOD/IOV Experiments needing aggregation (available here: https://defence-industry-space.ec.europa.eu/funding-and-grants/calls-proposals/orbit-demonstrationvalidation-20232026_en). The objective is to promote European competitiveness and non-dependence by offering flight opportunities through IOD/IOV for European experiments. The European Commission expects to select a number of experiments that would fly with the Horizon Europe Cassini In-Orbit Demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) service. The IHE1-4 Cubesat Project aims to provide the Horizon Europe In-Orbit demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) service with IOD/IOV Carriers based on European cubesats platforms, with a volume of 12U format. title: IOD/IOV SERVICE (HORIZON EUROPE) - IHE5-1 RIDESHARE OPPORTUNITIES FOR EXPERIMENTS NEEDING AGGREGATION
description: One of the main objectives of the Space Strategy for Europe is to foster a globally competitive and innovative European space sector, in particular by improving support to technological maturation, for sub-systems, equipment and technologies, including in-orbit demonstration and validation activities, to reduce time to market. To ensure the European Union non-dependence and competitiveness in technologies, there is a clear need for a regular, sustainable, cost-effective and responsive In-Orbit Demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) service in the European Union. Space flight heritage in real conditions and environment is often required to de-risk innovations such as new technologies, products, concepts, architectures, and operations techniques, are they for unique or recurrent, institutional or commercial missions. On 31 March 2023, the European Commission issued a call for expression of interest for IOD/IOV Experiments needing aggregation (available here: https://defence-industry-space.ec.europa.eu/funding-and-grants/calls-proposals/orbit-demonstrationvalidation-20232026_en). The objective is to promote European competitiveness and non-dependence by offering flight opportunities through IOD/IOV for European experiments. The European Commission expects to select a number of experiments that would fly with the Horizon Europe Cassini In-Orbit Demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) service. The activity "IHE5-1 Rideshare Opportunities for Experiments needing Aggregation" will result in a number of flight opportunities which will provide the Horizon Europe In-Orbit demonstration/Validation (IOD/IOV) service with a range of flight opportunities to fly IOD/IOV Experiments (selected in the frame of the call above) on-board existing missions. The procurement of Rideshare Opportunities for Experiments needing aggregation will be organized in two steps: Establishment of a pool of European Rideshare Service Providers for the implementation of Rideshare services in the 2024 - 2027 timeframe, through the award of frame contracts to each selected Rideshare Service Provider. Procurement of specific Rideshare services for selected IOD/IOV Experiments among the pool of European Rideshare Service Providers, through the award of Work Orders.The Rideshare service activities include: Conduct a thorough requirements analysis for each Experiment. Define the technical and operational requirements for Experiment accommodation, including interface specifications and environmental constraints. Develop detailed designs for the mechanical, electrical, thermal, and data interfaces between the Experiments and the spacecraft bus. Create Interface Control Documents(ICDs) for each Experiment. Develop a comprehensive Integration Plan that includes step-by-step procedures for integrating each Experiment onto the spacecraft bus. Identify required tools, facilities, and personnel for integration activities. Define Model Philosophy for the Experiment Define qualification and acceptance approach for the Experiment Develop a Test Plan that outlines functional and environmental testing procedures for the integrated Experiments. Conduct tests to validate the integration, including vibration, thermal, and functional tests. Verify interface compatibility between the Experiment and the available spacecraft bus. Integrate Experiments onto the spacecraft bus using appropriate interfaces and mounting techniques. Conduct functional and environmental testing to ensure Experiment integrity and readiness for launch on the spacecraft bus. Provide or procure the launch service and necessary ground support equipment. Monitor Experiment initial operations from the spacecraft bus. Perform in orbit operations and support to ensure Experiments achieve intended operational status and functionality. Deliver in orbit Experiment data to the Experiment Providers, with a right to use for ESA and EU. This project is funded by the European Union. ESA is the contracting authority and runs the procurement under the ESA/REG/001 rev.5. adapted as per the signed FFPA agreement."

title: S2P S2-NA-03: 2ND SPACE WEATHER NANOSATELLITES ENHANCEMENT - PHASE B/C/D/E
description: This activity will implement a second Space Weather nanosatellite mission to enhance the measurements to be collected by the Distributed Space Weather Sensor System. The mission follows the principle of providing mission/data-as-a-service to feed into (pre-) operational services. ESA is specifying the mission requirements to be achieved, including the requirements on the type, quality, cadence, and latency as well as availability of the measurement data to be provided. The design and implementation of a mission to collectthese measurements is under the responsibility of the awarded contractor. The initial data provision shall cover the first year of operations, with the option to extend the mission for two more years.

title: EUROPEAN TERABIT PER SECOND ETHERNET PACKET SWITCH/ROUTER IP CORE FOR MULTI-ORBIT CONSTELLATIONS (ARTES AT 5C.540)
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop, manufacture and test an Ethernet switch/router Intellectual Property (IP)core and test chip supporting layers 1 to 3 packet processing for constellations. The IP core shall be developed, implemented on a test chip using the optimal UDSM ASIC technology node(s) selected as part of this activity to achieve the desired performance, and tested using a validation breadboard.Targeted Improvements: Enabling a European or Canadian source of terabit class ethernet switch/routers for multi-orbit constellation applications.Description: Cost sensitive, high volume multi-orbit constellation solutions require a tailored ethernet packet switch/router adapted to high data rates (at and above 100 Gbps), number of ports (16 and more) and supported protocols. An ethernet switch/router, scalable in data rate and number of ports and supporting layer 1 to 3 protocols, is not available from a European or Canadian supplier. Existing commercial solutions cannot be readily adapted to the needs of satcom applications in low earth orbit and multi-orbit constellations.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach. In Phase 1, an ethernet switch/router IP core shall be developed utilising ultra-deep sub-micron (UDSM) ASIC technology (targeting 7nm or below) to achieve 1 terabit per second data throughput for low earth orbit and multi-orbit constellation applications. The data rateper port and number of ports forming a channel shall be configurable to suit multiple applications (configurable number of ports from 4 to at least 16 ports, with configurable port data rate from 1Gbps to at least100Gbps per port). Multi-protocol label switchingand the internet protocol shall be supported. Phase 1 will conclude with the completed IP core design, verified and synthesised in the design environment, to generate the ASIC test chip tape-out files ready for fabrication. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 2,000 kEuro.In the second phase, the IP core will be implemented in the selected UDSM ASIC technology as an ASIC test-chip (via a Multi Project Wafer Run or shared Full Mask Run). A validation breadboard shall be designed and built to undertake performance testing of thetest chip. The test chip shall be representative of a scaled version of a final product and shall be tested in relevant environment.IP cores developed in this activity shall be available for further development by ESA Member State and Canadian industries at fair and reasonable market conditions.

title: 5G DISTRIBUTED UNIT PROCESSOR AND ASSOCIATED NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORK G-NODEB SOFTWARE (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5A.099) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture, and test a processor breadboard and associated software implementing a distributed unit (DU) onboard a satellite. TheDU will implement Radio Link Control (RLC) and Medium Access Control (MAC) functions, optimized for Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN), to address processing, memory andpower constraints, as well as service needs in terms of cells and user numbers The feasibility and implementation of control unit (CU) functions on the 5G g-NodeB (gNB)should be addressed by the activity depending on the selected 5G system split and targeted system capacityTargetedImprovements: - Increase the DU throughput by a factor of 10 with respect to currently existing terrestrial network solutions (TN) implemented on space representative hardware.- Increase by a factor of 10 the number of cells handled by the DU, with respect to existing TN solutions.Description: Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs) require optimized handling of link-layer functions to mitigate the effects of long propagation delays, fluctuating signal conditions, and limitedbandwidth. Conventional NTNs rely on extensive ground infrastructure to manage link-layer functions such as scheduling, retransmission control, and resource allocation.Implementing full CU/DU on-board with high throughput is currently unfeasible due to the high system bandwidth to route and the limited processing power available.This activity shall develop a high-throughput (target 100 Gbps) satellite router breadboard, integrating an onboard CU/DU implemented on a radiation-tolerant multi-coreprocessor.This activity will design, manufacture, and test a processor breadboard and associated software implementing a distributed unit (DU) onboard a satellite.The Radio Link Control (RLC) layer will provide:1. Segmentation and reassembly optimized for dynamic satellite link conditions.2. Retransmission control managed onboard to reduce latency and dependency on ground stations.The Medium Access Control (MAC) layer will handle:1. Onboard scheduling and resource allocation to optimize time-frequency resource use.2. Adaptive HARQ (Hybrid Automatic Repeat Request) to balance error correction and latency.3. Inter-beam coordination to optimize multi-beam traffic distribution. The CU shall perform real-time processing, ensuring efficient and reliable network operation withoutexcessive feeder link traffic. Engineering tasks include system architecture definition, hardware / software integration, and performance validation through breadboardtesting in a representative NTN environment.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: CYBER SECURITY BUILDING BLOCKS FOR SPACE SYSTEMS
description: The objective(s) of this activity are the following:a) Design and implement an end-to-end Space Segment testbed that can constitute a security reference architecture, including a number of cyber security building blocks.b) Perform a security assessment and verification of the implemented security measures using the selected cyber security building blocks.c) Identify potential security enhancements, that can constitute candidates for further technical developments into products.The targeted current Technology ReadinessLevel (TRL) of this activity is 4 [RD1].WORK TO BE PERFORMED1 Work LogicThe work will be organised in two phases and the following tasks:Phase 1: Definition of cyber security building blocks and Space Segment testbedoTask 1: State-of-the-art survey of mission scenarios, security threats, relevant legislations and regulations and security technologiesoTask 2: Consolidationof Space Segment modular security reference architecture, including identification of required cyber security building blocks andspecification of system Space Segment security requirements.oTask 3: Specification of Space Segment testbed requirements (including incorporated cyber security building blocks), design and implementation and test planningPhase 2: Development, implementation and testing of cyber security building blocks and Space Segment testbedoTask 4: Development of the Space Segment testbedoTask 5: Space Segment Testbed Testing, Security Assessment and Vulnerability MitigationoTask 6: Lessons learnt and proposed roadmap for further (other than [RD16] building blocks development (including high level specifications)Note that phase 2 will be authorised to implement the agreed building blocks, subject to a successful Phase 1 and acceptance of a proposal for the conversion of the Phase 2 price from ceilingprice to Firm Fixed Price.

title: HIGH EFFICIENT COST EFFECTIVE SOLAR CELLS EXPRO+
description: Objective: Development of solar cells with high efficiency and cost reduction. 50% cost reduction of state of the art space solar cells. Target in efficiency of 28% BOL, 25% EOL and based on III-V multijunction technology.Description: The current landscape of satellite production is dominated by a strong need in the cost reduction. This is particularly true for the solar cells to be used in space application, where cost on system level is strongly related to efficiency. In order to remain competitive in this market sector significant development activities are required to not fall behind and create dependencies on non-European countries. Therefore, on solar cell level, innovative solutions are needed that aim at a best compromise between cost and efficiency. Furthermore, solar cell lead times from European solar cell manufacturers currently can easily exceed 24 months. This puts a threat also to a number of ESA missions which strongly depend on those solar cells. If Europe fails to change this situation quickly there is a high risk that these supply gaps might be filled by non-European suppliers. The consequences of such a scenario has been seen in the past in the terrestrial photovoltaic market and has to be avoided by all means. The target of this activity is to obtain 50% cost reduction with respect to state of the art space solar cells, with a target in efficiency of 28% BOL, 25% EOL and based on III-V multijunction technology. Implicitly a cost reduction will also be typically accompanied by a strong reduction in process time and consequently will lead to an increase in throughput and in production capacity. Thus, a European product will be made available which is at the same timecompetitive in terms of price and also available in sufficient quantities to address the market needs. Several strategies can be followed to reduce the costs, like e.g. increasing the automation and standardisation of all the processes within the manufacturing line of solar cells. Another important aspect would be the reduction of the epitaxial growth times by increasing growth rates. The first tests have been performed showing that growth times can be reduced from several hours to around 5-10 minutes. And then also spin-in from terrestrial photovoltaic production shall be investigated. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Solar cell designdefinition targeting BOL efficiency of 28% and 25% EOL (1E15 1MeV electron equivalent) with significantly reduced complexity allowing for cost reduction of 50% - Derivation of technology building blocks for achieving the above defined targets - First breadboarding of solar cells with the defined design and using innovative manufacturing processes to achieve the targeted cost reduction - Testing the breadboard, such as irradiation test campaigns with electrical performance tests before and after.

title: T309-801GD MULTI-ASSET DISTRIBUTED SIMULATIONS (EXPRO+)
description: Currently multi-asset simulations of exploration missions comprised of i.e. robotic assets,orbiters/relays and ground data systemsare performed individually and mostly in isolation byindividual sites with respective simulators for each asset. The goal of this activity is to investigatemulti-asset, distributed simulations capabilities for full end-to-end mission simulations of futureexploration missions spanning lander, orbiters, relays and surface assets in different locations.This activity investigates the various scenarios (i.e. current ExoMars simulation architectures, futureneeds of the Sample Fetch Rover (SFR) and European Large Logistic Lander (EL3) missions) andhow, within their respective mission scenarios, simulation systems can be distributed, synchronizedand orchestrated either in local (i.e. data center) environments, or across different agencies orindustrial partners.The challenge to beaddressed is to achieve the capability to execute full mission segments (suchas full egress campaigns) with all distributed teams and experts - usually distributed over differentagencies and industrial partners in a as realistic as possible set-up, meaning interactions,coordination and real-time data during the simulation shall be available to all actors within thesimulation. Various technological frameworks exist to interconnect simulators on the technical level.However, this activity shall specifically focus on thecoordination aspects, synchronousmanagement or orchestration that is required and suitable above the pure interfaces level to realizesuch distributed simulations. To validate defined architectures, using agile developmentmethodologies this activity aims at developing a proof of concept to demonstrate keyrecommendations of this activity. The final architecture and technology recommendations that couldsupport future SFR and EL3 mission simulation needs is captured in a roadmap for theirintroduction.

title: TERAHERTZ LOW-NOISE AMPLIFIER - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a low-noise amplifier (LNA) to approaching the THz boundary and to optimize the LNA noise performance by process evolutions and advanced design.Description: Continuous advancements in semiconductor technologies like Indium Phosphide (InP) and Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) pseudo-morphic and metamorphic high electron mobility transistors (pHEMT and mHEMT) have made low-noise amplifiers (LNA) possible at increasingly higher frequencies. Currently efforts are taken to reach frequencies close to 1 THz. Aggressive reduction of the gate length has been essential in this progress and gate-lengths have already been realized experimentally in 20 nm scale in a previous ESA project (ref. no. T106-603EF). Availability of low-noise amplifiers (LNA) at sub-mm wave frequencies and above 600 GHz is needed for future space-borne radiometers for Earth observation for three reasons: Firstly, employment of a low-noise pre-amplifier in front of a Schottky mixer allows improvement in receiver sensitivity. Secondly, substantial reduction of Local Oscillator (LO) power requirement is possible in heterodyne receivers by allowing low-barrier Schottky technology in the down-conversion. This can facilitate multipixel heterodyne instruments based on microwave photonics downconverter and centralized photonics LO. Thirdly, LNAs make direct-detection radiometers possible, allowing significant simplification of the receiver architecture, as nolocal oscillator will be needed. At system level, in complex heterodyne instruments, the LNA also helps in reducing backward leakage of the local oscillator signal, therefore improving system auto-compatibility. This activity aims at pushing the LNA technology towards THz regime based on the emerging state-of-the-art technologies and design skills. LNA demonstrators in this activity are designed, manufactured and tested at two dedicated frequencies in the vicinity of 1 THz. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Review the latest mHEMT process evolutions - Optimize the LNA noise performance by process evolutions and advanced design. - Design, manufacture and test a low-noise amplifier (LNA) at three frequencies of interest: 770 GHz, 874 GHz and 1.1 THz. - Compare the results with current state-of-the-art, derive lessons learned and provide roadmap for future related activities.

title: ADHA INSTRUMENT CONTROLLER UNIT (ICU) - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop an ADHA-compliant Instrument Controller Unit (ICU) usable standalone or with standard ADHAhardware for Earth, exploration, science, and navigation missions.Description:The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) is a collaboration between ESA, European satellite primesand data handling equipment suppliers. It includes the definition of an architecture for data handling unit basedon standard module functions. A standard module procurement flow has been defined -- as well as astandardized backplane connector and electrical interfaces. This allows independent development ofinteroperable modules that can be connected in ADHA units. This activity aims to develop an ADHA-compatibleICU (Instrument Control Unit), with integrated Data Processing Unit(s) (DPUs). The modules target the overall control functions of an instrument with several secondary units (FEE units, mechanism control units, cryocooler unit, etc). The modules will at least include an ICU processor module, and instrument I/O module(s). The ICU processor module shall be capable to act as the system controller of an ADHA unit, running high-levelinstrument application software and providing standard high-level interfaces for connection to the spacecraftplatform units, or other instruments and implementing all the necessary functions to control peripheral ADHAmodules in the unit, including network routing capabilities. The I/O modules willcover lower-level interface functions such as additional low-speed digital interfaces (CAN, RS422/RS485, etc), and discrete interfaces(HPCs, thermistor readout, heater control, secondary power, etc) and others typically found in an ICU unit.The ICU will be basedon state-of-the-art technologies, offering a higher level of integration and performancecompared to previous generation products, and be able to perform e.g. advanced (AI-based) FDIR methodsfor the monitoring and control of a payload.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Use case analysis of instrument control units for instruments on institutional missions.- Modules requirements analysis (use case analysis, ADHA documents, ADHA ICU draft specification),including functional split between ICU processor module and I/O modules.- ICU architecture design and key components trade-off and selection.- Modules engineering model design, including electrical, firmware, and base software.- Modules engineering model manufacturing.- Modules engineering model functional and performance verification and validation.- Validation testing of modules using an ADHA backplane, in an ADHA unit rack.- Performancebenchmarks and end-to-end data handling demonstration.Deliverables: Engineering Model, Report
