title: EFFECTS OF THE SPATIO-TEMPORALLY VARYING ATMOSPHERE ON SAR IMAGING: THE IONOSPHERE CASE - EXPRO PLUS
description: To derive more accurate expression of atmosphere irregularities effects with a focus on the ionosphere, and devise mitigation techniques for both geo- and sun-synchronous SAR imaging systemsDescription: For Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) systems the atmospheric turbulence is generally assumed to be time-invariant during the synthetic aperture time due to itsshort duration. Such assumption is not always correct, as horizontal atmospheric drifts and vortices exist. Especially for SAR systems at low frequency (P-Band, L-Band), SAR operating on repeat-track basis, geo-synchronous SAR systems characterised by long integration time and extensive imaging scene, the ionosphere can have an important role on the performance. Furthermore, both temporal andspatial variations of the ionosphere have to be jointly taken into account, which further complicates their characterisation. Therefore, the effects of the flowing ionospheric irregularities need to be investigated, aiming in particular to image shifts, defocusing and repeat-track interferometry. The aim of this activity is to provide a comprehensive analysis to evaluate effects of both spatial variation and flowing ionospheric irregularities on SAR systems operating both at P-, L- and C-band. In particular, the ionospheric scintillations, which act remarkably in the polar cap and equatorial zone at night need to be considered. The Ionosphere characterisation shall originate from previous developments, analyses performed in the framework of previous missions developments and from knowledge built up in the navigation community. This activity encompasses the following tasks: -Analytical models of the physical effects of spatial-temporally ionospheric background variations on the SAR signal. - Assessment of the impacts on the SAR performancesdemonstrating, both theoretically and numerically, the geometric fidelity, focusing aspect and interferometry quality (i.e., relative image shifts and the decorrelation of interferometric pairs, interferometric phase screen errors). - Validation of the models andof the performance analysis using ionospheric monitoring measurements (i.e., Global Positioning System). - Develop mitigation techniques. - The implementation of the aforementioned components in a software framework. The methods developed in this activity are expected to be developed in such a way that they can be later broadened to other atmospheric effects such as tropospheric scintillations. Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member Statescan access to it and can provide update to the community of users.Deliverables: Report, SoftwareProcurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SMEs RD Entities. Description: To derive more accurate expression of atmosphere irregularities effects with a focus on the ionosphere, and devise mitigation techniques for both geo- and sun-synchronous SAR imaging systemsDescription: For Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) systems the atmospheric turbulence is generally assumed to be time-invariant during the synthetic aperture time due to itsshort duration. Such assumption is not always correct, as horizontal atmospheric drifts and vortices exist. Especially for SAR systems at low frequency (P-Band, L-Band), SAR operating on repeat-track basis, geo-synchronous SAR systems characterised by long integration time and extensive imaging scene, the ionosphere can have an important role on the performance. Furthermore, both temporal andspatial variations of the ionosphere have to be jointly taken into account, which further complicates their characterisation. Therefore, the effects of the flowing ionospheric irregularities need to be investigated, aiming in particular to image shifts, defocusing and repeat-track interferometry. The aim of this activity is to provide a comprehensive analysis to evaluate effects of both spatial variation and flowing ionospheric irregularities on SAR systems operating both at P-, L- and C-band. In particular, the ionospheric scintillations, which act remarkably in the polar cap and equatorial zone at night need to be considered. The Ionosphere characterisation shall originate from previous developments, analyses performed in the framework of previous missions developments and from knowledge built up in the navigation community. This activity encompasses the following tasks: -Analytical models of the physical effects of spatial-temporally ionospheric background variations on the SAR signal. - Assessment of the impacts on the SAR performancesdemonstrating, both theoretically and numerically, the geometric fidelity, focusing aspect and interferometry quality (i.e., relative image shifts and the decorrelation of interferometric pairs, interferometric phase screen errors). - Validation of the models andof the performance analysis using ionospheric monitoring measurements (i.e., Global Positioning System). - Develop mitigation techniques. - The implementation of the aforementioned components in a software framework. The methods developed in this activity are expected to be developed in such a way that they can be later broadened to other atmospheric effects such as tropospheric scintillations. Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member Statescan access to it and can provide update to the community of users.Deliverables: Report, SoftwareProcurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SMEs RD Entities. title: POST-ISS PRE-PHASE A STUDIES - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to perform two parallel Pre-Phase A system studies for the Post-ISS Scenario3, engaging Europeanindustries expertise after an ESA-internal Concurrent Engineering cycle. The Post ISS Scenario 3 represents a strategically distinct option in which Europe leads the development of a modular, multi-partner Outpost in LEO. This scenario functions both as a long term autonomy instrument and as a risk mitigation path. The proposed Pre-Phase A studies aim at consolidating the feasibility, architecture, utilisation, and technology requirements of a European-led LEO outpost in cooperation with CSA, JAXA and additional partners. They will mature the Scenario3 Outpost concept to a level enabling ESA decision-making for the Post-ISS transition by end 2026.

title: S3-PD-01 NEOMIR PHASE B1
description: The purpose of this activity is to study in detail the system and subsystem requirements for a planetary defence mission that aims at building a space-based infrared telescope dedicated to detection and characterisation of Near-Earth Objects (NEOs) that approach from the direction of the Sun. The mission builds on extensive work done by the Agency and European industry between 2022 and 2026. The target is to reach a consolidated mission and satellite architecture, finalize the major trade-offs and generate system and subsystem level requirements. In particular, the study will provide a consolidated spacecraft design and payload interface supported by detailed analyses and prepare the implementation phase including the establishment of the spacecraft development plan, preparation activities for Phase B2/C/D/E1 procurement, and cost estimates. The study will be carried out in two phases: one phase of 18months with a goal of reaching the objectives of an SRR-level review, and an additional optional 6-months phase that will aim at ingesting additional data fed by the Agency on the payloads into the system level design.

title: S3-SW-07- SPACE WEATHER HOSTED-PAYLOAD DATA-AS-A-SERVICE DEMONSTRATOR
description: The objective of this activity is to implement and deliver a data service for Space Weather data based on a Hosted Payload approach. The following set of measurements shall be provided in near-real time from a Low Earth Orbit with an altitude around 1000 km:oThe flux of energetic electrons (0.3 - 3 MeV) and protons (10 - 200 MeV), as present in Earth's radiation belts and from Solar Particle EventsoThe flux of thermal electrons and ions (10 eV to 24 keV) to measure the 3D distribution of precipitating particles.The lifetime of the hosting mission is expected to be at least 5 years, so that the data service could be provided for an extended amountof time, while the activity only covers the first year of service provision. The launch of the hosting mission shall be before end of 2028. In addition to the instrument data also the associated ground processing prototypes shall be developed and delivered to ESAfor their integration to the Space Weather Payload Data Centre.

title: DERIVATION OF SPACEBORNE MISSION REQUIREMENTS FOR SOIL MOISTURE RETRIEVAL WITH CLOSURE PHASE EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: Surface soil moisture can be retrieved from SAR backscatter data; however, these techniques are sensitive to surface roughness changes and extensive spatial averaging is required. In the last years, a significant amount of work has been done to establish a framework for the retrieval of surface soil moisture from InSAR products. It is hereby proposed not to use the interferometric phase directly, since interferometric phase measurement are also sensitive to many other contributors (atmosphere, deformation, orbital errors,...), but to use the so-called closure phase. The closure phase is the cyclic product of spatially averaged interferograms between a combinations of three SAR acquisitions. The idea is to increase the accuracy to of surface soil moisture measurements by using theclosure phase method or by combining the closure phase method with amplitude-based techniques.Currently, there exists no mission dedicated to providing surface soil moisture products, which are retrieved from closure phase stacks. Even though ideas for such a missions exist, quantified Level-1 performance requirements that are compatible with the required surface soil moisture measurement accuracy when using this technique are not yet available. During this activity, a simulation tool shall be developed to systematically analysing the surface soil moisture retrieval performance from closure phase stacks in dependence of Level-1 product performances, instrument and mission parameters and scene parameters. After implementation and validation, this tool shall be used to analyse the sensitivity of the surface soil moisture retrieval performance as a function of the different Level-1 and system parameters. Further, this tool shall incorporate different models to analyse how the results depend on them. The performed analysis shall be used to derive instrument, mission and Level-1 performance requirements to achieve the best moisture estimation performance from closure phase stacks. The derived requirements shall be used to formulate recommendations for future mission ideas targeting the surface soil moisture retrieval from closure phases. The goal of this activity is to achieve a systematic analysis of the requirements, limitations and error sources of the closure phase techniques for surface soil moisture retrieval.

title: EGV-PILOT: GEODETIC FOUNDATIONS FOR FUTURE EARTH OBSERVATION - EXPRO PLUS
description: EGV Pilot is an ESA pilot study aimed at structuring, mapping and assessing the geodetic foundations required to support future Earth Observation missions and Earth system science. The activity focuses on the role of geodetic observations and products as foundational enablers for Earth system monitoring, mission preparation, and the generation of long term geodetic data records. It builds on internationally coordinated developments on Essential Geodetic Variables (EGVs), in particular within GGOS and IAG, and translates these advances into an ESA-relevant framework aligned with the Earth Observation Science Strategy (EOSS), FutureEO missions, and other ESA programmatic elements. The study will establish clear traceability between geodetic requirements, products, observing systems and future EO missions. It will assess the readiness and maturity of geodetic observations and products, identify missing or degraded capabilities, and analyse how future ESA space and ground segment infrastructures could strengthen the geodetic foundations. Explicit consideration will be given to synergies with ESA missions such as GENESIS and NGGM/MAGIC, as well as to preparedness for integration into Digital Twin Earth.

title: NAVISP-EL1-121-RESILIENT PNT BASED ON LASERS - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: General DescriptionThis activity aims to design and validate a laser-based positioning system as a resilient alternative to GNSS for safety-critical operations. It will develop a multi-beam optical receiver terminal capable of acquiring and demodulating PNT signals over an optical carrier. The system will implement real-time state estimation using ToA, TDoA, or AoA techniques. A functional prototype combining optical transmitter and receiver subsystems will be built and tested. Demonstrations will include multi-beam reception on land and an optical PNT link between airborne and ground stations. The goal is to provide secure, interference-immune PNT for applications such as precision instrument landing systems. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity

title: SUB-MM WAVE NOISE SOURCES FOR INTERNAL CALIBRATION SUB-SYSTEMS - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To evaluate the capability of heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) technology (such SiGe as and/or InP) as an internal calibrator noise source at sub-mm wave frequencies and manufacture a heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBT) based noise sources at two selected frequencies such as 325 GHz and 448 GHz.Description: Microwave radiometer calibration routine onboard a satellite is currently based on the measurement of external well known reference targets such as cold sky and onboard blackbody target. However, external calibration implies complex moving mechanics and long calibration cycles which are non-optimum from system performance perspective and therefore set certain limitations to instrument performance. Considerable improvements in smaller fluctuation of noise power density are foreseen by complementing or replacing the mechanically switched quasi-optical external calibration systems by internal calibration sub-systems (ICSS) based on electrically switched active semiconductor devices. Semiconductor based noise sources (cold or hot) are key blocks in these ICSS units which will benefit developments of future EO sounders and imagers on small platforms and cube-sats as well as multipixel imagers on bigger platforms. ICSS concept based active cold-loads have already been adopted in Copernicus Imaging Radiometer (CIMR). At higher mm-wave frequencies, hot load -based ICSS's are currently being developed for applications at 89 GHz and 183 GHz based on noise diodes and between 200-250 GHz based on HBTs. Development of a HEMT-based noise source is ongoing at 325 GHz. This activity aims to manufacture a breadboard of a noise source waveguide modules based on HBT technology (e.g. SiGe/InP/GaAs) at two selected sub-mm frequencies of interest for future EO instruments, such as 325 GHz and 448 GHz. The stability of the HBT-based noise sources will be compared with counterparts built on different technologies by means of theoretical assessment and experimental results where available. The HEMT technology provides advantage having the highest frequency capability as anoise source due to its high transition frequency which is already in 1 THz region. However, the anticipated advantage of HBT in comparison to HEMT is its inherently smaller fluctuation of noise power density - a key parameter for a calibrator. The recent developments in HBT technologies (both SiGe and InP) and their frequency capability open possibilities to implementation of a HBT noise source up to sub-mm region which would be a very desirable component for a stable ICSS's. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Noise source requirements definition from system level - Preliminary to critical design of a noise source waveguide modules basedon HBT technology at two selected sub-mm frequencies such as 325 GHz and 448 GHz - Manufacturing and characterization of the breadboardDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

Semiconductor based noise sources (cold or hot) are key blocks in these ICSS units which will benefit developments of future EO sounders and imagers on small platforms and cube-sats as well as multipixel imagers on bigger platforms. ICSS concept based active cold-loads have already been adopted in Copernicus Imaging Radiometer (CIMR). At higher mm-wave frequencies, hot load -based ICSS's are currently being developed for applications at 89 GHz and 183 GHz based on noise diodes and between 200-250 GHz based on HBTs. Development of a HEMT-based noise source is ongoing at 325 GHz. This activity aims to manufacture a breadboard of a noise source waveguide modules based on HBT technology (e.g. SiGe/InP/GaAs) at two selected sub-mm frequencies of interest for future EO instruments, such as 325 GHz and 448 GHz. The stability of the HBT-based noise sources will be compared with counterparts built on different technologies by means of theoretical assessment and experimental results where available. The HEMT technology provides advantage having the highest frequency capability as anoise source due to its high transition frequency which is already in 1 THz region. However, the anticipated advantage of HBT in comparison to HEMT is its inherently smaller fluctuation of noise power density - a key parameter for a calibrator. The recent developments in HBT technologies (both SiGe and InP) and their frequency capability open possibilities to implementation of a HBT noise source up to sub-mm region which would be a very desirable component for a stable ICSS's. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Noise source requirements definition from system level - Preliminary to critical design of a noise source waveguide modules basedon HBT technology at two selected sub-mm frequencies such as 325 GHz and 448 GHz - Manufacturing and characterization of the breadboardDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

title: T512-900GS CO-PHASING OF SEGMENTED MIRROR TELESCOPES FOR FREE-SPACE TO FIBERBASED QUANTUM COMMUNICATION (EXPRO+)
description: Large optical antennas provide higher gain and sensitivity, ensure high data transmission rates,improve weak-light signal detection and are therefore necessary in photon starving regimesapplications as interplanetary, deep space and quantum communication. Segmenting the mainmirror is a very cost-effective solution when building large telescopes. However, large collectingareas of superior optical quality per se are not sufficient to achieve the alignment performancerequired to transmit entangled photons over long distances without decoherence. Co-phasingdifferent mirror segments with the accuracy required for quantum communication protocolsconstitutes an acknowledged challenge.This activity aims to develop, test, and validate a breadboard co-phasing system for segmentedmirror telescopes for single mode fiber coupling, supporting next-generation quantumcommunication networks, long-distance optical links, and turbulence-free telescope operations. Thesystem shall be suitable for the alignment of large (6 m and above) segmented mirror antenna andshall grant the wavefront distortions, focus, and tip-tilt continuous correction. The system shallactively adjust themirror positions to compensate for thermal, mechanical, gravitational flexure, andother environmental disturbance to enhance beam quality, coupling efficiency, reduce optical losses,maintain interferometric stability and improve single-photon detection efficiency to support satellitebased Quantum Key Distribution (QKD).Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors(incl. SMEs). title: PROCESSING COMPONENTS FOR ARTIFICIAL NIGHTIME LIGHT REMOTE SENSING - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop processing algorithm for remote sensing techniques to be used for Artificial Night time Light detection. Description: There is a need to contribute to the feasibility assessment of remote sensing techniques for Artificial Night time Light detection which is considered crucial to monitor and understand the impact of global urbanization. This observable is very much needed with high spatial resolution at different times at night. This activity focuses on specific challenges in the processing of observations in order to reach the desired Scientific Readiness Levels. It will make a first step towards mitigating the identified challenges focusing on the ground processing steps at Level 1 and potentially at Level 2. These aspects include but are not limited to:- Cloud screening and impact of undetected clouds;- Understanding of the atmospheric scattering and transmission models at night time, e.g. due to typical atmospheric aerosols in order to apply proper atmospheric correction;- Moonlight influence;- Restoration process to correct from effects such as saturation and air-glow.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of the processing challenges related to Artificial Night time Light Remote Sensing;- Development and documentation of the processing algorithms;- Validation and performance assessment;- Identification of the way forward.As a further step the activity might consider also to go further up on Level 2 aspects. The pixel-levelrelationship between Night time Light and land features/human activities indeed requires furtherinvestigation. Although the potential to derive information on human activities is acknowledged, thelack of distinct texture information remains a challenge for accurately investigating various human activities at a finer scale. Deliverables of this study are mainly consolidated Level 1 and Level 2 (atmospheric corrections) Algorithm Theoretical Baseline Documents validated trough mock-up models and reference data.

title: SENTINELS EOPF VISUALISATION SOFTWARE AND SERVICE - EXPRO +
description: The re-engineering of the existing Copernicus Sentinel Data Processors will introduce a significant paradigm shift in User Level Data provisioning, harmonising the data format across the Sentinel missions, architecting scalable processing on cloud platforms, designing for direct compatibility with data science programming frameworks, and fundamentally facilitating take-up by providing access to analysis-ready and information-ready data. However, due to the extensive utilisation of Sentinel data within the Earth observation ecosystem, the transition to the new format needs to be managed with a substantial overlap with existing operations and encourage user adoption of the new format.The scope of this activity is to make available an open-source software for visualising and facilitating dynamic analysis of Earth observation data in Zarr format, particularly the EOPF data resulting from the re-engineering of theSentinel data processors, and to demonstrate the software's capabilities by deploying it operationally as a service.Beyond the delivery of the open-source software and demonstration service, the activity shall also provide insights into the definition and optimisation of the Zarr configuration for visualisation, and benchmark useful configurations in terms of pyramid layers, data chunking, compression, file size, and other relevant parameters.

title: SUPPLY CHAIN RESILIENCE ASSESSMENT FOR ELECTRIC PROPULSION PROPELLANT (ARTES FP 1A.135) EXPRO+
description: The ARTES industry heavily relies on xenon for in-orbit propulsion, with most GEO satcom missions using it for station-keeping and orbit-raising. However, recent global events like the COVID-19 pandemic and the conflict in Ukraine have disrupted the xenon supply chain. Meanwhile, demand for space propellants has surged due to the rapid expansion of the satcom industry, particularly LEO constellations. In response, companies are exploring alternatives, such as krypton, argon, and non-noble gas options like iodine, zinc, and bismuth. This proposed study aims to analyse the xenon supply chain, explore the feasibility of scaling production, and assess alternative propellants' commercial and technical viability. By addressing these challenges, the industry seeks to ensure sustainable propulsion solutions to meet its evolving needs.

title: EXPLORING SYSTEM ARCHITECTURES FOR BROADBAND DIRECT-TO-DEVICE COMMUNICATION (ARTES FP 1B.148) EXPRO+
description: This activity will explore system options for enabling broadband D2D satellite communication, with a focus on using higher frequency spectrum (i.e., frequencies above FR1, or above 7 GHz). This study will consider the frequency ranges already identified by the 3GPP for both terrestrial networks (TN) and satellite networks (NTN), as well as other higher frequency bands which are under discussion for possible IMT usage. System-level factors to be considered include signal propagation, coverage limitations, the physical constraints of mm Wave frequencies, innovative access and duplex mechanisms (e.g. TDD and HD-FDD), as well as future user equipment capabilities. Technological, economic, regulatory, legal, and operational implications shall also be evaluated to derive a viable futuresystem architecture.

title: HIGHLY EFFICIENT, ULTRA-COMPACT SOLAR ARRAY EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop solar arrays capable of high power (10s of kW) maximising figures of merit in terms of W/kg and W/m3, and develop dedicated deployment mechanisms to be used on planetary/lunar surfaces.Description: Exploration missions are going to requirehigh power but at the same time it is going to have strong limitations in volume and mass for the solar generator subsystem. Therefore, new innovative concepts must be developed to increase significantly the power per stowed volume. This asks for highest efficientsolar cells in combination with ultra lightweight and compact solar arrays including potentially new deployment mechanisms and photovoltaic assembly technologies. In addition, applications on planetary or lunar surfaces require dedicated solutions which address different constraints than deployments in space. In this activity a concept of solar array with a high stowed volume per power ratioand high power per area is developed. This concept makes use of highly efficient solar cells in combination with an ultra-compact andvery light structure and mechanisms. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Definition of ultra-compact solar array concepts targeting figures of merit of 200 W/kg and 60 kW/m3 bringing together highly efficient, ultra-thin solar cells and flexible modular photovoltaic assembly technologies. - Definition of solar array concepts and respective deployment strategies and mechanisms for applications on planetary or lunar surfaces. - Definition of technology building blocks. - Development of prototype components and breadboards - Manufacturing and testing of prototype components and breadboards.

title: AI SUPERVISED PROPULSION SYSTEM FOR HIGH PRECISION FORMATION FLYING - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To design (including the algorithm definition), implement and test an AI learning machine, deriving optimised thruster input parameter commands, based on received signals from the AOCS/Payload sensors.Description: High precision formation flying is a design solution for some of the very demanding high precision observation missions like gravity observation missions, distributed synthesised antennas in LEO or space based multi-spacecraft telescopes. In such missions, the AOCS of the spacecraft requires a very high thrust precision in microN region or even lower. In the LEO Earth Observation Missions, the propulsion system encounters significant challenges such as providing a very high precision thrust in a very large dynamics and for a very long lifetime of the mission.The precision of the thruster response directly depends on the precision of the electrical values. A method to overcome mentioned issues is to calibrate the PPU and AOCS system in the flight, however, this is not optimal as it leads to observation discontinuity. To address this, the activity introduces a machine learning AI intelligence, which observes the response of the propulsion system tothe signals directly coming from the AOCS sensors like ultra fine accelerometers complemented by. e.g., the Star trackers or Fine Guidance Sensors (FGS). The AI then adapts the commends to propulsion system based on its previous responses and to react to the input signals from the AOCS sensors. AI can also be used for failure analysis and to implement measures to overcome the failure in EOP or science deep space missions. This would minimize the necessary time, link time and link sessions required. This activity encompassesthe following tasks: - Algorithm selection, where the suitable AI algorithm from different types like "Stochastic Gradient Descent", "Constraint Satisfaction" or "AI Supervised Learning Algorithms" will be chosen. - Implementation, where the chosen AI algorithmwill be implemented in an PPU microcontroller or FPGA simulator - Testing and development plan, where first the implemented AI algorithm in the PPU microcontroller or FPGA simulator will be tested on a thruster set-up and at the end a development plan towards high TRL levels based on the requirements from potential missions will be prepared.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). Description: Objective: To design (including the algorithm definition), implement and test an AI learning machine, deriving optimised thruster input parameter commands, based on received signals from the AOCS/Payload sensors.Description: High precision formation flying is a design solution for some of the very demanding high precision observation missions like gravity observation missions, distributed synthesised antennas in LEO or space based multi-spacecraft telescopes. In such missions, the AOCS of the spacecraft requires a very high thrust precision in microN region or even lower. In the LEO Earth Observation Missions, the propulsion system encounters significant challenges such as providing a very high precision thrust in a very large dynamics and for a very long lifetime of the mission.The precision of the thruster response directly depends on the precision of the electrical values. A method to overcome mentioned issues is to calibrate the PPU and AOCS system in the flight, however, this is not optimal as it leads to observation discontinuity. To address this, the activity introduces a machine learning AI intelligence, which observes the response of the propulsion system tothe signals directly coming from the AOCS sensors like ultra fine accelerometers complemented by. e.g., the Star trackers or Fine Guidance Sensors (FGS). The AI then adapts the commends to propulsion system based on its previous responses and to react to the input signals from the AOCS sensors. AI can also be used for failure analysis and to implement measures to overcome the failure in EOP or science deep space missions. This would minimize the necessary time, link time and link sessions required. This activity encompassesthe following tasks: - Algorithm selection, where the suitable AI algorithm from different types like "Stochastic Gradient Descent", "Constraint Satisfaction" or "AI Supervised Learning Algorithms" will be chosen. - Implementation, where the chosen AI algorithmwill be implemented in an PPU microcontroller or FPGA simulator - Testing and development plan, where first the implemented AI algorithm in the PPU microcontroller or FPGA simulator will be tested on a thruster set-up and at the end a development plan towards high TRL levels based on the requirements from potential missions will be prepared.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. title: ENGINEERING DATA HUB CONSOLIDATION - EXPRO+
description: Objectives: To complement the Model Based Engineering Data Hub with features related to data governance (security, configuration management), traceability, trade-off, and data exploitation. Description A number of Agencies/industry working groups, such as the Digital Spacecraft Think Tank (DtSC TT) and the Model Based for System Engineering Advisory Group (MB4SE AG), are currently working on the problem of interoperability of tools. Interoperability of tools is supported by a Data Hub in charge of exchanging data. A firstversion is under development. This activity will complement it with the findings by the DtSC TT, mainly on security, configuration management and traceability. It aims at adding features identified in the MB4SE AG's Users Needs such as document generation, automatic budget calculation, trade-off, and dashboard production. It shall complement it with the results of a number of MBSE OSIP and TDE activities currently running and to configure it with the latest version of the Space System Ontology. Complements related to security: (1) mapping of security engineering concepts and semantics to those of system engineering - establishment of security granularity of data sets-, (2) bridging gaps in modelling fidelity between (early phase) system models and that required for security analysis, (3) link to the recent ECSS standards on security, (4) lack of adequate tooling. Complements related to configuration managementof the entire body of system knowledge: Decide on a configuration management policy between the modelling tools, the data hub or the infrastructure backbone. Address data governance and data management resulting from the DtSC data management group. Traceability: To demonstrate the compliance/traceability between the layer of system definition (system level N and N+1) based on model definition. To define a methodology allowing the traceability demonstration between the "needs model based" vs "solution model based" following the system lifecycle management with associated documents. Model based traceability Policy has to be defined to keep trace of the model baseline sources so that a requested update of a document can be performed based on the model relying on the state corresponding to the authoring document generation. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Specification of the missing functionalities;- Design and development;- Verification and validation;- Demonstration on an exchange use case;- Feedback to the ontology as needed.Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence. A future activity could bethe deployment of the Data Hub in an industrial context.

title: KA-BANDSINGLE POLARIZATIONTRANSMIT AND RECEIVE ACTIVE ANTENNA FOR LOW EARTH ORBITSATELLITES (ARTES AT 5B.251) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test a Ka-band single polarisation, combined transmit and receive, active antenna for low earth orbit satellites.Targeted Improvements: Reduction by a factor of 2 the numbers of on-board antenna.Description: TLow Earth Orbit (LEO) telecommunication satellites require compact and highly integrated antennas. These antennas require very large fields of view with a typical beam scanning range of up to 60 degrees from the boresight direction. Active direct radiating phased array antennas are attractive solutions for these satellites because they provide betterscanning capabilitiesas compared to phased arrays magnified by reflectors and are simpler in terms of accommodation. Current Ka-band active antennas aredesigned with separated transmit and receive functionalities as the large frequency band separation between the transmit and receive functions makes difficult to integrate them in the sameaperture. In addition, the small pitch required for such wide scan angles makes the accommodation of the radiating elements, associated beamforming network and active components challenging. Multi-layer printed technology represents a promising solution to achieve the integration of combined transmit and receive active antennas. Available now are technologies featuring 3-D integration capabilities with low losses and cross talk capable of realising micro-coax transmission lines or Air-Filled Substrate Integrated Waveguide with integrated active and passive component.This activity will develop aconcept of a combined transmit and receive active antenna with wide scanning range for applications in low earth orbit. This includes the developed thermal management and mechanical concept. Wideband beamforming and advanced manufacturing technologies will be investigated. Breadboarding shall be carried out to deriskthe most critical components (filtering function, radiating elements). A reduced antenna engineering model with critical functions comprising of at least one tile assembly of at least 10x10 radiating elementswill be manufactured and tested.

title: EDCP-07- DESTINE CORE SERVICE PLATFORM FRAMEWORK ADVANCED APPLICATIONS SERVICES
description: This activity is part of the European Commission DestinE initiative, that has the objective of developing and exploiting a highly accurate digital model of the Earth in order to monitor and predict the interaction between natural phenomena and human activities.This procurement aims at the expansion of the DestinE Core Service Platform (DESP) capabilities through the provision of attractive advanced applications and services which support the exploitation of DestinE generated data and information to actively contributeto the European Commission's Green Deal and Digital Strategy.The specific scope of this procurement is to build a rich and dynamicecosystem of DESP Registered Services making use of the Core Platform Services in place and unlock the potential of Earth-system modelling. This activity shall cover continuous on-boarding, setup, integration and operation of a wide range of applications and services focused on various thematic domains such as descriptive and predictive analytics, forecasts and simulations capabilities, analysis and modelling services, AI/ML based services, interactive representation of the Earth, and educational services.The setup and operations of DESP Collaborative Services are as well part of this procurement: open-source libraries; hosting environments where users can build repositories and publish datasets, AI/ML models and applications, and information resources such as code, data, text, graphics, videos, documents.The DESP Advanced Applications and Services activity is funded under the DestinE initiative (EU-funded programme) and will be open exclusively to economic operators that have their registered office in an EU Member State or that are from a Country associated to the Digital Europe Programme. This initiative will support the European Commission to achieve the sustainable development objectives and will contribute to the European Green Deal and Digital Strategy.The Invitation to Tender (ITT) package (Cover Letter, Statement of Work, Technical and Service Requirements, Special Conditions of Tender, Draft Contract, and Letter ofInvitation) will be available on ESA Star Publication (https://esastar-publication.sso.esa.int/), the ESA tendering website. Any Tenderer which is not yet registered with ESA as a potential supplier must complete the online questionnaire in esa-star: https://esastar-emr.sso.esa.int/. Further information on the registration process can be found on the Doing Business with ESA portal: https://doing-business.sso.esa.int/. Please, note that esa-star allows two levels of entity registration: "Light" and "Valid Full". This allows new users wishing to do business with ESA to carry out their registration in two steps. While "Light" registration will grant access to all esa-star services up to and including proposal submission, the award of ESA contracts requires "Valid Full" status. The issue of the Invitation to Tender is foreseen in February 2023. ESA intends to place one (1) contract as a result of this procurement for a duration of 12 months with the intention of extending the contract to cover DestinE continuation into the future.

title: T711-801SD ENSEMBLE AND SURROGATE MODELLING FOR DEBRIS ENVIRONMENT LONG-TERM SIMULATION (EXPRO+)
description: The current use of space is changing due to the launch of large constellation and small satellites, while we continue observing fragmentations and evolving disposal practices. As a result, there is an emerging need of access to long-term simulations of the environment both for spacecraft designers (e.g. to estimate collision flux in different scenarios) and for policy makers (e.g. to assess and communicate the response of the environment to different mitigation strategies). Currently, such predictions require complexmodels, which are available only to space agencies and few academic institutions, and rely on very extensive computational resources. The activity aims at leveraging novel modelling techniques to provide long-term simulations of the environment at a significantlower computational cost and with the flexibility to enable real-time exploration of the generated trends (e.g. visualise how change in the launch traffic affects the predicted debris population). This can be achieved through different techniques such as surrogate models built on dedicated long-term simulations. Other approaches rely on ensemble modelling, which involves the combinationof multiple models in the prediction process, and Particle-In-a-Box models, which could represent a way of achieving meaningful population trends in several traffic scenarios. The expected outcome is a tool able to generate assessments in a variety of test cases.A preliminary version of the tool can be encapsulated into a web-frontend to grant access to actors in the European space sector.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: 5G REGENERATIVE PROCESSOR AND ASSOCIATED SYSTEM TESTBED (ARTES SPL 5G/6G 5A.083) - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of this activity is to implement and test the signal processing portion of a 5G LEO satellite payload capable of handling several high throughput beams assuming an active antenna configuration. The demonstrator shall be based on a processor capable of controlling a reconfigurable beam-forming network (BFN) and performing signal (re-)generation andchannelisation of 5G waveforms. Targeted Improvements: Enable 5G regenerative payload functionalities currently not available. Description:The number of 5G subscriptions is estimated to reach 3.5 billion by the end of 2026. In this context, providing a truly ubiquitous coverage (even when traveling on cruises, high-speed trains and airplanes) whilst ensuring appropriate quality of service requires a tight integration between satellite and terrestrial networks. While geo-stationary satellites are well suited for covering very large areas with a limited number of satellites, they do not provide an optimal global interactive broadband connectivity due to their large delays and relatively high beam footprint on ground. For this type of service, constellations of hundreds or thousands of satellites in low orbit are preferred thanks to their lower latency and ability to provide higher overall system throughput. In order to achieve the ambitious targets expected by 5G New Radio (e.g., very high data rates, resources flexibility, mesh connectivity and rapid adaptation to traffic variations), these LEO payloads must rely on advanced technologies like phased array antennas, optical inter-satellite links and on-board regeneration. While solutions for on-board regeneration with DVB or CCSDS waveforms already exist, these cannot be exploited for the required integration of the space segment within the 5G ecosystem. This activity shall design and validate the main signal processing components for advanced satellite payloads providing 5G broadband connectivity. Specifically, the focus shall be put on developing the following components:1) High-speed modems capable of (re-)generating 5G waveforms with multiple Gbps of aggregated throughput.2) The on-board processor including switching/routing and control paths to connect the modems to the BFN to send/receive the signals to/from the different beam direction. The testbed shall be composed of the regenerative processor plus the appropriate ground support equipment to perform functional and performance verification of the developed payload components, including functionally representative building blocks of the payload front-end. As a minimum, this shall include a beam-forming network capable of generating multiple beams and capable of controlling hundreds of phased array feeds. It shall also be capable of verifying performance at system level (capacity) and link level (BER, FER, throughput) by simulating the impact of the components not developed within the testbed (e.g. antenna).

title: SCALABLE PROCESSOR ARRAY FOR DIGITAL BEAMFORMING (ARTES AT 5C.526) - EXPRO PLUS - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to develop a scalable processor architecture for digital beamforming applications. An elementary processing node of a scalable telecom phased array antenna will be designed and manufactured. Beamforming algorithms will be developed and integrated into a processor array testbed comprising several nodes in order to evaluate the concept.Targeted Improvements:- 50% power and volume reduction compared state of the art digital beamforming.- 50% improvement in the thermal management system due to the distribution of the processing.Description: Digital beamforming networks offer the highest level of flexibility to telecommunication payloads but at the same time incur high costs and increased power consumption.This activity will aim at reducing the complexity of such network, with the development of a custom digital processor firmware for state-of-the-art highly integrated processing technologies. Critical functions of this development include the interconnect and networking between the processing nodes of the processor array, the selection and customisation of algorithms for digital beam weighting and aggregation, as well as the accompanying transparent and regenerative digital operations, and how they will be mapped to theprocessing nodes of the digital processor array or supported by additional hardware for direct sampling up to Ka-Band and to achieve a modular and scalable architecture that enables building of large antenna arrays. Architecture trade-offs to minimise power consumption will be carried out and the thermal and physical constraints of such a processor array will be analysed. In the initial stage of the activity, a range of technology options shall be considered to define the elementary building node of the Scalable Processor Array.As a minimum, the following technology options will be studied: (1) RF System-on-Chip (RF SoC) technology with integrated wideband, high-speed data converters. (2) FPGA technology with external data converters (3) FPGA technology with external Analog to Digital Converters (ADCs) only, while the Digital to Analog Converter (DAC) is implemented inside the digital logic. The third option will allow for the evaluation of an all-digital signal transmission chain, with the support of Multi-Gigabit Transceivers (MGTs) for the DAC.Previous work has shown that FPGA-embedded MGTs can serve as 1-bit RF DACs, acting as the interface between the digital and analogue domains.The activity places priority on overall power consumption, while ensuring no adverse effects on the RF Figures of Merit to enable the definition of an optimal architecture for both phased array payloads and phased array terminals based on the same concept. In cases where external data converters are considered, high-speed interfaces suitable for wideband Software-Defined Radio (SDR) up to Ka-band applications should be chosen. Once elementary building node are identified, the activity will design, manufacture, and test a digital processor array testbed, comprising several processing array nodes and its algorithms for digital beamforming applications to demonstrate the Scalable Processor Array. The processor array shall be scalable to several hundreds of antenna elements. A mathematical model of the processor array architecture will be developed. title: TECHNOLOGIES AND ARCHITECTURES FOR REALISING COMPUTATIONALLY INTENSIVE FUNCTIONS WITHIN NEXT-GENERATION SATCOM SYSTEMS (ARTES FP 1B.147) EXPRO+
description: This study will explore how new processing technologies, such as AI accelerators, might be employed within future satcom missions to deliver mission critical functionalities across both the space and ground segments. The activity will commence with a review of future satcom use cases and mission profiles to identify critical computationally intensive functionalities. An in-depth survey and assessment of current hardware and software architectures, including CPUs, FPGAs, ASICs, AI accelerators, and Hybrid/Heterogeneous solutions will be performed and optimal implementation technologies for each critical functionality will be identified. The activity output will include a detailed roadmap outlining future hardware and software needs for next generation satcom systems which will be used to support engagement with European chip manufacturers to ensure alignment of satcom sector needs and future technology development.

title: IMPLICATIONS OF A ZERO-DEBRIS APPROACH TO FUTURE SATCOM MISSION DESIGN (ARTES FP 1A.129) - EXPRO+
description: Within the next three years there will be more satellites launched than in the past six decades combined. In recognition of this a new, stricter approach to space debris generation and mitigation is being developed that is likely to have cost and operational impacts on telecommunication missions either in the near term, by voluntary adherence, or in the longer term though launch authority mandate. These changes will include an expansion of protected orbital regions, improved end-of-life disposal rates, improved health monitoring, shorter orbital clearance time, mandatory energy passivation and zero planned orbital debris creation amongst others. Therefore, the first objective of this study is to assess the impacts that each of the Zero-Debris' approaches being developed would have if applied within the commercial satcom sector. As the first iterations of these recommendations are not aimed at the commercialmarket, they may benefit from adaptions towards commercial operators needs. Therefore, the second objective of this study is to generate commercial-satcom-specific adaptations, considering competitiveness and large-scale constellation operations from the outset.

title: STANDARDISED DE-ORBIT INTERFACE DEFINITION FOR LEO SATCOM-CLASS SPACECRAFT (ARTES FP 1A.130) EXPRO+
description: The objective of this activity is to define an active debris removal (ADR) interface standard that would allow third-party service providers to attach onto client satellites, thus enabling satellite operators to procure ADR as a service for their defunct satellites. A standardised interface that both ADR service providers and satellite manufacturers can design to, would help promote competition for such services, as well as avoid operators becoming dependent on a particular service provider. The interface should facilitate the non-cooperative rendezvous and capture of LEO telecom-class platforms at end-of-life. Ensuring that the interface can be produced with low recurring costs is therefore an important factor. Another key requirement is to define a standard that is sufficiently detailed to ensure cross-compatibility, but also allows both current and future ADR technologies to be used

title: DISTRIBUTED COMPUTING ARCHITECTURES AND STORAGE FOR SATELLITE CLUSTERS (ARTES FP 1B.142) - EXPRO+
description: The proposed activity seeks to address the limitation of on-board DC power in small satellite systems, by exploring the applicationof distributed onboard computing, and thereby grow the range of satcom applications that can be supported by such missions.Distributed computing in this context refers to computational decentralisation across several processors which are housed onboard separate satellites, i.e. implementing a form of inter-spacecraft RF data bus' in orbit. This parallels the notion of capacity 'pooling and sharing' hereinunderutilised computational capabilities elsewhere in orbit are leveraged to enhance individual mission efficiency and performance.An important goal of the investigation will therefore be to derive what is the range of payload powers (i.e. platform sizes) and orbital separations at which distributed computing is attractive, and in which scenarios local computing is a more favourable alternative.

title: EXPLOITING THE SYNERGY BETWEEN GROUND- AND SPACE-BASED RF MONITORING SYSTEMS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 3A.222) EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: Objective:The objective of the activity is to define, implement, and verify key scenarios that demonstrate the added value of a system integrating both ground- and space-based RF monitoring capabilities.Targeted Improvements:The following figures intend to depict the targeted improvement of a joint ground- and space-based system with respect to an individual ground- or space-based system:Increased detectionaccuracy of at least 20%. Enhanced geolocation precision of at least 15%. Expanded geographical coverage of at least 40%. Reduced response time of at least 30%.Description:While advancements in space-based monitoring technologies have been made, their integration with ground-based systems has not yet been fully realised. Previous efforts have concentrated primarily on enhancing the individual capabilities of either ground or space monitoring, often overlooking the potential benefits that can arise from a collaborative approach.Within Europe, there is an industrial base which offers ground-based interference detection solutions. This activity aims to support this industrial base by developing and validating the techniques to integrate space- and ground-based RF monitoring solutions. The maturity of solutions exploiting space- and ground-monitoring is currently low in Europe. It is foreseen thatthe activity will be supported by existing ground-based infrastructure provided by private parties or national regulators.This activity focuses on the definition, implementation, and demonstration of key scenarios to exploit the potential synergies of ground-based and existing space-based RF monitoring capabilities. These scenarios shall cover various domains, including but not limited to spectrum occupancy, geolocation accuracy, and interference detection, which shall be developed and verified in a representative environment. This involves the reproduction of RF interference conditions to demonstrate the added value of a joint ground and space RF monitoring system and using existing ground- and space-based RF monitoring systems. Additionally, the activity aims to establish operational concepts, including the definition of protocols and security aspectsfor data sharing, operational workflows, and collaborative methodologies that enable the two systems to complement one another effectively.

title: COMPACT AND HIGH PERFORMANCE SOLAR ARRAY EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop a compact and high-performance solar array with an increase in the power per stowed volume ratio, with an overarching goal to increase number of satellites per launch.Description: A compact solar array concept is essential for the mega-constellation market, which requires systems compatible with a multi-satellite launch scheme. For this reason, the solar array itself has to occupy a minimum volume when stowed, while maintaining a high performance figure. The main target is thus to find solutions toincrease the W/m3 figure of merit. This high compactness can be achieved by using flexible solar array technologies and/or fully flexible PVA (photovoltaic assembly) but these are not the only solutions. Therefore, to achieve the goal of this activity, any technology that can lead to an increase in the highest W/m3 is of interest. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Identification of solar array concepts allowing for reaching power per volume figures of > 30 kW/m3 and respective building blocks- Mechanical analysis of identified solutions - Development and breadboarding of technology building blocks required to meet the identified solutions in the previous task - Engineering tests

title: NAVISP-EL1-130-ROBUST GNSS TRACKER FOR SENSITIVE APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+
description: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safeguards system is designed to verify States' legal undertakings to use nuclear material for exclusively peaceful purposes. States declare their nuclear material and activities to the IAEA, and the IAEA verifies thecorrectness and completeness of these declarations.This requires robust and resilient GNSS trackers which can withstand sophisticated attacks (jamming, spoofing, and especially treacherous meaconing) and tampering attempts by State-level actors, providing Assured PNT (Trusted positioning data).The GNSS tracker shall be battery powered and capable of unsupervised operations. In previous projects (in particular, EL1-077) building blocks for this technology have been developed. The IAEA has expressed interest in a joint project to increase the protection against additional attacks identified and to raise the TRL level and to make the tracker ready forcommercialization. The objective of the activity is to study, design, implement and demonstrate a resilient and robust GNSS tracker to support IAEA safeguards activities, and other similar activities requiring Assured PNTThe tasks to be performed shall include:Based on EL1-077, the activity will study, design, implement and demonstrate the technologies required for the GNSS tracker, capable of detecting and mitigating jamming, meaconing and spoofing attacks, with focus on concrete uses cases and attack scenarios identified by IAEA.Additional technologies (for example tightly coupled INS and CRPAs) will be integrated into a functional prototype. As part of the demonstration, the prototype will be subject to thorough tests representative of challenging jamming, meaconing and spoofing scenarios mounted by capable attackers.The activity is part of a roadmap to make available to customers GNSS trackers with Assured PNT and will bring the technology to a TRL which will allow industry to make confident proposals for an Element 2. The activity will not include any Galileo PRS technology, as per NAVISP Declaration.

title: NAVISP-EL1-116-DESIGN OF CRPAS FOR AVIATION AND HIGH-ACCURACY SERVICES - EXPRO+
description: This activity focuses on designing Controlled Reception Pattern Antennas (CRPAs) to mitigate GNSS jamming and spoofing for aviationand high-accuracy services. It includes developing offline CRPA prototypes for both domains and performing laboratory tests combining RF and software simulations. The tests will characterize performance under nominal and non-nominal conditions, including GNSS feared events and hardware failures. title: DEVELOPMENT OF PVA AND BLANKET TECHNOLOGIES FOR SATURN MISSIONS SOLAR ARRAYS - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: ObjectivesTo develop fully European PhotoVoltaic (PVA) and Blanket technologies that can be used on a Solar Array for deep space missions to Saturn.DescriptionLarge solar arrays are currently being developed for telecommunication and scientific missions. Recent examples include the semi-rigid ENEO array, the fully flexible SolarFlex array of the Novacom 2 telecommunications satellite and the rigid array of the JUICE mission to Jupiter. With a high specific power, such arrays lend themselves for use in exploration missions. Feasibility studies have demonstrated that missions to Saturn, fully powered by solar arrays, are indeed feasible. In a recent development activity, the feasibility of a solar array architecture scalable up to 100 m2 per wing and with the capability to retract and re-deploy, to protect the array from damage, has been successfully demonstrated. In the frame of this study, the development of PVA and Blanket frame technologies suitable for the Saturn environment has been indicated as the main focus point for further development of suchsolar array architecture. Saturn environment places demanding requirements on PVA and Blanket technologies: the PVA shall be capable to supply power at very low temperatures and Sun intensities,and the blanket shall be lightweight yet strong enough to support the PVA and to sustain the large temperature range of a Saturn mission. Also, the blanket structure interface shall allow smooth deployment/retraction operations. The activity therefore encompasses the following tasks: Investigation into actual PVA LILT technologies and potential adaptations for its use on a Saturn mission (e.g. reduced thickness) Definition of blanket and blanket frame design, to act as PVA support and able to cope with the required temperature range Demonstration via mechanical and electrical analyses of the suitability of the selected design for the Saturn mission Demonstration of the suitability of the selectedtechnologies for the Saturn mission by means of thermal cycling and vibration tests of a representative Blanket segment (PVA and blanket) mock-up Identification of development needs Preparation of a roadmap

title: PORTABLE SELF-CALIBRATED RYDBERG ELECTRIC FIELD PROBE FOR ANTENNA MEASUREMENTS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To design and realize a first European portable self-calibrated SI-traceable Rydberg atom-based Electric field probe.Description:Accurate measurement of electric fields is crucial for the development and operation of RF communicationsystems, particularly in space missions. Conventional antennas need fine calibration for high-integrity reception. The calibration is performed by placing uncalibrated antennas in a known EM (electromagnetic) environment that is measured via a well-calibrated antenna which creates a dependency. Whereas Rydberg based receivers allow precise measurements of RF signals which is directly related to Planck's constant and hence can self-calibrate by relying on SI (international system of units)-traceable atomic standards The activity aims to develop a portable, self-calibrated Rydberg atom based electric field probe.The probe is based on the interaction of RF-fields with Rydberg atoms, where alkali atoms are excited opticallyto Rydberg states and the applied RF-field alters the resonant state of the atoms. For this probe, the Rydbergatoms are placed in a glass vapor cell. The vapor cell acts like an RF-to-optical transducer, converting an RF Efield to an optical frequency response. The probe utilizes the concept of Electromagnetic Induced Transition (EIT), where the RF transition in the four-level atomic system causes a split of the transition spectrum for the pump laser. This splitting is measured and is directly proportional to the applied RF field amplitude. Therefore, by measuring this splitting, we get a direct measurement of the RF E-field strength. This technique could allow traceable measurements over a large frequency band including 1-500GHz. The new approach has the following benefits: 1) it will allow direct SI units linked RF E-field measurements, 2) It is self-calibrating due to atomic resonances, 3) it will provide RF field measurements independent of current techniques, 4) the probe will not perturb the field during the measurement, since no metal is present in the probe.This activity encompasses the following tasks:-Assessment of different Rydberg atom-based methods of detection of RF fields.- Requirement consolidation and performance assessment.- Detailed concept design with analysis of critical functions.- Development of the breadboard and verification in relevant environment.- Development of a technology roadmap for an EQM.

title: GUIDANCE CONTROL ENTRY TECHNOLOGY FOR MARS PRECISION LANDING - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop and assess Mars guided entry and control algorithms for the entry and descent phases, including smart parachute or retro-propulsion triggering, and implement them as on-board software.Description: Entry, descent, and landing (EDL) of Mars missions are critical for ensuring the successful deployment of precision landers for human and robotic exploration. In particular, the entry and descent phases involve complex aero/thermodynamics which require precise guidance and control to achieve the proper conditions for deploying parachutes or for activating supersonic retro-propulsion. In fact, most of the dispersions occur in these phases, and while various approaches for guided-entry algorithms (reference path tracking, predictor-corrector methods, and model-basedtechniques) offer different advantages, all of these come at the expense of many challenges and trade-offs. This activity aims to trade-off different approaches for the design of Mars guided entry and control algorithms, in combination with smart parachute and/orsupersonic retro-propulsion triggering (when applicable), to reduce the dispersions that shall be removed by the landing phase. By assessing their performance through high fidelity Model-in-the-loop (MIL) simulations, the most effective algorithms can be identifiedand considered for numerically efficient and robust implementation as on-board guidance software. The added value includes improvedlanding precision, enhanced safety, and optimized entry and descent performance, which are all essential for the success of future Mars missions. The performance of the developed algorithms will be evaluated via high-fidelity dynamical simulations, while portability to flight processors will be assessed through profiling of the developed guidance control algorithms. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Consolidation/review of the proofs-of-concept and state-of-the-art of guided entry. - Definition of requirements, operational scenarios, use-cases, and preliminary validation and verification (VV) plan. - Detailed development of guidance and control algorithms with focus on performance, and optimization for embeddability. - Implementation and performance assessment ofalgorithms in an End-to-End Mars landing EDL simulator. - VV campaign of the proposed solutions and algorithms. - Assessment of computational performance on a space-graded processor through profiling. - Study synthesis, and recommendations for a technology roadmap to increase TRL.

title: HE-SWE-03B - GLOBAL MULTI-MOMENT MULTI-FLUID MODEL OF THE MAGNETOSPHERE
description: The Agency seeks to assess the applicability and operational potential of a multi-moment, multi-fluid modelling approach for forecasting and nowcasting the Earth's magnetospheric space weather environment. While current operational systems predominantly rely on global MHD models and fully kinetic approaches remain computationally challenging for routine use, this activity aims to demonstrate whether a multi-fluid framework can provide an effective balance between physical realism and operational performance. Bidders are expected to employ real observational data for model verification, validation, calibration, and performance enhancement, investigating techniques such as data assimilation, data-driven boundary conditions, and other observation-informed methods to improve forecasting capability and scientific fidelity. The activity should include comprehensive testing against measurements and reference models, the assessment of computational performance and operational suitability, and the quantification of forecasting skill for key space weather phenomena. The work shall identify the strengths, limitations, and maturity of the approach, while establishing a clear roadmap towards a future three-dimensional global magnetospheric forecasting capability that can operate faster than real time and support advanced operational space weather services.

title: CAVITY ENHANCED SOURCE OF FREQUENCY ENTANGLED PHOTONS FOR EFFICIENT QUANTUM NETWORK INTERFACES (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3H.003) EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop and test a narrowband entangled photon source for future quantum networks.Targeted Improvements:Higher key-rates enhanced by individual cavity modes. The generation of entangled photon pairs at multiple frequencies, taking advantage of enhanced output rates due to a finessed cavity, with a direct interconnectivity to the optical communication layer using quantum hardware.Description:A way to generate entangled photon pairs is through parametric spontaneous down-conversion, where high energetic pump photons can be converted into entangled photon pairs using a non-linear crystal. The energy of each photon pair must sum up to the energy of the pump-photon. That leads together with the momentum conservation to phase matching conditions, and hence the centre frequencies and the bandwidth of the generated photon pairs are defined.By periodically poling the crystal, arbitrary wavelength combinations of the photons can be selected. Placing the crystal inside an optical resonator, the output spectrum of the photon pair source can further be designed to be narrowband, with well separated frequency bins, allowing for efficient frequency multiplexing or for coupling to atomic systems, like memories, clocks, sensors.This activity will design, manufacture and test a photon pair source for frequency multiplexed transmission both for use with wavelengths defined in the C-band ITU and for coupling photons to an atomic system such as quantum memory. This is a versatile source for future quantum networks which exploits entanglement over more than one node and can efficiently couple to memories, clocks, sensors or computers.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: HIGHLY STABLE BANDPASS AND NARROWBAND FILTERS FOR THE INFRARED - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop reproducible and stable bandpass and narrowband filters with high spectral accuracy (90%) in the Mid-to-Long-Wave and Thermal InfraRed ranges.Description: Multi-spectral imagers require bandpass and narrowband filters with low tolerances and high spectral stability. The accurate placement of the spectral bands during manufacturing is particularly challenging for long wavelengths as layer thicknesses have to be met at the same accuracy for much longer deposition times. Stability is mainly influencedby the long-term stability of the coating layers due to potential diffusion processes, in particular, when the layers are not denseenough. The availability of the coating technology for infrared coatings is limited and requires further developments to meet the needs for future Earth-Observation missions working in the Mid-to-Long-Wave and Thermal InfraRed regions. The activity will focus on the development of infrared bandpass and narrowband filters and, in particular, on the associated coating technology to be able to produce reproducible and stable filters with high spectral accuracy (90%). Particular aspects of coating delamination, imperfections and degradation would be assessed carefully, accounting for relevant environmental conditions (e.g. vacuum, thermal, radiations). title: HIGH PERFORMANCE COST EFFECTIVE SOLAR ARRAY EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop solar array concepts targeting very high figures of merit in terms of power/volume and power/mass with the target values of 200 W/kg and 60 kW/m3 and manufacture prototype components and breadboards.Description: The solar array market is instrong need of solutions that have drastically improved figures of merit in terms of power/mass and power/volume. Targets are here 200 W/kg and 60 kW/m3. Those values are believed to be only reachable with flexible solar array concepts which are currently not available in Europe. Therefore, a number of building blocks are required such as new panel substrates/flexible blankets, interface withinnovative mechanisms, advanced photovoltaic assembly technologies and processes. There is a variety of different concepts based onflexible solar arrays available from non-European suppliers. For some missions non-European solar array suppliers have already beenselected due to non-available competitive European products. Therefore, strong development efforts are required to be competitive in this market segment. The target of this activity is to obtain a solar array concept targeting very high figures of merit in terms of power/volume (60 kW/m3) and power/mass (200 W/kg). The activity encompasses as a minimum the following tasks: - Identification offlexible solar array concepts compatible with indicated figures of merit - Definition of technology building blocks - Development of prototype components and breadboards - Development roadmap.

title: REGENERATIVE 5G NEW RADIO PHYSICAL LAYER IP (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5C.532) - EXPRO+RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to design a 5G NR Physical Layer IP which supports 5G New Radio (NR) for deployment on a Next Generation Node B (gNB) in space. The IP shall be compliant to 5G standards and designed for use on FPGA or ASICs for future modems in regenerative digital processors. The activity shall test and verify the developed programmable logic Ips and upper L1 software according to space quality standards compatible to a use in satellite on-board firmware and software.Targeted Improvements:Improvement in link budget by 3dB with respect to existing transparent 5G solutions. Enable implementation ofregenerative5G modems in FPGA programmable logic.Description: While terrestrial 5G Modem IPs exist, currently no 5G NR IP is available for implementation on radiation tolerant FPGAs or ASICs. The quickly developing 5G NR standardsmake it complicated to maintain such IP, therefore validation techniques based on auto coding tools shall be investigated to allow for quick updates to the IP.Current 5G NR payload concepts are mostly based on transparent payloads, as the 3GPP 5G-NR standard is not fully defined at this stage. The activity addresses this technicalproblem by developing complete 5G NR High PHY IPs for radiation tolerant system on chips used in digital processor modems. Thisinvolves the integration of Physical UplinkShared Channel (PUSCH) decoder and Physical Downlink Shared Channel (PDSCH) encoder channels. Compatibility with 3GPP standards, Open Radio Access Network (ORAN)and Small Cell Forum (SCF) specifications should be evaluated. This activity shall facilitate the deployment of efficient and high-performing wireless networks. Theinteroperability of different 5G NR Splits should be investigated (in particular, 3GPP Split 6, Split 7 and Split 2). Support to both FR1 and FR2 should be investigated, to ensuremaximum bandwidth. Different devices that could host such modem IP should be evaluated and used as referencefor the implementation. Currently, the fundamental conceptshave been validated in ground technologies, providing a solid foundation for this activity. The output of this activity is a fully functional and validated 5G NR High PHYimplementation using generic andmaintainable hardware design language (HDL) and software (SW). Porting of the IP to European FPGAs or ASICs should be evaluated.Tailoring of SW and HDL development standards and compliance to 3GPP standards should be demonstrated to ensure an easy adoption in future modems. Procurement Policy: Open Competitive Tender Type: C2Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: AUTHENTICATION TECHNOLOGIES FOR LOW-THROUGHPUT LOW-POWER SYSTEMS - EXPRO PLUS
description: To study, design and demonstrate the use of novel cryptographic schemes and signal processing algorithms for resilient low-throughput low-energy communication and PNT solutions.DescriptionAsset tracking devices or Internet-of-Things (IoT) connected devices that require Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) information rely on narrowband links, sporadic communication and on low-energy PNT solutions. These types of devices exchange information or determine their position only occasionally in order to maximize battery lifetime. They are nonetheless, susceptible to spoofing attacks and have little barriers against malevolent parties.The aforementioned applications rely on the broadcast of information with very low throughput, sporadic connection and that poses a challenge for source and data authentication. Added to this, asset trackers and IoT devices require that energy consumption is kept to aminimum andhardware implementation remains simple and thus, solutions based on conventional cryptographic methods cannot efficiently address their needs because they are potentially too demanding.This activity will investigate several cryptographic techniques such as selective verification, Broadcast Authentication Streams, and stream ciphers for message and signal authentication, as well as power-efficient verification strategies. It will trade-off use case specific performances, such as energy consumption, communication overhead,against achievable levels of security. This activity will enable resilient communication and PNT solutions for low-throughput and low-power applications and, while activity will focus on GNSS and IoT systems operating in licensed and unlicensed bands, the resultswill be applicable to any throughput- and energy-constrained system.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Assessing state-of-the-art relevant to the activity, in particular in low-energy PNT solutions, and in signal and message authentication for GNSSand IoT.- Designing and optimising signal and message authentication for low-throughput systems.- Implementing and testing the solutions in a laboratory environment.- Assessing and benchmarking performances.
