title: AI-BASED FAILURE PREDICTION TO IMPROVE OPERATIONAL PAYLOAD AVAILABILITY - EXPRO PLUS
description: To investigate and develop methodologies using AI, for prediction of core units and payloads failuresbefore their occurrence and assess how this information can contribute to system unavailability.DescriptionFailure detection plays an important role in monitoring the integrity of electrical components but alsounits, payloads and overall system. Failure detection is performed as part theFault Detection Isolation and Recovery (FDIR) system, however, at the moment, little is done in terms of failure prediction and assessment of changes in units behaviour. Most of the work performed in this scope targeting on ground data analysis and not on-board real-time assessment.Artificial Intelligence (AI) has the potential to contribute to a better failure prediction process by looking and analysing information coming from components/units/subsystems and assessing if theirperformance is decreasing with time. Failure and anomaly prediction capabilities based on datatrend prognostics could lead towards an increase in the overall availability of the system through either applying recovery actions before occurrence of failure, or allowing to perform a smoother and faster switch to the redundant branch which would result in less or no interruption of payload or system operation. Finally, such approach couldhave the potential to better understand the degradation effects of units and system and may lead to a better overall mission operationalavailability. The goal of the activity is to research mission payloads and understand how, throughthe use of AI, the outage can be minimised more than through the use of common and currentapproaches.The activity encompasses the following tasks:-Identification and gathering of potential data of payloads that could be used for AI development (e.g. Sentinel, MSG, Telecom, Constellations, etc.) and for overall Neural Network training- Identification of the best types of machine learning algorithms that allow to evaluate behaviours based on training data. Analysis of the statistical techniques, data distribution and probability theory. Provide methods to train and cross-validate and select as approachone of the two broad categories: supervised or unsupervised learning- Development of AI methodology to predict failures in payloads or core units with the scope of minimising outage- Apply the developed AImethodology to a small case study or proof-of-concept (e.g. at payload unit level) for which there is sufficient telemetry data available- Perform comparison between conventional availability results and the resulted availability when the new developed AI approach is being used- Provide inputs and lessons learned to the existing (i.e. SAVOIR) body of knowledge.

title: AGRICULTURAL AND ECOLOGICAL MONITORING SERVICES FOR UKRAINE - EXPRO PLUS
description: On 30 October 2025 ESA and Ukraine signed an Implementing Arrangement to define the content of and the arrangements for assistance to be provided by ESA to Ukraine, with a view to implementing Activities. Agricultural and ecological monitoring services for Ukraine and Black Sea region (SEN4STATUkr) is the first of these activities. Its objective is to improve the current practices in agriculture statistics on the basis of satellite Earth Observations. The work may include: the definition of gaps in agrarian statistics by comparing the practices of the Ukrainian statistical service and European practices; the collection of in-situ and auxiliary data and products to calibrate, run and validate Sen4Stat in Ukraine. This would result in the creation of information services on the basis of satellite data and in-situ monitoring in Ukraine in accordance with the requirements of national statistics and the developmentof recommendations for modernization of services taking into account relevant practices in EU countries.

title: GUIDANCE AND CONTROL DESIGN FOR ENCELADUS LANDER - EXPRO PLUS
description: To trade-off, design and test guidance and control algorithms for an Enceladus lander,from separation from the orbiter until touchdown on the surface.DescriptionOn top of the inherent complexity of any deep-space exploration mission, landing on Enceladus poses unique challenges: a poorly characterized, snow-covered terrain with hazardous surface features, the need to transit active plume regions, a demanding landingaccuracy requirement of 1 km (TBC), and stringent planetary protection requirements to minimize landing site contamination.Succesfully addressing these challenges will require extensive optimization of all lander subsystems, supported by detailed analysis from the earliest mission phases to shape the overall architecture. Particular emphasis must be placed on theGuidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) subsystem and its close coupling with propulsion, given the demanding levels of onboard autonomy and reliability required to ensure a safe and precise landing.This activity will address landing trajectory optimization, thruster selection and configuration, and the design, implementation, and testing of guidance and controlalgorithms capable of managing the full end-to-end lander mission, from separation from the orbiter to touchdown. It will also deliver a verification and validation (VV) facility capable to test the GC algorithms both in Functional Engineering Simulator (FES) and in Processsor-in-the-loop (PIL) environment. While the development of complex navigationalgorithms is excluded, the activity will produce simplified navigation performance modelsfor two different navigation scenarios, in agreement with the Agency: one based on vision basednavigation and another relying solely on inertial sensors and RF link measurements with the orbiter.This activity encompasses the following tasks: Trajectory design, optimization, and operational scenario definition, including requirements definition. Trade-off and detaileddesign of guidance algorithms including divert capability. Sizing, selection, and optimal configuration of propulsion actuators.Trade-off and detailed design of control algorithms. Development of simplified navigation performance models. Development of a FES including Enceladus environment/DKE design, GC algorithms.navigation performance models, propulsion models and propulsion plume / contaminationmodels. Verification and validation (VV) of the proposed design solutions and algorithms throughFES simulations. Port and validate the selected GC algorithms on a space-grade computer to performProcessor-in-the-loop (PIL) testing.

Particular emphasis must be placed on theGuidance, Navigation, and Control (GNC) subsystem and its close coupling with propulsion, given the demanding levels of onboard autonomy and reliability required to ensure a safe and precise landing.This activity will address landing trajectory optimization, thruster selection and configuration, and the design, implementation, and testing of guidance and controlalgorithms capable of managing the full end-to-end lander mission, from separation from the orbiter to touchdown. It will also deliver a verification and validation (VV) facility capable to test the GC algorithms both in Functional Engineering Simulator (FES) and in Processsor-in-the-loop (PIL) environment. While the development of complex navigationalgorithms is excluded, the activity will produce simplified navigation performance modelsfor two different navigation scenarios, in agreement with the Agency: one based on vision basednavigation and another relying solely on inertial sensors and RF link measurements with the orbiter.This activity encompasses the following tasks: Trajectory design, optimization, and operational scenario definition, including requirements definition. Trade-off and detaileddesign of guidance algorithms including divert capability. Sizing, selection, and optimal configuration of propulsion actuators.Trade-off and detailed design of control algorithms. Development of simplified navigation performance models. Development of a FES including Enceladus environment/DKE design, GC algorithms.navigation performance models, propulsion models and propulsion plume / contaminationmodels. Verification and validation (VV) of the proposed design solutions and algorithms throughFES simulations. Port and validate the selected GC algorithms on a space-grade computer to performProcessor-in-the-loop (PIL) testing.

title: GT1I-802GA MULTI-DOMAIN MULTI-MODAL AI CO-WORKER USING AN AGENTIC ARCHITECTURE
description: Agentic AI architecture refers to the design and implementation of AI systems that exhibit autonomy, make decisions, and adapt their behaviour with minimal human oversight. Ground systems engineers and operators today face increasing complexity, fragmentation, and cognitive load across all the domains of ground segment engineering, mission operations and space safety. Users must navigate siloed tools, disconnected data sources, and overlapping processes, leading to inefficiencies and duplicated effort. This activity addresses these challenges by developing an AI-powered" co-worker" - an intelligent, context-aware assistant designed to support users across all phases of the ground segment, as the 'entry-point' and orchestrator for user interaction with ground segment systems. Existing solutions based on Large Language Models (LLM)-are already supporting users by ingesting and summarising information from the various systems. An agentic approach significantly enhances such solutions by adding dedicated and specialised integrations with external tools and data source as well multi-step task breakdown and orchestration. This approach provides the user with a proactive, goal-driven and autonomous support. Building on existing operational solutions already tested by various missions, this co-worker will unify access to knowledge, streamline task execution, and reduce the need for bespoke tools. It will enable users to interact with all systems using human language and receive meaningful, actionable responses.The co-worker will be designed with intuitive interfaces and robust explainability to support decision-making and user confidence. It will integrate securely with MLOps platforms, supporting verification, validation (VV), monitoring, and risk mitigation by design. The system will be based on a state-of-the-art AI agentic architecture, leveraging modular, explainable, goal-oriented agents capable of reasoning across heterogeneousdata sources, orchestrating insights, and coordinating multi-step tasks. Employing multi-agent frameworks and model context protocol (MCP), the system will support task decomposition and specialisation, making it scalable and adaptive to varied user needs.

title: DEMISABLE TANK AND FILLDRAIN VALVE FOR CUBESAT PROPULSION (EXPRO+)
description: ObjectivesTo develop a demisable tank and a fill drain valve for CubeSat propulsion systems.DescriptionThousands of CubeSats operating in LEO have already and/or are planning to adopt chemical or electric propulsion systems to perform orbit insertion, deployment to the desired orbital planes, orbit changes, orbit maintenance, repositioning, collision avoidance and deorbiting at end of life.Yet several uncertainties remain on the demisability of elements constituting such propulsion systems. Some elements of those systems, like the tanks and the fill drain valves, might have high probability to survive during an atmospheric re-entry, due to the adopted system configuration (e.g. shielding effects of some parts on others that impact on the heat flux exposure or connections between components that influence the fragmentation process) and due to the materials adopted.Having reliable data on demisability of these elements is particularly important for the modelling phase of the re-entry analysis, to be able to mimic the entire system demise behaviour (e.g. fragmentation process and demise of the components). Overall, these uncertainties might significantly contribute to the increase of the system casualty risk budget and might create the need for adopting a more complex and expensive controlled re-entry strategies.Therefore, it is necessary to investigate the demise behaviour of elements of future Cubesat propulsion systems and to develop demisable design solutions to ensure compliance of future missions with the Space Debris Mitigation guidelines.This activity addresses any type of tanks and fill drain valves used on propulsion systems intended for Cubesats up to 16U and tasked to store any type of propellant in solid, liquid, or pressurised gas state. The targeted technologies are thus complementary to specific activities that target larger pressurised krypton tanks for LEO smallsat constellations.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Characterisation of the demise behaviour of selected typical tanks and fill drain valves through simulations and tests at component and material level to validate and improve the accuracy of the demise predictions models- Design definition and justification of a demisable tank and demisable fill drain valves- Breadboard manufacturing and functional tests- Generation of development plan for follow-up qualificationhttp://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: CHARACTERIZATION OF CONFORMAL COATINGS AS SN WHISKER RISK MITIGATION STRATEGY AT BOARD LEVEL - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To identify and test European sourced conformal coatings to mitigate the risk of Sn whisker growth on COTS itemsDescription: Use of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) components is becoming common in electronic units. These are typically finished with apure Sn finish which has been historically forbidden in space applications due to the risk of Sn whisker growth. The development ofSn whiskers can lead to short circuits within an electronic unit. This caused the loss of various telecommunication satellites in the early 2000s. The most promising method to mitigate this risk (without changing the plating of the components) is the use of conformal coatings. This activity assesses the ability of different conformal coatings to mitigate Sn whisker growth and investigate the influence of the coating process parameters (e.g. thickness, coverage of the application) on its efficacy. The impact of potential coating damage/defect will also be investigated, seeking to define workmanship criteria. Different test regimes for Sn whisker growthaccelerated testing shall be applied to comparing thermal cycling in ambient pressure, in vacuum and temperature/humidity aging. Different mission scenarios should also be considered (e.g. satellites, reusable systems and habitats). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Literature search to review of test approaches for accelerated growth of Sn whiskers and to identify the conformal coatings to test. The selection of coatings shall include all classes of coatings most used in space with focus on European sourced ones (e.g. silicones, polyurethanes, acrylic, parylene). - Test plan definition. a) test vehicle design using elementary samples (Sn plated uCu sheets for example) with high susceptibility to grow whiskers. This is to allow a controlled application of the coatings. b) test matrix: application parameters to be assessed for each type of coating (thickness, application method.); type of defectsto be introduced (scratches, incomplete application..) c) multiple test regimes shall be applied on different sets of samples. testduration shall double the one defined in JESD201A. d) methodology to assess the growth of whiskers over time (Visual inspection, Scanning electron microscope, tomography...) - Testing and results assessment: classification of the coatings investigated and definition of minimum thickness and workmanship criteria for each coating. Potential future work would include testing of the coating application on EEE device or assemblies prone to grow Sn whiskers, as well as extended test durations.Deliverables: Prototype, Report

title: THROTTLEABLE ENGINE FOR MARS ENTRY DESCENT AND LANDING (E4EX-008)
description: The Explore 2040 strategy outlines plans to increase both the mass and precision of future Mars surface missions over the coming decades, positioning this as a key strategic capability for Europe. In order to realise this goal, it is essential for Europe to further advance the development of guided entry landers and related technologies. The development of a throttleable engine assembly (engine and throttleable device) is a critical enabler for this advanced European Mars entry, descent, and landing capability.The primary objective of this initiative is to design and develop a throttleable engine assembly (engine and throttleable device) that supports precise and controlled descent and landing. The activity specifically focuses on chemical propulsion engines that utilise storablepropellants; cryogenic propulsion systems are excluded. The output of this activity will reach a TRL5 at throttleable engine assembly level by means of developing and verifying key performance characteristics of a full-scale throttleable engine assembly model. The activity will also identify technology gaps and prepare a development plan towards TRL6.

title: FORMATION FLYING AT CLOSE RANGE -EXPRO PLUS
description: Close Formation Flying (CFF) enables a new generation of distributed microwave instruments for Earth observation, where multiple small satellites fly within a few to tens of meters to synthesize a large virtual aperture for Synthetic Aperture Radar, Interferometric Radiometer, or Sounder missions. At such close separations, the relative geometry and timing between spacecraft directly determine instrument performance, such as coherence, resolution, or radiometric accuracy. Achieving this precision requires advanced relative navigation sensors, ultra-low-thrust propulsion, and tightly synchronized inter-satellite links capable of maintaining stable baselines under drag, solar pressure, third body and gravity gradients, as well as magnetic and thermal perturbations. Close Formation Flying (CFF) at short rangebelow 100 m and up to few metersrepresents the next step beyond the long-baseline formations demonstrated by several missions such as GRACE-FO and TanDEM-X. In this tight regime, inter-satellite distances are small enough for the formation itself to act as a distributed microwave aperture, enabling coherent sensing for SAR, Interferometric Radiometer, and Sounder missions. Unlike long-range formations, short-range CFF demands continuous, ultra-precise control to maintain millimetre-to-centimetre relative positioning, mitigate plume and thermal effects, and ensure microsecond to nanosecond synchronization and phase coherence. Building on heritage from PROBA-3 and related demonstrations, short-range CFF introduces new challenges in navigation accuracy, thrust resolution, and electromagnetic compatibility, but offers the potential for transformative gains in microwave imaging resolution, calibration stability, and measurement sensitivity.The objective of this activity is to determine the technical feasibilityof establishing, maintaining, and reconfiguring a close formation fly configuration (relative distance of less than 100 meters, target below 10m) for a specified distributed microwave mission (Distributed SAR, Distributed Radiometer or Distributed Sounder), and toidentify associated technology gaps and a development roadmap.

title: UNFURLABLE STEPPED REFLECTOR FOR HIGH FIDELITY RANGING SIGNALS AND PHASE STABILITY - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To design manufacture and test a new innovative Shaped Unfurlable Stepped Reflector for Next Positioning Navigation and Timing Small Satellite Antennas.Description: Future scenarios for the evolution in the Positioning Navigation and Timing services, see the introduction of small satellites as the most attractive solution for cost reduction and the use of different frequencies foreach specific applications. In Europe, for global coverage, consolidated technologies for array configuration have been developed in the past years showing excellent performance in terms of end of coverage gain, power handling and phase stability. However these technologies are not considered adequate for future small satellites, or hosted payloads where mass and volume are very strong requirements. Dual shaped reflector unfurlable stepped antennas, are considered one of the best candidates in this possible scenario, compatible with geostationary, inclined geostationary, medium, low medium , and low orbits, providing reduced stowed volume, and complexity in the overall RF antenna architecture compared with the equivalent array solutions. In addition this configuration will allow to minimize the gain variation over coverage (isoflux like pattern) compared to canonical shape unfurlable reflectors. One of the objectives of the activity will be to reduce the stowed footprint by around 60% for reflectors with a deployed diameter of 1.5 meters. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Identification, based on literature review and technical trade-offs, of the most promising technology and deployment methods; -Detailed design of the deployment mechanisms for the stepped reflector and reflector membrane/mesh support to guarantee the adequate shape to the surface after the completion of the deployment; - Manufacturing, deployment and RF testing of the breadboard to validate the concept.

title: DATA RELAY RF SIMULATOR SYSTEM - EXPRO PLUS (RE-ISSUE)
description: Objectives: The objective of this activity is to develop a system simulator for testing the RF links of multi satellite missions. The focus of the simulator should be the modelling of a full set of satellite and laned assets transmitters and receivers with their precise orbit determination around different bodies of the solar system (e.g. Earth, Moon, Mars).Description: There is a high interest in the development of cluster of data relay satellites for planetary exploration and navigation. There are different studies and developments ongoing related to this concept both for Moon and Mars. Such a simulator system for Moon and Mars is considered an asset to support the development of this cluster missions and to support the development and test of the user terminals in an operating environment.The objective of the activity is hence to develop a RF simulator of a data relay system. The simulator shall be able to interface via RF either with a user terminal unit or with a data relay unit and to: Model full satellite's cluster transmitters and receivers. Model user terminals' transmitters and receivers. Emulate the user terminal spacecraft dynamic motion on planet surface, orbit, or during descent and ascent from the surface: Doppler, Doppler rate and delay. Emulate the relay satellite dynamic motion in orbit: Doppler, Doppler rate and delay. Emulate transmitter and receiver antenna gain and phase patterns of the relay satellite and of the user spacecraft host. Emulate the interference generated by the multiple transmitters of the cluster. Emulate multipath effects. Emulate any atmospheric attenuation or delay effects (for Mars case). Emulate the (two way) range measurement function of the relay link to characterize the performance and functionality.The RF relay simulator shall emulate the signals of each satellite of the cluster in both Sband and K-band in a modular fashion (i.e. S-band module independent from K-band module). The data relay RF simulator system shall employ software in the loop and hardware in the loop techniques to allow the user to design the test scenarios and to control external hardware blocks. The main goal is to have full control of all aspects of the useroperating environment, to enable exact repeatability of the test and to allow the application of systematic errors or incidents that are normally impossible to verify or not tested during the RF compatibility tests. The Emulation of the relay satellites shall be configurable to emulate different relay systems such as different (type of) Moon or Mars scenario.The following tasks are foreseen in this activity: Revision and consolidation of requirements. Architectural and detailed design, including the design of the simulator system at system level and building block level. The detailed requirements for each buildingblock of the system should be derived. It shall be determined if each building block need to be developed or if there are COTS blocks that can be embedded. Implementation of the hardware and software needed to constitute the system simulator prototype. Test and demonstration of the simulator.Deliverables: Hardware prototype, Software, Report.

title: EVALUATION OF FAULT MITIGATION TECHNIQUESFOR NEUROMORPHIC HARDWARE ACCELERATOR - EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To analyse the impacts of fault propagation in spiking neural networks (SNN), propose design mitigation techniques, identify relevant neuromorphic IPs and select a baseline concept for implementation.Description: Future missions, including planetary landing, planetary exploration, docking, debris removal, space situational awareness, in-orbit servicing, etc. will need increased autonomy to address latency issues. This autonomy will rely on AI-driven computer vision and advanced computing capabilities. However,traditional neural network inferences typically require hardware platforms such as FPGAs or GPUs, which may consume anywhere from afew tens of watts to 100 watts. This high-power consumption may necessitate active cooling systems, impacting weight, volume, complexity, and ultimately resulting in additional costs and risks for missions. Safety-critical class 1 missions, including autonomous docking, autonomous landing, and autonomous rover/drone navigation, will require lower power, low footprint (pin count), scalable, and fault-tolerant hardware accelerators. Event-based processing with Neuromorphic technologies, show potential for the future of intelligent sensing, whether it involves event-based cameras, LiDAR, or radar sensors. Neuromorphic technology can address in an effectivemanner the challenge posed by edge AI, sustaining a high processing load, while keeping power consumption low (from few Watts to sub-Watt). Concrete use cases such as, autonomous landing, autonomous docking have been studied, validating Neuromorphic technology through the deployment on commercial device (COTS). Neuromorphic technology is suited for computer vision applications, planned activities should also confirm the suitability for radar as well. Few commercial IPs have shown potential in studies as explained above.However, additional work is needed to adapt a solution for space missions, ensuring low power, scalability, low pin count, and fault tolerance. Leveraging state-of-the-art neuromorphic commercially available IPs, this activity aims to propose a solution that addresses these needs effectively by designing a neuromorphic hardware accelerator using advanced rad hard ASIC technology. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Hardware accelerator specifications consolidation - selection and product roadmap definition - IP fault mitigation techniques analysis - Hardware accelerator architecture definition - Hardware accelerator design - Hardware accelerator validation / simulation.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators.For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: HYBRID MANUFACTURING FOR SPACE APPLICATION - EXPRO PLUS
description: To advance hybrid manufacturing strategies that integrate conventional and advanced techniques to enhance the performance, functionality and competitiveness of space hardware.Description:Hybrid manufacturing combines subtractive methods (e.g. milling, turning,grinding) with additive processes(e.g. powder bed processes, direct energy deposition). It may also include fabrication/joining steps like welding,bonding or brazing. This approach aims to overcome limitations of individual processes, enabling theproduction ofhigh-performance, competitive components. Such methodologies are of growing relevance particularly in propulsion, thermal management and structural systems. The key drivers include:- Geometric complexity: enabling the manufacture of intricate, topology-optimisedstructures difficult to realiseby conventional means alone.- Material efficiency: by adding material only where needed, hybrid manufacturing reduces waste and optimizes material usage.- Functional performance: enabling graded material properties, local reinforcements or tailored functionality.- Cost and lead time: consolidating steps, minimising waste and enabling complex geometries, though it mayrequire specialised planning, equipment and qualification.- Design flexibility: greater customization and flexibility in design, making it ideal for producing bespoke or low volume parts.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Survey of relevant techniques, materials and equipment capabilities relevant to a hybrid manufacturing approach.- Selection of two representative case studies with associated requirements (e.g. one propulsion component, one thermal management part).- Design and definition of the hybrid manufacturing route for each case study.- Manufacturing and functional testing of demonstrators. The utilisation of new digital methods for supportinghybrid manufacturing decisions is welcomed. This may include artificial intelligence techniques, such asdeep/federated learning techniques, as well as a focus on use-cases of generatively designed parts (whichinherently benefit from the hybrid manufacturing techniques), alongside the artificial intelligence and machine learning data-driven learning.- Economic analysis, including cost comparison with conventional approaches and life-cycle considerations.Deliverables: Breadboard, ReportNOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: TIME DIVISION DUPLEXING (TDD) KA-BAND IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT FOR NGSO 5G BROADBAND SERVICES (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3E.029)
description: The objective of the activity is to develop and perform an in-orbit experiment of Non-GeoSynchornous Orbit (NGSO) payload technology to prove the feasibility of Time Division Duplexing method in Ka-band for broadband services, allowing operators to gain access to 3 GHz of additional Ka-band spectrum (24.5 - 27.5 GHz) via 5G New Radio waveform in Frequency Range 2 (FR2).Targeted Improvements:Access to an additional 3 GHz of terrestrial spectrum between 24.5-27.5GHz. 30% improvement in spectrum efficiency due to Time Division Duplexing optimisation.Description: The use of Time Domain Duplexing (TDD) for satellite communications can provide access to an additional 3 GHz of Ka-band spectrum (24.5 - 27.5 GHz) via 5G New Radio waveform in Frequency Range 2 (FR 2). The feasibility of employing this technology in Non-Geosynchronous Orbit (NGSO) broadband systems depends on the round-trip time as well as on the waveform and system operations (e.g., synchronisation), which necessitate in-orbit tests to confirm feasibility. TDD technology is highly latency dependent, and there exists a number of technical challenges to be addressed in-orbit:- ability to synchronise uplink with downlink on the satellite payload as well as the user terminal- varying guard times that are required under various geometrical configurations- timing reference accuracy required by the payload- frequency of ephemeris update rate required at the terminal- RF front-end performance given the Tx/Rx co-existence- ability of the ground segment to schedule various uplink/downlink capacity allocations (from e.g. 90/10 down- to up-link ratio to 50/50 down- to up-link ratio). The activity shall therefore develop a scaled Ka-band payload engineering model, employing the 5G New Radio waveform and shall confirm the feasibility of TDD in Ka-band systems in real operating conditions by testing the payload in-orbit. The payload shall be embarked on a NGSO hosted payload service, for a period of at least 4 months, in order to test it under a variety of operating conditions (e.g., different elevations) and 5G New Radio waveform configurations (e.g., different guard time intervals). The activity shall implement all necessary elements for performing the in-orbit experimental mission, such as: - Licensing (e.g. under Article 4.4 of the ITU-R Radio Regulations) - Contracting a hosted payload service and mission operations - Ground segment provision.The activity shall be implemented in a phased approach, to ensure alignment with the latest 3GPP updates. title: CRYOGENIC OPERATIONS IN NEAR VACUUM: FLASH-DISINTEGRATION RELATED TO STORAGE AND REUSABILITY - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To investigate flash transformations during depressurization for superheated cryogenic liquids and to model and validateflash atomization, vaporization, condensation and icing processes.Description: Flash-boiling is an extremely complex physical phenomenon and includes nucleate boiling, bubble growth, droplets formation, evaporation and (possibly) solidification in a vapor-dropletmedium. In particular operating engine re-ignition, venting or attitude control devices results into hard ignition, erroneous forceand torque estimation and into 'ice' deposition on walls with potential damaging impact when breaking off. In order to model this complex flash-boiling process and solidification process, an integrated experimental and theoretical study shall combine synergicallydifferent disciplines and skills. An integrated comparative approach, based on detailed experiments, molecular dynamic simulations,modern molecular kinetic theory for modelling nucleation, bubble growth and evaporation processes, is a substantial leap forward with respect to the current modelling approaches that still heavily rely on empirical correlations or quasi-equilibrium assumptions. Experimentally, non-intrusive velocity and droplet size measurements in flash-boiling sprays, separation of ice particle areas from liquid droplet areas and visualization of the internal injector/orifice flow are envisaged, paired by systematic and controlled experiments on dropwise condensation/evaporation. These sets of experiments will provide then the basis for the development and validation of a comprehensive physical model, capable of describing and predicting the behaviour of cryogenic flashing jets. Theoretically, accurate models will be proposed to describe the evolution of the bubble size distributions within the nozzle flow (or liquid jets),the fragmentation process and the process of superheated dropwise evaporation. For the theoretical analysis, different approaches will be used: direct and approximated solutions of the Boltzmann equations, molecular dynamic simulations and the kinetic theory of homogeneous nucleation. The final goal is to include kinetic effects in the formulation of macroscopic models to improve the accuracyofthe predictions for large departure from equilibrium (i.e., at highly superheated conditions). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Cryogenic spray experiments - Superheated droplet evaporation experiments and modelling - Modelling of the boiling process and fragmentation.http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: PHASE 0 OF ECOSTARS - SUSTAINABLE SMALL PLATFORM DESIGN CONSOLIDATION- EXPRO PLUS
description: The EcoStar project is an ESA initiative aimed at embedding environmental sustainability into the design and development of space systems. By applying eco-design principles and life cycle assessment methodologies, EcoStar supports the transition toward greener spacecraft and aligns with ESA's long-term sustainability goals.This specific activity within EcoStar contributes to the achievement of ESA's Green Agenda Goals for 2030 (EGA 2030). The development and demonstration in orbit of ecodesigned technologies is essentialfor ESA's aspiration to pioneer on environmentally sustainable solutions and mitigate the future impacts of its missions. This phase 0 consolidation phase builds upon the outcomes of the SysNova campaign 24-P-M-OPS-12 "Pre-phase A System Study for an EcoStars IOD" that took place in 2025 for which there were 5 parallel activities. This design iteration is key to consolidate the early findingsand fully meet ESA sustainability objectives, including the consolidation of the assessment of environmental impact mitigation actions, further assessment of MAIT aspects and industrialisation approaches, and the compliance with the Zero Debris objectives.The procurement will be open competition to all industrial entities, ensuring an open competitive approach preparing further steps. Parallel contracts may be placed in case of competitive complementary proposals.

title: SPACE PROPULSION TEST ANOMALIES DATASET FOR MACHINE LEARNING ASSISTED FAULT DETECTION AND ISOLATION - EXPRO PLUS
description: An early and reliable anomaly detection is crucial in all propulsion test activities. It is particularly needed to reduce damages for the test infrastructure and the test specimen, as prototypes or unique infrastructures are often costly in manufacturing or refurbishment in case of damage. The costs associated with the damage of test specimens or test infrastructure show the importance of a suitable Fault Detection and Isolation system (FDI). Current redline-based fault detection systems used at the test facilities are very safe, but do not yet use modern methods such as artificial intelligence (AI) techniques. The space propulsion test is simply aborted if a time dependent sensor signal exceeds a given maximum or minimum value at a specific time or within a given time interval or if a sensor signal standard deviation level is too high. On the one hand, more sophisticated AI techniques have the potential to avoid the occurrence of redline-triggered test stops by identifying precursor patterns in the test data. On the other hand, these modern methods can be used to initiate countermeasures much earlier before critical values are reached. AI techniques are heavily dependent on available data for the training of the machine learning algorithm, and for a reliable evaluation of the final results. A publicly available reference data set is not existing within the community, due to a lack of publisheddata from propulsion tests. Nevertheless, dedicated data from propulsion tests should be present at test facilities across Europe.Due to a better usage of margins and less unintentional test aborts, AI methods allow a more economic usage of available test capabilities. An AI system would providea proper diagnostic in real-time from existing sensor data, to detect and classify abnormal behaviour during propulsion tests. In case of a critical test anomaly an emergency shutdown is triggered.The proposed activity aims to develop of a machine learning assisted anomaly/fault detection and isolation system for space propulsion test facilities, based on a dataset consisting of already available space propulsion tests.This activity encompasses the following tasks: Generation of known anomalies and nominal behaviour database from available space propulsion tests:o Identification of the requirements for the propulsion database.The requirements include the structure of the database itself, and the test data which should be included into the database.The structure of the database has to be optimised for the usage of a machine learning approach and should be suitable for a continuous development or enhancement.o Implementation of the databased and filling with already available data of space propulsion tests. Design and realization of a laboratory test bench setup Selection of a suitable existing test bench.o Identification of requirements for a test bench setup suitable for the testing of machine learning based FDI algorithms.o Integration of the setup into the existing test benchinfrastructure. Synthetic and real training data generationo Selection of a suitable numerical tool.o Generation of synthetic data for the training of a machine learning based FDI method.o Evaluation of the quality of the synthetic data against the database created previously.o Enhancement of the generation of real data using the test bench setup. Training of the machine learning based FDI systemo Development and training of the machine learning algorithm, using the synthetic dataset generated within the previous task.o Evaluation of the resulting algorithm against the spacepropulsion test anomaly database and enhancement of the quality of the machine learning algorithm using real data from propulsion tests. Verification and evaluation of the test anomaly detection systemo Assessment of the ability to reliably detect and isolateanomalies during space propulsion tests using the simplified but representative test setup.o Quantitative evaluation of the detection accuracy for the trained machine learning model. The uncertainty for novel operating conditions is evaluated. Furthermore, the potential improvement of the model by further data integration is investigated.

title: GT17-675GS -DISRUPTION TOLERANT NETWORKING (DTN) NETWORK MANAGEMENT
description: Disruption Tolerant Networking (DTN) is the network architecture taking the specific challenges, like frequently interrupted linksand large round-trip delays into account. DTN has been identified as a solution for next generation space missions, including Earth Observation missions, constellations, and Lunar and Mars communication networks.While the core protocols for DTN, such as the Bundle Protocol (BP) and Bundle Security Protocol (BPSEC), have been defined and initial BP deployments onground exist and in-orbitdemonstrations have been performed, associated management and operations concepts still need to be defined and validated in representative scenarios. This activity addresses the development of an overall DTN network management and operations architecture involving mission and network operations (including ground segment operations). Interoperability with other agencies and commercial partners will need to be addressed and the architecture shall take operational and security concerns into account. However, the focusison the overall operations concepts for a network of networks operated together withother agencies and commercial entities, ultimately forming a Solar System Internet'. It is expected that the proposed activity shall contribute to these important international challenges from a European perspective

title: HIGH FREQUENCY MINIATURE ACOUSTIC FILTERS FOR COMMUNICATION PAYLOADS (ARTES AT 5C.538) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop, manufacture and test miniaturised high frequency acoustic filters engineering models up to Ku-band.Targeted Improvements: Reduction of the size and mass with at least a factor of 10 compared with state-of-the art on-board technologies.Description: The market is continuously requesting mass and volume reduction improvements in payload technology. However, current state of the art electromagnetic (EM) resonator filter technologies, such as cavity and planar filters, all bulky and are reaching their limitation in terms of compactness. The introduction of acoustic wave filter technology has the potential to overcome these limitations, and the reduction in size and mass will enable integration into the payload receivers and frequency converters. In addition, the technologycan also offer semiconductor compatibility, enabling high integration of RF front ends. Currently, standard acoustic filter technology is limited up to S-band frequency capability, which prevents its wider use in telecommunication payloads equipment. The worldwide explosion in mobile smartphone usage has been enabled by the development of piezoelectricity-based acoustic wave resonators and filters. Various technical advances are ongoing in the frame of 5G/6G terrestrialinfrastructure applications. Recent developments in advanced engineered substrates such guided surface acoustic wave (SAW) and single crystal eXtended Bulk Acoustic Wave (XBAW), open the possibility of developing high performance and medium frequency filter components. Bulk Acoustic Resonator (BAR) technology has emerged during recent years where filters in the C-band has been demonstrated, and the quality of thin piezoelectric plates has improved. BAR devices offer high Q-values with a small size/footprint with critical dimension of the metallisation pattern not necessarily limited to the acoustic wavelength. This enables BAR devices in the C-band andbeyond.This activity will develop, manufacture and test engineering model acoustic wave-based filters up to Ku-band, for integration in telecom payloads. Suitable packaging technologies will also be assessed. The performance will be quantified by testing at wafer and packaged device levels under representative environment.

title: RETURNABLE TESTBED FOR IN-ORBIT MANUFACTURING PROCESSES FOR LARGE STRUCTURES O TELECOM SATELLITES (ARTES AT 3E.027) - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to develop and characterize an additive manufacturing process to enable in-orbit manufacturing of large structural parts for satcom applications (e.g. large reflector, large solar array, large radiator structure). An in-orbit test-bed will be designed, manufactured and operated. Test-samples and complex demonstrators will be produced in order to evaluate the developed end-to-end in-orbit manufacturing process.Targeted Improvements: Enabling large in-orbit manufactured satcom hardware (e.g. large reflector, large solar array, radiator structure) not possible today.Description: Recent studies have explored the possibility of making large structures in orbit for future satcom applications, revealing new opportunities for applications, services andmarkets.The use of in-orbit additive manufacturing could eliminate the constraints of the launch vehicle fairings and the complexity of the deployment mechanisms, which are currently required for large deployables (e.g. very large reflectors, radiators and booms) relative to the platform size. However, the effects of microgravity, thermal, vacuum, and radiation on the additive manufacturing process in space are not well known, especially when assessing the structural, thermophysical and thermoelastic properties of the fabricated parts.This activity will characterize, through the production of test samples, the space environmental effects on the additive manufacturing processes required for future in-orbit manufacturing of large structural parts for satcom applications. An onboard testbed, using well established additive manufacturing processes and space qualified materials, will bedeveloped, manufactured andvalidated. The testbed shall accommodate visual and in situ measurements of the manufacturing process (e.g. temperature, molecular/particulate contamination induced by the process, etc) as well as allowing for the retrieval of the produced specimens for post-analysis on Earth. The testbed will also be used to producecomplex demonstrators (e.g. reflectors, booms and radiators or representative parts thereof). All in-orbit produced parts will be returned to Earth for post-analysis.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach. The first phase of the activity will develop, manufacture and achieve flight readiness of the testbed. The testbed performance will be validated on ground with reference test samples being produced and characterised. Phase 1 output will comprise of:Flight ready in-orbit manufacturing testbed, characterised end-to-end manufacturing process and reference test samples. The second phase will launch and operate the test bed to investigate the end-to-end additive manufacturing process in the space environment. Phase 2 will produce test samples in-orbit for process and material characterisation that are collected and returned for on ground analysis and comparison.The test results will be fed into Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) models to optimise in-orbit manufacturing parameters and processes for the production ofthe complex demonstrators.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF IN-SITU MONITORING FOR LARGE SCALE ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING APPLICATIONS - EXPRO+
description: Objectives:To develop in-situ monitoring systems for Large Scale Additive Manufacturing by in-situ nondestructiveinvestigation.Description:Additive manufacturing processes for large metallic parts such as laser cladding or Wire and ArcAdditive Manufacturing (WAAM) are currently being developed to reach the quality standardsrequired by space application. One of the main challenges to be overcome is to control the qualityof the large parts printed as their inspection is complicated due to their large dimensions.Thisactivity aims at development of in-situ monitoring to allow to control the manufacturing process(e.g. cooling rates and associatedmicrostructure, geometrical deviation, lack of fusion, residualstresses, atmosphere and oxide creation) directly during manufacturing.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Establishment of overview of the most advanced Direct Energy Deposition (DED) processesfor large part production for launcher applications- Identification of target process and two materials of interest for launcher applications- Definition of specific parameters to be monitored including materials specific issues such ascooling rates for Inconel, and oxygen pick up for Titanium- Special consideration to monitor surface and sub-surface defects as some of the large partscannot be post processed or machined after DED processes.- Development of specific NDI methods for all identified parameters- Verification of NDI methods capabilities at samples level in comparison with destructive analysis- Production of several parts with varying geometry to assess residual stresses and geometrical deviations- Manufacturing of large part to demonstrate the capabilities of the NDI at component level. A defect catalogue for the DED process selected and the materials tested is aimed to be be created- Definition of a roadmap for the implementation of in process corrections when defects are detectedActivity serves the area of low cost and low mass solutions for launchers.

title: TRANSMIT AND RECEIVE DUAL POLARIZATIONACTIVE ANTENNA BASED ON SCALABLE TILE ASSEMBLYFOR GEOSTATIONARY SATELLITES (ARTES AT 5B.248) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test a scalable Ku- or Ka-band tile assembly enabling compact combined transmit and receive active antenna for satellites in geosynchronous orbit. This will include the development of a mechanical and thermal concept. Targeted Improvements: Reduction of the number of antennas at spacecraft level by a factor of 2. Description: There is a trend for telecommunication satellites in Geostationary Orbits to reduce the size of the platform whilst maintainingcapacity of the system. The accommodation of several active antennas in such reduced size platforms is becoming more challenging and the need for integrated transmit and receive phased array antennas is growing. The current feed chain solutions are often based onhollow or ridge waveguide technology which meet performance requirements but result in bulky implementations and therefore they arenot compatible for implementing transmit and receive in the same aperture while keeping both orthogonal polarisations. New ways of implementing RF components based on planar technologies have been previously studied but this technology is trading in insertion loss and RF bandwidth performance. New PCB based technology such as Air-Filled Surface Integrated Waveguide (AFSIW), gap-technology andadvanced manufacturing techniques have the potential to significantly reduce the volume with respect to the current state of the art, whilst maintaining good RF performance. Metamaterials, which are engineered materials with unique properties, are also a potential solution to reduce the volume of feed chain assemblies. This activity will develop in a concept of a dual polarised combined transmit and receive active antenna in Ku- or Ka-band. Trade-off studies of several antenna topology designs will be performed. Breadboarding of critical components of the feed chain will be carried out including the development of a low loss filtering solution. A breadboard of a tile assembly will be developed and tested. For the breadboard tile assembly off-the shelf high power amplifiers and lownoise amplifiers shall be baselined. Thermal and mechanical assessment and experimental tests of the tile-assembly will be carried to evaluate the performance of the developed active antenna.

title: SATELLITE BROADBAND AT A FIBER BROADBAND PRICE POINT (ARTES FP 1B.141) EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: This activity will study the architectural and technological advancements needed to deliver satellite-based broadband services fromGEO at a cost comparable to that of terrestrial networks. The study will firstly identify future applications, user profiles, performance benchmarks, and cost targets for future broadband service provision; survey existing satcom mission profiles, system architectures, satellite designs, and operational concepts; and subsequently formulate a system-level approach to deliver the expected use cases at the target price point when operating within a multi-orbit satellite architecture. The outputs from the activity will include the service definition, outline satellite design, and overall system architecture, as well as a roadmap to realise the technology developments needed to realise such a system.

title: S3-CL-05 SIMPLIFIED LCA AND ECODESIGN TOOL FOR SPACE MISSIONS - EXPRO+
description: Following the endorsement of the ESA Ecodesign Policy in October 2025, the systematic integration of ecodesign principles into ESA programmes and projects has become a key enabler for achieving ESA Green Agenda objectives. However, current Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) approaches remain too complex and resource-intensive for routine use during mission conception and preliminary design. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a simplified LCA and ecodesign tool for space missions, enabling rapid environmental assessments and the comparison of alternative design solutions during phases A/B1. The tool developed in this activity will provide a practical and harmonised means to support ecodesign implementation across the European space sector while ensuring consistency with ESA environmental datasets and European assessment methodologies. The project targets bringing the technology to TRL 6.

title: S3-CL-16 ROBOTICS CUBESAT DEMONSTRATOR MISSION STUDY AND PAYLOAD MATURATION EXPRO+
description: Robotics technologies are fundamental enablers for future In-Orbit Servicing missions. This activity aims to mature a generic robotic actuator integrating position and force sensing, active compliance and variable impedance control towards an in-orbit demonstration mission. The activity will consolidate the mission architecture and payload design, develop a Proto Flight Model, and mature the technology to TRL7 while advancing the overall demonstration mission towards implementation. The resulting mission will validate keyrobotic capabilities required for future servicing, docking and manipulation operations in orbit.

title: EFC3 - WORK ORDER - ESTEC WORKSHOP OPERATIONS SERVICE 3-TEC-ETM-0-008
description: The Test Centre division is operating a small workshop (electro-mechanical workshop, EMWS) to support the maintenance and operationof the Test Centre and the laboratories that are on European Space Research and Technology Centre (ESTEC) site. A set of machines and tool is available to offer a quick and flexible service to all teams located on ESTEC site. The machines range from conventional manufacturing to Computer Numerical control (CNC), from Printed Circuit Board (PCB) milling and engraving machines to standard soldering stations. Type of application may differ significantly from one workpiece to the next, encompassing various types of materials,from plastic and Aluminium to Titanium, Inconel etc., and various size, from very small, articulated 5-axes workpieces to sturdy, relatively heavy structures for dynamic testing. The Service in scope is to provide maintenance and daily operation of the EMWS, assuring the support to its customers in the field of product manufacturing.

title: HYDRON HAPS: HAPS-BASED OPTICAL NETWORK EXTENSION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.242) EXPRO+
description: Objective:The objective of this study is to develop a system concept extending High-throughput Optical Network (HydRON) services to High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) and their networks. To identify the technology gaps as well as the required development roadmap including estimations of schedule and costs.Targeted Improvements:To enable the connectivity of HAPS to an evolution of the satellite optical network system.Description:High-Altitude Pseudo-Satellites (HAPS) will play the role of an intermediate, airborne layer in a multi-domain/orbit communications architecture in line with the optical-6G concept. HAPS operate in the stratosphere at altitudes of 15 to 50 km, where they can maintain a near-stationary position for weeks or even months at a time. A single HAPS cancreate a wide-area communication cell that provides reliable connectivity to remote or rural areas where building traditional terrestrial infrastructure is uneconomical. A satellite-to-HAPS optical link can serve as a high-bandwidth feeder link, backhauling data from the HAPS to the satellite network and then to the terrestrial network, avoiding the need for a ground gateway in an inaccessiblelocation. HAPS can conduct long-term surveillance or monitoring missions over a specific area of interest, providing a significantadvantage over LEO satellites which only pass over a given point for a few minutes at a time. With an optical link, a HAPS can uplinkreal-time, high-resolution imagery and sensor data to a satellite (or another HAPS), enabling rapid analysis for applications like border security, environmental monitoring, or situational awareness. In the event of a natural disaster that destroys ground-basedcommunication networks, HAPS can be rapidly deployed to provide a temporary but persistent communications hub. The optical link to an optical backbone network like HydRON ensures that the HAPS remains connected to the global network, providing critical communicationcapabilities for first responders and civilians.The activity shall investigate user needs, requirements, and system concepts for HAPS-space bidirectional optical communications, to upgrade the HydRON System with an airborne layer. Technology gaps and relatedtechnology roadmaps shall be identified and addressed for any critical technology, including optical terminals. The system shall consider the management of cloud-blockage by combining space communications with e.g. a HAPS-to-HAPS free-space network or hybrid communications in RF. The concept shall consider the combination of security sensitive communications with logistic traffic. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator concept where the relevant technology as well as the operational concept can be verified. The activity will also contribute to the evolution of ESTOL.

title: BIOLOGY MULTIWELL - EXPRO PLUS
description: The proposed activity primarily aims at demonstrating the Biology Multiwell, a standardised sample holder and life-support system for biomedical tissue models.The secondary objective of the activity is twofold:- to use the Biology Multiwell for long-duration cell cultivation- to perform an early demonstration with the Biology Multiwell and CSA's MicroPREP facilityBy leveraging this opportunity with MicroPREP on the ISS, we aim to pave the way for future in-situ biology research post-ISS in LEO and beyond LEO. The standardised sample holder is intended to be compatible with accommodation in other facilities, such as MARIN.

title: SPIN-IN DEVELOPMENT OF TERRESTRIAL SOLAR CELL TECHNOLOGY FOR CONSTELLATION APPLICATIONS (ARTES AT 4F.175) - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective is to investigate use of cost-effective solar cells, using materials such as silicon or perovskites, currently available or under development for terrestrial applications, and test their suitability for satcom constellation missions as well as undertake any necessary adaptations.Targeted Improvements:Enabling an European or Canadian source of solar cells for constellation.Activity Description: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellation market is impacting the solar cell requirements, and parameters such as production rates is becoming a priority. Terrestrial solar arrays use predominantly silicon solar cells, but there are multiple variants (inc. homojunction cells, heterojunction cells) that are expected to have degraded performance in space environment mainly due to particle irradiation. Additionally, design features such as contact metallisation and cell interconnection schemes may need to be adapted to survive the thermal cycling environment to take full benefit of terrestrial solar cells for LEO constellation satellites.This activity will survey and test the different existing terrestrial solar cell technologies for space applications in low Earth orbit taking into account the specific space environment requirements (e.g. particle irradiation environment, thermal cycling, etc.).The survey results will be used to identify needed design changes and an engineering model of a terrestrial based solar cell for LEO constellation will be developed and experimentally tested.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors(incl. SMEs). title: BEYOND-EARTH COMMUNICATION NETWORK (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.215) EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to study and evaluate architectures for a beyond-Earth optical communication network, considering coverage, possible data relay services to missions and technologies involved. The resulting network architecture shall consider inter-spacecraft links as well as direct to Earth links, evaluating operational constraints and technology gaps.A roadmap explicitly describing the technology gaps and the required investment for developing optical communications for beyond-Earth shall beestablished, improving data return and coverage offuture missions.Targeted Improvements:To investigate the increase of data capacity compared to state-of-the-art beyond-Earth communications.To identify technology gaps and network architectures based on the network capacity simulation tool to be developed.Description:The study shall investigate trade-offs on beyond-Earth communication architectures involving data relay satellites (e.g., in various Lagrange orbits) as well as optical ground stations in strategic places on Earth. The study shall analyse operational constraints, planetary coverage and the required technologies. A concept of operations (CONOPS) of a beyond-Earth network shall be designed including the space and the ground segments. Initial requirements at mission, system, and subsystem level shall be developed and a roadmap identifying gaps and the required developments shall be established. Direct optical communications to Earth does not have unlimited availability, for example due to clouds, or if the satellite is close (or behind) to the Sun. A data relay satellite in GEO relaying the data via radio to ground shall therefore be included in thestudy. A software simulation tool shall be developed to analyse and optimise potential network architectures. Furthermore, a rough order of magnitude (ROM) cost of deployment and operation of the optical beyond-Earth network shall be established.

title: CORE STUDIES FOR THE ESA SENTINEL BENEFITS OBSERVATORY
description: This Tender shall provide for the core activities of ESA's Sentinels Benefits Observatory until 2028. Its core objective will be toprovide ESA with an oversight about notable Sentinels users, usages and benefits to support service improvements, inform programmatic aspects and promote general facts-based awareness through wide-spread uptake of impact assessment practices related to the use ofCopernicus space data. In the last decade, the use of Copernicus Sentinel satellites has become widespread in Europe and beyond and different studies have ben undertaken to demonstrate this. Since 2017, the ESA-managed Sentinel Benefits Study (SeBS) has investigated a number of cases based on a robust "bottom-up" methodology as well as developed thematic transversal analyses (see https://earsc.org/sebs) . The Agency intends to continue and expand the SeBS achievements, further enriching it in specific areas such as thequantification of non-monetary benefits (e.g. environmental and societal) and the potential benefits to be expected from future missions such as the forthcoming Sentinel Expansion Missions. Furthermore, it intends to liaise with experts and practitioners worldwide, pursuing overall advancements in the design of robust and structured assessment frameworks that could support comparative trend analyses along time, stimulate wide-spread grassroot information and promote a general culture of impact assessment practices among Sentinel users.

title: CONCEPTS FOR ULTRA-LARGE APERTURE ANTENNAS (ARTES FPE 1A.113) - EXPRO+
description: This study will explore techniques, topologies, and technologies for realising very large (i.e., more than 20 m in diameter) array antennas in orbit. The activity will consider feasibility in all frequency bands currently used for satcom as well as bands likely to be used in the future but will focus on operation at higher frequencies. In-orbit assembly of pre-manufactured modules as well as the signal combination of physically unconnected elements "formation flying" shall be assessed. Radiative element design, sub-array definition, beamforming, inter-element data connections, scalability, reliability, as well as power amplification, generation, and distribution shall all be considered. The study shall also include assessment of manufacturing and spacecraft integration feasibility.

title: AUTONOMOUS LEO ACCELERATED DEMO DOCKING TO ISS NODE (ALADDIN)
description: The LEO Cargo Return Service (LCRS) provides an ad-hoc partnership scheme, whereby private companies receive support from ESA for the development of commercial cargo transportation services to human outposts in LEO. Phase 1 of the LEO Cargo Return Service (LCRS), currently ongoing until June 2026 with two parallel contracts, covers the early development phases. The subject Phase 2 (ALADDIN) will complete the development and lead to the execution of up to two demonstration missions to the International Space Station (ISS). The original intention was for the LCRS demonstration mission to deliver cargo to the ISS by 2030. Per the current information, the operations and timeline of the ISS de-orbiting require that the demonstration missions to the ISS be executed within Q2/2029,because after that timeframe no docking port will be available for an LCRS vehicle. This activity is now named ALADDIN (Autonomous LEO Accelerated Demo Docking to ISS Node), to underline the fact that the primary objective is to award contracts targeting an early demonstration mission on ISS.However, in recognition of the challenges associated with this target launch date, the ALADDIN Invitation to Tender will give bidders the possibility to submit proposal(s) for:- a demonstration mission to the ISS by mid-2029, and/or- a demonstration mission to a future Commercial LEO Destination (CLD) by the end of 2031.Given that no specific details about the CLDs are available at this time, bidders selecting the second scope will be asked to base their proposals on the ISS requirements. The ALADDIN contractual phasing through slices is foreseen as follows:Slice I, from October 2026 up to and including Q4/2028.Slice II, from Q1/2029 up to and including the demonstration mission.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF SOUNDING ROCKETS BATCH 1 IN E3P PERIOD 4
description: Considering the scientific priorities for Sounding Rocket Experiments, five experiments selected by ESA through the Exploration Science Announcement of Opportunity (AO-2025-SR) for Sounding Rocket experiments for space- or microgravity-relevant research, are proposed for implementation and launch in 2027 and 2028.The following five experiments are proposed for implementation: CHIP-II: Charges in Planet Formation II;. Re-flight of the CHIP module.LifeACTImm: Unravelling immune cell dysfunction in Space and test of newcountermeasures. Re-flight of the micACTin module with new inserts and additional optical diagnostic.P-REX: Purified Regolith Extracted Volatiles. New module.FERMISE: Fire Experiments and Risk Mitigation for Space Exploration. New module based on the DLR TOPOFLAME module.LAMDA-g: Laser metal wire deposition in absence of gravity; new module.The current proposal covers the Development, Assembly, Integration and Testing (Phase C/D) for the acceptance of the modules listed above. The modules shall include all the specific experiment inserts (where applicable), shall be fully qualified and ready for flight on a Sounding Rocket with a microgravity time of no less than 6 minutes. The proposed activity also includes all the operational tasks of a typical Sounding Rocket launch campaign, namely: module verification, launch and flight operations, module recovery, data distribution, disassembly and return of any specific experiment samples, if applicable (Phase E/F).The overall industrial work is planned to be completed within 36 months, withlaunches of the experiments in 2027 and 2028.

title: T716-900SM DEMISABILITY OF CRITICAL COMPONENTS OF OPTICAL COMMUNICATION TERMINALS IN LEO (EXPRO+)
description: In recent decades, the amount of space debris has increased substantially, making it a critical issue for the space community. To mitigate the risks from debris proliferation and the surge in launch traffic, state-of-the-art regulations are evolving. For instance, under the ESA Space Debris Mitigation (SDM) Requirements (ESSB-ST-U-007 Issue 1, Nov. 2023), a re-entering spacecraft must not pose an on-ground casualty risk exceeding 10^-4. Consequently, at end-of-life, satellites must either perform a controlled reentry, which incurs enormous system-level impacts, or fully demise upon reentry. To achieve the "Zero Debris 2030" goal, it is crucial to ensure the demisability of all LEO satellite equipment. Optical communication terminals are being adopted on many LEO spacecraft as a solution for efficient data transmission, especially in the case of constellations that require high-speed data transfer capabilities.The demise behaviour of optical communication terminals has not been characterized yet and several areas of concerns have been preliminary identified, particularly regarding the presence of optical elements and their related supporting structures. Therefore, the systematic investigation of the demise behavior in terms of critical parts, fragmentation and identification of solutions to enhancedemisability of optical communication terminal is considered of high priority for the uncontrolled re-entry LEO platforms.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: HARMONY MULTISTATIC SAR CALIBRATION TRANSPONDER
description: Procurement of three Calibration Transponders to be used for the Harmony Mission external calibration, characterisation and verification during In-Orbit Commissioning and throughout mission operational phase.This Harmony Multistatic SAR calibration transponder activity will include, as deliverables, a set of calibration transponders, comprising of 2 fixed units, 1 portable unit as minimum. This hardware consists of specialized ground-based radar targets used for precise, autonomous calibration and quality checks of the full Harmony Synthetic Aperture Radar system. They provide a stable and remotely-controlled backscatter to ensure the accurate radiometric, spectral and geometric performance for Harmony applications. These transponders will need to be located strategically and enable continuous monitoring by receiving Sentinel-1 signal, processing and amplifying its signal and transmitting it back to both Harmony satellites in both an along-track and across-track possible configurations.The work shall be performed in line with the HarmonyMission development schedule and in particular with the planned mission launch in 2029.

title: T705-901SM DEVELOPMENT OF DEMISABLE STAR TRACKERS (EXPRO+)
description: In recent decades, the amount of space debris has increased substantially, making it a critical issue for the space community. To mitigate the risks from debris proliferation and the surge in launch traffic, state-of-the-art regulations are evolving. For instance, under the ESA Space Debris Mitigation (SDM) requirements (ESSB-ST-U-007 Issue 1, Nov. 2023), a re-entering spacecraft must not pose an on-ground casualty risk exceeding 10^-4. Consequently, at end-of-life, satellites must either perform a controlled reentry, which incurs enormous system-level impacts, or fully demise upon reentry. To achieve the "Zero Debris 2030" goal, it is crucial to ensure the demisability of all LEO satellite equipment. Star trackers (STR) are essential components for spacecraft in LEO, yet some uncertainties persist about their demise behaviour. With numerous STR variants available from European suppliers, investigating their configuration-specific demisability has become a high priority for both large and small LEO platforms facing uncontrolled re-entry. In a STR, the use of titanium in the optical barrel is driven by performance (matching the coefficient of thermal expansion of the lenses), and for some missions, moving to aluminum cannot be envisaged. Previous TDE activity, T826-701SY Platform Optics and Electronic Equipment Demise, revealed that in fully integrated STR units, the titanium barrel housing the lenses are most likely to survive reentry. While STRs once featured optical heads weighting around 3kg, newer designs, especially for satellite constellations, now incorporate much lighter sensors (300 - 400grams). As a result, the mass of titanium (or even in some case aluminium) is also reduced in this equipment, reducing or possibly eliminating the material surviving reentry. In tandem with emerging configurations, comprehensive characterization of STR demise behaviour is needed. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Characterize the demise behaviour of various STR configurations (from constellation grade to high-end class Alpha ESA missions). - Identify design improvements to enhance demisability. - Perform optimized CAD designs, breadboard manufacturing and functional tests. - Develop a follow-up qualification plan.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: T711-900SM CHARACTERIZATION AND GUIDELINES FOR FUTURE ELECTRONICS (EXPRO+)
description: In recent decades, space debris has surged to become a critical issue for the space community. To mitigate associated risks from debris proliferation and increasing launch traffic, regulations are evolving. For example, the ESA Space Debris Mitigation (SDM) Requirements (ESSB-ST-U-007 Issue 1, Nov. 2023) mandate that a re-entering spacecraft must not present an on-ground casualty risk higher than 10^-4. Consequently, at endof-life, satellites are required either to perform a controlled reentrydespite its significant system-level impactor to fully demise during reentry. The "Zero Debris 2030" goal hinges on the ability of LEO satellites to safely demise upon reentry. Since electronic cards account for a significant portion of a satellite's mass on both large and small platforms, assessing their demisability is paramount. Their behaviour during reentry is a high-priority investigation area for uncontrolled re-entry scenarios. Electronic cards widely use Glass Fiber Reinforced Plastic (GFRP).Previous TDE testing activities, T826-701SY "Platform optics and electronic equipment demise", have revealed that GFRP exhibits complex demisability behavior. Although the demise of GFRP is mainly limited by the viscosity of its glass fibers, the material visibly weakens and deforms under high temperatures, indicating that aerodynamic forces might indeed break it up. Thus, characterizing the mechanical effects induced by these forces is essential to accurately assess the criticality of GFRP in reentry conditions. In addition, deriving guidelines for the Printed Circuit Board (PCB) design in terms of size and fragmentation enhancing demisability performance is deemed necessary. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Develop suitable test samples and a test configuration to characterize the demise behaviour of electronic cards made with GFRP, considering both mechanical loads and heat flux.- Execute static chamber tests along with predictive modelling.- Formulate comprehensive guidelines to enhance the demisability of electronic cards.
