title: IMPROVED TTC SUB-SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE - EXPRO PLUS
description: To consolidate alternative solutions for on-board loss minimization. To develop the prototypes of the most relevant solutions identified, to confirm the predicted performance. To provide road-map to flight models. The state of art TTC Sub-System architectures for Science and Exploration missions are nowadays quite complex. In order to allow communications during all mission phases, several antennas are needed in combination with redundant High Power Amplifiers (HPA) and transponders (DST). The interconnection among these components is accomplished by the RF Distribution Unit (RFDU), which has to guarantee the maximum degree of reconfigurability and reliability to failures. In addition, it has also to implement the necessary filtering action, to allow full duplex communications. Its design is therefore quite complex encompassing the use of several switches, Diplexers, Filters and interconnecting waveguides (WG) runs. The latter can be quite long as they have to reach antennas which are typically far from the location of the rest of the TTC subsystem. All this results in high losses with RF power reduction in transmission and increased noise figure in reception.The design solutions used so far in the frame of ESA projects are quite recurrent with no major improvements in the last decades. As shown in a TTC Sub-System architecture survey carried out in 2017, different approaches exist, as identified for example by other agencies and already flown successfully in the past years. For a complex RFDU as used in Deep Space missions, we can consider RF path losses in the order of 1 to 3 dB in X-band and 3 to 4 dB in Ka-band, with significant impacts in terms of data return (up to50% reduction) and in terms of spacecraft recovery possibilities in case of anomalies (increasedoperations complexity and limitation on maximum achievable distance). Therefore, there is a clear need for loss reduction in the RFDU paths, through the implementation of novel solutions. A study is on-going to consolidate the possible alternative subsystem Architectures, and define relevant requirements. This will be completed in early 2024, but its conclusions need to be consolidated by experimental results. The activity shall focus on the specification, detailed design, development and tests of prototypes of the components which will have the most significant impact on the TTC subsystem performance and whose feasibility has to be demonstrated. Three main items have been already identified, which may need to be completed by additional technologies as an outcome of the on-going study:- Receiving only antenna with integrated low-noise-amplifier (LNA) and downconverter (D/C), with a possible alternative for a receiving and transmitting solution;- High-gain-antenna dual-band feed including receiving LNA and D/C, and with direct interface to power amplifier;- Transponder front-end to manage the interfaces with new antennas designs.Tasks:1. Consolidation of requirements and design2. Design and manufacturing of bread-boards3. Testing of bread-boards4. Development plan for flight models.

title: MARITIME LASER COMMUNICATION TERMINAL ENABLING OPTICAL LINKS WITH SPACE (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.012) - ON REQUEST
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a maritime laser communication terminal prototype to enable optical communication links between aship-based and a space-based laser terminals.TargetedImprovements:Enhance the reliability and stability of a laser communication terminal (LCT) in maritime environments for optical satellite communication. This will resultin a reliable and resilient system for bidirectional ship-space links.Description: While Laser Communication Terminals (LCTs) are being explored for aeronautical and land-mobile sectors, their use in maritime-satellite link applicationsremains untapped. Maritime LaserCommunication Terminal (MLCT) systems offer significant advantages, including secure communications (resilienceto jamming and low probability of interception), high data rates, direct line-of-sight links, which can enhance connectivity for ships but are not available yetin ESA Member States or Canada.This activity will develop and test MLCT prototype for maritime communication applications. It will assess the state-of-the-art for maritime LCTs andevaluate the constraints imposed by dynamic maritime environments, such as sea waves. Following this analysis, existing Pointing, Acquisition, andTracking (PAT) mechanisms, optical head mechanical designand optical communication systems will be benchmarked, and one will be selected andoptimised for effective performance in maritimeconditions. A prototype MLCT will be developed with Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP) specifications closeto a final product, ensuring compatibility with current and future planned space LCTs. The MLCT shall be designed for manufacturability at a competitivecommercial cost. The possibility of a test to be conducted with a satellite LCT should be explored

title: ADVANCED SUB-THZ PACKAGING TECHNOLOGIES - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop a 664 GHz direct detection receiver using innovative packaging techniques for future ultra-compact array instruments.Description: Future array instruments and ultra-compact payload instruments require ultra-compact receiver integrating all RF (Radio Frequency) functions with very small SWaP (Size, Weight and Power), removing complex mechanical and electrical interfaces such as standard waveguide flanges and DC/IF (Direct Current/Intermediate Frequency) coaxial connectors. Novel silicon micromachining techniques are key-enablers to develop ultra-compact RF front-end by integrating in a High-Aspect-Ratio silicon-wafer stack all the key components required to achieve state-of-the-art performance, including high-gain antenna, RF LNA MMIC (Microwave Monolithically Integrated Circuit), RF filters, diode detector, video amplifier and associated DC electronics.This activity aims to develop an integrated 664 GHz Direct Detection Receiver, including a novel high-gain flat-antenna, RF LNA MMIC, a narrow-bandpass filter, and a zero-bias detector with integrated video-amplifier. The developed receiver will be tested radiometrically, including beam pattern measurement, Noise Figure, Short-Term-Gain-Stability, and Gain response over temperature. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Design of an integrated direct detection receiver operating at 664 GHz. - Investigation ofsilicon-micromachined fabrication and packaging techniques for all critical RF elements: flat-antenna, waveguide active (LNA) and passive (filter) devices, RF/IF/DC interconnections. - Manufacturing and testing of a breadboard model. - Development plan and future roadmap.

title: T311-900SD DEBRIS ENVIRONMENT MODELLING IN CIS-LUNAR SPACE (EXPRO+)
description: Description: Currently, debris environment models for cislunar space are very limited as such have been primarily developed for Earth-bound orbits. Such models are a necessary asset for collision/impact risk assessment and traffic coordination. With the expansion of human activities beyond Earth, notably in cislunar space, there is an increasing need for models and tools to support missions. This need is reflected on the latest Space Debris Mitigation requirements for lunar orbits, including disposal and availability of space traffic coordination methods. With various studies having explored disposed objects and debris clouds in cislunar space, the development of such models becomes increasingly feasible. Methods and software tools to perform assessments in Earth orbits exist and are well-used. To ensure safe operations and sustainability in cislunar space, an extended density-based model can be used for risk event statistics, delta-v planning for collision avoidance manoeuvres and reliability assessment due to impacts. The model shall leverage the results of recent studies on debris and clouds around the Moon and build upon the well-established tools andmethodologies for Earth orbits. For the dynamically complex lunar orbits, a long-term propagator is needed to support the characterisation and evolution of the population. Under this activity, cislunar long-term propagators are aimed to be coupled with break-up, lunar impact, and traffic models to create a consistent debris and dust density map for the cislunar environment. To demonstrate the usability and mission application, the model shall be coupled with collision and impact risk assessment tool and tested on a Lunar mission design.

With the expansion of human activities beyond Earth, notably in cislunar space, there is an increasing need for models and tools to support missions. This need is reflected on the latest Space Debris Mitigation requirements for lunar orbits, including disposal and availability of space traffic coordination methods. With various studies having explored disposed objects and debris clouds in cislunar space, the development of such models becomes increasingly feasible. Methods and software tools to perform assessments in Earth orbits exist and are well-used. To ensure safe operations and sustainability in cislunar space, an extended density-based model can be used for risk event statistics, delta-v planning for collision avoidance manoeuvres and reliability assessment due to impacts. The model shall leverage the results of recent studies on debris and clouds around the Moon and build upon the well-established tools andmethodologies for Earth orbits. For the dynamically complex lunar orbits, a long-term propagator is needed to support the characterisation and evolution of the population. Under this activity, cislunar long-term propagators are aimed to be coupled with break-up, lunar impact, and traffic models to create a consistent debris and dust density map for the cislunar environment. To demonstrate the usability and mission application, the model shall be coupled with collision and impact risk assessment tool and tested on a Lunar mission design.

title: LUNAR EUROPEAN POWER PACKS: SYSTEM-LEVEL CONCEPT STUDY (E3CX-033) - EXPRO PLUS
description: This Lunar European Power Pack aims to accelerate the maturation of European thermal control and power systems as well as related electronics equipment enabling lunar night survival and lunar night operations in the frame of the ESA lunar roadmap. The output of the Lunar European Power Pack will be a European lunar end-to-end integrated advanced power pack validated design providing thermal control and power as a service to surface Payloads if integrated in the relevant mission's baseline. To enable sustained surface operations on the Moon, robust and autonomous power and thermal services are essential. These systems must be able to support a range of external clients including systems and payloads hosted on landers, rovers, surface shelters, or deployed payloads under harsh lunar conditions, from mid-latitudes to polar regions, ranging from daytime to night survival. The goal is therefore to deliver reliable energy and thermal regulation as a modular service, adaptable to multiple mission profiles and operational needs. Ensuring an efficient service/mass ratio is vital for the affordability and is therefore central to any activity.

title: HYDRON UPGRADE KIT: ESTOL-COMPLIANT PORTABLE MODEM UPGRADE KIT FOR OPTICAL GROUND STATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.091) EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop a portable modem that can be easily integrated in an existing optical ground station to make it compatible with ESTOL specificationsTargeted Improvements:Increased interoperability between existing optical ground stations and future satellite systems (e.g., HydRON).Description:There are a number of existing or planned optical ground stations (OGSs) that are currently used for scientific missions or to demonstrate quantum technologies. Those OGSs are not compliant to the ESA Specifications for Terabit/s Optical Links (ESTOL). To maximise the benefit of early Member State investments, the activity shall develop an upgrade kit" for multiple existing OGS infrastructures. An easy-to-integrate modem will facilitate the upgrade of such existing or planned OGSsand increase their interoperability with future commercial and institutional systems that will adopt ESTOL and its evolutions.Thisactivity shall develop a portable breadboard for an ESTOL-compliant modem. In the scope of the activity, it shall be assumed that thetarget existing OGSs have already been developed in terms of optical elements (e.g., aperture, adaptive optics, etc.) in order tobecompatible with ESTOL. The portable modem shall be connected to the optical part of the OGS by optical fibre, and it shall implement both transmit and receive functionalities. The modem breadboard shall come with a GUI and an interface control document to facilitate its fast and easy integration and use. The functionalities of the portable modem shall be validated in the Contractor's laboratory and in an existing selected OGS.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: NEW COMPOSITION OF GREEN HYPERGOLIC BIPROPELLANTS FOR ENGINE SHORT PULSE MODE FIRING EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesTo define a fast response green hypergolic bipropellant to be used in a new thruster capable to deliver short pulse modefiring.DescriptionCurrent hypergolic bi-propellants might be included in the candidate List for Substances of Very High Concern inaccordance to REACH (Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals) regulation limiting the use of those materials. Therefore, early development tests shall be pushed forward to improve pulse mode firing in comparison to state-of-the art. In addition, due to the toxicity of standard storable propellant and the costly associated infrastructure, new propellant shall be "green".This activity aims at developing a green propellant combination that spontaneously ignite when theycome into contact. To test this propellant, a new engine thruster breadboard shall be designed andmanufactured. The engine design shall be optimized together with the chosen propellant combination for pulse mode performance demonstration (firing <100ms).This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Trade-off justification for the green oxidizer selection- Fuel blends preparation- Qualitative drop tests- Long term stability test- Measurement of the ignition delay time (e.g. fast speed camera)- Engine Breadboard Design, Manufacturing testing (including vacuum ignition verificationand hot fire testing.

title: ERS-EO IOD-C - REDUCED INFORMATION AGE (I.E. DATA LATENCY FROM ACQUISITION TO PRODUCT DELIVERY)
description: In order to de-risk and accelerate the implementation phase of EOGS, the IOD/IOV activities will focus on short-term achievements delivered through targeted in-orbit experiments. These experiments are intended to provide early proof of concept and in-orbit validation, with demonstrable results available ahead of the next Ministerial Conference in 2028.The scope and objectives of the IOD/IOV activities are aimed at strengthening European autonomy, including enhancing the industrialisation of solutions already under development, and supporting pre-operational validation and technology demonstration.The technologies to be developed for EOGS space missions will be selected in consultation with the European Commission and Participating States, and in accordance with the main findingsof the EOGS studies. The technologies which are being considered are:- Secure inter-satellite links and IRIS interoperability;- Data management, on-board processing and dynamic satellite tasking to reduce latency;- Enhanced security features demonstrating resilience to the considered threats;- Serialisation and synergies (re-use) across the ERS fleet;- Increased agility and imaging capacity over crisis area;- Low-cost high-performance SAR and optical payloads with extended imaging capabilities; and- Platforms optimised for batch launches on European launchers and compatible with applicable clean space policies.Drawing on these findings, together with further consultation with industry through the Request for Information (RFI) released in July 2025 which received a substantial number of responses four main themes have been identified for the IOD/IOV activities.The In-Orbit Demonstration/Validation(IOD/IOV) activities are therefore organised into the following four themes:A. IOD-A: Low Luminance / Night VisionB. IOD-B: DynamicSatellite TaskingC. IOD-C: Reduced information age (i.e. data latency from acquisition to product delivery)D. IOD-D: Satellite Super AgilityThese correspond to areas where a further consolidation is needed (hence the relevance of conducting an IOD) before a feature of very high interest and relevance to the ERS-EO programme objective could be declared operational and included in the nominal configuration of the system.

title: 1 GBIT/S THROUGHPUT CPU-BASED DVB-S2/S2X SOFTWARE DEFINED RADIO (ARTES AT 7A.088) - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop and test a 1 Gbit/s DVB-S2/S2X demodulator and 500 Mbit/s multi-frequency TDMA modulator on a high performance x86, ARM, or similar CPU based Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) platforms.Targeted Improvements: 10-fold data rate increase compared to existing full DVB standards-compliant software defined radio implementations.Description: Current software-defined modems have demonstrated throughputs of around 100 Mbit/s, with some claims of significantlyhigher performance using specialised hardware and limiting the demodulator to one modcod only. Conversely, a high-performance modemrunning on a generic CPU platform opens up the possibility to deploy field-upgradable modems on server hardware for professional and governmental applications.This activity will study the implementation of DVB-S2 and S2X compliant demodulation algorithms as well as DVB-RCS2 MF-TDMA compliant modulation algorithms on high performance x86, ARM, or similar CPU based Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) platforms. A CPU-based software-defined radio with a throughput of 1 Gbit/s in DVB-S2X and 500 Mbit/s in MF-TDMA will be designedand developed. The software-defined radio will be tested in a relevant environment using a hardware modulator and burst demodulator, or dedicated test equipment.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. title: LOW POWER KA-BAND DIRECT CONVERSION RECEIVER MODULE (ARTES AT 5C.525) - EXPRO+ (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: The objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a 12bit direct conversion receiver module covering the full Ka-band with significant reduced power consumption in comparison to current state of the art.Targeted Improvements:- Enabling a European source of low power direct conversion Ka-band receivers.- Factor 5 reduction of power consumption compared to the State of the Art.Description: Today's flexible telecommunication satellites require receivers operating at higher frequencies and over a wider bandwidth than in the past, with a complex RF chain and lossyharnesses. A trend towards highly integrated solutions using direct sampling receivers compatible with Software Defined Radios (SDRs) is one solution, but the power consumption of these direct sampling architectures can be prohibitive for some applications. The available direct conversion receivers in Ku-band and Ka-band have power consumption figuresin excess of several Watts and limited conversion accuracy, constraining the application areas where these could be used for space telecommunication applications. A direct conversion receiver system in a single package integrating the Analog to Digital Converter (ADC) in the advanced semiconductor technology and using a time-interleaved ADCarchitecture can achieve the desired lower power consumption and higher conversion accuracy.This activity will develop a prototype wideband ADC with high-speed track-and-hold circuit, implemented as a System-in-Package (SiP) RF to digital front-end module including digital processing features, operating in upper Ka-band. Available State-of-the-Art low-power wideband ADC will be assessed, and a trade-off analysisperformed to determine the optimum RF chain architecture (including the track-and-hold with digital processing engine and high-speed interfaces) suitable for wideband SDRs operating in full Ka-bandapplications. The breadboard will be designed to meet key performance requirements in terms of power consumption (<500mW per channel), bandwidth, and input frequency. The noise and linearity performance shall be measured to determine suitability for a range of SDR scenarios also considering synchronisation and clock jitter requirements. The breadboard shall be tested in a representative RF chain architecture in a laboratory environment, to demonstrate direct sampling at upper Ka-band frequencies and assess viability for V/W band applications. Additionally, radiation tolerance shall be demonstrated by analysis to assess suitability of the low-power ADC for future applications in space.

title: LARGE INPUT VOLTAGE RANGE GAN BDR FOR PRIMARY BATTERIES EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesExplore topologies based on GaN switches and digital control to discharge primarybatteries down the minimum possible voltage.The objective is to maximise the use of the energy in primary batteries.Build a breadboard with the most promising option and test its performance.DescriptionPrimary batteries have very high energy density but they cannot be recharged. Thus, itsmain use is for one-time use cases, for instance, landers or launchers.Typically a lander will not have any solar array so its only energysource is a battery. Sincethey will not be recharged, primary batteries make total sense.To extract the maximum amount of energy,the battery voltage will go down as the currentis taken out. The lower you go in voltage, the more energy you extract.However, decreasing the voltage has serious implications for the power system. In general,DC/DC converters operate at high efficiency levels in a narrow input voltage range.Moreover, the topologies will limit the maximum and minimum input voltage, which meansthat, in mostcases, the DC/DC converter used to discharge the battery will limit theoperation and the performance.This activity aims at exploring DC/DC converter topologies that can operate through largeinput voltage ranges with high performance. Efficiency is also very important in landerapplications since it is paramount to waste as little energy as possible.There are topologies that can operate through larger ranges that have not been used inspace applications so far and can be adopted easily. Moreover, new GaN switchesimprove the efficiency of the system and, if controlled by means of digital devices, complexenergy management systems can be built. Thus, multiple stages could be connected insuch a way that the optimum operation point is always at reach.The activity aims at building a breadboard of a high efficiency, high input voltage rangeDC/DC converter with GaN switches and digital control. The breadboard will be tested toverify the performance.

title: FIRST! SIMULATION AND INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGIES FOR SPACE TRANSPORTATION - EXPRO+
description: This FIRST! activity aims to de-risk disruptive technologies related to Simulation Intelligence for future space transportation in Europe, and with high commercial interest. More specifically, it aims for short-term, quick maturation of disruptive commercially interesting technologies, e.g., using intelligent software, data and emerging Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled capabilities across three categories of interest. title: NEW EARTH OBSERVATION MISSION IDEAS (NEOMI) 2ND CYCLE - EXPRO+
description: NEOMI is an ESA research initiative. At its heart is a fundamental reconnection to innovative, blue-sky Earth Observation science by empowering new Space Mission Lead Investigators who will champion future Earth Observation satellite missions. It is designed to provide a framework for shaping novel scientific ideas and creating more opportunities to potentially develop bold, state-of-the-art EO missions within ESA. The primary objectives of the NEOMI study are: (1) to mature new mission ideas from Science Readiness Level (SRL) 0 to 3, documented in the NEOMI Mission Description Documents (MDD), which is the main output of this activity; and (2) to support scientists in becoming lead investigators for future EO space missions, including training on ESA processes, tools/techniques, procurement, and related topics.

title: FUTURE EUROPEAN ARCHITECTURE FOR EO CONSTELLATIONS - EXPRO+
description: The European Earth Observation Ecosystem is a cross-cutting vision for the future of Space Earth Observation. It is a holistic system-of-system perspective leveraging across systems/missions/programmatic elements instead of only looking at individual systems or programmes. With this in mind, the objective of the intended ITT will be to explore the niches in the EO mission Ecosystem to deliver knowledge derived from measurements collected at the relevant temporal and spatial scales necessary to underpin commercial applications targeting policy related needs. The assessment shall identify relevant National, and Supranational policies for which Earth Observation data could enable policy action, the current status thereof and the respective gaps. Based on examples of policy regulations the system needs and the preliminary mission definitions for an EO Constellation architecture shall be derived. As the EO Constellations bear a great potential for commercialisation also potential business cases for a fully operational service shall be assessed.Overall the Future European Architecture for EO Constellations addressing policy needs shall be designed to be (i) driven by active user's identified requirements addressing environmental regulations (ii), quality-certified as fit-for-purpose (iii) cost and schedule constrained (iv) scalable in terms of future constellation expansion and (v) developed as a service that will be owned and operated by private entities.

title: T709-902SD COLLISION AVOIDANCE INDUCED SPACECRAFT DESIGN AND OPERATIONS PLANNER (EXPRO+)
description: The space debris environment, space traffic, and the associated operational context are very dynamic. Yet, inearly spacecraft design, the expected effort for collision avoidance during the mission and disposal phasesneeds to be estimated. Existing models allow designers and operators to estimate the fuel budget.However, those are based on general assumptions and single source space surveillance data.With the introduction of the Zero Debris approach and the proliferation of space surveillance companies, theimpact of collision avoidance operations goes beyond fuel estimation and now requires to account for, amongothers, mission time loss, requiredground support, and varying data providers.This activity aims to create a software model building on current knowledge in mission operations in the contextof collision avoidance to facilitate state-of-the-art estimates for collision avoidance efforts. Based on more than20 years of collision avoidance practices, a robust assessment framework could be created, to be used:- in early mission design (phase A/B) to assess the feasibility and impact of collision avoidance compliance ondesign and operations, and- by spacecraft operators who need more realistic planning tools for operations and manoeuvre planning.

title: ADHA GNSS RECEIVER MODULE (AGNSSRXM) - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop a GNSS Receiver module compliant with the SAVOIR reference architecture and the ADHA specifications. Description: This activity aims at developing a new generation of GNSS Receiver module compliant with ADHA functional and interface requirements able to be integrated in an ADHA Unit with its backplane based on cPCI Serial Space standard.The GNSS receiver module shall support single and/or multiple antenna inputs. The antenna inputs shall support single frequency and/or multi-frequency (e.g. E1/E5) navigation signal reception. The hardware design shall allow high quality measurements, coherent between all inputs, to support applications such as precise orbit determination (POD) and GNSS radio occultation (GNSS-RO). The hardware shall comprise all elements needed for a navigation receiver, including RF frontends, an FPGA for the digital receiver frontend, and CPU, memory and timing subsystem. Operationalflexibility and reconfigurability of the hardware platform is foreseen, i.e. FPGA and receiver s/w are foreseen to be operationally reprogrammable. The GNSS function shall provide at least pseudo range, carrier phase and Doppler measurement for each satellite tracked and position, velocity and time. Tracking of at least 24 satellites in single frequency mode and of 18 satellites in dual/triple-frequency mode shall be supported. At least dual constellation (GPS and Galileo) is required. The ADHA GNSS Receiver module functions shall include all the capabilities of a standard spaceborne GNSS receiver excluding the antenna. The GNSS receiver module shall be designed and implemented to allow a flexible approach, allowing to remove/add components without design changes to support the different configurations (e.g. single/multiple antenna, single/multi-frequency, etc). The activity shall investigate the usage of COTS as well and assess the possibility to have a common reference design allowing to use either COTS or rad-hard components. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- AGNSSRxM Detailed Specification (compatible with other ADHA module and unit specifications).- AGNSSRxM HW SW preliminary design.- AGNSSRxM HW SW detailed design.- AGNSSRxM Manufacturing Test.- AGNSSRxM Validation Test within ADHA Unit and results.

title: QUALIFICATION PERFORMANCE ENHANCEMENT OF EUROPEAN SPACE ADHESIVES FOR STRUCTURAL AND OPTICAL BONDING - EXPRO PLUS
description: Objectives:To qualify a European space adhesive, focused on structural and/or optical bonding applications, andcapable to withstand ground, launch and space environment effects.Description:Europe lacks a fully qualified space-ready adhesive for structural and optical bonding, despite the criticalrole these materials play in ensuring mission integrity across thermal, mechanical, and vacuumenvironments. Current ESA missions depend on long-established non-European systems whoseformulations and supply conditions are outside European control, creating operational and industrial risks for long-term use. Furthermore, ESA's industrial partners rely onthe extensive past heritage andvalidation of these non-European solutions, and adapting a European solution would require having dataavailable so that it can be done with confidence. This activity focuses also on validating and qualifyingexisting European adhesive candidates to demonstrate their suitability for space-relevant bonding processes. Rather than developing new formulations, the goal is to rigorously benchmark available European products, perform the necessary environmental and mechanical testing, and generatea complete qualification dataset. This will enable large system integrators and subcontractors to adopt EU-sourced adhesives with confidence, strengthening European autonomy and ensuring dependable access to mission-critical bonding materials.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of available European adhesive formulators manufacturers and products with structural andglass-to-metal applications (focused on epoxies and potentially UV-curing adhesives, but otheralternatives are possible),- Review the TRL status, the performances already available and the manufacturing capabilities andidentify the gaps with respect to non-Europeanadhesives commonly used in space- Down select three with the largest potential with a focus on applicability. Characterize, if notavailable, asminimum E/G modulus in wide range of temperatures, CTE, thermal vacuum stability and outgassingperformance- Performadequate testing to verify the suitability of the adhesive/substrate solutions to the requiredenvironments. This includes space-application thermal response (at least thermal vacuum, mechanicalloads, adhesion strength) and dimensional stability tests (permanentpolymerisation shrinkage). It shouldalso include the main common substrates for these applications.- Apply and verify the use of the adhesive in the most common space-relevant adhesive bondingprocesses.The expected outcome is an increased TRL for European adhesives, supported by a comprehensive gap analysis of their properties, and the generation of robust performance data to make them available to theEuropean industry. The ultimate objective is to have qualified-European produced adhesives available toall space system integrators categories and subcontractors, facilitating a transition from non-European to fully European space adhesives.Deliverables: Technical report, Samples of developed adhesivesApplication/Need Date: All Missions Mission Classification: alpha, beta, gamma,delta.

title: LASER BREADBOARD FOR FUTURE WATER VAPOR LIDAR
description: QLEO, a mission proposed as candidate mission in the frame of the Call for Earth Explorer 12 mission ideas, aims to provide tropospheric profiles of water vapour at the global scale with a high vertical resolution and a low bias, to close an important observational gap for climate and atmospheric research. The mission uses a spaceborne Differential Absorption LiDAR (DIAL) that enables precise measurements of atmospheric water vapor and trace gases. Following the evaluation, the Advisory Committee for Earth Observation strongly commended QLEO for its high scientific interest, while further developments need to be undertaken to mature some critical technologies. Spaceborne DIAL systems rely on advanced laser technology capable of emitting multiple wavelengths with high energy and stability, ensuring accurate detection of atmospheric gas concentrations over large scales. For DIAL-systems, these wavelengths have to be matched to characteristic absorption lines that usually do not overlap with the emission wavelength of the laser source. For QLEO wavelengths around 935 nm have been identified. Recent advancements in the field of spaceborne high energy (>400 mJ) single-frequency laser sources at 1064 nm wavelength and improvements in frequency converters based on optical-parametric oscillators make multi-wavelength systems in other spectral range more feasible for space deployment. Based on these promising results, existing laser technology concepts for frequency converters can be further enhanced to define suitable architectures for multi-pulse generation around 935 nm, and to increase the maximum achievable multipulse repetition rate. The technology developed can be used in Earth Observation LiDAR payloads with multi-wavelength laser transmitters around 935 nm but also with some modifications at different wavelengths, with the potential of improving conversion efficiency and advancing pulse overlap strategies. The objective of the activity is to enhance the maturity of critical elements and to demonstrate the overall functions and performance of the laser sub-system through the development of a dedicated breadboard with testing. The activity will cover the following key tasks: Evaluate and compare suitable architecture for conversion from 1064 nm to 935 nm wavelength. Design, build and test a representative model for the non-linear crystal mount. Design, manufacture and test a full breadboard, which includes pump source, frequency conversion and emission at multiple wavelengths around 935 nm. Assess through an analytical model the system performance and durability under various energy and environmental conditions (i.e.: radiation, Laser-Induced Damage Threshold - LIDT, etc.). Define a qualification plan for opto-mechanical packages. Prepare a development plan for an Engineering Model.The tenderer will be expected to have access to a suitable pump laser source to be used as an input signal for the frequency conversion at 935 nm.

title: PHASE 0/A SYSTEM STUDIES OF THE CRYORAD MISSION
description: CryoRad is one of the four candidate mission concepts for the twelfth Earth Explorer (EE-12), approved by PBEO at its meeting of 17April 2024 (ref. ESA/PB-EO(2024)18). CryoRad would fill an important gap in observations of the cryosphere through the direct measurement of low-frequency passive-microwave brightness temperatures using a novel broadband radiometer. From these novel measurements key parameters such as the temperature profile of ice shelves, sea-ice thickness and sea-surface salinity in cold waters can be determined to improve our understanding of key processes in the polar regions. The mission would complement the upcoming Copernicus CIMR, CRISTAL and ROSE-L missions. The procurement in subject includes the Phase 0 system studies and Phase A system studies which will be performed through a phased contract. Subject to reception of good quality proposals, it is intended to place two parallel contracts. Phase 0: the Phase 0 system study will cover all elements of the mission architecture: space segment (platforms and instruments), ground segments, operations and exploitation concepts. These studies will be based on the Agency's Statement of Work (SoW) and the Mission Assumptions and preliminary Technical Requirements (MATER). Risk retirement activities will also be identified and initiated within the frame of the study, to raise TRL of critical technologies. The expected duration of the Phase 0 system studies is 14 months from kick-off to closure of the MAR. The results of the Phase 0 will be used as input for the down selection of two EE-12 missions out of four to progress to phase A. If the mission is selected the second phase of the contract will be initiated, otherwise the contract will be terminated. Phase A: The Phase A system study will address all elements of the mission architecture, namely space segment (platform and payload), ground segment, mission operations and exploitation. The Phase A system study will be based on the Statement of Work (SoW) applicable from the beginning of the contract and the System Requirements Document (SRD) established by ESA and consolidated at the end of the phase 0. Relevant technology pre-developments will be initiated within the frame of the study, to raise TRL of critical technologies, with the aim to reach TRL 4 by the end of phase A, and with a final goal to reach TRL 5 by the end of phase B1. The expected duration of the Phase A system studies is 18 months from kick-off to final approval of all deliverables. The results of the Phase A will be used as input for the down selection of one EE-12 mission out of the remaining two to progress to phase B1. It is expected that Phase B1 will be placed as a rider to the Phase 0/A contract of the EE-12 mission selected for implementation.

Description: CryoRad is one of the four candidate mission concepts for the twelfth Earth Explorer (EE-12), approved by PBEO at its meeting of 17April 2024 (ref. ESA/PB-EO(2024)18). CryoRad would fill an important gap in observations of the cryosphere through the direct measurement of low-frequency passive-microwave brightness temperatures using a novel broadband radiometer. From these novel measurements key parameters such as the temperature profile of ice shelves, sea-ice thickness and sea-surface salinity in cold waters can be determined to improve our understanding of key processes in the polar regions. The mission would complement the upcoming Copernicus CIMR, CRISTAL and ROSE-L missions. The procurement in subject includes the Phase 0 system studies and Phase A system studies which will be performed through a phased contract. Subject to reception of good quality proposals, it is intended to place two parallel contracts. Phase 0: the Phase 0 system study will cover all elements of the mission architecture: space segment (platforms and instruments), ground segments, operations and exploitation concepts. These studies will be based on the Agency's Statement of Work (SoW) and the Mission Assumptions and preliminary Technical Requirements (MATER). Risk retirement activities will also be identified and initiated within the frame of the study, to raise TRL of critical technologies. The expected duration of the Phase 0 system studies is 14 months from kick-off to closure of the MAR. The results of the Phase 0 will be used as input for the down selection of two EE-12 missions out of four to progress to phase A. If the mission is selected the second phase of the contract will be initiated, otherwise the contract will be terminated. Phase A: The Phase A system study will address all elements of the mission architecture, namely space segment (platform and payload), ground segment, mission operations and exploitation. The Phase A system study will be based on the Statement of Work (SoW) applicable from the beginning of the contract and the System Requirements Document (SRD) established by ESA and consolidated at the end of the phase 0. Relevant technology pre-developments will be initiated within the frame of the study, to raise TRL of critical technologies, with the aim to reach TRL 4 by the end of phase A, and with a final goal to reach TRL 5 by the end of phase B1. The expected duration of the Phase A system studies is 18 months from kick-off to final approval of all deliverables. The results of the Phase A will be used as input for the down selection of one EE-12 mission out of the remaining two to progress to phase B1. It is expected that Phase B1 will be placed as a rider to the Phase 0/A contract of the EE-12 mission selected for implementation.

title: HIGH SPATIAL RESOLUTION THERMAL INFRARED DISPERSIVE SPECTROMETER
description: TIR Push-broom dispersive spectrometers have been identified as an interesting alternative solution to Fourier Transform Spectrometer (FTS) for trace gases detection as benefiting from recent progress in infrared matrix detectors and grating technologies. Such instrument concept has thus the potential to provide high spatial resolution with an overall simpler instrument layout compared to FTS, which requires complex mechanism and moving parts, metrology unit and processing, as well as having high data rate. Furthermore, the dispersive spectrometer is free of spectral and spatial mixing of information during the data acquisitions. While there is goodheritage in Europe with push-broom dispersive spectrometers, none has been developed for space applications in the mid and long wave infrared spectral range. The activity proposes therefore to study and develop a dispersive imaging spectrometer prototype to demonstrate a level of performance compatible with high resolution Thermal Infrared (TIR) imaging spectrometry. The objective of the activity is to design and prototype the TIR dispersive imaging spectrometer with the intention to demonstrate key performances and assess critical aspects such as the spectral resolution, the sensitivity to straylight, the thermal stability and radiometric performance.

title: PRE-DEVELOPMENT OF A POWER EFFICIENT LOW-CURRENT DRY NEUTRALISER FOR NEXT GENERATION GRAVITY MISSION (NGGM/MAGIC) - EXPRO+
description: In the frame of the Missions of Opportunity enabled by international cooperation, ESA and NASA have coordinated studies of gravity monitoring constellations optimised to observe mass changes and transport in the Earth system. In 2016 the report from the ESA-NASA Interagency Gravity Science Working Group defined the benefits of such a unique cooperative effort. The objective of the NGGM - Next Generation Gravity Mission (also known as MAGIC - for Mass-change and Geosciences International Constellation ) is the long-term monitoring of the temporal variations of Earth's gravity field at high resolution in time (down to 3 days) and space (100 km). NGGM/MAGIC will observe Earth mass change and reinforce services by monitoring hydrology, cryosphere, oceanography, solid Earth and climate change. This gravity mission evolution will provide continuity of science and services with respect to predecessor missions like GRACE, GOCE and GRACE Follow-On and will complement other ESA Earth Explorer programme and Copernicus missions. The aim of this activity is to design, develop, manufacture and test one power-efficient low current stand-alone dry neutraliser system at Engineering Model (EM) level that would be suitable to be used for charge compensation of ion-emission based micro-electric propulsion system for NGGM that would include FEEP thrusters and micro propulsion RIT thrusters.

title: SOLAR SYSTEM INTERNET REFERENCE FRAMES AND TIME SYSTEMS - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To study the state-of-the-art concerning time and reference systems applicable to Solar System navigation and propose a definition of Solar System time and reference systems.Description: Currently ESA is developing interoperable communication and navigation services for the Moon (through Moonlight) and Mars (through MARCONI). To increase the autonomy of space missions across the full Solar System, and thus offloading the overloaded ground stations, ESA is developing a concept for Solar System Internet. Currently, spacecraft navigating in the Solar System rely on explicit, pre-planned setup of point-to-point communication links for their navigation. Such approach, does not scale well with the large number of missions planned in the future. Such a system would combine existing (i.e., GNSS) or planned (i.e., Moonlight, MARCONI) systems and would complement this with dedicated SSI nodes. These nodes would provide ranging capabilities through point-to-point links (as broadcast links are not scalable over long distances). As all spacecraft and SSI nodes are connected (through the Solar System Internet), raw data could be shared, through the decentralized network,enabling more advanced positioning techniques such as collaborative positioning. To achieve this goal, the definition of accurate timescale and reference systems, similar to GNSS or Moonlight, is crucial. The objective of this activity is to study the state-of-the-art concerning time and reference systems applicable to Solar System navigation, assess the gaps and suitability. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Analyse the state-of-the-art of existing Barycentric/planetary reference frames and timescales and the accuracy/availability of transformations between them (e.g., Mars planetocentric to Barycentric) - Investigate how the realizationof existing Barycentric/planetary reference frames can be improved using SSI PNT nodes, pre-selecting the most promising approaches. - Investigate the impact of relativity on Solar System PNT and assess the need for the definition of one (or more) Solar System timescale(s) and the relationship between them, pre-selecting the most promising approaches. - Implement the pre-selected reference frames and timescales, for usage in a Solar System PNT system, in a software simulator, such that end-to-end PNT performance assessment que be performed for the different models and PNT system configurations. - Based on the implemented models in the software simulator, assess the performance and suitability of the pre-selected Barycentric/planetary reference frames and timescales for a Solar System PNT system. - Based on the results obtained via simulation, propose one (or more) Solar System time and reference systems. title: INTEGRATED WIDEBAND POWER AMPLIFIER FOR CONVERGED SATELLITE/TERRESTRIAL 5G COMMUNICATIONS IN FREQUENCY RANGE 2 (FR 2) (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7B.085) - EXPRO PLUS RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a wideband power amplifier (PA) prototype, supporting both Satellite and Terrestrial 5G services in FR 2.Targeted Improvements:Increasing the PA fractional bandwidth by at least 10%.Enabling converged satellite/terrestrial 5G PA supply chain.Description: Most of 5G millimetre-wave deployment scenarios, such as Enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB), are based on Time Division Duplexing (TDD) and therefore use a single frequency band of 24.25 - 27.5 GHz for both transmit and receive. However, current and next-generation High-Throughput Satellites (HTS) rely on Frequency Division Duplexing (FDD), thereby requiring separate communications channels on separate frequency bands for uplink (e.g., 27.5 to 31.0 GHz) and downlink (e.g., 17.7 to 21.2 GHz). This architectural difference between terrestrial TDD and Satellite FDD normally leads to customised designed for different applications, increasing the barrier for satellites to entryinto upcoming 5G applications. In this context, a wideband and highly integrated power amplifier would be a key component to support multiple satellite and 5G millimetre-wave applications on ground. This feature is particularly attractive in the implementation of hybrid User Terminals for 5G, where at least two transmit bands are required.This activity aims at developing a wideband power amplifier prototype, supporting both satellite and terrestrial 5G services in FR 2. A review of monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) technologies and architectures suitable for wideband operation (covering as a minimum the 24.25 - 31 GHz frequency range) will be carried out. The activity will trade off and select at least one application scenario (e.g., Connected Car, Aeronautical), considering both distributed and centralised amplification schemes. The detailed designof a power amplifier prototype and associated circuitry shall be produced, based on the selected application scenario. Finally, the prototype shall be manufactured and tested.

title: SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS FOR SATELLITE-BASED ENTANGLEMENT DISTRIBUTION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3H.011) EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to define the technical requirements and conduct a sensitivity analysis for a satellite-based entanglement distribution system supporting at least the following experiments: verification of Bell's inequality, entanglement-based QKD, coupling with quantum memories, quantum teleportation, entanglement swapping.Targeted Improvements:To define the minimum sensitivity requirements for a multi-purpose satellite payload capable of verifying, within a single mission, the feasibility of entanglement distribution from space.Description: Future quantum information networks (QIN) will require entanglement distribution between nodes to provide services to the end users. QIN, like quantumcommunication networks, also benefits from satellite links.To realise these networks preliminary steps must be implemented and tested in an operationalenvironment.This activity aims to provide an overall feasibility study for these experiments, by defining the requirements for a multi-purpose satellite payload. The payload should be able to perform, and the analysis should consider, the following experiments: verification of Bell's inequality, entanglement-based QKD, coupling with quantum memories, quantum teleportation, entanglement swapping. In addition, a feasibility of heralded entanglement, hyperentanglement and additional identified experiments should be considered. The feasibility study shall cover the end-to-end quantum and classical downlink budget analysis, comprising the source, the ground receiver and detection system efficiency, and environmental effects on the atmospheric channel.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. title: DEMISABLE ELECTRIC PROPULSION THRUSTER FOR LOW EARTH ORBIT TELECOM CONSTELLATION SATELLITES (ARTES AT 4B.186) - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design and manufacture a fully demisable electric propulsion thruster as needed for low-earth orbit (LEO) telecom constellation satellites.Testing will include on an engineering model of the demisable thruster, and it shall include vibration, performance mapping and an endurance test of significant duration to confirm the design for demisability. Part of the activity is also the assessment and test of critical thruster components for demisability.Targeted Improvements:Enabling a European source of fully demisable electric propulsion thruster for telecom constellation satellitesDescription: In the lastdecades, the amount of space debris has increased substantially, and it is now considered a critical issue by the space community. State of the art regulations and policies are evolving to consider the risks associated to the debris proliferation and increasing launch traffic (e.g. ESA has made a leap forward in the protection of the space environment by issuing a new set of Space Debris Mitigation Requirements (ESSB-ST-U-007 Issue 1).Satellites of large LEO constellations are being requested to become fully demisable under these new requirements. Electric Propulsion (EP) thrusters are the preferred technology for European and non-European LEO telecom constellation satellites to perform orbit insertion, orbit changes, orbit maintenance, repositioning, collision avoidance and deorbiting at end of life. However, large uncertainties remain on the demisability of these thrusters due to the materials used (e.g. high melting temperature materials likeceramics and graphite) and lack of experimental data.This activity will in a first step characterise the demise behaviour of an electric propulsion thruster planned to be used in future LEO telecommunication constellations satellites.The experimental data will be used to correlate and improve the modelling accuracy of the fragmentation process and demiseof critical thruster components during re-entry.The activity will carry out an assessment and revision of all materials, parts andcomponents used in electric propulsion thrusters and develop alternative solutions to make the thruster 100% demisable. Dedicated plasma wind tunnel testing at material/part level shall be conducted for critical thruster components. An electric propulsion thrusters shall be designed with the goal to achieve full ablation during re-entry while retaining suitable performance for their mission application. An Engineering Model of the demisable thruster shall be manufactured and tested to evaluate performance. Testing shall include vibration, performance mapping and an endurance test of significant duration toconfirm non detrimental effects of the demisability.

title: CIMR COMPANION (OR CIMR-C) MISSION DEFINITION SCIENCE STUDY - EXPRO PLUS
description: Science Study (pre-Phase 0) to explore potential mission concept for a companion satellite to CIMR the context of the exploration step for a potential Mission of Opportunity. A Mission of Opportunity (MoO) is defined as an Earth Observation Research Mission in cooperation with a Space Agency outside ESA Member/Cooperating/Associated States.The Turbulent fluxes between the ocean and atmosphere are fundamental to understanding and quantifying the exchange of heat, moisture, momentum and gas between the ocean and the atmosphere. They directly impact atmospheric and oceanic variability, thereby modifying weather and climate, including precipitation patterns, terrestrial water availability, floods and droughts, and extreme events such as terrestrial and marine heatwaves.A key challenge to address is the fact that satellite-derived estimates of ocean-atmosphere fluxes are derived from multi-mission satellite data that are not co-located or contemporaneous in space and time leading to large sampling errors and uncertainties. Today, there is no satellite system designed to measure ocean fluxes from space.The Copernicus Imaging Microwave Radiometer (CIMR) is planned for launch in 2029 and will provide measurements of sea ice parameters sea surface temperature, ocean vector winds and salinity, basedon 1.4, 6.9, 10.65, 18.9 and 36.5GHz channels over a 1900 km swath. Since this mission uses a mesh reflector, it cannot include frequencies above Ka-band effectively ruling out lower troposphere air temperature and humidity sounding channels that are required tocompute collocated and contemporaneous ocean and atmosphere flux estimates.The CIMR companion mission concept definition science study will investigate and analyse different scientific solutions for a small-medium class CIMR-Companion mission that would providehigher frequency (e.g. 50-184GHz) channel capability. Together with the CIMR mission, these data would be used to retrieve lower troposphere air temperature and humidity profiles and supporting measurements to study:How do spatial variations in fluxes modify heat, gas (CO2), moisture and momentum transfer between ocean and atmosphereHow do they influence upper ocean and lower atmosphere characteristics?How do variations in fluxes impact evolution of storms, from polar lows to tropical cyclones, and upper ocean mesoscale structure evolution?How will our Earth system respond to changes in air-sea interaction in terms of global ocean turbulent heat and moisture flux contributions to the water cycle?This study will run in parallel and interact with the CIMR Companion Mission Concept Study, subject of a parallel ITT.The study will focus on sharpening the mission concept objectives and assess a first set of mission concept requirements. It will substantiate the scientific background and further consolidate the products requirements. Finally, the results of this study, along with those from the parallel system study, will be compiled into a comprehensive dossier that can be used to assess mission feasibility and potential implementation.

title: OPSTAR PHASES B2/C/D/E/F
description: The Optical Synchronized Time and Ranging (OpSTAR) In-Orbit Demonstrator (IoD) is one of the projects approved at CM25 under Component 3: Future PNT Demonstrators of the FutureNAV programme (hereafter referred to as "OpSTAR"). OpSTAR aims to validate the use of intersatellite optical links for Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT)a breakthrough technology poised to transform PNT systems as we know them today. While optical links are already well established in the field of satellite communications (SatCom), their application in PNT has yet to be demonstrated.OpSTAR will be implemented in two contractual phases, following a procurement conductedthrough an open Invitation to Tender (ITT) and financial contributions distributed between CM25 and CM28. Phase 1 focusing on detailed design, development of critical subsystems, final implementation, completion of development and system qualification up to System QAR (Phase B2/C/D) Phase 2 focusing on launch and exploitation (Phase E/F)OpSTAR is a necessary step before a potential future operational introduction of optical technology within Europe's Satellite Navigation infrastructure.The primary objectives ofOpSTAR are to:Qualify timing and ranging technology based on optical links (Space to Space and Space to Ground).Standardization/Interoperability of optical technology for timing, ranging and communication.Validate the resilience and autonomy expected improvements at system level.Validate improvements of performance at user and service level.Validate feasibility of new system concepts relying on optical technology.The OpSTAR activities will allow to:Design and develop the IoD infrastructure, including:oTwo satellites equipped with optical and L-Band navigation payloads.oThe associated ground segment, including an optical testbed composed of Optical Ground Stations (OGS) and synchronisation and processing facilities;oOptical test user range facilities to demonstrate user-level benefits.Launch and operate the satellites.Perform the in-orbit demonstration activities, including test user segment in-the-loop. Extrapolate the IOD results onto the full system architecture in order to draw lessons learned and recommendations for the adoption of intersatellite optical links potentially into an operational system

title: SENTINEL-6 NEXT GENERATION PHASE A-B1
description: The Sentinel 6 Next Generation (Sentinel 6 NG) mission is being initiated to ensure continued provision of Global Mean Sea Level (GMSL) observations and associated Copernicus data products, in alignment withthe Copernicus Space Component Long Term Scenario jointly defined by ESA, EUMETSAT, and the European Commission.Building on the performance and heritage of the Sentinel 6 Michael Freilichand Sentinel 6B satellites launched in 2020 and 2025, respectively, the Sentinel 6 NG mission will extend the long term reference altimetry record established through TOPEX/Poseidon and the Jason series. It will maintain, and aim to improve, the high precision sea level measurement stability required by Global Climate Observing System (GCOS) and continue to serve as the reference mission for calibration across the global altimetry constellation, as defined by Committee on Earth Observation Satellites (CEOS).As the procurement of a third first generation satellite (Sentinel 6C) has not been authorised, Sentinel 6 NG becomes essential to preventing a measurement gap and enabling performance improvements where feasible.The Sentinel 6 NG procurement foresees a structured two phase system study (Phase A and Phase B1) to mature the mission architecture and critical technologies. ESA intends to place two parallel contracts, subject to receipt of high quality proposals, to ensure adequatetechnical depth and to maintain competitive tension. Thesestudies will cover system-level assessment of the full mission architecture, including platform, payload, ground segment, operations, and exploitation. There will be a strong emphasis for re-use of payload instruments and sub-systems where possible, and use of the common platform whilst adopting new requirements on eco-design, security and space debris in-line with elements of the EU Space Act expected to be imposed on the Agency in due course.The procurement approach also allows for early technology pre development activities, targeting TRL 4 by the end of Phase A and TRL 5 by the end of Phase B1, to ensure mission readiness and reduce downstream development risk.The Phase A is planned to run for approximately 10 months, concluding with a Preliminary Requirements Review (PRR). Phase B1 will follow for six months, concluding with the Intermediate System Requirements Review (ISRR). The outcome of these reviews will inform the decision to proceed to Phase B2/C/D/E1 after the ESA Council at Ministerial Level (CMIN 28).

title: EDAP - EARTHNET DATA ASSESSMENT PROJECT
description: The Earthnet Programme provides the framework for "integrating" non-ESA missions (Third Party Missions) in the overall ESA Earth Observation (EO) strategy, allowing data access and supporting the development of new research and applications. Earthnet has continuously integrated over the last years an increasing number of TPMs, at a constant level of funding: in the current Earthnet Phase, data from 28 missions with 56 individual satellites (historic and operational missions) have been maintained, transferred where relevant to LTDP and made available to users. 50% of those missions are of European origin, the other 50% are international, mainly from Canada, US, Japan, India, South Korea.In the recent years, the Earth Observation capacity from space is growing extremely quick withthe multiplication of national, private, or Agencies missions; in particular the domain of high-resolution optical sensors and SAR (synthetic Aperture Radar) is exploding. The "New Space players" are now playing a central role in the EO international strategy. The global space panorama and the EO sector in particular have evolved into a highly dynamic and competitive environment. Some of these new missions are potential candidates for TPM or for Contributing Missions.As EO system architect in Europe, ESA needs to assessthe quality and the suitability of these missions. Also, this involvement in quality assessment would allow establishing a dialog with the mission provider in order to improve the overall coherence of the EO system and interoperability. This is in line with the objective of the Earthnet Programme: "Earthnet will continue to foster the cooperation with other Space Agencies and mission operators to provide data access to all active and already approved TPMs being implemented right now and for which agreements for the futureare being anticipated". In particular, the aspect related to data quality in general (e.g. data content assessment, calibration, validation, characterisation), following QA4EO guidelines, being a major component of the system, must be taken under high consideration. In addition, there is a growing need for Earthnet to strengthen the European capacity in assessing EO data quality in a multi-mission environment. This horizontal core role of Earthnet will be essential to allow interoperability across missions to foster synergies, to build Cal/Val capacity and knowledge in the TPMs and to facilitate both novel and evolution of existing applications.Inthis context, this activity aims at providing a cluster of expertise in various domains in order to perform quality assessment and the related capacity building in TPM framework especially for future missions. The domains of expertise cover Optical Sensor, SAR sensors and Atmospheric missions. The cluster of expertise will have to provide technical reports on data quality from various missions. Some missions are already identified; some other missions will be identified in the course of the project. In addition, specific studies related to data quality applicable to across missions will be asked.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF AN ELECTRIC THRUSTER OPTIMISED FOR SATURN TRANSFER FOR THE L4 SPACECRAFT (C219-0016MP)
description: The European Space Agency's next Science large-class mission (L4) will be dedicated to exploring Saturn's moon, Enceladus. Known for its active plumes and subsurface liquid ocean, Enceladus is a prime candidate in the search for extraterrestrial life. The missionis set to launch in 2042, with the spacecraft being assembled in space before embarking on its journey to Saturn. The spacecraft will sample Enceladus' plumes in 2053 and land on its south pole in 2058. Solar electric propulsion is the main candidate for propelling the spacecraft.The goal of this activity is to develop an electric thruster for the L4 spacecraft as propellant. The thruster shall be able to provide a specific impulse of at least 2500 s over a large power range [i.e. 9 to 20 kW] and a total impulse capability of at least 4 MNs/kW. As part of this activity, also a preliminary assessment of a dedicated test facility, to support development and qualification of such thruster, of shall be performed.

title: LARGE MODULAR ANTENNA WITH REDUCED GRATING LOBES (ARTES AT 5B.247) - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to develop a large antenna composed of modules or subarrays physically separated by multiple wavelengths in L-/S-Band, Ku- or Ka-band. This includes the development of wideband antenna beamforming and signal processing techniques to control the grating lobes and the necessary interconnectivity architecture to achieve the required phase and time synchronisation. Targeted Improvements: Enabling wideband beamforming for modular large apertures composed of multiple-wavelength-separated arrays.Description: Large antenna apertures up to tens of meters in diameter could enable many types of services in all orbits, including broadband, Internet of Things, and direct-to-device. However, today's launchers and platform choices often limit the size of the antenna to be deployed. Beamforming for apertures comprising multiple subarrays (modules, tiles) separated by a large electrical distance is possible, at the cost of grating lobes that degrade the performance of the antenna and extra complexity due to the required synchronisation. However, advanced beamforming techniques, such as multi-level beamforming as well as signal processing techniques, have the potential to reduce the interference introduced by grating lobes. This activity will study, develop, and implement widebandbeamforming and signal processing techniques to mitigate the effect of the grating lobes and to improve the antenna performance in terms of Carrier-to-Interference ratio (C/I) in L-/S-band, and in Ku- or Ka-band. The developed concepts will be implemented into anantenna breadboard and tested. The activity will be implemented in a phased approach where: Phase 1 will study array synthesis techniques to reduce the grating lobes, and the maximum electrical distance between adjacent subarrays to ensure that the resulting aggregate C/I will be above the threshold required for applications in L-/S-band, and in Ku- or Ka-band. Antenna performance in terms ofdirectivity, grating lobes, sidelobe level, C/I, and Equivalent Isotropic Radiated Power (EIRP) will be evaluated against distance between adjacent arrays. An interconnectivity architecture and critical technologies enabling the antenna beamforming, including interconnectivity and synchronisation, will be investigated and tested by a limited-scale derisking breadboard. Signal processing solutions that do not require a main processor will be studied where the processing is implemented in each module and then combined. Phase 1 output shall comprise a beamforming and signal processing concept supported by analysis and derisking test results as well as adefinition of an antenna baseline. The developed concepts shall be further developed in Phase 2 and implemented into an antenna testbed in L-/S-Band, Ku- or Ka-band (to be confirmed in Phase 1) capable to fully evaluate the performance and grating lobe suppression of the modular antenna aperture. The testbed will consist of 5-7 tiles (to be confirmed in Phase 1), each tile representing aco-located array antenna of limited size with several tiles implementing the beamforming network and interconnectivity. The antenna tile beamforming patterns and performance shall be tested as well as the combined beamforming performance of all tiles to evaluate the grating lobe suppression efficiency.

title: ESCA+ INDUSTRIAL SYSTEM ARCHITECT - EXPRO PLUS
description: The contract will cover a period of 18 months encompassing the system requirements consolidation, the definition of the system architecture and the initiation of the industrial phase of the ESCA+ project, with an option, to be activated at the discretion of the Agency, for a single extension for a further period of 6 months to cover the kick-off and ramp-up of the implementation phase.The tenderer will begin the activity providing support to define high-level requirements (interfacing also with the relevant Spanish userscommunity) and technical architecture of the ESCA+ system, which will support the development of the tender data package(s) of the industrial definition study to be released in Q3/Q4 2026. The tenderer will also support the preparation and maintenance of the project risk register, integrated schedule and project costs assessments.Once the space segment contract(s) will be placed, the tendererwill support the Agency to maintain the system architecture, its interfaces, the system requirement document and its apportionmentsto lower-level requirements to achieve the mission objectives. This work will also include support on the generation of ground segment requirements and of system operations requirements, as well as the assessment of the interoperability of the planned ESCA+ system with ERS-EO element 1; these outputs will then be used as key inputs for the ground segment tender expected in Q4 2027.The optional extension of the activity will continue the monitoring of output of the space segment implementation phase with respect to the mission objectives and requirements.

title: COPHASING OF A LARGE SEGMENTED TELESCOPE FOR EO EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop and validate the different steps necessary for the cophasing of a large Earth observation segmented telescopeDescription: Large telescopes (primary mirror diameter > 2-4m) have strong potential for Earth Observation applications: - persistent monitoring for security and disaster management from GEO - secure remote sensing from higher orbits (> 1200km), avoiding LEO debris impacts - high resolution for infrared missions (for which large pupils are mandatory). - very high resolution from LEO The segmentation of the large primary mirror is extremely useful to drastically improve the manufacturing/polishing schedule (multiyear gain) and to reduce the risk of development of a large monolithic primary mirror, particularly if the segmented mirror is not deployable. Technical maturity is high for ground segmented telescopes but is very low for Earth observation space telescopes, in particular in Europe. The key enabling technology behind the segmentation of a large primary mirror is the cophasing of the telescope segments, allowing to optimize the optical quality of the telescope. This critical technology that must be adapted to space use. In particular, the coarse cophasing must be based on a method and reference equipment that can be used and located on-board the payload. The finecophasing on an extended scene (essential for an EO application) need development as very little literature available on this topic. This activity would prove the feasibility of the full cophasing (coarse + fine phasing on star + fine phasing on extended scene) of a segmented telescope, with measurements on a small scale breadboard (2 to 4 segments) in order to correlate the results. The activity would encompass the following main tasks: - Coarse phasing: simulations and measurements on 4-segment small scale breadboard - Fine phasing on star: simulations and measurements on the breadboard. - Fine phasing on an extended scene: algorithm developments preliminary tests . - Roadmap and way forward.

title: PROTOTYPE OF A ROBUST VERY-CLOSE RANGE NAVIGATION SYSTEM FOR RENDEZVOUS AND DOCKING/CAPTURE EXPRO+
description: To trade-off, develop and test a visual navigation system able to robustly estimate the relative states to a target at, or close toa docking or capture location.Description: Navigation in close proximity to a target object is a challenging task because the accuracy needed to achieve docking or capture grows inversely with the distance from the target and, at the same time, as the target gets closer, typical target sizes greatly exceed the field of view of a wide-angle cameras (hence limiting the options on pose estimation techniques) and visual features are reduced (because only a fraction of the target is visible through the cameras). Availabilityof depth information can greatly assist the navigation task in very close proximity and several techniques and passive hardware devices (e.g. plenoptic and other light-field cameras) are available, using raw and/or pre-/post-processed data, in order to support the generation of a depth map (partial 3D model generated on-the-fly) of a target. In the first part of this activity, an assessment of the performances, robustness and computational needs and efficiency of the different approaches for generation of a depth map willbe performed considering the realistic but very demanding conditions (illumination, occlusions on the target surface, etc.) applicable to this phase of a rendezvous manoeuvre. Subsequently, the above assessment will be incorporated into a trade-off exercise versus other vision-based navigation strategies aimed at robustly estimating the relative states to a target. Following the closure of this trade-off, a visual navigation system will be defined and the corresponding image processing algorithms, data fusion process, andnavigation filters will be designed and implemented in a software prototype, which will undergo testing at software and GNC level (including functional and performance testing) in a representative simulation environment. The demonstration of the suitability of the developed algorithms shall also be achieved using a processor-in-the-loop (PIL) setup. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Review of technical literature specific to the problem of very-close range relative navigation in space. - Consolidation of applicable requirements and scenarios. - Assessment of depth-map generation techniques. - Trade-off and preliminary design of navigation system architecture. - Detailed design of the navigation system algorithms, including deployment in a software prototype - Validation of the algorithms in a representative simulation environment. - Verification on a representative flight processor.

title: ESA MERCHANDISE SOURCING, STORAGE AND ONLINE SHOP
description: ESA is seeking an official merchandising supplier capable of managing the development, production, storage, and global distributionof ESA-branded merchandise. ESA merchandise should remain diverse and engaging, reflecting ESA's legacy, current missions, and future endeavours, while also resonating withbroader market trends. The anticipated launch date for services is 1 January 2025.

title: NAVISP-EL1-123- QUANTUM MAGNETOMETER AND ALGORITHMS FOR INTEGRATED MAP MATCHING AND MAP BUILDING - EXPRO PLUS
description: General DescriptionThis activity aims to design and demonstrate a quantum magnetometer-based navigation platform for GNSS-denied environments. It leverages Earth's crustal magnetic anomalies as a positioning reference and integrates quantum sensing technologies for high-resolution magnetic measurements. The system will include AI-based filtering algorithms for noise suppression and real-timemap matching. It will also feature onboard magnetic map-building capabilities to enable robust navigation across multiple domains. Aprototype will be developed and validated through field demonstrations in selected operational scenarios. For more info, visit https://navisp.esa.int/opportunity

title: T512-901GS INTEGRATED CRYOGENIC OPTICAL READOUT FOR SCALABLE SINGLE-PHOTON DETECTORS ARRAYS (EXPRO+)
description: The increasing demand for high-performance, scalable single-photon detection in quantum communication,deep-space optical links, and astronomical observations require low-power, high-bandwidth cryogenic readoutsolutions, driving the need for an integrated photonic readout that mitigates power dissipation and enhancessystem scalability. Recent studies have demonstrated that photonic readoutsin cryogenic environmentsreduce power dissipation and increase bandwidth.The aim of this activity is to address the limitations ofhigh-power dissipation, large deadtime, and jitter in multipixelSNSPD arrays by integrating photonic readouts, within the cryogenic environment. This solution ensuresscalability of SNSPD arrays while maintaining optimal cooling and performance metrics and addresses marketneeds for stable, high-performance detectors in low-temperature environments.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs).
