title: ERS-EO IOD-D - SATELLITE SUPER AGILITY
description: In order to de-risk and accelerate the implementation phase of EOGS, the IOD/IOV activities will focus on short-term achievements delivered through targeted in-orbit experiments. These experiments are intended to provide early proof of concept and in-orbit validation, with demonstrable results available ahead of the next Ministerial Conference in 2028.The scope and objectives of the IOD/IOV activities are aimed at strengthening European autonomy, including enhancing the industrialisation of solutions already under development, and supporting pre-operational validation and technology demonstration.The technologies to be developed for EOGS space missions will be selected in consultation with the European Commission and Participating States, and in accordance with the main findingsof the EOGS studies. The technologies which are being considered are:- Secure inter-satellite links and IRIS interoperability;- Data management, on-board processing and dynamic satellite tasking to reduce latency;- Enhanced security features demonstrating resilience to the considered threats;- Serialisation and synergies (re-use) across the ERS fleet;- Increased agility and imaging capacity over crisis area;- Low-cost high-performance SAR and optical payloads with extended imaging capabilities; and- Platforms optimised for batch launches on European launchers and compatible with applicable clean space policies.Drawing on these findings, together with further consultation with industry through the Request for Information (RFI) released in July 2025 which received a substantial number of responses four main themes have been identified for the IOD/IOV activities.The In-Orbit Demonstration/Validation(IOD/IOV) activities are therefore organised into the following four themes:A. IOD-A: Low Luminance / Night VisionB. IOD-B: DynamicSatellite TaskingC. IOD-C: Reduced information age (i.e. data latency from acquisition to product delivery)D. IOD-D: Satellite Super AgilityThese correspond to areas where a further consolidation is needed (hence the relevance of conducting an IOD) before a feature of very high interest and relevance to the ERS-EO programme objective could be declared operational and included in the nominal configuration of the system.

title: ESA SPACE WEATHER SERVICE NETWORK PRE-OPERATION, EVOLUTIONARY MAINTENANCE AND DEVELOPMENT
description: The present activity pursues two main objectives.First, it shall ensure the continued high-quality provision of pre-operational space weather services under the existing SWE Service Network. This includes maintaining the availability of the products and servicescurrently included in the Network portfolio through the SWE Service Portal, ensuring the integration of newly developed or updated products, providing first- and second-line end-user support, delivering tailored bulletins to high-priority users, and performing continuous and evolutionary maintenance of key service components.In addition, the service catalogue shall be updated and adapted to reflect emerging and future needs of a European operational space weather service.Second, the activity shall define, design, and implement a modern Research-to-Operations-to-Research (R2O2R) framework for space weather products and services. This shall include the analysis of existing processes, the specification of the target framework, and its practical implementation within the SWE ServiceNetwork.The outcome of the activity shall enable the transition towards a new generation of the SWE Service Network and an updatedversion of the ESA SWE Service Portal.The procurement shall require the application of high standards in software engineering, theactive involvement of end-users within the R2O2R lifecycle, and the delivery of a professional, high-quality user experience for the web portal, including modern software practices, advanced graphical design, and robust human-machine interfaces.

title: M2 PCIE NVME SOLID STATE DRIVES FOR FUTURE MASS STORAGE SOLUTIONS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a memory array based on M2 PCIe NAND flash memory Solid State Drives modules and characterise the radiation effects and possible mitigation methods at software and hardware levels.Description: High density Mass storage solutions based on NAND flash memory Solid State Drives (SSD) are widely used in data server applications and present a great opportunity for space applications. However, their reliability and their tolerance to radiation-induced effects have not been evaluated so far. M2 PCI ExpressNon-Volatile Memory (NVM) storage drives are now commonly used System on Module (SoM) devices, similar in size to Double Dada Rate (DDR) memory modules used in personal computers, and capable of storing over 1TB of data. These SoMs incorporate advanced Error Detection and Correction (EDAC) systems to manage the frequent occurrence of bad blocks and bits in 3D NAND Flash Memories. These devicescan be used in a Redundant Array of Independent Disks (RAID) due to Peripheral Component Interconnect Express (PCIe) interface. Thecombination of powerful EDAC and the hot redundancy of RAID is beneficial for addressing the anticipated radiation effects and wearout in NAND Flash memories when used in Space. The non-volatile nature of these memories helps preventing data loss during power cycling to recover Single Event Functional Interrupts (SEFI) in the control electronics. Additionally, these storage drives are currently used in high-speed computation nodes where radiation effects caused by neutrons and alpha particles are a concern. The PCIe interface is widely supported in commercial processors and FPGAs, and will be featured in the next generation of space-graded processorsand FPGAs. The PCIe interface targets to enable the use of very high density, compact, non-volatile memories modules, for the nextgeneration platform and payload units (OBCs, solid state mass memories, ICUs, etc). This proposal aims to develop a RAID array controlled by a European processor or FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Arrays), using various M2 PCIe NVMe SSD modules. This setup enables the assessment of feasibility and reliability concerning radiation and wear out effects, paving the way for a new concept of extremelyhigh-density data storage for space applications. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Selection of several candidateM2 PCIe SSD devices from different manufacturers. - Development of a Single Event Effect (SEE) test setup for SSD drives using thePCIe compatible European processor / FPGA in RAID configuration. - Proton and heavy ion SEE testing- Assessment of the test results and proposal of further mitigation techniques if needed.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: ANONYMITY AND POST QUANTUM SECURITY SUBSCRIBER IDENTITY MODULE (SIM) TECHNOLOGY FOR 5G/6G NTN (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 3D.040)
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop advanced and post-quantum Subscriber Identity Module (SIMs) for 5G/6G NTN. The focus is to improve user anonymity for robust non-terrestrialnetworks (NTNs) used for governmental applications which have a more urgent need for post-quantum anonymity protection than the commercial market. These SIMs shall implementsecurity improvements of the part of the primary authentication protocol which is implemented in the SIM. Additionally, the corresponding SIM provisioning infrastructure and the corenetwork responsible for the communication with the SIMs will be developed.TargetedImprovements: Enablinga European or Canadian source for robust NTN SIM (Physical Universal Integrated Circuit Card (UICC) or Embedded UICC (eUICC)) for 5G/6G satellite constellation withhardened primary authentication protocolDescription: Current 5G Universal Subscriber Identity Modules (USIMs) to be used in Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) for Satellite Communication (SATCOM) terminals lack adequate protectionagainst user tracking when assuming a quantum attacker. While 3GPP is working on the migration to post-quantum cryptography, the privacy needs in governmental NTN networks arehigher than in usual mobile networks and regulatory needs will require the full post-Quantum migration as early as 2030 for governmental communication solutions. An appropriatesolution therefore needs to be developed earlier than the 3GPP timeline foresees.The activity will design, develop and test prototypes of advanced 5G/6G USIMs integrating security improvements to the primary authentication protocol (user tracking enhancements inNTNs and anticipated regulatory requirements for post-quantum cryptography), with all components adhering to GSMA/ETSI security standards and targeting Common Criteria evaluationto prepare for future accreditation.The activity will evaluate two implementation paths to address this need: Physical Universal Integrated Circuit Card (UICC) development, potentially as an applet on an existing smartcard platform, or Embedded UICC (eUICC) with appropriate SIM profiles for multi-provider service access. Post-Quantum Key Exchange Management (KEM) implementations on smartcards prove the technical feasibility of implementing such protocols in the UICC approach.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach.The first phase will study the implementation of post quantum security in the authentication protocol and perform a trade-off analysis between the two implementation paths. It will designand develop an initial prototype of the USIM and provisioning infrastructure compatible with standardised 3GPP interfaces between USIM and Mobile Equipment and perform the designof the security functions of the Core network solution to interoperate with the USIM. Phase 1 deliverables consist of architecture and design documents, initial documents to prepare thecertification, software prototype and adapted core network functions to interoperate with the software. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 700 kEuros.In the second phase, the activity will further develop and test the USIM components (UICC or eUICC), create the complete SIM provisioning infrastructure, and develop and test the corenetwork security functionsincluding the Subscriber Identifier De-concealing Function (SIDF) to support enhanced authentication of the USIM to the network. Phase 2 deliverables includethe adaptation of smart card including applet design and SIM printer or chip development for eUICC and refined certification preparation.During the activity, dissemination towards 3GPP standardisation shall be performed to ensure futureindustry adoption.

title: END-TO-END DEMONSTRATION OF 5G NEW RADIO (NR) FOR FUTURE RAILWAY MOBILE COMMUNICATION SYSTEMS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7C.086) - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of this activity is to develop the necessary 5G New Radio (NR) ground segment prototypes for servicing the Future Railway Mobile Communication System (FRMCS) via satellite and demonstrate the capability with end-to-end in orbit testing.Targeted improvements:Ensure compliance to the FRMCS safety and performance requirements by demonstrating the feasibility of servicing via a satellite link, complementing the terrestrial network. Provide ETSI RT standardisation group with the required inputs for satellite.Description:The Future Railway Mobile Communication System (FRMCS), being a successor of the GSM-R system, is planned to be operational before GSM-R's predicted saturation in 2030. In this respect, ETSI (European Telecommunications Standards Institute) is already preparing the relevant FRMCS standard. In the frame of this work, satcom is established as a componentof the future system. More specifically, the integration of satcom to FRMCS was identified to be more straightforward when satcom is employing 5G NR, which is going to be the air interface for the terrestrial FRMCS access. Regarding the terrestrial FRMCS 5G NR access, live trials are planned by 2024, as it is targeted for the first stable version of FRMCS to be available for procurement by the beginning of 2025.To establish satellite with solid foundation in FRMCS, and to demonstrate its capability to service the terrestrial gaps of communication,it is essential that a similar activity will take place also for satellite. This activity will therefore validate with a real in-orbit demonstration the capability of satellite to service operational trains with FRMCS while using the 5G NR air interface. For this purpose, ground segment prototypes (i.e., modems on board trains and for gateways) will be designed via FPGA or SDR-based developments and validated initially in a lab environment and then on field versus the FRMCS requirements. Whenever possible, COTS RF/antenna equipment should be used for the purpose of this development. Both ForwardLink and Return Link will be considered to demonstrate the interactivity of FRMCS use cases. The best candidate satellite connectivity (in terms of orbit, frequency), as well as trains of different speeds and different local environments (e.g. rural, suburban, urban) will be considered, to exhibit the response of the satellite 5G NR link and its compliance to the FRMCS requirements over a plethora of scenarios characterised by different multipath, fading and interference conditions. In addition, switching between satellite and terrestrial 5G NR networks will be showcased to offer insight on the performance of the handover that takes place when the train transitions between coverages. Satellite switching willalso be demonstrated in case a satellite constellation is considered for the live trials.The outcome of the work will feed the ETSI FRMCS standardisation through the participation to the ETSI RT standardisation group.

Description: The objective of this activity is to develop the necessary 5G New Radio (NR) ground segment prototypes for servicing the Future Railway Mobile Communication System (FRMCS) via satellite and demonstrate the capability with end-to-end in orbit testing.Targeted improvements:Ensure compliance to the FRMCS safety and performance requirements by demonstrating the feasibility of servicing via a satellite link, complementing the terrestrial network. Provide ETSI RT standardisation group with the required inputs for satellite.Description:The Future Railway Mobile Communication System (FRMCS), being a successor of the GSM-R system, is planned to be operational before GSM-R's predicted saturation in 2030. In this respect, ETSI (European Telecommunications Standards Institute) is already preparing the relevant FRMCS standard. In the frame of this work, satcom is established as a componentof the future system. More specifically, the integration of satcom to FRMCS was identified to be more straightforward when satcom is employing 5G NR, which is going to be the air interface for the terrestrial FRMCS access. Regarding the terrestrial FRMCS 5G NR access, live trials are planned by 2024, as it is targeted for the first stable version of FRMCS to be available for procurement by the beginning of 2025.To establish satellite with solid foundation in FRMCS, and to demonstrate its capability to service the terrestrial gaps of communication,it is essential that a similar activity will take place also for satellite. This activity will therefore validate with a real in-orbit demonstration the capability of satellite to service operational trains with FRMCS while using the 5G NR air interface. For this purpose, ground segment prototypes (i.e., modems on board trains and for gateways) will be designed via FPGA or SDR-based developments and validated initially in a lab environment and then on field versus the FRMCS requirements. Whenever possible, COTS RF/antenna equipment should be used for the purpose of this development. Both ForwardLink and Return Link will be considered to demonstrate the interactivity of FRMCS use cases. The best candidate satellite connectivity (in terms of orbit, frequency), as well as trains of different speeds and different local environments (e.g. rural, suburban, urban) will be considered, to exhibit the response of the satellite 5G NR link and its compliance to the FRMCS requirements over a plethora of scenarios characterised by different multipath, fading and interference conditions. In addition, switching between satellite and terrestrial 5G NR networks will be showcased to offer insight on the performance of the handover that takes place when the train transitions between coverages. Satellite switching willalso be demonstrated in case a satellite constellation is considered for the live trials.The outcome of the work will feed the ETSI FRMCS standardisation through the participation to the ETSI RT standardisation group.

title: DUAL-BEAM KA-BAND-BASED MULTI-ORBIT AERONAUTICAL FLAT PANEL ANTENNA (ARTES AT 7C.106) - EXPRO+ (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test a Ka-band based (Ka-only or Ka and Ku) dual-beam electronically scanning flat panel antenna able to simultaneously connect to two satellites located at two different orbits. Four beams, two for transmit and two for receive path , will be implemented with two apertures.Targeted Improvements: - 50% antenna surface reduction required for the generation of 2 simultaneously active antenna beams compared to conventional phased array implementation.- Complexity reduction of the associated beamforming networks compared to phased arrays based on digital beamformers or multi-band beamformers.Description: The growing trend of combining the use of GEO and NGSO satellite systems for the provision of in-flight connectivity to airplanes suggests the use of antenna terminals able to connect simultaneously to two satellites located on different orbits. A possible operational scenario could envisage the use of LEO satellites for latency-sensitive content to be supplemented by GEO satellites connectivity, possibly over congested areas that are commonly found in lower latitudes that do not require extreme antenna scanning angles to connect to equatorial orbits. At higher latitudes, two concurrently operated antenna beams could simultaneously connect to two LEO satellites to provide aggregate data traffic. The approach of deploying a single antenna aperture per antenna beam leads to doubling the overall terminal surface occupation. Alternatively, producing more than one beam from a single array of radiating elements would require complex design for the radiating elements themselves as well as for the associated beam-forming network. The observation that connecting to NGSO systems does not require scanning the antenna beams to very wide angles suggests that the inter-element spacing can be relaxed, allowing for interleavingtwo simple arrays sharing a common antenna surface, each array could then be fed by a simple single-beam beam-forming network, resulting in a practical implementation.This activity will design a dual-beam electronically scanning flat panel antenna to exploit a common surface to implement two simultaneously operating antenna beams connecting to two satellite operating from different orbits and possibly at different frequencies (Ku- or Ka-band), this for the transmitting as well as for the receiving antenna functions. This will result in an antenna aperture generating two independent receiving beams and a second one generating two independent transmitting beams. A reduced scale prototype of a dualbeam flat panel antenna, either operating in transmit or in receive mode, will be developed and tested.

title: PRESERVATION ASSETS OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCESERVICE (PAOM-SER)
description: ESA operates one of the world's largest Earth Observation (EO) data archives, with data from missions dating back to the mid 1970s.Preserving these datatogether with the information and tools needed to interpret and use themis essential to analyse long-term environmental changes and support future decision-making. Within the EOF-EOS framework, long-term preservation of ESA's EO data holdings (Heritage Missions, Earth Explorers, Third Party Missions) and associated information and software is ensured through the Space Data Preservation System (SDPS), with assets located at ESRIN and external sites.Despite major progress, a significant volume of EO heritage data remains stored on legacy media at ESRIN and still requires transcription, recovery, and preservation in line with international standards. Beyond preservation and access, heritage data must be curated and improved to ensure continuity and comparability with newer missions. The generation of thematic collections and geographical datasets has further enhanced their usability and value.The Preservation Assets Operations and Maintenance (PAOM) Service will:Operate, maintain, and evolve Space Data Preservation System (SDPS) assets located at ESRIN;Manage the ESRIN EO Legacy Media Archive and Transcription Chains and perform legacy media transcription and data recovery;Generate thematic collections and geographical coverages using heritage data;Manage the ESRIN laboratory activities in support to transcription chains set-up and Philab Air Quality Platform activities, and manage and maintain the ESRIN AF Antenna;Support local visits at the Heritage Missions Walkthrough and Memorabilia Wall located at ESRIN and heritage missionsrelated outreach activities.

title: MULTIBEAM GATEWAY ANTENNA FOR SATCOM CONSTELLATIONS (ARTES AT 6B.147) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a single aperture Ka or Q/V band gateway multibeam antenna, capable to serve multiple satellites located in a large field of view.Targeted Improvements: Replacing multiple (up to 12) gateway antennas based on reflectors with a single aperture multi-beam gateway antenna ; Reducing by a factor 10 the complexity ofa conventional active array antenna.Description: With the proliferation of satellite constellations, there is a strong interest, need, and market opportunities for innovative multibeam antennas for Gateway stations. These antennas should be able to generate multiple simultaneous beams in order to guarantee the link with different satellites. Existing gateway antennas are mainly based on reflectors dishes repointable mechanically, and able to track a single satellite instantaneously. Multibeam gateway antennas based onactive phased arrays are also under development. They can generate multiple simultaneous beams, but they are not competitive yet interms of complexity, power dissipation, thermal issues, cost. For these reasons, in this activity innovative multibeam antennas with a reduced complexity should be developed. The beamforming could be analogue, digital or hybrid. A significant simplification can be obtained by limitingthe multiple beams directions in a limited portion of the field of view where the majority of the satellitesareexpected to be visible. In facts, the number of active controls in the antenna is proportional to the extension of the angular field of view. Another simplification can be obtained by assuming a minimum angular separation between two contiguous beams corresponding to two different satellites. The design must be customisable based on the longitude and latitude of the gateway station considering also the orbital position and orientation of the constellations to be served. By applying these simplifications and customisations, significant simplifications in the gateway antennas should be obtained.The activity will design, manufacture and test a singleaperture Ka or Q/V band gateway multibeam antenna, capable to serve multiple satellites located in a large field of view. At least twopromising technical solutions will be identified and studied. Trade-offs will be carried out and the most promising concept willbe selected and implemented in a reduced scale prototype. The developed multibeam gateway antenna will be tested in a relevant environment establishing a link with a real satellite and scanning two independent andsimultaneous beams.

title: INTEGRATED SUBMILLIMETRE WAVE ANTENNA-COUPLED DUAL-POLARIZATION FOCAL PLANE ARRAY AND DETECTION CHAIN
description: Objective: To develop an integrated submillimeter wave antenna-coupled dual-polarization focal plane array and detection chain for space and ground applications.Description: Submillimeter wave focal plane array (FPA) based on very sensitive detectors like transition edge sensor (TES) technology have been proposed in several cosmic microwave background missions like SPICA and LiteBIRD as wellas ground experiments. The European technology for the realization of such FPA and receiver chains has been demonstrated as individual building blocks. Further developments are required to optimize the design and further implement the full receiver chain. For scientific objectives, large-format millimeter and submillimeter arrays (40-400GHz) with moderate sensitivity (10-18 WHz-1/2) are required in two linear polarizations and high polarimetric purity over large fractional bandwidths. The most promising solution consistsof using microstrip-coupled TESs and waveguide horns to maintain clean beams with a high degree of frequency independence and straylight rejection. Miniature on-chip superconducting RF components, such as directional couplers and bandpass filters, will be used toprovide additional functionality.This activity is divided into phases, it is expected to be run by a prime being responsible for thefull system, with contributions of different institutes for the following sub-systems and it encompasses the following tasks perphase:Phase 1 (budget: 4000 k, duration: 24 months):- Design and development of an antenna-coupled TES bolometers, including theortho-mode transducer (OMT) and on-chip bandpass filter and TES bolometers.- Development and packaging of lightweight low frequency feedhorns, considering additive manufacturing or advanced manufacturing techniques (including modelling, development of manufacturingprocesses and the manufacturing of test demonstration devices).- Development and packaging of drilled profiled horn arrays, optical and thermal CTE optimization and the refinement of manufacturing processes considering corrugated silicon platelet feed horn arrays.-Development of frequency division multiplexing (FDM) cold readout, including a two stage SQUID (superconducting quantum interference device) system and high-quality factor LC filters.Phase 2 (budget: 3000 k, duration: 12 months):- Implementation of a testbed detection chain, considering the TES noise and the noise equivalent power (NEP) demonstration in single-pixel and multiplexing and the development of algorithms for 1/f noise correlation among pixels in same readout chain.- Demonstration of the integration and thecryogenic performance of the FPA, including a fully representative FPA breadboard model (50%-pixel population), the FPA packaging and integration, feedhorn integration and full module testing (cryogenic optical testing).

title: ROBUST NAVIGATION SYSTEM FOR PLANETARY LANDERS - EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesTo implement and test navigation reinitialisation logics that maximise the likelihood of safe recovery from navigation filter divergence during descent and landing.DescriptionA lander's navigation system faces extreme challenges in an environment that is poorly modeled and highly variable, leading to complex sensor stimulations and interactions across a wide range flight paramteres (e.g. altritude, attitude, etc.). Vehicle dynamics demand rapid deceleration from high velocity to a complete stop. During descent and landingan irreversible phase in most missionsaborts or retries are impossible due totrajectory physics. Landing failures can often be traced back to a navigation failure driven by these effects. Recovery from an uncontained navigation failure is exceptionally unlikely. However, a failure in the navigation system should not automatically lead to total loss of navigation capability. A well-designed system includes multiple health monitors and acceptance conditions, from low-level sensor electronics to high-level navigation filter updates. Monitors are periodically checked to enable the fastest possible recovery action,which may involve reconfiguration, switching to backup units, or discarding faulty measurements. Despite these safeguards, some failures propagate into the estimatedstate vector, often causing fatal consequences and loss of navigation function. This typically results in an inability to safely contact the surface. But before reaching this critical failure, a robust navigation design should incorporate an ultimate fallback: an on-the-flyreinitialization procedure. This activity broadly addresses the implementation and testing of reinitialization procedures, starting with the detection of navigation system failures. The following tasksshall be conducted:1. Implement or adapt ageneric precision navigation solution to be tested in Enceladuslanding scenarios. The navigation design shall build on establishedcompany orconsortium heritage and use performance models for image or terrain-relative processing.2. Develop a stochastic failureinjector, preceded by thorough research into critical failuresthrough detailed sensor and pseudo-sensor analysis, navigation system review, andhistorical mishap investigations.3. Perform trade-offs and implement navigation filter reinitialization logics along with theirtriggering conditions.4. Conduct performance and robustness simulation campaigns.5. Port and validate the selected reinitialization procedure on a Processor-in-the-Loop(PIL) setup integrated with the navigation flight software, verifying result reproducibility andembeddability.

title: PLANETARY PROTECTION - RISK INFORMED DECISION MODELS FOR ICY WORLDS - EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesCreate a probability of contamination model that will guide mission teams in assessing the planetary protection categoryand implementing associated requirements. This model will include a conservative estimate of poorly known parameters, such as:i) bioburden at launchii) cruise survival for contaminating organismsiii) organism survival in the radiation environmentiv) probability of landing on Europa or Enceladusv) mechanisms and timescales of transport to a subsurface liquid water environmentvi) organismsurvival and proliferation before, during, and after subsurface transferDescriptionThe activity will give mission teams increasedflexibility when implementing Planetary Protection and will result in cheaper, more sustainable, and responsible exploration of IcyWorlds.The work will be divided into different work packages, aimed at:acquiring scientific dataintegrating such data into the model.Collection of data:WP1: Bioburden at launch and survivability. This task will examine existing molecular biology and metagenomics data, as well as produce new ones as applicable.Phenotypic predictions from metagenomic datasets and using suitable training datasets from public repositories.WP2: Transport mechanism in Icy Worlds, modelling transport of contamination with focus on Enceladus. title: POSITIONING-INDEPENDENT AIR-INTERFACE TECHNIQUES FOR 6G NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORKS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7B.092) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: Objective of the activity is to develop and test positioning-independent techniques for Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) air interfaces.TargetedImprovements:Enable positioning independency for ground NTN terminals.Description: The development of a positioning-independent air-interface is deemed essential for future 6G NTN. Conventional 5G NTN terminals rely heavily on GNSS for positioning andtiming information, which means a terminal with no or poor GNSS reception cannot use NTN technology. Moreover, GNSS signals are vulnerable to spoofing and jamming,which can compromise the reliability and security of the communication links. By developing positioning-independent techniques, NTN terminals can operate without relying onGNSS or other positioning systems / sensors, enabling indoor coverage which is one of the goals in 6G for NTN as defined in the 3GPP roadmap. This feature is also crucialfor maintaining reliable communication in various scenarios, including critical infrastructure and emergency response. Positioning-independent modems can then operate inenvironments where positioning signals are weak or unavailable, such as indoors, urban canyons, or remote areas. This flexibility enhances the overall coverage and reliabilityof NTN services.This activity will explore the use of alternative techniques and protocols enabling a positioning-independent NTN air interface. Techniques and protocols shall be implementedin a modem prototype and evaluated in a real-time testbed possibly based on open radio stack.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: SECURE ON-BOARD AND ACCESS CONTROL ROUTER FOR FUTURE SATELLITE COMMUNICATIONS SYSTEMS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 5A.097) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop an on-board router with secure tagging, access control and filtering capabilities suitable to route traffic from users with different securitypriorities (e.g. commercial, governmental, etc.) to support future LEO, MEO and multi-orbit satellite communications systems.TargetedImprovements: Enabling novel capability, not existing today inESA MS, which will allow to route securely user traffic with different security constraints in large satellite communicationsconstellations.Description: Due to the increasingly shared nature of satellite communication systems, specifically at the level of the payload and inter-satellite links, there is a need for traffic filtering androuting capabilities based on different security requirements.This activity will extend the capabilities of regenerative payloads, by considering the authenticated source of the traffic and related security priorities, in order to include fine-grainedfiltering and dynamic routing. The onboard router shall be able to decide how to route packets, depending on the authenticated source (based on the validated tag), securityrequirements, destination ,type of traffic data, etc. The onboard secure routing module shall interface with a key management system managing keys used to validate theauthenticity of traffic for different entities. Algorithms specific for onboard policy-based filtering will be developed, considering various criteria for filtering and routing. In addition tofiltering based on authenticated tags, source, but also destination, packet protocol and header information, the algorithms will need to consider the varying latency anddynamic/scalable network topologies. The policy-based routing configuration will have to be dynamically reconfigurable, and shall consider, in addition to the onboard processingand memory constraints, the available inter satellite links or the available ground stations for routing decision-making. Under increased load, the router may furthermore be able torestrict the allocation of onboard resources to ensure the prioritised/efficient processing of critical traffic data. Segregated zones for management/operational purposes, as well asfor traffic with different security requirements shall be considered.The activity will design a secure on-board router enabling the filtering and routing based on the authenticated source of the traffic, integrated with a key management system. Theactivity will then implement the selected design as a payload module and perform verification and validation of the module by testing the overall resilience of the module.

title: 4D EARTH CORE+ - EXPRO+
description: Over the past decade, our understanding of Earth's core dynamics has significantly advanced, largely due to the continuous geomagnetic field data provided by the ESA Swarm mission. These long-term observations, combined with progress in geodynamo numerical modelling, have greatly improved our ability to analyse rapid magnetic field variations. However, several key questions remain unanswered, particularly regarding the causes of the eastward flow growth beneath the Pacific, the acceleration and deceleration of high-latitude jets, and some detected wave motions at specific latitudes. Further investigation is needed to understand transient core motions and the role of hydro-magnetic waves, with a strong focus on uncertainty estimation. Addressing these challenges requires extending the analysed time period to improve predictive capabilities and exploring the feasibility of machine learning methods for potential geomagnetic field forecasting. The 4D Core+ initiative is dedicated to tackling these issues, with the ultimate goal of deepening our comprehension of Earth's deep interior.

title: ADVANCED SUB-THZ PACKAGING TECHNOLOGIES - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop a 664 GHz direct detection receiver using innovative packaging techniques for future ultra-compact array instruments.Description: Future array instruments and ultra-compact payload instruments require ultra-compact receiver integrating all RF (Radio Frequency) functions with very small SWaP (Size, Weight and Power), removing complex mechanical and electrical interfaces such as standard waveguide flanges and DC/IF (Direct Current/Intermediate Frequency) coaxial connectors. Novel silicon micromachining techniques are key-enablers to develop ultra-compact RF front-end by integrating in a High-Aspect-Ratio silicon-wafer stack all the key components required to achieve state-of-the-art performance, including high-gain antenna, RF LNA MMIC (Microwave Monolithically Integrated Circuit), RF filters, diode detector, video amplifier and associated DC electronics.This activity aims to develop an integrated 664 GHz Direct Detection Receiver, including a novel high-gain flat-antenna, RF LNA MMIC, a narrow-bandpass filter, and a zero-bias detector with integrated video-amplifier. The developed receiver will be tested radiometrically, including beam pattern measurement, Noise Figure, Short-Term-Gain-Stability, and Gain response over temperature. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Design of an integrated direct detection receiver operating at 664 GHz. - Investigation ofsilicon-micromachined fabrication and packaging techniques for all critical RF elements: flat-antenna, waveguide active (LNA) and passive (filter) devices, RF/IF/DC interconnections. - Manufacturing and testing of a breadboard model. - Development plan and future roadmap.

title: FREE SPACE PROPAGATION MODEL FOR MULTIDIMENSIONAL QUANTUM STATES (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3D.032) ON REQUEST EXPRO+
description: Objective:The objective of this activity is to evaluate optical attenuation and distortions caused by atmospheric turbulences between space and ground on temporal multidimensional quantum states for multidimensional quantum key distribution through the development and validation of a testbed.Targeted Improvements:-Enabling multidimensional quantum key distribution.-Experimental characterisation of the atmospheric effects for the use of multidimensional quantum key distribution on satellite-to-ground links.-Contribution to the definition of requirements for future multidimensional Quantum Communication (QC) services.Description:Current two-dimensional qubit states (e.g. !01>) transfer information using a superposition of two orthogonal vectors. Multidimensional qubitstates, e.g. !0123...>, are capable to transfer more information due to an increased number of orthogonal vectors compared to qubitstates, and are more resilient against noise. In free space links, atmospheric turbulence induced fading with their influence over optical wavefront causes significant perturbation of the multidimensional temporal modes of the QC signal. Currently, there are well-defined techniques for an evaluation of atmospheric turbulence effect over the quality of a classical free-space optical (FSO) linkutilising number of different phase screens as well as spatial light modulators (SLM). While breadboards implementing those techniquesexists and are quite available for FSO channels, the influence of the fast induced fading due to scintillations over multidimensional temporal modes of transmitted single photons in a QC channel remain unevaluated. This activity will bring together theoretical scientific groups and applied technology development in the field of optical free space transmission to deliver simulation tools which will be integrated into a testbed for quantum communication. This activity will extend the capability of satellite to ground links from the transfer of two-dimensional qubit states to transfer of multi-dimensional qubit states. i.e. more information can be transferred per qubit (single photon) and it has a higher resilience against atmospheric turbulence induced quantum noise and consequently a lower Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER) will be achieved.

title: ERS-EO IOD-B - DYNAMIC SATELLITE TASKING
description: In order to de-risk and accelerate the implementation phase of EOGS, the IOD/IOV activities will focus on short-term achievements delivered through targeted in-orbit experiments. These experiments are intended to provide early proof of concept and in-orbit validation, with demonstrable results available ahead of the next Ministerial Conference in 2028.The scope and objectives of the IOD/IOV activities are aimed at strengthening European autonomy, including enhancing the industrialisation of solutions already under development, and supporting pre-operational validation and technology demonstration.The technologies to be developed for EOGS space missions will be selected in consultation with the European Commission and Participating States, and in accordance with the main findingsof the EOGS studies. The technologies which are being considered are:- Secure inter-satellite links and IRIS interoperability;- Data management, on-board processing and dynamic satellite tasking to reduce latency;- Enhanced security features demonstrating resilience to the considered threats;- Serialisation and synergies (re-use) across the ERS fleet;- Increased agility and imaging capacity over crisis area;- Low-cost high-performance SAR and optical payloads with extended imaging capabilities; and- Platforms optimised for batch launches on European launchers and compatible with applicable clean space policies.Drawing on these findings, together with further consultation with industry through the Request for Information (RFI) released in July 2025 which received a substantial number of responses four main themes have been identified for the IOD/IOV activities.The In-Orbit Demonstration/Validation(IOD/IOV) activities are therefore organised into the following four themes:A. IOD-A: Low Luminance / Night VisionB. IOD-B: DynamicSatellite TaskingC. IOD-C: Reduced information age (i.e. data latency from acquisition to product delivery)D. IOD-D: Satellite Super AgilityThese correspond to areas where a further consolidation is needed (hence the relevance of conducting an IOD) before a feature of very high interest and relevance to the ERS-EO programme objective could be declared operational and included in the nominal configuration of the system.

title: FIRST!7 STRUCTURES, MATERIALS, MECHANISMS AND PROCESSES FOR SPACE TRANSPORTATION - EXPRO+
description: This ITT targets short-term, quick maturation of disruptive technologies across five categories of interest:A.Optimised materialsfor composite and/or metallic structures: technologies that bring significant performance improvements in terms of mass, robustnessor sustainability like (but not limited to) vitrimers, nanocomposites, new resins, fibers, metallic alloys, including Europeanization of alloys or key materialsB.Optimised processes for composite or metallic structures: technologies that bring significant improvement in terms of recurring costs or sustainability. It would include (but not only) new winding techniques, thermoplastic welding,advanced manufacturing like AFSW and DED, resin fiber moulding, repair and online inspection techniques. In that topic, full automation and increasing role of AI could be of highest interest for disruptive improvementC.Disruptive composite technologies for Space Transportation in cryogenic environment: the compatibility of composite materials with cryogenic substances (propellants in particular) is a major issue, and being able to easily store cryo fluids in composite structures can bring significant performance gains. Proposed technologies can cover cryogenic linerless composites tank, cleaning processes, innovative structural junctions, interfacesfor fluidic element and sealing for CFRP cryogenic tanks. The above list is not exhaustiveD.Electro-Mechanical Space Transportation structures: like (but not limited to) technologies that allow quick and efficient health check for reusable structures or in-orbit structure. It can also include multi-functional structures like integrated raceways, structural energy systems and structural actuatorsE.Mechanisms for space transportation systems: Deployment, releasing, locking or grabbing mechanisms are key for new space transportation systems like reusable structures or OTVs. The existing technologies are often complex, heavy and expensive. This category aims at proposing disruption in this matterParallel contract, 1 @500kEUR and 1@1 MEUR per category, are contemplated, the number and value of which may vary depending on the interest of the proposals, and availability of the respective nationality budgets.

title: BEYOND 5G HUB OVER-THE-AIR TECHNOLOGY VALIDATIONS (ARTES 4.0 5G/6G 3F.063) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and implement over-the-air Beyond 5G (B5G) satellite system demonstrators that validate Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) technologydevelopments in realistic conditions.TargetedImprovements: Fostering the adoption of B5G satellite technologies.Description: A number of technical developments in the area of B5G over satellite already take place as part of the ARTES Work Plans and other research activities. So far, thesedevelopments have not always been evaluated and performance demonstrated in an end-to-end or system context, which is paramount for attracting the interest of keystakeholders such as terrestrial parties.To fill this gap, this activity will develop and implement a number of over-the-air system demonstrators thatwill validate the outcome of various B5G technology developmentsin a number of Terrestrial / Non-Terrestrial Networks (TN / NTN) integrated architectures. Besides, they will be implemented in an incremental manner to allow incorporatingthose developments at an early stage. As a minimum, the activity will demonstrate the use of 5G New Radio (NR) over satellite in different orbits using either transparentpayloads or space segment that has some on-board processing capabilities. A number of existing and planned experimental or commercial payloads could offer suchprocessing capability. Until these become available, the activity will target B5G over-the-air demonstrations using existing space segment and Release 19+ 5G NTNdevelopments. Furthermore, the demonstrations will include Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning (AI/ML) concepts and algorithms to highlight their potential in optimizingthe TN/NTN convergence. Additional demonstrations will be added as soon as technology developments mature following the agile approach proposed forthis activity.The activity will seek synergies with ARTES deliverables, testbeds, hubs, and in-orbit experiments, as well as with various European and national projects that are alreadybeingbuilt-up.

title: E4EX-006 MARS ADVANCED ENTRY, DESCENT AND LANDING CAPABILITY (MEDAL) - PHASE A
description: The next European mission to land on Mars will be the Rosalind Franklin Rover mission, which relies on non-European input for key elements on the entry, descent and landing module. The rover will enter on a ballistic entry with no additional means for precision landing. Increase in mass and precision of future Mars surface missions in the coming decades is a strategic capability for Europe, as outlined in the Explore2040 strategy implementation roadmap. To achieve this ambition, Europe must advance developments of guided entry landers and their associated technologies, avoiding technological dead ends as the capability progresses. The Mars surface lander that is the subject of this study will target a high precision landing (2-7 km major axis), which could be the first in a roadmap of increasingly precise and heavier landers, eventually aiming for a pinpoint landing accuracy of a few 10s of metres.The objectives of this activity are to:- demonstrate the technical and programmatic feasibility (Phase A) of the first mission thatwill utilise an advanced entry descent and landing capability on Mars. Advanced entry,decent and landing (EDL) is defined as a capability toland on Mars with a higher level ofmass, guidance and precision than will have been achieved in Europe following the landingof Rosalind Franklin and includes fully European critical technologies.- assess a sustainable roadmap of technology developments suitable for increased precisionand mass landings on Mars in future missions, to avoid technological gaps and dead ends.

title: FLIGHT DYNAMICS AND PRECISE NAVIGATION SUPPORT SERVICES
description: The RFP covers the activities to be executed, and the deliverables required by the European Space Agency in relation to Flight Dynamics and Navigation Services.The Flight Dynamics Division (OPS-GF) provides Mission Analysis, Flight Dynamics and Precise Navigation end-to-end solutions to ESA and 3rd party space projects. The provision of these solutions relies on infrastructure and mission specific systems also falling under the Division's responsibility. To provide the above solutions, the Flight Dynamics Division relies on Flight Dynamics operations engineering services procured from European Industry. The responsibility for the provision of these services to the Agency lies with the respective consortia.This RFP specifies all services to be provided for the Flight Dynamics Division. The services are broken down in 5 Work Packages: WP 1 EO - Earth Observation Missions WP 2 GFF - Test and Validation and System WP 3 MDDE - Mission Design and S/C Dynamics Estimation WP 4 TADC - Trajectory Analysis and S/C Dynamics Control WP 5 NAV - Precise NavigationThe definition of the required services is based on the current knowledge on the required activities for the different missions/projects and work packages. It needs to be understood that the requirements may be subject to changes depending on several driving factors such as launch dates, spacecraft, and ground segment performance, changing user/science requirements etc.The RFP covers all services and tasks to be performed by the Service Provider.

title: ADAPTIVE FOREST MANAGEMENT: RESILIENCE AND REGROWTH EXPRO+
description: The Adaptive Forest Management (AFM) project will be awarded for the execution of two activities - AFM Resilience and AFM Regrowth.The first contract of AFM - AFM Resilience - is dedicated to advancing our understanding of forest resilience, pioneering EO methods to map indicators that show the capacity of forest ecosystems to withstand, adapt, and reorganize following gradual climatic changes and abrupt disturbances. AFM Resilience targets international and EU policy frameworks, supporting them with approaches for the estimation and mapping of current and future resilience of Europe's forests.The second contract of AFM - AFM Regrowth - focuses on the monitoring and quantification of forest regrowth, supporting improved understanding of forest recovery dynamics and their contribution to being effective carbon sinks in the future. AFM Regrowth targets both policies of the EU and international/national frameworks, monitoring and analysing the post-disturbance, natural, or post-restoration trajectories of vegetation.

title: OPTIMIZED NITROGEN-VACANCY CENTERS DIAMOND SAMPLES FOR MAGNETOMETERS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a process to select and produce in an industrial way Nitrogen-vacancy centers Diamond samples for magnetometry applications.Description: Magnetic field measurements from low Earth orbit are important for understanding Earth's magnetosphere, monitoring of space weather, and studying geophysical processes. These measurements provide insights into solar-terrestrial interactions and help mitigate risks to both orbital infrastructure and terrestrial systems. However, classical magnetic sensors face limitations in sensitivity, long-term stability, and integrability due to size, weight, and power (SWaP) constraints of space missions. As with the onset of small platforms (i.e. cubesats), these challenges become increasingly apparent. With quantum sensing technologies emerging as a transformative solution for future Earth Observation missions. One particularly promising platform is quantum magnetic field sensors based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond. Their unique electronic and spin properties enable scalar and vector magnetometry with high theoretical sensitivity, robustness, radiation hardness, and potential for miniaturization make them anideal candidate for space applications. NV-based sensors combine the advantages of high performance and integrability, offering an alternative to overcome the limitations of classical sensors. Despite these benefits, quantum sensors still face challenges such as the need for further power consumption optimization, noise suppression, and integration into spacecraft systems.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Literature review on NV centre generation - Development of samples based on EO needs - Characterisation testing - Process review for large manufacturing of NV samples.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: PARAMETERS AFFECTING RF CORONA BREAKDOWN - EXPRO PLUS - RE-ISSUE
description: To develop and test analytical models and RF breadboards that allow identifying the parameters influencing Corona breakdown effect.DescriptionGas discharge or Corona breakdown is becoming more and more a serious threat to spacemissions. In the event of Corona, the loss of the whole RF chain is unavoidable and this type ofdischarge can completely volatilize the RF chai. Therefore, a number of space missions have beenalready lost due to this effect.The destructive phenomena appears when, once in orbit, the RF component is not properly vented,the materials outgass excessively or in launchers and re-entry vehicles where there is a fast processof depressurization/pressurization. To address this, it is necessary to determine all the parameters playing a role in the development of the breakdown and its' contribution in the amplitude of the discharge. Some of these parameters are the type of gas, the actual pressure, temperature, RF power and RF signal characteristics (CW, modulated, etc..). Further conditions will have to be addressed during the first phase of the investigation.Unfortunately, there is no standard reference document to be used when assessing or testing Corona breakdown. In fact, one of the main concerns within the scientific community is the lack of defined design and test margins. In order to generate such document, a list of parameters affecting Corona need to be addressed in an exhaustive activity which, includes not only analysis but also supporting testing. Description: To develop and test analytical models and RF breadboards that allow identifying the parameters influencing Corona breakdown effect.DescriptionGas discharge or Corona breakdown is becoming more and more a serious threat to spacemissions. In the event of Corona, the loss of the whole RF chain is unavoidable and this type ofdischarge can completely volatilize the RF chai. Therefore, a number of space missions have beenalready lost due to this effect.The destructive phenomena appears when, once in orbit, the RF component is not properly vented,the materials outgass excessively or in launchers and re-entry vehicles where there is a fast processof depressurization/pressurization. To address this, it is necessary to determine all the parameters playing a role in the development of the breakdown and its' contribution in the amplitude of the discharge. Some of these parameters are the type of gas, the actual pressure, temperature, RF power and RF signal characteristics (CW, modulated, etc..). Further conditions will have to be addressed during the first phase of the investigation.Unfortunately, there is no standard reference document to be used when assessing or testing Corona breakdown. title: SATELLITE COMMUNICATION TEST-BED ON-BOARD THE INTERNATIONAL SPACE STATION (ARTES AT 3A.118) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST) RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop, deploy and operate a flexible software-defined radio communication testbedwith a frequency flexible RF front end on the International Space Station, supporting a wide range of frequencies up to Q/V band addressing 5G, signal processing and advanced techniques. Targeted Improvements: Enabling innovative and fast developments of future satcom applications from UHF to Q/V band that are difficult to achieve with on-ground testing only. Description: Nowadays, there isno capability to develop and test in-orbit novel satellite communications payload functionalities in an agile manner that suits thedemands and pace of industry. The current in-orbit test opportunities available as hosted payloads on larger missions take often yearstoget in-orbit data, whilst the faster pace in-orbit demonstration CubeSat missions lack the power and continuous connectivity capabilities needed for the testing of sophisticated telecommunications functions and for which testing on ground only is not sufficient. In this activity, a flexible software-defined radio communication testbed with a frequency flexible RF front will be designed,deployed on the International Space Station and operated, supporting a wide range of frequencies. The testbed will provide unprecedented capabilities in terms of (line-of-sight) exposure, processing power, high-bandwidth ground connectivity, enabling RD into newwaveforms, processing methods, 5G and connectivity scenarios. The testbed will be used to: - develop and test communication links at low elevation angles to increase availability and system capacity; - develop and test novel low power M2M/IoT techniques in representative interference conditions; - interactively develop and test interference mitigation, monitoring and localisation techniques, takinginto account low Earth orbit characteristics and low elevation angles; - develop and test air-interfaces related to 5G with the goal to enable the reuse of terrestrial hardware for space 5G nodes and - contribute to the evolution of the CCSDS payload data telemetry standard. The testbed will allow 24 months of operation for emulation of a wide range of payload functions in space, enabling rapid iterations in the development, deployment and testing. Footnote: On Delegation Requestactivities will only be initiated onthe explicit request of at least one National Delegation.

title: S2-LT-04 + S2-LT-05 DEMONSTRATION OF THE OPERATIONAL CAPABILITY, ROBUSTNESS ENHANCEMENT AND MARKET READINESS OF NETWORKED LASER DEBRIS TRACKING - EXPRO +
description: The activity aims to mature and expand the Debris Laser Tracking Network toward operational readiness and market applicability. It focuses on improving automation, system performance, product accuracy, and end-user alignment, while also addressing legal and regulatory constraints for compliant laser ranging operations, including potential ranging to active satellites.The network will be expanded by integrating at least one additional Satellite Laser Ranging station, upgraded to support debris laser ranging also during daytime, to improve station automation, and to interface with the DLTN automation framework.A coordinated observation campaign, involving end users and the ESA Laser Ranging Station, will validate the enhanced operational concepts, demonstrate improved network performance, and assess the benefits of simultaneous operations across multiple debris ranging stations. The activity will deliver technical notes, market concepts, observation data, software, and station hardware upgrades over an 18-months contract period

title: RECEIVER TECHNIQUES AND ALGORITHMS FOR PNT SOLUTIONS WITH ONLY 1 AND 2 LEO SATELLITES IN VIEW - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view, based on the optimised fusion ofall the available estimations along time.Description: The use of LEO-based systems on top of current GNSS systems (in MEO orbits) is being considered to improve the achievable user performances, in particular in challenging user scenarios. To ensure that at least3 or 4 satellites are in view by any user on ground, a much larger number of LEO satellites than for MEO is required to be used inthis case. In this context, it is of high interest to investigate techniques exploiting signals received by LEO satellites when only 1 and 2 LEO satellites are in view by a ground user. This would enable, for example, to exploit LEO satellites with reduced constellations with a limited available number of satellites visible, and/or while a full LEO-PNT constellation is still being deployed. Theobjective of this activity is to design PNT techniques and algorithms relying on only 1 and 2 LEO satellites in view,, including transitions between 1 and 2 satellites, based on the optimised fusion of all the available estimations along time, including at least:- ToA (Time-of-Arrival), FoA (Frequency-of-Arrival) and AoA (Angle-of-Arrival)-like estimations; - Multi-epoch / synthetic apertureprocessing solutions exploiting the fast satellite geometry change; and, additionally, if introducing benefits to the above : - Clock coasting; - Inertial sensors measurements; - DEM (Digital Elevation Model)/height sensors ; The suitability of the proposed solutions is aimed to be assessed based both on simulations and real data. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define and design innovative techniques and algorithms in the areas identified above; - Develop the required tools/software for the assessment/test of the innovative techniques and algorithms; - Assess/test the different techniques and algorithms in realistic simulated conditions, and with real signals from LEO satellites; - Identify the most promising techniques/algorithms based on the results obtained;- Propose the way-forward to further mature each of the promising techniques/algorithms identified.Procurement Policy: C(2) = Activities in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSI is requested. title: HIGH BANDWIDTH INTERFACE RADIATION MITIGATION IP CORE FOR PROGRAMMABLE LOGIC DEVICES (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5C.489) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to develop, implement and test a 100 Gbps class interface radiation mitigation IP core for programmable logic devices for application in Low Earth and Geostationary Orbits. This includes hardware radiation characterisation and testing. Targeted Improvements: 3 to 4 times improvement of high-speed serial link data rate (from 32 Gbps to 112 Gbps) under radiationconditions. Description: State of the art programmable logic devices have the potential to enable high throughput nodes on satellites, machine-to-machine and internet of things applications on small platforms with limited resources, and wideband RF signal identification using machine learning. Powerful devices are available but are radiation sensitive.This activity will select and characterise relevant functional blocks of a state-of-the-art COTS programmable logic device with 100 Gbps class high bandwidth interfaces. A laboratory breadboard will be developed together with electrical ground support equipment (EGSE) suitable to perform radiation characterisation including Single Event Effects (SEE), Displacement Damage (DD) and Total Ionising Dose (TID). A radiation mitigation approach shall be developed and implemented in a radiation mitigation IP core in order to compensate for identified critical performanceimpacts. The device with the radiation mitigated IP core will be radiation tested and the performance will be compared to the unmitigated hardware performance.

title: ARIEL - COOLER CONTROL ELECTRONICS (CCE) - RE-ISSUE
description: Ariel is the M4 mission in the Scientific Programme. It was adopted in November 2020 by the Science Programme Committee and is proceeding into the implementation phase, with the Spacecraft Prime contract to be kicked off by the end of 2021. Ariel will investigatethe atmospheres of many hundreds of diverse planets orbiting different types of stars to address fundamental scientific questions.Ariel is designed as a dedicated survey mission for transit and eclipse spectroscopy. Ariel observations require a specifically designed, stable payload and satellite platform with broad, instantaneous wavelength coverage extending from the visible to the infra-red (500 nm to 7.8 m). The detector technology selected to cover this wave range makes use of HgCdTe CMOS detectors. These detectors are optimised for astronomical observations, providing high Quantum Efficiency with low noise. As the cut-off wavelength of these detectors increase, these performance characteristic require operations in a colder environment. While the Ariel FGS instrument (500 nm to 1.95 m) can operate by making use of the passive cooling capabilities of the Ariel PLM (with the V-groove radiators), the AIRSinstrument (1.95 m to 7.8 m) requires further cooling down to 42 K with an active cryo-cooler. A Joule-Thomson (JT) cooler is therefore integrated in the system design and makes use of Neon as its working fluid (boiling point of 27.05 K at 1 atm). This cooler is developed by RAL (UK), under the responsibility of the UK Space Agency, within the AMC, as specified in the MLA, and builds on their experience from the Planck Helium JT cooler. This Ne JT Cooler is controlled by a warm electronic box, the CCE (Cooler Control Electronics), which is the subject of this procurement. While the cooler remains under the AMC's responsibility through UKSA and RAL(UK), the Agency, through the Ariel Project, has agreed to provide support to UKSA for the procurement of the CCE. Through this activity, the Contractor will be requested to provide the CCE, including development models as well as the Flight Model and spares. The due dates for these models range from 2022 to 2024, to secure the Ariel launch date. As well as providing the CCE unit, the contractwill cover the position sensor board, which interfaces to the CCE unit on the compressor. The contract will cover the full design and development of this CCE in line with the Ariel requirements.

title: MULTI-BAND DUAL-BEAM C-TO-Q/V SATCOM ANALOGUE BEAMFORMING INTEGRATED CIRCUIT (ARTES AT 7B.091) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a wideband analogue beamforming integrated circuit (BFIC) capable of covering the entire frequency range from Cto Q/V-band, with two beams. This BFIC will serve as a modular and scalable solution for user-terminal flat-panel arrays, enabling multi-band and multi-product compatibility.Targeted Improvements: - Frequency coverage extended from C-band to Q/V-band in a single BFIC.- Fostering high-volume production scalability and economies of scale.- Enhanced design modularity, enabling flat-panel antennas to scale in aperture size (same number of beams) and/or number of beams (same aperture).Description:Conventionally, different BFICs have been used in applications at different frequency bands, e.g., the C- to Q/V-bands relevant to satcom. Also, such conventional BFICs typically generate a single beam. To enable the use of thesame BFIC in a broad range of satcom products, this activity will develop a next-generation dual-beam analogue BFIC with wideband coverage from C- to Q/V-band. Thus, the envisioned BFIC will serve as a fundamental building block for future flat-panel antenna arrays, supporting scalable designs by allowing additional BFICs to be integrated based on performance requirements. The development of this BFIC shall leverage insights from recent state-of-the-art wideband single-/dual-beam BFICs, such as the C- to Ka-band BFICs, which are developed outside ESA Member States. These contributions highlight the growing industry demand for multi-beam and frequency-agnostic BFIC solutions, which can reduce system complexity and accelerate product development, with the potential for higher volumeproduction in comparison to single-band BFICs. Therefore, the envisioned BFIC will cover the entire C- to Q/V-band range and generatetwo beams, which will enable its reuse across multiple product lines and reduce the need for band-specific BFICs. The design willemphasise performance consistency across the wide frequency range, minimising variations in gain, noise figure, and linearity.Additionally, the activity will assess the thermal and power consumption challenges associated with multi-beam and broadband analogue BFICs at millimetre-wave frequencies, ensuring that the proposed solution is viable for both low- and high-end satcom applications. Successful execution will position Europe as a leader in wideband BFICs, securing our competitiveness in the evolving satcom ecosystem. The wideband analogue BFIC will be tested against DVB-S2/S2X or 5G-NR waveform in a relevant environment.

title: INTELLIGENT SIGNAL MONITORING UNIT FOR PAYLOAD EQUIPMENT AUTONOMY, HEALTH MONITORING, AND RECONFIGURATION (ARTES AT 5C.530) - EXPRO PLUS (RE-ISSUE)
description: The objective of the activity is to design, build and test a monitoring unit and associated testbed capable of executingalgorithms, including but not limited to Artificial Intelligence (AI), in real time, to monitor signal and telemetries of RF payloads, trigger autonomous reconfiguration and raise alerts to future autonomous satellites or simply to ground.Targeted Improvements:The operation of constellations requires efficient management of payload performance, health monitoring and reconfiguration when necessary. Current on-board signal monitoring is limited to low frequency telemetries, like temperature readings, avionics telemetriesor health flags, which is not sufficient for autonomous monitoring satellite communication payloads. Closed-loop monitoring of analogue-to-digital converters that interface with antenna calibration channels, beamforming calibration, interference detection, clock monitoring units and other high frequency telemetries is required. These applications are challenging because of the high data ratesand the difficulty of processing radio frequencysignals. Additionally, these algorithms need to run on-board, because of the number of satellites in constellations and the volume of telemetry data.Advances in monitoring algorithms are becoming more mature, for example adapting beamforming coefficients automatically to improve transmission when interferences or failures occur at module or instrument level and initiating a reconfiguration before equipment breaks down, which demonstrate the viability of the concept and together with the progress in more efficient processors and FPGAs, the execution of such algorithms on-board is possible.This activitywill study monitoring algorithms, including convolutional and recurrent neural networks, for broadband payload architectures and develop an intelligent monitoring unit (ISMU) breadboard. The ISMU shall be compatible to the required signal bandwidth and input RF lanes and autonomously trigger mode change or recalibration when a performance drop, health degradation, external interference or failure is detected. Finally, a combined hardware and software testbed will be developed, capable to assess the monitoring andautonomous reconfiguration capabilities, and measure the performance improvements achieved in overall Quality of Service (QoS).

title: ATTITUDE AND ORBIT CONTROL SYSTEM FOR SATELLITE OPTICAL COMMUNICATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 4C.070) RE-ISSUE
description: Objective:The objective of the activity is to develop an attitude and orbit control system (AOCS) dedicated to the pointing accuracy requirements of optical and quantum communications systems. Targeted are non-geostationary platforms to achieve highly accurate pointing as needed for inter-satellite and satellite-to-ground links.Targeted Improvements:Tenfold improvement of attitude control and pointing/tracking accuracy from non-geostationary satellites to enable optical and quantum communications.Description:Fornon-geostationary satellites, body pointing is a possible technique to achieve the required coverage, however the accuracy requirements for optical communications are more stringent than the current state-of-art, especially for quantum communications because of link budget constraints. This activity will develop a new attitude and orbit control system (AOCS) system for optical and quantum communications. Developments will be carried out addressing the selected coarse-pointing approach as well as the required control electronics. The main engineering tasks include the trade-off of coarse pointing approaches, considering platform limitations and opticaltelescope requirements, development of a AOCS prototype and the control software and electronics required to accurately point and track the optical beam with quasi-hemispherical field-of-regard.

title: EXPERIMENTAL VERIFICATION OF PARTICLE CONTAMINATION REDISTRIBUTION DURING LAUNCH EXPRO PLUS - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: To manufacture representative fairing mock-ups and perform test campaigns to understand particle contamination redistribution during launch and provide inputs for modelling software.Description: There is currently no possibility to quantify the particle contamination of spacecraft from encapsulation under fairing until separation in space. The current assumptions for the associated allocation are coming from launch service providers and are based on analyses. The considered budgets are significant and are representing, for contamination sensitive missions, most of the total allocation. Consequently, important operational constraints are imposed during the spacecraft MAIT to be able to sustain such contamination levels without overcoming the end-of-life requirements. Thus, to adapt the operational constraints at spacecraft or at launcher level to meet the target particle cleanliness requirements, itis key to quantify properly the particle contamination induced during this step via dedicated test campaigns using representative mock-ups. The mock-ups are aimed to be used under various testing environments to allow the assessment of the particle redistributionusing adequate monitoring techniques. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Preliminary Requirements definition from various European launcher fairing design and identification of the key parameters to ensure representativeness at mock-up level; - Design and manufacturing of representative fairing mock-ups; - Identification and selection of relevant particle contamination monitoring techniques; - Environmental testing of the instrumented fairing mock-ups to characterize particle contamination redistribution; - Processing of the obtained data to be used as input for modelling tools.

title: BEYOND 5G HUB OVER-THE-AIR VERTICAL SEGMENT VALIDATIONS (ARTES 4.0 5G/6G 3F.062) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test integrated satellite-terrestrial solutions for Beyond 5G (B5G) use cases. To deliver such solutions, the activity will developsystem demonstrators that will validate B5G Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) solutions in realistic operational conditions, using over-the-air field trials.TargetedImprovements:Enabling the adoption of satellite by B5G verticals.Description: The prospect of satellite in B5G is far-reaching. B5G and in particular B5G NTN will build onthe capabilities of today s 5G networks and services, including those enabled byfuture 5G-Advanced and 6G. However, capitalising on this new opportunity will require satcom stakeholders to overcome many challenges, such as demonstrating thetechnical validity ofB5G NTN solutions under specific operational environments while fulfilling industries requirements, and understanding how to natively integrate future 6GNTN services in the operations of these industries. Building and launching B5G NTN infrastructure and services involves complex, time consuming and costly transformationalprojects at every level of satellite and terrestrial systems.To fillthis gap, this activity will develop, validate and demonstrate B5G NTN solutions for various vertical markets, including direct-to-device, IoT, automotive, transportation,maritime, health, energy, agriculture and emergency response. It will consolidate industrial requirements that will translate into the technical specifications of systemdemonstrators. Demonstrations will use existing spacesegment. The developments will leverage on leading industrial solutions and open-source technologies wheneverpossible, to support diverse requirements of market verticals, with guaranteed Quality of Service (QoS) and other connectivity enablers as required. These will coveradaptations and enhancements of edge nodes, user equipment and network implementations to integrate satellite. The resulting systems will be validated and demonstratedusing over-the-air field trials allowing the concerned verticals to verify the performance of B5G NTN in a realistic operational conditions of their use cases.The activity will seek synergies with ARTES deliverables, testbeds, hubs, and in-orbit experiments, as well as with various European and national projects that are beingdeveloped.
