title: ADVANCED VERIFICATION AND VALIDATION TECHNIQUES FOR NEURAL NETWORK-BASED AOCS/GNC SYSTEMS EXPRO+
description: Objective:The objective of this activity is to ensure the compatibility of machine learning augmented AOCS/GNC systemswith the stringent flight qualification process for mission-critical applications.Description:Despite superior performance exhibited, neural networks still lack performance reliability, robustness,efficiency and explainability. This raises concerns for adoption in mission-critical space applications, imposingthe need for development of verification and validation (VV) tools to verify desirable properties for neuralnetworks-based space control system, such as robustness to unforeseen conditions. Neural networkverification refers to the problem of verifying whether the output of a neural network satisfies certain propertiesfor a bounded set of input perturbations. Important as well is the problem of learning neural networks thatcertifiably meet certain specifications on desired input-output behaviours.Potential solutions to those issues are the use of convex optimization for Neural networks, applying smoothapproximations of the nonlinear activation functions can make the problems tractable without loss ofconservatism. System robustness can be assessed by embedding adversarial noise and uncertaintiesensuring the output map remains bounded.A major challenge is to developand provide a series of efficient numerical verification and validation algorithmsto resolve the large-scale type of decision problems imposed by the nature of neural nets. The nature of thesealgorithms results from a trade-off between computational speed versusaccuracy. The aim is to developvarious numerical approaches with difference sampling, tiling and set approximation strategies.Inthis activity, GNC/AOCS benchmarks will be assessed for a range of neural network VV problems, focusingon the image processing and navigation functions. Furthermore, a series of numerical tools allowing to formallysolve the above VV problems shall be developed.The following tasks are foreseen for this activity:- Literature survey on VV strategies for neural network augmented GNC/AOCS systems.- Gap analysis and areas of improvement.- Definition of benchmark scenarios and requirements definition.- Trade-off justification and development of VV strategies and algorithms.- Definition of VV metrics and test plan.- Implementation on representative numerical setup.- Detailed analysis of the VV strategies and algorithms.

title: IN SITU PROPELLANT LIQUEFACTION TRANSFER AND STORAGE FOR MOON AND MARS EXPRO+
description: To define and demonstrate a scalable, modular, transportable liquefaction system to support propellant production for sustainable surface access at Moon and Mars.DescriptionSustainable exploration of the future will rely on ISRU produced propellants with the common oxidizer being Liquid Oxygen (LOX).Building on ongoing in situ resource utilization (ISRU) studies this activity focuses on the aspects necessary for the conversion of ISRU products into useful propellant.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Survey of the industrial plant and processes currently used for liquefaction, transfer and storage of candidate propellants which are obtainable in gaseous form at the Moon or Mars (oxidiser LOX and fuels LH2, LCH4, LCO) and achievable specific production rates w.r.t mass and power required- Assessment of required production rate requirements for generic tank volumes and mission cadences- Examine the alternative processes available and demonstrate a suitable scaling of the processes and hardware to meet the requirements- Define the concepts for potential flight hardware. Local environmental conditions and any unique opportunities for heat rejection tothe environment shall be considered- Trade off of the developed process based on opportunities for cost, power and mass optimisation and the relative complexity of technology development. Typically such applications require process heat rejection management for the propellant chill down. The miniaturization of this through highly compact heat exchangers in flight weight, propellant compatiblematerials shall be investigated- Down select the processes and elaborate and optimise a preliminary design, per propellant, whichshall be developed providing detailed layout/configuration and mass estimates. The baseline system shall be defined as modular and scalable supported by digital mock up and detailed process analysis/simulation- The activity shall be ultimately supported by the definition, manufacture and test of early, ground based, module level, breadboards for key technologies/processes.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF IN-SITU REAL-TIME SENSOR FOR MOLECULAR CONTAMINATION MONITORING OF FLIGHT HARDWARE - EXPRO PLUS
description: The number of future missions with higher and higher cleanliness requirements is constantlyincreasing (e.g. LISA, AEOLUS-2). Current monitoring methods for molecular contamination do onlyallow a limited representativeness with regards to the actual levels deposited on sensitive surfaces.Indeed, molecular contamination witnesses can almost never be placed close enough to the sensitive surfaces (for accessibility precautionary reasons) and cannot provide constant monitoring due to the incompatibility with some of the testing environments. Besides, measurements are performed periodically in laboratory environment and only provide punctual values, typically on monthly basis. For all these reasons, contamination measurements can only be taken as estimateand hypotheses are needed inorder to evaluate the levels on sensitive surfaces. This situationbecomes critical for highly sensitive items and clearly the morestringent are the requirements, thehigher risks are undertaken.Having the capability to perform in-situ real-time monitoring of the molecular contaminationdeposited on sensitive surfaces will allow to determine the actual contamination levels and to identify which phases are the most critical. Such a technology will contribute to ensure that the instrument performance will be met and will provide the capability to quickly implement mitigation actions if contamination levels increase unexpectedly. In addition, the use of this technology can be extended in flight. Operation in-flight will allow the optimization of the commissioning anddecontamination phases, thus ensuring optimal performances while maximizing instrumentavailability during the mission.Currently, two technologies are considered for the development of such a sensor, either based onOptical Micro-Electro-Mechanical-System or on micro-wave transduction.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Design definition considering the operational constraints- Manufacturingof breadboard to experimentally assess the suitability of the selected technology and its robustness against typical environment- Definition of a test plan and implementation of the associated test campaign laboratoryenvironment to determine the evaluated system performance- Identification of the required steps to manufacture a qualification unit for in-flight operationProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: ADAPTIVE OPTICAL LENSES FOR COMPACT OPTICAL CORRECTIONS IN SMALL SATELLITE PAYLOADS - EXPRO PLUS
description: One of the challenges facing many compact optical payloads (imaging, spectrographic, Lidar, etc.) is identifying ways to maintain performance whilereducing the payload size and power that they can fit on ever-smaller satellite platforms. Active correction systems for medium or large size instruments aremainly based on deformable mirrors (either primary mirror or conjugate of the entrance pupil on the instrument). These are very efficient correction tools butmay require a volume and power not compatible with smaller payloads such as small or nano satellites.An alternative to this approach is the use of adaptive lenses which can be implemented inside the optical layout without need for e.g. high-quality pupilreimaging. Adaptive lenses have achieved a good level of maturity in on-ground applications (e.g. microscopy, beam shaping, telescope systems, etc.) but haveyet to be considered for space applications. By nature, the COTS aspect of adaptive lenses would allow to use them for mass-produced nano or small satellites at a competitive price. The correction abilities could range from compensation of thermo-elastic deformation affecting image quality (low-order aberrations), to line-of-sight compensation of thermally-induced drifts, to staring function implementation allowing to compensate satellite motion to increase integration time.The proposed activity aims at developing an engineering model of an adaptive optical lens suitable for compact instruments for small satellites. The adaptivelens will be analysed in terms of components and materials to adapt them to the space environment, in particular, interfaces to the payload, space radiation andvacuum. The following tasks are foreseen in the frame of this activity: Identification of a target payload and platform and the consolidation of requirements for an optical payload. Analysis of changes required to the existing product (drive electronics and adaptive lens). Breadboarding and testing of materials to identify sensitivity to radiation and vacuum environments. Detailed design of the adaptive optical lens engineering model. Manufacturing of the engineering model. Verification and testing in a relevant environment including in a complete telescope set-up.

title: THERMAL CONTROL FOR LUNAR NIGHT SURVIVAL - EXPRO PLUS (E3CX-039)
description: This activity aims to validate a thermal and power management system capable of supporting infrastructure elements through the harsh conditions of the lunar environmentspecifically the temperature excursions between day and night at various latitudes.The use case centers on operating an atomic clock on the lunar surface (Lunar Time pathfinder - in close cooperation with NAV), a high-precision system essential for future navigation, synchronisation, and autonomous operations. Its continuous function requires tight thermal stability and uninterrupted power, making it an ideal benchmark for stress-testing survival capabilities.By demonstrating that wecan sustain such a system through a full lunar day/night cycle, we directly de-risk a key challenge in long-duration surface missions. The outcome would be a proven solution for maintaining critical assets in lunar night conditions, laying the groundwork for scalable infrastructure and long-term presence on the Moon.

title: [C207-026EP] ADVANCED LOW FREQUENCY ELECTRIC FIELD PRE-VERIFICATION METHOD
description: In the frame of the CTP of '' Pre-Verification of THOR Electro Magnetic Cleanliness Approach'' (ref.: C207-020FM) the above listed problems have been already investigated but extensive validation of the simulation tool has not taken place yet. Therefore, in orderto identify and further decrease the remaining uncertainty of the method established for THOR, the tasks mentioned below under ''task list'' are proposed.Task list:- Extensive validation of the tool by utilizing various on-ground and/or in-flight test data. Theobjective is to identify the remaining uncertainty in the low frequency range of 0.1 Hz - 10 MHz.- Establish unit level conducted emission characterisation method that is more suitable for the analysis. Also consider to utilize radiated emission data from harnesses (and units) that are characterised by alternative methods, e.g. reverberation chamber or TEM cells. The objective is to feed thesimulator with inputs that is more suitable for system level analysis than the existing unit level results tested by standard methods.- Implement a method that is capable to remove the facility impact from the model and predict the in-space performance.- Study well established electromagnetic simulation methods, with focus on effectiveness for harness (e.g. method of moments) and implement it in the model.- Assess the correlation of the electric fields with the associated magnetic fields that are typically dominating at these low frequencies and summarize the characteristics of the effective wave impedance.The newly developed test and analyses methods from this activity could be utilised on Plasma Observatory units as an addition to the standard methods.A pre-verification method with the targeted improvements will be important for all next generation missions that carries instruments that are sensitive toelectric fields below 10MHz like the in-situ plasma instrumentation of Plasma Observatory or M-Matisse or the ground penetrating radar of EnVision (SRS) but already flying missions would have benefitted from it like RPWI and RIME of JUICE or RPW-ANT of Solar Orbiter.

title: ON-BOARD EVENT-BASED DEBRIS DETECTION AND COLLISION AVOIDANCE FOR LEO SATELLITES EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective:To develop an on-board system for autonomous, real-time debris detection, tracking, and avoidance using amulti-sensory payload.Description:The growing presence of space debris in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) threatens satellite operations and spacesustainability. Small, fast-moving debris is difficult to detect yet capable of inflicting significant damage. Current avoidance strategies heavily depend on ground-based tracking and human-in-the-loop decisions, which can be slow and constrained by communication delays. This proposed activity builds upon a precursory ESAactivity NEU4SST - Neuromorphic Processing for Space Surveillance and Tracking, which produced valuable insights and a limited dataset. This dataset however was generated with a ground-based sensing focus and lacks realism, metadata richness, and orbital context required for space-borne applications.The aim of this activity is to demonstrate autonomous collision avoidance capabilities through real-time spacedebris detection and avoidance in LEO using event-based datafusion. To achieve this, this activity will develop a realistic, high-fidelity simulated dataset that mimics the operational environment of a spacecraft equipped with an event-based camera and navigation sensors (GNSS, IMU). This includes dynamic scenes with sub-10 cm debris, representative lighting conditions, orbital motion, and synchronized multi-sensor outputs. This dataset will be used tovalidate real-time detection, tracking, and collision avoidance algorithms based on Machine Learning. Edge-based processing algorithms will be demonstrated running on representative space grade or space-relevant embedded hardware platforms to evaluate their performance and feasibility under hardware constraints. In addition to the simulation-based prototype, the activity will develop a testbed prototype that integrates a physical event-based camera with a processing unit capable of executing the developed algorithms. Thissetup will allow demonstration of key capabilities, including object detection, data fusion, andautonomous decision-making.Thisactivity encompasses the following tasks:- Design and implement an on-board autonomy architecture using an event-based optical camera to enable decentralized decision-making for collision avoidance across spacecraft.- Develop edge-based processing algorithms for real-time debris detection and tracking, leveraging simulatedand semi-simulated datasets from the on-board sensory suite to estimate debris size, assess conjunction risk,trigger alerts and to optimize autonomous manoeuvres.- Implement on-board autonomous conjunction risk assessment and collision avoidance manoeuvre planning,including demonstration of the system on low-power space-grade/space-relevant hardware to evaluateperformance and reliability in constrained environments.- Simulate and validate high-fidelity LEO scenarios in controlled lab environments, including variable debrisdensities, orbital regimes, and dynamic interaction scenarios,tobenchmark system performance underrealistic operational conditions.Deliverables: Prototype, ReportsThis activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

Description: Objective:To develop an on-board system for autonomous, real-time debris detection, tracking, and avoidance using amulti-sensory payload.Description:The growing presence of space debris in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) threatens satellite operations and spacesustainability. Small, fast-moving debris is difficult to detect yet capable of inflicting significant damage. Current avoidance strategies heavily depend on ground-based tracking and human-in-the-loop decisions, which can be slow and constrained by communication delays. This proposed activity builds upon a precursory ESAactivity NEU4SST - Neuromorphic Processing for Space Surveillance and Tracking, which produced valuable insights and a limited dataset. This dataset however was generated with a ground-based sensing focus and lacks realism, metadata richness, and orbital context required for space-borne applications.The aim of this activity is to demonstrate autonomous collision avoidance capabilities through real-time spacedebris detection and avoidance in LEO using event-based datafusion. To achieve this, this activity will develop a realistic, high-fidelity simulated dataset that mimics the operational environment of a spacecraft equipped with an event-based camera and navigation sensors (GNSS, IMU). This includes dynamic scenes with sub-10 cm debris, representative lighting conditions, orbital motion, and synchronized multi-sensor outputs. This dataset will be used tovalidate real-time detection, tracking, and collision avoidance algorithms based on Machine Learning. Edge-based processing algorithms will be demonstrated running on representative space grade or space-relevant embedded hardware platforms to evaluate their performance and feasibility under hardware constraints. In addition to the simulation-based prototype, the activity will develop a testbed prototype that integrates a physical event-based camera with a processing unit capable of executing the developed algorithms. Thissetup will allow demonstration of key capabilities, including object detection, data fusion, andautonomous decision-making.Thisactivity encompasses the following tasks:- Design and implement an on-board autonomy architecture using an event-based optical camera to enable decentralized decision-making for collision avoidance across spacecraft.- Develop edge-based processing algorithms for real-time debris detection and tracking, leveraging simulatedand semi-simulated datasets from the on-board sensory suite to estimate debris size, assess conjunction risk,trigger alerts and to optimize autonomous manoeuvres.- Implement on-board autonomous conjunction risk assessment and collision avoidance manoeuvre planning,including demonstration of the system on low-power space-grade/space-relevant hardware to evaluateperformance and reliability in constrained environments.- Simulate and validate high-fidelity LEO scenarios in controlled lab environments, including variable debrisdensities, orbital regimes, and dynamic interaction scenarios,tobenchmark system performance underrealistic operational conditions.Deliverables: Prototype, ReportsThis activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: PROCUREMENT OF THE LISA CHARGE MANAGEMENT DEVICE
description: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is the first space mission designed to observe theuniverse via gravitational waves, ripples in the fabric of space time caused by the acceleration ofmassive objects in the universe. The LISA observatory consists of three identical spacecraft (eachwith a mass/power of about 2700Kg/>3kW), forming an equilateral triangular constellation of 2.5million km side-length, in trailing or leading orbit with respect to the Earth at about 50 million km. Thepassage of a gravitational wave results in a modulation of the length of one arm with respect toanother, which is detected using laser interferometry.ESA is responsible for the mission, including procurement of the spacecraft and the launch vehicletogether with the development of the ground segment to control and operate the spacecraft (fromthe Mission Operation Centre - MOC) and to perform the science mission planning and process thedata products, including archiving (from the Science Operation Centre - SOC). The ESA MemberStates and NASA contribute to the mission with several payload elements (ESA CFI to the Prime).ESA has also the overall responsibility of the verification of the mission performance.The Charge Management Device (CMD) is part of the Gravitational Reference Sensor System(GRS). The Gravitational Reference System (GRS) is built on heritage from LPF, with adaptationsto implement the lessons learnt. The GRS contains test masses that act as fiducial points of theinterferometer. To achieve the LISA stringent requirements on measurement sensitivity, the TestMasses must be kept free of charge to avoid acceleration noise from cosmic rays and electric fieldinteractions, which would compromise measurement sensitivity at low frequencies. LISA thereforeuses the CMD that employs ultraviolet (UV) light via thephotoelectric effect to discharge the TestMasses, a technique successfully demonstrated during the LISA Pathfinder mission.For each spacecraft, the Charge Management Device (CMD) consists of UV LEDs and associatedcontrol electronics.The Executive believes it prudent to take action now to limit any potential damage to the Programmestemming from the unstable situation with NASA. Acknowledging the urgency of the situation, theSPC has requested the Executive to investigate European industrial solutions. This paper outlinesthe approach being taken by the Executive to fulfil this action.Even though there have not been specific technology developmentactivities on the LISA CMD, thehardware, designed and developed by the Imperial College London (UK) for the LISA Pathfindermission constitutes relevant heritage; additionally, the technology behind a charge managementsystem is less challenging than that of theTelescope and the Laser; henceforth the Executive isconfident that there are several European suppliers capable to design and procure the LISA CMDsas per project needs.The cost target indicated in this paper is derived from comparable commercial units, including theseries production factor, in common with other LISA electronics units. It is expected that TRL 6 canbe achieved in the second half of 2027.The Executive intends to proceed with the release of an open, competitive tendering for the provisionof the Charge Management Device for the three LISA spacecraft, with three different contractualphases to be activated according to the evolution of the geopolitical scenario: Phase 1 ending with the PDR expected in 2027. (The activity may be stopped at this pointand transferred under national funding.) Phase 2 ending at the delivery of the Qualification Model (TRL8) expected in 2029 Phase 3 ending at the delivery of the Flight HW for one spacecraft (activation of the Phase 3foreseen at the end of 2028) expected in 2031 Phase4 ending at the delivery of the hardware for the 3 spacecraft (activation of the Phase4 foreseen at the end of 2028, but possible also later if required).The Executive would like to highlight that the above phasing should not be interpreted as rigidlyconsequential, e.g. Phase 3 can be activated prior to completion of phase 2. The approach is aimedat positioning the European industry to produce flight hardware at contained risk from 2029 (as TRL8achieved) and safeguard the overall LISA schedule:The envisaged timescale for the present procurement is as follows: 24 September IPC Procurement Proposal approval Sep 2025 ITT preparation and release Oct/Nov 2025 Bid preparation Dec 2025, endorsement by Special SPC Dec 25/Jan 2026 Bid evaluation Feb/Mar 2026 Contract Proposal approval at IPC Mar/Apr 2026 Negotiations and contract KOGiven the advanced status of the project and the urgency of the procurement actions, nospecific geographical return distribution requirements will be set. However, the ITT will includea preference clause for under returned countries in the Science Programme. In addition, theTenderers will be requested to favour the participation of SMEs and Midcaps in their consortium anddemonstrate pursuing such involvement by using e.g. esa-star communication features, RFIs orother means.ACTION REQUIREDThe IPC is invited to approve the initiation of competitive tendering for the procurement of the LISACharge Management Device.

title: MONITORING, STATISTICS AND REPORTING SERVICE (MSRSER)
description: The proposed Monitoring, Statistics and Reporting Service is part of the second element of a set of procurement actions planned to progressively implement the Earth Observation Framework for the EO Science Missions (EOF-EOS). The Service will provide a holistic view of the entire EOF-EOS by monitoring system performances and providing quantitative elements to drive optimal resources allocation, enhance user experience, support mission operations coordination and facilitate proactive problem resolution. More specifically, this service will provide valuable insight on the dataflow throughout the entire EOF-EOS, including data rate and volumes, as well as on the level of utilised resources and on the overall "health" status of operational set-up exposing a comprehensive understandingof the EOF-EOS to operational actors as well as decision-makers potentially triggering targeted actions and service quality improvements. It will include a set-up, operations and continuous evolution of the Service and ensure exposing EOF-EOS metrics and information at different levels of aggregation customised to the user needs. The Contract is planned to be kicked off by Q3 2026 for a nominal duration of 3 years and with the possibility to further extend for one year to ensure continuity with the follow-up procurement.

title: SPACE DEBRIS COMPLIANT MICROSATELLITE PLATFORM FOR LARGE SATCOM CONSTELLATIONS (ARTES AT 4A.104) - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of this activity is to design, develop, manufacture and test a new microsatellite platform suitable for large satcom constellations, in compliance to ESA's space debris mitigation requirements.Targeted Improvements:- Achieve compliance to evolving space debris mitigation requirements, including in passivation, timely and reliable deorbiting, and sustainable operations.- Reduce the overall system complexity of a constellation implementation by 30% in comparison to using existing nanosatellite designsActivity Description: Over the past years, the market has seen a consistent and considerable increase in large nanosatellite constellations for telecommunications. A large amount of these satellites are built to the cubesat standard (or variations of it). This largeincrease of orbiting space assets has raised concerns on the sustainable use of space and as a result many space organisations and nations have taken a proactive step. In particular, the European Space Agency recently released an update on the Space Debris policy, posing more stringent requirements for the design and operation of satellites, which current nanosatellites were not designed to be complaint with. Additionally, the CubeSat standard was not developed to facilitate mass manufacture, and assembling, integrating and testing CubeSats is often a time consuming, challenging process involving many manual steps.This activity will create a platform design comprising, structure and core avionics compliant to the ESA Space debris mitigation requirements (ESSB-ST-U-007) as well as optimised for cost effective mass production. The platform does not necessarily need to adhere to the existing CubeSat standard; however, compatibility is an advantage. If the platform developed is not compatible with existing cubesat deployers, a complementary deployment system has to be proposed. The development and testing on the breadboard should show the reduction in AIT effort and the estimations on the production time should be calculated to show the potential for mass manufacture. An Engineering Model of the nanosat platform (i.e. structure and core avionics) and its corresponding deployment system will be designed, manufactured and tested inenvironmental and radiation representative conditions to demonstrate core functionality and required reliability. The activity willalso develop a Product Assurance and Quality Assurance plan, a manufacturing plan and an appropriate tailoring to the ECSS that demonstrates future compliance to the functional and space debris mitigation requirements.

title: GENERIC CADU PROCESSOR FOR THE COPERNICUS EXPANSION MISSIONS
description: As part of the Copernicus programme, the Copernicus Expansion (COPEX) missions are designed to enhance and expand the capabilities of the Sentinels first generation missions to address EU policy and gaps in Copernicus user needs.In this context, ESA intends to initiate the development of the operational instrument data processors (COPEX-DP), allowing to generate the specific Level-0 and Level-1 data for each Copernicus Expansion Mission, to be integrated and operated as part of the Copernicus Missions, Data and Operations Management Framework (EOF-CSC).The COPEX-DP development will adhere to the principles of the ESA Copernicus Earth Observation Processor Framework (EOPF) and to the principles of harmonisation, open source and flexibility, as well as native compatibility with cloud-based environments. More specifically, the COPEX-DP development will target the processing scalability and adaptability as well to future technological advancements (e.g., GPU, HPC, etc) to face the performance challenges introduced by the COPEX Missions in terms of data volumes and processing complexity.In this context, the European Space Agency (ESA) announces the intended ITT for the development of a Generic Channel Access Data Unit (CADU) Processor for the Copernicus Expansion Missions, including the validationwith simulated and real satellite data and potential evolutions during the Space Segment development phases. The output of the CADUProcessor will serve as input to the operational Level-0 processors for each COPEX mission. The activity is intended to cover the processors development activities as well as an optional maintenance and evolution phase possibly covering up to the end of the satellite commissioning phase for each COPEX mission.This ITT is part of a comprehensive procurement strategy involving six open competitive tenders for the COPEX-DP development, including:-A Generic CADU Processor development (scope of this ITT)-A separated ITT for the specialised Level-0 and Level-1 operational processors development for each of the following missions: CRISTAL, LSTM, ROSE-L,CIMR, CHIME. These ITTs are planned to be issued gradually between 2024 (CRISTAL) and 2026. Intended ITTs will be published accordingly in due time

title: 6G NETWORK EMULATOR FOR NON-GEOSTATIONARY SATELLITE CONSTELLATION (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.043) - EXPRO PLUS - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to design, develop, and test a software-based demonstrator that shall allow to perform comprehensive trade-offs among new 6G network features optimised and adapted to NGSO systems.Targeted Improvements:Enable the network topology and protocol stack functional split of 6G Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) systemsDescription: In the frame of Low Earth Orbit based 5G systems, it has been highlighted that the 5G gNodeB protocol functions and the available splits (e.g., the Centralised Unit,the Distributed Unit, and the Radio Unit) have not been optimised for such Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) systems, where very particular architectural characteristics, mobility aspects, latency constraints, and on-board hardware are determining some limitations.The activity shall design, develop, and test a software-based demonstrator to allow for comprehensive trade-offs analysis between the whole range of new possible concepts for regenerative payload, allowing 6G access node functionalities from space. The activitywill- critically review the current 5G protocol stack split and highlight the main constraints over NGSO systems;- investigate alternative network topologies and protocol stack optimisation to overcome these NTN limitations;- identify the proper packet/networksimulator and the specific technical requirements;- implement and test this intended software tool;- evaluate the main beneficialimpacts of the new 6G NTN architecture and network functions. title: SPACE PACKAGING FOR LARGE FORMAT CMOS IMAGE SENSOR - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop large format detector packaging solutions compatible with space constraints and requirements. A technology development model shall be manufactured based on an existing large format CMOS image sensor and environmental testing performed.DescriptionTheuse of high performance, custom developed images sensors in Space Missions is of paramount importance for fulfilling the mission objectives. The trend in the commercial market is to develop products of increased resolution and performance by moving to detectors with smaller pixels and bigger formats. Such increase in format is also attractive for space instruments, however, in space applications the challenges in capturing images are not in line with the use of small scale pixels. Large pixels offer the advantage of high full-well capacity and eventually devices of high dynamic range. This combination of high resolution and big pixels drives the technology to large format detectors.One of the challenges in developing large format detectors for Space, is the packaging and the necessary qualifications of the packaging process to be compatible for operation in Space. Especially when such service is not availablein-house the Foundry where the detector wafers are manufactured, the need to establish such capability is very important.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of requirements (Technical, PA/QA)- Selection of test vehicle and pre-packaging electro-optical testing- Design of a custom package (if needed)- Packaging process development including PID (Product Identification Document), management of the cleanliness and ESD- Development of screening procedures and Lot Acceptance Test procedures- Packagingof appropriate number of samples, Electro-optical testing and evaluation testing according to Test Plan- Application to Certification Processes (as applicable)- Preparation of next required steps towards qualification and certification

title: T811-802SD ELECTROMAGNETIC INSTRUMENT FOR NON-DESTRUCTIVE ON-ORBIT DETECTION OF MM-SIZE SPACE DEBRIS (EXPRO+)
description: Three main lines of detectors have been studied at low TRL level to detect mm-sized space debris without having to resort to destructive impact detection technologies: continuous wave radars, coincidence laser sheets, and LIDAR technologies. All of these technologies have strengths and weaknesses to reach the goal of deploying a monitoring system in debris dense regions. There is a so called "mm-size gap" where currently no dedicated measurements of the space debris population exist, but the energy upon impact with these particles can still be mission critical. It is thus required to bring down the uncertainties in this size regime. Mission proposals are being studied to close the gap, or at least demonstrate the capability of characterising the population. Promising technologies are non-destructive measurements if they succeed in creating large effective detection areas. However, precursor studies are ongoing and parallel developments have not been systematically compared and trade-off yet.This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Compare and assess the three technologies, and where possible COTS versions, w.r.t. the objective of providing a long-term monitoring capability at orbital altitudes of 800 and 500km. - Optimise detector design with regards to minimal complexity/risk/cost and maximal number of detectable particles in the mm range. - Breadboard the critical detector technologies.

title: THERMAL MODELLING OF SATELLITES FOR NON-GRAVITATIONAL FORCES TOWARDS MILLIMETER LEVEL ORBIT DETERMINATION - EXPRO PLUS
description: It has been demonstrated that knowledge of the temperature of GNSS satellites can be used fornon-gravitational forces modelling leading to improvements in orbit accuracy. The concept can beapplied to all missions requiring improving current centimeter accuracy towards millimeter level orbitdetermination, such as GENESIS-1 and Sentinel satellites. Further improvements are possible bymerging conventional thermal models (such ESA model ESARAD) with 3D solar pressure models (such ARPA in NAPEOS). Besides orbit accuracy empirical parameters become more physical leading to benefits in science. With acceleration magnitudes in the 1e-9 m/s2 order, model improvements are also beneficial for future gravimetry missions. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- data and parameter acquisition as raw telemetry readings (In the case of GNSS, for instanceusing relevant statistical models) per satellite family..-design and implementation of force models and sensing strategies;- tests on real and simulated data targeting GENESIS-1, Sentinel 6, GNSS and other missions.

title: PHOTONIC ANALOGUE TO DIGITAL CONVERSIONFOR FUTURE HIGH THROUGHPUT TELECOMMUNICATIONPAYLOADS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5F.053) EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to demonstrate analogue to digital conversion using photonic integrated circuits for high throughput telecommunication payloads.Targeted Improvements:Enable analogue to digital conversion of Ku/Ka- and Q/V-bands signals by photonic integrated devices.Description:Photonic Analog to Digital Conversion (ADC) of RF signals consists of photonicsampling and quantisation of the RF signals. Photonic sampling has been previously demonstrated at Ka-band using the subsampling technique, while photonic quantisation has been previously achieved for low frequencies but not in Ku-band and above.This activity shall develop and demonstrate (in a test-bed) direct RF to digital signal conversion by optical means at Ku/Ka band frequencies, usingsuitable Photonic Integrated Circuits (PIC). The feasibility of the extension of the frequency range to Q/V-band shall be evaluated. The main engineering developments shall include photonic ADC module design, PIC design and simulation, PIC fabrication and characterisation (two iterations), PIC package design, assembly and testing (two iterations), control board design, photonics ADC module assembly, testing and validation.

It will involve surveys and interviews across ESA Member States to evaluate awareness and adoption of best practices. title: FM SERVICES FOR HQN AND HQD
description: The current FM outsourced services contract for HQB and HQD has been extended until the move of the HQB population to the renovatedHQN, currently scheduled for March 2023. A new FM contract is therefore required for the FM operations and services in the new HQN and in HQD. This new contract will commence on 1 September 2022 prior to the formal delivery to ESA of the new HQN (scheduled for1 December 22), and therefore overlap by a minimum of seven months with the current contract as some FM operations need to be begunas from September 22 in HQN.The new HQN will have a wide range of new features. It will be a state-of-the-art sustainable buildingwith significant built-in flexibility. There will be a large conference centre that will transform HQN's capacity to host high level meetings. Associated facilities are also foreseen to welcome delegations, staff and visitors to this new working environments. New FM services will be required to support these changes including the following:The vision of the current contract was to have asingle consolidated contract for all activities but this consolidation proved its limitation and in order to have numerous proposals and , this to drive the highest performance level in a building which in many different aspects represents a paradigm shift in theprovision of the workplace in ES ,the initiating service will separate the work packages and while encouraging bidders to provide the full range of FM services also allow bids for a single, or limited number of domains. On this basis , FM initiated an open competitive with 4 different work packages: 1.Multi-Technical (optimised building performance, user comfort, building information modelling etc)2.General Services and Cleaning (cleaning, mail, heavy gang, helpdesk, VIP transport etc); 3.Catering, (including VIP service); 4.Operations of the ESA Visitor Space ShopThe companies will have the possibility to respond to one or more work packages. The analysis of the proposals will be organised by work package and combination of work packages will be considered in order to optimise the services offered by the market while ensuring the most efficient use of the Agency's resources. The final decision will therefore award from one to four different contracts.

title: G-BAND SOLID-STATE POWER AMPLIFIER - EXPRO+
description: There is currently a limited understanding of the cloud feedbacks and precipitation in climate models and numerical weather predictions, which is a major source of uncertainty. To reduce this uncertainty, a better characterization of cloud and precipitation vertical structure is required. A solution consists of combining measurements from multi-frequency radars with frequencies ranging from 10 GHz to above 200 GHz. Therefore, inclusion of G-band would be highly beneficial for retrieval of several new scientific products. The G-band radar will require a high transmitted power. The 238 GHz solid-state power amplifier has been identified as key risk areafor which early technology assessment needs to be undertaken. The activity aims to develop and test a breadboard of a solid-state power amplifier at 238 GHz based on state-of-the-art technologies providing 250 mW of saturated output power.

title: DIGITAL TWIN OF A SPACECRAFT AUTONOMOUS AND COLLABORATIVE INTELLIGENT MULTI-AGENT SYSTEM (ARTES AT 4G.050)
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, implement and test a smart digital twin that can be used to develop and testautonomous satcom building blocks and their collaborative interactions. Examples of building blocks are the onboard computer and remote terminal unit, software, power management and fault detection, isolation and recovery. The digital twin will enable the exploration of a wide range of innovative solutions for managing single or multiple hardware failures, advanced testing aspects and autonomous systems tosupport controlling the S/C.Targeted Improvements: Enabling intelligent satcom satellites and constellations by creating a digital twin tool for faster, flexible and integrated development and testing of intelligent (autonomous) satcomsystems based on multi-agent architecture, not existing today in Europe.Description: The market is continuously requesting satcom systems to improve in adaptability, resource efficiency, autonomy and fault tolerance. The introduction of intelligent satcom systems has the potential to not only improve the operational efficiency and reliability of the satellite or satellite constellation but also enhanceits ability to perform complex tasks in orbitwith minimal or no intervention from ground. To enable future intelligent satcom constellations, implementation of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) will be pivotal. The decentralised, collaborative nature of MAS allows each system to operate independently, but cooperatively, managing subsystems and components within a satellite, an entire constellation of satellites or even the complete end-to-end satcom system, including the ground segment. This will result in coordinated behaviour,optimal resource utilisation, safereconfigurability, autonomous decision-making among spacecraft, predict and manage overall system/constellation behaviour, identify and resolve potential anomalies, and support mission operations through continuous synchronisation with real-time telemetry data.This activity will develop a satellite digital twin based on a MAS architecture. The digital twin shall be designed to run in parallel with a referenced system development and shall be capable of updating itself using the reference system incoming telemetry. The digital twin shall be a digital model of a reference satellite with a refined digital model of the avionics (OBDH and AOCS/GNC). Other blocks (e.g. power, thermal management) will be modelled at higher, architecture level. The digital twin shall encompass a diagnosticmodule, for health monitoring and prognostics, including analysis of performance drifts, anomalydetection and failure prediction. The digital twin shall track the state of the spacecraft, even in conditions that differ from those anticipated at launch. The digital twin shall predict future behaviour and guide operational decisions with insight into the systems internal dynamics. It shall be able to assist in the evaluation of design and spacecraft configuration choice and trade-offs andperformances.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 shall include the development of the digital twinconcept and software architecture with a maximum budget range of 1200kE. Phase 1 output will comprise of a digital twin architecture and preliminary digital models of critical avionics blocks.- Phase 2 shall include the full development of digital models of the avionics blocks as well as diagnostic models. The remaining blocks shall be developed at architecture level with critical functions.Phase 2 output will comprise of the digital twin software beta version.

title: ERS-EO ALPSTAR PHASE A/B1 STUDY FOR A BESPOKE SAR MISSION WITH OPTIONAL ELINT (ACTIVITY 3)
description: The ALPSTAR Phase A/B1 study for a bespoke X band SAR mission, with optional ELINT capability, aims to define a technically feasible, sovereign European space segment architecture aligned with emerging user needs and the ALPSTAR federated concept. Conducted through up to two parallel industrial contracts within participating states, the study focuses on the design of a high performance SAR payload as the primary driver, including its integration on a mature platform (TRL 8-9), while assessing the feasibility, added value,and implementation impacts of incorporating an ELINT capability either as an embedded or hosted payload. The activity includes mission and system architecture definition, interface specification with the ground and federation layers, compliance with SRD and evolving MRD use cases, and evaluation of key technologies and TRL gaps. It further delivers preliminary design solutions, end to end performance considerations (including L0/L1 processing and ELINT simulation), trade offs, and a credible roadmap toward flight readiness. Outputs also encompass a comprehensive development and procurement plan, industrial organisation, launcher options, and robust ROM cost and schedule estimates for subsequent B2/C/D/E phases, ensuring decision readiness for the ALPSTAR Governance Board.

title: T711-901SD DYNAMIC LOCATION AND TIME-WINDOW UNCERTAINTIES DURING UNCONTROLLED RE-ENTRY (EXPRO+)
description: Historical data associated with the uncontrolled re-entry of satellite and rocket bodies yielded that, as a rule of thumb, the driving uncertainty of where these events take place can be linked to 20% of the remaining orbital lifetime and that there is an underlying 50% uncertainty on the drag experienced between 80 and 200 km. These uncertainties are mostly empirical and neglect any relationwith the actual object shape and resulting drag, and feature as input to design for demise envelope condition when it comes to establishing fragmentation altitude and as such influence casualty risk reduction developments. Recently satellites have started to collect data and continue operation from 200km down to re-entry, allowing the investigation of said data from Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO)missions and the re-entry predictions of re-entry experiments to define a more realistic time windows for the re-entry epochs and dynamically accounting for (at least) the solar activity indexes. Linked to this initial uncertainty is the historical data on re-entry locations and debris found on-ground, to verify the accuracy of the on-ground impact probability for uncontrolled re-entry and the empirical correcting factors based on equatorial bulge and solar activity index. The activity aims to reduce the margins on uncertainties associated with initial break-ups during atmospheric destructive re-entry by recalibrating on data gathered from VLEO missions and re-entry experiments.

title: FUTURE EARTH OBSERVATION ARCHITECTURE FOR MONITORING EARTH SYSTEM TIPPING POINTS - EXPRO PLUS
description: The European Earth Observation Ecosystem is a cross-cutting vision for the future of Space Earth Observation, leveraging across systems, missions, and programmatic elements instead of focusing on individual systems or programmes. Embedded in this framework, the activity "Future Earth Observation Architecture for Monitoring Earth System Tipping Points" will define what the European EO ecosystem should look like by 2050 to monitor and understand climate tipping dynamics. The study will consider both the critical tipping phase and the aftermath, designing capabilities to quantify and observe processes once tipping has occurred. It will identify essentialobservables, assess current EO assets and their optimisation potential, and propose new mission concepts to fill observation gaps. A key output will be a scenario-driven high-level Mission Definition Document (MDD) and action plan, detailing system requirements for both pre- and post-tipping phases. Leveraging ESA's EO Reference Architecture Blueprint and publications from the ESA Tipping Elements Project, the activity will integrate spaceborne and in-situ data to propose innovative mission designs. This work will guide stakeholders on the EO architecture needed to address cascading climate risks and resilience loss.

title: PHASE A OF SHIELD MISSION - EXPRO+
description: The SHIELD mission is aiming at the utilisation of a Sun-Earth Distant Retrograde Orbit (DRO) to enable in-situ observations of thesolar wind upstream from Earth to increase the warning time and improve the impact prediction of incoming Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) from the current about 20 min to over 200 min. Preliminary studies shows that the mission will require a constellation of 4-9 satellites to ensure that at least one satellite is sufficiently close to the Sun-Earth line to provide the required in-situ observation data.The Phase A study shall assess the overall feasibility of the mission and cover the establishment of mission implementationplans (management, engineering, and product assurance), identification of technology pre-development needs, trade-off of system andoperation concepts, derivation of technical requirement specifications and a thorough risk assessment. The procurement will be opencompetition to all industrial entities, ensuring an open competitive approach preparing further steps. Parallel contracts may be placed in case of competitive complementary proposals.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF A STANDARDISED PROCESS FOR PHOTONIC INTEGRATED CIRCUITS (PICS) AND ELECTRONICS INTEGRATION TECHNOLOGY (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5F.042) EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: To improve the level of integration between photonics and electronics circuits, which will enable performance and efficiency gains, size reduction and scalability to a high-density photonic integrated circuit (PIC)-based system with 100+ actuators.Targeted Improvements:Improvement in the system scalability (from 10s to 100s actuators per chip) to enable high-density PICs to beintegrated with driving and control mixed-signal electronics circuits. Improvement in the bandwidth of the connection between PIC and electronic circuit. BW 30 GHz is targeted.Description:Photonics Integrated Circuits (PICs) have been identified as enabling technology for future optical and photonics equipment for satellites due to their advantage of reduced SWaP and cost of equipment. Thebroad range of PIC technologies (InP, GaAs, SOI, TFLN, SiN and hybrids) is an advantage, but this variety creates a stumbling blockin implementation for space. In addition, PICs-based equipment requires a dedicated driving electronics, which will often need to operate at higher frequencies (30 GHz) and high voltage or current. This creates a particular challenge for high density PICs which may incorporate a large number of components with 100s of actuators. If we could work towards a unified photonics-electronics integration process and a suitable package assembly for all very high-density PICs, it would facilitate faster implementation of this technology. The considered photonics-electronics connectivity solutions include, but are not limited to, wire-bonds, ribbon-bonds, flip-chip, and heterodyne integration techniques. A coordinated activity is required to support primes (which have interest in all PIC platforms) as well as numerous SMEs packaging companies and European PIC foundries.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted tonon-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: T709-802GD UBIQUITOUS SECURE ACCESS TO MISSION OPERATIONS SERVICES (EXPRO+)
description: Traditionally space mission ground segment architectures are centralised with peer-to-peercommunication and data/file exchange, single commanding authority over assets, replicated privatedata stores and segregated security management per organisation. Typically, operational networksare isolated and the access by external parties is tightly controlled.Distributed Operations (DO) has becomea pressing topic in light of the COVID19 pandemic(teleworking), and in support of particular missions and stakeholders, for shared/hosted platformoperations (e.g. robotic instrument operator on a platform) or federated collaborative assetoperations (e.g. lunarrover and orbiter). This also includes federated mission planning, operationspreparation and simulation. Extended and more flexible yet secure interfacing with industry andsharing of information with external entities is therefore more necessary than ever. Thisthenpresents several security challenges for which no common solutions have yet been defined.This activity aims at building capabilities which will support mutually trusted inter-agencycollaboration and industry to provide DO services for multiple clients. To achieve this, it investigatesand designs appropriate security architectures and demonstrate the critical functions in support ofsecure DO use cases, e.g.:Federated Identity and Access Management for multi-centre operations; Public Key Infrastructures,Certification Authorities (building on emerging CCSDS Intergovernmental Credential Authority);Secure multicasting; Access Control implementation for (potentially cloud-based) distributed dataarchives; Secure Mission Operations Services including extensions to the associated CCSDSstandards; Security of new communication protocols, File Based Operations, Delay TolerantNetworking and Multi-Route / Multi-Hop communication support; Zero trust architectures includingauthenticated and encrypted software functions and services; Secureand flexible policyorchestration for multi-centre operations.

title: T709-812GS CLOUD BASED DATA RETURN IN A MULTI MISSION MULTI CLOUD PROVIDER CONTEXT (EXPRO+)
description: Today commercial cloud providers offer scalable cloud-based capabilities to transfer and process data, a problem also pertinent tospace missions. In that context, economy of scale effects as realized by cloud providers have the potential to drastically improveefficiency, performance and scalability of ground segments. Satellite science and housekeeping telemetry, typically received at ground stations distributed around the globe, is today transferred over dedicated wide area networks, before finally processed and made available to users. In addition, also auxiliary data like radio science data, in particular Delta DOR measurements shall be considered. This activity looks at the potential of cloud-based data return and distribution, enabling a cloudbased processing. Focusof this activity is, injection of data into a cloud close to a ground station. title: OPEN RADIO ACCESS NETWORK FRAMEWORK FOR THE END-TO-END MANAGEMENT OF REGENERATIVE NON-TERRESTRIAL-NETWORK ACCESS NODES (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.039)
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to enhance the existing Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) framework to support 5G/6G Non-Terrestrial-Network (NTN) payloads, while integrating the ORAN adaptations with conventional ground segment control centres.Targeted Improvements:1) Adapt the of Enhanced Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) interfaces to support Non-Terrestrial-Network (NTN) 5G/6G payload2) Improve the ORAN Transport network layer3) Enable the Integration of ORAN interfaces into the ground segment operations for system interoperability4) Enable new applications for NTN payloads.Description: Open Radio Access Network (ORAN) specifications are on the brink of reforming the 3GPP radio network fabric through the development and standardisation of open interfaces that provide vendor interoperability, disaggregation of radio protocol stack, access to Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML enabled Radio Intelligent Controllers (RICs) and a framework for Service Management and Orchestration (SMO). The complexity required for the management and optimisation of hybrid TN/NTN (terrestrial/non-terrestrial network) radio platforms, make ORAN an ideal candidate for handling mobility, resource allocation, quality of Service optimisation, multi-connectivity, and spectrum sharing amongothers.Currently a solid background exists to build upon and expand the current ORAN standards and interfaces to support the NTN regenerative payloads, the interworking between TN/NTN nodes and the open interface integration with ground segment Network Operations Centres (NOCs).To tackle the main challenges, this activity is expected to:1) Enhance ORAN architectures with respect to the deployment of optimised interfaces between ground and space.2) Support the adaptation of the ORAN application protocol and service models, to support the 5G/6G NTN payloads.3) Optimise the ORAN transport network association to support the satellite motion out of aspecific geographical area.4) Develop and test real and non-real time Radio Intelligent Controller (RIC) enabled AI/ML applications (xApps, rApps) for NTN node mobility, traffic steering, quality of serviceoptimisation and resource allocation.5) Integrate the ORAN open interfaces with a real or emulated/simulated NOC terminating the interface, to optimise the resource allocation of regenerative NTN nodes.6) Integrate the TN and NTN existing nodes under the same RIC and Service Management and Orchestration (SMO) platform.7) Deliver an end-to-end testbed that follows the OpenRAN workflow and demonstrate the performances for various scenarios with different service requirements.

title: ASSESSMENT OF ORGANIC MATERIALS AND PRODUCTS RELEASED ON ENCELADUS BY SPACECRAFTS - EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesTo develop computer simulations/models (fed by data) and predict how gases released by a spacecraft would spread across Enceladus, interact with the surface, and in turn understand to what extent they would contaminate the icy world.DescriptionBased on L4 - lander to Enceladus mission architecture, this work will create a model to predict how different organic materials carried by the lander will spread to Enceladus' surface, the source of contaminants, chemical reactants, and their interaction with the Enceladus environment (for both mono and bi-propellant).This will be done considering the different environmental conditions at the target body (i.e., solar wind plasma, magnetic field), accounting for primary mechanisms by which a neutral molecule can turn into a positively charged ion (i.e., photo-ionisation by absorption, charge exchange through collision, etc.), and the actual landing trajectory parameters planned for the mission.Previous work done on organic contamination in the frame of the former ExoMars rover mission for the MOMA (Mars Organic Molecular Analyser) and Argonauts on modelling volatile interaction on the Moon surface will also be used.

title: S2-SD-12 ROCKET BODY RE-ENTRY RISK FALCON 9 CASE STUDY - EXPRO+
description: On February 19, 2025, at around 4:46 a.m. local time, over Polish territory, in the area west of the city of Poznan, an uncontrolled re-entry into the lower layers of Earth's atmosphere occurred involving a stage of the Falcon 9 upper stage. It was followed by the fragmentation of the object and the fall of its parts to the Earth's surface over an area spanning several dozen kilometres.Fortunately, re-entry events where fragments are identified on-ground are rare and when the associate risk does not materialise, they provide a scientific opportunity. Large uncertainties on destructive re-entry physics and dynamics in the very low Earth orbit ( < 150km ) can be constrained by studying the physics associated with the fragment generation and final impact location, as demonstrated by recent studies targeting break-ups recoded by on-ground all-sky telescope systems.The activity aims to maximize the scientific return of the Falcon 9 re-entry event, without usage of proprietary information. This shall be based on constraining the impact trajectory based on available ground recordings, impact points and orbital trajectory data. The likely break-up aerothermodynamics, including ablation is to be assessed and reconstructed. The lesson learned from the analyses shall be used to draw general conclusions onthe re-entry predictability and risk associated with elongated upper stages, including past and future risk assessments for the orbital population, and educational outreach to raise awareness.

title: ADVANCED RF INTEGRATION TECHNIQUES FOR APPLICATION IN HIGHLY DENSE MILLIMETRE-WAVE ACTIVE ANTENNAS - EXPRO PLUS RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a breadboard of a millimetre-wave active array sub-module which demonstrates high integration techniques of critical RF functions. Description: High density millimetre-wave active antenna arrays, which are anticipated for future LEO missions require highly integrated RF functionality to meet the strict periodicity/lattice spacing requirements at such high frequencies. Novel techniques will be necessary to physically integrate the transmit and/or receive MMIC (Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit) with the beamforming functionality whilst managing the RF and DC interconnectivity and thermal heat dissipation issues that will result from such high integration. For such high frequency applications (V-/W-bands), RF electrical interconnections become critical, and loss should be minimised to maintain system efficiency, therefore the use of flip-chip connections or re-distribution layers, should be investigated. In addition, coupling and parasitic inductances need to be minimised to optimise electrical performance and unit to unit consistency. Careful 3D electromagnetic analysis is required to optimise the advanced RF structure performance. The proposed activity aims to develop new and novel manufacturing, packaging and advanced RF integration techniques which provide improved, highly integrated and repeatable performance for millimetre-wave active array applications. The advanced RF integration technique shall be an alternative to PCB (Printed Circuit Board) assembly technologies and could include, but not be limited to techniques such as 3D microelectronics, Fan Out Wafer Level Packaging (FOWLP), flip-chip/hot-via, antenna-inpackage, micromachining, precision additive manufacturing, etc., thereby demonstrating high performance, high integration, and miniaturisation. A breadboard shall be designed, manufactured and tested to demonstrate the electrical, mechanical and thermal aspects. The breadboard shall target a generic mm-wave application which demonstrates the integration of RF functionality in an advanced RF structure, suitable for an active antenna. Novel interconnection/packaging techniques shall only be considered and novel techniques for thermal management shall be proposed. The following tasks are foreseen in the frame of this activity: Requirements review:o Definition of application and review of requirements.o Initial design requirements identification. o Technology trade-off and down-selection. Breadboard preliminary design:o Initial demonstration of solution to meet fundamental requirements. o Preliminary manufacturing process flow definition. Breadboard detailed design and analysis:o Detailed RF and thermal performance analysis. o If deemed necessary, different test vehicles can be designed to evaluate specific performance parameters.o Detailed manufacturing process flow definition. o Definition of test and verification plan. Breadboard manufacturing and test:o Exercise of manufacturing process flows.o Assemble breadboard demonstrator and/or test vehicles.o Test against verification plan. Results analysis and evaluation.

title: MINIATURISED POWER SUPPLY FOR ARRAYS OF DETECTORS ON THE PAYLOAD - EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop a miniaturised power supply for arrays of detectors on the payload.Description: Detector arrays on Earth Observation (EO) spacecraft require a dedicated local power regulation for each of the detectors (CMOS or infrared). These local powerregulators ensure the supply of low noise voltage rails with specific sequencing and timing. New technologies such Gallium Nitride High-Electron Mobility transistor (GaN HEM FET) would allow to significantly reduce the size of such power supply hence making the complete system much more compact. This activity aims at miniaturising the DC/DC converter by using GaN FETs and Integrated Components(ICs), providing an efficient yet small converter. Moreover, the switching should be as smooth as possible to avoid synchronisationof all the supplies in a hard switching pattern (which would be detrimental for the overall power system). The overall efficiency and Electro Magnetic Compatibility (EMC) performance shall be significantly improved. Overall, the target power supply is targeted tobe 50% smaller and to have a much reduced Electromagnetic interference (EMI), allowing for improved sensor performance. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Study and trade-off of the optimum architecture (electrical, mechanical and thermal) - Breadboard of miniaturised power supply - Perform breadboard testingDeliverables: Breadboard, ReportProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: DIGITAL CONTINUITY FOR DIGITAL SPACECRAFT AND DIGITAL TWIN SPACECRAFTS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:To develop a unified and traceable data management system that enables the consistent integration of data,simulation models, and tools related to digital twin spacecraft across multiple disciplines, mission phases, and mission types. The solution shall be based on the Space System Ontology (SSO) for its semantics yet shall allow for flexibility in the mapping towards different sources and authoring tools.Description:The digital twin spacecrafts represent virtual representations of the spacecraft throughout the project lifecycle with synchronised interaction means. Examples are the digital twin spacecraft "as designed", "as built" but also "as operated". The data and information into (and out of) these digital twins come from the underlying digital spacecraft context, a federated set of databases and system information systems that capture all thespacecraft data and knowledge available. Within this eco-system, comprising and supporting variousstakeholders with different roles, digital continuity refers to the consistent andtraceable integration of data,models, and simulation tools across different disciplines, mission phases, and even across differentmissions.This means that all the data, simulation models and discipline-specific tools are reusable and interoperablethroughout the entire spacecraft lifecyclefrom early design through to operations. More specifically it includes the mapping of the lifecycle usage of models and data and defining how simulation assets contribute to various phases and ensuring their continuous integration. The simulation artefacts include the mission scenarios as input to the test scenarios and time-series data as output of the simulation and AIV test campaigns. Within the RatioSim community already a system-level simulator reference architecture exists that serves as a basis.Within ongoing Digital Twin Spacecraft activities an overview is created of the spacecraft data fromrequirements to mission/system design, up to PLM and CAD data. The SSO defines the semantics of the dataand the domain specific concepts. By taking theOverall Semantic Modelling for Space Systems Engineering(OSMoSE) methodology, the generation of the information system in line with the data and semantics isensured and to large extent automated.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Analysis of the lessons learned, including:- Formal semantic approach of space system ontology and OSMoSE for overall semantic interoperability,- RatioSim system level simulator reference architecture, specifying the ecosystem, specification,development and usage of any systemlevel simulator as basis for digital twins.- Use-cases and data specifics coming from pilot digital twin activity. This includes the different roles ofdifferent stakeholders.- Digital twin spacecraft and digital spacecraft data management aspects.- High levelarchitecture definition of data management system supporting the digital twin spacecrafts.- Definition of methodology to define the semantics of the data into space system ontology model (top downand bottom-up approach, allowing for configuration and flexibility).- Development of the data management system, following the OSMoSE guidelines for generation of theinformation system based on the created SSO.- Testing and verification of the developed system using real-life data/simulators for a number of digital twinuse-cases.Deliverables: Prototype, Report, Software

By taking theOverall Semantic Modelling for Space Systems Engineering(OSMoSE) methodology, the generation of the information system in line with the data and semantics isensured and to large extent automated.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Analysis of the lessons learned, including:- Formal semantic approach of space system ontology and OSMoSE for overall semantic interoperability,- RatioSim system level simulator reference architecture, specifying the ecosystem, specification,development and usage of any systemlevel simulator as basis for digital twins.- Use-cases and data specifics coming from pilot digital twin activity. This includes the different roles ofdifferent stakeholders.- Digital twin spacecraft and digital spacecraft data management aspects.- High levelarchitecture definition of data management system supporting the digital twin spacecrafts.- Definition of methodology to define the semantics of the data into space system ontology model (top downand bottom-up approach, allowing for configuration and flexibility).- Development of the data management system, following the OSMoSE guidelines for generation of theinformation system based on the created SSO.- Testing and verification of the developed system using real-life data/simulators for a number of digital twinuse-cases.Deliverables: Prototype, Report, Software

title: ADHA SECURITY MODULE - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To derive a standard set of requirements for the ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) Security Module and implement a prototype form-factor equivalent ADHA module.Description: The ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) has been initiated through a collaboration between ESA, European satellite primes and data handling equipment suppliers. The initiative has resulted in the agreement on an architecture for data handling unit based on standard module functions. A standard module procurement flow has been defined, as well as a standardized backplane connector and electrical interfaces. This allows independent development of interoperable modules that can be connected together in ADHA units. More advanced security functions are expected to be required in future ESA missions. The modular format of the proposed solution will enable faster adoption, and verification of new security technologies, in different unit configurations. This activity aims to perform analysis work to derive a standardization of the security function within an ADHA module form-factor, to allow the development of ADHA-compliant security products, which can be utilized together with other existing ADHA products, such as ADHA OBC. When implemented in the ADHA 3U form factor, such units are of particular interest for use in mid-size satellite platforms as well (less than 500kg mass). For prototyping purposes, the target of this activity is an elegant breadboard (EBB) of the ADHA security module in 6U format, based on the security function requirements defined in this activity. The extended format will provide the required design margins for the prototyping and demonstration phase. The long-term goal, this technology development, is the adaptation of this security module to an ADHA 3U module form factor. This activity encompasses thefollowing tasks: - Analyse the use-cases for dedicated security modules in data handling systems, both for platform and payload - Derive the detailed generic requirements for ADHA Security Modules, including functions, performances, electrical and software interfaces, etc. and present the specifications for review of the ADHA consortia and industrial working group - Derive the architectural design of a prototype ADHA Security Module - Derive a prototype electrical and software design of an ADHA Security Module, as an EBB in ADHA 6U format. - Perform functional validation of the prototype and demonstrate a representative use-case for the ADHA Security Module - Derive a roadmap for bringing the derived design to an ADHA 3U security module EM/EQM/FM.

title: T811-904SD RISK MODELLING FOR RE-ENTRY FRAGMENTS GOING THROUGH AIRSPACE (EXPRO+)
description: In the current era of large satellite constellations, more satellites are being launched than ever before and, as a result, more satellites are also re-entering the Earth's atmosphere; Most of them doing so in an uncontrolled manner. Unsurprisingly, the amount ofre-entries has been steadily increasing in recent years and is expected to continue rising in the coming years. This trend not onlyincreases the risk of large fragments reaching the ground, but also introduces hazards from smaller debris in the airspace. The increased number of uncontrolled re-entries imposes a growing risk on air traffic, directly affecting flight operations and leading to significant economic losses. A notable example is the uncontrolled re-entry of the Long March 5B (CZ-5B) rocket, which prompted the closure of Spanish airspace in November 2022, a decision made under limited information and unclear criteria.Existing gaps, such asthe presence of millimetre- to centimetre-sized fragments that remain in the atmosphere after a destructive re-entry, are well recognised and can often lead to overly conservative risk assessments. Several attempts have been made to incorporate air-traffic density models into re-entry risk assessment tools. However, key gaps remain that must be better understood to accurately evaluate aircraft vulnerability to uncontrolled re-entries and the resulting debris. Improved modelling of subsonic fragments generated after the main break-up phase is essential, as this phenomenon is still poorly understood. In addition, current risk assessment tools need to integrate dedicated aircraft risk models.The objective of the activity is to characterise and assess the risks due to subsonic space debris re-entry fragments crossing airspace. title: CRISTAL LEVEL-2 OPERATIONAL HYDRO-CRYO DATA PROCESSORS (CRISTAL2OP)
description: The Copernicus Space Component (CSC) includes a series of Sentinel missions developed by ESA, whose success has led to an expanded programme. Among these new missions, CRISTAL (Copernicus Polar Ice and Snow Topography Altimeter) will deliver highresolution measurements of landice elevation, seaice thickness, ocean surface topography, and water level height for rivers and lakes. Most notably, CRISTAL will be the first dual-frequency altimeter providing high-resolution measurements of snow depth over sea ice. These data are essential for monitoring icesheet and glacier evolution, seaice variability, and other key climate indicators while supportingoperational applications.The objective of this ITT, CRISTAL Level-2 Operational Hydro-Cryo Data Processors (CRISTAL2OP), is to establish and implement the operational baseline for ESA's CRISTAL Level2 data dedicated to Cryosphere and Hydrology applications. Thescope covers the following thematic domains: sea ice (Arctic, Antarctic and icebergs), land ice (ice sheets, ice shelves and mountain glaciers), and inland waters (rivers, lakes and estuaries). Processing for global ocean applications is not part of this ITT. Theactivity includes the complete development of the ESA Hydro-Cryo CRISTAL Level2 operational Thematic Data Processors, ensuring thatthe future EOFCSC infrastructure can process and manage CRISTAL mission data in line with mission requirements and the EOFCSC operations concept.The core objectives of the activity are:To define the format for the operational ESA Hydro-Cryo CRISTAL Level-2 products To design, develop and test the operational ESA Hydro-Cryo CRISTAL Level-2 Data Processors To define the Auxiliary Data Files necessary for the generation of the Level-2 productsTo support the integration of the ESA Hydro-Cryo CRISTAL Level-2 Data Processors in the operational framework
