title: APPLICATION PROPAGATION ENVIRONMENT (APEX)
description: The Application Propagation Environment (APEx) aims to increase the uptake and reuse of RD application project results, especially algorithms and workflows, and ensure their long-term availability to the EO community. To facilitate this, APEx will build on European cloud-based EO platform services offered in the Network of Resources (NoR) and integrate, develop, and provide dedicated services such as facilitating algorithm hosting and on-demand execution, algorithm maturity enhancement or the instantiation of working environments.APEx will develop and provide a set of services categorised as (1) instantiation services and (2) propagation services. As part of the instantiation services, APEx will be able to provide managed, and highly configurable working environments that correspond to the common needs of the ESA RD application projects in order to share and maintain project results with the community. To achieve this, APEx will integrate existing EO platform services from the NoR portfolio with Common Architecture Building Blocks and, in some cases, also newly developed services (i.e., "delta" services, currently not existing in the NoR portfolio). The APEx instantiation services will be dynamically instantiated/deployed and shall be configurable in terms of selected components. They will allow for tailoring in "look feel" according to specific project or application contexts.As part of the propagation services, APEx will facilitate the persistent availability of RD application algorithms to the community by coordinating and aggregating algorithms that will be hosted in APEx compliant and interoperable EO platform environments and continuously monitor their availability and functioning. The central APEx portal will aggregate and index all hosted services and make them persistently accessible to the community along with other project results. Other APEx propagation services include the Algorithm Maturity Enhancement. This service will develop and offer a streamlined solution for enhancing RD algorithms in terms of computational performance and efficiency following a dedicated process that includes technical source code analysis, benchmarking, and refactoring. Further propagation services include the Cloudification of EO toolboxes and support for algorithm intercomparison exercises. Generally, APEx services shall extend the ESA NoR portfolio for not yet existing service types needed for instantiation and propagation. For the initial 2-year contract instantiation services shall be supplied to at least 20 projects within this current APEX activity, with the aim to on-board these as NoR services within the initial contract. For the 3-year extension period, such NoR-onboarded services can directly be requested by the projects via the NoR and the APEx activity only has to cover service evolution.

title: MACHINE LEARNING FOR ATMOSPHERIC IMPACT OF LAUNCHERS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a Machine Learning (ML) model to simulate the interaction of launcher exhaust gas with all atmospheric layers, in the frame of LCA and complementary to test bench and existing measurements (i.e. FIREWALL activity).Description: In the frame of ESA's Green Agenda objectives, most ESA's missions have been tasked to perform Life Cycle Assessment (LCA). However, LCA in the frame of space transportation is lacking data, especially when it comes to understanding the interaction of exhaust gas and species formed through ablation process during re-entry in the different layers of the atmosphere. This activity targets to model the interaction of the exhaust gas with all layers of the atmosphere using Machine Learning (ML). The activity aims at investigating whether AIcan generate a reliable dataset capturing exhaust plume and atmospheric interactions, which would serve as a reference or comparisonpoint during measurement campaigns. Having access to such tools would significantly enhance the efficiency of analysis once exhaustplume measurements become available. This activity complements the ongoing efforts on LCA and FIREWALL activity. The FIREWALL (Facilitate Inquiry of Rocket Emission Impact with Atmosphere Lower Layers) activity aims to better understand the interaction between the engine exhaust plume and the different atmospheric layers. It results with the assessment of several in-situ and remote sensing technics, to prepare a plume measurement campaign. The modelling focuses on the following four observations vectors and their respective types of observation: - Satellite: OH, H2O, PMC, rocket contrails and greenhouse gases (CO, CH4); - Balloons and sounding rockets: gas concentration, Ozone and temperature variation; - Ground measurements: aerosols, debris, accurate gas concentration, etc.; - Aircraft: reactive NOx, CO2, ozone loss, CIO, aerosol and CH4. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Perform a state-of-the-art analysis on the ML methods used for atmospheric sciences; - Identify the potential modelling use cases: relevant exhaust species and corresponding altitude; - Identify the available dataset for each potential use cases; - Select the most promising use cases,including the exhaust species and the altitudes as well as the preferred ML approach; - Train and test the model; - Validate the model with upcoming measurement campaigns (e.g., FIREWALL Phase 2) and/or existing available data (e.g. from satellite observations, test benches exhaust plumes); - Define recommendations for future, parallel or complementary development. Software shall be deliveredunder an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access it and can provideupdate to the community of users.

title: ARGONAUT DIGITAL TWIN - END-TO-END VERIFICATION APPLICATIONS INITIAL STUDY - EXPRO+
description: Each Argonaut lander consists of multiple elements that will be procured, developed, testedindependently and eventually as a whole. title: GT1D-604GD PILOT DIGITAL TWIN SPACECRAFT FOR OPERATIONS AND ASSEMBLY, INTEGRATION AND TEST WITH A PILOT MISSION
description: A Spacecraft Digital Twin (DT) is a digital representation of a spacecraft and the engineering processes. A spacecraft DT takes Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) information, simulation models and simulator data, together with "in-field" (physical) data to represent the spacecraft. This activity focusses on using the combination of models and data to create outputs supporting verification and operations of the spacecraft and aims at providing a pilot covering key aspects of a DT in the engineering, AIT and operations phase. The aim is to deploy a pilot in the operational environment for AIT purposes.The outcome of the use cases shall serve both as a prototype for a generic DT framework allowing easy development of a DT as well as a pilot for a selected specific mission. A case study mission shall be selected taking into account, usage of EGS-CC, availability of Simulation Modelling Platform(SMP) based models.

title: HIGH FREQUENCY AIRBORNE RADIOMETER INSTRUMENT FOR THE SUPPORT OF FUTURE ALTIMETRY MISSIONS
description: Satellite altimetry plays an essential role in producing sea level and waves products such as sea surface height (SSH), significantwave height (SWH), mean sea level and near surface wind/wave products. Today, a low frequency channel microwave radiometer is in general used to correct the altimeter range for water vapor path delay over ocean. The wet tropospheric correction (WTC) is consideredas one of the largest source of uncertainty in sea level estimate. As any artificial temporal drift in the wet tropospheric correction translate immediately to a similar drift in the mean sea level, there is a need for extremely well calibrated radiometer instrument to retrieve this wet tropospheric correction in support of the accurate altimeter measurement. Depending on the targeted temporal and spatial scales, some recent studies and projects ("Radiometer Instrument for Swath Altimeter missions", Sentinel-6 HRMR instrument, Sentinel-3 NG-T) have shown that the two existing classes of satellite altimeters such as the conventional nadir looking altimeters and the wide swath altimeters would both benefit from the addition of one or several high frequency channels (89/165/175 GHz) to the low frequency channels (18.7/23.8/36.5(or 31.4) GHz) already used for the WTC retrieval. The advantages brought by the addition of the high frequency channels in the microwave radiometer are severalfold. For a given RF radiating aperture, the high frequencyradiometer would exhibit a high spatial resolution and therefore shall be less prone to land contamination in coastal areas that would directly impact the uncertainty of the WTC based on brightness temperature measurement near the coastline. For wide swath altimeters, a multibeam microwave radiometer combining the low and high frequency channels would help to retrieve the WTC across-track with an increased accuracy and with better spatial resolution commensurate with the high spatial resolution radar retrievals from a swath altimeter. Moreover, the high frequency channels (typically 89 GHz or 165/175 GHz) can provide additional information for precipitation screening. This new proposed activity aims at developing an airborne demonstrator instrument to validate the benefits of the high frequency radiometer measurement, to support the continued improvement of the altimeter measurement and observation capabilities. The activity shall start with the detailed analysis of user requirements and the design of the instrument, then continue with themanufacturing, integration and test of the airborne system and finally concludes with the airworthiness certification on an airborne carrier and a functional test flight to validate the airborne radiometer function and performance and collect first experimental data.

title: NAVISP-EL1-109 5G LOCALISATION FOR SAFETY OF LIFE APPLICATIONS IN RAIL - EXPRO+
description: With the Future Railway Mobile Communication System (FRMCS) poised to replace the legacy GSM-R railway mobile radio system of the European Rail Traffic Management System (ERTMS), it could potentially play a role in position and speed determination in safety-related railway applications, considering the significant deployments of FRMCS that are expected. The objective of this activity is to study, design, and implement a proof of concept that demonstrates the exploitation of FRMCS / 5G NR signals in addition to or supporting other sensors (e.g., GNSS, rotational, inertial, radar-based, optical) in a multi-sensor platform targeting Advanced Safe Train Positioning (ASTP) - i.e., either basic (safe odometry information) or full ASTP (safe position, speed, acceleration and odometry information). The proof of concept is to be validated using measurements obtained from a test campaign with real 5G NR data gathered from the railway environment.

title: GAN HEMT THRESHOLD VOLTAGE STABILISATION FOR HIGH FIDELITY SIGNAL QUALITY EXPRO PLUS
description: To characterise and develop a generic stabilisation methodology for GaN HEMTs used in navigation payloads.Description:Gallium Nitride (GaN) Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuits (MMIC) are critical enabling components for current and future Positioning, Navigation and Timing (PNT) systems. GaN High-electron mobility transistors (HEMT) are prone to early life threshold voltage shift generally attributed to charge trapping effects. Depending on the MMIC design and operating conditions (temperature, DC bias,RF power) this threshold voltage shift has been shown to alter device RF performance beyond acceptable drift limits. Exact root cause and generic methodology for threshold voltage stabilisation has not been established so far by manufacturers or end-users leading to increased risk and qualification effort of the components for space missions. The objective of this activity is to fully characterise trapping related degradation mechanisms in GaN MMICs and develop a generic stabilisation methodology available for all end-users. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Selection of test devices for implementation on MMIC single stage amplifier - Characterisation test campaign - Generic screening procedure definition

title: QUANTUM PULSE GATING DEMONSTRATORFOR SINGLE PHOTON BASED OPTICAL COMMUNICATION DURING DAYLIGHT (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3H.001) - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to design, build and validate a Quantum Pulse Gating breadboard optimising daytime optical communication, facilitating the integration of non-cryogenic silicon baseddetectors and eliminating the need for complex cryogenic systems.Targeted Improvements:- Up to 3 orders of magnitude improvement in background noise rejection compared to current solutions.- Reduction of power, volume and mass by a factor of 10, through integration of non-cryogenic detectors.Description:Single photonoptical wireless communication systems needed for applications including Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and High Photon Efficiency (HPE) links are limited in performancesubstantially by the effects of background noise.State-of-the-art cryogenic Superconducting Nanowire Single Photon Detectors (SNSPDs) lead to bulky and heavy systems that due to narrowband spectral filtering of the received signal, do notallow the extraction, in a lossless manner, of the single temporal mode from the remaining background noise and hinder the attainment of high-purity heralded quantum states.Other solutions do exist, InGaAs Single Photon Avalanche Diodes (SPADs) suffer from poor performance, or silicon-based Geiger mode detectors with a quantum efficiency of > 70% - operatein proximity to the visible part of the spectrum, but do not currently provide an equivalent solution to the SNSPDs.A possible solution is a Quantum Pulse Gating (QPG) system, which filters only the signal temporal mode from the input beam, whilst leaving the remaining multimode background noise at theinput frequency of the unused idler beam.QPG systems are based on sum-frequency generation techniques within a non-linear medium utilising a pulsed laser which leads to very high-efficiency (>80%) coupling for ground laserreceivers and facilitates efficient operation even during daytime conditions.Several challenges such as the use of broadband communication pulses, and design of the non-linear medium as well as signal synchronisation of the onboard transmitter and the ground receiverneed to be addressed.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF EUROPEAN SEALING MATERIALS COMPATIBLE WITH PROPELLANT LIQUIDS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop European sealing materials compatible with propellants and highly oxidizing media.Description: Perfluoroelastomers with mineral fillers are used as inert sealing materials in propulsion systems. The currently used materials are of mainly US origin. The formulations of the materials undergo regular changes, e.g. in filler materials or the polymer system, which may lead to their obsolescence. On the other hand, they are considered as strategic materials and their testing with the use of propellants is expensive. Thus introduction of European alternatives would be highly advantageous and would possibly help to avoid high qualification costs. This material shall be compatible with such propellants as hydrazine and monomethylhydrazine, as well as oxidizing media, such as dinitrogen tetraoxide. No content of potential catalysts of propellants decomposition or REACH-affected ingredients is allowed. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Market research to identify all currently existing solutions, - Identification of the starting formulations, - Testing and optimization of these preliminary formulations, taking into account a long-term storage requirement applicable for many space missions, - Development of a breadboard demonstrator in form of small machined O-rings, - Testing of the breadboard demonstrator to prove the application-relevant properties, in particular compatibility with the selected media over typical mission lifetime, - Final summary and assessment of application constraints of the newly developed O-rings.Deliverables: Breadboard, Report.

title: SENTINEL-1 NEXT GENERATION PHASES B2/C/D/E1
description: The Sentinel-1 Next Generation will guarantee the continuity from the first generation, therefore, dedicated to day-and-night monitoring of land, ice and oceans, and responding to Emergency Management services. With respect to the first generation, the Next Generation will provide enhanced performance and so improving the servicing to the existing applications, as well as enabling new services, related to: soil moisture, land cover mapping, crop type and status discrimination, forest type and forest cover (e.g. in support to biomass estimation), food security and precision farming, maritime surveillance, natural and anthropogenic hazards and the operational monitoring of the Cryosphere and polar regions including automatic sea ice mapping and land ice monitoring.The Payload will be based on a Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) in C-Band and will also have an Automatic Identification System (AIS) instrument in support to the achievement of mission maritime objectives by augmenting the SAR payload data for ship marine traffic applications.The Sentinel-1 Next Generation procurement comprises the development of an improved Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging in C-Band and an Automatic Identification System (AIS) instrument, and their embarkation onboard and Manufacturing, Assembly, Integration and Test of the Spacecraft. It also includes all the activities necessary for potential embarkation of a Laser Communication Terminal (LCT)for payload data downlink via inter-satellite laser-link.The following contractual mandatory options apply:1.The Phase E1 of the first Spacecraft (i.e. PFM),2.The manufacturing, assembly, integration and test (MAIT) of the recurrent spacecraft Flight Model (FM2) up to the confirmation of acceptance by the Agency, achieved at the corresponding Flight Acceptance Review (FAR); and 3.The development and delivery of the Spacecraft Simulator for Flight Operations.

title: ESA EO INFORMATION SYSTEM (EIS)
description: ESA EO Information System (EIS) Invitation to TenderESA is preparing the release of the Invitation to Tender (ITT) for the ESA Earth Observation Information System (EIS), planned for Q1 2026.The procurement for EIS will cover the definition, implementation andoperation of a single, flexible, and programme-independent EO data information system, governed by ESA and its Member States. This environment shall offer an opportunity for multi-programme EO initiatives (in particular, ESA Copernicus Space Component CSC-4 and ESA Digital Twin Earth) and for European industry to access a robust foundation on which to develop, prototype and maintain competitive operational services and applications, maximising synergies and reducing time, risks and development costs.EIS will enable:Access to a unified data storage architecture and exploitation system, established on EU sovereign clouds and based on state-of-the-artsolutionsEO data management services and Digital Twin Components development, prototyping, evolution and maintenanceAccess to harmonised representations of heterogeneous datasets for processing, as well as for AI modelling and trainingEfficient hosting of services and applications allowing industrial partners to manage such services and applications under their own respective governanceThe EIS procurement will be released as one open competition divided into two lots:Lot 1 - ESA Information System backbone: development, operations, and evolution of an architecture of cloud-managed services integrated in a project-based data exploitation system, established on EU sovereign clouds and based on state-of-the-art solutions.Lot 2 - Unified Data Management: development, operations, and evolution of an innovative EO-related data architecture to streamline the representation of diverse datasets, including areference open source EO application demonstrator.Tenderers will be invited to submit a separate and self-standing tender per Lot. They will be allowed to submit tenders for both Lots. To ensure the selection of the best expertise of European industry, the Agency will award each Lot to separate legal entities, and no single entity may hold contracts for the two Lots.The EIS procurement isfunded under the Copernicus Space Component CSC 4 and EarthWatch ESA Digital Twin Earth programmes.

title: COHERENT TRANSCEIVER FOR FREE SPACE OPTICAL COMMUNICATION AND TIME AND FREQUENCY TRANSFER (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5F.047) RE-ISSUE
description: Objective:The objective of the activity is to prepare the development of an optimised 100Gbps coherent transceiver for satellite free-space optical communications through the atmosphere. This activity shall address the optimisation of the digital signal processing, including the time-diversity algorithms based on the current state-of-art coherent transceiver solutions. It shall also attempt to implement a time and frequency transfer function.Targeted Improvements:To achieve reliable satellite-ground bi-directional communications through the use of space-optimised coherent transceivers. This shall improve one order of magnitude the current optical channel capacity (current missions with dedicated transceivers are targeting 10Gbps).Description:The activity will build on existing COTS transceivers design but will propose and demonstrate the required optimisation for cross-atmospheric links. Transceiver functionalities related to the optical fibre medium shall not be included, while functionalities required by the free-space links will be introduced and tested (e.g. interleaving, FEC, time recovery, carrier frequency recovery). The main tasks are -State-of-art analysis of the current coherent transceivers implementation-Design of the transceiver for satellite cross-atmospheric links-Scaled breadboard development and testing of the selected configuration in laboratory environment.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND SPACE QUALIFICATION OF EUROPEAN 1550 NM DISTRIBUTED-FEEDBACK LASER DIODE MODULE
description: Objectives: To develop up to space qualification a European 1550 nm DFB Laser Diode module in a butterfly package.Description: Distributed-FeedBack (DFB) Laser diode modules at 1550 nm are a key enabling technology in a wide range of applications in space missions: Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) downlinks, inter-satellite relays, optical communication terminals, and RF-Photonic telecom payloads. This optical source is ideal forvarious emerging functions such as LIDAR, optical sensing, optical switching, and coherent optical communication.The establishment of a space-qualified European supplier for a DFB Laser diode module at 1550 nm is essential in the context of future European spaceprograms, where no full European solution is available at this targeted wavelength.To contribute to the EEE component European Sovereignty initiative, critical elements of the module, in particular the DFB laser diode chip and packagingelements, shall be developed.The 1550nm DFB laser diode module will have the following characteristics:single frequency, highpower, narrow linewidth, low relative intensity noise, and high reliability in a butterfly package.The activity is divided into twophases. During the first phase, a new design in line with the market needs will be developed and characterized. The ESCC evaluationfirst for the Chip-on-Submount and then for the laser module will be carried out to assess the physical limit of the devices to define the parameters for ESCC qualification, the safe operating area, and the failuremodes/mechanisms.The second phase will start with the industrialization of the production and will conclude with the ESCC qualification tests to demonstrate product compliance with customers' needs and space application constraints. It is expected that the product will be presented for introduction in the EuropeanPreferred Part List (EPPL) and to the European Qualified Part List (QPL).The activity encompasses the following tasks:Phase 1: Development, Pre-Industrialisation and Evaluation- Consolidation of the module technical requirements based on space users'needs.- Design / delta-design activities for chip, chip on submount and module.- Characterization of performances on prototypes and delta-design activities- Preparation of ESCC evaluation (Process Identification document, Evaluation Test plan, production documentation) - Manufacturing of evaluation test batch- ESCC evaluation testing- Finalization of ESCC specifications and production documentationPhase 2: Industrialization and Qualification- Finalization of manufacturing process including subcontractors and suppliers-Production of the qualification batch- ESCC Qualification TestingDeliverables: Hardware (sample of evaluation and qualification),Report, (test results andESCC specifications)This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: PHOTON COUNTING VIS DETECTORS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop and mature architectures for photon counting pixelated detectors in the visible range.Description: The trend of improving readout noise performance has approached the threshold where high performance imaging detectors can count the number of photoelectrons collected in each sampling period. This ultimate performance limit allows the contribution of readout noise to be entirely removed, eliminating a contribution to the signal to noise budget of instruments. In this activity, pixel architectures able to reach photon counting sensitivity in the 400-800 nm wavelength range are being explored. The assessment targets large focal plane arrays operating at high photon flux rates typical of Earth Observation applications. Other aspects such as susceptibility to thespace radiation environment and feasibility of manufacture within current CMOS imaging fabrication processes are considered. Following the requirements and device architecture assessment, this activity proposes a device design. In the case that suitable prototypedevices are already designed, detailed characterisation of their electro-optic performance shall be performed, with an assessment in a critical radiation environment. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements Review - Photon counting device architecture assessment - Device preliminary design; - Device assembly and test setup preparation; - Detailed electro-optic testing; - Assessment of device performance change under a critical radiation environment.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restrictedto non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: RELIABILITY OF ELECTRONIC ASSEMBLIES IN CRYOGENIC ENVIRONMENT - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of the activity is to evaluate materials and processes (solder alloys, PCB, adhesive and EEE devices) suitable for manufacturing of electronics operating or exposed to very low temperatures (-80/-270C).DescriptionThe use of electronics at very low temperatures (<-80C) poses a challenge for the reliability of the assemblies. The materials and processes currently used for electronic assembly manufacturing are typically tested and qualified for operation in the range 55/+85C. Applications at temperatures <-80C can trigger different failure mechanisms. The materials experience an increase in strength and reduction in ductility whilstcreep and stress relaxation do not any longer occur, limiting the ability of the solder to act as stress relief element.The change in stress distribution in the assembly of a device can move the failure from the solder joint to the component or to the PCB. Other phenomena as change of phases can take place with dramatic effect on performance, for example the change of phase of Sn which can lead to the Tin pest.The knowledge and experience in reliability of electronic assembly in extreme low temperatures is limited and even the definition of requirements and test conditions to evaluate electronic assemblies for these conditions is a complex task.Thecharacterization of the materials and evaluation of assemblies at extreme low temperature will provide data to aid designers and manufacturers to make an educated choice of the materials/design for a specific environment and to define suitable test approaches for verification of processes The development of this knowledge is the base to enable the development and manufacturing of electronicunits suitable for landers to the surface of planets, moons (Earth moon, giant planets moons), samples return missions, units located on the outside of spacecrafts (booms) for missions in the outer solar system or electronics located in cryostats.Tasks to be implemented:- Literature survey of state of the art for low temperature electronics and selection of candidate materials (e.g. PCB, solder alloy, EEE parts)- Test plan definition for basic characterization at elemental level at low temperature (incl. modulus, CTE,strength, phase changes, fatigue)- Test plan definition for testing of assemblies in thermal cycling and long term exposure at lowtemperatures- Modelling and test implementation- Result evaluation, definition of recommendations and identification of future development needsFuture activities will be defined on the basis of the outcome of this campaign

title: FRAME-BY-FRAME SWITCHING OF DVB-S2X AND RCS2 IN RETURN LINK (ARTES AT 3C.053) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a prototype terminal capable of DVB-S2X and RCS2 real-time switching in the return link utilising a Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) modem ASIC. In a second step, the activity will develop a hub burst demodulator and scheduler, capable of using both, DVB-S2X and RCS2 frame types, allowing aflexible bandwidth share based on traffic types. End-to-end testing will include performance evaluation of the full return link comprising hub and user terminal.TargetedImprovements: Increase return link spectral efficiency up to 30% and demonstrate throughput beyond 100 Mbaud while retaining the intrinsic flexibility of MF-TDMA to retain low latency for lowthroughput applications.Description: In 2024 DVB updated the DVB-RCS2specification to include non-geostationary satellite systems. This allowed DVB-S2X constant or burst mode in the return link, allowing higher spectral efficiency and throughput. DVB-S2X and RCS2 can be mixed within the return link time plan, and a single terminalcan theoretically switch between them on the fly. This allows the increase of return link spectral efficiency up to 30%, through the implementation of S2X in the return link to carry traffic requiring large frames in a steady stream more efficiently, while retaining the ability to carry bursty, small packets more efficiently the majority of the time.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- In the first phase, the activity will focus to develop the software controlling the COTS modem ASIC and to develop aprototype terminal capable of DVB-S2X and RCS2 real-time switching in the return link and to test and evaluate the performance in alaboratory environment. The budget for this phase is up to 750 kEuro.- The second phase will develop a hub burst demodulator and scheduler, capable including a software or FPGA-based burst demodulator capable of switching between DVBRCS2- based MF-TDMA and DVB-S2X frames in real-time. A scheduler algorithm will be developed and tested able to accommodate the expected traffic types, with intelligent switching between frames as needed. Finally end-to-end testing will include performance evaluation of the full return link comprising hub and user terminal in a relevant environment.

Description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a prototype terminal capable of DVB-S2X and RCS2 real-time switching in the return link utilising a Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) modem ASIC. In a second step, the activity will develop a hub burst demodulator and scheduler, capable of using both, DVB-S2X and RCS2 frame types, allowing aflexible bandwidth share based on traffic types. End-to-end testing will include performance evaluation of the full return link comprising hub and user terminal.TargetedImprovements: Increase return link spectral efficiency up to 30% and demonstrate throughput beyond 100 Mbaud while retaining the intrinsic flexibility of MF-TDMA to retain low latency for lowthroughput applications.Description: In 2024 DVB updated the DVB-RCS2specification to include non-geostationary satellite systems. This allowed DVB-S2X constant or burst mode in the return link, allowing higher spectral efficiency and throughput. DVB-S2X and RCS2 can be mixed within the return link time plan, and a single terminalcan theoretically switch between them on the fly. This allows the increase of return link spectral efficiency up to 30%, through the implementation of S2X in the return link to carry traffic requiring large frames in a steady stream more efficiently, while retaining the ability to carry bursty, small packets more efficiently the majority of the time.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- In the first phase, the activity will focus to develop the software controlling the COTS modem ASIC and to develop aprototype terminal capable of DVB-S2X and RCS2 real-time switching in the return link and to test and evaluate the performance in alaboratory environment. The budget for this phase is up to 750 kEuro.- The second phase will develop a hub burst demodulator and scheduler, capable including a software or FPGA-based burst demodulator capable of switching between DVBRCS2- based MF-TDMA and DVB-S2X frames in real-time. A scheduler algorithm will be developed and tested able to accommodate the expected traffic types, with intelligent switching between frames as needed. Finally end-to-end testing will include performance evaluation of the full return link comprising hub and user terminal in a relevant environment.

title: IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT OF INTELLIGENT AUTONOMOUS AVIONICS ENABLING MULTI-ENVIRONMENT SATCOM SATELLITE OPERATION IN LEO (ARTES AT 3E.033) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop, launch and test autonomous and intelligent avionics enabling satcomconstellation satellites to operate autonomously across multiple environmental conditions in Low Earth Orbit (LEO). Breadboarding and in-orbit testing of critical platform functions including health monitoring, orbital control and resourcemanagement will be carried out. As part of the in-orbit experiment, a payload technology demonstrator will be developed to experiment with innovative approaches of autonomous payload configuration and control.Targeted Improvements: Enabling autonomous operation and reconfiguration of a satellite in a range of orbital LEO environments. This entails orbital control, platform resource management, health monitoring capability, autonomous decision-making capability and autonomous communication to ground.Description: Satellite operators currently face limitations when relying on single orbits (e.g. geostationary or low Earth orbit) for communications. These limitations affect system performance, resilience, and service continuity, especially in the aviation, maritime, governmental, and remote enterprise networks sectors. There is a growing need for an intelligent on-board control system that is capable to operate constellation satellites in multiple orbital LEO altitudes and environments. Such avionics systems must operate reliably across multiple orbital shells under varying environmental conditions, such as radiation, power constraints, and thermal fluctuations, particularly in very low earthorbits. Developing avionics that could autonomously detect the need for adaptation/changes of orbit and will enable:- autonomous multi-orbit operation- orbital transfer- repositioning of satellites in fleet and constellations.The activity will develop an intelligent avionics module enabling autonomous operation. An experimental satcom platform and payload will be developed and an in-orbit experiment will be carried out across a large range of space environmental conditions (e.g. eclipse period, radiation levels, thermal loads) in LEO.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:Phase 1 (budget up to 2 MEuro) will design, develop and integrate an intelligent avionics module to full engineering model enabling autonomous satellite operations. Phase 1 will develop and test:- autonomous operations logic that enables real-time system response to varying environmental conditions- adaptive AOCS and GNC functions to adapt to different orbits- health monitoring and diagnostic decision-making- autonomous TTC communication to ground.Phase 2 will develop the flight engineering model of the avionics module. A satcom experimental payload will be developed tosupport experimentation with intelligent, autonomous payload reconfiguration (e.g. transmit power, beam pointing, coverage change, temperature stabilisation, etc.) to maintain services during dynamic events such as orbital transfers and changes to operational space environmental and resilience response to sub-system failure. Avionics and payload will be integrated into a satellite. Phase 2 will launch and operate experiments in multiple LEO altitudes and environmental conditions.

title: DUAL SATELLITE IN-ORBIT TESTBED FOR SENSING AND COMMUNICATION FOR LOW-POWER DEVICES (ARTES AT 3E.034)
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and launch a dual satellite in-orbit testbed for sensing and communication for low-power devices with both transmit and receive user capability and inter-satellite link.Targeted Improvements: Enabling the development of protocols and operations concepts for the communication and geolocation from space with low-power terrestrial devices.Description: There is currently no European in-orbit capability to test and validate low-power communication directlybetween LEO satellites and standard ground devices. This limits the development of protocols, modulation schemes, and system architectures for emerging applications in low-power geolocation, environmental sensing, and ubiquitous IoT connectivity. This activity will develop a test bed that supports the exploration of disruptive use cases in low power direct communications between terrestrialdevices and LEO satellites. The testbed will comprise two satellites operating in tandem that can (at a minimum):- Establish a bi-directional low power (Tx/Rx) communications link between satellite and terrestrial devices- Provide Inter-satellite links (ISL) between the two, supporting cross-traffic, redundancy as well as geolocation of devices and interference sources- Test new protocols (e.g. SigFox, LoraWan, Bluetooth) and modulation schemes optimised for low-power signals.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1 with a budget of up to 3MEuro will design and develop a dual-satellite payload testbed able to directly communicate with terrestrial low-power devices. It will mature the key technologies and communication protocols from using simulation and laboratory testing to demonstrate feasibility and system readiness for in-orbit demonstration. Deliverables from Phase 1 are a summary report and full engineering model.- Phase 2 will build the flight equipment, launch, and operate the dual-satellite platform toexperiment with direct low-power, low frequency communications in orbit. The in-orbit experiment will test real-time user communications, validate geolocation concepts, evaluate inter-satellite link performance and collect performance data to inform future protocol standardisation and system architectures. Deliverables from Phase 2 are a summary report and 2 x flight engineering models.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT OF A DEPLOYER FOR STACKED SMALL SATCOM SATELLITES (ARTES AT 3E.035) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: Objective: The objective of the in-orbit experiment is to conduct an experiment and develop the ability of a stack of small satellites to be deployed from a launch vehicle. The activity will design and build a launch vehicle adapter, satellite deployer and compatible test satellite/s which will be subjected to an on ground and in-orbit experiment test campaign examining the deployment dynamics from a launch vehicle in microgravity conditions and subsequent orbit behaviour of the launch vehicle upper stage and test satellites.Targeted Improvements: Enabling a European or Canadian source for small satellite deployers for stacked satellites within the launch vehicle fairing, allowing for 50% increase in utilisation of the launchvolume compared to the current state of art.Description: Current satellite deployment approaches which integrate satellites on a vertical satellite payload adapter structure within a launcher fairing underutilise the available volume, limiting the number of small satellites that can be launched per mission. Stacked satellite integration could increase volume and mass utilisation by up to 50% for a given launch increasingthe number of satellites deployed per mission, reducing mission capex and reducing time to deploy an operational constellation. However, there are no European solutions currently in use for deploying multiple small satellites in a stacked configuration. A Small Satellite Design Guideline (SSGL) has recently been developed that provides design guidelines forplatform developers which allow for the horizontal and vertical stacking of multiple satellites in medium and heavy lift launch vehicles. This concept has carried out critical technology derisking through on-ground tests and simulations.This activity will make use of the SSGL and the activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1, with a budget of up to 4 MEuro, will design and develop the Stack Deployment Mechanism and LV adapter, Test Satellites and validate their mechanical and deployment performance in ground-based environments and simulations preparing it forthe in-orbit experiment. Deliverables from Phase 1 are Study Report and Full Engineering Models of the deployer and test satellites.- Phase 2 will build the flight equipment, launch, and operate the satellites. The structural performance of the stack will be monitored through the launch phase. The deployment performance will be investigated through satellite GNSS and attitude data, as well asrelative position and poise estimation from sensors based on the launch vehicle adapter. Data generated in this phase help to increase the precision of mathematical models and digital twins used for solving satellite motion during deployment and orbital mechanicsverification required to refine the SSGL. Deliverables from Phase 1 are summary report and flight engineering models of the deployer and test satellites.

title: INTEGRATED AVIONICS AND PLATFORM DESIGN FOR A SCALABLE HIGH ASPECT RATIO SATCOM SATELLITES FOR CONSTELLATIONS (ARTES AT 4C.074)
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design build and test a scalable High Aspect Ratio Satellite (HARS) platform encompassing the development of an integrated avionics architecture (including core functionality, minimal harnessing and modular interfaces). A second phase will extend the work and develop a scaled engineering model of a HARS platform with integrated thermal solution and with integrated avionics. The design shall be applicable to HARS from 1m to 4.6m, and able to be scaled up to 8m.Targeted Improvements: - Reduction in mass by 25%- Reduction in AIT time by 50%- Half the overall part count compared to the current state of art for SatCom satellite in the 500-2500kg range.Description: High aspect ratio satellites allow for the efficient and fast development and deployment of satellite communications constellations. High aspect ratio platforms also offer distinct advantages for satcomapplications including enhanced solar power generation and large surface areas for payload antennas. Nevertheless, this concept presents challenges inthermal management, accommodation of standard equipment, accommodation in launch vehicles, deployment into orbit.Additionally, the effective production of high aspect ratio satellites will require design for assembly methodologies not currentlyin use.To address these challenges this activity will design build and test a scalable High Aspect Ratio Satellite (HARS) platformencompassing the development of an integrated avionics architecture. The design shall be applicable to HARS platform from 1m to 4.6m, and able to be scaled up to 8m.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach:- Phase 1, with a budget of up to 2 MEurowill develop the enabling technologies resulting in an integrated avionics design and test them as a scaled engineering model. Thefunctionality of the platform shall include:1. Core avionics functions (OBC, Thermal, ADCS/AOCS, GNSS, TTC, FDIR).2. Modular interfaces to allow integration will peripheral equipment (AOCS sensors and actuators, data storage, thermal equipment, ISL, propulsionunits, payload/payload controllers).Deliverables of Phase 1 include a Summary report and scaled engineering model of the core avionics.- Phase 2 will extend the work and develop a scaled engineering model of a platform with a primary structure that includes anintegrated thermal solution and integrated harness. A structural solution for the stacking of additional HARS within the launch vehiclewill be included. A compatible satellite dispenser/payload adapter for integration into the Launch Vehicle will also be developed. The combined avionics/satellite/dispenser will be tested in a representative environment capturing the equipment level loads, equipment and structure interactions.Deliverables of Phase 2 include a Summary report, scaled engineering models of a satellite platform and dispenser.

title: FULLY DIGITAL ACTIVE TRANSMIT AND RECEIVE ANTENNAS FOR EMERGING MEDIUM EARTH ORBIT CONSTELLATIONS (ARTES AT 5B.256)
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop an architecture of a fully digital active transmit and a fully digital active receive antenna with a high number of radiating elements (i.e.4000) and capable to generate a significant number of beams (i.e. 1000) to support MEO satellite constellations. A transmit and a receive scaled engineering model will be designed and developed and experimentally tested to evaluate the performance.Targeted Improvements: Enabling development to achieve fully digital beamforming with an increase of about a factor of two of number of beams in comparison to current state of art in MEO.Description: The first generation of medium-earth-orbit (MEO) satellite systems have been using passive antennas employing reflectors to generate multiple beams. In the second generation of MEO satellites, active antennas started to be adopted in combination with digital beamforming. Recent developments in this field have seen active antennas that offer global coverage, low latency, maximum flexibility, multiple gigabits per second capacity, independent electronic repointing of the individual beams, reduced interference, and coexistencewith GEO satellites sharing the same frequencies. Active antennas enable also RF-power-allocation reconfigurability amongst the beams. Today, there is a need to develop the next-generation MEO satellites for commercial and governmental applications. The main expected improvements are associated to increasedcommunication data rate and flexibility, requiring larger antennas and an increased number ofbeams.This activity develops an architecture of a fully digital active antennas with a high number of radiating elements (i.e. 4000) and capable to generate a significant number of beams (i.e. 1000). Radiating elements, beamforming network, and the thermal design components shall be designed, optimised, manufactured and tested. For the active components, existing commercial-off-the-shelf products may be used, prioritising European products. The digital processor development is not part of this activity. However, interfaces and interconnects between the digital beam ports of the fully digital antenna and the payload processor shall be defined, quantified and implemented. Use cases for different types of MEO orbits shall be evaluated including inclined orbits and equatorial ones. The antenna design shall exploit power efficient solutions to deliver digital beamforming tasks reducingthe processing in the digital domain. Recent advances in area of reconfigurable beam forming networks and exploitation of symmetries when designing beaming networks will bestudied.The scaled engineering models shall include active and passive RF and digital building blocks of the antennaand beamforming network and shall be scalable to meet the performance requirements of the difference MEO use cases

title: SPECTRUM COEXISTENCE LABORATORY (ARTES 4.0 SPL 4S 3A.229) - EXPRO+
description: The objective is to develop a standardised test laboratory to evaluate the coexistence of various satellite and terrestrial systemswithin a realistic, emulated, and controlled environment.TargetedImprovements: Enable a quantified and objective assessment of mutual interferences. Reduce satcom service outage due to interference from third systems to less than 0.1%.Description: Traditional methods of interference analysis and simulation, which often rely on static models and assumptions, are insufficient to describe thereal-time interactions and variability ofsatellite and terrestrial telecommunication networks. For example, in assessing the potential interference of new NGSO systems, it is mandatory to describe the dynamic radio resourceallocation strategy of the NGSO systemunder test to assess its dynamic effects on incumbent systems such as NGSO, GSO, or terrestrial mobile networks. Moreover, current analysistools are limited to assessing the interaction between the system under test and specific victim incumbent systems, ignoring the rest of the environment, i.e. additional incumbent systemsthat may also be affected. A standardised coexistence test laboratory is essential to address these challenges. By providing a controlled environment that accurately emulates real-worldoperational scenarios, this laboratory will enable a comprehensive evaluation of spectrum coexistence. The use of standardised plug-in modules, interfaces (e.g. API, RF, IF, DIFI), anddescriptors will facilitate the modelling of various satellite and terrestrial systems and their interactions, ensuring that the assessments are both accurate and confidential. title: AIRBORNE G-BAND RADAR INSTRUMENT FOR THE SUPPORT OF FUTURE ATMOSPHERIC MISSIONS
description: Cloud feedbacks and precipitation systems remain the primary source of uncertainty in Earth climate models and numerical weather predictions. To enhance our understanding, there is a crucial need to comprehensively characterize the vertical structure of clouds and precipitation. This involves observing the microphysical, dynamical, and radiative processes occurring at cloud scales. A solutionto provide such observations involves leveraging measurements from multi-frequency radars spanning frequencies from 10 GHz to above200 GHz. Using multiple frequencies facilitates the characterization of a broad spectrum of particles, from heavy precipitation to small ice crystals. Notably, the inclusion of G-band, operating at 1.5 mm wavelength (i.e. about 200 GHz), offers significant advantages in three key areas: boundary layer clouds, cirrus and mid-level ice clouds, and precipitating snow. Recent technology advancements in millimetre-wave technology (such as RF mixer, high power transmitters, etc.) have enabled the development of G-band radars. Successful investigations with ground-based radar (UK-CEOI funded GRACE experiment) and airborne radar (US NASA JPL Vapor In-cloud Profiling Radar (VIPR) experiment) have validated the potential of G-band radar for cloud and precipitation research. Following these successful experiments, ESA has initiated an instrument system study (On-going contract no: 4000139352) to explore the possible instrument implementation of a G-band spaceborne radar for 2 different ESA mission categories, a micro-satellite platform (Scout like mission) and a high reliability large platform (Earth Explorer like mission), to identify the technological gaps and to define the associated technology roadmap. The proposed activity aims at developing a representative airborne cloud radar instrument demonstrator to validate the benefits of the addition of G-band radar measurement for Earth observation.

title: C207-0023FI 4K COOLING SYSTEM (RE-ISSUE 1-12863)
description: Cryogenic cooling below 10K has been used on various ESA Science mission in the past such as ISO, Herschel, Planck and the MIRI instrument on JWST and is essential to achieve background limited performance in the mid-Infrared, far-infrared, THz and -wave regime,addressing several domains identified by the Voyage 2050 expert committee as potential themes for M-class missions. Deep cryogenic cooling is also required in utilising advanced detector technologies such as transition-edge superconducting (TES) microbolometers for X-Ray and microwave instruments or KID (Kinetic Inductance Detector) detectors for the THz/wave range. Taking into account the lessons from the Athena study on the cryogenic system, a 4K cooling system compatible with the programmatic constraints ofa M-class mission can be achieved by: One entity providing the 4K system, limiting the I/F management at ESA/Prime, reducing the non-recurrent overhead at supplier level and avoid duplication of test campaigns. Re-using already developed multistage Cold Finger Assemblies (CFA) and Joule Thompson systems from previous activities. Re-use existing qualified compressors from Earth Observation/Ariel mission, which also enables the re-use of qualified Cooler Drive Electronics. This TDA will therefore build on previous developmentson cryocoolers to maximise the synergies with single stage systems and is split into two phases:Phase 1: Preliminary design of the 4K cooler system Breadboard(s) of the 4K cooler critical elements, demonstrating the achievable end to end performancePhase 2: Detailed design of the 4K cooler system. Manufacturing of a 4K cooler system Engineering model. Performance and environmentaltest campaign. Qualification plan for the 4K cooler system.

title: DESIGN OF HIGH FREQUENCY FOLDED WAVEGUIDE TWT - EXPRO PLUS
description: Ka-band has gained significant traction in recent years for the implementation of active instruments in Earth Observation. Both Ka-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Swath Altimeters have been actively studied and developed, offering several advantages: Compact Instrument Design: The short wavelength of Ka-band allows for smaller and more lightweight instruments. For interferometric applications, the moderate baseline at this frequency simplifies platform implementation. Enhanced Sensitivity to Small-Scale Features: Ka-band is particularly responsive to fine surface structures such as snow grain size, roughness variations, and small water bodies. Higher Spatial Resolution: The combination of short wavelength and high available bandwidth enables finer resolution in both azimuth and range, improving observation capabilities.One notable example of this technology is the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission, developed jointly by NASA and CNES. SWOT utilizes Ka-band radar interferometry to provide global measurements of water surface height. Similarly, the Sentinel-3 Next Generation Topography (S3NG-T) mission addresses comparable objectives, contributing to the Copernicus Altimetry Constellation, which provides fundamental measurement data for Earth observation. The high-power source plays a crucial role in Ka-band SAR and swath altimetry systems, as it directly influences overall system performance. Due to the high frequency of the Ka-band (approximately 35.75 GHz), efficiently amplifying RF power presents a significant challenge. In conventional high-power amplifiers (HPAs), especially helix-based traveling wave tubes (TWTs), component dimensions are becoming increasingly small, leading to complexities in manufacturing, assembly, and thermal management. The objective of this activity is design new TWT topologies for space HPAs at Ka-band, capable to handle high average power (beyond 160 W) and a peak power higher than 2000W BOL. The TWT based on a new topology shall be designed and experimentally validate. One breadboard will be designed, manufactured, and rigorously tested to validate its performance. The activity aims to reach TRL 4.

title: RYDBERG RECEIVER-BASED MICROWAVE RADIOMETER - EXPRO+
description: Microwave radiometer instruments play a crucial role in Earth Observation (EO) by retrieving key atmospheric parameters such as humidity, chemical composition, temperature, and pressure. These measurements are essential for numerical weather prediction algorithms and climate monitoring. Conventional microwave radiometers operate across multiple frequency bands, often requiring complex receiver front-end architectures with low-noise amplifiers (LNAs) and frequency mixers. Rydberg atom-based quantum sensors offer a promising alternative for microwave radiometry with sensitivity enhancement as main driver. By leveraging the sensitivity of Rydberg atoms to electric fields, such sensors enable direct, absolute measurements of microwave radiation without the need for conventional amplification or mixing stages. The objective of this activity is to develop a microwave radiometer based on Rydberg receiver technology and assess its performance, including potential calibration strategies. The activity will focus on the detailed design of the radiometer, identifying suitable architectures, critical system components and evaluating achievable sensitivity and stability. Dedicated test campaigns for the building block selection, sub-system de-risking, radiometer lab model testing and full integration radiometer prototype is required for step-by-step de-risking purposes. A full breadboard of the Rydberg-based integrated receiver will be developed to experimentally validate its performance, including stability aspects. The results will be compared with existing microwave radiometer technologies in terms of radiometer performance, size, and mass. This activity aims to demonstrate Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4.

title: RFI DETECTION AND MONITORING INSTRUMENT DEMONSTRATOR
description: Passive and active Earth Observation (EO) instruments operate in a very wide variety of frequency ranges expanding from Very High Frequency (VHF) to hundreds of gigahertz (GHz). Microwave instruments are equipped with very sensitive receivers, capable of measuring Earth's geophysical parameters from signals generated or reflected by Earth's surface or atmosphere. Most of the instruments are designed to make use of specific frequency ranges which are regulated worldwide through the Radio Regulations of the International Telecommunication Union. However, radio-frequency interferences (RFI) can corrupt the acquired data. This is particularly true in the range going from L-band up to few tens of GHz as shown in multiple technical publications, and this is also where the number of ground communication systems is expected to increase rapidly in the next few years. With the advent of raising human terrestrial activity and broadband microwave instruments for Earth Observation where both protected and unprotected bands can be sensed, a good knowledge regarding worldwide RFI presence and distribution is required. Some bands of interest for EO are not protected by international regulations. This is because regulations are the outcome of compromises among several spectrum users. This knowledge about existing RFI can help to ensure the feasibility as well as an efficient design approach for new EO missions, including an optimum use of the allocated/available bandwidth for the operation of the instruments and a tailored RFI detection and, of required, mitigation strategy. Existing and under-development RF monitoring systems are tailored for specific frequency bands and they do not cover the range of interest for Earth Observation missions.The system under consideration here would help gain global knowledge about RFI in a large number of frequency bands used by future EO missions and do so in a consistent way across frequencies. Several of the targeted bands are used by EO sensors, but the bands used for the communication links in X- and Ka-band are also covered. Data from this system would help protect EO instruments in multiple ways, including selection of frequency, minimization of data loss in EO instruments and design of suitable receiver chain. TRL for the building blocks of an RFI monitoring system (antenna, RF Front End, on-board digital processing) has been increased in the last years through exhaustive trade-off and selection of the most suitable solutions for, among others, the algorithms for spectrum monitoring, RFI detection and localisation. The objective of this activity is to perform the detailed design of a compact and cost-efficient in-orbit RFI mapping system capable to cover the range of frequencies where the protection of EO sensors is most critical. The activity aims to reach TRL 4 for all critical mission elements for a future in-orbit demonstration on-board a CubeSat platform. TRL level will be increased by breadboarding tasks in representative space hardware to be assembled and tested in a laboratory environment in a mock-up CubeSat platform. The ground/space data processing tools will be also developed.

title: NV MAGNETOMETER FOR EARTH OBSERVATION - EXPRO+
description: Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) magnetometers utilize quantum defects in diamond to achieve high-sensitivity magnetic field sensing. They offer compactness, highly localized vector measurement capabilities, intrinsic orthogonality, high dynamic range and potentially high accuracy measurements through calibration to fundamental constants. This is making them promising alternatives to traditional magnetometer technology for Earth observation applications. However, challenges related to sensor integration, noise reduction, and long-term stability must be addressed first. This activity aims to develop a Nitrogen-Vacancy-based magnetometer to demonstrate the technology's competitiveness for future Earth observation missions. The activity begins with a requirement analysis and feasibility study to identify a concept and subsystem requirements necessary to comply with the requirements, assess feasibility, and produce a preliminary Interface Control Document (ICD). Following this, a detailed design and simulation task will be conducted, focusing on system architecture, thermomechanical, electromagnetic and optical simulations, and circuit development to refine the magnetometer concept. Based on this design, high-risk subsystems that require further validation will be identified and breadboarding activities executed to mitigate integration and performance uncertainties. Finally, the magnetometer development and testing will involve constructing a full, structurally integrated magnetometer, performing functional validation, and calibration. The magnetometer's performance will be thoroughly assessed at a suitable facility, and comprehensive documentation will be prepared to support future developments and potential deployment in Earth observation missions. This activity aims to demonstrate Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4.

title: C-BAND VERY HIGH POWER LOW LOSS FERRITE SWITCHES AND CIRCULATORS
description: Active remote sensing instruments such as Scatterometers or Synthetic Aperture Radars operate at peak power levels of few kilowatts and average power levels which can reach few hundred of watts. Ferrite switches and circulators are key building blocks for the RF front-ends of these type of instruments, performing functions such as protection of High Power Amplifier, matching functions and signal routing. Several ferrite switches are cascaded when higher isolation between Tx and Rx needs to be achieved or simply due to the high number of ports in a routing network. Insertion losses play an important role in terms of instrument performance. By careful material, topology and magnetisation point selection (for circulators), the optimum operating point regarding losses and power handling capabilities can be achieved. The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test C-band very high power low loss ferrite switch and circulator.

title: NEW EARTH OBSERVATION MISSION IDEAS (NEOMI) - EXPRO+
description: NEOMI is a new element addressing the scientific preparation of new mission ideas at a very early stage before entering Phase 0. Its primary goals are to scientifically mature novel and early mission ideas, and to prepare scientists to get involved in the definition, design, and implementation of future space missions. Within the framework of this activity up to three individual contracts (of 250 kEuro each) are awarded to develop ideas for an EO mission and to mature the science. The scientific developments comprise: Identifying a scientific problem or a societal challenge that can be addressed by a satellite mission, establishing a scientific objective for the future space mission, drafting a specific mission objective and outlining the related observational requirements. Finally, a measurement concept shall be proposed and justified. As part of these development activities, the successful consortia shall attend ESA's On-Boarding workshop and present their ideas to scientist and engineers working at the Agency. Are you ready to boost future Earth Observation space missions?

title: ULTRA DEEP SUB-MICRON INTERFACE AND SYSTEM-IN-PACKAGE TECHNOLOGY - RE-ISSUE
description: To develop, industrialise and perform ESCC evaluation of the European highspeed interfaces for the Ultra Deep Sub-Micron Processors and FPGAs in a System in Package (SiP).The electrical power available in space is a precious resource and sets bounds on the functionality and performance realisable in spacecrafts. Advances in semiconductor technology over years have been able to push these boundaries further afield for Telecommunications, Earth-observation,Exploration and Science missions. Thanks to ESA, EC and national funding FPGA Brave Family and GR7xx microprocessors have been successfully developed using 65nm and 28nm technologies. New technologies (e.g. N7 or Finfet 7nm) have much to offer to the next generation of devices and wouldtarget a fourfold increase in digital gate density, power efficiency and highspeed serial line communication speed. Indeed, the 112Gbps high-speed serial interface cannot be realised on the FDSOI 28/22nm technology.The increasing cost and complexity of the advanced technology necessitates to leverage the existing Intellectual Property (IP) core functional blocks to the fullest extent. Only moving those functions that benefit significantly from a port and/or enhancement to the new technology should be considered. Specifically, the digital logic and high-speed serial interfaces are prime candidates. Slower and higher voltage as well as analog functionality should remain in the FDSOI 28/22nm, where cost of their port does not weight up against the accrued benefit.This approach, also known as chiplet architecture, uses a low-latency low power die-to-die interface on an organic substrate to link the different dies in the current technologies (FDSOI 28/22nm) and most advanced technologies (N7 and below). This chiplet architecture paradigm allows a larger number of components to be realised through reuse, scalability and the addition of new chiplets. As a result, the total system development cost and time to market for a component is significantly reduced. The practical implementation of this chiplet architecture approach in suitable packages will also be the objective of the activities defined in the technology line UDMS of the GSTP EEE Component Initiative.This activity aims to develop the High Speed Serial Interface up to 112Gbps in Finfet technology (N7 or below) and to demonstrate compatibility with optical transceivers at 112Gbps with SiP technologies. The activity is divided into 4 phases.The aim of the first phase is to consolidate the selection of requirements for the interfaces and Ultra Deep Sub-Micron (UDSM) technology (node N7 and below), as well as Multi-Chip Module (MCM) System in Package (SiP), wherein these will be validated and ESCC evaluated. The UDSM interfaces required by the telecom processor, microprocessor and FPGA are Double Data Rate (DDR) memory interfaces, the die-to-die (D2D) interface, 112Gbps High Speed Serial Interface (HSSL) supporting both 400G Ethernet and PCIe up to Gen 5 and additional UDSM supporting functionality. The collective is henceforth referred to as the UDSM Interface library. Furthermore, the requirements will be determined for the SiP component representative of the UDSM FPGA or processors containing these interfaces.Environmental operational conditions will be defined for the interface library elements and package. Where already existing, the interfaces will be electrically, and radiation tested to assess the degree of technology maturity and radiation mitigation necessary. License conditions for the use of the European UDSM interface technology in space components for all consortiummembers shall be agreed upon as well as access to the UDSM foundation and platform library. Alignment with future customers technical and commercial requirements shall be ensured. The demonstrator chip for UDSM interface library and SiP package to be ESCC evaluated will be defined, representative of future processors, domain specific accelerators and/or FPGAs in the UDSM technology.In the second phase the interface library elements will be developed with emphasis on low power consumption and operation in space. Due regard shall be given to their future integration into telecom processors, microprocessors and FPGA with proper pinout layout, IP and package models. The interfaces will be integrated into the demonstrators chips to ensure comprehensivevalidation with at least a representative future processor, domain specific accelerator and/or FPGA. Where necessary test chips shall be manufactured to de-risk the silicon design as well as its operation in the selected SiP package and on a Printed Circuit Board (PCB). Design validation with the test chips as well as performance analysis in the laboratory will be performed to ensure that future implementations will meet performance and functionality requirements.Radiation mitigation techniques for the selected UDSM technology shall be established and verified either by simulation or by radiation testing. The MCM SiP package to contain the demonstration integrated circuit will be designed that ensures complete electrical validation of the interface library elements and further compatibility testing with electro-optical transceivers. The accompanying PCBs will facilitate the validation testing, electrical as well as environmental and provide a demonstration board for the technology.In the third phase the UDSM interface library elements will be manufactured on a demonstration chip. The MCM SiP package will be manufactured and assembled with the demonstration chip(s) together with PCB to enable electrical validation as well as compatibility testing with electro-optical transceivers. Environmental testing will be performed to verify correct operation in the representative space environment. The signal transmission performance will be measured and characterised with suitable electrical equipment. Where necessary improvements to the design will be implemented and provided for manufacture and testing such that the final version of the design can be demonstrated to work inside current and/or future UDSM processor and FPGA.In the fourth phase the component, consisting of the SiP package containing the demonstrator chips, will be ESCC evaluated to establish the perimeter for which future products containing these interfaces and packages can be ESCC qualified.This activity will benefit from synergies with other activities of the GSTP EEE Component (e.g. SiP qualification, co-packaged optics).The 4-phases activity encompasses the following tasks:Phase 1: Specification and Initial Validation of UDSM Interface and SiP Technology- Consolidation of application, commercial and development needs as well as constraints (time to market, license for technology and IP access, quality, package availability, ...), technical specificatis, manufacturing, validation and ESCC evaluation requirements- Consolidation of the requirements for UDSM interfaces and MCM SiP package, including a flow down from all the application use cases- Determination of the demonstrator chips and SiP requirement specification- Feasibility analysis of technical requirements with technology trade-off, risk analysis including development and commercial needs and constraints (time to market, cost, license agreements, package availability, ) leading to a develop plan with smart decision gates for the activity phases and consortium organisation with commercial and licensing arrangement- Review of the interface application cases- Review available package implementation options- Review of the demonstrator chips and SiP requirement specification- Develop plan for each of the interfaces and controllers (DDR, HSSL, D2D, ..) as well as additional supporting UDSM functionality including design, validation, demonstration, future implementation and ESCC evaluation- Develop plan for the MCM SiP package including design, validation, demonstration, future implement

title: EARTH OBSERVATION SENSORS RFI TOOLBOX - EXPRO PLUS
description: Earth Observation missions operate under the Earth Exploration Satellite Service (EESS) of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). Passive and active Earth Observation (EO) sensors operate in a very wide variety of frequency ranges expanding from around 40 MHz to hundreds of GHz, and each frequency band allows the observation of specific geophysical parameters of the Earth's system.Other services also try to grow their capabilities by exploiting new frequency bands, sometimes in the same bands or in bands adjacent to those used by EO sensors; this also requires interference analyses to be carried out. In this context, the need for proper simulation tools to perform interference analyses between EO sensors and ground-based systems operating or planning to operate in the same frequency bands or in adjacent frequency bands becomes apparent.The objective of the activity is to develop a software which would enable interference studies involving EO sensors (active and passive) and ground-based systems. The following scenarios are to be included:-Interference from ground-based systems into passive EO sensors-Interference from ground-based systems into active EO sensors-Interference from active EO sensors into ground-based systemsThe software has to include also a library of all the propagation effects that may be relevant for the studies outlined above.

title: MAINTENANCE AND OPERATIONAL SUPPORT SERVICES FOR THE ESTRACK GROUND STATIONS OF MALARGUE KOUROU AND INTEGRATED LOGISTIC SUPPORT SERVICES - 2026-2031 (5+5 YEARS)
description: The subject of this procurement is the Maintenance and Operation (MO) Services for the Kourou Malarge Stations, as well as Integrated Logistic Support (ILS) Services for the ESA Tracking Stations Network (ESTRACK). The procurement will cover three service domains: MO Services for the ESTRACK 3rd Deep Space Station (DS-3) in Malarge, Argentina.MO Services for the ESTRACK Ground Station "Diane" in Kourou, French Guiana.ESTRACK Operations Control Centre (OCC) related ILS Services at ESOC including the maintenance of the ESTRACK Configuration Data Base (ECDB) and other related tools. It is envisaged that these domains may be awarded under a single contract or, depending on the outcome of the competition, distributed across multiple contracts (further explanation isprovided in the section "Justification of Proposed Procedure" below). A detailed description of the above-mentioned service domains is as follows: The Maintenance and Operational Support Services for DS-3 comprise: The provision of public services (electrical power, water, office communication, etc) required for the operation of the station.The provision of the site security services (guarding).The provision of the on-site maintenance services for the operational equipment and site facilities.The provision of theoperational support services at the site.The provision of logistic support for all operational components exchanged between Europeand Argentina. The Maintenance and Operational Support Services for the "Diane" Station in Kourou comprises: The provision of the on-site maintenance services for the operational equipment and site facilities.The provision of the operational support servicesat the site.The interface with CNES/CSG for the provision of the logistic and general services (power, water, sewage, communication, security, etc). The ESTRACK OCC Integrated Logistic Support (EILS) Services comprises the provision of logistic support services including handling of spares, repairs, shipment/transport, custom supervision, documentation management, asset management support, evolution of the services through engineering activities, the maintenance and tailoring of the ECDB (ESTRACK Configuration Database) and support the Agency for the ESTRACK asset management. The phase-in as required in one or all above domains shall be provided during the three-months period from 1st of August until 31st of October 2026, i.e. until the end of the current contract. The proposed procurement action requires an estimated total maximum funding of up to 65 M covering the 5-year base period plus an optional 5-year extension, distributed across each domain and the phase-in.
