Description: The subject of this procurement is the Maintenance and Operation (MO) Services for the Kourou Malarge Stations, as well as Integrated Logistic Support (ILS) Services for the ESA Tracking Stations Network (ESTRACK). The procurement will cover three service domains: MO Services for the ESTRACK 3rd Deep Space Station (DS-3) in Malarge, Argentina.MO Services for the ESTRACK Ground Station "Diane" in Kourou, French Guiana.ESTRACK Operations Control Centre (OCC) related ILS Services at ESOC including the maintenance of the ESTRACK Configuration Data Base (ECDB) and other related tools. It is envisaged that these domains may be awarded under a single contract or, depending on the outcome of the competition, distributed across multiple contracts (further explanation isprovided in the section "Justification of Proposed Procedure" below). A detailed description of the above-mentioned service domains is as follows: The Maintenance and Operational Support Services for DS-3 comprise: The provision of public services (electrical power, water, office communication, etc) required for the operation of the station.The provision of the site security services (guarding).The provision of the on-site maintenance services for the operational equipment and site facilities.The provision of theoperational support services at the site.The provision of logistic support for all operational components exchanged between Europeand Argentina. The Maintenance and Operational Support Services for the "Diane" Station in Kourou comprises: The provision of the on-site maintenance services for the operational equipment and site facilities.The provision of the operational support servicesat the site.The interface with CNES/CSG for the provision of the logistic and general services (power, water, sewage, communication, security, etc). The ESTRACK OCC Integrated Logistic Support (EILS) Services comprises the provision of logistic support services including handling of spares, repairs, shipment/transport, custom supervision, documentation management, asset management support, evolution of the services through engineering activities, the maintenance and tailoring of the ECDB (ESTRACK Configuration Database) and support the Agency for the ESTRACK asset management. The phase-in as required in one or all above domains shall be provided during the three-months period from 1st of August until 31st of October 2026, i.e. until the end of the current contract. The proposed procurement action requires an estimated total maximum funding of up to 65 M covering the 5-year base period plus an optional 5-year extension, distributed across each domain and the phase-in.

title: ONTOLOGY DEPLOYMENT CAPABILITY - EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesTo enable the Space System Ontology formal models to be disseminated and used to implement interoperability of MBSE toolsDescriptionThe ESA Agenda 2025 mandates the digitalisation of ESA projects. The main issue to be solved is the interoperability of tools. Tools can be interoperable if the data to be exchanged has a common meaning, a common semantic. This is achieved by developing an ontology. The Space System Ontology is under development using a formal language. It is possible to use the formal model to (i) initialize a documentation of the ontology by verbalization of the model, (ii) create a data base allowing to populate the ontology (i.e. to create instances of the object types defined in the ontology) and (iii) create tools allowing to translate various different physical representations of the same concepts.This allows to verify that a concept expressed in a MBSE tool is compliant to the ontology, and to translate it into another MBSE tool. Typical application examples are translation of MBSE models between Capella,Cameo, Enterprise Architect, or European Ground Segment Engineering Framework, including translation between various SysML representations, leading to interoperability between the tools of LSIs, and Agencies. Another goal is to configure the Data Hub, a central tool ensuring digital continuity between different engineering tools. In particular, to be effective, the ontology must be supported by automation to enable interoperability of tools and enable configuration of tools.A potential solution for (i) is to use the so-called "derivations" of Object Role Modelling (ORM) that describes the semantic equivalence of a concept expressed by two stakeholders, and to generate a translator between these two expressions. This translator is then complemented with the exporter/importer from the specific tools of the stakeholders. The solution for (ii) targets in particular the data hubs, that need to be adaptable to potential updates or refinement of the ontology, without forcing a change of the data hub code. It may depend on the selected data hub, and targets mainly the Model Based Engineering Data Hub (MBEH) and the GSEF (for GS OPS aspects).This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Identification of exploitation tools in compliance with the progress of the Data Hub and the needs of industry and projects at the time of procurement.- Specification of the tools- Design and development of the tools- Verification and validation of the tools- Demonstration of the tools for several scenario of exchange between various tools and various stakeholders.Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence.

title: EXPLORATION OF AGENTIC AI AND DECISION INTELLIGENCE FOR EO - EXPRO+
description: Agentic AI and Decision Intelligence (DI) are shaping the future of many domains, promising to provide a framework where autonomous, goal-driven AI agents are integrated with data analytics, social science, decision theory, managerial science and human expertise to support the decision-making process. In Earth Observation, Agentic AI can automatically synthesize multi-source data and generateactionable insights, while Decision Intelligence can ensure these insights translate into transparent, explainable, and policy-relevant decisions. Together, they form a new paradigm for turning vast data into timely, adaptive, and intelligent actions. The objective of this activity is to perform a six months theoretical and methodological study on the integration of Agentic AI and Decision Intelligence and its application to Earth Observation to support decision-making in a broad set of fields, such as climate change, environmental monitoring, sustainability, adaptation, disasters response, security and resilience.

title: PREDICTIVE QUALITY OF SERVICE (QOS) PROTOCOL FOR NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORKS IN SUPPORT OF AUTOMOTIVE SERVICES (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.023)
description: Objective:This objective of this activity is to develop and test an extended protocol to address the support of predictive Qualityof Service (QoS) in Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs). The activity will also undertake the necessary investigation and selection of data-driven algorithms to automate predictive QoS in NTN.Targeted Improvements:Features enhancement to align NTN solutions in an integrated NTN/TN ecosystem in support to automotive services. This is a critical technology element to enable support of important automotive use cases.Description:The 5G Automotive Association (5GAA) has developed the concept of predictive Quality of Service (QoS), now part of 3GPP standards for Terrestrial Networks (TN). This method allows to adjust application behaviour before the predicted QoS change takes effect, which is important in certain automotive use cases, such as remote and autonomous driving. QoS is measured in an objective way in 5G 3GPP for Terrestrial Networks (TN), this is done via a set of 5G QoS attributes [3GPP TS 23.501 cl. 5.7], e.g., packed delay budget and error rate. However, an equivalent or similar method is not available for NTN. The proposed activity will therefore investigate, trade-off, select and validate the following aspects: 1) model for services adaptation over NTN (e.g., LEO and/or multilayer NTN), time requirements, exchanging info in cars and network components (e.g., edge computer in car); 2) develop the architecture and the interfaces for integrated NTN/TN; 3) consider different deployment options of QoS provision in single/multiple operator domain and multiple MEC deployments typical in automotive i.e. roadside/car/onboard satellite; 4) develop prototype solutions and validate through testbed; 5) perform over-the-air demonstrations

title: OPEN REPROGRAMMABLE SPACE INFRASTRUCTURE TESTBED FOR BEYOND 5G (B5G) END-TO-END SOLUTIONS AND SERVICES (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3E.019)
description: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a reprogrammable testbed in space to permit the experimentation of Beyond 5G (B5G) satellite features and capabilities and enable technology verification and demonstration; rapid validation of end-to-end solutions and services, following the principles of continuous development/continuous integration. B5G satellitefeatures will be implemented in the testbed as part of the activity to demonstrate its capabilities.Targeted Improvements:Enabling development infrastructure for B5G satellite systems not existing today.Description:With the establishment of Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) firmly as part of 3GPP rel. 17, we are witnessing efforts for the validation of initial designs and deployments of integrated terrestrial (TN) and NTN networks to offer Enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB) and Internet-of-Things (IoT) services.Nonetheless, the work to define Beyond 5G (B5G)/towards 6G continues with the roadmap rapidly evolving alongside the 3GPP standardisation process, e.g., NTN enhancements included in rel. 18, advanced NTN features already proposed for Rel. 19 and initial assessments of B5G/towards 6G space infrastructure. However, evaluating the implementation of new architectures is challenging mainly due to immaturity of technology and lack of means for continuous development and validation of new capabilities, which hinders the time to market for NTN solutions.The objective of the activity is then to develop and test a reprogrammable testbed for space infrastructure to permit the experimentation of 5G/6G satellite features and capabilities and enable technology verification and demonstration; rapid validation of end-to-end solutions and services, following the principles of continuous development/ continuous integration. The testbed will implement featuresbased on mid to longer term technology trends such as cross-layer communication, dynamically programmable backhaul, OpenRAN implementations, use of AI/ML onboard, context aware routing and increased importance of security-by-design. Candidate features will be assessed and expected performance, benefits and costs for each will be identified and documented. The activity will implement and demonstrate enhanced NTN features (rel.18/19) in orbit using either transparent or regenerative payloads with onboard storage and computing and routing capabilities and intersatellite links as/if applicable.The testbed could be embarked for example on the ISS, existing/planned smallsats, and/or as hosted payload. The activity will take stock of all ongoing 5G satellite developments and propose convincing demonstrations. The activity will seek synergies with ARTES SPL 5G deliverables and testbeds as well as various European 5Gplatforms and projects and national initiatives that are already being built-up.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach and features will be proposed and implemented by activating CCNs.

title: DRONE-BASED VALIDATION OF OPTICAL GROUND STATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.072) EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop a drone-based testing tool for optical ground stations to enable validation and functioning of their subsystems; prior to engaging with satellite passes.Targeted Improvements:To provide a 99% reliabilityand readiness improvement of optical ground station via realistic testing of optical space-to-ground links, via the de-risking of optical communication links betweenSimulation of a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite pass over an optical ground terminal using a dronesystem.Description:At present, there is limited possibility to validate the pointing, acquisition and tracking (PAT) performance of an optical ground station. Sun-illuminated satellites in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) are commonly used to perform tracking tests, but these tests are not representative with respect to wavelength and dynamics of the link, as well as only able to be executed when the sun is illuminatingthe satellite before nightfall or before sunrise. This activity will solve this testing shortcoming by fullyemulating realistic LEO satellite passes with a drone based representative satellite emulator.This activity shall address these technical problems with the objective to design, build and validate a dronebased platform to endtoend validate optical communication ground terminals for realistic LEO satellite passes and other orbits. A modified optical communication terminal can be flown on a drone, emulating the satellite pass, for realistic testing of the pointing, tracking and acquisition system of the optical ground station, as well as the data transmission. This concept will allow to validate several aspects of optical ground terminals: pointing, acquisition and tracking, ephemeris format processing, optical downlink/uplink, time transfer. The tool shall emulate an optical communication payload on a satellite, so the drone appears as a usual satellite to the optical communications ground terminal. Ground stations can use this platform for validation testing without relying on a satellite time. The following tasks shall be addressed in the frame of this activity: critical assessment to establish satellite equivalent optical link methodologies, simulation and evaluation of optical drone-to-ground station links, development of the required platform for a representative environment, verification, andvalidation of optical ground terminals. Activity deliverables include the software suite to command the on-board components and hardware platform (drone) equipped with all required tools, including the laser terminal.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: CAN BACKPLANE INTERFACE MEZZANINE BOARD - EXPRO PLUS
description: To build a mezzanine board to interface with a CAN bus on the units' backplane.Description:As part of the APA (Advanced Power Architecture) initiative, a standardised approach is being developed for internal communication between APA modules within an APA unit. This activity supports that effort by designing a compact, reusable TM/TC interface based on the CAN bus, known for itsreliabilityand simplicity.The mezzanine will serve as a common building block / solution for all APA modules, reducing integration effortandpromoting consistency across designs. By consolidating all required components into a small footprint, it simplifies system architecture, supports modularity and eases procurement, manufacturing and recurrence.This activity focuses on developing a compact mezzanine PCB that integrates five essential components required for CAN-based backplane communication (FPGA or microcontroller, ADC, voltage reference, CAN transceiver and XTAL/oscillator). The goal is to consolidate these elements into a small 30x30 mm footprint, supporting a range of external interfaces and operating on a 3.3V supply.This modular solution aims to simplify internal communication across systems where CAN is the preferred protocol, offering a reusable and scalable interface.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidate the CAN protocol implementation.- Architecture definition (evaluating if FPGA-based or microcontroller-based).- Identify two suitable options for each one of the 5 required components, prioritising compact packaging and cost.- Design a 30mm x 30 mm PCB accommodating the 5 components and ensuring signal integrity andmanufacturability, ready to be assembled into an APA module and to interface with CAN bus and the APA module.- Implement the software or the VHDL code with the CAN protocol.- Prototyping and testing, assemble and validate the board to confirm functionality and performance.Deliverables: Breadboard,ReportNOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF THE END- TO END PERFORMANCE SIMULATOR FOR ERS EO
description: The scope of the procurement is the development of the End-to-End Performance simulator within Element-1 of the European Resiliencefrom Space, ERS EO programme, in order to perform a functional simulation of the contribution to the end-to-end performance of the Earth Observation Governmental Service (EOGS) system of various federated components, including the EU Member States owned assets accessible through agreed pooling and sharing mechanisms, the European commercial assets and a potential EU-owned core component. The simulator will allow to explore different EOGS scenarios, based on acustomized set of attributes for each system component (number of satellites, orbits, ground segment architecture, transport layer, interfaces and interoperability hypothesis, security architecture and expected scalability of components) and to assess the effectiveness ofvarious pooling and sharing mechanisms. The simulator will allow to run technicooperational scenarios (representative of future potential operations) and compute figures ofmerit, while testing different operation concepts and governance assumptions such as pooling and sharing mechanisms, and supporting the trade-offcost-benefit analysis for the consolidation of the System Architecture for EOGS.

title: E3CX-029 NEXT GENERATION ELECTRIC PROPULSION FOR EXPLORATION STUDY - EXPRO+
description: High-power Hall Effect Thrusters (HETs) are considered a key technology for deep space missions due to their balanced thrust and fuel efficiency, enabling long-distance travel, complex manoeuvres, and reduced mission durations with respect to very-high Isp systems. Compared to gridded ion engines, HETs offer a better balance of thrust and efficiency, with simpler, more robust designs. Their scalability makes them ideal for future missions involving heavy payloads and/or human exploration. Current European and U.S. developments show promising performance at higher voltage that existing high-TRL solutions, but further progress needs to be driven by mission-specific requirements. With this activity, the Agency plans to consolidate the requirements and initial design of a single thruster high-power thruster that is capable to cover the Agency's future Exploration needs.

title: CATHODE FOR OXYGEN-RICH ENVIRONMENT (ARTES 4.0 AT 4B.172) EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE (1-11640)
description: The objective of the activity is to develop, manufacture and test a cathode for use as a neutraliser in electric propulsion systemsand suitable for operation in an oxygen-rich environment for a long duration of time (e.g. >5 years).Targeted Improvements:Enabling cathode capable of operating in an oxygen-rich environment for more than a few hours.Description: Platforms operating in Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) require prolonged and/or continuous use of Electric Propulsion (EP) to counter the atmospheric drag over a very long period of time (>several thousand hours). During this time EP elements will be exposed to an oxygen-rich environment and oxygen could even be used as a propellant. High-efficiency electric propulsion systems typically use an electron emitter, or cathode, toneutralise the flux of positive ions generated and accelerated by the thruster. Current state-of-the-art cathodes are very sensitiveto oxygen exposure due to rapid oxidation of the emitter material. Operation in VLEO requires the cathode element to be redesignedto sustain a constant exposure to atomic oxygen during its operation.This activity will develop and manufacture a breadboard of anelectron-emitter cathode that can act as a neutraliser in a thruster fed with an oxygen-rich working gas. The goal is to achieve extraction efficiency above 95%, less than 250W input power, and an erosion rate sufficiently low to ensure operation for several thousands of hours. The breadboard performance will be tested, and short-duration endurance tests will be carried out. An erosion modelwillbe developed and used to predict and confirm the lifetime of the cathode.

title: S3-CL-03 ERASE PHASE A ACTIVE DEBRIS REMOVAL MISSION FOR LARGE UNPREPARED LEO PLATFORMS - EXPRO+
description: ESA intends to implement a Zero Debris policy by 2030 and has a long-term vision for a sustainable and safe space environment leveraging on the development of a space circular economy.Large Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites in particular present significant risks, both in terms of potential collisions and ground casualty hazards resulting from uncontrolled re-entry. The ESA's Clean Space Office has been pioneering the study of ADR since 2012, starting with the e.Deorbit study, followed by the ClearSpace-1 and the CAT mission in more recent years, under the ADRIOS initiative part of the ESA Space Safety Program. In the past years there has been growing interest in ADR services targeting large LEO debris objects. This topic has recently been the focus of discussions and studies between ESA and external stakeholders, including EUMETSAT in the frame of a feasibility study (e.g. CDF) and the European Commission(EC) via its ISOS framework. This led to the implementation of industrial activities for a 6 month ERASE phase 0 mission and systemstudy which was kicked-off Q1 of 2026.The activity proposed here is to further mature the concept of the ERASE mission up to the Preliminary Requirement Review (PRR) milestone. The result of the activity and the maturation of the ERASE concept should be in linewith the outcomes of an ESA Preliminary Requirements Review as described by the ECSS. If successful, ESA intends to follow this study by the Phase B1 and a eventual full mission implementation acceptance after CMin 2028

title: USE OF EXISTING LEO SIGNALS FOR A NEW HYBRID GENERATION OF EMERGENCY RADIO-BEACONS: FEASIBILITY AND DEMONSTRATION - EXPRO PLUS
description: Current GNSS-based emergency radio-beacons face critical limitations in harsh environments where signal reception is impaired, suchas during natural disasters, under snow or rubble, in war zones with jamming/spoofing, or in areas with limited sky visibility. This proposal aims to explore a disruptive solution: the development and demonstration of a new hybrid generation of emergency radio-beacons that combine GNSS with Low Earth Orbit (LEO) Signals of Opportunity (SoOp) and LEO-based communication (LEO-COM) systems. Theconcept leverages the unique properties of LEO signals, including stronger signal power, diversified frequency bands (e.g., L/S/Ku), global coverage, and improved signal geometry, to enhance resilience, positioning accuracy, and signal availability in GNSS-deniedor degraded environments. In parallel, LEO-COM will be used to transmit auxiliary emergency messages, augmenting the conventional 406 MHz distress signal and enabling faster, more reliable Search and Rescue (SAR) responses. The innovation lies in the integration of multifrequency, multi-constellation LEO/GNSS receivers with LEO-COM communication in a compact, low-power device, tailored for both regulated Safety-of-Life sectors (e.g., aviation, maritime) and mass-market applications (e.g., hikers, mountaineers). The activity will include the design, prototyping, and testing of a handheld or wearable device, validating performance in relevant environments. By moving beyond GNSS-only solutions and embracing LEO-based technologies, this high-risk/high-gain activity has the potential to redefine emergency beaconing capabilities, laying the foundation for a new generation of resilient, globally connected SAR devices, and pushing the boundaries of current emergency location technologies.

title: SMART PROPELLANT TANK (ARTES AT 4B.167)
description: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a smart propellant tank with embedded sensors enabling direct monitoring of internal tank pressure and temperature and active thermal management through embedded heaters.Targeted Improvements:- Increased precision of propellant gauging (20% to 50%)- Improved propellant temperature management- Reduced system-level assembly, integration and test effortDescription:Space propulsion needs constant monitoring of several parameters for both on-ground testing and in-orbit gauging and health monitoring. In typical designs, several standalone equipment is added to the system, such as pressure transducers, thermo-couples and heaters. Each of those external components requires a dedicated design review and needs to be individually tested. Also, they come with additional hardware and management cost due to the several different suppliers involved. Individual components imply increased inaccuracies during the acquisition, which degrades the precision of gauging analysis. Some majorchallenges to overcome in the project include the manufacturing process to embed sensors (i.e. during wrapping), repeatability and calibration of sensor accuracy and positioning, mechanical effects on fibre overwraps and impact on design limits, reliability, and the impact on on-ground assembly, integration and testing if the sensors are damaged. The sensors to be used could include traditional strain gauges, pressure transducers, thermistors, or newer piezo gauges or other sensors. A smart propellant tank, with embedded sensors enabling direct monitoring of internal tank pressure and temperature, and with an active thermal management through embeddedheaters, increases the gauging precision and avoids additional surface mounted pressure transducers and thermistors. This could be achieved for example by using carbon fibre over-wrap, new technologies such as titanium silicon carbide wrap, other filament windingmethods, or 3D printing techniques.An active plug-and-play, reduced-volume tank (Scaled Engineering Model) will be designed, manufactured and tested to verify its performance compared to a conventional tank/thermal equipment/pressure transducer set-up.

title: ARIADNA STUDY - ORGANOID INTELLIGENCE AS A RESERVOIR COMPUTING PARADIGM FOR TIME-SERIES PREDICTION - EXPRO PLUS
description: Future spacecraft will need onboard learning that stays accurate while using very little power and surviving harsh radiation. One promising route is reservoir computing: instead of training a large, power-hungry AI model, you let a complex dynamical system "naturally" transform streaming data, then train only a lightweight readout. This exploratory activity pushes that idea further by using living biology as the reservoir. The activity aims at building a compartmentalized neuronal organoidorganized with a connectome-likewiring patternand use it as a physical computing substrate to learn and predict complex, multi variable chaotic time-series. Building on recent successes with simple cell cultures and simulated whole-connectome systems, this work moves from bio inspired designs to truly biological computingtesting whether structured, connectome guided organoids can deliver robust prediction performance in environments where conventional hardware struggles.

title: RADIATION EFFECTS INSIDE THE SPACECRAFT COMPATIBLE WITH ADHA DEVELOPMENT- EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a breadboard of a radiation detection unit based on Advanced Data Handling Architectures (ADHA) in order to minimise on-board resources, while improving the integration and deployment.Description: The Agency has had success developing and flying radiation monitors, starting with the REM in the 90's, the SREM in the 2000s, and the EMU and NGRMs since 2017. These monitors have all been self contained and externally mounted, with masses and power requirements exceeding 1 kg and 2 W - low resource, butnot insignificant. Some of these instruments have housed dosimeters, but none have provided measurements within the other spacecraft units. At the moment, there are no low resource radiation monitors available capable of integration within the spacecraft and its units where the sensitive systems are located and capable to provide useful, unparalleled feedback to satellite operations. The benefits include enabled monitoring of the spacecraft health, and providing useful operational diagnostics, and accurate information on the environment. Radiation monitors are the first modules to be discarded during phase A of design due to additional mass and power budget constraints. This disrupts the huge potential of in-orbit data collection, which affects radiation model accuracy and uncertainty a measure, Radiation monitor will allow to manage approach to radiation effects, potentially extending mission lifetimes and opening the door to widespread use of COTS. It is envisaged that this should become standard on all platforms as part of S/C 'health' data - as is already done with thermal measurements. In order to enhance the European competitiveness for LEO applications for mid-size satellites, it is aimed to design and test a portfolio of standardized dosimeters and memories. By including the radiation monitors in the Advanced Data Handling architecture (ADHA), standardized, interchangeable, and inter-operable electronics modules equipped with the latest generation of microelectronics components can be integrated within the spacecraft units. Components and commercialprocesses from European foundries and manufacturers shall be baselined for dose measurements. Several configuration can be considered: detection unit embedded into each ADHA board, detection unit placed at different point of ADHA or to be considered as a standalone board. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - A trade-off shall be made between of the different solutions considered -Breadboarding and functional testing - Total ionising Dose and SEE testing - Roadmap to fully characterise and fly European memories once they become availableDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

In order to enhance the European competitiveness for LEO applications for mid-size satellites, it is aimed to design and test a portfolio of standardized dosimeters and memories. By including the radiation monitors in the Advanced Data Handling architecture (ADHA), standardized, interchangeable, and inter-operable electronics modules equipped with the latest generation of microelectronics components can be integrated within the spacecraft units. Components and commercialprocesses from European foundries and manufacturers shall be baselined for dose measurements. Several configuration can be considered: detection unit embedded into each ADHA board, detection unit placed at different point of ADHA or to be considered as a standalone board. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - A trade-off shall be made between of the different solutions considered -Breadboarding and functional testing - Total ionising Dose and SEE testing - Roadmap to fully characterise and fly European memories once they become availableDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

title: ASSESSMENT OF AERO-THERMO-MECHANICAL CYCLING LOADS W.R.T. REUSABILITY: DEFINITION AND IMPACT - EXPRO PLUS
description: To assess the cyclic aero-thermo-mechanical loads, for reusable space transportation systems andthe impact of those loads on the operational lifetime.DescriptionWhen exploiting reusability for transportation vehicles, their lifetime and cost estimation depends on (sub)systems undergoing both low (ascent and re-entry) and high-cyclic loads (vibrations, aerodynamics, thermal) which impacts their lifetime of the used materials and equipment.Currently, no general guidelines or requirements are in place to allow the designer to anticipate thetype of materials to be used in the design, the impact on the performance, cost, etc. Therefore, ageneric approach is needed to lay out the basics for a properly defined system analysis.The activity is aimed to be generic and cover a wide range of reusable concepts. It considers atleast the following elements: a. Evaluation on aero-thermo-mechanical cycling loads b. Providingdesign requirements and approach c. Preparing the basis for the ECSS handbooks and standardsupdates w.r.t. reusability.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Definition of reusable vehicles and their missions in a generic way, covering a wide rangeof conceptual designs and applications.- As the loads differ a lot pending on the ascent and return trajectory, the cyclic loads andtheir impact shall be derived for launchers based on VTVL, VTHL, HTHL. For re-entryvehicles, this is based upon sub-l and super orbital trajectories. Generic vehicles and trajectories are aimed to be used.- Definition of static and cycling loads.- The respective loads and their cycles are aimed to be derived along with variations covering both the external (stagnation regions, surfaces, control surfaces..) as well as the internal flow path i.e. the propulsion units (injectors, combustors, throats, nozzles etc...).discrimination is made for the type of vehicle and the kind of propulsion unit (e.g. liquid, solid, electrical, airbreathing...)-sessment of the dimensioning loads.- A first assessment is aimed to be made upon the sizing loads, both for the internal and external flow paths for the full range of investigated space vehicles in T1. The most dimensioning ones are investigated in more detail and applied on the related vehicles, necessary during a first design loop- Updates of ECSS handbooks and standards.- A generic layout of a handbook drafted making maximum use of the layout of existing handbooks w.r.t. expandable vehicles. Complement them and prepare the design approach for various classes of reusable vehicles.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: DVB/3GPP HYBRID TERMINAL FOR BROADBAND APPLICATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7B.078) - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, develop and test a user terminal integrating DVB and 3GPP functions to enable seamless utilisation of satellite DVB-based systems, satellite 3GPP based systems and terrestrial 3GPP based systems in a single terminal. Targeted Improvements: Foster the integration of conventional satellite interfaces with 3GPP satellite and terrestrial systems. Description: The 5th generation of wireless broadband networks (5G) promised a new paradigm in communications, offering higher transmission rates, higher reliability, very low latency, and connectivity to remote areas. When the 3GPP included NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) features in release 17 of its specification, satellite officially entered the 5G world. As of today, most of satellite broadband systems use the DVB-Sx standard, however as satellite players are starting to experiment with 5G NTN implementations, it is expected that future satellite systems will adhere to this air interface. It is anticipated that both interfaces will co-exist for a long period (considering the life cycle of satellite systems), opening the door to hybrid user terminals that could equally exploit both interfaces. Furthermore, as 5G keeps deploying in the terrestrial infrastructure, such hybrid terminals might combine satellite and terrestrial connectivity as well. This could introduce a variety of advantages in terms of availability (i.e., more systems available for diversity), connectivity resilience (hot link redundancy) and security (i.e. simultaneous data transmission through multiple paths, reducing the risk of data lost and interception). title: T711-902SM INNOVATIVE RESILIENT SATELLITE SPACE SYSTEM DESIGN TECHNOLOGIES FOR ZERO DEBRIS (EXPRO+)
description: Space debris poses a significant risk to operational satellites, with hypervelocity impacts (HVIs) being a major concern. The energy and frequency of such impacts vary across different orbital environments and developing robust spacecraft that can withstand theseimpacts while remaining functional is vital for sustainability. Current shielding technologies struggle with mass and volume constraints, making them less viable for certain missions so more efficient, lightweight, and innovative solutions are required. This activity involves a system level study of potential technologies for HVI shielding, that outputs conceptual designs for implementing those technologies at system level, supported by material testing and simulations. A trade off will highlight the most feasible and promising conceptual designs that merit further work.

title: CLIMATE SPACE: USING EARTH OBSERVATION FOR CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION - EXPRO+
description: The present procurement is issued as part of the ESA CLIMATE-SPACE programme. It builds on and forms part of the work done under the ESA Climate Change Initiative (CCI). Adaptation is the process of adjustment to actual or expected climate and its effects, to moderate harm or exploit beneficial opportunities. The objective of this activity is to investigate the usability of EO to develop new adaptation indicators and/or risk indicators used to monitor adaptation actions. The aim is to develop novel indicators grounded in,or based solely on, EO in several feasibility case studies that can investigate the indicators usability across climate timescales (decades).

title: QUANTUM INFORMATION NETWORK SIMULATOR TOOL DEVELOPMENT (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.212) EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop a quantum network simulation allowing to model, assess the performance and compare various architectures of satellite-based quantum networksTargeted Improvements: Simulator calculating possible distances, qubit exchange rates, state fidelities using satellite links (LEO, MEO, GEO) under realistic conditions with (in near future) available hardware. Description: Designing a quantum network at European and global scale will require a large effort which often is impractical or simply cannot be emulated in the laboratory. Nevertheless, prior to field deployment, network performance needs to be approximated. This requires modelling and development of simulation tools and is particularly relevant for satellite which once in orbit cannot be modified. There is a range of quantum network modelling tools for fixed fibre-based architectures, however, there lack modelling and simulations tools for quantum networks incorporating dynamic satellite links, therefore parameters directly related to satellite connectivity such as free space path through the atmosphere, time delay related to the satellite altitude, inclination, and velocity. This activity will aim to leverage on the existing models while developing a satellite related module of the model that can be based on open access, and as much as possible be compatible with existing modelling tools. Depending on the use case, different key performance indicators (qubit rate, link distance and availability) will be required from the quantum networks. A versatile network simulator should enable to generate these KPI for satellite configurations and allow for integration with similar models for terrestrial fibre based quantum networks. title: LIGHT CONDUCTION AND DIFFUSION MATERIALS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF LIGHT INTENSIFIED PHOTOBIOREACTORS
description: ObjectivesTo increase the efficiency of photobioreactors by an improved design of light conduction anddiffusion inside the reactor.DescriptionThe need for regenerative life support systems for long term space missions necessitates a questfor increased efficiency of Photobioreactors. The light intensification of photobioreactors is animportant building block to increase the return on investment with respect to light energy introducedvs oxygen yield in a defined volume.Previous activities have identified as a priority the need to progress on specific technologies, suchas the type of light sources and on innovative materials for light conductionand diffusion (e.g.polymers, leaking rods, specific optical fibers, lightning fabrics). This activity attempts to push theboundaries of photobioractor efficiency even further (compared to BIORAT-1) by investigating amore efficient light diffusion and as well characterization of the impact on the process and thebiomass.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review the state of the art for light intensified photobioreactiors and energy efficient lightguidance systems- Design a test bench with realistic operational parameters (light, flow, active species etc.)and test the most optimal configuration to achieve best possible efficiency w.r.t. volumetricoxygen and biomass production- Assess the potential biological effects of immersed light sources and possiblecountermeasures against fouling and clogging- Provide a development plan for operational hardware on ground and in space includingMAIT aspects for an operational scenario and define the scaling laws.

This activity attempts to push theboundaries of photobioractor efficiency even further (compared to BIORAT-1) by investigating amore efficient light diffusion and as well characterization of the impact on the process and thebiomass.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review the state of the art for light intensified photobioreactiors and energy efficient lightguidance systems- Design a test bench with realistic operational parameters (light, flow, active species etc.)and test the most optimal configuration to achieve best possible efficiency w.r.t. volumetricoxygen and biomass production- Assess the potential biological effects of immersed light sources and possiblecountermeasures against fouling and clogging- Provide a development plan for operational hardware on ground and in space includingMAIT aspects for an operational scenario and define the scaling laws.

title: NAVISP-EL1-105-HYBRID BLACK-WHITE-MODELLING ESTIMATION AND MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS FOR PNT ENGINES - EXPRO PLUS
description: This activity aims to design, implement, and validate hybrid estimation algorithms for Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) engines, combining traditional optimal estimation techniques (white-box) with machine learning-based methods (black-box). The project will develop a smart oversight controller to dynamically balance performance and computational constraints, ensuring robust and interpretable solutions suitable for safety-critical applications. The hybrid PNT engine will be tested on commercial GNSS receivers in challenging environments, such as urban canyons and multipath scenarios, with the goal of achieving improved accuracy and resource efficiency. The outcome will include a prototype receiver, processing tool, and a roadmap for further development and commercialization.

title: IP CORES FOR HIGH-SPEED ADC DAC INTERFACE - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop and verify reusable digital IP cores fully implementing the JESD204B/C high-speed interface standards, addressing current and future high-speed data acquisition and conversion EEE devices. DescriptionNext generation Earth Observation, Telecom and broadly Software-Defined Radio payloads exploit high-speed Analog-to-Digital (ADC) and Digital-to-Analog (DAC) devices, which requirehigh-speed digital interfaces to cope with the throughput demand in the order of gigabit-per-second (Gbps). Furthermore, these devices are thoroughly used in Multiple-Input/Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems, and therefore require synchronisation for simultaneous operation. Two major protocols are JESD204 and ESISTREAM; while the former is an industry standard adopted by many EEE suppliers, thelatter is supported by one supplier.Commercial JESD204 IP cores exist, but they are either open, but prohibitively expensive; locked to a development tool/device vendor; locked to a given ADC/DAC vendor. Furthermore, these IP cores have not been developed with the Space environment in mind, therefore require hardening against single-event effects (SEEs), which may not be possible due to their closed nature. Meanwhile, ESISTREAM IP, is open source and provided free by the supplier, however its' verification status requires improvement and its' adoption is unclear. With many ESA missions and industry products relying on devices having JESD204 interfaces, it is imperative to have verified, SEE-hardened, configurable and device technology independent IP cores.The provision of aJESD204 IP core covers two different needs simultaneously: interface of ASIC/FPGA with existing EEE components, and a building-block for future EEE ADC/DAC devices. The IP cores will be part of the ESA IP Core's portfolio, making it accessible for future ESA projects and missions, devices and also for smaller companies.Activity encompasses the following tasks: - Study the latest JESD204 standard, derivation of requirements and identification of configurable parameters - Develop verification environment based on Universal Verification Methodology (UVM) - Development of JESD204 IP cores for Transmit and Receive in VHDL, and verification using UVMframework - Development of user-friendly IP core configuration tool for tailoring based on specific device/mode requirements - Synthesis on representative FPGA devices: space-qualified BRAVE, RTG4/PolarFire and COTS (Xilinx) - Trial synthesis for selected ASIC targets - Laboratory demonstrator with representative FPGA and data conversion devices - Produce User Manuals, with integration guidelines

title: ANNULAR FOCUSING PLANAR LENS FOR (MULTIPLE-BEAM) CONICAL SCANNING IMAGERS - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop an annular focusing planar lens for conical scanning imagers. Description Conical scanning is required for different earth observation missions based on radar and radiometric instruments. Two mission concepts submitted to the Earth Explorer 11 campaign proposed this kind of solution, Wivern and Stream. Typically, this specific beam scanning is achieved by spinning the entire antenna system around the nadir axis. Although effective, this solution presents several problems. Specifically, vibrations can cause de-pointing which might impact the instrument performance. Moreover, mass is an issue since the rotation of the full antenna system requires counterweights of similar mass.An annular focusing quasi-optical system can be used to simplify the mechanical beam steering solution. In fact, this particular configuration presents an annular focus region which matches the conical scanning requirement. Annular focusing reflectors have been shown to provide good performance in one scanning plane. However, an offset configuration will limit the performance in the rest of the field of view.The activity aims at defining an annular focusing planar lens solution which is symmetric and can achieve similar performance over all the scanning planes. The study focuses on the requirements of the mission concepts such as Stream, Ka-band, proposed at the Earth Explorer 11 campaign or GPM Core Observatory Ku and Ka-band instruments, measuring precipitation from low-earth orbit. Different configurations shall be compared, such as planar printed single, dual lenses and onstrained lenses. A focal plane array can be used to generate the spot beams along the annular focusing region. If the number ofrequired feeds is too large, a simple mechanically spinning feed shall be considered and compared in terms of complexity with a fullysampled solution. More than one concentric rings of feeds can be used to generate multiple-beams allowing simultaneous observationsat different angles. A trade-off shall be carried out in terms of scanning capabilities, mass, efficiency and thermal stability. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Consolidation of the requirements - Trade-off analysis among several solutions and identification of the most promising antenna configuration- Design and detailed analysis Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: ROBUST LASER SAFETY SUB SYSTEM BASED ON REAL-TIME VIDEO DATA - T812-701GS (EXPRO+)
description: Objectives:Design a multi-tier passive laser safety system for the safe automated operation of laser (Class 4) emitting optical ground stations.Develop and validate an image recognition based real-time laser-aircraft collision warning system with low failure probability, using cameras in different spectral regions.Demonstrate low failure probability by integrating and testing the developedsystem in a suitable, existing laser ranging station.Description:Upcoming operational networks of Laser Ranging Stations (LRS; e.g. for Galileo 2nd Generation (G2G) orbit monitoring or for commercial debris collision avoidance services) require full robotic operation.A key enabling element of such optical ground stations is a failure proof recognition of aircrafts in the surrounding airspace, to avoid collision of the laser beam with the aircraft. It is essential that one can demonstrate the robustness of the system and agree with local authorities on procedures to get an operational permission to operate such a Class-4 laser based ranging stations. Any single sensor alone (e.g. visible cameras, infrared cameras, air traffic transponders and collision warning system) does notcover all air traffic (ground traffic is easily covered with existing proven methods). Data fusion of all receivers is required. Monitoring cameras with failure-proof image recognition are the missing element to replace an observer that is required by most authorities. The observer is a show-stopper for any operational application, as it drives operational cost and does not allow a fully integrated measurement and operation pipeline.This activity thus addresses the failure-proof aircraft image recognition system in a sensor combination of cameras in different spectral regions.In a follow-on activity, it is intended to integrate this sub-system intoan overall passive laser safety system at higher TRL, together with the remaining non-optical air traffic detection systems, and validate the failure tolerance of the overall system.C3: Activity restricted to SMEs RD organisations, preferably in cooperation

title: HIGH SPECIFIC POWER PHOTOVOLTAIC ASSEMBLY COMPONENTS AND MODULES (ARTES AT 4F.174) - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test thin solar cells, a photovoltaic assembly (PVA) module of very high specific power (140 W/kg) and develop new processes for solar cell thinning, welding, laydown.Targeted Improvements:Doubling the specific power of the state-of the art photovoltaic assembly with standard rigid solar arrays (benchmark 60-70 W/kg) Description: In recent years, flexible solar arrays have become more popular as they enable lighter and thinner structures and solar cells. However, the current technology for the rest of thephotovoltaic assembly, such as protective shielding, diode, cell interconnection and suitable interconnection solutions, compatible with the necessary low mass and flexibility requirements, are not yet available.This activity will design, manufacture and test thin solar cells, a photovoltaic assembly (PVA) breadboard of very high specific power (140 W/kg) and develop new processes for solar cell thinning, welding and lay down. This includes lift-off and handlingprocesses of thinned solar cells as well as solutions for interconnection of solar cells and welding technologies allowing for embedding shielding material into a laminate. Different innovative PVA concepts based on low mass and flexible technologies will be investigated,breadboarded and tested.

title: S2P P2 S2-VS-04 SPACE-BASED OPTIMISED SMALL SPACE DEBRIS DETECTION SIMULATION
description: The development of space debris population models and of architecture analyses of sensor networks depends on reliable detection simulation software. While such software exists for ground-based detectors, its adaptation to space-based platforms to address emergingspace-based small debris detection systems in Europe and globally is missing. title: DEVELOPMENT OF A EUROPEAN SIC SUBSTRATE SOURCE FOR GAN MMICS - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop European high-purity semi-insulating SiC substrates for manufacturing of GaN MMICs.Description: Gallium Nitride (GaN) Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuits (MMIC) are key components for all space applications and are commonly used in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) for Earth Observation satellites and in Solid State Power Amplifiers (SSPA) for Navigation, Telecommunication and Science missions. Currently, European GaN MMIC foundries are dependent on non-european sources for HPSI (High-purity semi-insulating) Silicon Carbide (SIC) substrates needed as base material for Gallium Nitride (GaN) epitaxial growth and manufacturing of high performance GaN MMICs. This dependency on non-European material is identified as a major risk for future availability of European GaN-on-SiC MMICs. The objective of this activity is to develop a European source for HPSI 4" SiC substrates satisfying the needs of European GaN foundries in terms of substrate quality, availability and cost. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Market analysis for the definition of the user needs - Baseline process definition (crystal growth, material purification and substrate processing) and preliminary validation - SiC substrate growth and processing trials - SiC Substrate quality characterization (insulation, bowing, defects density, etc.) - Assessment of suitability with respect to epitaxial GaN growth - Industrialisation roadmapdefinition.Deliverables: Breadboard, Reporthttp://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: DESIGNING SATCOM MISSIONS TO ENSURE DARK AND QUIET SKIES (ARTES FP 1D.025) EXPRO+
description: The recent deployment of large communication satellite constellations has significantly increased both electromagnetic emissions and reflections from in-orbit spacecraft, impacting ground and space-based astronomical observatories. This study will therefore seek to develop emission and reflectivity recommendations applicable to future satcom satellites, balancing the needs of both astronomersand satcom operators and manufacturers. The activity will include consultation with stakeholders from both communities to generate mutually acceptable recommendations for achievable and verifiable requirements, as well as a technology development roadmap for anynew capabilities implied.

title: SPACE-BASED INTER-DOMAIN ROUTING ARCHITECTURES (ARTES FP 1C.046) EXPRO+
description: The goal of this study is to explore the feasibility, implications, and complementarity of space-based inter-domain routing compared to the ground-based approach currently employed within large satcom networks. (I.e. establishing IXPs in orbit). The study will assess the technological, economic, regulatory, legal, and operational factors to identify the most viable and beneficial approach forfuture global satellite communications infrastructure, and hence generate insights into both the viability and advantages of transitioning from ground-based inter-domain routing to a space-based approach for future satcom systems.

title: SINGLE APERTURE TRANSMIT-RECEIVE PHASED ARRAY ANTENNA FOR KA BAND TERMINALS (ARTES AT 7B.083) - EXPRO+
description: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test a single aperture transmit-receive flat panel antenna for broadband applications in Ka band.Targeted Improvements: Decrease of antenna surface by up to 40% compared to separate aperture design.Description:An increasing number of Non-Geostationary Satellite Orbit (NGSO) constellations using Ka band in the user link, have engaged into concrete plans for deployment. A key element of these systems is the user terminal, which needs to offer enhanced flexibility and compactness whilst remaining cost effective. The ability for these terminals to support transmit receive (Tx/Rx) modes with a single radiating array aperture (as already available in Ku band) would significantly reduce the antenna dimensions compared to a solution utilising separate antennas for Tx and Rx. Combining Tx and Rx is challenging to implement in Ka-band due to the large gap between downlink l (17.2-21.2 GHz) and uplink (27.5-31 GHz) frequencies in contrast to Ku-band where the frequency gap is much smaller. For these reasons, at present, most of Ka-band flat panel user terminals are based on separate Tx and Rx antennas. Promising solutions are emerging to overcome such constraints, for example interlaced array designs and polarisation discrimination between Txand Rx to achieve improved isolation. This activity will develop a partial prototype of a reduced size Tx/Rx antenna array in Ka band. The partial prototype shall implement the antenna array and the beamforming, either analogue, digital or hybrid, and be of sufficient scale to demonstrate the performance of the overall antenna. A reduced size Tx/Rx phased array hardware prototype of a broadband user terminal antenna will be manufactured, tested and the performance compared to a solution employing 2 separate antennas.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. title: 500 AMPERE CLASS POWER UNIT FOR ONBOARD PAYLOAD SIGNAL PROCESSING HARDWARE IN COMMUNICATION SATELLITES (ARTES AT 5C.516)
description: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test a 500A class power unit capable of supplying DC power for both large on-board and AI processors for use in communication satellites.Targeted Improvements: Improved current supply capability of voltage regulators by a factor of ten enabling the use of high performance AI processors (GPUs and TPUs) in future telecom satellites.Description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) processors, such as those based on Graphics Processing Units (GPU) or Tensor Processor Units (TPU) can consume hundreds or even thousands of watts of power. European available rad-hard power supply solutions are available for high performance FPGAs but limited to a few amps and are not suitable for AI processors. To enable the application of AI in satellite communications it is necessary to address the challenges required by those processors, of very high supply currents. Promising concepts exist in terrestrial applications for data centres such as Point of Load regulators, multi-phase buck converters and fixed-ratio isolated converters. Together with the use of GaN power devices, power supply solutions are now in reach to achieve the power output and high currents needed for AI processors. Hence this activity will develop a very high current and high power processingunit for high performance AI processors up to 500A and a breadboard will be manufactured and tested.

title: ADVANCED HETEROGENEOUS INFERENCE DATA PROCESSING MODULE - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop a modular data processing module for missions that will require extreme processing power, high speed serial interfaces and AI acceleration, to produce on board data products or to handle very high data rates.Description: In the space embedded systems domain, we are now witnessing a very novel trend. While "classical'' processing ASICs keep suffering of the usual, widening, performance gap between "terrestrial" processors and space grade ones, on the counter recent developments especially in SRAM-based FPGAs have brought "edge" technologies for space use, providing a possible quantum leap for processing in space.One of the most notable novelties is the availability of some Commercial Off the Shelf System-on-Chip components also in space-grade packages, which deliver previously impossible application and system-level performance for space edge computing applications. Being based on 7nm node, they are a huge step from previous 65 and 45 nm space grade "pure'' FPGAs since they also include heterogeneous compute engines with a breadth of hardened memory and interfacing technologies for far superior performance/watt targets.Especially for payload data processing tasks, these devices will likely replace any future dedicated ASSP and call for availability of sophisticated, RHBD, processor IP cores for specific applications (like Machine Learning acceleration) and for dedicated HW/SW codesign, use of advanced OS (like Linux). The engineering challenges in using these components in space are very demanding: although radiation data show that for example some 7 nm technology will provide SEL and SET-free devices, management of soft errors, design of stable GHz clocks and high speed links, design of a power distribution system capable of delivering e.g. 100 A @ 0.8 V, PCB design and thermal dissipation design are all very critical.The activity will identify a target use case and perform all the design activities starting from architectural design identifying the main building blocks. A survey on related implementation metrics shall also be performed (e.g. from the system requirements, user needs, the choice of data handling architecture then FPGA package, IP cores gate count, performance and interface requirements, DDR and NVRAM memory, storage capacity, high speed serial links, max dissipated power, form factor etc.). This shall consider not only the functions that will be supported in the current activity but also foreseen extensions (e.g. DNN acceleration implementation in programmable logic, direct RF payload processing), which will restrict the list of available selections.The final development of a flexible, reusable and cost-effective generic processing module for institutional. And commercial satellites (150+ kg class) in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) is aimed at accelerating machine learning processing functions. The software infrastructure will be designed as an open environment potentially by passing usual space software quality checks, to facilitate the evaluation and testing of newly developed on-board applications through end-to-end system scenarios. The software suite is expected to be based on opensource applications, such as Linux OS, OpenCL, OpenMP, PyTorch, etc. The goal is to create a building block suitable for the Satellite-as-a-Service (SaaS) concept. Moreover, the activity will also foresee the definition of a development roadmap for deploying the technology on planned and future IOD mission(s) for concerned validation campaigns in the frame of an E2E system scenario.The following tasks are foreseen within this activity: Identify specific use cases and derive detailed requirements. Analyze requirements and trade-offs to determine the optimal architectural design and functional allocation. Develop detailed designs for the electronic module in EQM quality and associated ground support equipment (EGSE). Implement the design, including the selection and integration of FPGA, processor IP cores, memory, and other components. Manufacture, assemble, and integrate the EQM module into a relevant unit environment. Conduct thorough testing of the module and its EGSE. Develop a roadmap for deploying the technology on future In Orbit Demonstration (IOD) missions, enabling validation campaigns in end-to-end system scenarios.Deliverables: Reports, EM module and relevant EGSE.

title: INTERPLANETARY SPEED-ELEC: AUTONOMOUS FAST-TRACK TO OUTER SPACE - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a breadboard of applied-field magnetoplasmadynamic (AF-MPD) propulsion unit compatible with various vehicle scale architectures and can also be used in combination with a nuclear platform.Description: Renewed interest in nuclear electric propulsion (NEP) has emerged in recent years, driven by the growing demands of interplanetary exploration and deep-space missions for which this technology would act as an enabler. Initial studies for NEP Missions (Project RocketRoll) defined the need of 300KW+ power reactors to provide significant advantage with respect to missions using traditional solar electric propulsion. This power level has significant consequences at satellite and propulsive sub-system level, and highlights the need to developed high efficiency, highthrust density propulsive systems. Previous ESA studies have highlighted the potential and confirmed the feasibility of the AF-MPD technology to deliver high thrust and Isp capabilities with a very reduced volume and mass factor, compared to existing technologies.This activity is aimed to further advance into the breadboarding of an AF-MPD thruster that is designed for specific NEP mission needs, and the analysis of the thermal and power loads management at sub-system and system level. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Review the system requirements from previous Nuclear Electric Propulsion studies (i.e. project RocketRoll) and derive the corresponding requirements at system and propulsive sub-system level, considering scalability for various missions. - Design an AF-MPD thruster assembly optimised for a Nuclear EP platform, including the anode, cathode, magnetic field generator and thermal management system. - Justify the design through engineering analyses - Manufacture and test a breadboard model of the thruster assemblyto verify the main characteristics, including performance, erosion, discharge stability and thermal stability - Re-evaluate the vehicle architecture with the obtained results including a propulsion system model - Generate roadmap to complete full development up to qualificationhttp://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Review the system requirements from previous Nuclear Electric Propulsion studies (i.e. project RocketRoll) and derive the corresponding requirements at system and propulsive sub-system level, considering scalability for various missions. - Design an AF-MPD thruster assembly optimised for a Nuclear EP platform, including the anode, cathode, magnetic field generator and thermal management system. - Justify the design through engineering analyses - Manufacture and test a breadboard model of the thruster assemblyto verify the main characteristics, including performance, erosion, discharge stability and thermal stability - Re-evaluate the vehicle architecture with the obtained results including a propulsion system model - Generate roadmap to complete full development up to qualificationhttp://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: TTC TIME TRANSFER IN DEEP SPACE - EXPRO PLUS
description: To implement additional function in Deep Space Transponder, providing accurate onboard time based on telemetry, tracking, and command (TTC) signals and time transfer.DescriptionCurrent Deep Space Transponders include, in addition to uplink Telecommand (TC) and downlink Telemetry (TM) data communications, the functionality of two-way code-based ranging and turnaround carrier phase coherency. The two-way ranging functionality is based on sequences that can be e.g. Pseudo-Noise (PN) ranging (phase modulated together with the TC/TM data, and turned around either transparently (bent pipe) or regeneratively), or using Spread Quadrature Pseudo Noise. Space missions could benefit in increased accuracy and onboard autonomy from a timestamping function. It is based on a one Pulse-Per-Second (1 PPS) signal and time information generated by the transponder based on the PN ranging epoch combined with known range information and other information from ground segment, thus implementing one-way time transfer from earth.The implementation involves the TTC receiver locking to the PN uplink sequence and generating regular epoch. The ground station is performing 2-way ranging usingthe PN-ranging signals, including removal of ambiguity and other processing on the orbit. This information including ranging/range-rate from the ground station is then uplinked to the TTC receiver via telecommand. The receiver then performs a Timing algorithm and dynamic model, to generate onboard time using the received epoch timing and the information uplinked from the ground station. Thisonboard time can then be used in a timestamping function that is useful in several missions. The onboard time can be synchronised to universal time coordinated (UTC).The activity includes breadboarding the additional time transfer functionality, as upgrade to existing Deep Space Transponder functionality, operating in X-Band (7/8GHz) or Ka-Band (26/32GHz).The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of the time transfer techniques and maturity of elements needed to generate onboard real time clock synchronised to UTC- Confirmation of parameters needed for the implementation including ranging code rates and sequences- Design of architectural defining the elements needed- Detailed design and simulation, including (Timing) algorithm, PN epoch generation, 1PPS generation- Implementation and verification of timing functions breadboard including software / FPGA / Hardware in line with detailed design- Demonstration of timestamping function- Plan for upgrade path of Deep Space Transponder

title: FIRST! - INNOVATIVE MECHANICAL JOINING TECHNOLOGIES FOR METALLIC AND COMPOSITE STRUCTURES - EXPRO+
description: Space Transportation vehicle structures being manufactured and built in separate parts, joining techniques have been highly used inthe last decades. When added-up, these joins can induce significant mass penalties as well as assembly times and costs that could be reduced with smarter concepts. Moreover, with the fast progress of CFRP, advanced manufacturing and enhanced metallic alloys for structures, the need of new techniques to join these different materials is more and more acute. New joining technologies are needed to join composite parts, and composite/metallic parts. These joining technologies shall be light weight and low cost and they also have to be easy to manufacture, control and maintain.

title: DUAL-ACTIVE 5G NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORK MODEM WITH SMART RESOURCE MANAGEMENT (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7A.089) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a 5G NTN dual active modem prototype with active resource management for improving link reliability and performance, whileoptimizing the space segment resources utilization.TargetedImprovements:-doubling the peak data rate compared to state of art modems.- reduction by half link outage time.Description: The need for a dual-active modem in 5G Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) arises from the growing demand for reliable, high-performance communication links particularly inscenarios where terrestrial networks are unavailable or unreliable. A dual-active NTN modem can maintain two simultaneous satellite links, significantly reducing the risk ofoutages caused by shadowing, fading or interference. At the same time, it provides an additional communication channel that enables load balancing across space segmentnodes, helping to distribute traffic efficiently and improve peak user data rates. Active resource management is essential in this context. Strategies must be designed todynamically allocate resources based on real-time link conditions and performance metrics. These strategies should ensure that the satellite system can optimize keyperformance indicators, such as peak data rate and service availability, while minimizing the resources allocated to each link and network node (e.g. payloads). Developingcontrol plane methodologies is also a critical aspect of this solution. The control plane manages the signalling and control information required for the operation of thecommunication links. It enables the system to gather real-time measurements of links conditions, which are essential for making informed decisions about resource allocationand link management. These methodologies also provide mechanisms for communicating decisions to the network including satellites and user terminals ensuring that thesystem can adapt to changing conditions and maintain optimal performance.This activity will develop a prototype dual-active 5G modem, potentially based on open radio stacks, and implement a testbed to evaluate the prototype under realisticconditions. This testbed will include a channel emulator with multiple RF interfaces to emulate themultiple links. Channel performance as well as satellite system resourcesallocation will be tested for various operational scenarios, and both resource management methodologies and control plane techniques will be assessed.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: NEURAL COMPRESSION FOR IMPROVED BANDWIDTH AND POWER CONSUMPTION EFFICIENCY EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesTo improve compression performance identify statistical properties of data using ML, yielding improved data throughput and science utility.DescriptionNeural compression methods for astronomical data can enhance compression performance by exploiting mission-specific statistical properties. Unlike generic entropy coders, neural models incorporate advanced probability estimators that adapt to uniquedata distributions observed in cosmic measurements. These architectures often leverage autoencoder or diffusion frameworks, parameterizing the probability density of input samples with high fidelity. Consequently, the model can produce compact representationswhile ensuring bit-level accuracy is preserved. Reduced data volume translates to lower bandwidth consumption, mitigating bandwidth constraints and lessening reliance on highpower transmission components. Onboard, power requirements for data handlingdecrease, allowing systems to allocate energy resources more efficiently for other mission criticaloperations. Additionally, neural compression frameworks can be retrained or finetuned to reflect new observational conditions, maintaining optimal performance as mission parameters change. Overall, this approach can yield notable gains in data throughput, resource allocation, and scientific utility in scenarios where preserving exactmeasurements while minimizing data transmission is imperative.Tasks of the activity:Task 1: State-of-the-Art Analysis- Conduct a comprehensive analysis of classical (including CCSDS compressionstandards) and AI-based compression algorithms relevant to astronomical data. Thisincludes both lossless and lossy methods.Task 2: Performance Requirements Identification- Identify the performance requirements focusing on acceptable compression ratio,acceptable loss tolerance for lossymethods and real-time processing requirements,considering possible constrains for onboard deployment in Enceladus.Task 3: Data SetIdentification and Algorithm Design- Identify or generate the necessary data sets and design the algorithms.- Identification of continuous performance monitoring mechanisms to ensure the stabilityand robustness of the solution in the presence of uncertainty. This includes consideringon-the-fly compression errors monitoring and fallback strategies to classical methods.Task 4: Implementation and Deployment- Implement and deploy the algorithms on a representative board.Task 5: Verification and Validation- Verify and validate the implementation, including assessment on the performance of AIbasedmethods compared to classical algorithms.

title: T201-0001OP HOUSEKEEPING DATA COMPRESSION FOR L4 (SATURN MOONS) DEEP SPACE MISSION (EXPRO+)
description: This study will look at existing compression algorithms (eg. POCKET, others) and tradeoffthe best one for the domain in question making considerations such as usage of onboardstorage, performance and usage of on-board computing resources, rate ofcompression, data loss and errors, effect of long propagation delays, etc.The study will then implement the compression algorithm software. The software will havean on-board component to perform the compression and correspondingly a groundcomponent to decompress and channel the data to the respective virtual channels towardsthe mission control system. The performance shall be demonstrated using the Juice HKdata production model (HK parameters and acquisition rate configuration), real JUICEmission HK data, and a JUICE on-board processor emulator (or equivalent HW) as abenchmark. The Ground component shall be developed such as to integrate with ESAbaseline MCSsystems (eg. EGS-CC).The interaction of Ground with the on-board software component shall be proposedfollowing a PUS compatible approach - initially creating a private service - but implementedin such way as to be able to propose an update to the PUS standard in the future toincorporate a dedicated HK data compression service.
