title: AUTOMATED PHASED ARRAY FACTORY CALIBRATION FROM RADIATION PATTERN USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (ARTES AT 7B.082) EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of this activity is to develop automated factory calibration of phased arrays to improve the manufacturing process for satellite user terminals in the context of LEO constellations leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning techniquesTargeted Improvements: - Enable factory calibration (less than 1 second) from single-shot radiation pattern measurements of phased arrays. - Error between post-factory calibration theoretical should be below 0.5dBDescription:Traditionally, satellite manufacturing was focused on producing a limited number of bespoke satellites for GEO orbits. However, the rise of LEO constellations demandsa shift towards mass production, requiring efficient assembly and testing processes. This statement extends beyond satellite payloads to LEO user terminals, where phased arrays are becoming ubiquitous for constant asset tracking. With satellite user terminal systems increasingly reliant on phased arrays, precise calibration becomes crucial for optimal performance. Calibration involves ensuring precise alignment and amplitude matching of each element to achieve optimal beamforming, thereby maximising signal strength, and minimising interference. Still, current manual calibration methods are mostly labour-intensive, time-consuming, and prone to errors, presenting a challenge to the efficiency goals of mass manufacturing. To overcome this, there is a need to develop AI/ML solutions capable of extracting calibration insights from single-scan radiation patterns measurements. Previous research has demonstrated the potential of AI/ML techniques in synthesising radiation patterns, identifying faulty elements and predicting unmeasured phased values speeding up calibration of antenna arrays. Building upon these advancements, this activity will streamline the calibration process of phased arrays using AI/ML techniques. Rather than using brute force or iterative methods, the objective is to achieve fast calibration and accurate in a single shot. Additionally, the AI/ML engine will be capable to cope with process, voltage, and temperature variations inherent to the integrated circuits used in phased arrays, ensuring robust calibration across manufacturing batches. This approach not only addresses the immediate challenge of mass-producing user terminals but also lays the foundation for adaptabletesting systems capable of accommodating variations across manufacturing batches. By transitioning from labour-intensive manual methods to streamlined single-shot calibration, manufacturers can achieve greater efficiency and accuracy in production. The developed calibration process will be implemented in a combined software and hardware test-bed that will be developed, and the performance ofthe developed calibration process will be tested.

title: VERY HIGH PHASE-STABLE RIGID RF CABLE ASSEMBLY EXPRO+
description: To develop and characterise a high phase-stable RF cable assembly using mineral dielectric materials for precision space applications, ensuring low insertion loss and temperature-stable phase.Description:Rigid coaxial cables are essential for maintaining phaseconsistency and signal integrity in high-frequency spaceborne RF systems, such as those used in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) payloads. These cable assemblies are currently deployed in several key ESA Earth Observation Programme (e.g., Copernicus, Biomass, MetOp-SG), where precise control of signal phase is critical for performance. At present, European missions rely on non european manufactured mineral-based RF cable assemblies, particularly those using silicon dioxide (SiO2) dielectric technology. These imports are subject to export restrictions, creating strategic supply chain limitations for Europe. The most promising solution is the SiO2-based coaxial cable, offering extremely low insertion loss and exceptional phase stability across a wide temperature range (-270C to +1000C). This makes it particularly suited for spaceborne systems where thermal variations are extreme, and phase precision is essential.Unlike conventional PTFE-based dielectrics, which exhibit the "knee" effect near +19C and cause significant phase drift, SiO2 cables provide consistent electrical behavior and superior long-term reliability. The proposed activity aims to develop a European SiO2-based RF cable assemblies that:-Withstand high power levels (hundreds of watts),-Operate over a wide temperature range (from cryogenic levels to +300C),-Exhibit low insertion losses across frequency bands up to Ka-band,-Remain multipactor-free,-Providesultra-stable phase performance (targeting =10 ppm/C).This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Development of RF cable assemblies based on SiO2 dielectric materials. - Development and integration of RF connectors (e.g., TNC, SMA) compatible with mineral-based cables. - Characterization of electrical, thermal, and mechanical performance, including phase stability and insertion loss across operational conditions. - Identification of Limitations, Improvements and roadmap for future space qualification.For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: T811-901SD AI AND HARDWARE ACCELERATED LOW-SNR DEBRIS DETECTION ALGORITHMS (EXPRO+)
description: Currently un-trackable debris large enough to destroy or disable spacecraft needs to be monitored and trackedto archive the Zero Debris targets. Algorithms must be developed that optimally use the existing and newsensor infrastructure to detect this small cm-size debris. Track-before-detect methods allow combining theinformation from multiple frames to detect objects fainter than the single frame sensitivity limit. Matched filtersenhance the signal-to-noise ratio based on expected signal patterns. The algorithms are similar for radars orpassive optical systems, but in both cases very computationally demanding due to the large search space.Space-based optical payloads can detect faint targets otherwise invisible from ground due to the distance oratmospheric attenuation. Satellite hardware limitations render naive algorithms implementations infeasible foron-board processing. The performance of such algorithms is described with a probability of detection curveand false alarm rate depending on some threshold. Lower detection thresholds allow detecting fainter targetsbut lead to more false positives. AI algorithms have proven to be successful in classifying patterns and arepromising post-processing steps to reduce the false alarm rate. The reduction of false alarms allowsdownlinking only relevant data.The goal of this activity is to develop image and signal processing methods to detect small debris in low signalto-noise scenarios using processing hardware such as FPGA/GPU/NPU platforms and additional AIapproaches for data reduction.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: PROCESSOR TECHNOLOGY FOR DIRECT SATELLITE-TO-DEVICE 5G/6G COMMUNICATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 5A.088) - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, develop and validate through testing a scaled demonstrator of a regenerative digital processor supporting NTN 5G/6G waveforms for direct satellite-to-device communications, being highly power efficient, manufacturable efficiently in large quantities, using COTS elements and suitable for the deployment in V/LEO space environments.Targeted Improvements: - 25% improvement in link budget.- 50% reduction in power consumption and size.- Enabling direct satellite-to-device 5G/6G communications through Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN), currently not available.Description: Current developments for regenerative payload processors are in progress however further advancements are required. in view of direct satellite-to-device 5G/6Gcommunications, the development of a bespoke 5G/6G regenerative processor is essential, to achieve high power-efficiency, compact, low-cost, volume production, supporting of high data throughputs, scalable, future-proof for the next generation of 5G/6G waveformsTheadvent of low and very low earth orbit constellations (V/LEO) coupled with the recent developments in 5G/6G satellite technologies create an opportunity for suchregenerative processors. It is anticipated that the integration of terrestrial 5G New Radio access with non-terrestrial-networks (NTN) satellite access enables ubiquitous connectivity to handheld and non-hand-held 5G/6G devices, including IoT devices, which can switch seamlessly between terrestrial and satellite networks. To achieve a high level of integration, innovative satellite payload concepts are required such as V/LEO satellite architectures utilising active antennas and onboard regenerative digital processors to support reconfigurability, flexibility, frequency hopping and dynamic frequency and power allocations ona per-beam basis, together with alignment to future NTNradio access technologies, in particular future 3GPP releases. Network resilience is another important key factor, as well as the realisation of economies of scale.This activity will design, develop and test a scaled demonstrator of a regenerative digital processor for 5G/6G. The activity shall encompass the consolidation of requirements, the design of a bespoke 5G/6G NTN regenerative processor reference architecture that supports the objectives of low power-consumption, volume production, economies of scale, high data throughputs, scalability, 3GPP NTN compatibility and network resilience as required for the usage in V/LEO satellite constellations targeting 5G/6Gcommunications needs.The demonstrator shall validate critical elements of the regenerative processor technology. The demonstrator shall be verified against functional requirements on regenerative payload operations and the processor configuration. Finally, the technology shall be demonstrated in a test configuration, simulating a typical use-case set-up, compatible with the latest satellite NTN 3GPP release.

title: ASIC/FPGA WITH 112 GBPS OPTICAL I/OS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5C.480)
description: The objective of this activity is to develop the technology step needed to enable the use of optical interconnects at speeds of up to 112 Gbps. This should be demonstrated through testing of an integrated digital signal functions (ASIC and FPGAs) with the developed electro-optic transceiver photonic integrated circuits that form the optical I/Os to replace traditional electrical I/O.Targeted Improvements:Increase the data rate throughput up to 112Gbps per wavelength and through the technology change leverage a 30% power reduction (mW/Gbps) and size/mass reduction compared to today's solution.Description:Modern telecommunication satellites use onboard digital processors to be able to provide the increasing capacity to serve the economics of delivering traffic via space thatcustomers request. High throughput digital processors are the core of such payloads, capable of producing Tbps of intra-processor traffic. Enabling these large intra-processor traffic rates requires the most efficient interface technology possible, as power consumption and size are critical. A solution to this is the use of intra-processor optical interconnects to replace traditional electrical interconnects. The first operational satellite equipped with fibre optic interconnects running at 12.5 Gbps has been launched recently and this trend will only continue towards higher bit rates and higher integration of photonics within the processor equipment.In fostering this evolution, the Agency has funded the development of stand-alone optical transceivers operating at 28 Gbps and 56 Gbps for use in the next generation of processed payloads, representing the current state of the art for space applications. Payloadintegrators have stated the desire for optical interconnects that can operate at higher bit rates whilst also reducing the overall power consumption, volume, and mass of the onboard processors. To achieve this would be through the integration of the optical transceivers and the ASIC/FPGA in a single package. Various techniques would enable this, but no such development has been pursued so farfor use in space and any attempt will require the redesign of the circuits involved in order to meet the radiation susceptibility needs. The proposed activity would include a review of the electronic chips that will require and can support high throughput I/Os, the packaging techniques that can allow the integration of microelectronics and photonics, selection of the most appropriate baselinesolution and a demonstrator of suitable space ready solution of an ASIC/FPGA with 112 Optical I/Os.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: MINIATURISED L-BAND FILTER - EXPRO+
description: The European Space Agency's (ESA) Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity (SMOS) mission, launched in November 2009 under the Earth Explorers program, continues to deliver high-quality global maps of soil moisture and ocean surface salinity. Its payload, the Microwave Imaging Radiometer with Aperture Synthesis (MIRAS), is an L-band interferometric radiometer that achieves unprecedented resolution [RD 1 - RD 5]. However, the image reconstruction process still exhibits spatial ripple errors caused by antenna pattern variations between receivers, independent of radiometric noise or modelling inaccuracies. These variations significantly impact reconstruction accuracy, especially when the inter-element spacing exceeds the Nyquist alias-free limit, as seen in SMOS. To address these limitations, extensive research has explored alternative antenna configurations designed to enhance image quality through alias-free array designs while improving spatial resolution [RD 6-RD 9]. Proposed antenna arrays feature a large number of closely spaced, dual-polarizedradiating elements. Each polarization has dedicated receive chains that amplify and filter signals, down-convert them to IF frequencies, and digitize them as complex samples. The combination of dense element spacing and numerous receiver components necessitates miniaturization. A critical component of the receiver is the high-performance RF filter, which must provide effective out-of-band interference suppression while maintaining a uniform and reproducible transfer function across all units. Currently, coaxial resonator filters fulfil this role; however, their bulkiness conflicts with the receiver's miniaturization requirements.Several alternative technologies, including SAW, BAW, SIW, and dielectric filters, offer significant potential for size reduction while maintaining performance. Since the RF filter is positioned after the low-noise amplifier, insertion loss is not a primary design constraint. This flexibility allows for innovative design approaches, such as pre-distortion techniques and lossy filter theory, to further enhance efficiency and integration.The objective of this activity is to design and experimentally validate miniaturized filters for L-band radiometers operating within the 1400-1427 MHz frequency band, satisfying SMOS or equivalent specifications. Two breadboard prototypes,implementing alternative technological approaches, will be designed. A manufacturing run of at least six units per design, yieldinga minimum of twelve units, will be followed by rigorous performance validation testing.The activity aims to reach TRL 4.

Description: The European Space Agency's (ESA) Soil Moisture and Ocean Salinity (SMOS) mission, launched in November 2009 under the Earth Explorers program, continues to deliver high-quality global maps of soil moisture and ocean surface salinity. Its payload, the Microwave Imaging Radiometer with Aperture Synthesis (MIRAS), is an L-band interferometric radiometer that achieves unprecedented resolution [RD 1 - RD 5]. However, the image reconstruction process still exhibits spatial ripple errors caused by antenna pattern variations between receivers, independent of radiometric noise or modelling inaccuracies. These variations significantly impact reconstruction accuracy, especially when the inter-element spacing exceeds the Nyquist alias-free limit, as seen in SMOS. To address these limitations, extensive research has explored alternative antenna configurations designed to enhance image quality through alias-free array designs while improving spatial resolution [RD 6-RD 9]. Proposed antenna arrays feature a large number of closely spaced, dual-polarizedradiating elements. Each polarization has dedicated receive chains that amplify and filter signals, down-convert them to IF frequencies, and digitize them as complex samples. The combination of dense element spacing and numerous receiver components necessitates miniaturization. A critical component of the receiver is the high-performance RF filter, which must provide effective out-of-band interference suppression while maintaining a uniform and reproducible transfer function across all units. Currently, coaxial resonator filters fulfil this role; however, their bulkiness conflicts with the receiver's miniaturization requirements.Several alternative technologies, including SAW, BAW, SIW, and dielectric filters, offer significant potential for size reduction while maintaining performance. Since the RF filter is positioned after the low-noise amplifier, insertion loss is not a primary design constraint. title: IMPLEMENTATION OF AN ESERO (EUROPEAN SPACE EDUCATION RESOURCE OFFICE) IN LATVIA
description: The European Space Education Resource Office (ESERO) is ESA's main project in the field of formal and non-formal early childhood, primary and secondary education. Under the coordination and steering of ESA and the national space agencies and offices, and with the support of national institutions and organizations active in the field of formal and non-formal education, the project aims at enabling capacity building in the school level teacher and educator communities and at designing and promoting the use of didactic resources and activities that make use of space as a context for the teaching and learning of STEM-related disciplines.National ESERO offices are established to implement activities across their hosting country. title: HIGH THROUGHPUT REPROGRAMMABLE DATAPLANES FOR ON-BOARD SATELLITE COMMUNICATION PROTOCOL IMPLEMENTATIONS (ARTES AT 5D.041) - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop high throughput programmable dataplanes on hardware used for space applications. Satcom protocols (e.g. beyond at 3-levels MPLS, Source-Routing, CCSDS USLP, DVB GSE) will be implemented and tested.Targeted Improvements:Improve the throughput of on-board reprogrammable dataplanes of Field Programmable Gate Arrays, Network Processing Units and Central Processing Units by at least a factor of 3.Description: Packet switching in satellite constellation networks is still not as mature as it is in terrestrial networks. Currently, ASICs, FPGAs, Network Processing Units (NPUs), and CPUs are all considered as possible packet processing hardware on board satellites. One common shortcoming of all these approaches is the rigidity of the data plane protocol stack driven by Size, Weight and Power (SWaP) constraints. This makes it very difficult if not impossible to deploy novel data plane protocols, improve the network throughput, update or expand mission objectives, and collect in-network telemetry after launch. Programmable data plane technologies in terrestrial networks allow developing and deploying new packet formats and forwarding functions in operational networks. The same packet processing hardware can be used for different business objectives asthe requirements and the techniques evolve. One of the key innovations promised by data plane programmability is the ability to collect new types of user data telemetry from inside the operational network by re-programming the data planes. Other possibilities include Quality of Service (QoS) enforcement and protection against denial-of-service attacks. P4 (Programming Protocolindependent Packet Processors) and POF (Protocol Oblivious Forwarding) are two examples open-source languages that enable network engineers to re-program the network data plane.This activity will investigate the use cases for programmable data planes for satellite constellation networks. FPGAs, NPUs, and CPUs shall be assessed and selected with regards to the availability of supporting compilers and vendor-specific external functions for programmability of their data planes used for space applications. A reference use case (6x610Gbps packet switch) and satcom protocol

title: IMPROVED TTC SUB-SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE - EXPRO PLUS
description: To consolidate alternative solutions for on-board loss minimization. To develop the prototypes of the most relevant solutions identified, to confirm the predicted performance. To provide road-map to flight models. The state of art TTC Sub-System architectures for Science and Exploration missions are nowadays quite complex. In order to allow communications during all mission phases, several antennas are needed in combination with redundant High Power Amplifiers (HPA) and transponders (DST). The interconnection among these components is accomplished by the RF Distribution Unit (RFDU), which has to guarantee the maximum degree of reconfigurability and reliability to failures. In addition, it has also to implement the necessary filtering action, to allow full duplex communications. Its design is therefore quite complex encompassing the use of several switches, Diplexers, Filters and interconnecting waveguides (WG) runs. The latter can be quite long as they have to reach antennas which are typically far from the location of the rest of the TTC subsystem. All this results in high losses with RF power reduction in transmission and increased noise figure in reception.The design solutions used so far in the frame of ESA projects are quite recurrent with no major improvements in the last decades. As shown in a TTC Sub-System architecture survey carried out in 2017, different approaches exist, as identified for example by other agencies and already flown successfully in the past years. For a complex RFDU as used in Deep Space missions, we can consider RF path losses in the order of 1 to 3 dB in X-band and 3 to 4 dB in Ka-band, with significant impacts in terms of data return (up to50% reduction) and in terms of spacecraft recovery possibilities in case of anomalies (increasedoperations complexity and limitation on maximum achievable distance). Therefore, there is a clear need for loss reduction in the RFDU paths, through the implementation of novel solutions. A study is on-going to consolidate the possible alternative subsystem Architectures, and define relevant requirements. This will be completed in early 2024, but its conclusions need to be consolidated by experimental results. The activity shall focus on the specification, detailed design, development and tests of prototypes of the components which will have the most significant impact on the TTC subsystem performance and whose feasibility has to be demonstrated. Three main items have been already identified, which may need to be completed by additional technologies as an outcome of the on-going study:- Receiving only antenna with integrated low-noise-amplifier (LNA) and downconverter (D/C), with a possible alternative for a receiving and transmitting solution;- High-gain-antenna dual-band feed including receiving LNA and D/C, and with direct interface to power amplifier;- Transponder front-end to manage the interfaces with new antennas designs.Tasks:1. Consolidation of requirements and design2. Design and manufacturing of bread-boards3. Testing of bread-boards4. Development plan for flight models.

title: ESTRACK GROUND STATIONS MONITORING AND CONTROL TAILORING SUPPORT SERVICES
description: The ESA Tracking Stations Network (ESTRACK) is a strategic infrastructure, ensuring European independent access to space. ESTRACK provides global space link connectivity for a wide range of ESA and external missions, e.g. Low and Near Earth, Cis-Lunar, Deep Spaceand Human Spaceflight.ESTRACK ground stations are equipped with a Monitoring Control (MC) system which is the basis for the high-level of automation achieved in the operations of the stations. The purpose of this activity is the configuration and tailoring ofthis system to support the individual spacecraft missions from the stations, enable the monitoring and commanding of the different ground station functionalities, adopt new operational concepts and allow MC of new devices that are deployed to the stations duringupgrades.The service requires detailed understanding of the station operability, MC systems andautomation language and interfaces. It requires close interactions with the assigned stationengineers and the representatives from the supported missions.The tailoring activity encompasses the production of procedures written in a dedicatedtailoring language, for which the IPR shall vest in the Agency.The support covers, in particular, tailoring, test validation, training, maintenance, first linesupport and incidentanalysis.

title: PRE-PHASE A OF EUCOR INSTRUMENT - EXPRO PLUS
description: Solar storms can prove dangerous to modern technology. They can endanger astronauts and satellites, and disrupt communications, computers, power supplies and navigation systems on Earth. This makes Space Weather a matter necessitating constant vigilance, with spacecraft watching for events on the Sun that may cause troubles on Earth in the coming minutes and days. A coronagraph is an essential instrument for a Space Weather mission. A coronagraph blocks the bright solar disk to reveal the faint outer solar atmosphere, the corona, where Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) originate. These instruments are essential for detecting and tracking CMEs and solar wind flows in real time, providing the early warnings needed to mitigate space weather hazards. Operational missions like Vigil require a compact, reliable coronagraph capable of continuous monitoring from a stable vantage point, as the NOAA Compact Coronagraph (CCOR) currently planned for integration on Vigil. Developing this capability in Europe is key to ensuring autonomous, long-term space weather forecasting.The proposed activity is a pre-phase A study for a European Coronagraph instrument (EUCOR) for future operational space weather missions. The scope of the proposed activity is to lay the groundwork for a European Coronagraph instrument, including a survey of European industrial capabilities, and a conceptual preliminary design that makes use as much as possible of existing technologies and capabilities in ESA member state, and the identification of required technology developments. This would be required as a precursor to a complete phase A study with associated pre-development activities as required to reach TRL 5-6. The procurement will be open competition to all industrial entities, ensuring an open competitive approach preparing further steps. Parallel contracts may be placed in case of competitive complementary proposals.

title: OPTIMAL MICROELECTRONICS ARCHITECTURE FOR HIGH DATA RATE IMAGE DETECTOR READOUT - EXPRO+
description: The introduction of advanced semiconductors, optics and packaging technology has led, increased readout speeds, to an over tenfold increase in image detector sizes as witness on today's mobile phones. The increased data rates have been made possible by the reduction in power consumption through miniaturization, integration and use of advanced semiconductor technology and packaging. Notably, the integration of the readout electronics into the sensor and specifically the 3D stacking technology. The introduction of this technology into space would lead directly to higher resolution and faster space imaging payloads. The determination of the most effective use of this technology for space through evaluating the mostsuitable microelectronics architecture from a manufacturing, packaging and electrical perspectiveis the objective of this activity. The output of the activity are the requirements applicable for the realisation of this microelectronics architecture. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Survey of commercial integrated and 3D stacking technology for image sensors technology;encompassing, front-side/backside illumination, and through-silicon-via/hybrid stack technology;- Analysis of the technology related to integrated and 3D-stacking image sensors including the architecture andsupply chain;- Identification of the micro-electronics elements of the technology;- Assessment of suitability and benefit of the technology for space image sensors for the visible and infrared ranges;- Development of the microelectronics architecture suitable for space image sensors (circuit, 3D semiconductor stacking and packaging);- Determination of the circuit and 3D semiconductor stacking requirements;- Reporting on the survey, analysis, evaluation and microelectronics architecture and requirements for image detectors.

title: BROADBAND HIGH POWER TRANSMITTER FOR FUTURE RADAR SOUNDERS - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test a broadband high power amplifier for future subsurface radars in science missions.RIME is a radar sounder instrument optimized for the penetration of the Galilean icy moons up to a depth of 9 km. The instrument is unique as it is the first one to be deployed in Jupiter and the outer Solar System capable of performing direct subsurface measurements. Throughout the development of RIME, few technological challenges had to be faced due to the complexity of such low frequency radar, the length of its dipole antenna and the multinational industrial set up.At present, only a broadband dipole for multi-mode subsurface radars is being developed though an ESA contract, while the rest of the radar elements rely on non-EU suppliers. This activity proposes to develop a broadband transmitter that fits to the dipole and matching network under development. The broadband nature of the transmitter will enable multi centre-frequency chirps to exploit the broadbandness of the dipole antenna. The activity will also focus on designing and manufacturing an amplifier with higher RF power (>200W) in order to improve the radar performance such as its penetration depth. Finally, this development will enable an overall performance enhancement due to the co-design of the different constituents with same radar performance goals in mind. These predevelopments shall constitute the basis for future subsurface radars in future planetary missions e.g. JUICE follow-on.The activity shall start with the review of the current subsurface radar as used in Juice. In synergy with the dipole and matching network development already in place, the activity shall focus on means to increase the power of the transmitter attending to technological options for the transmitter chain, including power handling of the dipole. Following the detailed design, the activity shall continue with the design, manufacturing and testing of the high power transmitter. Testing of the complete transmitter chain including the antenna shall be also foreseen. The activity shall conclude with an assessment of results and the feasibility of such radar concept based on the obtained results.

description: The objective of this activity is to evaluate the pros and cons of a weather-proof optical ground terminal (without protective domeenclosure) and to breadboard critical sub-systems. Targeted Improvements:At least 50% faster optical ground station deployment.Description:Today telescopes for ground based free-space optical satellite communication are originating from astronomical telescopes. The current need for optical ground telescopes has changed significantly and other requirements have become design drivers,namely low central obscuration, transmission in the optical C-band, laser transmitter mounting and system integration. title: GT1I-618GD AI FOR AUTOMATION OF MISSION OPERATIONS SYSTEMS TESTING AND VALIDATION
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) has proven its value in multiple applications, especially in thoserelated to automation. The Artificial Intelligence for Automation (A2I) Roadmap identifies aset of use cases where AI should be used to support automation of mission operations.This activity will focus on three different use cases related to systems testing and validationthat will leverage supervised and unsupervised learning, natural language processing(NLP), Large Language Models (LLMs), active and continual learning to build accurate andexplainable software solutions. Specifically, these are: Deviation analysis in validation and regression testingoutputs. Currently,investigating system failures is very time consuming and it requires great expertiseand research in past logs and supplier documents across multiple systems to findroot causes. In the future, if an issue occurs, an AI system could efficientlyexamineaggregated logging and monitoring information to help detect similar issues thatoccurred in the past as well as potentialsolutions. By using data sciencetechniques many logs can be analysed efficiently to identify items which most likelyexplain the root-cause of the issue. This will decrease the amount of time neededfor the root-cause analysis of the problem and ensure isolationofan error in asystem of systems becomes more efficient. AI-supported test case creation. Adapting to new systems requires a high manualeffort. As systems are complex, numerous tests are required to validate the correctfunctioning. Especially regression tests require a high manual effort and are thuscost intensive. An AI solution can support experts by automating the creation oftest cases for ground segment software applications. The AI system couldautomatically generate a large amount of reliable test cases thatarecustomizedto the system and constraints. These test cases can then be used for validating theviability of the solution. Automated test report generation. High manual effort is required during thesystems testing and validations phase to generate test reports and analyze themto decide on next actions to be performed, as test reports are typically writtenmanually. The use case aims atdeveloping an AI-based system to change theprocess by aggregating all relevant data, by using for instance NLP techniqueswith transferlearning to automatically generate the content of the test reports andLLM with Retrieval-Augmented Generation.

title: BI-DIRECTIONAL GENERIC CHARGE/DISCHARGE MODULE FOR GENERIC STORAGE SYSTEM - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a bi-directional DC/DC converter able to charge and discharge a generic storage system with a targeted reduction of 50% area and mass in the charge/discharge system.Description: Most of the current state of the art considers a dedicated converter for charging and a dedicated converter for discharging power into and from the energy storage system. This has impacts on the overall area and mass, as just half of the circuitry is in use at a given time. For those missions where mass and volume is a concern, a bi-directional converter allows to increase the power density and therefore to minimize mass and volume. In addition, currently the solution to charge and discharge an energy storage system is specific to the energy storage system in use. This activity aims to develop a bi-directional charge and discharge module, allowing the same circuitry to be used for charging and for discharging. The benefit of the bi-directionality reduces the area and the mass of the HW by 50%. On top, it is intended to analyze a generic solution to cover different energy storage systems (e.g. Li-Ion batteries and RFCS -Regenerative Fuel Cell Systems-). This provides a lot of flexibility, since the HW of the power management subsystem does not depend on the energy storage system, and therefore could be produced in advance. This also could lead to a reduction in time to delivery by 30%, by allowing recurrent use of the same design. The objective is challenging because the behavior of these storage systems is quite different and the converter must adapt to them. A charger/discharge module with bi-directional capability based on a non-isolated DC/DC topology with new switching devices (e.g.GaN based switches) and a versatile control system to adapt to the different storage systems. Possibly digital control may be considered to perform an adequate management of the battery or RFCS. The activity encompasses the following tasks: - Confirmation of the scope of the charger/discharge (energy storage systems to be compatible with, power levels...) with a final consolidation of the preliminary requirements - Identify potential solutions (best topologies, control logic, switching devices...) and perform dedicated trade-offs to select a baseline - Design of the baseline, with the appropriate design analysis - Prototype manufacturing of a bi-directional charge and discharge module - Testing of a prototype - Analyse test results, identify and check deviations, implement corrections on the prototype if any to cover deviations to a final designDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

title: CALL FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST TO THE ACCELERATED INVESTMENT PROJECT - ESTEC PHASED CONSTRUCTION OF ESTEC OFFICE, LAB AND ORBIT BUILDINGS - STAGE 1
description: ESA is seeking to procure the construction, in 3 phases, of buildings to:1) Replace buildings in zone B, C, D (with the exceptionof the portion of building Dg which is replaced by the Hertz 2.0 project) which now accommodate 1,250 people with a working environment in modern settings and with a net surface (meaning excluding toilets, circulation areas and ancillary space) not exceeding the current one,2) Host laboratories to replace those currently in zones B, C and D (except for these zone D labs that will move to theHertz 2.0 building) and not exceeding their overall current size,3) Host a catering facility replacing the Lunch Pad restaurant.Further works are the reorganisation of the parking areas to be able to free up parking A for new buildings while maintaining adequate parking capacity at ESTEC, and the adaptation of roads and corresponding general site infrastructures, and utilities.The new buildings will be connected by walkways, the main one being the Orbit, whose elliptical shape will give the project's central area itscharacteristic form.The current estimated construction phases (subject to change due to operational or technical needs) are envisioned as:Phase 1: the construction of two new office buildings, of the future building housing the laboratories, and of a portion of the Orbit.Phase 2: the construction of one office building and of another section of the Orbit.Phase 3: the completion of the last office building and the last section of the Orbit, and any external landscaping works remaining.

title: MICROLENS ARRAYS FOR INCREASED SENSITIVITY OF CRYOGENICALLY COOLED DETECTORS FOR OPTICALAND QUANTUM COMMUNICATION LINKS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.076) EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a microlens array placed on a cryogenically cooled detector at less than 6 Kelvin. The increased efficiency of the photodetector allows a simpler integration in an optical ground stationto enable long distance optical and quantum links.Targeted Improvements:Increase of the effective photon collecting area of a cryogenically cooled detector by at least a factor of 10. This leads to an increase in sensitive area of between 10 and 100 depending upon the choice of photodetector.Description:The current state-of-the-art low-Kelvin cryogenically cooled detectors (e.g. superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors) for use in free-space optical and quantum communication links have an extremely small active area which often results in significant coupling loss of the received light due to misalignment.Microlens arrays have the potential to overcome coupling these challenges as they effectively increase the area in which the light can be received by the detector. However, solutions for cryogenictemperatures are not available yet.This activity will review microlens array materials and manufacturing techniques (e.g. printing, etching) and select the material and technique which is most suitable for integration with a cryogenically cooled detector. Selecting the most suitable match of cryogenically cooled detector and microlens array for serving free-space beyond-Earth communications or free-space Quantum Key Distribution applications, after a trade-off. Manufacturing, assemble, integration and testing of the system under representative operating conditions. Testing will include thermal cycling and an investigation on the structural integrity of the system. Before and after thermal testing, the optical and detector performance of the system in a representative lab-setup will be tested.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. title: ULTRA COMPACT ELECTRIC PROPULSION SYSTEM FOR HIGH ASPECT RATIO (HAR) SATELLITES - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop an ultra compact electric propulsion system suitable for drag compensation, Collision Avoidance Manoeuvres (CAM) and de-orbiting at EOL of High Aspect Ratio (HAR) satellites having a thickness of less than 5 cm operating in LEO. The compact electric propulsion system shall have performances comparable to systems with classic form factor.Description: High Aspect Ratio Satellites, also known as flat satellites, are a type of satellite design characterized by a thin, flat structure rather than a traditional three-dimensional structure. These satellites are often lightweight, compact, and are designed for a variety of applications.Flat satellites typically have a compact design with limited available space. Integrating a propulsion system within the constrained volume of a flat satellite is challenging. The propulsion system must be designed to fit into the thin structure without compromising the primary mission objectives or increasing the overall mass significantly. Flat satellites often have limited power resources,and the propulsion system must operate within these constraints. The compact design of flat satellites can also lead to challenges in managing the heat generated by propulsion systems. Thermal considerations are crucial to prevent overheating and ensure the proper functioning of both the propulsion system. Flat satellites are frequently used for communication purposes, and the propulsion system must be integrated without interfering with communication antennas or other sensitive equipment. This requires careful placement and design to avoid signal degradation or other performance issues. Flat satellites often require precise orbital maneuvers or station keeping to maintain their positions or perform specific tasks. Propulsion systems must provide the necessary thrust and control for these maneuvers, and the flat satellite's geometry may impact the effectiveness of traditional propulsion methods. This activity supports the implementation of the TEC GEN Vision 2040 for the theme Ultra Compact Satellites, by targeting the design, development and prototype testing of an ultra compact electric propulsion system complete of thruster, electronics, fluidic management and tank.This first development step allows to verify the concept of compact electric propulsion system in relevant environment and contributes to support the long term objective of enabling mobility of Ultra Compact Satellites, including Direct-to-Device (D2D) communication satellites in LEO, by means of in orbit propulsion. Follow up technology maturation and qualification activities are envisaged. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements Specification Definition - Design definition and justification - Prototype manufacturing and performance characterization test including endurance testing - Development PlanDeliverables: Breadboard, Report

title: USE OF STATE-OF-THE-ART AR/VR INPUT DEVICES IN SPACE APPLICATIONS - EXPRO PLUS
description: To assess the state-of-the-art of AR/VR input devices for use in space applications, for enhanced user interaction with better usability and with more natural interactions.DescriptionThis activity shall assess the state-of-the-art of Augmented and Virtual Reality (AR/VR) input devices such as gloves, hand gestures, 3D mouse and eye tracking, for better usability and with more natural interactions. The goal is to improve the user interaction with AR/VR applications, for manned and unmanned missions, such as for astronaut training, test design verification, remote testing, virtual spacecraft monitoring and control, advanced data visualization and remote support. In astronaut training and operations, during the execution of procedures in AR/VR, the selection and control of (virtual) tools, such as wrenches, pliers and cutters is essential. The use of interactive gloves is promising in this context and shall be further explored in this activity. The provision of feedback (vibrations) to indicate e.g. when contact is made, will be very helpful for the astronaut, to understand the progress and completion of performed activities. In spacecraft operations, AR/VR can be applied to remote maintenance activities of ground stations and telescopes, as well as to virtual spacecraft applications in support of mission operations. These environments require specific mobility of the users, such as hands-free operations or operations in tight spaces and also the ubiquitous use e.g. in control rooms. Here, devices that register gestures (e.g. Leap Motion) or 3D mouse devices shall be studied, in addition to the use of gloves. In testing, AR/VR can be applied to support the test execution. In addition, the mechanical design of test equipment could be supported, where the test setup can be verified more comprehensively in advanceof the actual testing. The constraints on the interaction with the AR/VR applications are very similar to the use cases for training and operations as described above. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Analysis of the use case scenarios - Assessment of the needs in the areas of testing, training and operations (manned and unmanned) - Propose reference architectures based on modern input devices - Develop a demonstrator, covering the usage in the identified areas, for a limited number of selected AR/VR input devicesThe outcomes of this activity shall provide an overview of current and future AR/VR input devices suitable for spaceapplications, as well as to derive an approach for using these devices in a variety of space applications, addressing the current shortcomings in the use of AR/VR in space applications.

title: DESIGN-FOR-DEMISE (D4D) MODEL WITH AEROTHERMODYNAMIC SIMPLE SHAPES EXPRO+
description: Objective: To improve the accuracy of re-entry and design-for-demise predictions by the generation and consolidation of aerothermodynamic models used for space object component-oriented re-entry simulation tools.Description: To predict the survivability of debris during atmospheric re-entry and assess the potential risk on the ground, ESA has developed various industry standard tools and methodologies to support mission designers. Nowadays, engineering methods are used to precompute the aerodynamic coefficients of basicgeometric primitives. However, this approach relies on simplifying assumptions, leading to significant uncertainties in survivability calculations. High-fidelity approaches have shown to have less uncertainties then simplified methods, leading to potential reduction in the design margins applied to design-for-demise activities. Nevertheless, their systematic application has been limited due tocomputational costs. To improve the usability, interpolation scheme between high-fidelity simple shapes to represent more complex component can be envisaged. This activity is intended to generate an open-source DSMC (Direct Simulation Monte Carlo )/CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) database capable of handling a wide variety of topologies and to develop a proof-of-concept representative of the complex geometries of the spacecraft components. The only open-source deliverable will be the database. This activity encompassesthe following tasks: - Build a AEDB/ATDB (AEro/AEroThermo) database of pre-computed values for simple shapes by designing, runningand analysing a series of high-fidelity flow simulations (using CFD (Computational Fluid Dynamics) and DSMC (Direct Simulation Monte Carlo) for a set of simple shapes and flow conditions relevant to the design-for-demise of spacecraft. - Develop a methodology to derive the drag coefficient and heat flux for more complex shapes and realistic objects by leveraging the numerical database of simpleshapes and applying interpolation schemes. - Apply this methodology to one specific spacecraft equipment type, known to produce ground casualty risk and then considered critical for demisability (e.g. propellant tanks, reaction wheels, magnetorquers and opticalpayloads).Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access to it and can provide update to the community of usersDeliverables: Prototype, Report, Software.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: ARIADNA STUDY - TOTIMORPHIC LATTICES AS A ROBOTIC PLATFORM FOR SPACE EXPLORATION - EXPRO PLUS
description: Imagine a spacecraft structure that can change its shape on commandstiff when it must hold loads, flexible when it must adapt, andreconfigurable when a mission needs something new. This activity will build and test a physical prototype of a "totimorphic lattice": a programmable 3D structure made of repeating units that can be actively actuated to morph its form Using a computational framework developed at ESA's Advanced Concepts Team, it aims to "reprogram" the lattice continuously with differentiable optimizationso thestructure learns the best way to move and redistribute forces to achieve a desired shape or mechanical behaviour. The ultimate goalis to move from simulation to reality: run controlled laboratory experiments, measure performance, and validate whether these shape-shifting lattices can become a robust, reconfigurable structural platform for future space exploration.

title: PHOTONICS-BASED OPTICAL APERTURE FOR LASER COMMUNICATION TERMINALS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5F.056) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a thin optical aperture leveraging advances in integrated photonic technology to reduce the size andweight of space-based optical communication terminals.TargetedImprovements:Reduction of both size and weight of satellite laser communication terminals by 50%.Description: Optical communication terminal solutions with lower size and weight are required to serve the increasing role of small spacecraft for satellitecommercialisation by maximising the amountof payload space for mission-enabling processing or sensors. State-of-the-art optical communicationterminals are often too bulky and heavy for such small platforms and a leap in technology is required. This activity will seek innovative integrated photonicsolutions to replace the telescope subsystem of an optical communication terminal and eliminate as much as possible the need for free-space propagationinside the laser terminal. By doing so, it is expected to greatly reduce the size and inertial mass of the telescope subsystem, enabling for instance furtherreductions in steering assembly size, weight and power.This activity will design and prototype a photonic aperture (or flat telescope) that shall provide good beam quality (for coupling/emitting into/from singlemode waveguides such as single-mode fibres), shall be relatively large (at least several cm in diameter) or provide enough optical gain to enable convincingreplacement of conventional beam expansion and free-space propagation optics (traditional telescope assemblies) in space optical communicationterminals. A foundry-compatible fabrication process of the photonic aperture shall also provide a low-cost telescope alternative by eliminating the need forexpensive optics and assembly and alignment touch labour.The following tasks are envisioned:- Identify the potential solutions and latest innovations in integrated photonic able to replace conventional optical aperture assemblies in space-basedoptical communications for small platforms and/or use cases where accommodation of optical communication terminals is drastically constrained bytheir size and weight.- Develop a preliminary design and expected performance of the chosen solution.- Manufacture and test a prototype and evaluate the performance in a representative laboratory environment.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). This activity will seek innovative integrated photonicsolutions to replace the telescope subsystem of an optical communication terminal and eliminate as much as possible the need for free-space propagationinside the laser terminal. By doing so, it is expected to greatly reduce the size and inertial mass of the telescope subsystem, enabling for instance furtherreductions in steering assembly size, weight and power.This activity will design and prototype a photonic aperture (or flat telescope) that shall provide good beam quality (for coupling/emitting into/from singlemode waveguides such as single-mode fibres), shall be relatively large (at least several cm in diameter) or provide enough optical gain to enable convincingreplacement of conventional beam expansion and free-space propagation optics (traditional telescope assemblies) in space optical communicationterminals. A foundry-compatible fabrication process of the photonic aperture shall also provide a low-cost telescope alternative by eliminating the need forexpensive optics and assembly and alignment touch labour.The following tasks are envisioned:- Identify the potential solutions and latest innovations in integrated photonic able to replace conventional optical aperture assemblies in space-basedoptical communications for small platforms and/or use cases where accommodation of optical communication terminals is drastically constrained bytheir size and weight.- Develop a preliminary design and expected performance of the chosen solution.- Manufacture and test a prototype and evaluate the performance in a representative laboratory environment.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: MULTI-APERTURE DIGITAL COHERENT AND INCOHERENT GROUND MODEM FOR OPTICAL COMMUNICATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.081) - EXPRO+ (ON REQUEST)
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test a digital coherent and incoherent signal combining receiver that utilises multiple smalltelescopes, achieving a large effective collection area.TargetedImprovements:Reduction of system cost and complexity by using multiple small apertures to avoid the use of a larger aperture with an adaptive optics system whilemaintaining the total corresponding coupled power-in-fibre.Enabling modular system design, allowing incremental future upgrades to enhance link power budget.Description: The logical progression in optical receiver development is to use a modular receiver design with multiple apertures combined coherently and incoherently.Firstly, small aperture telescopes are significantly less affected by atmospheric disturbances and can operate with cost-effective hardware, such as tilt tracking.Secondly, advancements in large Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) and digital signal processing (DSP) blocks can significantly simplifythe optical part of the receiver and enhanced reliability, while shifting the complexity to the digital domain. Functional verification of proposed idea hasbeendemonstrated in laboratory environment by research groups.The present activity shall analyse and demonstrate via a free-space-optical experiment at minimum 10 Gbps for coherent and up to 10 Gbps for incoherentmodulation (e.g. DP-QPSK, OOK) receiver system over atmospheric turbulence conditions that are representative (or worse) of those encountered inGEO/MEO/LEO. A receiver should perform optical front-end conditioning, followed by digital coherent and incoherent multi-channel combination, and thenprovide an output toa modem.This demonstrator will feature, but not be limited to, the following critical functions: cost-efficient tilt-tracking stage, optical multi-channel front end unit withdigital coherent and incoherent combiner, electrical output to a modem.

title: HYDRON EVO: MULTI TBPS SPACE BACKBONE NETWORK (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.241) EXPRO+
description: Objective:The objective of this study is to investigate the High-throughput Optical Network evolution (HydRON EVO) as the backbonenetwork enabling a total capacity of tens to hundreds TbpsTargeted Improvements:To assess the feasibility of optical space backbone network with total capacity in the range of tens to hundreds TbpsDescription:Following the terrestrial network analogy, backbone (long-haul) networks provide capacity beyond Terabit-per-second (Tbps) per single line (with links beyond 800 Gbps per wavelength). The current HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network) demonstration system will demonstrate single-link communications from 2.5G to 100Gbps, addressing both user access and the lower datarate backbone links. To enable growth of optical space networks, as an extension of the terrestrial fibre network, a space backbone is required to support multi-Tbps capacity in space. The backbone should be interoperable and interface with multiple networks like the one developed in HydRON demonstration system. However, using DWDM technologies and commercial coherent transceivers, the single link capacity can be increased beyond Tbps, and by aggregating multiple channels the network capacity can be increased to tens or even hundreds Tbps.This activity shall address the design and technology trade-offs of a space network backbone exceeding several Tbps and serving other space networks. It shall provide a set of requirements and a system concept. It shall be verified by analysis that the system concept is scalable at higher rates. Interoperability aspects shall be analysed, to guarantee the connectivity among networks (including terrestrial fibre networks). Technology gaps shall be identified and technology roadmap provided. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator concept where the relevant technologyas well as the operational concept can be demonstrated, to further push the technology borders in terms of data rates/capacity aiming to maintain the strategic leadership position of the Europen/Canadian Industry The activity will also contribute to the evolutionof ESTOL.

title: SPECTRUM SHARING TECHNIQUES FOR BEYOND 5G (B5G) AND 6G 3D NETWORKS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3A.185)
description: The objective of the activity is to investigate and develop spectrum reuse and sharing techniques for integrated NTN-TN 3D networksthat allow them to pool, share, and rapidly reallocate spectrum on demand among their heterogeneous components/segments. The techniques will be prototyped in a testbed to be implemented as part of the activity.Targeted improvements:Enabling spectrum reuse and sharing in integrated NTN-NT 3D networks.Description:Spectrum demand for all wireless services continues to increase while service and operational convergence create more diverse, complex, and interconnected systems, such as the ones envisioned with the integration of terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks (TN and NTN respectively) which is now being considered for Beyond 5G/ towards 6G.While spectrum reuse and sharing may potentially satisfy the growing demand, the emerging complexity, dynamics, and heterogeneity of the different wireless systems involved make the TN-NTN integration at radio resource management (RRM) level technically challenging with existing approaches. For example, previous activities did not consider airborne layers (e.g., HAPS, UAVs), or N-system, N-band dynamic sharing where access priorities vary by band, location, and time. In future networks, the motion of network nodes such as NGSO satellites or HAPS can require updates at RRM level orders of magnitude faster that done before, or potential link outages caused by the high dynamic environment can require quick system reactions untenable by a purely centralised spectrum management approach.To address these issues, the activity will investigate, develop and test spectrum reuse and sharing techniques for integrated NTN-TN 3D networks that allow them to pool, share, and rapidly reallocate spectrum on demand among their heterogeneous components/segments.The activity will follow a phased approach. The first phase will analyse and design spectrum sharing techniques for heterogeneous integrated NTN-TN 3-dimensional (3D) networks by identifying requirements and protection criteria for the individual NTN and TN components, identifying approaches and key innovations needed, and estimating the expected gains (capacity, access) and impacts (technical, operations, regulatory). The second phase will implement the solutions in a prototype consisting of an emulation environment where the developments will be characterised and their benefits and impacts assessed. The results will be used to engage with regulators and relevant standardisation bodies for subsequent deployment /adoption.The activity will seek synergies with other ESA 5Gdeliverables and testbeds as well as various 5G platforms projects from European and national initiatives that are already being built up.

title: 3U VERSION OF THE ADVANCED POWER ARCHITECTURE (APA) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a small three-rack-unit version of the Advanced Power Architecture (APA) with aim of having a highly compact architecture fit for small missions.Description: The Advanced Power Architecture (APA) is being designed for general ESA mission /medium scale platform but is not addressing smaller mission needs. This activity aims at developing the APA concept in a three-rack-unit (3U) version; this footprint would be suitable for smaller satellites up to 500 kg. The activity targets to investigate the miniaturisation of the already identified functions by integrating novel technologies such as digital control and Gallium Nitride High-Electron Mobility transistor (GaN HEM FET). The Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA) has already a 3U version which, if coupled with a 3U version of the APA, it would enable a single frame for a very compact avionics system. In fact, the APA will provide the input power interface, the TM/TC interface, the internal power rails and the internal communication bus. Thus, any platform function not needing internal high speed data communication buses could fit perfectly in the 3U APA. For instance, the solar array drive function or any motor drive function, propulsion valves drive functions, thermal control, etc. The activity targets to enhance industrialisation of power units for mid-size satellites by having the full power system functionality integrated in one unit. If deemed adequate for the application, a cost-effective solution could be available by having the components as COTS. A strong focus on manufacturability and industrialisation will be done, focusing on automatic manufacturing, planar transformers, SMD components, etc. This activity focuses on the development of the Solar Array Regulator (SAR) module with miniaturised DC/DC converter and on the Solar Array Drive Electronics (SADE) demonstrating the applicability of the concept to the entire avionics functions. These will be the firstbuilding blocks for the development of the complete functionality. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Converter andfilter size reduction thanks to the use of HEM FET (GaN) - Inclusion of the Solar Array Drive Electronics to embed all potential EPS need - Design and manufacturing of a breadboard - Test of the breadboard - Validation and verification - Way forward for industrialization

title: SUSTAINABLE MINERAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT - EXPRO+
description: Sustainable mineral resource management involves the responsible extraction, use, and conservation of mineral resources to meet present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs. It emphasizes efficient mining practices, minimizing environmental impacts, and restoring ecosystems after extraction. An important component of this approach is the use of Earth observation technologies, which allow the detection of (critical earth) minerals, continuous monitoring of mining activities, land degradation and water quality. The development of novel EO solutions and tools improve transparency, support better decision-making, andhelp detect unsustainable practices in near real time. Combined with recycling, resource efficiency, and strong environmental policies, Earth observation enhances the ability to balance economic development with environmental protection and social responsibility,ensuring long-term sustainability of mineral resources.

title: CONSULTING FOR DEVELOPING IMPLEMENTATION SOLUTIONS, FOSTERING PARTERNSHIPS AND COOPERATIONS FOR THE IRIS PROGRAMME - EXPRO PLUS
description: In an era where secure, sovereign communications are paramount, the European Commission and the European Space Agency (ESA) are spearheading an ambitious initiative: IRIS (Infrastructure for Resilience, Interconnectivity and Security by Satellite). This next-generation satellite constellation aims to bolster Europe's digital sovereignty and provide resilient communication services across the continent. In close cooperation with the EC, ESA is seeking independent expert advice to support the development of strategies and implementation solutions for the IRIS2 Programme. More specifically, a consultancy support is required to promote and initiate the establishment of new partnerships and co-operations for IRIS governmental infrastructure and services with third-party nations to the EU27. In addition, on top of the current system capabilities, the needs for the improvement of the data relay layer of IRIS2 (i.e. linked with the European Resilience System, ERS-COM) for National and International initiatives (constellations) should be investigated as well.

title: 5G AUTOMOTIVE MAKERSPACE (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.010)
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, develop and test automotive prototypes following 5GAA workplans and increase the number of companies working on automotive satellite communications by 30%. Targeted Improvements: Novel hand-over methods between satellite and terrestrial networks supporting use cases as formulated by 5GAA and miniaturised automotive terminal baseband units.Description: The 5G Automotive Association (5GAA) workplans highlight various architectures and technologies that need to be developed to enable automotive satellite communications.These range from antenna integration, protocol development, 5G NTN prototypes with specific automotive characteristics and predictive terrestrial-satellite handover for 5G automotive connectivity.This activity will support the evolving 5GAA workplans and carry out up to about twenty five prototyping activities. This will include novel automotive antenna integration concepts, novel handover schemes and 5G air interface robustness tests. As the 5GAA workplan is continuously evolving, subsequent further prototyping activities will be defined by ESA during the activity, in accord with the prime contractor. This will allow initiating small prototyping activities in line with work-areas defined in the 5GAA workplan. The activity will engage with the community of start-up companies, university spin-offs, very small companies which often implement projects in the spirit of open-source hardware and full sharing of intellectual property, and normally do not engage with ESA. title: CDSE ONBOARDING FOR COMPLEMENTARY DATASETS
description: The Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (CDSE) continues to expand its portfolio by onboarding new, high-value Earth Observation datasets that further strengthen the platform's scientific, operational, and analytical capabilities.This procurement invites contractorsto fully integrate these datasets into the CDSE, building on the platform's open and extensible architecture to ensure seamless ingestion, publication, and access through scalable, standardised interfaces.The activity will enhance user experience by enabling richer interactive visualisation, detailed data exploration, and advanced data processing across the ecosystem.

title: EO DOWNSTREAM ENGINEERING SUPPORT SERVICES 2026-2031
description: ESA's Earth Observation Programmes need to continue integrating technological innovation coming from the digital sector in a structured way to maximise programmatic efficiency. Science and Application RD activities are implemented as a series of industrial contracts, and these require coordination to ensure coherence across activities and make best use of the advancing state-of-the-art of Information Technology. This comprises e.g. cloud computing, AI, blockchain, information security and the related activities in initial quick prototyping accompanying the specification process, independent validation, technical assessment, and integration support. The efficient technical execution of Earth Observation Science and Application RD requires expert support to the ESA Technical officers in these areas of digital technologies, which can be procured as an industrial service. Such a service shall act horizontally across EO downstream activities (science and applications) to ensure a harmonised approach in use of digital technologies and information security implementation. Required services will cover expert support in the area of digital technologies on:Support theTO in review and validation of project deliverables.Technical support in liaison with external bodies (e.g., CLAIRE, GEO, CEOS, OGC). Definition of best practices and standards to be applied across projects. Integration support across different projects into the larger EO ecosystem.Technical assessment of improvement opportunities across projects. Support to configuration baseline and change management. Support to Phi-lab sprints preparing available environments to experiment application of emerging digital technologies to the EO domain.Support to ESA-organised events and demonstrations.Provision of technical input for contributions toconferences, workshops and communications.

title: END-TO-END PERFORMANCE SIMULATOR (EEPS) FOR KEYSTONE - EXPRO+
description: In this project an end-to-end performance simulator shall be developed for the Earth Explorer 12 candidate mission Keystone. The Keystone satellite will carry a THz radiometer, an IR radiometer and a UV-Vis spectrometer to observed the mesosphere and lower thermosphere. The mission has five scientific target areas: 1) the upper-atmosphere thermal balance, 2) atmospheric diurnal variations, 3) the upward coupling between the middle and upper atmosphere, 4) the downward coupling between the magnetosphere and the atmosphere and 5) model benchmarking. Industrial consortia will propose concepts for the mission. The primary objective of the end-to-end performance simulator is to show that these mission concepts enable the observation of geophysical variables, related to the mission objectives, within the scientific requirements.

title: SYSTEM PHASE A STUDY - NGGM
description: In the frame of the Missions of Opportunity enabled by international cooperation, ESA and NASA have coordinated studies of gravity monitoring constellations optimised to observe mass changes and transport in the Earth system. In 2016 the report from the ESA-NASA Interagency Gravity Science Working Group defined the benefits of such a unique cooperative effort. The objective of the NGGM - NextGeneration Gravity Mission (also known as MAGIC - for Mass-change and Geosciences International Constellation ) is the long-term monitoring of the temporal variations of Earth's gravity field at high resolution in time (down to 3 days) and space (100 km). NGGM/MAGIC will observe Earth mass change and reinforce services by monitoring hydrology, cryosphere, oceanography, solid Earth and climatechange. This gravity mission evolution will provide continuity of science and services with respect to predecessor missions like GRACE, GOCE and GRACE Follow-On and will complement other ESA Earth Explorer programme and Copernicus missions. This activity corresponds with the Phase A system studies, whose main objective will be the determination of the programmatic, technical and technological feasibility of the mission within its boundary conditions. The activity will cover all elements of the mission architecture, namely the satellite (i.e. instrument and platform), the launcher, the flight operation concept and the ground segment, to the extent of detailed required at Phase A level in line with ESA standards and such to support the cooperation with NASA. The latter will be actively supported through specific Tasks in the system study. The activity will also cover the development approach and in particular the plan to reach TRL 5 for critical technologies at the end of Phase B1. To this end, the initiation of technology pre-development activities on critical technologies will also be part of the Phase A.

title: SMOS DISC (2026-2028)
description: The focus of this activity is on the algorithm and product maintenance, evolution, long term monitoring and quality control within the scope of the SMOS mission for what concerns the SMOS instrument (Level 1) and geophysical (Level 2) data products. title: RYDBERG ATOM-BASED ALL-OPTICAL RADIO-FREQUENCY RECEIVERS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.010) EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop, and test two IP cores that implement the transmitter and receiver digital functions of the coherent and non-coherent 10 Gbps air interface optionfrom the ESA Specification for terabit/s optical Links (ESTOL). The IP cores shall cover in scope both the optical inter-satellite links and the optical space-ground links included in ESTOL.Targeted Improvements:Develop non-coherent IP core to reach 10 Gbps from the current offering at 2.5 Gbps. Also, develop a coherent IP core to improve the sensitivity of the non-coherent one.Description:The activity shall design, develop, test two IPcore that implement the transmitter and receiver of the 10 Gbps coherent and non-coherent air interface options from the ESTOL. TheIP cores shall implement the data link layer of the transmit/receive devices, including randomization, FEC encoding/decoding, framing/de-framing, modulating/demodulating, CRC, digital synchronization etc. The IP cores shall encompass both optical inter-satellite links and optical space-ground links (bidirectional). For the latter, a time diversity method, as specified in ESTOL, shall be included in the IP. The IP cores shall be tested against software implementations of the ESTOL specifications and shall become part of the ESA IP core portfolio. It shall be implemented and tested in a commercial FPGA.

title: 3D IONOSPHERIC MODELLING - GT18-009EP
description: Characterising the ionosphere is crucial for radio link users. Most models currently in use for ionospheric weather nowcasting and forecasting applications approximate the ionosphere using a single thin-shell approach with a fixed height of e.g. 350 km, which is an approximation suppressing the vertical structure of the ionosphere. 3D modelling has the potential to provide resolution of more complex structures and their evolution in electron density, particularly during disturbed conditions and hence improve overall accuracy.The software prototype shall be developed to demonstrate how the inclusion of a 3D model at the core of space weather service provision can improve the space weather services for satellite navigation and telecommunication users and complement existing 2D products such as TEC mapping. A set of priority requirements will be defined for further development of the underpinning modelling.The development shall take existing proven modelling concepts, particularly the results of the TRP activity "3-D Ionospheric Total Electron Content Modelling", which describe properties of the ionosphere to build a model implementation including all established required functionality.The development shall target a model that can be operated in near real-time and utilise measurements from ground based observations systems and also GNSS radio occultation measurements. These observations are measured routinely and the measurement data is already part of the Space Situational Awareness (SSA) Space Weather Segment (SWE) system. The model operation shall be verified with a reproducible set of test data in order to ensure correct operation within a pre-defined parameter space of input variables. The model results shall be validated against pre-defined observables in test data and in test campaigns with other models with similar capability. The model developed in this activity shall be implemented on the SSA system and a final verification shall be performed to confirm that the implemented model behaves as expected.
