title: DELTA DEVELOPMENT OF TECHNOLOGY BUILDING BLOCKS FOR SOLAR CELLS TARGETING EOL EFFICIENCIES BEYOND 33% EXPRO+
description: ObjectivesTo develop solar cells targeting end of life efficiencies > 33%.For European industry, it is required to continue developing technology building blocks that could lead to disruptive solar cell technologies resulting in a future efficiency leap. Manufacturing process improvements are needed to allow producing new solar cell structures at commercially competitive costs. For realizing EoL efficienicies beyond 33% it is inevitable to work also on the remaining factor. That means only materials shall be allowedin the cell concept that can offer very high remaining factors. This excludes, e.g. (In)GaAs subcells which are the basis of all cell concepts currently investigated. Then, such a cell design can most probably only be realizable by a so-called semiconductor bonding technology (SBT) concept which allows for combining multi-junction cells grown on different growth templates intoone device. Due to the highly sophisticated concept dedicated development effort is needed to bring the related technology building blocks to therequired maturity level. If SBT is as expected, this might also mean a shift from 4 and 6 inch technology to 8 inch technology since all tools currently available for this purpose require 8 inch wafers.This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Theoretical analysis of best suited materials for achieving highest EoL efficiencies. - Development of technology building blocks that allowfor reaching highest EoL efficiencies. This includes but is not limited to: characterisation of semiconductor materials with respect to radiation hardness, inverted and upright lattice-matched and mismatch epitaxial growth, semiconductor bonding, growth on 8" wafers, lift-off and layer transfer processes. - Combination of building blocks in final solar cell design - first breadboard solar cells with high EoL efficiencies - Beginning of life and end of life characterisation of solar cells

title: PROCUREMENT OF THE LISA TELESCOPE ASSEMBLY
description: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is the first space mission designed to observe theuniverse via gravitational waves, ripples in the fabric of space time caused by the acceleration ofmassive objects in the universe. The LISA observatory consists of three identical spacecraft (eachwith a mass/power of about 2700Kg/>3kW), forming an equilateral triangular constellation of 2.5million km side-length, in trailing or leading orbit with respect to the Earth at about 50 million km. Thepassage of a gravitational wave results in a modulation of the length of one arm with respect toanother, which is detected using laser interferometry.ESA is responsible for the mission, including procurement of the spacecraft and the launch vehicletogether with the development of the ground segment to control and operate the spacecraft (fromthe Mission Operation Centre - MOC) and to perform the science mission planning and process thedata products, including archiving (from the Science Operation Centre - SOC). The ESA MemberStates and NASA contribute to the mission with several payload elements (ESA CFI to the Prime).ESA has also the overall responsibility of the verification of the mission performance.For each spacecraft, the LISA Telescope Assembly (LTA) consists of two ultra-stable Zerodurtelescopes. Each telescope is mounted on the Moving Optical Subassembly (MOSA), which hostsall the optical elements.The Executive believes it prudent to take action now to limit any potential damage to the Programmestemming from the unstable situation with NASA. Acknowledging the urgency of the situation, theSPC has requested the Executive to investigate European industrial solutions. This paper outlinesthe approach being taken by the Executive to fulfil this action.Although there have not been specific technology development activities on a LISA Telescope, allthe Large Space Integrators in Europe have amply demonstrated substantial capabilities to designand procure complex telescopes in several flying Scientific Missions. The Executive is thereforeconfident that European Industry can provide the LISA Telescope Assembly as per requirementsand in the needed timeframe.Several industrial discussions have taken place during July and August, that allowed the Executiveto refine the original cost estimates and get confirmation about the throughput rate necessary tomeet the LISA needs.The Executive intends to proceed with the release of an open, competitive tendering for the provisionof the Telescope Assembly for the three LISA spacecraft, with three different contractual phases tobe activated according to the evolution of the geopolitical scenario: Phase 1 ending with initial testing of the breadboard model expected Q4-26. (The activitymay be stopped at this point and transferred under national funding.) title: HIGH-FRAME RATE, HIGH DYNAMIC RANGE MWIR/LWIR DETECTOR - RE-ISSUE
description: To develop and characterise of a high-frame rate, high dynamic range detector array. Future Earth Observation mission studies have identified the need for high-frame rate, low noise, high dynamic range, 2D array detectors with high efficiency in the Mid Wave Infrared (MWIR) to Long Wave Infrared (LWIR) waveband to support Fourier Transform Spectrometer based instrumentation.This activity aims at developing a new readout integrated circuit (ROIC), suitable for detectorhybridisation and operation in the Mid Wave Infrared and Long Wave Infrared wavebands, consequently operating at temperatures as low as 50 K. The ROIC shall offer frame rates in the thousands per second, on-chip pixel binning and a high dynamic range.The targeted objectives of this activity are ROIC design and manufacture and ROIC functional verification and characterisation.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Detector specification review- Preliminary ROIC design- Detailed ROIC design- ROIC manufacture- ROIC characterization- Detector roadmap preparationProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. title: HARMONY VALIDATION CONCEPT CONSOLIDATION VERIFICATION METHODOLOGIES - EXPRO+
description: This activity aims to define the validation approach for the scientific data products of the Harmony mission, which is ESA's Earth Explorer 10 mission currently under development and planned for launch in 2029. The main objectives include creating an initial version of the Harmony products validation plan, identifying the main challenges for the validation of each product, and supporting the development of a calibration and validation strategy for Harmony. The work is organised into tasks that involve analysing product specifications, generating an inventory of in-situ networks and instruments, addressing critical needs in pre-launch campaigns, designing and prototyping in-situ networks, and creating a validation roadmap

title: NAVISP-EL1-103 - PRECISE AND STABLE NAVIGATION WITH QUANTUM ACCELEROMETER - EXPRO+
description: Quantum accelerometers offer a promising solution to address drift and inaccuracies in traditional Inertial Navigation Systems (INS), especially in challenging environments with limited GNSS signals. They provide high-precision navigation, long autonomy, and effective fault detection, making them ideal for Safety of Life (SoL) applications like underwater, maritime, rail, aviation, and automotive. This project builds on previous feasibility studies, aiming to integrate quantum accelerometers into navigation systems, overcoming challenges such as vibrational noise, vehicle dynamics, and non-linear errors, while optimizing performance for specific user domains.

title: NAVISP-EL1-110-USER EQUIPMENT PLATFORM FOR POSITIONING WITH 5G/6G NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORKS - EXPRO PLUS
description: The future 5G and 6G non-terrestrial networks (NTN) will offer continuous and ubiquitous coverage, serving predominantly terrestrial users in remote and underserved areas. The latest 3GPP releases imply that the user equipment (UE) must be equipped with the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receiver determining its position, velocity, and time (PVT) to be able to connect to NTN. To alleviate the dependence of UE on GNSS, the use of 5G NTN signals for positioning is being actively studied. Although various conceptsand solutions to provide PVT with NTN have been identified, the development and prototyping of representative user side solutions remain to be addressed in detail. Current NTN system studies would greatly benefit from design, evaluation, and breadboarding of realistic user equipment algorithms and solutions. The activity will design and develop a generic user equipment platform in the form ofhardware and software to evaluate and trade off user-side processing solutions and algorithms for PVT with NTN. The positioning performance of the UE will be validated using a representative NTN simulator.

title: AUTONOMOUS AND ADAPTABLE ATTITUDE AND ORBIT CONTROL FOR SATCOM CONSTELLATIONS (ARTES AT 4C.075) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, develop and test an Attitude and Orbit Control System (AOCS) with increased level of on-board autonomy, robustness to failures, mission adaptability for satcom constellations.Targeted Improvements: - Increased AOCS autonomy, reduction of ground Telecommands, flight procedures and operational constraints by 30%- Faster response to on-board failures/improved system availability by 20%- AOCS adaptable to different missions, facilitating industrial re-useDescription: Telecom missions make use of frequent communication ground control and current state-of-the art AOCS for such missions have a limited degree of on-board autonomy. While this may simplify the overall design of AOCS on-board functions, it results in a significantground operational effort such as mode-switching and specific configuration changes.Moreover, today's AOCS architectures require significant effort and time to be adapted for different missions. Recent studies have shown that increased level of autonomy can be potentially achieved for specific operations such as orbit raising to nominal orbit (e.g. to GEO), orbit management (e.g. station keeping) or collision avoidance. Furthermore, otherstudies showed that implementing a single-mode AOCS with virtual sensors/actuators abstraction modules employing advanced estimation/control techniques could potentially reduce the operational effort in managing theAOCS during the mission.The activity will design, develop and test (in a high-fidelity simulator with Processor in-the-loop) a novelAOCS on-board software based on state-of-the art single AOCS mode and virtual sensors/actuator modules consisting of all the mainAOCS functions (sensors/actuator processing, estimation, guidance, control, embedded FDIR). The AOCS software willimplement advanced estimation, control, optimisation algorithms alongside decision-making capabilities, enabling the system to adapt to various spacecraft configurations/mission phases without mode transitions and ground assistance. In addition, the AOCS software will run with any number or types of sensors/actuators requiring minimal adaptation and will be agnostic to the type of on-board processor used. Theusecase shall cover all the mission phases from separation orbit acquisition to nominal pointing modes, orbitalmanoeuvres, safe mode and controlled re-entry.This activity shall demonstrate and evaluate:- reduction of operational effort and ground interfaces thus increasing on-board autonomy- increased availability thanks to embedded FDIR- adaptability of the architecture to any mission phase- re-usability for different missions.This activity complements the definition work performed on the architectures for autonomy identified in the frame of the Intelligent System Initiative.

title: GROUND STATION FOCAL PLANE ASSEMBLY AND ACQUISITION SYSTEM FOR LOW-ELEVATION OPTICAL COMMUNICATION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.087) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop the ground equipment required to enable optical communication with spacecrafts at low elevation angles,including Optical Ground Station (OGS) downlink fibre coupling and Pointing, Acquisition Tracking (PAT) sequence elements.TargetedImprovements:The target improvement for LEO-Ground optical communication links is to increase of theoperation time by a factor of two. The target improvement forGEO-Ground optical communication links is to increase the usable spatial coverage of the GEO satellite by a factor of two.Description: To date, numerous optical satellite communication links have beensuccessfully demonstrated. Most of these experiments have operated at elevationangles exceeding 25 degrees to overcome significantatmospheric propagation challenges, such as intense turbulence. However, for LEO satellites,about half of their visibility in a circular orbit occurs between 5 and 25 elevation. Therefore, overcoming challenges with low elevation optical links coulddouble operation time. For GEO satellites, the elevation angle remains constant; however, enabling low-elevation links can potentially double thesatellite's spatial coverage on Earth. Moreover, improvements in low-elevation optical links have significant impact on both classical and quantumcommunications.This activity will examine the necessary techniques and develop the required hardware to facilitatelow elevation optical communication links through theatmosphere. This will involve namely: Study the required techniques to enable low elevation links and provide trade-off analysis Design and develop the PAT fibre-coupled receiver systems of an OGS that enables optical communication links at low elevations Integrate the optical PAT/receiver systems to an identified OGS Perform an experimental link campaign at low elevations Analysis of the obtained results and conclude on a way forward towards higher TRL of the technology developed under this contract.

Description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop the ground equipment required to enable optical communication with spacecrafts at low elevation angles,including Optical Ground Station (OGS) downlink fibre coupling and Pointing, Acquisition Tracking (PAT) sequence elements.TargetedImprovements:The target improvement for LEO-Ground optical communication links is to increase of theoperation time by a factor of two. The target improvement forGEO-Ground optical communication links is to increase the usable spatial coverage of the GEO satellite by a factor of two.Description: To date, numerous optical satellite communication links have beensuccessfully demonstrated. Most of these experiments have operated at elevationangles exceeding 25 degrees to overcome significantatmospheric propagation challenges, such as intense turbulence. However, for LEO satellites,about half of their visibility in a circular orbit occurs between 5 and 25 elevation. Therefore, overcoming challenges with low elevation optical links coulddouble operation time. For GEO satellites, the elevation angle remains constant; however, enabling low-elevation links can potentially double thesatellite's spatial coverage on Earth. Moreover, improvements in low-elevation optical links have significant impact on both classical and quantumcommunications.This activity will examine the necessary techniques and develop the required hardware to facilitatelow elevation optical communication links through theatmosphere. This will involve namely: Study the required techniques to enable low elevation links and provide trade-off analysis Design and develop the PAT fibre-coupled receiver systems of an OGS that enables optical communication links at low elevations Integrate the optical PAT/receiver systems to an identified OGS Perform an experimental link campaign at low elevations Analysis of the obtained results and conclude on a way forward towards higher TRL of the technology developed under this contract.

title: PRINTED CIRCUIT BOARD TECHNOLOGY FOR AUTOMOTIVE CONFORMAL ANTENNAS (ARTES 4.0 AT 7C.083)
description: The objective of the activity is to investigate, develop and test conformal Printed Circuit Board (PCB) technology using a novel approach, such as additive manufacturing to "print" the antenna for the automotive market. Targeted Improvements: Enabling conformal board of patches with distribution feed and integration of amplifiers on the reverse side, able to follow the shape of a car roof. Description: Conventional PCB technology is an appealing technology to implement cost-effective antennas that could meet the automotive market needs. However, flat surfaces do not fit easily into car rooftops while multilayer PCBs can hardly be shaped. The aim of this activity is to develop conformal PCB technology that could be compatible with the design of shaped antennas. One approach could be to use additive manufacturing to "print" an antenna that follows the shape of the surface. Metal printing has been demonstrated and could be investigated. The suitability of different types of material that can be printed will be investigated for this application. As part of the initial study, investigations about the suitability of the technology to create antennas at common satellite communication frequency bands (e.g. S, Ku) will be carried out (looking at the accuracy and ability to create elements of larger sizes for example). The technology shall demonstrate the ability to produce an antenna curved in 2 axes. Two breadboards for different frequencies will be realised in the activity. Assembly of active components onto the antenna will also be addressed within the activity. Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: E3CS-039 PARTICLE DETECTOR INSTRUMENT TO SEARCH FOR STRANGE QUARK MATTER SQM-ISS - EXPRO+
description: SQM-ISS will perform the first large systematic search - using active detectors - of slow-moving massive particles in cosmic rays, such as Strange Quark Matter (SQM), primordial black holes and other new particles. The SQM-ISS instrument uses a dual detector setup consisting of scintillator and piezoelectric detectors, which allows to probe a very wide range of particle types, mass and energies, ensuring a high probability of discovery of such new particles. In absence of any signal, the SQM-ISS instrument will allow to establish an upper limit for a wide range of particle fluxes.

title: HIGHLY EFFICIENT 20 W S-BAND AMPLIFIER FOR 5G-CONNECTED CARS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7C.082) - RE_ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a highly efficient 20 W S-band Power Amplifier.Targeted Improvements:Efficiency higher than 70% - enabling technology for S-Band automotive applications.Description:Recent studies have shown the potential of satellite communications for 5G-connected cars. Although various frequency bands may be envisaged, the S-band can offer a simple systems architecture as well as a satisfactory link budget. However, due to the low gain of S-Band antennas, a dedicated high-power amplifier is necessary to close the link while offering a small footprint and high efficiency.This activity aims at developing such a power amplifier, which must be compatible with the constraints of the automotive market. A 20 W S-Band prototype, with 70% minimum efficiency, shall be designed, manufactured and tested.

title: NAVISP:EL1-099: LOCATION, TRACKING AND SALVAGE SUPPORT OF LOST SHIPPING CONTAINERS AT SEA - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: Each year 226 million container boxes are shipped. About 1600 boxes/year (0,002%) are lost at sea. The boxes are afloat for days toweeks before they are sinking grounding. The objective of the activity is to study, design and develop a location and tracking system for lost containers at sea based on PNT-infrastructure plus IoT based PNT-COM package (Tracking Tracing Device). One of the main innovations is to address the primary problem area: L-Band antenna could be under water, which causes high absorption loss in RF. The tasks to be performed will include the location of lost containers considering the absorption of RF-Signals in seawater and discussing possible directions of solutions, establishing low-frequency tracking transmitter to support salvage, build-up an experimental system, and conduct tests.

title: NAVISP-EL1-101 - UNDERWATER AND UNDERGROUND NAVIGATION USING MUONS - EXPRO+
description: When cosmic rays reach the upper part of the Earth's atmosphere, several particles are created, including muons. Muons, elementary particles with the same charge of the electron but with bigger mass, can travel through any kind of material, including water and rock. Muons can be used for navigation using Reference Detectors. The objective of this activity is to consolidate and demonstrate underwater and undergroundnavigation using Muons, with a target performance better than the performance of Muon Positioning Systems reported in literature.

title: THE EUROPEAN EARTH OBSERVATIONECOSYSTEM:EVOLUTION FROM 2040+ EXPRO+
description: The European Earth Observation Ecosystem: Evolution from 2040+ is addressing evolution options of the European Earth Observation Ecosystem overall System Architecture. It will follow a scenario based approach to consider future use cases and needs in a holistic manner. As a baseline input, the study will start from documented user/mission needs of existing systems in operation, implementation and planned missions. Space as well as ground segment aspects are to be addressed identifying the core observatory functions and analysing the synergies of a multi-mission ecosystem concept. Building from the established baseline, innovative scenarios for the time horizon 2040-2060 will be developed around a mandatory set of core/continuity missions with reference mission performance characteristics complemented by additional elements in a mixed system-of-systems architecture approach. Elements to be addressed in the activity include the identification and justification of core/continuity observatory functions, their respective resilience and availability in the future , complementary observation and data processing functions, amongst others. The identification and elaboration of multi mission synergies and system optimization/streamlining of satellite mission functionality is a mandatory element of the study.

title: SECOND SCOUT CYCLE: SYSTEM CONSOLIDATION STUDIES
description: The Earth Observation (EO) Directorate of the European Space Agency (ESA) launched a new framework to develop scientific missions for Earth Observation exploiting the new space initiative and complementing the well-established series of Earth Explorer research satellites. With this new family of small satellites, ESA intends to respond to the dynamism of a quickly evolving scientific and technological environment in the Earth Observation sector by reducing the time and cost to deliver demonstrations of novel EO techniques in the Earth sciences, taking advantage of new development methodologies, higher-risk approaches and existing assets.Following the strong interest expressed in the Scout framework, and the experience drawn from the first Scout cycle, the Agency intends to initiate a second Scout cycle to ultimately deliver 2 new Scout missions with high scientific merit.The Scouts rely on an agile and flexible approach to timely deliver scientific value. Scout missions are therefore not in-orbit demonstration missions nor commercially driven missions. Scout missions are characterised by a pro-active role of industry and academia, a low-cost approach and a rapid development cycle (3 years from start of implementation to flight acceptance). It is mandatory that Scout missions are based on an observing technique and instrumentation with sufficient scientific and technological maturity to be implemented within the boundary conditions of the Scout programme.Scout missions shall be consistent with a strictly contained Cost-at-Completion (35 M at 2024 e.c.for all industrial development costs for the space segment, including launch services, adaptation of existing ground segment or ad hoc ground segment development, and operations of the mission until end of the in-orbit commissioning phase). It is therefore mandatory that candidate missions are based on an observing technique and instrumentation with sufficient scientific and technological maturity from the onset, so as to secure a quantifiable science return in such a limited development period. It i expected to rely on already developed smallsat/cubesat platforms, with adaptations limited to the payload accommodation requirements. The objective of this procurement is to conduct system/mission consolidation activities - for a maximum budget of 700 k and a maximum duration of 9 months - on (up to 4) selected candidate Scout mission concepts, pending reception of offers of good quality.

title: EU-AFRICA SPP - INSTITUTIONAL COOPERATION
description: This tender aims to implement the activities required for the Institutional Cooperation component of the EU-Africa Space Partnership Programme (funded by DG INTPA under the Global Gateway initiative). The relevant activities will span across the entire period ofthe first phase of the programme (2025-2028) and are to be implemented at continental level. Therefore, the main objective of this tender is to strengthen the institutional capacity of the African stakeholders in preparation of operating the African Space Agency (AfSA) in terms of programmatic design and planning, knowledge transfer as well as outreach. The activities deployed to achieve thisobjective will include: 1) Technical Assistance in support of four Joint Task Force Groups including dedicated studies for each of the four supported sectors (earth observation, navigation, communication, astronomy), 2) Technical Assistance to scope and specify facilities useful to be installed in the AfSA including design studies for facilities such as a Concurrent Design Facility and Cubesat Support Facility which should be conducted and provided to the AfSA inception team, 3) Knowledge Transfer activities aimed at supporting the delivery of high-quality, sector-specific training to African experts to build their technical skills and leadership abilities in space-related fields, and 4) Development of innovative communication tools including an online African Newsroom.

title: S2-SW-06C SPACE WEATHER CAPABILITY DEVELOPMENT FOR IONOSPHERIC AND GEOMAGNETIC CONDITIONS
description: This activity will include two high priority capability developments with the aim to both provide new and improved products for endusers in Southern Europe and to investigate the potential future advances in related SWE Service Provision expected to be enabled through utilisation of the data from the planned Aurora mission. Both Southern Europe and Arctic region are targeted by this combinedactivity with the aim to explore potential synergies in terms of long-term development planning in both the ionospheric and geomagnetic conditions domains- Space Weather Product Developments for Southern Europe Part 2This activity will focus on further developingthe SWE Service Network capabilities targeting end users in Southern Europe. The activity will build on the work that has been carried out by two parallel SSA studies "P3-SWE-XXIII User requirements for Mediterranean region", followed by "P3-SWE-XXXVIII: SWE Products for Southern Europe Phase 1" which have both characterised regional user requirements, and further developed regional space weather capabilities tailored towards user needs in this region.This activity will particularly focus on expanding the SWE Services through development and incorporation of improved and/or additional products into the SWE Service Network in both geomagnetic conditions and ionospheric domains, with a regional focus.- Aurora Mission Data Utilisation StudyThis study will focus on the utilisation of measurement data foreseen to be provided by the Aurora mission, currently being developed within the ESA Space Safety Programme. The main aim of Aurora is to monitor the interaction of the solar wind and CMEs with the Earth environment along with the identification and nowcasting of geomagnetic disturbances. These capabilities are expected to underpin substantially improved service capabilities, particularly for users operating at high latitudes.The analysis will primarily focus on utilisation of the data to support advanced modelling and shall highlight the expected benefits in terms of improved service provision in particular for end users operating at high latitudes.The expected benefits shall be demonstrated by means of existing models and real/simulated data and may utilise the modelling framework currently under development within the P3-SWEXLV activity focussed on 3D magnetospheric modelling. Requirements for model and tool development in order to optimally utilise data from both Aurora-D (single satellite) and Aurora-C (4 satellites) for the purpose of space weather modelling, nowcast and forecasting shall be produced.

title: SPIN-IN OF SLIPRING TECHNOLOGY FOR SATCOM APPLICATIONS (ARTES AT 4E.096) - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to select an off the shelf European slipring technology for terrestrial applications and demonstrate its suitability for Satcom applicationTargeted Improvements: Improving by 20% of power density, lifetime, mass, volume, and lead time.Description: Solar Array Drive Mechanism (SADM) require complex slip-ring technology often leading to long delivery times. However, slipring technologies for terrestrial applications exist and are used widely in industries such as aerospace, medicine, energy and industrial manufacturing, including vacuum applications. The newest developments in terms of contact materials and manufacturing could be leveraged to simplify the design and reduce lead times making use of existing manufacturing capability, production rates could be achieved as needed for satcom constellations.This activity will study and test slipring technologies available for terrestrial applications, perform trade-offs and select one design for spin-in for space applications. A slipring engineering model willbe developed and tested to evaluate the performance for a satcom mission profile.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: ASSESSMENT OF OPEN-SOURCE LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS WITHIN THE SATCOM SECTOR (ARTES FP 1A.128) EXPRO+
description: Artificial Intelligence-powered Natural Language Processing (NLP) models are revolutionising the way we operate and function withinour society. Large Language Models (LLMs) based on these technologies enable us to process and comprehend vast amounts of information quickly and accurately. This activity aims to generate a satcom-specific open-source LLM for use within the participating state satcom sector. The activity will include selection of the best open-source LLM to use as a starting point; enhancement of the base performance of the model by fine-tuning (i.e. training) with satcom domain-specific data; and comparison of its enhanced performance against state-of-the-art commercial models. Finally, the activity will generate recommendations and advice on how organisations and companies within the European satcom community can further train/fine-tune the model with their own proprietary data for their own (private) use.

title: E3CX-023 - EXPERT - LUNAR REMOTE CAMP STUDY - EXPRO+
description: The objective of the proposed parallel studies is the development of a lunar remote camp as a secondary habitat concept to support further lunar missions surface operations. The outcome of the parallel studies will be a comprehensive concept for the system requirements, architecture, subsystems (maturity and availability) and propose roadmaps, including breadboard development, for critical subsystems and technologies. The proposed parallel studies will analyse habitat technologies to lead to a concept design that can serve a variety of use cases such as a potentially mobile, remote camp or safe haven for Artemis landing missions, but also augmentation/protection of foreseen surface infrastructure elements. The following tasks are foreseen to be included in the work scope:- concept development based on several use cases and taking into consideration available landing capacities (Argonaut or else)- definition of subsystems based on European technology capacities;- development of the product tree of such habitation system based on maturityand availability in Europe.- defining and proposing breadboard of major elements for a lunar secondary habitat.- definition of crew systems and communication considering European communication assets such as Moonlight.- detailed trade-off between hardshell andinflatable elements for the pressure hull- roadmap development and conclusion with a comprehensive roadmap for further development, including potential demonstrators.

title: NEXT GENERATION MULTI-BEAM SCANNING MICROWAVE RADIOMETERS FOR METEOROLOGICAL APPLICATIONS - EXPRO PLUS (RE-ISSUE)
description: To define multibeam scanning microwave radiometers for next generation satellite meteorological operational systems. To develop a proof-of-concept breadboard demonstrating the functionality and validating the performance of the critical elements. DescriptionMicrowave radiometers represent a key element of satellite meteorological systems, and are among the instruments providing greater impact to numerical weather prediction uncertainty as well as climate monitoring. Future systems will require the implementation of radiometers with higher accuracy and radiometric resolution.For example, current generation of microwave radiometers for temperatureand humidity sounding (i.e. MWS Microwave Sounder) are based on across-track mechanical scanning of a single beam over a wide swath. This approach, although simple from an implementation point of view, it limits the achievable radiometric resolution, due to the limited integration time per pixel. The implementation of a multibeam system, possibly based on a combination of electronic and mechanical scanning, would allow for much higher observation/integration time per pixel, which, in turn, would provide a substantial performance improvement. This activity addresses at possible microwave radiometers concepts based on multiple-beam scanning, and develops a proof-of-concept breadboard of the instrument front-end for the critical technology. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirements review starting from MetOp-SG and next generation systems - Identification of instrument concepts based on multiple beams and fast hybrid electrical/mechanical scanning, trade-off different antenna front-end architectures and baselineselection - Development of a proof-of-concept breadboard of the critical front-end technology - Functional verification and performance - Roadmap for technology development

title: COST REDUCTION OF PHOTOVOLTAIC ASSEMBLY - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to optimise photovoltaic assembly production, such as developing automatic process, using cheaper components, etc., to reach 25% cost reduction on system level.Description: The last decade shows a continuous increase in the demand of power in space as well as a strong push from end customers to reduce costs, particularly on constellation satellites. On the other hand, cost reduction on photovoltaic assembly (PVA) has not improved significantly along the years and the level of automation is still low or not fully implemented which is the consequence of limited production need in this area. However, projections suggest that the demand for solar cells or PVA will significantly increase in the coming years. Therefore, the cost reduction on photovoltaic assembly is a key element to respond to the increase demand for reasonable cost and to maintain competitiveness in Europe. The proposed activity shall look into different implementation alternatives to achieve cost reduction on PVA level. Some of them are the following: Developing automated processes. Achieving higher level of modularity. Reducing number and complexity of preparation steps. Including inspection steps within automated processes. Using cheaper components such as Commercial Off the Shelf Components (COTS) or terrestrial solar cells with flight heritage (e.g. micro or nanosatellites) which imply adaptation of the solar array design. The latter could affect the PVA performance, which is acceptable if system level cost benefit is achieved.Ideally performance of reference PVA shall not be affected when implementing cost reduction steps. All these measures would contribute to reduce cost on photovoltaic assembly level as well as to prepare European Space industries for large scale production and thus maintain competitiveness in Europe.The tasks foreseen in the frame of this activity are the following: Selection of material, processes and components to be used for the Design Verification Test (DVT) sample. Acceptance testing at component level on the procured items. Manufacturing and integration processes to meet the engineering design requirements. Engineering tests to demonstrate maturity of the design (coupon level test). This shall also include performance measurements that allow for an /W assessment at system level demonstrating that the objective can be met with the optimised design.Deliverables: Design verification test sample. Report.

title: PROTOCOL FOR 5G INTEGRATED NETWORKS TO ENHANCE RELIABLE POSITIONING (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.024) - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of this activity is to design and develop a simulation testbed for secure delivery of assistance data with5G satellite networks to enhance positioning.Targeted Improvements:Foster the use of 5G satellite networks to enhance positioning with ubiquitous, reliable, and secure delivery of assistance data. Enable secure time and frequency synchronisation in existing or future telecommunication infrastructure.Description:Various positioning use cases, such as high-accuracy or integrity, rely on receiving assistance data to enhance the positioning performance beyond what can be obtained by using messages broadcast by the global navigation satellite system (GNSS). Currently, the 5th generation (5G) terrestrial networks provide a native mechanism to delivery assistance data through the 3GPP LTE positioning protocol (LPP), enhancing the performance of mobile users within the coverage of the network interms of time to first fix, position accuracy, and/or integrity. Important benefits of 5G terrestrial networks in this context include the intrinsic reliability and security of communication channels. The expansion of 5G to direct-to-device satellite networks in low-Earth orbit (LEO) will enable new use cases and enhance the existing ones, by providing continuous and ubiquitous connectivity across the globe. In terms of enhanced positioning, 5G satellite networks could adapt protocols and solutions of terrestrial networksto allow for secure delivery of the assistance data also to remote areas or to ensure no service interruption, enabling use cases such as autonomous shipping or GEO referencing sensor data. To achieve this, the protocols and solutions currently available in terrestrial networks need to be adapted and simulated for the satellite networks. Enhancing positioning with assistance data delivered through secure channels will also serve telecommunication infrastructure. It will bring the trust in time and frequency synchronisation, currently achieved by using unprotected GNSS messages. The activity will: 1) Review the relevant standards and study/identify network architectures providing assistance data to enhance positioning with 5G satellite networks. 2) Consolidate use cases and performance targets benefiting from secure delivery of assistance data, targeting worst-case positioning users requiring high-accuracy and integrity in relevant scenarios, such as in remote areas, denied environments, or during network congestion. 3) Design and develop a representative end-to-end testbed capable of simulating network architectures and modelling high-fidelity user environments considering the identified use cases. 4) Assess the performance of the assistance data dissemination with 5G satellite networks considering the consolidated use cases using the developed testbed.

title: EARTH OBSERVATION-BASED AGRICULTURAL INNOVATIONS IN NIGERIA
description: This tender supports the implementation of EO Application Innovation in Nigeria under the European Space Agency - European Commission's DG-INTPA Contribution Agreement, with a focus on deploying Earth Observation (EO) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologiesto advance climate-smart agriculture in Nigeria. The project aims to enhance the machine learning (ML) and AI capabilities of the National Space Research and Development Agency (NASRDA) and other federal agencies. It will provide specialized training to their personnel as well as key agricultural stakeholders, while co-developing an open-source Climate-Smart Information System (CSIS). This CSIS will integrate satellite EO data, IoT sensors, and predictive analytics in collaboration with NASRDA. Core activities include theestablishment of a Geospatial ML/AI Training Center (hardware), the design and delivery of targeted training, the deployment and validation of IoT tools across seven pilot farms, and the development of the EO-based CSIS supported by AI/ML and IoT technologies. Asan additional component of the project, a "West Africa Space ML/AI-driven Agro-Climatic Resilience and Sustainability Conference" will also need to be scoped, which will facilitate regional knowledge exchange and institutional collaboration.

title: NON-DESTRUCTIVE VERIFICATION OF THERMAL INTERFACES IN AMBIENT CONDITION - EXPRO PLUS
description: Support reduction in cost and time for telecom satellite testing by facilitating reliable ambientverification of thermal interface conductance.DescriptionConsidering the tendency to move towards ambient testing, rather than vacuum testing, for recurringflight models, there is a need to reliably verify the workmanship of key characteristics of the thermalcontrol system in ambient conditions. One of these critical parameters is the thermal conductanceof interfaces between dissipative equipment and radiators/heat pipes. One way to approach thisproblem is to look for out of family behaviour, or by comparison with past tests. However, this onlyworks when reference data is available and therefore a more general way to actually "measure" thethermal conductance of the interface in ambient is highly desirable.The activity investigates the best non-destructive testing techniques that could be used to verify thermal interfaces in ambient conditions. A physical test matrix would then be executed to assess the performance of the chosen method(s) for different equipment, fillers, and mounting substrates.This will involve both vacuum and ambient testing to gain confidence in the accuracy of the chosentechniques.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Requirements consolidation- State of the art review and selection of best measurement technique- Elaboration and manufacturing of test matrix (coupons)- Execution of the tests- Final reporting and roadmap for industrialisation.

title: ADVANCED DEMAGNETISATION METHODS - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop advanced deep demagnetisation techniques, as enabling technologies for next generation in-situ space plasma sensing missions and gravitational sensors missions.Description.For spacecraft projects requiring magnetic cleanliness, flight units are demagnetised via a standard procedure using an homogeneous field of 3 to 5 Hz, slowly exponentially increasing up to 5 mT, then slowly decreasing. This demagnetisation field profile comes from a procedure applied to military submarines many decades ago, and was never justified for being optimal for space equipment.It involves dedicated expensive equipment: Helmholtz coils sufficiently large and capable of withstanding the high currents involved, high power audio or 4-quadrant amplifier, and a waveform generator with high dynamic range.According to existing practice, this is supposed to be preferably performed in a compensated Earth field environment, so two more pairs of Helmholtz coils are needed, and two adjustable high-stability current supplies to compensate the horizontal and vertical components of the Earth's field.The procedure has to be performed 3 times, once along each main axis of the unit under test.In spite of the sophistication of the method, which can provide some spectacular results, the outcome can also be disappointing, meaning that equivalent or better results can sometimes be obtained with morerudimentary methods.Magnetic cleanliness is a necessary design and verification activity for missions flying experiments inherently sensitive to on-board magnetic field.Ferromagnetic materials are used in many parts for very good technology reasons. One limitation to the reduction of the spurious magnetic field at the experiment sensors location is how deep and how systematically the ferromagnetic materials can be demagnetised.Re-visitation of the demagnetisation procedures used for science missions, through a double approach: review of the methods used in other industrial sectors and of the physical background of demagnetisation procedures, so as to spin-in or develop techniques either permitting a deeper demagnetisation,or easier / faster to implement than the current ones.Task list:1) Review of the demagnetisation procedures used in the various industrial fields;2) Review of the physical background of demagnetisation;3) Theoretical assessment of the procedure used for space equipment:frequency, dynamic range, peak amplitude progressiveness, etc.4) Experimental comparison of the results obtained with various demagnetisation methods and parameters;5) Recommendations for space equipment.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TO SUPPORT THERMAL ENGINEERING ACTIVITIES - EXPRO+
description: Objectives: To enable fast adoption of Artificial Intelligence into thermal community processes to improve efficiency and to reducedevelopment costsDescription The use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has exploded in recent years to support wide range ofengineering activities, and the trend is set to continue as new hardware (e.g. Graphical Processing Units (GPU) and analogue computing cores) together with more advanced software platforms become available. These advances will likely not be driven by the space engineering sector, but by a wide range of other sectors. Nonetheless, the space engineering (thermal) domains need to be ready to adopt thesetechnologies as they become available in order to drive efficiency and reducecosts. The expected benefits are twofold:- Reduced development time and cost (e.g. in the case of faster design surveys, faster test correlation or model exchange);- Improved quality and/or performance (e.g. in the case of optimization use case, or use of hitherto unexploited data sets).A number of potential usescases for AI are already envisaged. One of the most noteworthy is the use of surrogate thermal models to support activities such as: fast sizing for design and worst case assessment, faster than real time solutions for digital twins, AI derived reduced models to support advanced control applications, model reduction and correlation, etc.In addition, other uses cases can be envisaged such as exploitation of new data sets (thermal cycling, operations data), for anomaly detection during operations and flight, or optimization of design solutions for advanced thermal control technologies. One of the key challenges is to derive findings that are targeted at normal thermal engineers and the focus of the physical interoperability of AI based solutions to give confidence in their use. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Critically assess which thermal engineering activities can benefit the most of the useof AI technologies;- Demonstrate the uses of AI to support the chosen use cases and assess performance. Ensure proper interfaces with engineering tools and emerging data models / digital twins;- Derive recommendations from the activity, with a focus on non-AI-specialists, and disseminate to the communitySoftware shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence.

title: IMPROVEMENTS TO 5G THROUGHPUT AND EFFICIENCY USING UE EQUIPPED WITH GALILEO HIGH ACCURACY SERVICE (HAS) (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.020) - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: Improve the timing and positioning accuracy of a 5G User Terminal through the use of Galileo HAS to improve synchronisation and reduce user link offsets and guard times, thus improving latency and throughput.Targeted Improvements: Galileo HAS offers an order of magnitude improvement in positioning accuracy for receivers compared to a standard GNSS signal. All 5G user terminals rely on GNSS for timing and synchronisation, therefore such an improvement in accuracy will enable a corresponding reduction in timing offset and guard times.Description: Future 5G systems will benefit from increased throughput through higher accuracy timing signals. Galileo HAS signals are already on air and a 5G user terminal would benefit using HAS to improve synchronisation and reduce user link offsets and guard times, thus improving latency and throughput. This activity will develop a breadboard prototype of a 5G user terminal implementing Galileo HAS receiver. Testing will include an over the air field test.

title: TECHNOLOGIES TO ACCURATELY ESTIMATE THE BATTERY STATE OF CHARGE - EXPRO PLUS
description: Some new Li-Ion batteries have a very flat IV (current-voltage) curve. Thus, as they are discharged the voltage stays very flat. The classical method to measure the state of charge (SoC) was simply to measure the voltage. However, this is more complicated now because there is not a big change in voltage. Therefore, it is not possible to accurately estimate the SoC. This has very critical system level implications. A high battery discharge typically triggers an FDIR (Fault Detection, Isolation and Recovery) process to reconfigure the spacecraft, go to SAFE mode and be sun pointed. If the SoC is not accurately estimated, there could be no remaining energy in the battery to perform this critical manoeuvre.Some satellites are already suffering this issue and workarounds are being discussed. Therefore, it has been identified the need to understand how to really measure the SoC to implement a reliable system.The proposed activity aims at assessing various methods to achieve the above, in coordination with battery manufacturers. The various methods have to be implemented in an electronic circuit, aiming at minimising the complexity while having a good accuracy. The various methods should then be tested to understand the real accuracy of the system to select the most adequate one.As a minimum, the following methods shall be assessed:Modelling of the battery performance in an on-board FPGA (field-programmable gate array). Very high accuracy voltage sensing. In/Out Coulomb counting. Battery internal impedance estimation.The following tasks are foreseen in the frame of this activity:Review the state-of-the-art systems to estimate state of charge.Analyse the most promising methods.Trade-off the best possible candidate.Design the SoC estimator system.Build a breadboard of the SoC estimation system.Test the circuit.

title: S2-SW-06B: SPACE ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERISATION, NOWCAST AND FORECAST
description: This activity will continue to develop SWE Network capabilities in support of spacecraft operations and human spaceflight. It will build on developments and planning work taking place within the Space Radiation Expert Service Centre along with developments carried out within the P2-SWE-XIII Advanced SWE Service Prototypes, P3-SWE-XXXI Space Radiation Applications for Spacecraft Operators and in particular the P3-SWE-X and S1-SW-14.2 Space Environment Nowcast and Forecast development parts 1 and 2.The activity will develop both models and tools geared towards characterising the Earth's trapped radiation environment and resulting effects, targeting theneeds of both spacecraft operators and human spaceflight. Products and tools available to support rapid post-event analysis, nowcast and forecast of the space environment shall continue to be developed and validated. The range of indices available for spacecraft operators shall be extended, taking into account direct feedback from end users, and additional focus shall be placed on uncertaintydescription such that all products can be provided along with realistic confidence levels.

title: HIGH TEMPERATURE HEAT TRANSPORT SYSTEM FOR OXYGEN PRODUCTION ISRU PILOT PLANT - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop a high temperature heat transport system for oxygen production ISRU Pilot Plant, providing temperature control for the pilot plant vacuum distillation cavity.DescriptionThe ISRU Pilot Plant mission concept comprises the down-scaled production of oxygen in support of sustainable human lunar exploration. The oxygen production process is based on molten-saltelectrolysis of lunar regolith. One of the challenges in the ISRU Plant operation is the thermalmanagement of the processes, such as regolith sintering, electrolysis, salt recovery, fluidmanagement and processing, and LOX storage. These, take place at different temperatures, goingfrom high temperatures (up to 1100degC) to cryogenics.The plant requires a solution to provide temperature control with a variable conductance to adedicated radiator for the pilot plant vacuum distillation cavity, operating alternatively at 600degC(distillation) and 900degC (salt re-melting). Furthermore, the developed system will cover other functions such as temperature homogenization of thermal cavities for regolith processing at high temperatures and temperature control of large thermal zone operating at 750degC.This activity aims at developing a breadboard (BB) of a high temperature heat transport system for oxygen production ISRU pilot plant based which is freeze tolerant and has heat transport capabilityup to 700 W with heat transport distance of 1 m. The system shall be able to operate in temperaturerange of 400-1100degC.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of existing technologiesand trade-offs of various housing materials and workingfluids.- Development of the technical specification- Detailed design of the high temperature heat transport system- Manufacture of breadboards (BB)- Testing of the Breadboards in the specified temperature range under vacuum conditions.- Correlate test results and provide a detail assessment on the future work.

title: COMMERCIAL OFF-THE-SHELF (COTS) DIGITAL TO ANALOG CONVERTER PRE-EVALUATION - EXPRO PLUS
description: There is a limited availability of qualified/radiation hardened DAC with high resolution. Currently,with just one 16-bit high speed and one high precision low speed qualified DAC available from twodifferent manufacturers. At the moment, state of the art DAC have 16 or higher bits, low powerconsumption and good linearity at medium speed. Such DAC have high demand, therefore oftencommercialdevices are proposed without any knowledge on radiation robustness in heavy ions fordestructive event (SEL: Single Event Latch-up)and functional interrupt (SEFI: Single EventFunctional Interrupt).As the organization of the test campaign is often lengthy and the realization of test set up requireslarge effort and specific skills, the benefit of this activity would be to offer a set of relevant radiationdata on state of art DAC to designers in an early stage of the design of an instrument.This activity encompasses thefollowing tasks:- Perform a market survey and select 4 best candidates (selected based on precision, knowledge of the technology, power consumption, speed and input/channel configuration, linearity). title: DIGITAL TWIN SUPPORTED DESIGN AND MANUFACTURING OF THRUSTERS FOR CONSTELLATIONS (ARTES AT 4B.188) - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a digital-twin based design and manufacturing methodology for thrusters for LEO satellites, allowing higher accuracy thrust predictions significantly improving the development and verification approach and fuel margin philosophyTargeted Improvements:- Reduction of electric thruster manufacturing, assembly, integration, test duration andcomplexity by 25%. - Reduction of satellite propellant level margins by 5% - Increase sustainability of propulsion systems by reducing the propellant and power required for ground testing.Activity Description: Thruster performance is very sensitive to small design variations and manufacturing tolerances and often full batch firing testing is required to confirm the thruster performance. This is not acceptable for large electric thruster orders for constellation, which typically require to test one out of ten thrustersto achieve effort and delivery time requirements. Accurate thruster performance prediction is also important to reduce propellant margins at satellite level, needed to compensate for possible underperformances of the untested engines.This activity will develop and test a digital-twin based design and manufacturing methodology to accurately predict the individual thruster performance (e.g. thrust, thrust vector and Isp) with respect to those of the product family of a widely used thruster technology. The sensitivity of thruster performance on the geometric variation and material property variation of the unit will be studied. A digital twin able to predict the thruster performance will be developed. A modular thruster breadboard with adjustable geometry as well as a thruster test bed will be developed, manufactured and characterised. The thruster breadboard will be tested and used to train the digital twin model. The achieved accuracy of the thruster performance prediction when compared to test results will be statistically evaluated and compared to the target of achieving a partial acceptable test philosophy of 1 out of 10 thrusters.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: DUAL BAND KU- AND KA-BAND LOW NOISE AMPLIFIER FOR FUTURE FLEXIBLE PAYLOADS (ARTES AT 5C.528) - EXPRO+ - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test an engineering model of a dual band (Ku- and Ka-band) Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) for future flexible payloads.Targeted Improvements:Enabling technology for seamless Ku- and Ka-band flexible payloads.Description: Current flexible satellites offer flexibility in terms of coverage and in-band frequency reconfigurability (e.g. Ku-band and Ka-band). However, this reconfigurability is frequency band specific and satellites requiring simultaneous operation in both bands, are required to duplicate frequency specific equipment, bringing a high penalty in terms of cost, mass and volume. A European source of state-of-the-art dual band LNAs which can offer both Ku-band and Ka-band capability for in-orbit configuration would provide the payload withenhanced and seamless multi-band flexibility and is an enabling step towards achieving frequencyagnostic payloads.This activity will design, build and test a dual band LNA engineering model covering the full Ku- and Ka- telecombands. The LNA shall have comparable RF performance to existing state-of-the-art single band MMIC devices (noise figure lower than2dB, with gain greater than 35dB) and lower power consumption compared to existing wideband LNAs, targeting less than 500mW. The engineering model shall be tested for critical functions including performance over temperature.

title: ORBITAL MANEUVERING ENABLED BY GAUGING AGGREGATE PROPERTIES (OMEGA) - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop robust time-varying guidance and control strategies for in-orbit servicing assemblyusing predictive dynamical models.This activity is part of the mini project "Spacecraft Clustering Technologies". This mini-project aims at developing technologies to attach multiple defunct spacecraft to a controlled large orbital structure with the double goal of securing the spacecraft materials for future use, while at the same time removing the risk of collision. The operational "Spacecraft Clustering" scenario foresees a tug that departing from a large orbital structure, approaches and captures a defunct spacecraft. The tug returns to the orbital structure, attaches the defunct spacecraft to the structure, and provides the structure with orbital maneuvering ability.The tug GNC system will need to handle large changes in the mass distribution, structural flexibility and environmental perturbations introduced by contact, manipulator movement or propellant transfer. In these cases, the system dynamic variations are significant and static linear feedback strategies are insufficient to ensure good pointing performance and disturbance rejection. Multivariable robust and linear-parameter varying control provides a strong framework to address these challenges.Furthermore, for a large variety of manoeuvres expected during in-orbit servicing assembly, the resulting disturbances can be anticipated using a sufficiently accurate predictive model of the dynamics (as input to feed-forward control). However, obtaining such accurate models is not a trivial task since the physical phenomena involved in robotic in-orbit servicing or assembly missions are highly nonlinear.To overcome such challenges, modern methods (including machine learning) can be combined with online system identification and parameter estimation strategies to produce physically meaningful predictive models together with uncertainty bounds.This activity aims at enabling the stabilisation of spacecraft assemblies (either servicer + serviced spacecraft or elements of a structure under construction) for the benefit of a wide range of future in-orbit servicing and assembly missions.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Literature survey- Scenario requirements definition- Development of learning enhanced robust and adaptable control guidance algorithms- Implementation on representative space processor- Worst case analysis of the methods- Conclusions and recommendations

title: IN-FLIGHT ELECTRO-STATIC DISCHARGE MONITOR FOR SPACECRAFT - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop non-intrusive sensors for the characterization of Electro-Static Discharge on Spacecraft (e.g. for LEO constellations) together with an on-board events detection algorithm based on advanced approaches (e.g. AI based).Description: Electro-Static Discharge (ESD) phenomena on spacecraft have been estimated to contribute to around 20% to 25% of satellites anomalies overall.Yet, in-flight characterization of spacecraft ESDs in-flight has never been undertaken in a systematic way. In addition, while mitigation strategies are known for classical s/c configurations, new technologies (e.g. flexible solar arrays) require specific characterization in terms of risk (including in-flight) in order to demonstrate their maturity. The need for ensuring European space assetsresilience in LEO combined with the trend to mass product, fly and operate low power low mass constellation satellites calls for efficient and standardized environmental effects diagnostics, among which the one proposed here. The occurrence of ESDson Spacecraft in-flight depends on specific spacecraft electrical configurations and coupling with environments. LEO constellations growing market are subject to such risk as reported in the case of present constellations with thousands of events observed in flight (GEO (telecom, earth observation), MEO (navigation, orbit raising), as well as SSO polar environments also present a risk in that respect) due toboth surface and internal charging. From there, identifying relevant probing location on spacecraft systems where to systematicallyaccommodate non-intrusive /low resources sensors (e.g. current probes and well located RF receivers) would be of high interest to primes, spacecraft designers and agencies to improve our understanding of ESD phenomena in space and its relation to anomalies. In particular, the systematic integration of such sensors on low resource low mass constellation elements should enable large scale environmental effects diagnostics and improve the constellations resilience. This activity shall carry two phases in parallel or sequentially: Phase 1 - Review the state of the art in ESD detection and monitoring on spacecraft - Propose a concept design for a non-intrusive and system embedded method to detect, locate and measure arcing waveform signals onboard satellites - Perform breadboard testing to demonstrate critical functionalities - Define a consolidated design for an ESD monitor - Define a way forward to reach a TRL of 6 Phase 2 - Assess available methodologies (including AI/ML based) and propose a concept design for an on-board events detection algorithm - Develop a breadboard model to simulate events detection and test the detection method - Consolidate the design and propose a detailed design - Establish a development roadmap.http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

title: JOINT SATELLITE COMMUNICATION AND RADIO FREQUENCY SENSING FOR 6G NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORKS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.042) EXPRO+
description: The objective of this activity is to develop, implement and test a radio frequency air interface for joint satellite communication and sensing purposes in a representative system scenario and a commonly selected frequency band. A test-bed will be used to evaluatethe ranging/RF sensing accuracy and achievable throughput without degradation of the communication channel.Targeted Improvements:Compared to the existing opportunistic sensing systems using communication signals, improve the accuracy and performance of the detection and ranging measurement by 50%. Improve the throughput efficiency of the joint communications and sensing air interface by 40%compared to the state of-the-art.Description: Joint communication and sensing (JCAS) emerged as a way to improve the utilisationof the spectrum resources as well as the infrastructure both at space and on ground by sharing the same physical layer solution. Several emerging application scenarios such as space situational awareness (SSA), maritime surveillance, autonomous shipping, air traffic control of UAVs as well as in-land geo-localisations and machine-to-machine communications in remote areas are examples of possible joint satellite communications and sensing applications. Standardisation bodies, such as 3GPP or ETSI, are in fact now discussing JCAS from the operational and regulatory perspectives. Current research results indicate that advanced signal processing techniques in the air interface design would allow coexistence of radio detection and ranging to share spectrum with satellite communicationssystems. Other strategies such as sharing the transmit/receive hardware units, waveform adaptations and design could also be employed. During this activity, the performance of the joint air interface design in terms of critical parameter such as the estimation accuracy as well as the achievable communication throughput shall be compared with the results based on the opportunistic signals fromexisting 3GPP waveforms. Furthermore, the outcome of the activity will be presented to the relevant 3GPP standardisation groups (SAand RAN) and serve as a benchmark for possibly new air interface standards, servicing both remote sensing and communication services. The following technical challenges need to be addressed: - The design of an air interface that allows measuring accurately signal characteristics at the receiver (such as timing, phase and directional of arrival) for remote sensing while maintaining a high spectral efficiency for communications, and full-duplex operation with a capability of continuous transmission and reception for remotesensing applications. - The complexity of transmitters and receivers that reach the required accuracy for remote sensing while minimising the impact on the communication link throughput, would require architectural design trade-off and techniques selection and verifications. - Definition of scenarios regarding available and future payload technologies (antenna, front-end and processing). Description: The objective of this activity is to develop, implement and test a radio frequency air interface for joint satellite communication and sensing purposes in a representative system scenario and a commonly selected frequency band. A test-bed will be used to evaluatethe ranging/RF sensing accuracy and achievable throughput without degradation of the communication channel.Targeted Improvements:Compared to the existing opportunistic sensing systems using communication signals, improve the accuracy and performance of the detection and ranging measurement by 50%. Improve the throughput efficiency of the joint communications and sensing air interface by 40%compared to the state of-the-art.Description: Joint communication and sensing (JCAS) emerged as a way to improve the utilisationof the spectrum resources as well as the infrastructure both at space and on ground by sharing the same physical layer solution. Several emerging application scenarios such as space situational awareness (SSA), maritime surveillance, autonomous shipping, air traffic control of UAVs as well as in-land geo-localisations and machine-to-machine communications in remote areas are examples of possible joint satellite communications and sensing applications. Standardisation bodies, such as 3GPP or ETSI, are in fact now discussing JCAS from the operational and regulatory perspectives. Current research results indicate that advanced signal processing techniques in the air interface design would allow coexistence of radio detection and ranging to share spectrum with satellite communicationssystems. Other strategies such as sharing the transmit/receive hardware units, waveform adaptations and design could also be employed. During this activity, the performance of the joint air interface design in terms of critical parameter such as the estimation accuracy as well as the achievable communication throughput shall be compared with the results based on the opportunistic signals fromexisting 3GPP waveforms. Furthermore, the outcome of the activity will be presented to the relevant 3GPP standardisation groups (SAand RAN) and serve as a benchmark for possibly new air interface standards, servicing both remote sensing and communication services. The following technical challenges need to be addressed: - The design of an air interface that allows measuring accurately signal characteristics at the receiver (such as timing, phase and directional of arrival) for remote sensing while maintaining a high spectral efficiency for communications, and full-duplex operation with a capability of continuous transmission and reception for remotesensing applications. - The complexity of transmitters and receivers that reach the required accuracy for remote sensing while minimising the impact on the communication link throughput, would require architectural design trade-off and techniques selection and verifications. - Definition of scenarios regarding available and future payload technologies (antenna, front-end and processing). title: EU-AFRICA SPP - CONTINENTAL INNOVATION
description: This tender aims to implement the activities required for the Continental Innovation component of the EU-Africa Space Partnership Programme (funded by DG INTPA under the Global Gateway initiative). The relevant activities will span across the entire period of thefirst phase of the programme (2025-2028) and are to be implemented at continental level. This component aims at strengthening the African space private ecosystem and facilitate European-African industrial cooperation. Therefore, the main objective of this procurement is to setup a capacity development program dedicated to the EO private sector in Africa including: 1) the implementation of trainings aimed at empowering young African entrepreneurs and researchers to develop private sector EO applications and services, 2) the development of mentoring and grant issuing programs to support African start-ups, and 3) the setup of matchmaking events and activities between European-African EO innovators, industry and private investors at continental scale.

title: NAVISP-EL1-107-ULTRA-HIGH SPATIAL RESOLUTION GNSS RECEIVER FOR AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRY - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: The ability of exploiting the spatial dimensions has allowed array antennas to be exploited in various applications, e.g., multipath and interference mitigation; spatial diversity; and localization. Consequently, over the past years, array antennas have been deployed in GNSS receivers either to provide a spatial filter or to improve the SNR level using beamforming techniques. In order to achieve a high spatial resolution, a large array antenna aperture should be used. The manufacturing process of a large array antenna aperture, with fully synchronized and phase-coherent radio frequency (RF) chains, is very expensive and complex. Therefore, increasing the array antenna aperture, using a limited amount of antenna elements, is the main objective of this activity. In this activity weproposed a moving array antenna instead of a single antenna receiver. By exploiting the vehicle movement, the aperture of the arrayantenna (with a limited number of antennas) can be virtually expanded to provide the virtual effect of hundreds of antennas.

title: TERABIT PER SECOND ETHERNET SWITCH FOR CONSTELLATIONS WITH OPTICAL INTERSATELLITE LINKS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5F.046)
description: The objective of the activity is to develop, manufacture and test a technology agnostic ethernet switch intellectual property (IP) core supporting layers 1 to 3 as needed for constellations with optical intersatellite links. The core will be implemented and tested on a field programmable gate array. The data rate and number of ports shall be configurable, and multi-protocol label switching, Flex Ethernet and internet protocol shall be supported. Targeted Improvements: Enabling a European or Canadian source of space compatible ethernet switches for low earth orbit constellations.Description: Cost sensitive low earth orbit constellation solutions require a tailored packet switch adapted to the need with respect to data rate above 10 Gbps, number of ports (16 and more) and supportedprotocols. A technology agnostic ethernet switch, scalable in data rate and number of ports and supporting layer 1 to 3 protocols, does not exist in the space industry. Commercial solutions are available as black box solutions that cannot be modified. They provide much more functionality, which makes them unattractive for the cost sensitive application case in low earth orbit constellations. Commercial solutions of much more capable switches are available but cannot be adapted to the application need. Flex Ethernet, multi-protocol label switching, and internet protocol are currently discussed but suitable solutions could not be found in ongoing technology studies. The activity will develop a technology agnostic ethernet switch that can be implemented in different hardware solutions. A representative breadboard will be developed, manufactured and tested. The main engineering tasks are the development of the switch IP core in line with the requirements for the low Eorbit constellation application, testing of the IP core on at least two selected technologies and testing of the IP core implemented in a breadboard.

title: ULTRA-EFFICIENT COMPACT CARRIER ENVELOPE FREQUENCY DETECTION UNIT FOR OPTICAL FREQUENCY COMBS - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to build a Carrier Envelope Offset frequency (fCEO) detection demonstrator with fiber in-coupling and fCEO electrical signal to reduce the coupling losses into the optical waveguide to enhance the overall frequency conversion efficiency. The power consumption of a frequency comb is directly related to the (small) pulse energy required to detect the carrier-envelope offset frequency (fCEO) of the pulsed source. Typically, fCEO detection requires sufficient pulse energy to generate an octaves panning spectrum and second harmonic generation (SHG) of the red end of the spectrum. This drives the optical power requirement, and hence power consumption, on the optical source (oscillator and often optical amplifier). Current technology involves a highly nonlinear optical fiber (HNLF) to broaden the spectrum and a nonlinear bulk crystal for frequency doubling. New technologies based on a Photonic Integrated Circuit (PIC) offers the prospect to substantially reduce this pulse energy (by factor of ten). Demonstration of a packaged, Carrier Envelope Offset frequency (fCEO) detection demonstrator unit with fiber in-coupling and fCEO electrical signalout which shall also take full advantage of any recent development enhancements in the capabilities of integrated photonics. Particular emphasis is taken to reduce the coupling losses into the optical waveguide to enhance the overall frequency conversion efficiency.The following tasks are foreseen in this activity: Development of a fCEO based on the new Lithium Niobate on Insulator (LNoI) or Lithium Niobate on Silicon Nitride (LNoSN) or any other competitive platforms. Provide a few possible design options to explore. Trade off the various designs to meet the primary goal of enhance efficiency and system simplification. Manufacture the final design for assembly and verification test at system level. Provide verification of the (10x) enhanced performance using bulk and waveguide technologies as demonstrators. Develop preliminary device packaging options, without sacrificing performance.
