title: NEXT-GENERATION PROTOCOL FOR OPTICAL HIGH-SPEED LINKS - EXPRO PLUS
description: In 2019, the SpaceFibre ECSS standard was published. SpaceFibre is a high-speed protocol similarto commercial protocols such as PCI express and USB 3, which allows data rates of up to 10 Gbpsper lane (via optical, can be further extended by multiple lanes).Technically, for non-space applications, these capabilities were state-of-the-art in the mid 2000s. Inthe meanwhile, commercial protocols moved on to support much higher data rates (28, 56, 112Gbps), which require different Serializer/Deserializer (SERDES) techniques (e.g. PAM4) and linecodes (e.g. 64b/67b, 128b/130b, 242b/256b).There is no protocol option, targeting such performance figures that has been evaluated on spacequalified hardware. Commercial IP cores often come at high cost and with difficult license terms,therefore an alternative for the European space industry is required. Several Europeanmanufacturers work on optical transceivers suitable for space applications that provide data ratesbeyond 10 Gbps per lane. However, required standardisation efforts for the components as well asinteroperability status between different solutions needs to be clarified.This activity encompasses the followingtasks:- Survey of all components and aspects related to the network physical layer that requirestandardisation, including e.g., connectors, fibres, transceivers, repeaters, data rates, andnumber of lanes- Survey of space and terrestrial high-speed link protocols related to the datalink layer thatare suitable for optical on-board communication. The survey includes the critical assessmentof the capabilities of different protocols (scalability, adaptability to future transceiverimplementations, increasing number of data rates, number of lanes, improved encodingschemes and error correction schemes), of the implementation complexity in space-qualifiedhardware, and cost/licensing aspects- A trade-off and selection of a preferred solution- Survey of validation aspects for optical high-speed communication links- Design and manufacturing of a basic COTS-based breadboard, demonstrating thecapabilities of the chosen protocol- Testing and validation of the COTS-based breadboard.

title: COMPLEMENTATION OF ANAEROBIC BIOREACTOR FOR WASTE DEGRADATION FROM LONG-TERM HUMAN MISSIONS - RE-ISSUE
description: Re-supply and waste management are a critical elements of a crewed space exploration. A significant part of pressurized cargo uploaded mass consists of packaging material (0.3 kg/person/day) which cannot be recycled into resources and become mission waste. Currently, no waste management practice has been implemented in space other than sealing and mixing waste items (metabolic and non-metabolic), followed by manual compaction and temporary storage intocargo vehicles and subsequent disposal (return to earth or destructive re-entry). This approach to waste management is unfeasible to sustain, especially in missions with increased distance from Earth (e.g. lunar outpost surface missions) and reduced frequency of re-supply. MELiSSA C1 Waste Compartment is the only waste biodegradation process envisaged so far for space applications in Europe. Yet, its complete microbial consortium and dynamics remain unknown and it is fully devoted to transform the metabolic waste derived from the crewed mission.This activity aims at improving the waste management strategy for future missions beyond LEO byexpanding the waste input suitable for the MELiSSA Waste Compartment. This approach supports the creation of a synthetic microbial community capable of transforming both metabolic and nonmetabolic waste. This is atechnology push to explore improved robustness and efficiency of the C1 consortium specifically in view of the capability to adapt towaste from packaging.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of existing microbial communities ubiquitously present in the MELiSSA anaerobic bioreactor which are capable of biodegrading the alternative packaging material developed in a previous activity. Compatibility with key microbial consortium and operating conditionsin MELiSSA anaerobic bioreactor shall be addressed.-Microbial consortium complementation and preliminary full testing of the metabolic and nonmetabolicwaste degradation efficiency. Special attention shall be paid to the population dynamics and resilience, macro- and micro-compounds mass balances, energy balances,methanogenesis inhibition and inhibition of secondary toxic metabolites formation during the conversion process.- The update of mathematical models equations to transform the mechanistic model of the waste anaerobic bioreactor into a white-box model. This allows a complete control and predictability of the system with full knowledge of its genomic potential.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: PHASE A FOR SPACE CLOUD MISSION - EXPRO PLUS
description: Data centres are the backbone of our digital infrastructure. With the rise of artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing and theinternet of things (IoT), the amount of data generated and processed daily is increasing at a fast pace, and the demand for data centres is constantly growing. Unfortunately, data centres are massively energy hungry, thus environmentally impacting, although efforts are done in terms of energy sources and optimisation of use and recovery of heat generated. One possible expected alternative is to build the data centre in space, and several companies are working on the concepts to making this a reality. The concept is not new, but the evolution of the environment is giving a new push, and studies are on-going or being initiated.The overall objective of the Phase A for Space Cloud Mission is to perform a feasibility assessment with the aim to prepare for the Space Cloud Mission. Parallel contracts may be placed in case of competitive complementary proposals

title: 5G NEW RADIO (NR) NON-TERRESTRIAL NETWORKS RELEASE 18 PROTOCOL STACK ENHANCEMENTS (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.011)
description: The objective of this activity is to develop the software protocol stack for Release 18 enhancements related to 5G New for Radio (NR) for Non-Terrestrial Networks. The software protocol stack development shall be based on a testbed considering both the User Equipment (UE) and g-NodeB (gNB) features and operational procedures.Targeted Improvements:Enable 5G NR NTN system performance simulations with the latest Release 18 modifications.Description:The 5th generation of wireless broadband networks (5G) promised a new paradigm in communications, offering higher transmission rates, more Internet of Things (IoT) and internet application connections, high reliability, very low latency, and connectivity for remote areas. The 5G New Radio (NR) adaptations for Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs) have been introduced for the first time in the 3GPP Release 17 specifications, to support network offloading, coverage enhancements, connectivity resilience and service continuation in remote areas. With the support of the ARTES 5G Workplan, open-source software protocol stack versions have been implemented for NTN Release 17, starting from the Open-Air Interface (OAI) and from the SRS library. Based on the current 3GPP work item description, the new Release 18 will introduce further features related to the support and the enhancements of 5G NR services in satellite networks. Among the new features, it is recalled that NTN Release 18 will supportdownlink/uplink coverage enhancement techniques, network verified UE location capabilities, NTN-TN mobility enhancements for service continuity, and the support of above 10 GHz satellite frequency bands. The proposed activity shall thus foresee the following steps: a) Review the latest 3GPP specifications for the NTN scenario (i.e., Release 17) and identify the missing models and capabilitiesof the selected library to be enhanced with features of Release 18; b) Identify key features planned for Release 19 to be added to the library; c) Software design and development of the new functions in the protocol stack of both UE and gNB to support bi-directional communication links for both GEO and NGSO satellite networks; d) Thorough laboratory validation of the new software library capabilities. This activity should target publicly available licensing model (i.e., GPL licensing).

title: POWER MODULE WITH ADVANCED BATTERY MONITORING AND ELECTRICAL POWER SYSTEM TELEMETRY MANAGEMENT CAPABILITIES (ARTES AT 4F.169)
description: The objective of the activity is to develop, manufacture and test a power module with a new concept for Li-Ion battery management and with an advanced Electrical Power System Telemetry able to collect, store, retrieve and process large quantity of data related tothe Status of the Power System (SA, Battery, PCDU). A digital oscilloscope for the Built-In Test function and a function to analysein flight the degradation of solar arrays will be implemented in this new power module.Targeted Improvements:- Enabling automatisation of the assembly, integration and test; and in-flight anomaly investigations; and In-flight test data harvesting with a built-in test architecture.- To provide large quantity of data for Artificial Intelligence learning processDescription: One of the parameters used to trigger the satellite safe mode is the level of energy stored in the battery. However this parameter is an estimation and is typically set rather low, giving not much time to react. Monitoring the energy consumed by the different loads, and with an appropriate algorithm, could allow to immediately check if the satellite is on the path to enter the safe mode with a large time margin and thus the rundown time of the satellite would be reduced. The telemetry provided by Satellites is a reduced dataset, sub-sampled to a few hundred sample per seconds with a traditional design, which this is barely sufficient for anomaly investigations. Advanced Failure Detection Identification and Recovery (FDIR) as well as the learning phase of an AI (artificial intelligence) algorithm when applied to satellites and constellations, require a large quantity of data. Thus there is a need to increase the power moduleand battery health monitoring capabilities and sampling rate. Additionally, the inclusion of a Built-In Digital Oscilloscope would eliminate the need to have accessible test points, improving reliability and reducing the size of the boards. Also, the proposed activity will also benefit the solar array, for which it is hard to assess the degradation status while on flight. This intelligent module will implement a system to characterise the degradation in flight. In some terrestrial applications, "Built-in Test" functions are already implemented in industrial equipment. Often the equipment is so densely packed that there is no possibility to connect test probes, which means that telemetry data set includes already test data. Data need to be stored and then accessed when needed. A fast data link connection to a processor for onboard processing and/or to damp the data to mass memory must be established. For the battery health monitoring, the main development area will be the implementation of a continuous energy balance calculations considering instantaneous generated, stored and consumed power. The AI algorithm could be used to check if the balance is "sound" much earlier, thus detecting a performance drift far prior to failure. For the solar array monitoring, a sweep of the Current / Voltage curve ofthe solar array can be performed to understand the degradation status. Depending on the power system topology, several options can be used to perform the sweep while continuing with the operations in a nominal way.A power module breadboard, with battery advancedmonitoring and telemetry management block, will be designed, built and tested to demonstrate additional capabilities can be added to the power system.

title: RISC-V INSTRUCTION SET ARCHITECTURE SIMULATION MODEL AND EMULATION IN VIRTUAL PLATFORM FOR HARDWARE-SOFTWARE CODESIGN - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop a simulation model of a RISC-V (reduced instruction set computer) instruction set architecture (ISA) processor and peripherals, in a suitable hardware-software co-design environment, and perform design space exploration of a system-on-chip.Description:RISC-V is an open-source and royalty-free hardware instruction set architecture based on RISC principles. An open ISA is remarkably interesting for space due to several reasons: It reduces potential difficulties in license negotiation or export restrictions. It allows to perform modifications for radiation mitigation. It adds or modifies instructions to execute functions that are frequently required by space applications, such as bit manipulation, sub-word arithmetic, vector or SIMD (single instruction, multiple data) computations.RISC-V has been gaining popularity in the past years, and its use in space is now close to a reality thanks to several on-going system-on-chip (SoC) developments that will embed RISC-V multi core processor, along with several other interfaces to enable their use in satellite payloads and platforms, such as SpaceFibre, TM/TC (telemetry/telecommand) or cryptographic functions. The successful adoption of this architecture and embarking of the future SoC depends in a great extent on the features of the hardware, and on the availability of software development tool chains that enable the programming of the cores with suitable on-board software.Hardware and software developments around RISC-V can benefit greatly from the hardware-software co-design development flow, which simultaneously considers hardware and software within the design process. This enables the co-development and co-verification of hardware and software using simulation and/or emulation with the help of tools such as virtual platforms where simulation models of the processor ISA, and models of other components of the SoC can be executed at different levelsof abstraction, and with the required simulation speed. A fast ISA simulator of RISC-V facilitates early software development and the development software tool chains. All this before the first hardware prototypes are available.ESA has promoted the development of the SoCRocket virtual platform, which has been made available to missions and projects. This platform is comprised by several functional blocks, and can be used to simulate a SoC, but now, only LEON based systems are currently supported.This activity aims at developing a simulation model of RISC-V that can be executed in a suitable virtual platform at an appropriate abstraction level, easing the development of software, and enabling hardware-software co-design and design space exploration of a system-on-chip.The main tasks to be accomplished are: Assess the suitability of a virtual platform to simulate a RISC-V based SoC considering trade-offs related to accuracy of the models and simulation speed, SoCRocket and possible alternatives. Create a simulation model of the RISC-Vinstruction set, that can be integrated in a virtual platform, directly or through an emulator, and aid the development of software. Develop and integrate new functional blocks in a virtual platform, such as: SpaceFibre, TM/TC functions, cryptography, Ethernet. Design space exploration in a RISC-V based multicore model of a SoC.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: COMPACT SPECTROMETERS USING METASURFACES - EXPRO PLUS
description: To demonstrate a novel ultra-compact spectrometer system by exploring the use of metasurfaces and other planar optics.DescriptionRecent developments in planar optics technology have shown a promising path towards the miniaturization of traditional optical instruments like spectrometers (e.g., on-going OSIP study "Compressive Sensing of Trace Gases: Replacing Diffractive Elements by anostructured Transmission Filters on a Detector"). The incorporated, highly scalable wafer level technology further allows a cost-efficient manufacturing. For Earth Observation (EO), building on those promising preliminary developments is a major opportunity to monitor trace gasses from several small spacecrafts and to decrease the size and the costs of the overall optical payload.Nano-structures can be engineered to either have a lens, grating, retarder, anti-reflection coating, or filter function; or even a mixture of these functions in a single robust element. By incorporating a tailored computational data processing chain e.g., using compressive sensing algorithms or machine learning, the overall performance (e.g., sensitivity, spectral resolution) can be optimized while the required data rate and the integration costs can be minimized. A metasurface-based spectrometer resulting from a combination of dispersive engineering, nano-lithography, systems design and computational processing can therefore render future optical payloads with extremely small form factors as well as high robustness and cost efficiency.The final outcome of this activity is an ultra-compact planar spectrometer system that demonstrates the potential of this technology in the frame of EO applications.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Explore metasurface designs targeting representative specifications for EO- Definition of system-level spectrometer design- Component level development, integration, and demonstration of planar optics- Integrated system breadboard to demonstrate functionality and performance testing.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses.

title: LUNAR LASER COMMUNICATION TERMINAL (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5G.045) - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to first design a Laser Communication Terminal (LCT) concept suitable for communicationover lunar distances. In a second step, the activity will develop an engineering model of a CCSDS compatible transceiver with critical functions including coding, synchronisation, and modulation. Targeted Improvements: Enabling a European or Canadian lunar communication terminal operating with a data rate one order of magnitude higher than current designs, with Earth (from 100s Mbps to 10Gbps), and compatible with the lunar orbit environment. Description:This activity will enable a European or Canadian laser optical terminal source of future lunar LCTs, requiring high data rate links. LCT links are currently available for near-Earth (LEO, GEO) and for deep-space (beyond the Moon) applications. The latter is not suited for this type of link as it is based on the ""high-photon efficiency"" standard and limited to data rate inferior to that required for lunar communications. Lunar links require the development of both a modified LCT concept and a new transceiver, capable of delivering at least 5 Gbps, for which the standard is currently under definition at CCSDS. Currently several LCTs (transceiver included) for Earth orbit applications are available and several others are under development in Europe. The Lunar LCT concept and transceiver that will be developed in this activity, will have to be adapted for lunar distances and the specific operating environment. The design shall support coding, synchronisation, and modulation forat least 5 Gbps rate over lunar distance.

title: MODEL-BASED SYSTEM ENGINEERING FOR INTERFACE MANAGEMENT - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop an interface engineering toolset providing electronic data sheet support for avionics and software development of space applications.Description: In deploying Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) in space projects, one of high priority elements is the management of interface. This activity builds upon a concept of exchange of interface called Electronic Data Sheet (EDS) which applies to software interface and equipment functional interface and is extended towards electrical interface. This activity aims at providing a toolset to support interface engineering activities, with the following capabilities: Provide means to capture the Electrical and Data interface of an equipment, with different levels of abstraction, from functional to physical. Process this input data to generate ECSS-compliant Interface Control Documents (ICD). Generate EDS material in a flexible way: the design shall provide customizable backend templates allowing to adapt to existing, legacy EDS formats already in place at system integrators. Compatibility with an MBSE process and supporting the transition between system and software developments. Compliance to ECSS-E-ST-10-24C standard (Interface Management). title: TRANSMIT-RECEIVE BEAMFORMING AND FRONT-END CIRCUITS AND CHIPS FOR Q-V BAND SATCOM TERMINALS (ARTES AT 7C.097) - RE-ISSUE
description: Objectives: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test integrated circuits of the critical beamforming functions in silicon technologies, enabling Q/V-band electronically steerable antenna for satcom terminals. As a minimum, two types of integrated circuits will be developed. One chip shall be a multichannel transmit-receive beamforming radio frequency integrated circuit (RFIC) and the second chip shall be a multichannel transmit-receive front end. Targeted Improvements: Enabling high-data rate electronically steerable Q/V band SATCOM terminals. Description: Deployment of Q/V band feeder links has accelerated, and Q/V band is expected be used also for high-throughput user links such as airborne terminals to leverage the available spectrum. As in Ku and Ka band, Q/V band terminals will require electronically steerable antenna. The architecture of a Q/V band electronically steerable antenna is expected to be similar to architectures used at Ku- and Ka-band, but key building blocks are not available in Europe. This activity will develop key building blocks enabling Q/V electronically steerable antennas for satcom terminals. A multi-channel beamforming transceiver and a transmitreceive front end with polarisation control will be designed, manufactured, and tested using European technology. Advanced packaging options will be selected (Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC), Wafer-Level Chip Scale Packaging (WLCS), Ball Grid Array (BGA), System in Package (SiP), etc.) for the chips. Functionality will be tested in a sub-array configuration that will consist of a number of multi-channel beamforming transceivers connected to transmit-receive front ends.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: END-TO-END PERFORMANCE SIMULATOR (EEPS) FOR CRYORAD - EXPRO+
description: In this project an end-to-end performance simulator shall be developed for the Earth Explorer 12 candidate mission CryoRad. The CryoRad satellite will carry a low-frequency wide-band radiometer to observe the cryosphere. The mission has four primary focus areas: 1) ice temperature profiles, 2) intraglacial water, 3) sea-surface salinity and 4) sea-ice thickness. Industrial consortia will propose concepts for the mission. The primary objective of the end-to-end performance simulator is to show that these mission concepts enable the observation of geophysical variables, related to the mission objectives, within the scientific requirements.

title: CRYOGENIC TESTING OF STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS FOR PROPULSION APPLICATIONS - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop test capabilities and generate performance data for CFRP components subject to mechanical loads in presence of large thermal gradients DescriptionNovel designs and advanced materials offer distinct advantages in strength/weight ratio, leading to mass savings and improved performance. Limited availability of test data and test facilities reduces the ability to assess/chose candidate materials and design solutions for use in a variety of structural launcher components when operating in challenging thermal environments.Critical structural components may operate under large thermal gradients during flight operation. Current conceptual designs of liquid propulsion systems foresee the use of structural items coupling cold components (e.g. cryo-tanks) to hot parts like thrust structures. Validation and verification of such design features becomes very complex and difficult to be performed in a representative thermal environment. Reliable test data on material performance under such large thermal gradients are thus increasingly valuable for current and future development and applications such as in launcher propulsion systems.This activity aims at developing unique testing capabilities and tools that allow representative testing of advanced structures under mechanical loads and complex thermal environments, i.e. application of static and dynamic mechanical loads and simultaneously large thermal gradients through structural components. The data is aimed to enable mechanical performance evaluation as well as model validation of advanced design concepts.This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Identification of features in space structural designs that experience high mechanical loads concomitant with large thermal gradients. Possible candidates are COPV/skirt connections, interface between cryogenic tank and engine thrust frame, structural fixtures and interfaces for cryogenic components. - Definition of testing requirements - Manufacturing of representative test specimens - Design the test for performing mechanical loading in superposition with application of large thermal gradients - Representative testing of the manufactured hardware in the representative thermal/mechanical environmentDeliverables Hardware, ReportProcurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: ASSESSMENT OF GRAPHENE BASED DEVICES AS MULTI-GAS SENSORS FOR HUMAN SPACEFLIGHT - EXPRO PLUS
description: To assess the potential of functionalized graphene devices as 'electronic nose' for human spaceflight applications to detect hazardous substances in space habitat atmospheres. Description:Graphene is an emerging novel semiconductor material that can be used for a wide range of applications. By treating the surface with different reagents, it can be made reactive to certain molecule types (functionalization). When a specific molecule 'docks' to the surface, changes in electrical resistance can be measured ('Chemristor'). Graphene-based gas sensors have the potential to be miniaturized, made light-weight and operate with low energy consumption compared to existing solutions such as mass-spectrometers. They could therefore be easily distributed over various habitat/ station modules or used within a spacesuit to act as early warning/ indicator systems. A previous PECS study (ESA contract no. 4000126337). used graphene/silver to collect trace gases and an IR spectrometer to detect them. In contrast, this activity intends to use graphene directly for both, collection and detection, thereby dropping fully the need for a spectrometer. This enables extreme miniaturization compared to state of the art solutions. This activity aims at assessing the potential of functionalized graphene devices for human spaceflight applications to detect hazardous gases, such as e.g. H2, O3, CO, CO2, NO, NH3, Hydrazine and others. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Identification of potentially occurring hazardous target substances expected in habitat modules- Perform a trade-off on the available sensing capabilities with respect to the identified hazardous gases.- Selection of different surface functionalisation routes for Graphene (-oxide) enabling peakresponse at the respective targeted substances.- Manufacturing of individual Graphene chemristor elements corresponding to above functionalization for the most targeted substances.- Combination of the individual chemristor elements to create a sensor array (demonstrator),supported by an intelligent readout (e.g. machine learning based) scheme to reach an electronic nose for the target substances. This shall be done by using not only peak responses from the chemristor sub-elements but instead taking substance 'fingerprint' signatures from the full array, to determine both, substance types and concentration levels at the same time.- Electrical characterization wrt selectivity, sensitivity, reaction time, refresh time, temperatureand operational stability, power consumption.Procurement Policy: C(3) = Activity restricted to SMEs RD Entities. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_for_SMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses.

title: DUAL BAND KU- AND KA-BAND POWER AMPLIFIER FOR FUTURE FLEXIBLE PAYLOADS (ARTES AT 5C.515) RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test an engineering model of a multi-band (Ku and Ka-band) integrated power amplifier for application in Lower Earth Orbit satellites, enabling seamless flexibility and reconfigurability for active antenna arrays. Targeted Improvements: Enabling technology for seamless Ku- and Ka-band flexible payloads:- reduces mass and volume by 50%,- improves reliability, bill of material and qualification effort by 50%.Description: Current flexible satellites offer flexibility in terms of coverage and in-band frequency reconfigurability. This reconfigurability is frequency-band specific as these satellites can operate in either Ku-band or Ka-band, but not both. However, frequency agnostic antennas are needed for future satcom systems. A key building block for such systems are multi-band power amplifiers. A multi-band power amplifier could offer both Ku-band andKa-band capability for in-orbit configuration and could provide the payload with enhanced and seamless multi-band flexibility. Thisactivity will design, manufacture and test a multi-band Microwave Monolithic Integrated Circuit (MMIC) power amplifier breadboard covering both Ku and Ka band to achieve nominal operating power level in the range of 2W to 4W with greater than 35% power added efficiency at amplifier module over both frequency bands with minimised footprint, enabling future multi-band active antenna arrays in LEOsatellites.

title: E2CS-050 - LUNAR COLD AND TRANSIENT VOLATILE-RICH RETURN SAMPLE CHAIN NEEDS - EXPRO+
description: The imminent return of new samples from the Moon, including those with the most transient properties, e.g., cold-trapped and transient volatile-rich samples, imposes new requirements and needs driving the lunar sample return chain. Constraining and prioritising a quantified and justified set of return sample requirements will inform the critical technical needs that are to be developed and implemented for the safe collection, best preservation and optimised utilisation of novel and diverse return samples. These requirements will inform the planning and development for Europe's endeavours for future lunar sample return.

title: MINIATURISED SELF-BIASED CIRCULATORS/ISOLATORS FOR GAN APPLICATIONS - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop miniaturized self-biased circulators and isolators, based on hexaferrites, as Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) for Ka-band GaN applications. Description: Due to the recent developments in GaN technologies, miniaturized RF passive components, are needed to be directly integrated inside the PCB (Printed Circuit Board) as MMIC (Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit). Current designs of circulators and isolators consistently include bulky magnets needed to polarize the ferrites. Mount-on coaxial circulators are not suitable to be integrated directly in the equipment at high frequencies (Ka band and beyond). Therefore, removing magnets appears as one of the main solutions to improve the integration of these components. This technological step requires the use of self-biased (auto polarized) ferrites in their remanent state, known as pre-oriented hexaferrites. Thus, the need to develop innovative MMIC circulators and isolators based on hexaferrites for Ka band GaN applications. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Literature review and market survey; - Technology and process review for the selection of promising solutions;- Development and Manufacturing of the self-biased circulators and isolators; - Characterization of isolator/circulator RF performance, including, as a minimum Sparameters and thermal cycling; - Identification of limitations, improvements and roadmap for future space qualification.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: SCI-S NETAPP STORAGE EVOLUTION
description: The ESA's Programmatic IT section (PIT) manages all the ESA's Science and Operations department (SCI-S) programmatic IT infrastructure, applications and services. Due to the continuous growth of data volumes and the increasing demand for flexibility, performance,availability, and operational simplicity, there is a need to evolve the current SCI-S NetApp storage system. The new infrastructuremust not only scale efficiently but also deliver enhanced capabilities to meet future enterprise storage requirements.This transformation involves a shift in architecture, moving towards a more modern and resilient platform. The goal is not only to keep pace with technological advances, but to anticipate themdeploying a solution that is robust, future-proof, and aligned with our current andfuture IT storage needs.Additionally, to complement and protect the primary storage architecture, a secondary storage system is required to enhance data resilience and support operational recovery strategies. While the primary system provides high performance and automated tiering, the secondary system acts as a dedicated snapshot repositoryensuring data is protected against accidental deletion, corruption, or system failure, without impacting the performance of the primary environment. The secondary system needs to be based on a unified HDD-based storage architecture designed for cost-effective and reliable data protection

title: HIGH POWER OPTICAL TERMINATION - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop a high power optical termination for polarisation maintaining fibers.DescriptionOptical feeder-links to and from future terabit telecommunication satellites will require high powertransmit beams. The continuous development of optical amplifiers for space applications has demonstrated optical power of 10 Watts and next generation is targetting 100 Watts. This opens the question on the definition of the optical interface between the fibered optical amplifier and the beam in free space that would minimise the risk of catastrophic optical damage to the fiber end.The currently available space qualified connector is not designed to cope with several Watts. To help with the high power, this activity aims at developing a fiber termini or a connector in order to provide the thermal management of the high power, a robust mechanical interface to the focal plane and deliver a high quality optical beam.Typical reliability requirements are based on GEO type application for 15 to 18 years, radiationhardened, 500 thermal cycling resistant and capable to operate in vacuum. The type of the output fiber is expected to be a polarisation maintaining at 1550 nm,and the cable assembly is to be testedagainst thermal cycling and humidity, mechanical environments and radiation resistance as aminimum.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Establish requirements specification based on focal plane suppliers- Design and materials selection- Prototype of the high power termination, draft of the product identification document and thetest plan- Environmental testing (thermal cycling, humidity, mechanical environments, and radiations)- Draft detail specifications.

title: HIGH IMPEDANCE SURFACE FOR SMALL SATELLITE APPLICATION - EXPRO PLUS
description: To mitigate signal interference for space PNT users by means of High Impedance Surface.DescriptionIn the past years the using ofGNSS signal for precise in orbit determination of the satellites positioning has been extensively used. The effort to miniaturize the GNSS RX antenna , making it compatible with a multi frequencies and multi constellation scenario, gave the possibility for the deployment of the Precise Pointing Positioning in space, even for small satellites. Those kind ofantennas, designed to have a high phase centre stability over frequency and small phase centre variation over angular range, minimizes the distortions of the received GNSS signal, allows the receiver to get the best estimation of the PNT parameters. Impacts in one of those antenna parameters is translated to a severe degradation in the GNSS receiver chain performance.As well known in the scientific community, one strong factor that might effect phase centre stabilityand phase centre variation is represented by the multipath. Several solutions have been proposedfor ground users, and one of those is considered very attractive for those space applications wheremass and total high are considered very critical (e.g. small satellite application like LEO PNT ,satcom or future science missions ). The proposed solution is based on specific artificial surface,printed on PCB and surrounding the antenna, that mitigate the RF currents flow on the body of thesatellite, a consequently, reduce its scattering effects on the antenna radiation pattern.In addition, this solution allows to increase the isolation between antennas working at the samefrequency band, helping the interleaving of Transmitter (TX)and Receiver (RX) service on the samesatellite (e.g. LEO PNT or SATCOM operating in L-band).The objective of the activity is the investigation and implementation of special RF surfaces (e.g. cutoff or non cut off printed corrugation), in order to reduce as much as possible the current flow on the satellite body, allowing improvement of :1) the antenna phase centre performance in a complex environment ;2) the isolation between possible TX and RX antennas mounted on the same satellite.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Identification, based on literature survey and technical trade-offs, the most promising technology and- Deployment method;- Detail design of the deployment the most promise artificial surface;- Manufacturing and testing of the breadboard to validate the concept.

title: PRISE (PARTICLE RADIATION INSTRUMENT AND SPECTROMETER FOR EUROPE) - EXPRO PLUS
description: Continuous in-situ monitoring of the energetic particle environment is one of the pillars for space weather now- and fore-casting, and also serves as basis for development and improvement of models for in-flight prediction of the radiation environment.Radiation monitor development for recurrent flights has traditionally focused on measurement of electrons and protons from the Van Allen belts or from Solar Particle Events with instrumentation based on relatively simple detection concepts, with small mass, volume, power, and telemetry budgets. While enabling embarkation on a number of missions, simple designs typically implycompromising on detection efficiency, particle identification purity, particle energy range andaccuracy in energy determination.A new instrument concept with slightly larger budgets (mass, power, volume, data) than traditionalmonitors, shall overcome the compromises in performance, and provide new "gold standard" setsof high accuracy measurements. The instrument shall serve as cross-calibration reference for thenetwork of lower resource radiation monitors. A modular concept shall allow mission-optimizeddesign, and a wider range in particle species and energies if flying complementary designs withdifferent sensor configurations on multiple simultaneous missions.This activity aims at designing a high accuracy, European radiation instrument with instrumentmeasurements covering electrons, protons and ions with a combined extended energy range 0.1 -8 MeV (electron) and 1 - 500 MeV/nuc (protons/ions) with sufficient statistics. Compared to standardmonitors, it is expected that this instrument will achieve better energy resolution (x2), higher channelpurity (10x) and better sensitivity to low fluxes (x10). The instrument concept shall be based on a modular design with dedicated sensors for particle/energy range, configurable per mission.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Measurement requirements consolidation- Investigation of possible detection methods available for identified particle species andenergies- Detailed instrument concepts based on assembly of complementary detection methods- Instrument concepts performance analysis by detailed simulation in realistic environments- Trade-off of performance, technologies and needed resources.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation(in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. title: S2-SW-06D: SOLAR AND HELIOSPHERIC WEATHER TOOLKIT DEVELOPMENT
description: This activity will further extend the capabilities of both the Solar Weather Expert Service Centre and the Heliospheric Weather Expert Service Centre, building on high priority developments identified in the Expert Service Centres' Definition and Development plans. The activity will start with an analysis of available solar event onset modelling techniques and their current maturity level, asseen in the context of space weather monitoring and forecasting. Targeted development will lead to a suite of solar event onset modelling capabilities which will be integrated into the SWE Network as a toolkit on a test and validation basis. The toolkit will utilise existing solar measurement data where applicable, and shall be integrated into the SWE Portal as part of the Space Weather Service Network, with the underpinning modelling capabilities being made available for integration into the Virtual Space Weather Modelling Centre. Recommendations for future solar event onset modelling development in support of SWE Services shall be produced followinga period of test and validation as part of the SWE Network. This activity shall further build on preliminary results of the P3-SWE-IV.2: Use of L5 Data in CME Propagation Models study and will include development of advanced tools to support forecasters in CME characterization and arrival time forecasting with the aim to reduce uncertainties and facilitate integration of multiple data sourcesand types. These shall be developed, tested and validated utilising current data sources in preparation for future utilisation of data from the Vigil mission when available. Recommendations and a roadmap for further development shall form part of this activity with the aim to ensure optimal utilisation of data from the Vigil mission when available. Forecaster training in use of the tools shall be included as part of the activity.

title: PHASE A FOR A SPACE CIRCULAR ECONOMY MISSION - EXPRO PLUS
description: ESA is encouraging the implementation of a circular economy' in space that ensures long-term orbital sustainability through in-orbit servicing. Several activities comprise the circular economy in space, namely on-orbit assembly, on-orbit manufacturing, and on-orbit recycling, all supported by technologies for on-orbit servicing, rendezvous, and close-proximity operations. These technologies will allow us to treat orbital space as a finite resource, re-use space assets, and minimize the waste associated with building and disposing of spacecraft.ESA concluded a studies campaign in early 2025, which supported four pre-Phase A industrial feasibility studies looking at on-orbit refurbishment, manufacturing, and recycling in Earth orbit. From these studies, two concepts have been selected as winners of the campaign and their concepts have been consolidated together with ESA experts by performing Concurrent Design studies at ESA ESTEC Concurrent Design Facility. As outcome of this work, ESA has identified on-orbit refurbishment as its primary near-term goal for the next generation of circular economy activities through in-orbit servicing capabilities. The scope of the proposed work will be to mature the on-orbit refurbishment concept with a Phase A study focusing on the design of an in-orbit demonstration missions and the identification of the critical technologies to be developed in the next coming years.The procurement will be open competition to all industrial entities, ensuring an opencompetitive approach preparing further steps. Parallel contracts may be placed in case of competitive complementary proposals.

Description: ESA is encouraging the implementation of a circular economy' in space that ensures long-term orbital sustainability through in-orbit servicing. Several activities comprise the circular economy in space, namely on-orbit assembly, on-orbit manufacturing, and on-orbit recycling, all supported by technologies for on-orbit servicing, rendezvous, and close-proximity operations. These technologies will allow us to treat orbital space as a finite resource, re-use space assets, and minimize the waste associated with building and disposing of spacecraft.ESA concluded a studies campaign in early 2025, which supported four pre-Phase A industrial feasibility studies looking at on-orbit refurbishment, manufacturing, and recycling in Earth orbit. From these studies, two concepts have been selected as winners of the campaign and their concepts have been consolidated together with ESA experts by performing Concurrent Design studies at ESA ESTEC Concurrent Design Facility. As outcome of this work, ESA has identified on-orbit refurbishment as its primary near-term goal for the next generation of circular economy activities through in-orbit servicing capabilities. The scope of the proposed work will be to mature the on-orbit refurbishment concept with a Phase A study focusing on the design of an in-orbit demonstration missions and the identification of the critical technologies to be developed in the next coming years.The procurement will be open competition to all industrial entities, ensuring an opencompetitive approach preparing further steps. Parallel contracts may be placed in case of competitive complementary proposals.

title: PROTOCOL STACK ENABLING VOICE-CALL USING NON-TERRESTRIAL IOT WAVEFORM (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3F.013) - RE-ISSUE
description: The activity aims at the development of new functions in the protocol stack, in support of voice calls using the latest NTN NB-IoT waveform. The activity shall select the most promising voice encoder/decoder technology and shall demonstrate its fixability over a NB-IoT communication link via satellite..Targeted Improvements:Enrich the portfolio of satellite services supported with the NB-IoT technology.Description:With the endorsement of the Release 17 NTN NB-IoT specifications from the 3GPP community, new satellite services are recently announced based on this M2M/IoT technology. Currently, these services are intended only for short messaging and positioning information in the context of Machine-to-Machine (M2M) applications. On the other hand, relatively broadband type of services supported by the 5G NR standard is difficult to be initiated at the satellite L-/S- band, due to the limited capabilities of the current legacy systems and the need for dedicated non-geostationary satellite constellations. Looking at Voice-over-IP (VoIP) services, the latest AMR (Adaptive Multi-Rate) codec works with variable bit rates ranging from 4.75 to 12.2kbps, and with 20ms data arriving interval among the data packets. Consequently, it is of interest to evaluate the adoption of the NB-IoT standard to support voice calls in satellite networks. The activity shall therefore undertake the following steps: a) Review the latest 3GPP specifications for the NTN scenario (i.e., Release 18) and the identified solutions for satellite coverage enhancements; b) Given the current state-of-the-art AMR codec, design and develop the new functions in the protocol stack of both UE and gNB to support VoIP services for NGSO satellite networks; c) Thorough laboratory validation.

title: ELECTRICALLY CONDUCTING THERMAL INSULATORS - EXPRO PLUS (RE-ISSUE)
description: To identify and develop candidates for functional materials with high electrical conductivity as well as high thermal isolation.DescriptionElectrical grounding is a mandatory per-requisite to control electromagnetic interference (EMI), from direct current (DC)over alternating current (AC) up to radio-frequency disturbances. In missions requiring stringent thermal control however high thermal insulation may be necessary, for example in hot environments and/or for cold instrument detectors like on ATHENA, infra-red observatories (L5), or cosmic microwave background mission (L6). But electrical conductivity and thermal insulation are typically mutually exclusive, because the high mobility of electrons in electric conductors allows those electrons also to increase their temperature and thus transport heat when moving in the electrical current flow.Functional materials like structured composites or meta-materials with engineered material properties could combine these usually exclusive properties. As a first step, candidate materials need to be identified and prescreened for space applications. To serve as efficient electrical grounding path, the electrical conductivity is important over a wide frequency range.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review existing functional materials like structured composites and metamaterials regarding electrical conductivity and thermal insulation properties- Design a group of 5 functional materials which maximize electrical and minimize thermal conductivity - Implement and manufacture 10 samples of 2 designed materials- Characterize o their effective electrical conductivity (both real and imaginary part, to limit reactive contributions like inductive or capacitive), and o thermal insulation, also regarding relation with applied voltage and current AC current frequency , and temperatures.

title: COMPACT LOW FREQUENCY ANTENNAS FOR DEPLOYMENT ON THE LUNAR SURFACE - EXPRO PLUS
description: To develop compact low frequency antenna and its' deployment mechanisms for the Astrophysical Lunar Observatory (ALO).Description: There is a proposed mission concept to establish a lunar observatory on the far side of the Moon. The advantage of placing the observatory on the far side of the moon is the low RF interface in the frequency band of interest (2- 80MHz), which is not observable on the Earth. To measure at such low frequencies with sufficient angular resolution an interferometer is needed consisting of at least a thousand individual antennas positioned in an array on the lunar surface. This approach has been used on Earth for experiments such as LOFAR and the upcoming SKA telescope. However, since each antenna has to be transported to the lunar surface and then deployed, a new antenna architecture needs to be developed. This activity performs a detailed trade-off study of the best antenna design and deployment mechanism. Possible solutions include inflatable structures, printed antennas, unfurlable booms and other concepts. The main design driver for the ideal solution is to minimize the mass and volume of the antenna when stowed. The target is to be able to pack several hundreds of individual antennas with integrated electronics into the European Large Logistics Lander (EL3). From the trade-off study, the most favourable concept shall be selected to be breadboarded. The final test demonstrates the deployment and RF performance.This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Detailed review of possible antenna architectures that can operate in the region of 2-80MHz; - Detailed review into possible deployment mechanisms that could be used on the lunar surface; - A trade-off study considering: frequency, antenna architecture, and deployment mechanism should be performed;- Select the concept for breadboarding;- Develop a breadboard antenna, designed and built to the representative volume;- Demonstrate a full deployment along with an RF measurement.

title: WAVEFRONT SENSOR FOR OPERATION UNDER STRONG ATMOSPHERIC TURBULENCE (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.041) (RE-ISSUE)
description: Objective: This activity aims at investigating different wavefront sensor technologies in order to identify the best suited one for operation under strong atmospheric turbulence conditions in optical communication applications. Targeted Improvements: 100% increased wavefront sensor performance under strong atmospheric turbulence conditions. Description: Optical beams propagating through the turbulent atmosphere undergo phase and amplitude fluctuations, causing random fading and surges in the signal which leads to irradiance fluctuations when coupled into a single mode fibre. Adaptive Optics aims at counteracting these wavefront impairments. Wavefront sensors are one of the key elements of an Adaptive Optics loop, together with the deformable mirror and the controller. Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensors (SH WFS) are among the most popular sensors used to infer the wavefront error in astronomy due to their simplicity, speed, and efficient use of light. However, SH WFS were shown to not perform well under strong atmospheric turbulence (occurring, for instance, at low elevations during LEO/Ground optical links or during daytime). This is due to the fact that standard least squares reconstruction algorithms assume that SH WFS measurements are equal to the average phase gradient within each sub-aperture. However, this assumption does not hold anymore in case of strong scintillations. Furthermore, the re-constructor cannot form an estimate of the branch points appearing in the phase front in the presence of strong scintillations. Other effects occurring during strong turbulence conditions contribute to make the reconstruction more complex (e.g. the phase is not uniform over a sub-aperture, the spots formed by the micro-lenses can be imaged out of the nominal area on the detector). The present activity aims at exploring and testing alternative wavefront sensing methods to identify the one showing the best performance under strong atmospheric turbulence conditions (e.g. WFS based on interferometers, holographic elements, pyramid, curvature, or combined methods etc.). Different wavefront sensor technologies shall be investigated theoretically and an experimental test bench shall be developed to compare the two best suited ones. Strong turbulence conditions shall be defined by a Rytov variance >0.3. Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). title: OPTICAL GROUND STATION NETWORK TESTBED (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6B.128)
description: The objective of this activity is to develop an optical ground station network testbed to which parties can connect their ground station and prototype network-related aspects for optical and quantum communications in an operational network environment. Targeted Improvements:Reduction of manual link planning and analysis effort. Testing and simulation capabilities for optical end-to-end data delivery. Description:The objective of this activity is to develop an optical ground station network testbed to which parties can connect their ground station and prototype network-related aspects for optical communications in an operational network environment. Data delivery testing and validation can only be evaluated and tested in an optical ground station network context, in which ground station and subsystem developers usually do not have access. This shall be addressed within this activity by providing a network testbed to which OGS developers can connect their system for network testing. The following specific aspects shall be covered: -Link handover between ground stations. -Link planning: e.g. weather forecast. -Method data is handled: end-to-end data delivery and on-board data erasure. -Generation of managed parameters for link planning: e.g. data rates, coding options, automated repeat queries. The testbed shall comprise the following elements: -An online platform with human-to-machine and machine-to-machine interfaces to request links, visualize the execution, and deliver the data. -Scheduling and link planning capabilities. -Overall data return optimisation capabilities. -Data delivery end-points for the data recipients. -Visualisation of the measurement and command parameters of each ground station in the network. -Capability to include simulated and real ground stations; e.g. ESA's IZN-1 optical ground station can be made available under this activity to be used as an operation ground station for network testing. "

title: DEVELOPMENT OF A SOFTWARE BASED GENERIC OPTICAL GROUND STATION MODEL (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6B.126)
description: The objective of this activity is to develop and test a software platform acting as an abstraction layer between the optical groundstation software client and the various software and hardware modules and their interfaces. Software implementation to be agnostic to operating systems and shall be based on object-oriented techniques to enable creation of a generic optical ground station model prior to programming. Testing shall and use commercially available computer platforms and shall take place in a pre-operational environment. Targeted Improvements: A tenfold increase in the operational readiness of optical/quantum communication ground stations, whilst future proofing its modularity and scalability. Description: An optical ground station (OGS) can be modelled as an assortment of different optical hardware (HW) and software (SW) modules and their interfaces, e.g., dome, telescope, lenses, mirrors, imaging devices, lasers, detectors etc. All parts of an OGS shall be ideally controlled by a single computer. Nevertheless, universal connectivity between apps/programmes and the equipment they need to control is not obvious. A standardised interface applicable to a range of equipment used in OGSs does not exist today. An object-model SW platform hosting drivers for the various parts of an OGS would allow devices and equipment from different vendors and applications to communicate efficiently with each other. This shall enable the efficient management and control of OGS resources by a single computer, even with several computers sharing partial access. The envisaged SW abstraction platform between the OGS client and the various modules and their interfaces shall remove any HW dependency in the client, making thus OGSs more modular, compatible with more devices, easier maintainable, and further testable. The special object that converts the interface of one object so that another object can understand is called adapter. The adapter is a structural design pattern that allows objects with incompatible interfaces to collaborate. Relevant technologies that act as a bridge between SW clients and HW devices are already used widely to control astronomical equipment with great success. The ASCOM initiative since 1997 (an abbreviation for Astronomy Common Object Model) is eliminating the need to write special code for each astronomy device. The INDI library since 2003, an open-source SW to control astronomical equipment, is based on the Instrument Neutral Distributed Interface (INDI) protocol and acts as a bridge between SW clients and HW devices. Both initiatives are community driven and supported by professionals and amateurs. This activity shall develop and test a SW platform that will act as an abstraction layer between the OGS SW client and the various SW and HW modules and their interfaces. The target platform shall hide the implementation details and provide the user only with the information on what the object does as part of the OGS, instead of how it does it. The property of abstraction is inherent to object-oriented programming languages. Therefore, implementation shall be based on object-oriented techniques. The solution shall support operation across different computer operational systems, including MacOS, Linux and Windows. The activity shall provide means to validate the SW platform using commercially available computer platforms. Testing shall take place in a pre-operational environment. Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). This activity shall develop and test a SW platform that will act as an abstraction layer between the OGS SW client and the various SW and HW modules and their interfaces. The target platform shall hide the implementation details and provide the user only with the information on what the object does as part of the OGS, instead of how it does it. The property of abstraction is inherent to object-oriented programming languages. Therefore, implementation shall be based on object-oriented techniques. The solution shall support operation across different computer operational systems, including MacOS, Linux and Windows. The activity shall provide means to validate the SW platform using commercially available computer platforms. Testing shall take place in a pre-operational environment. title: DEVELOPMENT OF ON-ORBIT MANUFACTURING PROCESS FOR LARGE ANTENNA REFLECTOR - EXPRO PLUS
description: To select, develop and demonstrate on a breadboard a process relevant for on-orbit manufacturingof large antenna reflectors.DescriptionThe size of the Telecommunication satellites is limited by the dimensions of the launcher fairings.This applies to components of the satellites where a larger size results in increased performance and capability of the system. Larger solar arrays result in more power available for a given platform and increased payload capability. Larger antenna reflectors lead to a smaller emitted beam and therefore higher gain, higher data throughput and the ability to divide the available power between an increased number of smaller beams. Current solutions for large reflectors rely on deployablesystems, which have highly complex manufacturing and testing routes, which result in long lead times and high cost. The ability to manufacture antenna reflectors and booms on orbit allows to alleviate the limitation of the fairing size and the impact of the launch vibrations, thereby enabling very large size antennae and improved system performance. Manufacturing and assemblyprocesses for on-orbit manufacturing have been proposed and tested on ground by several actors,including in Europe. The first in orbit demonstration missions for in-situ manufacturing and assemblyof spacecraft components are scheduled in the U.S. before 2025.This activity proposes to select, develop and demonstrate a process relevant to future on-orbitmanufacturing of large antenna reflectors. The process to be developed could be an on-orbit manufacturing technique,to produce antenna structural components (e.g. antenna frame structural beam, boom, reflective surface elements) or an on-orbit assembly technique, to join structural components together (e.g. joining of reflector membrane on the antenna structure frame). The emphasis will be put on continuous or semi-continuous processes (over batch processes). This, inorder to address antenna concepts involving large structural elements (e.g. large mesh or trussstructure), as opposed to concepts relying on assembly of a high number of small constitutive elements, which have been explored in previous activities.The activity encompasses the following tasks:- Reviewof use cases for very large antenna reflectors- Review of existing and potential solutions for on-orbit manufacturing and assemblyof large antenna reflector structural elements (composites, polymers, metals, ceramics)- Definition of requirements for the manufacturing method- Trade-off and selection of manufacturing method to be developed- Manufacturing and characterization of small-scalespecimens- Design and manufacturing of a breadboard and demonstration of elemental performance requirements- Development plan towards on-orbit demonstration.

title: KA-BAND SATELLITE TERMINAL PROTOTYPING FOR FUTURE RAILWAY MOBILE COMMUNICATION SYSTEM (FRMCS) (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 7C.093) - RE-ISSUE
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, develop and validate in a lab environment a Ka-band satellite terminal prototype (i.e., modem and antenna) allowing to offer 5G NR FRMCS services via satellite while equipped on trains. Targeted Improvements: Ensure by 2030 the 100% coverage of railway lines by FRMCS and the consistency of passenger safety among the whole line. Description: The Future Railway Mobile Communication System (FRMCS), being a successor of the GSM-R system, is planned to be operational before GSM-R's predicted saturation in 2030. satcom is already established as a component of the future system and extensive work already took place to trade-off the best candidate satellite scenarios for the FRMCS servicing. Among the various options considered in terms of frequency bands, satellite orbit and air interface, the work concluded that one of the most promising and mature scenarios for immediate service is a 5G NR transparent GEO system in the Ka-band. Nevertheless, specific 5G NR terminals that mitigate the particularities of the railway environment for such satellite system are currently not available. This activity will therefore pave the way for such a terminal, by designing and developing a HW-based, Ka-band satellite terminal prototype for future usage on board of trains and 5G NR FRMCS communication connectivity via satellite. The HW-based terminal prototype will include both a 5G NR FRMCS modem and a satellite antenna integrated [FDP1] as necessary to form a complete solution. The activity will be supported by existing literature and on-going ESA activities, which highlight the best 5G NR configurations (e.g., numerologies, multiplex scheme), the best antenna solutions (e.g., parabolic vs. flat panel) and the best train installation options (e.g., single vs. dual antenna) for the mitigation of the channel impairments. These technical conclusions will be incorporated into the HW based modem and antenna solutions to form a state-of-the-art integrated terminal prototype. The integrated prototype shall use and/or upgrade COTS components (e.g., 5Gmodem parts, railway broadband antennas, RF front ends), and integrate them as necessary to adapt to the particularities of the satellite scenario. In addition, it shall be able to offer connectivity with existing transparent GEO satellites of today, without requiring modifications to the space segment and the feeder ground network component. The integrated solution however shall be able to achieve the demanding performance requirements of FRMCS despite the challenging railway-to- -satellite channel. The performance of the developed terminal prototype shall be validated in a laboratory environment with extensive testing under various realistic channel conditions.

title: HIGH FREQUENCY AIRBORNE RADIOMETER INSTRUMENT FOR THE SUPPORT OF FUTURE ALTIMETRY MISSIONS
description: Satellite altimetry plays an essential role in producing sea level and waves products such as sea surface height (SSH), significantwave height (SWH), mean sea level and near surface wind/wave products.Today, a low frequency channel microwave radiometer is in general used to correct the altimeter range for water vapor path delay over ocean. The wet tropospheric correction (WTC) is consideredas one of the largest source of uncertainty in sea level estimate. As any artificial temporal drift in the wet tropospheric correction translate immediately to a similar drift in the mean sea level, there is a need for extremely well calibrated radiometer instrument to retrieve this wet tropospheric correction in support of the accurate altimeter measurement. Depending on the targeted temporal and spatial scales, some recent studies and projects ("Radiometer Instrument for Swath Altimeter missions", Sentinel-6 HRMR instrument, Sentinel-3 NG-T) have shown that the two existing classes of satellite altimeters such as the conventional nadir looking altimeters and the wide swath altimeters would both benefit from the addition of one or several high frequency channels (89/165/172 GHz)to the low frequency channels (18.7/23.8/36.5(or 31.4) GHz) already used for the WTC retrieval. The advantages brought by the addition of the high frequency channels in the microwave radiometer are several fold. For a given RF radiating aperture, the high frequency radiometer would exhibit a high spatial resolution and therefore shall be less prone to land contamination in coastal areas that would directly impact the uncertainty of the WTC based on brightness temperature measurement near the coastline. For wide swath altimeters, a multibeam microwave radiometer combining the low and high frequency channels would help to retrieve the WTC across-track with an increased accuracy and with better spatial resolution commensurate with the high spatial resolution radar retrievals from a swath altimeter. Moreover, the high frequency channels (typically 89 GHz or 165/172 GHz) can provide additional information for precipitation screening.This new proposed activity aims at developing an airborne demonstrator instrument to validate the benefits of thehigh frequency radiometer measurement, to support the continued improvement of the altimeter measurement and observation capabilities. The activity shall start with the detailed analysis of user requirements and the design of the instrument, then continue with themanufacturing, integration and test of the airborne system and finally concludes with the airworthiness certification on an airborne carrier and a functional test flight to validate the airborne radiometer function and performance and collect first experimental data.

title: KA-BAND TRANSMIT SPARSE ACTIVE PHASED ARRAY AND BEAMFORMING NETWORKS FOR NGSO USER LINKS (ARTES AT 5B.240)
description: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test a partial RF breadboard of a transmit Ka-band, active phased array antenna and associated beamforming network for user links NGSO, exploiting irregular layouts for the radiating elements and beamforming networks.Targeted Improvements: In comparison to a standard, fully populated array:- 25% reduction in the number of active controls,- 5% increase in the DC to RF power efficiency at antenna level due to the reduced exploitation of amplitude tapering,- 15% reduction in the overall mass for the entire antennaDescription: After two decades of research and development sparse arrays have been successfully deployed in space, although not by European companies. The main advantages offered by aperiodic arrays include:- sidelobe levels that may be controlled by implementing a density-tapering strategy with a reduced exploitation of the amplitude tapering;- a reduction of the number of radiating elements for a given aperture size with a limited reduction of the beamwidth;- anaperiodic spatial distribution that allows spreading and controlling the grating lobe power;- suitability for wideband applications thanks to the reduction of grating-lobe levels;- less problematic mutual coupling thanks to the unequal inter-element spacings.In this activity, active phased array antennas exploiting sparse radiating element layouts and sparse topologies for beamforming networks shall be developed for Non-Geo-Stationary-Orbit (NGSO) satellite user links. One of the main challenges is the design of beamforming networks compatible with irregular layouts for the radiating elements. The difficulties are not only related to RF aspects; accommodation and thermal control are also of paramount importance and require consideration due to the non-homogeneous character of the power generation and dissipation caused by the irregular distribution of array control centres. For this reason, transmit and receive operations could be implemented in two separated antenna apertures. Single vs dual-polarisation operations shall be traded off,and the two most promising and sufficiently different architectures shall be identified for a detailed design covering RF, mechanical and thermal aspects. The most critical components should be identified, manufactured, and tested.

title: COPPHIL: EO SERVICE DEVELOPMENT TRANSFER
description: The procurement aims to implement the activities and tools required for developing and transferring Earth Observation (EO) pilot services and skills for decision making and monitoring of policy implementation in the Philippines. The initiative will focus on threeselected EO pilot services ground motion monitoring, land cover, forest crop mapping and benthic habitat monitoring. The procurement will support national mandated institutions to adopt advanced processing tools, access and use large amounts of free and open EOdata from the Copernicus program. The relevant activities will span across the entire period of the CopPhil initiative and will require a strong physical presence in the Philippines. The activity is part of the National Copernicus Capacity Support Action Programme(CopPhil) in the Philippines funded by DG-INTPA and delegated to ESA for implementation. The main objective of CopPhil is to facilitate the uptake of Copernicus data in the Philippines with an initial thematic focus of three predefined pilots. The CopPhil initiative will rely on close cooperation between the European Commission (DG-INTPA, EU Delegation in Manila), ESA and the Government of Philippines as partners. Considering this context all CopPhil activities and related procurements are planned as international cooperation expressly encouraging the collaboration and joint consortia between Europe and the Philippines.

title: POWER BUS ISOLATION DEVICE TO ACHIEVE RELIABLE ELECTRICAL PASSIVATION(ARTES AT 4F.176) - EXPRO+ RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of this activity is to design, develop, manufacture and test a power bus passivation isolation device providing a physical gap on the power path at the end of mission suitable for telecom satellites.Targeted Improvements:- Enabling above 95% reliability for permanent electrical passivation- Achieving an operating thermal range of -150 to +120degC.- Reduce the complexity of implementation of electrical passivation by more than 50%Activity Description: Due to the increase of human-made objects in Earth orbit, especially with many constellation programmes, it is paramount to reduce the risk of collisions in orbit. Regulations and policies are evolving and include the need of electrical passivation and a probability target for a successful passivation until spacecraft disposal. The current state of the art techniques for electrical passivation typically isolates the battery from its power source via electronic switch or electromechanical devices. These techniques lack a high probability successful passivation isolation when there is no satellite thermal control anymore and continuous exposition to radiation. This activity will develop an electrical isolation technique for satcom missions in all Earth orbits, based on introducing a physical gap on the power path of the spacecraftto prevent for example the charging of batteries after end of mission. The isolation performance shall not be influenced by the thermal environment or by radiation effects. Different potential solutions to achieve the desired passivation isolation performance andreliability will be studied including existing technologies such as a pyro device (e.g. pyro connector). A passivation isolation device scaled engineering model will be designed, manufactured and tested to evaluate its performances.

title: TUNABLE LASER SOURCE FOR OPTICAL GROUND SUPPORT EQUIPMENT - EXPRO PLUS
description: Optical straylight characterization of critical components and radiometric/spectral on-ground characterisation/calibration are vital to meet thesystem requirements of optical payloads, from CubeSats to large Earth Observation payloads. Typically, satellite projects are procuring dedicated Optical Ground Support Equipment (OGSE) for the calibration and validation campaigns consisting of various calibration sources (thermal emitters, lightemitting diodes or lasers) and an optical bench adapted to the payload. Rather than using different source types it would be beneficial to have a single universallight source covering the needs of several missions.The most challenging requirements for these sources are the coverage of a broad spectral band from ultra-violet to the infrared, a narrow spectral emission,sufficient output power and high reliability. All these parameters combined within a single system will ensure a failure-free operation during the resource intensivecalibration and characterisation campaign. A continuous wave tunable laser system will be the most suitable solution to meet those requirements for differentmissions. The availability of such tunable lasers will enhance the versatility of OGSE and reduce cost through the reuse of the source.The objective of this activity is to develop and build an engineering model of an illumination system for an optical instrument calibration OGSE based onindividually tunable laser modules. This will cover the relevant wavelength optical instrument calibration.The following tasks are foreseen in this activity: Assessment of current continuous wave laser-based illumination sources. Conceptual design of the overall laser system. Detailed design of the individual building blocks modules and an engineering model of the entire system including control software.Manufacture, assemble, align, and test the engineering model. Demonstrate the suitability of the system in a representative OGSE setup.
