title: REDUCED-COMPLEXITY ANALOG AND HYBRID BEAMFORMING NETWORKS (ARTES AT 7B.084) - EXPRO PLUS - RE-ISSUE
description: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a beamforming network with reduced hardware complexity (e.g., number of beamforming ICs or beamforming nodes) for mm-wave phased array antennas for ground terminalsTargeted Improvements: - Reduction of the number of beamforming chips by at least 50%. - Reduction of power consumption by at least 50%. - Reduction of silicon area, hence of costs, by at least 50%. - Reduction of digital control complexity by at least 50%Description:Today's phased arrays rely on feeding elements, i.e., every element requires a dedicated channel that applies required beam weights (amplitude, phase steering) generated separately for each element (digitally or in polar/vector modulators). This approach is increasingly complex with the trends towards higher frequencies, where spacing between array elements cannot accommodate the required number of beamforming nodes or chips.Therefore, seeking concepts that reduce hardware complexity is currently among the most important topics in RD. One of the many approaches to reducing Beamforming Network (BFN) complexity is to seek symmetry in the phased array configuration (e.g., placement of radiating elements w.r.t the centre axis) or in the beams or the beam shapes that are generated. Then, the BFN feeding network can be simplified and symmetrical elements can be fed by a dedicated symmetrical BFN that requires fewer nodes. This activity will develop and test a beamforming network with reduced hardware complexity (e.g., number of beamforming ICs or beamforming nodes) by at least 50% while maintaining performance of array. Existing BFN concepts will be reviewed, covering digital, analogue, and hybrid BFNs. Hardware complexity reduction techniques will be explored, and two most promising concepts will be selected for implementation. Dedicated RFIC design activities are anticipated implementing a novel beamforming IC topology and BFN. A representative scaled version of a mm-wave phased array BFN will be implemented to demonstrate the hardware complexity and power consumption savings

Thisincludes mission planning and operational products production and validation, missionoperation continuity and maintenance, anomaly handling and investigation, performanceanalysis and reporting and user acceptance of flight/mission ground segment systems andspace-to-ground system and system operations validation. It includes those tasks as well asspecific tasks to missions in preparation and critical phases such as LEOP, Orbit Insertions,flybys, etc. Depending on the technical area or family of mission, some real time tasking suchas the traditional SPACON tasks (routine pass conduction, logging and reporting, first-lineanomaly handling, and coordination with on-call engineer for mission-specific support) maybe also part of the FOE Services. For early phases of the missions or for missions not tobeoperated by ESOC, the service support will also cover the required operations engineeringsupport within the different areas of expertise

title: S2-SW-10: CANADIAN PARTICIPATION IN THE ESA SPACE WEATHER SERVICE NETWORK FEASIBILITY STUDY
description: This feasibility study shall analyse Canadian space weather assets including measurement, modelling and service provision capabilities and carry out initial pre-developments demonstrating these assets potential incorporation into the ESA Space Weather Service Network. Assets providing data access to be reviewed shall include both space and ground-based sensors along with data archives and repositories.Available assets shall be reviewed in terms of the Space Safety Programme's space weather customer and service requirements baseline along with the current level of service provided by the existing Space Weather Service Network in order to highlight priority areas where Canadian assets are expected to bring substantial capability enhancements. Consideration shall be given to the development planning prepared by the five Expert Service Centres participating in the network to ensure complementarity.Recommendations shall include identification of a set of high priority product development activities in key areas highlighting the potential contribution of Canadian space weather assets and capabilities both alone and in combination with other existing or potential SWE Service Network participants. Predevelopment shall take place in order to produce a set of representative product mock-ups. The first products shall be foreseen for integration into the SWE Service Network within the 2026 timeframe.

title: EXPRO NAVISP ELEMENT 1 - EL01-009: SPACE GNSS RECEIVER FOR IN-ORBIT DEMONSTRATION OF PRECISE POINT POSITIONING (PPP)
description: This EXPRO+ procurement is part of the NAVISP Programme, under Elelment 1, Work Plan 2017.The object of the activity is to design, develop and validate/verified a GNSS space receiver capable to perform on board precise orbit determination (P2OD) in real time using precise GNSS orbit and clock corrections provided either by Geostationary satellites or Galileo Commercial Service (thus allowing on board autonomy w.r.t to ground stations). The concept is similar to what is performed on ground in techniques based on GNSS PPP(Precise Point Positioning). The product is targeting a cubesat mission (so cubesat form factor) and the activity will also analysisthe mission characteristics and requirements for a potential IOD (in orbit demonstration) of the concept.

title: SENTINEL-3 NEXT GENERATION TOPOGRAPHY MICROWAVE RADIOMETER ADVANCED B2 AND PHASE B2/C/D
description: This procurement proposal specifically addresses the S3 NG-T Microwave Radiometer (MWR) Phase B2/C/D implementation within the overall S3 NG-T space segment procurement context. In this respect it is recalled that for the S3 NG-T space segment Phase B2/C/D implementation, an instrument first' procurement approach in envisaged. In particular, the instruments Contractor(s) will be pre-selected and will then be identified as mandatory subcontractors in the subsequent Invitation to Tender (ITT) for the space segment Prime Contractor. For the Microwave Radiometer (MWR) instrument, the instrument Contractor will be preselected via an Open Invitation to Tender. The content of the selected proposal, as negotiated by ESA, will then be made available to the spacecraft Tenderers. Subsequently, the selection of the spacecraft Prime will take place via an Open Invitation to Tender, encompassing the complete Sentinel-3 NG-T space segment including the identified pre-selected MWR instrument Contractor that shall be part of the resulting Industrial Consortium responsible for the S3 NG-T implementation. In the frame of the spacecraft Open ITT, the Tenderers will be required to perform the necessary due diligence during the bidding period to secure the full contractual responsibility throughout the Phase B2/C/D activities. A comprehensive description of the S3 NG-T Phase B2/C/D implementation, including general principles, specific procurement provisions and intended procurement schedule are provided in the dedicated IPC information note "Outline of Sentinel-3 Next Generation Topography Phase B2/C/D Procurement Provisions" (ESA/IPC(2024)176).

For the Microwave Radiometer (MWR) instrument, the instrument Contractor will be preselected via an Open Invitation to Tender. The content of the selected proposal, as negotiated by ESA, will then be made available to the spacecraft Tenderers. Subsequently, the selection of the spacecraft Prime will take place via an Open Invitation to Tender, encompassing the complete Sentinel-3 NG-T space segment including the identified pre-selected MWR instrument Contractor that shall be part of the resulting Industrial Consortium responsible for the S3 NG-T implementation. In the frame of the spacecraft Open ITT, the Tenderers will be required to perform the necessary due diligence during the bidding period to secure the full contractual responsibility throughout the Phase B2/C/D activities. A comprehensive description of the S3 NG-T Phase B2/C/D implementation, including general principles, specific procurement provisions and intended procurement schedule are provided in the dedicated IPC information note "Outline of Sentinel-3 Next Generation Topography Phase B2/C/D Procurement Provisions" (ESA/IPC(2024)176).

title: DEVELOPMENT OF SERIALIZER AND DESERIALIZER IP CORE FOR ULTRA DEEP SUB MICRON TECHNOLOGIES - EXPRO PLUS

Due to the importance to provide this functionality in a timely manner, this dedicated activityhas been defined with the aim to develop a Serializer and Deserializer (SERDES) IP Core to enableHSSL to at least 32Gbps and up to 56Gbps.This IP Core will support the different HSSL protocols used in space like SpaceFibre, Ethernet, PCIe, JESD204. Specifically the HSSL IP Core will be compliant to the newer PCIe 5.0 and Ethernet802.3cd link operation. TheHSSL IP Core will support power efficient operation both for short range as well as long range applications (two optimized implementations might be considered). The outcome of this activity shall be made available whenever required with concomitant activities, and in particular the GTE3- 101ED and shall be made accessible for future developments ofEuropean space products.The activity encompasses the following tasks :- Identify the space component requiring SERDES IP Core and targeted UDSM technology and foundry- Determine the HSSL requirement specifications and suitable commercial SERDES IP Core design- Perform Radiation test of selected HSSL in the targeted UDSM technology- Design radiation harden HSSL IP Core with improvedperformances- Validate the HSSL IP Core functionalities and performances on test vehicles, including radiation hardened operation- Demonstrate compliant operation on optimised and corrected design- Perform functional ESCC testing, characterization, andevaluation- Make the HSSL IP Core available and support the integration into the activity GTE3-101ED- Package the HSSL IP Core for use into future developments Deliverables include SERDES IP Core, Simulation model files, samples of the test chips and documentation as per applicable Standard for IC development, tailoredas required for the development of reusable IP.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: FEASIBILITY AND PRE-DEVELOPMENT OF INFLATABLE TANKS PROPELLANT STORAGE - EXPRO PLUS
description: To provide a feasibility analysis about the construction, storage, deployment, and operation of propellant tanks that are inflatable.Description:This activity aims at providing a detailed feasibility analysis on the construction, storage, deployment, and operation of propellant tanks that are inflatable. It is envisaged that these propellant tanks can be used to store cryogenic propellant(LOX, LCH4, LH2) or to store conventional propellant (O2, H2, CH4, CO). Most important, inflatable propellant tanks can be used to store the gases produced by using in situ resources in a Regenerative Fuel Cell Systems (RFCS) in electrolysis mode. Applications tothe Moon and Mars will be addressed.Major critical points (material compatibility with propellant, zero boil off for cryogenic propellant,...) are aimed at being investigated and solutions proposed.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Trade-off analyses of inflatable tank design- Prototype and test a proof of concept (for different applications and propellants for Moon and Mars scenarios)- Roadmap development plan

title: LOW VIBRATION AND ANGULAR MOMENTUM LASER TERMINAL (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.003) EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design a Laser Communication Terminal (LCT) to enable communication links with various satellites at the Lagrange point 2 (L2) with hemispheric pointing rangeand a minimized vibration and angular disturbance profile.Targeted Improvements:To increase the return data rate from beyond-Earth communication by a factor of 10 compared to typical RF payload missions (75 Mbps - class links).Description:Multiple space telescopes have been placed at Lagrange point 2 (L2) and this trend will continue in the future because it is an ultra-low disturbance environment. Laser communication terminals(LCT) can provide very high data return rates from L2. However, the (angular) vibrations induced by the LCT shall not disturb the spacecraft operations.The activity shall perform the conceptual design of an optical communication terminal for L2 with hemispheric pointing range and minimized vibration and angular disturbance export. Critical functions of the LCT (SWaP, minimization of angular momentum during coarse pointing, etc.) shall be breadboarded.

title: PHASE A OF SOLAR SYSTEM INTERNET PATHFINDER MISSION - EXPRO PLUS
description: The Phase A of Solar System Internet Pathfinder Mission will advance the definition of a mission in cis-lunar space to demonstrate reliable routine operations of an optical trunk link between Moon and Earth, advanced space internetworking, and technologies for Deep Space Positioning Navigation and Timing. A preceding SSI Pathfinder Concurrent Design Study defined the required payload suite to support these objectives but kept the way to implement the mission open. The SSI Node-1 Phase A1 activity is expected to perform a trade-off between an implementation as a dedicated mission addressing the needs of upcoming lunar missions or as hosted payloads on planned lunar missions and will conclude with a Mission Definition Review. The procurement will be open competition to all industrial entities, ensuring an opencompetitive approach preparing further steps. Parallel contracts may be placed in case of competitive complementary proposals.

title: ADVANCED RF INTEGRATION TECHNIQUES FOR APPLICATION IN HIGHLY DENSE MILLIMETRE-WAVE ACTIVE ANTENNAS - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test a breadboard of a millimetre-wave active array sub-module which demonstrates high integration techniques of critical RF functions. Description: High density millimetre-wave active antenna arrays, which are anticipated for future LEO missions require highly integrated RF functionality to meet the strict periodicity/lattice spacing requirements at such high frequencies. Novel techniques will be necessary to physically integrate the transmit and/or receive MMIC (Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit) with the beamforming functionality whilst managing the RF and DC interconnectivity and thermal heat dissipation issues that will result from such high integration. For such high frequency applications (V-/W-bands), RF electrical interconnections become critical, and loss should be minimised to maintain system efficiency, therefore the use of flip-chip connections or re-distribution layers, should be investigated. In addition, coupling and parasitic inductances need to be minimised to optimise electrical performance and unit to unit consistency. Careful 3D electromagnetic analysis is required to optimise the advanced RF structure performance. The proposed activity aims to develop new and novel manufacturing, packaging and advanced RF integration techniques which provide improved, highly integrated and repeatable performance for millimetre-wave active array applications. The advanced RF integration technique shall be an alternative to PCB (Printed Circuit Board) assembly technologies and could include, but not be limited to techniques such as 3D microelectronics, Fan Out Wafer Level Packaging (FOWLP), flip-chip/hot-via, antenna-inpackage, micromachining, precision additive manufacturing, etc., thereby demonstrating high performance, high integration, and miniaturisation. A breadboard shall be designed, manufactured and tested to demonstrate the electrical, mechanical and thermal aspects. The breadboard shall target a generic mm-wave application which demonstrates the integration of RF functionality in an advanced RF structure, suitable for an active antenna. Novel interconnection/packaging techniques shall only be considered and novel techniques for thermal management shall be proposed. The following tasks are foreseen in the frame of this activity: Requirements review:o Definition of application and review of requirements.o Initial design requirements identification. o Technology trade-off and down-selection. Breadboard preliminary design:o Initial demonstration of solution to meet fundamental requirements. o Preliminary manufacturing process flow definition. Breadboard detailed design and analysis:o Detailed RF and thermal performance analysis. o If deemed necessary, different test vehicles can be designed to evaluate specific performance parameters.o Detailed manufacturing process flow definition. o Definition of test and verification plan. Breadboard manufacturing and test:o Exercise of manufacturing process flows.o Assemble breadboard demonstrator and/or test vehicles.o Test against verification plan. Results analysis and evaluation.

title: ROSE-L L2 OCEAN PROCESSOR ACTIVITY - EXPRO +
description: The Radar Observing System for Europe - L-Band (ROSE-L) is being developed by the European Space Agency (ESA) as one of the Copernicus Expansion (COPEX) missions, and will fill the need for L-band SAR data for Land Monitoring, Emergency Management, Marine Environment Monitoring and Security Services. One of ROSE-L objectives is to provide continuity of current observations in order to establish long and reliable time series of measurements. This includes, e.g., the provision of Level-2 Ocean data similar to the ones currently available for the Sentinel-1 mission. To support this goal, this activity aims to prototype and develop the ROSE-L L2 Ocean processor which will be deployed in the Copernicus Ground Segment. The activity will be divided in two phases. The first phase is dedicated to the consolidation of algorithms and product performances, definition of the calibration and validation approach and prototyping activities. The second phase is mainly dedicated to the evolution of the prototype into the operational processor, and it also includes the consolidation of cal/val approach, and support to the integration in the ground segment.

title: AUXILIARY DATA GATHERING SERVICE
description: The purpose of this procurement is the provision of the operational Copernicus Sentinels Ground Segment Auxiliary Data Gathering Service (ADGS). The Auxiliary Data Gathering Service, is a critical service in charge of collecting the Auxiliary Data necessary for the generation of Sentinel 1, Sentinel 2 and Sentinel 3 Level-1 and Level-2 User Data from external sources (such as ECMWF, etc) and making them available to the Sentinels data production and reprocessing services, ensuring their consistency. The ADGS includes all activities necessary to retrieve or receive the auxiliary data from the auxiliary data providers, reformat the data in accordance with the data processors interfaces and provide these data with high availability to the various consumers within the within the Copernicus Sentinels Ground Segment.?

title: LAB-ON-A-CHIP INSTRUMENT FOR FUTURE PLANETARY MISSIONS -EXPRO PLUS
description: Future lander missions will target planetary bodies of astrobiological relevance such as those proposed in the frame of the Voyage 2050 programme (e.g., ocean worlds and dwarf planets). Lab-on-a-chiptechnologies are already known since a while and are established in the meantime on the market, using sophisticated microfluidic sample handling,together with very sensitive detection techniques using fluorophore immunoassays specific for molecules/functional groups. this enables the detection of organics and biomarkers down to the ppt level. The advantage is the high specificity and the benign sample handling allowing for the nondestructive detection of complex molecules. Although proposed and planned in the past, a microfluidic detection system has not yet been flown or baselined for upcoming missions.Targeting for example icy/ocean worlds on the Iovian moons, lab-on-a-chip devices can perform in situ (bio)chemical analyses Its light-weight and miniaturised design forms a compelling technology for future deep space missions, given the limited resources. The challenge is here to adapt the technology such that it can operate in this harsh environment (temperature, radiation).This activity shall focus on assessing the following:- Existing LoC instruments relevant for in-situ measurements in space (incl. sample handling).- The behaviour/performance of the LoC under cryogenic conditions (i.e., required adaptations w.r.t. typical LoC).- The susceptibility of the devices and reagents to the radiation environment- Any potential dependencies and synergies with other instruments (e.g.,sample handling and preparation of the surface sample).

Description: Future lander missions will target planetary bodies of astrobiological relevance such as those proposed in the frame of the Voyage 2050 programme (e.g., ocean worlds and dwarf planets). Lab-on-a-chiptechnologies are already known since a while and are established in the meantime on the market, using sophisticated microfluidic sample handling,together with very sensitive detection techniques using fluorophore immunoassays specific for molecules/functional groups. this enables the detection of organics and biomarkers down to the ppt level. The advantage is the high specificity and the benign sample handling allowing for the nondestructive detection of complex molecules. Although proposed and planned in the past, a microfluidic detection system has not yet been flown or baselined for upcoming missions.Targeting for example icy/ocean worlds on the Iovian moons, lab-on-a-chip devices can perform in situ (bio)chemical analyses Its light-weight and miniaturised design forms a compelling technology for future deep space missions, given the limited resources. The challenge is here to adapt the technology such that it can operate in this harsh environment (temperature, radiation).This activity shall focus on assessing the following:- Existing LoC instruments relevant for in-situ measurements in space (incl. sample handling).- The behaviour/performance of the LoC under cryogenic conditions (i.e., required adaptations w.r.t. typical LoC).- The susceptibility of the devices and reagents to the radiation environment- Any potential dependencies and synergies with other instruments (e.g.,sample handling and preparation of the surface sample).

title: COPEX-DP CRISTAL
description: The Copernicus Polar Ice and Snow Topography Altimeter (CRISTAL) mission is being developed by the European Space Agency (ESA) as one of the Copernicus Expansion (COPEX) missions with the objective to measure and monitor sea-ice thickness, overlying snow depth and ice-sheet elevations.CRISTAL will feature a payload that comprises an Interferometric Radar altimeter for Ice and Snow (IRIS) and a Microwave Radiometer (MWR). IRIS will be used to measure the thickness of sea ice and the snow that covers it, as well as the height of the world's ice sheets and glaciers. The dual-frequency operation will enable more accurate measurements than earlier ice-monitoring altimeters. These datasets will support maritime operations in polar oceans and contribute to a better understanding of climate processes through monitoring the cryosphere to fully assess, predict and adapt to climate variability and change.In this context, the European Space Agency (ESA) announces the intended ITT for the development of the CRISTAL operational Level-0 and Level-1 data processors (CRISTAL-DP), encompassing the IRIS and MWR instruments, to be integrated and operated as part of the Copernicus Missions, Data and Operations Management Framework (EOF-CSC). The activity is intended to cover the processors development activities aswell as an optional maintenance and evolution phase possibly up to the end of the CRISTAL-A satellite commissioning phase.These CRISTAL data processors will adhere to the principles of the ESA Copernicus Earth Observation Processor Framework (EOPF) and to the principles of open source, flexibility, native compatibility with cloud-based environments, scalability and adaptability to future technological advancements (e.g., GPU, HPC, etc.).Intended Schedule: ITT Issue: Q4 2024 Planed Kick-Off Date: Summer 2025ThisITT is part of a comprehensive procurement strategy involving six open competitive tenders for the COPEX-DP development, including:-A Generic CADU Processor development (ITT)- A separated ITT for the specialised Level-0 and Level-1 operational processors development for each of the following missions: CRISTAL (scope of this ITT), LSTM, ROSE-L, CIMR, CHIME. These ITTs are planned to be issued gradually between 2024 (CRISTAL) and 2026. Future intended ITTs will be published accordingly in due time.

title: OPTICAL BURST SWITCHING IN OPTICAL SATELLITE NETWORKS - EXPRO PLUS
description: "All-Optical" Satellite Networking (OSN) using Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) for theGround-Space, Inter-Satellite and Space-Ground links gains traction with the emergence of relevantcommercial systems and ESA's Hydron proposals. They are based on the concept of "circuit switching" where dedicated optical wavelength channels called "lightpaths" are allocated to a particular connection. Circuit switching is inherently a lower efficiency approach in terms of link-load utilization in exchange for link reliability. Alternative techniques include "packet switching" where each "satellite node" would process "optical packets" instead of "lightpaths". Optical Packetswitching requires some kind of "optical buffering" which is not feasible in practical terms rendering this approach of no practical interest. An intermediate approach is the "optical burst switching" (OBS) which requires no buffering and relies on the use of a dedicated wavelength channel to provide the control commands to the onboard wavelength routers which are reset for a period of time (software-defined network (SDN)). Buffering can take place electronically at the entry/exitnodes (ground or satellites) where the traffic is "sourced" and/or "sunk". This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Review of the status of Packet/Burst Switching in Fiber Optic Networks. Identification of solutions to the buffering issue and explain the applicability of Software Defined Networking;- Analyse the differences in using OBS over an OSN as opposed in-ground networks, in terms of increased delays and more frequent link interruptions, provide a conceptual design of a OBS over the various types of OSN. Assess the potential benefits in terms of link utilization and other network parameters in each type of OSN and provide an SDN-OBS-OSN architecture for further analysis by simulation and laboratory Demonstration;- Simulation of OBS in the selected types of OSN. Measure link utilization, packet loss, delay, etc.- Demonstrate the feasibility of OBS in the selected types of OSN in a laboratory using appropriate equipment to simulate the OSN links;- Conclusions and Recommendations for possible further development.At the end of the activity, a clear picture of the applicability of OBS in WDM OSN is expected tohave been established. In case of positive recommendation, the activity will also provide a roadmap for all the necessary technologies to be developed.

title: PHOTONIC COMPONENTS' RELIABILITY MODELS FOROPTICAL AND QUANTUM COMMUNICATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5F.052) EXPRO+ ON REQUEST
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop reliability models for photonic and optical components used in optical andquantum communications. The models will be developed based on reliability growth test and failure results analysis.Targeted Improvements:Creating a common reliability database/model of photonic component failure mechanisms for all ESA Member States' users. Enabling modelling of photonic components failure mechanisms. Increasing the knowledge of failure mechanisms for the selected photonicscomponent families and enabling trade-offs/redundancy schemes for the better sizing of future constellations.Description:To increase the reliability of photonics technologies, it is first necessary to create a database of the component families foreseen to be used for optical and quantum communication. Once the status of each of these families is assessed, in terms of currently availabledata and the effort needed to build reliability models, it will be possible to prioritise the need for testing. This will identify the components' family with the least amount of information, high risk of failure and potential impact of failure for ongoing and future designs. The test protocols and sample sizes will be defined based on pre-test analyses, with sample sizes of at least ten components for each family being anticipated. The duration of the tests will be selected to achieve failure of all components, to develop a comprehensive understanding of the failure mechanisms involved. The failures will be investigated, and reliability models will be derived. The outcome will consist of a database including model characteristics information and tentative failure rates for different use contexts.

title: CALL FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST: ACCELERATED INVESTMENT PROJECT (ESTEC) PROCUREMENT OF INTERIOR REFURBISHMENT WORKS OF AA, AE, AF, AG, AH TOWERS - STAGE 1
description: Located in Noordwijk, ESTEC is a hub for the European Space Agency's activities. The site covers 40 Ha of land and hosts a large Test Centre, high-tech laboratories and office areas for circa 2,700 people working daily on site.This procurement is for the interior renovation of the Aa Ae Af Ag and Ah office towers at ESA ESTEC, which have never undergone a major renovation since they were built in 1989. This undertaking aims to complement and finalise the office tower refurbishment efforts that already commenced in 2022 with the renovation of the Ac and Ad towers, now completed.The scope of this undertaking covers the interior renovation of 5,400 m2of floor space into a modern, innovative, comfortable environment, achieving high levels of thermal, acoustic and visual comfort for users and efficient use of energy and utilities, while respecting the architectural integrity of Van Eyck's original design, in accordance with current legislation and architectural standards.The refurbishment works of these office towers Aa Ae Af Ag and Ah are intended to take place in one phase, after completion of their corresponding detailed design and engineering definition (already awarded to an architect company following a separate procurement action), starting in June 2025 and until March 2027. ESA plans to procure, via a single contract, the execution of the refurbishment works.ESA intends to procure with a two-stage tendering. The first stage will constitute an open call for interest. The second stage, limited to 3-5 bidders selected during the first stage, will consist of a restricted competition through a competitive dialogue.

title: STAGE 1 TO SUPPORT SERVICE FOR COPERNICUS DATA AND THE CCM ACTIVITY - H2.2/2023/005 H4/2023/007
description: Copernicus aims to improve and expand the full range of environmental monitoring applications: climate change, land cover, vegetation monitoring, ocean color, sea surface temperature, sea level rise, sea and air pollution, air quality monitoring, ground motion, etc. These applications achieve the best results when they combine a wide range of Earth Observation (EO) data generated by various types of satellite sensors: SAR, Optical Very High, High and Medium Resolution, Altimetry, Atmospheric Composition, hyperspectral, thermal infra-red, multispectral etc. In order to be able to meet this need for wide ranging types of EO data, Copernicus makes available to users not only data from the Copernicus Sentinels but also data from other (commercial) complementary missions, called Copernicus Contributing Missions (CCM). The quality of Copernicus Sentinel data is rigorously analysed by teams of scientific EO experts, who calibrate and validate the data received from the sensors to ensure that the data distributed to users are fit for purpose andmeet the stringent data quality requirements. These teams are called the Mission Performance Clusters (MPCs), and their contracts are managed by the Data Quality team in ESA's Earth Observation Directorate. The scope of the MPCs is being enlarged as they will soontake over responsibility for overseeing the quality not only of the Copernicus Sentinel data but also of the CCM data. This qualitycontrol of the CCM data is currently handled under the PRISM contract, by the Copernicus Coordinated Quality Control (CQC) function.A support service is required in order to handle the day-to-day supervision of these two operational branches (Data Quality for Sentinel and CCM data and the CCM Activity), to ensure an efficient coordination of the end-to-end operations of the CCM Activity andthe Copernicus Data Quality services, under ESA's overall management.

title: KA-BAND ANTENNA ARRAY SUBSYSTEM FOR LAUNCHERS COMMUNICATION VIA DATA RELAY
description: The current TM link between the launcher and ground is done through the different ground station depending on the specific trajectory. These ground stations services are costly. A lower cost alternative would be to use a Relay System such as EDRS, but for this purpose a K-band antenna is needed to be installed. As the K band presents a bigger attenuation than the current S band a low profile,K band array is needed to increase the gain and cope with the losses. In order to maintain the link while the launcher is rotating it is necessary to constantly point the array towards the Relay satellite. The system design needs to be robust and independent fromthe launcher central computer, in order to maintain the communication in the event of a major problem of the launcher. The pointingcontrol function is therefore preferred to be implemented inside the communication subsystem. The design options for the control function are to be evaluated at the beginning of the activity (e.g. use of GNSS signal and/or passive retrodirective pointing using forward link beacon signal). The design is aimed at covering all the requirements of a launcher external element including the low profile, extreme mechanical and thermal conditions taking into account the thermal dissipation, and the typical TED (Thermo-Elastic Distortion). The activity also studies the end to end link system design (including link budget), to have a robust link with continuousconnection during the complete trajectory, leading to definition of key design elements including antenna gain, size, number of elements, RF losses, bandwidth, transmit RF power, data rates and associated modulation and coding to be used. The modulation and coding is to be in compliance with relevant standards and compatible with Data Relay systems in Ka-Band. The critical functions breadboarding is to include the representative elements to prove the complete system, including at least Ka-Band phased array elements and pointing control. The test results on performance of the antenna subsystem are fed into a final analysis on the end-to end system performance and robustness, to confirm the system design. This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Requirements Review and Consolidation- Preliminary Design- Breadboard implementation- Breadboard testing- Way forward towards development to reach flight model and recommendation on remaining onboard elements to be developed/completed

title: LITHIUM FREE BATTERIES FOR LOW EARTH ORBIT SATCOM CONSTELLATIONS( ON REQUEST) (ARTES AT 4F.177) - EXPRO+ (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to develop, manufacture and test batteries from sustainable and ESA Member States sourced materials with high cycle life at high Depth of Discharge (DoD) and a good rate capability for small communication satellites in LEO.Targeted Improvements:Enabling a European or Canadian source of lithium free space battery for LEO satcom constellations.Description: Currently the state-of-the-art technology for energy storage in satellites are Li-ion batteries, however this technology relies on materials which are not readily available in ESA Member States and have limited lifetime and power density. Consequently, Li-ion batteries Deep of Discharge (DoD) in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) applications is severely limited (typically 20%), further reducing the effective energy densities. Over the past years, manufacturers have reached high power density and promising life cycles with technologiessuch as Na-ion batteries (up to 5 kW/kg and over 5000 cycles, with an energy density of up to 160 Wh/kg) which could revolutionise energy storage in telecommunication satellites.An inherent advantage of lithium free batteries is also, that they areconsiderably more sustainable and use ESA Member States available raw materials, such as hard carbon on the anode side and Prussianblue analogues on the cathode side for Na-ion batteries.This activity will improve the effective energy density of batteries for small satellites and secure ESA Member States' independence by using environmentally friendly materials, that are easily accessible. A lithium free battery breadboard made of non-critical materials will be designed, developed, manufactured, and tested to demonstrate both compliance with space requirements and high cycle life at depth of discharge and power relevant to telecommunication satellitesin Low Earth Orbit.

title: Q-BAND TRANSMIT ACTIVE ANTENNA FOR COMBINED USER AND FEEDER LINK ON LEO SATELLITES (ARTES AT 5B.249) - EXPRO+ (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: The objective: The objective of this activity is to develop a Q-band transmit, scalable active antenna for the combined user and feeder links for Low-Earth-Orbit (LEO) broadband applications.Targeted Improvements:- Enabling broadband services in Q-band for LEOsatellites.- Eliminating the need for separate user and feeder link antenna.Description: Satellite telecommunication systems haveexperienced an increased traffic in Ku and Ka frequency bands and higher frequency bands are targeted to satisfy the increasing required capacity. Currently, Q/V bands are mostly used for feeder links on (Very)-High-Throughput-Satellites (V)HTS Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) satellites, and passive antenna solutions already available and active ones under initial development. While feeder link beams are fixed on GEO systems, in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites the feederbeams benefit from repointing of an array antennasolution as it provides more flexibility and reliability and the ability to dynamically assign multiple beams to multiple gateways and users.This activity will design a highly integrated Q-band direct array antenna for LEO satellites allowing multi-beam operations for both user and feeder links. This shall include a mechanical and thermal management concept. An engineering model of an antennatile (at least 10 cm x 10 cm size) will be developed and tested. The engineering model tile shall contain the most representative passive and active components. Commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) active components can be considered. The thermal management systemshall be designed, and representative components shall be included in the antenna tile engineering model.

title: ATTITUDE AND ORBIT CONTROL SYSTEM FOR HIGH ASPECT RATIO SATCOM SATELLITES ( ON REQUEST) (ARTES AT 4C.072) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test an Attitude and Orbit Control System (AOCS) architecture for high aspect ratio satellites in Low Earth Orbits (LEO) and Very Low Earth Orbits (VLEO), capable as well to perform controller and propulsion-less de-orbiting operations.Targeted Improvements:- Enabling AOCS for high aspect ratio satellites- Enabling high aspect ratio satellite to perform a controlled re-entry manoeuvre.Description: High aspect ratio (HAR) satellites are of increasing interest for satcom users, due to several advantages at system level over a more traditional design (e.g. easier accommodationin the launcher, possibility to have larger surfaces for a given volume to accommodate solar arrays, antennas, radiators, etc.). However, the AOCS for such satellites takes onadditional degrees of complexity both on the hardware architecture and the modelling andcontrol algorithms side, such as limited volume for actuators accommodation such as wheels, or the compensation of increased atmospheric drag in specific attitudes when flying at lower altitudes in VLEO. The controlled re-entry for such satellite class poses additional AOCS technical challenges which require specific attention.This activity will design, manufacture and test an AOCS engineering model for a single High Aspect Ratio (HAR) spacecraft in at least two scenarios; nominal VLEO or LEO operations and a controlledpropulsion-less re-entry case from VLEO. Possible AOCS architectures, flight dynamics modelling, on-board algorithms and associatedoperational concepts will be studied. Currently available sensors (e.g. star trackers, gyros, etc) and actuators (e.g. wheels, magnetorquers, control moment gyros, etc) will be assessed andrequired adaptation will be identified for the HAR configuration. Breadboarding of AOCS hardware will be carried out and AOCS algorithms developed. An AOCS subsystem scaled engineering model will be developedand implemented into a AOCS testbed. The testbed will be used to evaluate the performance for a nominal mission scenario in VLEOor LEO and a controlled re-entry scenario without the need of propulsion system. The re-entry scenario shall be tested representative environment (e.g. wind tunnel).

title: APA SOLAR REGULATOR MODULE FOR BATTERY BUSES - EXPRO PLUS
description: The Advanced Power Architecture (APA) is a standard concept for the Power Conditioning and Distribution Unit (PCDU). APA follows the interoperable and interchangeable modularity approach applied for the project ADHA (Advanced Data Handling Architecture) that started in 2020. APA is aimed to be fully compatible with ADHA so that together they will form the kern of a satellite platform.As ADHA, APA is composed of two elements: a standardized Unit rack (element 1) that providesstandard services to a set of Power Modules (element 2) that populates the rack to make an APA PCDU. The power unit can be built upon modules from different manufacturers, based on performances, cost, programmatic constraints. This approach allows strong reduction of development time and recurrent costs, faster development and adoption of more performing technologies in great part enabled by the envisaged interoperable and interchangeable modules that compose the system.The definition the Advanced Power Architecture and related Standardization of the development ofthe APA element 1 (rack product) is being addressed in a dedicated activity funded by the Preparation Element of the DPTD and by the Future EO Program (ESA/IPC(2022)1,add.42). The modules that compose the element 2 of the APA are subject to several TDE activities. Element 1 outputs (APA Unit requirements and standard requirements for APA Modules) will be used as inputs to Element 2 activities. Element 2 outputs (APA Modules) will then be used as input to Element 1 (for the validation of standard power modules requirements and overall APA architecture).GaN advantages (e.g. high switching frequency, thermal performance, inherently radiation tolerant),allowing a more compact power cell, will be fully exploited in combination with resonant power conversion techniques. Digital control techniques provides flexible and reliable control of the power cell and a first level failure detection isolation and recovery (FDIR)in the module.This activity aims to develop the Solar Regulator module (SAR) for battery buses with Maximum Power Point Tracking capabilities.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- Consolidation of APA Requirements (generic and specific modules)- Trade off and evaluation of the most promising Conversion Power Cell topologies- Preliminary and detailed design definition- Manufacturing and testing the module- Contribution to the APA Unit integration and test, including APA standardised documentationand interoperability/interchangeability test.

title: ULTRACOMPACT 778 NM RUBIDIUM SECONDARY OPTICAL FREQUENCY STANDARD - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop an ultracompact, secondary, optical frequency reference based on a two-photon transition in Rb vapour at 778nm.Description:Ultra-stable miniature atomic clocks are being considered for space applications. The Rubidium two-photon transition secondary frequency standard has demonstrated interesting performance metrics with a further potential for ultra-low size, weight and power (SWaP) integration.Currently, such an approach is hindered by the lack of miniaturized laser sources with suitable power levels and spectral properties as well as a compact physics package design taking advantage of the full capabilities of the integrated photonics and microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) gas cell technology platforms.This activity aims at exploiting these enabling technologies and developing a further concept of a compact high-performance atomic physics package for an ultra-compact secondary optical frequency standard. The goal of this activity is to provide a fractional frequency stability < 10 - 12 at 1 second integration time implemented using integrated photonic techniques.The following tasks are foreseen in this activity: Evaluate sources of integrated photonic laser systems delivering the wavelengths and the required spectral properties for the defined system approach. Develop Rb cell techniques and technologies targeting an ultracompact 778 nm rubidium secondary optical frequency standard using chip-scale photonic integration. Demonstrate the fractional stability performance achievable using the chosen chip-scale photonic approach. Evaluate chip-scale optical frequency combs with SiN Kerr comb techniques to provide an initial stabilized direct optical-RF link. Provide a packaging solution to maintain the preliminary performance achieved.NOTE: This activityis currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The finallist of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: TGO-MEX RADIO OCCULTATION - EXPRO+
description: RO occurs when the transmitter of a radio signal appears to set behind a planet, as viewed from a receiving station. The radio signal is refracted by the atmosphere and ionosphere causing a frequency shift; analysing this frequency shift allows reconstruction of a high-resolution vertical profile of density (and thus pressure and temperature) in the neutral atmosphere and ionospheric electronabundances in the ionosphere. Spacecraft-to-Earth RO has been carried out for many decades by planetary missions, but the opportunities for this are limited by the orbital geometry and ground station availability.

title: ACTIVE LOCAL STRUCTURAL CONTROL OF VERY LARGE SPACE STRUCTURES - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop a breadboard of a local active control system, which demonstrates the capability of locally regulating the stiffness of very large structures in space.Description: Large space structures are expected to exhibit structural modes at low frequency likely to couple with the AOCS control system. For very large structures it is expected that the attitude control will be achieved by distributed sensors and actuators, which may potentially result in relative high loads and displacements. Past activities have shown the potential of local structural control by using strain sensors co-located with active elements for local structural stiffening (e.g. based on piezo technology).This activity is expected to provide an assessment on the critical aspects of very large structures, including: Interaction between structure and AOCS (criticality of structure stiffness vs. mass). Feasibility to reduce structural resonance through passive and/or active structuraldamping. Criticality of pointing and stability requirements, e.g. for solar power generation maintaining sun-point for solar generator surface and Earth pointing for power transmission. ROM evaluation of internal loading on structure to ensure satisfactory capability of structural design, material selection and joining technologies. Feasibility for redundancy in the design and performance of very large structures, assuming potential failure in structure or structural joining elements as well as on AOCS sensors and actuators over the anticipated in-orbit lifetime.In consideration of the above, this activity targets the development of a local active control system breadboard together with an on-ground testbed representative of very large structures in space to demonstrate this technology.The activity will encompass thefollowing tasks: Identify candidate sensing and stiffness regulators suitable for local strain sensingand stiffening. Assess and optimise the integration of strain sensing and stiffness regulators into structural elements in view of optimising the local controllability of stiffness. Design a distributed control system that drives the local stiffening systems toachieve global stabilisation and control goals. Define a suitable verification and validation process for the designed distributedcontrol system. Define and setup a ground testbed representative of very large structures in space. Demonstrate the distributed control system on a suitable scaled breadboard,adapted for laboratory environment and deployed on the ground testbed.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.

title: END-TO-END MODELLING OF THE RADIATION HARDNESS ASSURANCE PROCESS - EXPRO+
description: Objectives: To develop an integrated software toolkit to assess the relative contributions to overall errors and uncertainties in the radiation hardness assurance process and estimate the true risk of failures. Description: The current process for Radiation Hardness Assurance (RHA) attempts to ensure compliance to mission robustness, reliability and availability with respect to radiation. This includes a range of measures addressed at different stages of the process. environment models are often applied with confidence levels and margins which in isolation may not sufficiently mitigate risk, the transport of radiation through shielding can incorporatea great deal of hidden margin (depending on the level of detail of the radiation model) but this can also be reduced to near-zero through detailed analysis and effects in components based on test data are highly susceptible to component specifics combined with other degradation parameters and temperature variations. Given this myriad of factors the true risk of component failure is not easy to discern. This activity shall address Radiation Hardness Assurance (RHA) as an integrated approach from radiation environment modelling to component acceptance to determine true risk levels for the end-to-end process. This shall include assessment of the probabilities of component failure for various environments using different methods for capturing environmental variability, radiation model fidelity and uncertainties in component test data and related statistical approaches. This shall be able to incorporate a digital representation of the spacecraft for radiation transport, test data for components and a range of orbital environments thereby spanning multiple disciplines in spacecraft design and quality assurance and extracting benefits from adopting a Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) approach. The system shall incorporate estimates of errors and uncertainties at each step of the process to derivean estimate of the true risk of failure. This activity shall encompass the following tasks: - Investigate the requirements and definition of process by consultation with radiation experts in industry as well as at ESA - Establish the use cases and collect relevant radiation effects data to test in the software; - Design of the software architecture leveraging existing assets to link orbits, environments, propagation and effects; - Develop algorithms to propagate uncertainties through the different steps of the RHA process;- Derivation of "true risk" estimates and comparison with current approaches; - Make recommendations for the maturation of this integrated (MBSE) approach Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community Licence.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. For additional information please go to:http://www.esa.int/About_Us/Business_with_ESA/Small_and_Medium_Sized_Enterprises/Opportunities_forSMEs/Procurement_policy_on_fair_access_for_SMEs_-_the_C1-C4_Clauses

SMEs) is required. description: HE-ESA-017 - STAGE 1 - PRS PAYLOAD ADVANCED CAPABILITIES AND TECHNOLOGIES FOR GALILEO EVOLUTIONS The objective of the activity is about the design, development and proof-of-concept of innovative Payload architectures and technologies able to fulfil well identified advanced capability requirements to be targeted for Galileo Evolutions. title: ROSE-L STUDY: ALGORITHMS FOR THE MITIGATION OF IONOSPHERIC EFFECTS IN ROSE-L PRODUCTS - EXPRO+
description: This study, titled 'Algorithms for the Mitigation of Ionospheric Effects in ROSE-L Products', will be issued as part of the ROSE-L Science Support Plan (SSP), which formalized the need to reach SRL 6 at the end of Phase C. One of the necessary steps, as foreseen by the SSP, is to make sure that the mission effectively addresses the sources of disturbance on L1 and L2 products and prepares theadequate solutions to mitigate them. The current activity will be dedicated to fulfilling such need for what concerns the ionospheric disturbances. The work will be in particular aimed at: 1) verifying the impact of ionosphere on ROSE-L products' performance, with a focus on Level-1 products and 2) supporting the ROSE-L project on mode design trade-offs, such as providing recommendations on the split-band configuration and burst design aspects in relation to the achievable interferometric performance.

title: IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT FOR HIGH THROUGHPUT OPTICAL COHERENT TRANSCEIVERS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.008) ON REQUEST
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to de-risk high throughput (100-200 Gbps), cross-atmospheric optical communication fordirect to Earth (DTE) and feeder-links. The second objective is to collectstatistics on link quality and availability to support the design of high throughput optical space/ground links.Targeted Improvements:To demonstrate 10x higher throughput than the currently available optical transceivers for space applications from VLEO and LEO.Description:The objective of the activity is to de-risk developments of > 100 Gbps coherent transceivers used for the high throughput cross-atmospheric optical communication for direct to Earth (DTE) andfeeder-links. The activity will consist of the procurement of a cubesat with excellent body pointing capabilities in the order of a few tens of microradians to carry an optical communication payload.It will include an optical communication terminal with two 100-200 Gbps coherent transceivers (Tx and Rx), optical amplifiers and a modem. The development also includes hardware to be installedin an optical ground station to receive and transmit data towards the satellite. Estimated duration is 24 months(12 months development + 12 months IoE).

title: COHERENT RECEIVER TECHNOLOGIES FOR BEYOND-EARTH COMMUNICATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.002) EXPRO+ ON REQUEST
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop receiver technologies based on coherent detection of pulse-position modulated (PPM) signals for bidirectional inter-spacecraft links targeting distances above 1.5AU. The feasibility shall be demonstrated through a laboratory breadboard. A beyond-Earth pointing, acquisition and tracking strategy shall be investigated.Targeted Improvements:Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvement and increased data rate compared to Geiger mode detection using avalanche photo-receivers.Description:The sensitivity and data rate of the high photon efficiency (HPE) optical communication can be significantly increased by coherent detection of pulse-position modulation. A laboratory breadboard will demonstrate the suitability of coherent reception for inter-spacecraft communications targeting link distances above 1.5 AU, comparing the performance with the current state of art. The activity shall perform a trade-off analysis, performance simulation and the development of a laboratory demonstration. It is expected to improve the resilience on background light, since coherentcommunications are more robust to interference from undesired light sources. Furthermore, this activity will contribute to building the technology required for interplanetary networks supporting human exploration, commercial and scientific missions.

title: FLIGHT DETECTOR ARRAY FOR PHOTON STARVED LINK ACQUISITION, TRACKING ANDCOMMUNICATION (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.005) EXPRO+ ON REQUEST
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop an on-board photon-counting detector array for deep-space laser communication terminals (LCT) with the capability to detect, acquire and track an uplink beacon from Earth. It shall have an uplink data demodulation capability implemented.Targeted Improvements:To enable development of a European photon-counting detector for tracking anddata reception.Description:The number of missions to Mars is expected to increase over the next years as many nations (USA, Russia, China, India, UAE, Europe and Japan) have already sent and/or planned to send missions to the red planet and its moons. The deep-space optical communication (DSOC) demonstration on-board NASA's Psyche spacecraft launched in October 2023 will demonstrate optical links up to distances of 2.7 AU in 2025. ESA considers a Mars bound mission equipped with a laser communication terminal for 2033.The present activity will design and prototype a photon counting detector array enabling (1) precise beam tracking of a dim laserbeacon, and (2) have a co-integrated modem function conforming to the high-photon-efficiency data reception implementation.

title: IN-ORBIT SATELLITE GUIDE STAR FOR EFFECTIVE WAVEFRONT PRE-COMPENSATED UPLINKS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.006) EXPRO+ ON REQUEST - EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this study is to evaluate the technical feasibility the technological needs and it shall produce a detailed design of the payload / system, for a satellite guide star (SGS) in geostationary orbit. The SGS shall be compared and evaluated against multiple ground-based laser guide stairs (LGS) for feeder link applications.Targeted Improvements:Increase the performance of adaptive optics pre-compensated uplinks by 30% under harsh turbulence conditions, at a cost less than that of a ground-basedLGS system. The cost shall consider an end-to-end system, for both the space and ground segments, including recurrent and operatingcosts.Description:Uplink and downlink laser communication paths are separated by the point-ahead angle. Turbulence causes a deterioration of the transmitted and received wavefront of the optical communication signal for ground-to-space links. Correction of the received wavefront is mainly done by measuring the wavefront errors and correcting the spatial modes of the wavefront deformationusing adeformable mirror (DM). However, due to the angular separation of transmit and receive paths, the downlink wavefront measurements may not be suitable to pre-correct the wavefront on the uplink.Ground-based laser guide stars (LGSs) are a well-known technique to overcome this issue. However, they suffer from major limitations: the inability to effectively detect the tip-tilt componentsof the wavefront error, high cost, operations at wavelengths outside the optical C-band, difficulty to operate them during daytimeconditions (due to limited brightness), their finite angular size, and they have to be installed in every OGS as part of the end-to-end feeder link network (hence multiplying the recurring and operating cost of these LGSs by the number of OGSs).An alternative approach is to operate a satellite guide star (SGS) on a small platform (e.g. a CubeSat) in proximity of the GEO satellite. This may prove to be much more cost-effective when compared with ground-based LGS systems and overcomes the previously listed challenges. Key challenges of the SGS are to employ a reliable guidance, navigation and control (GNC) system on-board the small satellite, to maintain a quasi-fixed position with respect to the mother spacecraft, accurately point towards the OGS and ensure that the SGS can never harm the mother spacecraft. Finally, the SGS must operate over the lifetime of the GEO satellite.The goal of the activity is to design to a conceptual level in-orbit SGS systems, perform a trade-off of all investigated concepts and a ground-based LGS system and to provide recommendations for future development and activities of the SGS system.

title: ON-BOARD AUTONOMOUS PLANNING TOOL FOR SPACE TO GROUND OPTICAL COMMUNICATION LINKS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 5H.007) EXPRO+ ON REQUEST
description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to develop and test a distributed (on-board and ground) software solution enabling theautonomous planning of space-to-ground optical links. The activity will implement an adaptive algorithm to dynamically redirect optical links to available ground stations using predictive models for local atmospheric conditions.Targeted Improvements:100% improvement in the optical space to ground link establishment success rate, when compared to the non-adaptive link scheduling.Description:Successful demonstration of optical communication links on multiple space missions and recent advances in atmospheric prediction models and adaptive routing strategies offer promising avenues for mitigating the impact of adverse weather conditions on communication reliability. Based on local atmospheric conditions prediction at each ground station and precise orbital data of satellite locations, this activity shall develop an autonomous optical link planning tool to automate and optimize scheduling of interconnected multi-orbit satellite constellations to optical ground. This toolshall be either integrated into a laser communication terminal or be a software component directly executable by an on-board processor linked in either case with a corresponding ground communicationagent. The envisaged solution will incorporate real-time weather and atmospheric data as well as historical patterns into the link planning process. It shall include adaptive algorithms to dynamically 'adjust communication parameters, such as modulation schemes anderror correction codes, and optimize the link performance during changing weather conditions. The activity will develop a test bed to evaluate the software planning tool in a laboratory environment simulating various scenarios, different weather conditions, satellite orbits and mission types.

title: ACTIVE SKY SURVEILLANCESYSTEM FOR OPTICAL GROUND STATIONS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 6C.074) EXPRO+ ON REQUEST
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design, prototype, and test an eye-safe active system surveying an area around thehigh-power laser transmission direction of optical ground station (OGS) for aircraft and cloud detection using real-time monitoring.Such system will reinforce airspace safety and support future OGS autonomous operation and scheduling. The objective includes real-time monitoring of atmospheric conditions.Targeted Improvements:Aircraft range and detection performance improvement, increasingstation availability by approximately 50%. Support for future OGS autonomous operation and scheduling and real-time directional atmospheric monitoring.Description:Laser-emitting ground stations require careful considerations in terms of airspace safety and particularly for applications requiring high-power laser beams (e.g. beacons, space debris laser ranging,optical feeder links, atmospheric remote sensing), measures must be taken to ensure laser safety in the sky. Passive detection systems, including visible and multispectral cameras, and passive radars are being explored for aircraft detection. However, they are limited in terms of distance coverage and rely on external illumination sources of opportunity (e.g. sunlight, DVB-T) or on object thermal signature. Other transponder-based solutions (ADS-B) are also used, however not all aircraft are equipped with such systems and these approaches may not besufficient for a future laser safety system.This activity will focus on the design and prototype of an eye-safe active system surveying an area around the high-power OGS beam for both aircraft and cloud detection, with a dual focus on reinforcing OGS aircraft safety and supporting autonomous decision-making with real-time monitoring of the atmosphere. This system will complement large field of view imagers and improve characterization performance. During station downtime periods due to e.g. cloud coverage, the system will provide additional information by monitoring atmosphere physical parameters (e.g. cloud base height, cloud profiles, aerosol properties) to support local weather forecast developments. The system developed in the frame of this activity shall be tested in an existing optical ground station.The main engineering tasks will include system requirement consolidation, design, prototype, and field validation.

title: IN-ORBIT TEST OF PROTOTYPE RE-FUELLING TECHNOLOGIES FOR GREEN PROPELLANTS (ARTES AT 3E.028)
description: The objective of this activity is to design, manufacture and test in-orbit prototype refuelling technologies for green (non-toxic) self-pressurising propellants, enabling the adoption of these technologies in multi-orbit satellite communication constellations.Targeted Improvements: - Extension of satellite on-orbit life by > 100%.- Reducing spacecraft propellant mass by >50%.Description: One of the challenges for multi-orbit Satcom networks is to find an effective and convenient solution for refuellable propulsion systems. Self-pressurising green propulsion systems (chemical and electrical) and can be refuelled in orbit provide an excellent option. They have many advantages over conventional hydrazine-based chemical propulsion systems, such as being non-toxic, cheaper, highly scalable, and accessible. Developing refuelling technology of these systems will enable spacecraft to be refuelled several times during their lifetime, reducing the propellant load needed at launch, improving in-orbit manoeuvres (collision avoidance, orbit changes, disposal) and prolonging mission life. Refuellingcapabilities are expected to be needed first for Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) and Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) missions but could also apply to future Low Earth Orbit (LEO) missions. These technologies are already under development outside of ESA Member States and, while some work has been performed (e.g. in-orbit refuelling activities for cryogenics, Xenon, and MON-MMH/hydrazine), this technology is not yet available in ESA Member States.The activity will be implemented in a phased approach. The first phase will design, manufacture and achieve flight readiness of an in-orbit refuelling payload forinvestigating technologies for green (non-toxic) self-pressurising propellants. Phase 1 outputs will comprise of a functioning in-orbit propellant transfer system including the propellant coupling interfaces and the pumping technology needed to make the propellanttransfer. Phase 2 will launch and operate the propellant transfer system in orbit, testing in the microgravityenvironment (up to several hours) allowing for the characterisation of the gravity-dependent effects and their impact on the transfer performance (e.g.proper gas/liquid separation, complex two-phase flow phenomena). Additionally, a fluidic model of the propellant transfer system willbe developed. Outputs of Phase 2 will consist of: The results from the in-orbitexperiment verifying docking interface (includingleakchecks before/during/after docking and transfer), evaluating the propellant transfer performance and efficiency (rate and percentage of propellant transferred); as well as improved fluidic modelling for the design of propellant transfer systems.

title: Q/V BAND PHASED ARRAY ANTENNA FOR AERONAUTICAL APPLICATIONS (ARTES AT 7A.079) - EXPRO+
description: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture, and test a Q/V band phased array antenna demonstrator for aeronautical applications, including the antenna radiating elements and the main passive components of the beamforming network.Targeted Improvements: - At least twice the number of beams and 3 to 4 times more compact volume compared to Q/V band mechanically scanning antennas.- 2 to 3 times reduced volume compared to Ka band antennas.Description:Today, terminal antennas are mainly exploiting Ka and Ku frequency bands. However, a growing number of satellite operators show interest in the emerging Q/V frequency band both for Geostationary Equatorial Orbit (GEO) and for Non-Geostationary Satellite Orbits (NGSOs). This includes new concepts envisaging service links to base stations and backhaul in Ka as well as in Q/V band. Required components and beamforming networks (BFNs) are increasingly becoming available, especially at Q-band, but these neither address the specific requirements of the satcom market nor cover the higherV-band range. For aeronautical applications, in particular, the Q/V band may enable improved performance (in terms of bandwidth, volume), while still maintaining acceptable link budgets with LEO/GEO satellites.In this activity, a Q/V band phased array antenna for aeronautical applications, suitable for GEO or NGSO satellites shall be developed. The demonstrator shall include antenna radiating elements and the main passive components of the BFN. Active commercial off the self (COTS) components will be included in the final demonstrator. Innovative solutions like those based on multilayer technology will be considered. A trade-off between two solutionswill be performed: one with an antenna aperture combining both transmit and receive functionalities, and one with two separate antenna apertures for the transmission and reception. A single circular polarisation in transmit and a single orthogonal circular polarisation in receive mode can be considered. The antenna demonstrator will be capable of generating two simultaneous beams (minimum target 1 beam). Scanning capabilities between -55 and + 55 degrees in every azimuthal plane shall be guaranteed. A Q/V band demonstrator including 8x8 radiating elements and customised passive BFN to generate two simultaneous beams shall be manufactured (separate Q and V band apertures or a single combined aperture) and tested. Active COTS components will be included in the final demonstrator toguarantee integrability with passive components and to improve the demonstrator representativeness

title: TOXIC FREE JOINING OF RF PASSIVE ASSEMBLIES(ARTES AT 5C.531) - EXPRO+
description: The objective of the activity is to develop a sustainable end-to-end joining process for RF passive low and high-power assemblies including waveguides and feed chains. This will include investigation of sustainable brazing and surface coating techniques. The developed end-to-end joining process will be fully evaluated on an RF feed chain and a waveguide assembly.Targeted Improvements:- Enable sustainable manufacturing of RF passive assemblies by eliminating toxic elements used in traditional metal-joining techniques. - Reduction of energy consumption of up to 30% when metal-joining techniques are used.Description: RF passive assemblies are widely used in telecommunication satellites. This includes waveguides and feed chain assemblies, and in the next decade, large numbers of waveguide components are anticipated to be deployed in Telecom GEO and LEO satellites. These components are mainly made of individual Aluminium alloy parts which are often joined by brazing. Current brazing fillers have melting temperatures which are close to the melting temperature of the alloys that is joined. The high temperature requires the use of flux additives to mitigate corrosion inthe joint area. These fluxes can contaminate or corrode the joints and they are toxic. This result in delicate process conditions toensure the hardware is not affected by the brazing and often leads to a significant number of rejected parts.This activity will investigate and trade-off sustainable, eco-friendly metal-joining technique eliminating the need for toxic flux additives as well ashigh processing temperature compared to the standard brazing techniques. Selecting the most promising one, an end-to-end sustainable joining process with significantly reduced energy consumption will be developed including internal and external surface treatment.Engineering models of one simple and one complex RF assembly will be manufactured and tested. Testing will include passive intermodulation to fully evaluate the developed end-to-end process.

title: COMPACT LOW FREQUENCY ANTENNAS FOR DEPLOYMENT ON THE LUNAR SURFACE
description: ObjectivesTo develop compact low frequency antenna and its' deployment mechanisms for the Astrophysical Lunar Observatory (ALO). DescriptionThere is a proposed mission concept to establish a lunar observatory on the far side of the Moon. The advantage of placing the observatory on the far side of the moon is the low RF interface in the frequency band of interest (2- 80MHz), which is not observable on the Earth. To measure at such low frequencies with sufficient angular resolution an interferometer is needed consisting of at least a thousand individual antennas positioned in an array on the lunar surface. This approach has been used on Earth for experiments such as LOFAR and the upcoming SKA telescope. However, since each antenna has to be transported to the lunar surface and then deployed, a new antenna architecture needs to be developed.This activity performs a detailed trade-off study of the best antenna design and deployment mechanism. Possible solutions include inflatable structures, printed antennas, unfurlable booms and other concepts. The main design driver for the ideal solution is to minimize the mass and volume of the antenna when stowed. The target is to be able to pack several hundreds of individual antennas with integrated electronics into the European Large Logistics Lander (EL3). From the trade-off study, the most favourable concept shall be selected to be breadboarded. The final test demonstrates the deployment and RF performance.This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Detailed review of possible antenna architectures that can operate in the region of 2-80MHz - Detailed review into possible deployment mechanisms that could be used on the lunar surface - A trade-off study considering: frequency, antenna architecture, and deployment mechanism should be performed - Select the concept for breadboarding. - Develop a breadboard antenna, designed and built to the representative volume - Demonstrate afull deployment along with an RF measurement.

title: QUANTUM MEMORY FOR C-BAND OPTICAL SIGNALS (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3H.002) EXPRO+
description: Objective: The objective of this activity is to design a quantum memory breadboard compatible with the telecommunication C-band wavelengths. The memory shall have the capability to store single photonsefficiently for long storage times, and high capacity, whilemaintaining their quantum state with high fidelity, such that it can be applied in quantum networks based on satellite links. This breadboarding activity shall allow for benchmarking performances and understanding system requirements, as well as defining further development steps (for increasing storage time and capacity) together with implementation concepts (ground-based vs space based).Targeted Improvements:A quantum memory is an enabling technology for long-distance quantum network communication.Description:A quantum memory is a device which stores the quantum state of an incoming photon and efficiently retrieves the same photon-state on-demand without disturbing the quantum state. Such a deviceis an enabling technology for scalable long-distance quantum communicationbecause it allows the synchronisation of otherwise probabilistic events and store the quantum state until entanglementhas been created in other nodes. To reach global distances, satellites will be needed in the communication chain. Although there is significant research and development effort ongoing for many years, the required quantum memory performances have not yet been demonstrated. Experiments have been focusing mostly on optimizing the performances of single parameters, without combining them all into a single system. The key challenge for quantum memories to be considered for satellite-based links is the storage time, where the time-of-flightfor optical signals to a LEO satellite and back to Earth sets a lower threshold. The memory needs to be able to store many qubits to enable some reasonable rate of exchange of quantum information.The activity aim is to develop a quantum memory breadboard (for instance based on a rare-earth-ion-doped crystal) which is compatible with operation at C-band wavelengths. The emphasis is on engineering a solution in which all the critical system parameters for connection via satellite (i.e. storage time, capacity, efficiency) can be demonstrated simultaneously, albeit without achieving the theoretically best possible performances. This is considered a startingpoint to advance the technology readiness level of quantum memory, which will in turn allow for an increased understanding of the operational trade-offs and define a realistic architecture for quantum communications. Operational trade-offs will include operating the memory as an absorptive type (storing entangled photonsreceived as an input) or emissive type (where the memory itself is used to generate the entangled photons).Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required.
