title: ARTES 4.0 STRATEGIC PROGRAMME LINE OPTICAL COMMUNICATION SCYLIGHT ROLLING WORK PLAN FOR 2020 - 2021
description: 1. Introduction: The work plan was established based on an ESA internal "ARTES ScyLight Call for Ideas" and reflects the findings from industry workshops or the consolidation process with stakeholders, like National Delegations, operators, service providers, satellite manufacturers, industry and experts. In addition, the work plan lists activities inherited from the former ARTES ScyLight Element work plans that will be issued under the new legal framework of the ARTES 4.0 Strategic Programme Line (SPL) "Optical Communication - ScyLight". 2.Strategic Activities: A number of activities are identified as of immediate strategic importance as they supportadvancement of optical communications technologies, e.g. towards the "fibre in the sky" vision, or they address system relevant elements. Some of those activities have been addressed in ITTs under the legacy ScyLight Element, but have not resulted in contracts, due to lack of overall budget within the Participating States' allocations. However, those activities are still considered of high strategic value and are listed again (or slightly modified) in the proposed work plan. Furthermore, the SPL Optical Communication - ScyLight is supposed to evaluate the benefits of optical communications in more general terms, also beyond pure near Earth satcom applications. Lastly, ScyLight is aiming to foster the maturity of the industrial landscape in Europe/Canada to prepare for future upcoming markets. Some of those strategic areas are listed below.- Foster Industrial Landscape- Atmospheric Effects- Optical Communication Terminal Technologies- High Data Rate and RF/Optical Coupling- Quantum Communications- Standardisation3. Implementation: Thefollowing implementation philosophy will be followed: Phasing: phasing of the contractual activities may be considered, depending on the risks associated with the development, the maturity of the technologies, and potential early market perspectives. ParallelContracts: in accordance with the ARTES 4.0 Implementing Rules, parallel contracts may be awarded. Procurement Policy: the following procurement policies are foreseen for the proposed activities:C: Activities in open competition without any further restrictions. C1:Activities in open competition limited to non-Large System Integrators (LSIs) as prime. LSIs are allowed to participate as sub-contractors.C2: Activities are in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSIs is requested.C3: Activity restrictedto SMEs RD organisations, preferably in cooperation.C4: Activities in open competition, subject to the SME subcontractingclause.Implementation Category (formerly "Priority"): the activities comprising the SPL Optical Communication - ScyLight Work Planhave been designated as either B (Baseline) - formerly P1, or R (at the Request of delegates). The assignment of activities to these categories is not a declaration of technological, commercial or programmatic priority; instead, it simply indicates whether an activity requires a prior request from a Delegation for the ITT to be generated and released. ITTs for activities designated priority B will automatically be generated by the Executive. The planned ITT issue dates are indicated in Annex II; however, baseline activities for which industry and/or Delegations declare an interest will be implemented as a priority. Such interest can be notified directly to the ARTES ScyLight Programme Office. Invitations to tender for activities designated R will only be initiated either: On the explicit request of at least one delegation, or On the initiative of the Executive following consultation of the JCB.

title: EXPRO+ NAVISP ELEMENT 1 (NAVISP-EL1-011): RESILIENT, TRUSTWORTHY, UBIQUITOUS TIME TRANSFER REISSUE
description: This REISSUED EXPRO+ procurement is part of the NAVISP Programme, under Elelment 1, Work Plan 2018.An accurate, secure and reliable time transfer is a key enabler for emerging fixed and mobile services worldwide. A number of different applications like autonomous vehicles, terrestrial positioning, 5G mobile broadband, mobile multimedia broadcast, power grids, terrestrial positioning services, financial operations, IoT, big data and cloud processing will require secure and reliable time information to be able to work correctly and efficiently. The time information will not only need to be transferred securely, but also accurately and in a seamless and ubiquitous manner, which is quite challenging for solutions based on GNSS only.Based on the above it seems necessary to put forward innovative and complementary methods of time transfer, focusing on the use of non-GNSS technologies. In order to enable an overall seamless provision of secure, ubiquitous and reliable time information, alternative solutions will be conceived to complement thecurrent GNSS time transfer techniques with the emerging fixed and mobile servicesThe main objective is to demonstrate feasibilityof time transfer using GNSS complementary technologies (e.g. signals of opportunity from LEO constellations or terrestrial infrastructure) that would provide secure, ubiquitous, and reliable time information.The activity shall focus on efficient and affordable implementations of time transfer techniques leveraging existing and emerging space-based and terrestrial technologies.

title: MULTI-DIMENSIONAL TWO-PHASE HEAT PIPE NETWORK ARTES AT 4D.061)
description: The objective of the activity is to develop a two-phase multi-dimensional heat pipe network breadboard enabling 30% improved thermal performance.Thermal models shall be developed to assist in the design and shall be validated on the breadboard.Targeted Improvements:Improve the thermal performance by more than 30% compared to state of the art.Description: Conventional heat pipe networks use two types of heat pipes. Long heat pipes distribute the heat along the length of the panel. Crossing heat pipes, mounted on top of the long heat pipes, uniformly spread the temperature between the long heat pipes. Unfortunately, this mounting technique createslarge temperature differences between heat pipes due to the various thermal interfaces. Two-dimensional, two-phase structures have been developed where the main and crossing heat pipes are connected together, thereby eliminating the thermal interfaces. However, the fluid distribution and flow within the 2D network is complex and cannot be modelled with existing thermal analysis tools. It has also been shown that conventional design andmanufacturing guidelines for standard heat pipes are not suitable for complex 2D two-phase networks. The tools and dedicated thermal models developed within this activity will be used to optimise and better predict the behaviour and performance of large and complex two-phase networks. They will be embedded within existing thermal analysis software, increasing the analysis capability as well as providing the capability to optimise complex two-phase networks. A two-phase heat pipenetwork breadboard will be manufactured and tested to verify the models.

title: INTER SATELLITE LINK V-BAND SOLID STATE POWER AMPLIFIER MODULE (ARTES AT 5C.381)
description: The objective of the activity is to design, develop and test an enabling inter satellite link V- Band solid state power amplifier module breadboard delivering 10W saturated power with better than 15% efficiency for Intersatellite RF links of at least 10Gbps over a distance of 1000 km.Targeted Improvements:Enabling technology development for RF Intersatellite links achieving 10Gbps and beyond in the 1000 km distance range.Description:Future NGSO constellations, GSO relay satellites relay and also multiple access telecom reconfigurable satellite systems require high data-rate inter-satellite-links (ISL) to overcome feeder link capacity saturation.RF ISL have been demonstrated more than 20 years ago and current ISL achieve 1-2 Gb/s per channel. Higher data rates are achieved with optical ISL such as on EDRS with up to 1.8Gb/s over long distances and 5.625Gb/s over short distances. An alternative or complementary solution is RF data links using a very high frequency band where significant bandwidth is available (59 to 71 GHz). More than10Gb/s is feasible for distances of up to at least 5000km and even higher data rates for short distances.In order to enable RF ISLat10 Gb/s and above, this activity will design and develop the critical technology: a V-Band solid state high power amplifier (SSPA) module. A concept for the RF output section of the ISL shall be selected and a breadboard of a 10 W V-Band SSPA module shall be manufactured and tested with a power added efficiency of at least 15%.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). For additional information please go to EMITS news "Industrial Policy measures for non-primes, SMEs and RD entities in ESA programmes".

title: LOW-PROFILE PHASED ARRAY ANTENNA FOR PROFESSIONAL TERMINALS FOR BROADBAND GEO SYSTEMS (ARTES AT 7A.042) (RE-ISSUE 1-8925)
description: The objective of this activity is to design, build and test two (one for Ka- and one for Q-/V-band) bi-dimensional (2-D)phased array demonstrators produced in a low-profile technology for the professional market.Targeted Improvements: Enabling technology to allow the use of millimetre-wave technology in phase array antennas for the professional market.Description: The offeringof the new satellite communication systems are putting a continuous pressure on antenna performance size and costs. In particular, low-profile and low-cost high-gain antennas that permit obtaining directive pencil beam, relatively large bandwidth, and agile electronic beam scanning are demanded by the professional market.These antennas shall work in both transmit and receive in either Ka or Q/V frequencybands. The Q/V band is of interest for high data rate Point-to-Point communications.In this framework, millimetre-wave technology could provide extended bandwidth for high-capacity links in Ka-Band and Q-/V-band systems for fixed or mobile terminalswith various advantages in terms of performance, size and cost.The Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) is an example of a technology that may beconsidered.This activity is expected to provide two phased array demonstrators; one for Ka- and one for Q-/V-band, using millimetre-wave technology and supporting the following requirements:.They shall be capable of TX/RX functions. .They shall exhibit significant improvement as compared to existing products..They shall be able to scan a single beam at least up to 60 degrees from the boresight direction in all the azimuthal planes and satisfy the regulatory aspects.It is expected that in this activity a detailed trade-off between RF performance, beam steering capability and manufacturing aspects is carried out.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activityrestricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). For additional information please go to EMITS news "Industrial Policy measures for non-primes, SMEs and RD entities in ESA programmes".

title: GUIDELINES FOR THE SAFE USE OF LASER TECHNOLOGY (SCYLIGHT SL.004) EXPRO+ (RE-ISSUE OF ITT 1-9260)
description: The objective of the activity is to establish guidelines for the safe use of laser technology, addressing:1)Transmission through the atmosphere (to/from satellites or to/from unmanned aerial vehicles) with an emphasis on human eye safety.2)Space-to-space or ground-to-space links and the risk of blinding/damaging other space assets (international space station (ISS), satellites with optical instruments, etc.).3)Handling of laser technology in assembly, integration and test (e.g. terminals/optical components).Ground-to space and space-to-ground laser communication links through the atmosphere, like high data rate feeder links or satellite-to-UAV/RPAS links, have the potential to unintentionally illuminate manned aerial vehicles (e.g. commercial airliners) as they cross the laser beam, which brings a risk of human eye damage, particularly for high-intensity earth-to-space links. Other risks, especially for high power applications, include the inadvertent blinding of space or airborne assets (e.g. ISS, optical satellites) and human eyedamage when handling laser components and subsystems during, for example, satellite assembly, integration and test. Various studiesand activities relevant to the domain have been undertaken and should be considered as inputs to this activity. In this activity the various risks associated with the use of laser technology in the implementation and operation of a satellite communication system shall be identified and categorised. Handling and operational constraints and protection measures shall be established for each ofthe identified risk scenarios and consolidated in a set of safety guidelines for industry and operators.

title: LARGE UNFURLABLE REFLECTOR SURFACE ASSEMBLY FOR KA-BAND APPLICATIONS (ARTES AT 5B.169) ( RE-ISSUE OF ITT 1-8909)
description: Objective of the activity is to design, develop and verify an unfurlable reflector surface assembly suitable for use in large European antennas operating in the 20 - 35 GHz frequency range.Targeted Improvements: Enabling technology development for a new source of unfurlable reflectors capable of generating the high gain, narrow beams needed in terabit/s high throughput satellite systems.Description: The next generation of high throughput satellites (HTS) that are intended to reach terabit/s capacity requirehighly directive antennas and hence large radiating apertures with diameters ranging from 3.5 to 5 metres at Ka-band. Due to the accommodation constraints of the launcher fairing, only antennas with deployable apertures can meet this need. Large antennas with unfurlable reflectors have attracted significant interest in Europe in recent years as critical technology for European non-dependence.Reflector antennas of the 5 metre class operating at Ka-band will be a key enabler for the next generation of HTS. However, today areflective surface that can be stowed and unfurled without compromising the surface accuracy and thermal stability is not available.In this activity a large unfurlable reflector surface assembly shall be designed and developed with adequate RF and mechanical properties for Ka-band applications. Investigations shall include promising solutions, such as metallic mesh or carbon fibre reinforcedsilicone (CFRS) for the RF reflective surface, as well as a suitable support structure, such as a carrying net made of tensioning ties. A prototype of large reflector surface assembly shall be manufactured. The built prototype shall then be tested, including verification of thedeployment, surface accuracy, RF and passive intermodulation performance. Limitations and improvements to utilize the technology forantenna diameters up to 8m shall be identified.Procurement Policy: C(2) = A relevant participation (in terms of quality and quantity) of non-primes (incl. SMEs) is required. For additional information please go to EMITS news "Industrial Policy measures for non-primes, SMEs and RD entities in ESA programmes".

title: ARTES SCYLIGHT ROLLING WORK PLAN
description: This first ScyLight Workplan has been established based on an ESA internal "ARTES ScyLight Call for Ideas". It will be amended reflecting the findings from Industry Workshops or the consolidation process with stakeholders, like National Delegations, Operators, Service Providers, Satellite Manufacturers, Industry and experts which will take place in the next months. The activities have beenselected in line with the programme objectives for Line 1 (Common System and Technologies Activities) and Line 4 (Quantum Cryptography Technologies).Line 1 covers ESA-initiated market and system studies including optical transmission/propagation studies, as well as ESA coordination of user and expert groups (i.e. satellite primes, operators, service providers, industry) to define the roadmap and derive ESA Invitations to Tender (ITTs). This Line also covers ESA- initiated development activities on critical and commonlyrequired components and their validation, evaluation and in-orbit verification, and supports coordination efforts with standardization bodies.Line 4 is dedicated to Quantum Cryptography technologies and covers the related development as well as in-orbit and service demonstration, including Quantum Key Generation and Distribution systems, and the demonstration of related end-to-end systems.2.ImplementationPhasing: Phasing of the contractual activities may be considered depending on the risks associated with the development, the maturity of the technologies, and potential early market perspectives.Parallel Contracts: In accordance with the ARTES ScyLight Implementing Rules, parallel contracts can be awarded in ARTES ScyLight. Procurement Policy: The following procurementpolicies are foreseen for the proposed activities:C:Activities in open competition without any further restrictions. C1:Activities in open competition limited to non-Large System Integrators (LSIs) as prime. LSIs are allowed to participate as sub-contractors.C2:Activities are in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSIs is requested.C3:Activity restricted to SMEs RD organisations, preferably in cooperation.C4:Activities in open competition, subject to the SME subcontracting clause.Priority: The activities comprising the ScyLight Work Plan are designated as either Priority 1 or 2. The assignment of activities into these categories is not a declaration of technological, commercial or programmatic priority. Instead, it simply indicates whether an activity requires a prior request from a Delegation for the ITT to be generated and released. ITTs for activities designated Priority1 will automatically be generated by the Executive. The planned ITT issue dates are indicated in Annex 1, however Priority 1 activities for which industry and/or Delegations declare an interest will be implemented as a priority. Such interest can be notified directly to the ARTES ScyLight Programme Office.Invitations to tender for activities designated Priority 2 will only be initiated either:on the explicit request of at least one delegation; oron the initiative of the Executive following consultation of the JCB.

title: SINGLE-CHIP 71-86 GHZ TRANSCEIVER RFIC FOR AERONAUTICAL SATCOM APPLICATIONS (ARTES AT 6A.074) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: The objective of the activity is to design, manufacture and test an integrated W-band transceiver Radio Frequency Integrated Circuit (RFIC) configurable as transmitter and receiver covering the 71-86 GHz band for aeronautical satcom applications. Targeted Improvements: Enable satellite aeronautical broadband services in W-band. Description: The maturity of Silicon technologies allows for the implementation of multifunctional and reconfigurable circuits in higher frequencies (above Q/V) enabling the use of those frequencies for various satellite telecommunications applications. In this activity, a multifunctional Radio Frequency Integrated Circuit (RFIC) will be designed in a suitable process, such as SiGe or GaAs to allow for low cost manufacturing. The development is targeting the aeronautical market although this could apply to other market segments. The transceiver will allow high-speed baseband data generated in an aircraft/spacecraft to be modulated to the appropriate W-band (uplink/downlink, i.e. 71-76 GHz or 81-86 GHz). Likewise, the transceiver will allow the high-speed data modulated in the W-band to be down-converted to one of two selectable outputs:1) Ka band to allow direct re-routing to Ka-band downlink;2) low IF to allow for direct demodulation. The RFIC will include a LO generationsub-circuit (VCO, frequency divider, frequency multipliers, etc.), an IQ up-converter and an IQ down-converter, an amplifier capable of driving external HPA MMIC and a low-noise amplifier. The final breadboard will demonstrate the functionality of the RFIC in allpossible configurations, conditioned by external circuitry and external HPA and LNA. Within this activity, a roadmap for "designformanufacture" of W-band transceiver RFIC in package for mass production shall be established. Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. SMEs). For additional information please go to EMITS news "Industrial Policy measuresfor non-primes, SMEs and RD entities in ESA programmes". Footnote: On Delegation Request activities will only be initiated on the explicit request of at least one National Delegation.

title: ARTES 4.0 SPL OPTICAL COMMUNICATION - SCYLIGHT: RF AND OPTICAL HYBRID GATEWAY ANTENNA (6C.002/SL.024)(ON DELEGATION REQUEST) - EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective:The objective of this activity is to investigate a telecom gateway antenna able to work simultaneously in both the RF (Ka- Q/V-Band) and optical wavelengths.Targeted Improvements:This product is currently not available and it would allow a phased migration from RF communications to optical communications.Description:There is a clear trend in the need to increase bandwidth in order to increase the data rate, within the telecommunications domain. Gateway traffic is currently routed to GEO satellites via Ku- and Ka-Band frequencies, but to allow an increase in the data rate and to release additional bandwidth for users, gateway trafficis starting to look at using Q/V band frequencies. An eventual move to W-band and finally optical links will follow.In this activity, it is intended to perform a study that will analyse the possibility of having in the same antenna (10m class) RF and optical links. In the first phase of the project the optical link will be considered as a down-link only. In a possible second phase, complexity will be added to the system to cover also the possibility to have an optical link in uplink as well.Several antenna layouts will be studied and a trade-off will be performed in order to identify the best architecture. Such a trade-off will also verify the pros cons of a hybrid antenna with respect to systems composed of separate RF and optical terminals.

title: ARTES 4.0 SPL OPTICAL COMMUNICATION - SCYLIGHT: SPACE QUALIFIED FAINT PULSE LASER SOURCE FOR QUANTUM KEY DISTRIBUTION (5G.003/SL.012)(ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: Objective:The objective of the activity is to develop and qualify a faint pulse laser source for space-based quantum key distribution systems.Targeted Improvements:Increase the technical readiness level of faint pulse laser sources suitable for quantum key distribution applications from 5 to 7. Description:Quantum key distribution systems using protocols based on faint laser pulses require a photon source emitting less than one photon per pulse on average. The information required for quantum key distribution can be encoded in the physical properties of the photons, such as their polarisation, phase or timing. This activity shall design, buildand qualify a faint pulse source for space-based quantum key distribution applications. This shall include a first conceptual system design to define the interfaces and requirements for a technology demonstration mission. The faint pulse source hardware shall include the laser source itself, as well as the required optics and electronics to control the photon states. The performance of the weak pulse source (especially the pulse repetition rate and the precision of amplitude and photon state control) shall be suitable forestablishing a quantum link between either a low earth orbit satellite or a geostationary satellite using existing optical terminals and a typical optical ground station. A qualification test campaign shall demonstrate the robustness of the source against mechanical, thermal and radiation loads.

title: SSA P3-SWE-XXXVIII ENERGETIC PARTICLE FORECASTING IN HELIOSPHERE
description: Solar energetic particle (SEP) forecasting has been identified as a key capability gap in the current provision of heliospheric weather forecasting within the Heliospheric Weather ESC. Physics-based models are computationally very demanding and therefore challenging to use for operational forecasting needs where fast results are required in order to provide the necessary lead times. This activity will combine expertise in both empirical and physics-based SEP modelling geared towards forecast provision. It will start with federation of both existing mature empirical and physics-based products targeting SEP forecasting, providing a comparison of different techniques and addressing current strengths and weaknesses through robust performance assessment. In addition, and in line withthe Heliospheric Weather ESC and Space Radiation ESC definition and development planning, a consistent approach to adopting SEP forecasting products will be proposed for the SWE network. The proposed approach will assess the current state of the art and take intoaccount work currently ongoing within H-ESC utilising magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) modelling. The activity will include a working demonstration of the new SEP forecast.

title: SUPPORT TO QUIC STANDARDISATION (ARTES FPE 1D.019)
description: Satellite communication links have specific characteristics that undermine the performance of commonly used Internet protocols, notably TCP, in part because performance over satellite was not a major consideration during the development of those protocols. Specifically, the long propagation delay imposed by GEO satellite links and their asymmetric nature lead to poor TCP performance. Unless addressed, this can result in a poor user experience, and significant under-utilization, contributing additional latency during the time that it takes TCP to ramp up to the available capacity (especially a concern as access speeds increase).Performance Enhancing Proxies (PEPs) are a solution developed to mitigate these performance limitations, utilising a range of quite different technologies. One widely used method splits the TCP protocol connection, allowing the endpoints to increase the sending rate beyond the limits that their own mechanisms would impose. This isolates the satellite service by installing proxies that terminate TCP connections withthe endpoints at one or both sides of the satellite service. Proxies allow an application flow to increase its sending rate, thanksto a reduced Round Trip Time (RTT) between the endpoint and the proxy, and an understanding of the capacity available for the satellite service (either configured or measured). This allows the application to ramp-up faster and take less time to utilise the available capacity of a satellite link. PEPs can also implement higher-level application functions that benefit web traffic and can improve interaction with the radio/resource management functions, e.g. pre-fetch/proxy and Domain Name System (DNS) interception.With a growing desire to preserve the privacy of Internet communications, there has been a notable increase in the proportion of encrypted traffic sent over the Internet, and this will soon become a significant proportion of all web traffic. Initially, there was a major surge in the use of Transport Layer Security (TLS) with https, and whilst this introduced complexity into proxy functions, it does not have a major impact on PEPs that operate at the TCP layer, because there PEPs were still able to modify the TCP protocol headers.While PEP solutions have thus enjoyed success in many deployed systems, the solutions they provide are now being challenged. A newgeneration of secure protocols is now emerging that integrate security into a User Datagram Protocol, UDP, transport layer. The major exponent of such technologies is QUIC, a protocol originally proposed by Google LLC, but that has since become an Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF) work item, expected to result in interoperable specifications. QUIC adoption was originally dominated by Google services, but the publication of an IETF standard specification can be expected to be followed by deployment of more QUIC clients and server platforms - expected to result in a rapid rise of encrypted traffic. QUIC transport fully encrypts all transport protocol headers, rendering these information elements invisible to middleboxes in the network (such as PEPs, traffic classifiers, and other devices used to support network operations). Moreover, QUIC authenticates the endpoints of a connection, making it impossible fora PEP to terminate the PEP connection without explicitly being configured as a proxy for the content origin.The first IETF standard version of QUIC (currently named QUICv1.0) is expected to be finalised early in 2019. To meet this deadline, work for QUICv1.0 has been focussed upon topics such as connection setup, encryption services, and interface to the upper-layer web protocols. However, the QUIC standards process does not conclude in early 2019; rather it will then move to address topics that could not be completed in time for this release date. Specifically, introducing multipath and forward error correction extensions to the QUIC standard is one of the key goals of the IETF working group. Satellite-optimised specifications of such extensions will be crucial to the performance of satellite systems in future integrated terrestrial-satellite 5G architectures. The opportunity to influence the design of the interaction between QUIC and the network path it uses will largely appear in the following 18-24 months as topics are prioritised for QUIC v2.0 and new techniques are proposed, analysed and incorporated into the specification. QUIC has been designed to accelerate transfers across normal Internet paths. Like HTTP2, it promises mechanisms that are also expected to help mitigate the effect a satellite propagation delay - such as reducing the number of RTTs to complete a web transfer, multi-streaming to reduce head of line blocking, more rapid access to new capacity and the ability to compress information (remove redundancy). Indeed, some of the core transport mechanisms being proposed for QUIC are also a central feature in many satellite PEP systems. Because key mechanisms are stillto be standardised in IETF QUIC, the real interactions using a satellite service are, as yet, unknown. There are therefore open questions about the expected performance of QUIC over satellite. The proposed activity therefore comprises three distinct tasks:Task 1: Evaluation of QUICv1.0 performance over satellite linksThe goal of this task is to assess the performance of the QUIC protocol over paths including satellite links via the use of analytical models, simulations and measurements. The assessment will include different scenarios involving a range of technologies (e.g. different types of PEPs, symmetrical and asymmetrical paths) relevant for the analysis. The running Future Preparation work plan activity "Mitigation Techniques for Addressing the Impact of Latency on Services over Satellite Networks" (1B.118) has already selected QUIC as one of the test cases that will be investigated as part of its emulation campaign to be conducted in the first half of 2019. The work of this task will therefore be closely coordinated with this running activity and implemented in the most efficient manner (e.g. possibly via CCN to activity 1B.118 to cover any additional simulations or measurements not currently incorporated, or stand-alone support tasks to cover expertise outside of the current consortia). This work is timed to coincide with the finalisation of the QUICv1.0 specification, and its final publication mid-2019.Task 2: Definition of proposed features for QUICv2 for satelliteUnder this task, based on the analysis performed in Task 1, the contractor willseek to identify and define mechanisms to improve the performance of QUIC when used in paths that include a satellite link. The modifications can include adaptations to the QUIC protocol itself (as proposed features for QUICv2), introduction of multipath operation to exploit both terrestrial and satellite paths, integration of link layer forward error correction and/or network coding to improve link resilience in satellite mobile channels, design recommendations for middleboxes for satellite networks, and the cases where the use of alternative protocols is needed (i.e., fall back to TCP).Task 3: Standardization and RecommendationsThis task will runin parallel with Tasks 1 and 2 and will focus on supporting the standardisation of the identified QUICv2 mechanisms through the IETF, possibly by including features on the roadmap for QUICv2. In addition, the work will include efforts to raise awareness within the satellite community of the potential for QUIC, and the implications for future satellite-based internet traffic.In summary, there is short-term potential to influence the on-going development of standards for QUIC, specifically the features to be added to the QUICv2.0 roadmap. In addition the activity can provide input to the satellite community to help them address the future development of PEP functions in satellite equipment. As a increasing proportion

title: PL_RM20-21 DUAL FLOW BIPROPELLANT LATCHING VALVE DEVELOPMENT
description: Currently there is in Europe neither an off-the-shelf dual flow bipropellant latching valve nor is there one under development. Latch valves are required for any bipropellant (e.g. NTO/MMH) propulsion system. Strictly speaking it is not necessary to use dual flowlatch valves, since however both fuel and oxidizer are always required simultaneously it makes from system point of view sense to use dual flow latch valves providing simultaneous supply of oxidizer and fuel.The goal of the activity is to increase the TRL on theequipment of a Dual Flow Bipropellant Latching Valve.The objective of this activity is the design, manufacturing, development and testing of an engineering valve model for the use with standard propellants (e.g. N2H4, MMH and N2O4). The compatibility with green propellants would be an asset. The activity shall include a requirement definition from a qualified source, demonstrate fast response times (e.g. < 10ms), excellent leak tightness after a representative life cycle and at temperature extremes and completion of a PDR datapack.

title: SSA P3-SWE-XLIX / P3-SWE-XL ENHANCED IONOSPHERE MODELS FOR EVENT ANALYSIS INCLUDING IONOSPHERIC SCINTILLATION PRODUCTS FOR ARCTIC
description: This activity will develop a self-consistent high latitude electrodynamics model which will provide information on the ionospheric state resulting from the couplings with the solar wind. The resources will include processed data products providing the user with acontinuous set of ionospheric parameters (e.g. TEC) and atmospheric heating variables facilitating data analysis capability for current and past events. Targeted development will enable the provision of combined information on the ionosphere based on data assimilation techniques and physics-based models. The validation of the model will be done by comparison with space and ground based experimental datasets. This activity will develop and demonstrate new space weather products based on real-time data and modelling combined with current understanding of the relationship between ionospheric phenomena observed in the polar region and GNSS signal scintillation, providing timely information to regional users on ionospheric conditions and their expected impact on positioning activities.

title: LARGE DEPLOYABLE REFLECTOR FOR IOD PREPARATION
description: Unfurlable deployable antenna reflectors are commercially available from US suppliers. European developments have been carried out to TRL 4 for the deployable structure within GSP, TAS and TRP activities with a strong involvement of ESA and following the recommendations of the Large Deployable Antenna Working Group. European IPR has been demonstrated so far for 6 m aperture. In order to progress the TRL of all the critical elements and components not yet developed in running precursor activities a further step is required, in preparation of IOD. Currently the TRL is 4 for the deployable structure, 2 for the reflecting surface, 3 for the deployment devices.The activity will start with a review of the potential platforms and launchers to be used for IOD and establish requirements and interface as targets for the EM design.These will include Earth Observation requirements. Critical breadboarding tasks will be performed to verify main functions and materials parameters related to environment (GEO and LEO).The activity will then aim at the design of the demonstrator reflector assembly and critical breadboarding of the elements with the lowest TRL, mainly the reflecting mesh with the shape control network, the deployment and hold down mechanisms and the deployable arm. The full reflector assembly willbe designed and built. Functional testing, including deployment repeatability and shape accuracy will be performed.Hardware to be produced during this activity are:- Breadboards for verification of functional and environmental requirements (including Earth Observation applications)- Demonstrator model of representative quality for a flight demonstrator, to be tested for deployment functionsand main critical environments.It is foreseen that the full testing (RF, structural, environmental) and eventual refurbishment forEQM or PFM will be covered in another activity.

title: LISA-ITT-009 Battery
description:
The gravitational wave observatory LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) has been selected as ESA’s third large class mission (L-3) within the Cosmic Vision programme. LISA’s mission objective is to observe gravitational waves from space in the frequency band of 0.1 mHz to 1 Hz, not accessible from ground-based observatories. 
The mission architecture consists of a constellation of three spacecraft placed at the vertexes of a near-equilateral triangle with side length of about 2.5 million km (LISA Constellation). An overview of the LISA mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/LISA
OHB, prime contractor for the programme, has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the LISA programme, building the industrial consortium.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the LISA Battery.
The battery is part of the LISA Electrical Power Subsystem (EPS). The battery will be rechargeable Li-Ion type battery. This battery will supply the spacecraft with electrical energy when Solar Array power is not available or not sufficient, mainly during launch and transfer phases and during eclipse phases of the satellite. The satellite will be launched with a fully charged battery in order to be able to support the transfer and LEOP scenario until the solar array has been deployed.
The procurement of the Battery will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements. Additional requirements on geo-return may be specified in the ITT data package.

title: Automation of MultiSensor Turret (TMS) ( B11 )
description:
CNES-CSG wants to digitalize its activities in order to :
•	Reduce reconfiguration delay in between two launches
•	Maintenance and Operation reduction costs
•	Turn the CSG into an attractive spot for new space operators
•	Improve space base availability
•	Daily life improvement and simplification

Description

CNES has optical facilities to follow the launchers after their lift off, for technical and media purposes.
They consist in visible and infrared video cameras, mounted on a turret, called TMS (Multisensor turret). CNES has several TMS.

Up to now, TMS are hand controlled by one or several operators who perform camera configuration and hand follow-up of the launchers

The aim of this activity is to modernize or replace these TMS in order to make them fully remote controlled:
-	Remote set-up
-	Auto-tracking of the launcher

These TMS will be design to endure French Guyana climatic conditions.
In option these TMS will made easily transportable.

Inputs will consist in a requirement specification or a technical specification
Deliveries will consist in one or several automatized TMS, operationally qualified.

title: ARGONAUT – S-Band Medium Gain Antenna Assembly  (S-MGAA)
description:
OHB System AG, a subsidiary of the European space and technology group OHB SE, is acting as subcontractor to Thales Alenia Space (TAS-I) who has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) as prime Contractor for the realization of the ARGONAUT mission. Under its subcontract, OHB is responsible for the EPS, TT&C and GNC subsystems up to flight readiness. 
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the Argonaut LDE S-Band Medium Gain Antenna Assembly (S-MGAA). As part of the TT&C subsystem, the S-MGAA is responsible to provide a directional S-band communication link with the relay satellite enabling the LDE to transmit telemetry, video, and receive commands while maintaining antenna pointing toward the relay satellite.

title: ARGONAUT – E-Pump Switch Box (ESB)
description:

OHB System AG, a subsidiary of the European space and technology group OHB SE, is acting as subcontractor to Thales Alenia Space (TAS-I) who has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) as prime Contractor for the realization of the ARGONAUT Lunar Descent Element (LDE). Under its subcontract, OHB is responsible for the EPS, TT&C and GNC subsystems up to flight readiness.

title: EnVision – Radiator Panel
description:
EnVision is a Venus orbiter mission selected by ESA’s Science Programme Committee as the fifth Medium-class mission in the Agency’s Cosmic Vision plan. It will be the first mission to investigate Venus from its inner core to its upper atmosphere, characterising the interaction between its atmosphere, surface/subsurface and interior. It aims at providing a holistic view of Venus, studying the planet’s history, activity, and climate. EnVision is an ESA-led mission in partnership with NASA who are providing the VenSAR instrument, Deep Space Network support for critical mission phases and Aerobraking support.
ESA is responsible for the mission, including procurement of the spacecraft and the launch vehicle together with the development of the ground segment (both to control the spacecraft, and for scientific purposes). As with most Science missions, the instruments are provided by Member States and International Partners contributions, with ESA providing several specific payload elements: the SRS dipole antenna; the MRO; the VenSpec-U detectors; the VenSpec-H detector and cooler assembly.
An overview of the EnVision mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/EnVision_factsheet.
Thales Alenia Space Italy, prime contractor for the programme, has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the EnVision Satellite, building an industrial consortium in which OHB System AG, a subsidiary of the European space and technology group OHB SE, is responsible for the MTP-Bus.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the Subcontractor for the EnVision Radiator Panels.
Led by OHB System AG, the Contractor is responsible for the manufacturing of the fully equipped Radiator Panels for the EnVision Spacecraft. Within the Contractor’s responsibility is the application of the thermal hardware (heat pipes, OSRs, etc.), according to the specifications provided by OHB.
The procurement of the Radiator Panels will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).

title: LISA-ITT-070 CFRP Struts
description:
The gravitational wave observatory LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) has been selected as ESA’s third large class mission (L-3) within the Cosmic Vision programme. LISA’s mission objective is to observe gravitational waves from space in the frequency band of 0.1 mHz to 1 Hz, not accessible from ground-based observatories. 
The mission architecture consists of a constellation of three spacecraft placed at the vertexes of a near-equilateral triangle with side length of about 2.5 million km (LISA Constellation). An overview of the LISA mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/LISA
OHB, prime contractor for the programme, has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the LISA programme, building the industrial consortium.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the LISA CFRP Struts.
The CFRP Struts are part of the LISA platform tertiary structure. They connect different mechanical elements and combine metallic end-caps for attachment and a CFRP middle section. The combination of the CFRP section to the metallic end-caps is considered a critical structure technology and will require adequate design and verification or heritage.
The procurement of the CFRP Struts will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements. Additional requirements on geo-return may be specified in the ITT data package.

title: LISA-ITT-067 LCA Integration MGSE
description:
The gravitational wave observatory LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) has been selected as ESA’s third large class mission (L-3) within the Cosmic Vision programme. LISA’s mission objective is to observe gravitational waves from space in the frequency band of 0.1 mHz to 1 Hz, not accessible from ground-based observatories. 
The mission architecture consists of a constellation of three spacecraft placed at the vertexes of a near-equilateral triangle with side length of about 2.5 million km (LISA Constellation). An overview of the LISA mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/LISA
OHB, prime contractor for the programme, has been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the LISA programme, building the industrial consortium.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the LISA LCA Integration MGSE.
The LISA LCA Integration MGSEs shall provide several mechanical elements, such as trolleys and frames, to support the integration of the MOSA into the LCA. It shall enable flexible and safe height adjustment and rotation of the LCA to allow access for AIT operations, as well as provide a stable MGSE structure to support the LCA during test activities.
The MGSEs will be used under ISO 5 cleanliness conditions and in direct contact with high performance optical instruments. Therefore, the GSEs shall ensure full instrument safety, and special care shall be taken in the selection of materials to comply with the magnetic cleanliness requirements of the LISA project.
The procurement of the LCA Integration MGSE will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements. Additional requirements on geo-return may be specified in the ITT data package.

title: EnVision Spacecraft Independent Software Verification and Validation (ISVV)
description:
EnVision is a Venus orbiter mission selected by ESA’s Science Programme Committee as the fifth Medium-class mission in the Agency’s Cosmic Vision plan. It will be the first mission to investigate Venus from its inner core to its upper atmosphere, characterising the interaction between its atmosphere, surface/subsurface and interior. It aims at providing a holistic view of Venus, studying the planet’s history, activity, and climate. An overview of the EnVision mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/EnVision_factsheet.
Thales Alenia Space Italia (TAS-I) is issuing this ITT as EnVision Prime Contractor, and conducting the procurement under the principles of ESA Best Practices for the selection of subcontractors. TAS-I will release an Invitation To Tender for the procurement of the Independent Software Verification and Validation (ISVV).
Independent Software Verification and Validation (ISVV) is an engineering practice intended to improve quality and to reduce development risks of the On-board Software.
The main objective of ISVV activities is to find issues that would really provoke a mission loss, severe mission degradation or major non-compliance to requirements.

This objective will be reached by performing the following main tasks:
•	independently verify the SW components subject of this ISVV contract
•	independently analyze the specifications, the design and justification documents, the source code and test results
•	identifying critical areas
•	proposing validation tests and stress testing on the identified critical areas

title: EnVision Spacecraft System Support for TM/TC Data base preparation
description:
EnVision is a Venus orbiter mission selected by ESA’s Science Programme Committee as the fifth Medium-class mission in the Agency’s Cosmic Vision plan. It will be the first mission to investigate Venus from its inner core to its upper atmosphere, characterising the interaction between its atmosphere, surface/subsurface and interior. It aims at providing a holistic view of Venus, studying the planet’s history, activity, and climate. An overview of the EnVision mission and its objectives can be found on the Agency website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Space_Science/EnVision_factsheet.
Thales Alenia Space Italia (TAS-I) is issuing this ITT as EnVision Prime Contractor, and conducting the procurement under the principles of ESA Best Practices for the selection of subcontractors. TAS-I will release an Invitation To Tender for the procurement of the engineering support for the TM/TC Data Base.
The EnVision TM/TC database (also referred to as Spacecraft Reference Database – SRDB) will be a structured interface layer that enables communication between human operators and the EnVision spacecraft onboard software (SW) in a clear and manageable way, abstracting the complexity of raw binary data.
It provides a comprehensive and organized repository of all Telemetry (TM) and Telecommand (TC) definitions used throughout the mission, in accordance with the ECSS PUS-C standard. This includes parameters, packet structures, formats, units, limits, and relationships, which together define how information is exchanged with the spacecraft. The EnVision TM/TC database structure will be based on the SCOS-2000 standard. 
The selected contractor will be responsible for the management, integration, and formal delivery of all the Envision TM/TC database related products, ensuring compliance with project requirements and quality standards. All the task will be carried out in coordination with the TAS-I team in Turin, providing on-site personnel for all the period of interest.

title: Replacement of Mutualized data network ( D4 )
description:
Context

CNES-CSG wants to digitalize its activities in order to:
•	Reduce reconfiguration delay in between two launches
•	Maintenance and Operation reduction costs
•	Turn the CSG into an attractive spot for new space operators
•	Improve space base availability
•	Daily life improvement and simplification

Description

CNES is responsible for high rate data transport over the whole Space center (600km²) and for every player.
This network is currently based on IP technology on MPLS, using optical fibers (and called CAIMAN)

CNES wants to improve or replace this network to take into account new requirements:
-	reduction of operating costs (licenses cots, administration costs,…)
-	dynamic bandwidth allocation
-	easy interface with future CNES facilities (5G radio network, IoT,…)
-	Connection with new players

The new network will transport current data streams, and will potentially be qualified as SIIV (Vital Information System)

Inputs will consist in a requirement specification or a technical specification
The delivery will be the new network, qualified for operations and sensible data transmission.

title: Republication : Borne FASO 2.0 - work order (DIGIT-A3-)
description:
CNES-CSG intends to renew the system called FASO whose purpose is to edit work request orders for people who have to work on the CSG Space base.
Those work orders are generated from the scheduling and planning tool.

Currently, the system is physically disconnected from the planning tool. This enforce manual exports to specific physical ‘stations’ located at some specific places where each person who is supposed to work on the Space base will retrieve its work order.
When the job is finished, the reporting has to be manually done within the planning tool.

The purpose of the project is to :
•	Automate both import of the work orders and export when the job is completed
•	Allow all industrial partners or temporary workers to access those workorders despite the fact that they are not known on the CNES active directory
•	Allow access to those work orders from mobile devices to facilitate the on site interventions

Delivery will consist in the new FASO system

title: EO Network of Resources 2023-2028 - Best Practices ITT to procure services from resource and platform tier providers
description: Exploitation Platforms are a central element of ESA's Earth Observation (EO) Innovation Europe concept, which aims at the integration of EO data and information for a much broader use, for scientific, social and economic purposes, as well as for the generation of new commercial applications and services. The EO Network of Resources (NoR) initiative promotes the use of European resource and platform services to facilitate a simplified and efficient exploitation of EO data in cloud environments. The initiative incentivizes providers to contribute to a common framework harmonising the access to their services and helping the user to work with the data. RHEA has been awarded the EO Digital Platform – EO Network Of Resources 2023-2028 contract (AO/1-11738/23/I-EF), the follow-up of the project Procurement of Earth Observation Exploitation Platform Network Resource Services (ITT AO/1-9217/18/I-LG) finished in November 2023. RHEA has therefore the mandate to select under the supervision of ESA, and via ESA’s Best Practices Processes, the services of eligible Resource and Platform Tier Providers for the next phase of the Network of Resources. The NoR portal (https://nor-discover.org) lists in an online directory all the onboarded providers together with their NoR service portfolio. ESA can sponsor or co-fund scientists and value adding users for eligible research, development and pre-commercial projects. The portal also provides users with links to each providers helpdesk and website. This intended tender is for the selection of Resource Tier and Platform Tier providers using cloud services with collocated Sentinel and non-Sentinel data. Resource Tier and Platform Tier providers wishing to contribute to the NoR service directory are invited to provide a proposal. Following the previous NoR Open Call, the tender process is made as simple as possible for interested service providers to respond to.

title: Recommissioning of the S3A Facility
description:
The project's objective is to recommission the currently disused S3A building to accommodate empty or fueled payloads before their resume campaigns at the S3B/S1 or S5 EPCUs and/or the EFA.

The objective is to meet the increased production rate at the Launch Base and guarantee the availability of the EPCUs.

 

CNES has defined a payload storage strategy that takes into account the SVG constraints and those related to the overall building rehabilitation.

 

S3A is a former filling and encapsulation building with existing installations and systems:

Propellant retention systems in the highbays
Three cranes in the filling and encapsulation halls
An air conditioning system including a toxic vapor extraction function
An obsolete fluid and air network for operational activities and maintaining the building's airtightness
An obsolete toxic gas treatment system in the filling halls
Technical rooms
 

All of these systems will be upgraded to meet the project's objectives.

title: Drone fleet for CSG Protection and Security (Pre-launch sweep drone – E8) (Doubt removal drone – E6) (Multi-missions drone – C13) (Tethered drone)
description:
Context:
Today's UAVs have increasingly powerful, sophisticated and versatile technological capabilities, which can provide considerable support for surveillance and protection of people, operations and installations.
Given its operational scope, the CSG wishes to use drones for the following activities:
- Sweep the CSG and surrounding area prior rocket launch.
- Clearing up suspicious incidents.
- Tracking transfers and convoys of hazardous materials.
- Atmospheric measurements (toxic and non-toxic gases).
- Supervision during accident response.
Description:
To facilitate systems integration and ensure optimized management of resources during operations, a single ecosystem or architect is envisaged to cover the various missions.
The fleet could include several models (aerial, wired, unmanned ground vehicle, maritime) and different on-board sensors.
The drones can be deployed automatically, but can also be controlled remotely by an authorized pilot at any time.
To facilitate the transmission of instructions to remote areas, and the escalation of alerts, the data flow will be encrypted and retransmitted securely to various points on the CSG:
- Sweep operation: replace the sweep of the CSG and surrounding area currently carried out by helicopter with a plane/drone before each rocket launch. The drone will follow a pre-programmed path, while taking video footage.
- Doubt removal: the drone will travel to the site where the incident has been detected to verify the nature of the situation (in the event of a perimeter alarm being triggered, rapid observation in the event of a particular situation, inspection, etc.).
- Follow-up of transfers and convoys.
- Atmospheric measurements (toxic or non-toxic gases) during launches or for pollution research in the event of an accident.
- Accident response supervision: photo/video recognition, determination of impacted areas, delimitation of perimeters. Reconnaissance around buildings in the event of a crisis, to ensure that people reach a rallying point. Search for victims, debris, demining, post-launch mapping.

Description: Vigil (formerly known as Lagrange), is an ESA Space Safety Programme (S2P) mission dedicated to position a satellite at the Lagrangian point L5 with the objective to perform continuous observations of the Sun and in particular, the space between the Earth and the Sun thereby providing measurement data for operational space weather services.

The current satellites which monitor Space Weather are nearing the end of their life and need to be replaced to ensure continuity of solar observations. These current satellites primarily operate from a science perspective, with the focus on studying the Sun for scientific purposes. However, an operational monitoring capability is now required to ensure accurate and timely forecasts are consistently available to provide advanced warnings of solar activity which threatens Earth, so that appropriate mitigation actions can be taken.

The ESA Vigil Mission will provide operational forecasting from the L5 Lagrange point, whilst a complimentary mission performed by the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration will provide operational forecasting from the L1 Lagrange point.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement of Solar Array by Airbus Defence and Space Ltd as Prime contractor of the Vigil project. The supplier selection will be made in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development (including the required qualification activities), manufacturing, testing and delivery of the Solar Array.

The function of the Solar Array is to generate electrical energy during sunlight periods to be consumed by the spacecraft equipment and instruments and to recharge the battery.

Physically the Solar Array is anticipated to be a single body mounted panel (i.e. non-deployable) unit consisting of:
•	Panel structure;
•	Photo Voltaic Assembly (PVA) on the sun facing side;
•	Thermal hardware to control the temperature;
•	Transfer harness;
•	Thermistors for temperature measurement;
•	Bleed resistors.

The Solar Array shall be delivered as Proto-Flight Model (PFM) which will be used for flight accompanied by a set of MGSE required for spacecraft integration, lifting, handling, etc as specified in the statement of work.

The Invitation To Tender will be addressed to economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose registered office is established in such Member and Associated States which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating State in the ESA Vigil project.

title: Thruster Orientation Mechanism (TOM)
description:
Each LISA TPS will consist of two TOMs, one primary and one redundant. Each TOM will support one HET. The purpose of the TOM is to adjust the orientation of the thruster to precisely align the direction of the force to the centre of mass of the Spacecraft in order to avoid generating disturbance torques when the Hall Effect Thruster is thrusting. This will allow for uncertainties in the position of the spacecraft centre of mass as the Xenon propellant is depleted during orbit raising.
The TOM satisfies three main functions, which are to support the HET, to deploy and drive the thruster position, and to provide the necessary functional links between the HET, xenon flow controller and the spacecraft.
The TOM enables a controlled angular movement of the HET about two orthogonal and independent axes. This commanded position is then held for thruster firing with the TOM actuators in an unpowered mode without back driving. Position control can be by step counting (if stepper motors are used), and absolute position sensors as well as physical end stops are needed
The procurement of the TOM will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements”. Additional requirements on geo-return may be specified in the ITT data package.

The main objective is to upgrade all systems by improving the air cushions movements of the CCU3 in order to increase the flight time necessary to perform docking and undocking operations.
This upgrade will have to increase the reliability of the CCU3.

title: Rehabilitation of S5 maintenance workshop
description:
The S5C maintenance workshop no longer meets the functional needs and ergonomic, technical, or safety requirements of the activities carried out there.

It is composed of two enclosed, air-conditioned spaces used for storing small electrical and mechanical equipment, maintenance operations and training new staff.

It also consists of a semi-open space that is the heart of mechanical maintenance activities, particularly for work on equipment related to payloads. It contains fixed machine tools, workbenches, and several storage cabinets.

Finally, above these two areas, there is an open space for storing furniture and bulky equipment.

It is therefore necessary to redesign these three areas of the workshop in order to respond more effectively and efficiently to electrical and mechanical maintenance needs, the training of new operators, and the storage of equipment on the upper floor, which we wish to close in an air-conditioned environment.

title: ESPRIT WIT ECLSS Air Check Valve (ACV)
description:
The Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The Gateway – European System Providing Refueling Infrastructure and Telecommunication (ESPRIT) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with refueling, logistic and telecommunication functions (this latter function will be provided with a different element that will reach Gateway at a different time). The ESPRIT includes contributions from USA, and Canada. 
The ESPRIT WIT is the Windowed Infrastructure Tunnel devoted to the logistic and circular viewport functions, in addition to the Primary Structural function of the complete system.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the development and qualification of the ECLSS Air Check Valve (ACV) in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).
The Air Check Valve (ACV) is part of the Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS). 
ACV is a mechanical valve installed downstream of the Cabin Fan and it provides a reverse pressure protection in the environmental system supply. 
Being the CFAs cold redundant units, the Air Check Valve avoids unwanted backflow through the still fan and, of course, in case that the fan is not operating due to a failure. 
The ACV consists of a simple butterfly valve that opens when the air flows through the fan and remains closed when the fan is not operating. 
Its definition, development, qualification and the procurement of the equipment represent the object of the present tender.
Further information concerning the ESPRIT campaign can be found on the Agency’s website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon. 
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

title: TRUTHS PHASE AdvC/C/D - Invitation to tender: Payload Monitoring & Control System (PMCS)
description:
TRUTHS (Traceable Radiometry Underpinning Terrestrial- and Helio- Studies) is an element of the European Earth Watch Programme.

TRUTHS will help deliver improved confidence in Earth Observation (EO) data gathered from space and the forecasts driven by this data.
This mission will enable the upgrade of the performance of the EO system, both in space and on the ground. The mission will facilitate the development of a global, climate observatory, delivering data of unprecedented accuracy with SI traceability - establishing a 'standards laboratory in space'.

TRUTHS was authorised at ESA CMin22 for a Phase B2/Advance C, whereas the continuation of the mission through Phase C/D-E1 is subject to further approval at ESA CMin25.
In this framework, Airbus Defence and Space Ltd will release an Invitation To Tender for the procurement of the PMCS HW and SW for the TRUTHS Phase Advance C (1 year), with a mandatory option for Phase C/D. 

Procurement of PMCS will be split into two parts:
1. PMCS HW, which includes the models, the Boot Loader Software (BSW) and the hardware dependant software (HDSW))
2. PMCS Application Software (ASW)
The tenderer can decide to submit an offer for any of the two parts (HW or ASW) as well as for both (HW + ASW).

The Invitation To Tender will be addressed to all ESA Member States, since the geographical return of the mission is subject to change at ESA CMin25.

description:

The renovation of these systems is necessary for the operation of the launch base. That could involve the extension of the campus network of the CSG : CAIMAN (Carrier MAN).
The existing networks to be extended are exclusively IP/Ethernet networks. CNES wishes to supply and install equipment to extend these existing networks. The final setup of equipment will be carried out by the CSG operator. 
Some remote sites need the deployment of a specific solution (i.e. : wifi bridge, FH, 4G/5G internet access, …)

title: Rehabilitation of the office area at S3F
description:
The increased frequency of Ariane and Vega launches will swiftly highlight the necessity for greater customer availability and office reception capacity for teams engaged in campaign activities. In line with the current expansion, we have identified the necessity to upgrade the S3 area, which would enable the execution of additional satellite campaigns at the EPCU S3B.

In order to meet these needs, it is necessary to replace the existing customer office area at S3F with a new office building. This will modernise the current bungalows, which are no longer suitable for hosting satellite customers. The objective is to be able to host several satellite customer teams simultaneously.

The reception of satellite customers and the management of activities in the S3 zone also require the rehabilitation of the site manager's coordination office in order to supervise the enlarged S3 zone with the ZSE/ZSP.

All of these activities also induce the creation of the PPE store, with the aim of providing local support for operations throughout the S3 and ZSE/ZSP zones.

We are therefore expecting an office area to be set up for satellite customers, EPCU agents, and anyone else who needs to work in the S3 zone, with efficient logistics flows in line with the growth of activity in this zone.

title: ARGONAUT LDE – Life Cycle Analysis [LCA]
description:
Argonaut LDE (previously named EL3, European Large Logistics Lander), is one of the keystones of the “Terrae Novae” exploration capabilities presented at Council Meeting 2022. Argonaut LDE aims at enabling a substantial and sustained European presence on the surface of the Moon ensuring Europe remains a key player in space exploration. Argonaut LDE aims at providing an autonomous European capability for regular large robotic surface missions for an extended duration. This provides the possibility to conduct independent missions if required as well as being a significant and visible contribution to the international sustainable exploration of the lunar surface.

The mission is designed to support both human and robotic exploration by providing a multipurpose lander known as the Lunar Descent Element (LDE):

•	Lunar Descent Element (LDE): 
o	A recurring lander, common to all ARGONAUT LDE missions. 
o	Designed to be compatible with different delivery missions without undergoing modifications; 
o	The LDE provides the functions of Payload transport to the Moon’s surface as well as the main mission functions common to all the different missions. 

The LDE is equipped to deliver various payloads through a mission-specific interface, typically referred to as the Cargo Platform Element (CPE). For the purpose of clarity the CPE and the related Payload are subject to a separate procurement under ESA’s responsibility. 
Thales Alenia Space Italy, have been Contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the Argonaut Lunar Descent Element (LDE) which will be used for the first mission in 2031. 

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the Argonaut LDE - Life Cycle Analysis (LCA)

The procurement of the LCA studies will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

The start of the present ITT is scheduled no earlier than beginning of September 2025.

title: S3 zone air network segregation
description:
A 7 bar air production station now meets the compressed air needs of several geographical areas, bringing together the establishments of Regulus, Europropulsion, ArianeGroup, Avio-G, Air Liquide Spatial Guyane, Arianespace, BEAP, ZSE, ZSP and S3 Zone.
As part of the arrival of new launch operators and the transfer of ownership of certain areas to CNES, it has become necessary to rethink the 7 bar air production/distribution network in order to guarantee a clear and equitable distribution in terms of operation, investment, consumption and maintenance, for all subscribers.
The main objective of the project is to create independent air production and distribution for the areas operated by CNES CSG, namely the ZSE, the ZSP and the S3 zone. The new installations should allow CNES to control outages for its own maintenance needs and thus limit the operational impact. CNES's responsibility for network maintenance will also be limited to the areas operated by CNES.
To achieve this, a mastery of the current network is necessary, and a map of the air network will be established in order to identify, in particular, the dead branches to be isolated or put into hibernation. The solutions chosen to meet the need will have to take into account a general upgrade of the network in the identified areas.

description:
In the framework of its activities at the Guiana Space Center (CSG), CNES must renew one 30 meters Truck-Mounted Aerial Platform. This truck allows to access equipment at height.

The truck, which is the subject of this pre-publication, must have the following equipment to perform its main functions:

30-meters working-height aerial platform mounted on a 4×2 truck chassis.
Diesel engine delivering at least 180 HP for reliable performance.
Articulating boom with multi-joint design for maximum reach and flexibility.
Platform capacity of 230 kg to safely carry two operators and tools.
Hydraulic outriggers with automatic leveling for fast, stable setup.
Joystick controls in both basket and base for precise movement.
Safety features including overload cutoff, fall arrest anchor points, and emergency descent.
Operator cab with air conditioning, ergonomic seat, and wide-angle viewing windows.
Tropical-grade cooling system, corrosion-resistant paint, and sealed electrical components.
Supplier to offer OEM parts support, local service network, stocked spares, and full warranty

title: ARGONAUT LDE – Quick passivation system design
description:
Argonaut LDE (previously named EL3, European Large Logistics Lander), is one of the keystones of the “Terrae Novae” exploration capabilities presented at Council Meeting 2022. Argonaut LDE aims at enabling a substantial and sustained European presence on the surface of the Moon ensuring Europe remains a key player in space exploration. Argonaut LDE aims at providing an autonomous European capability for regular large robotic surface missions for an extended duration. This provides the possibility to conduct independent missions if required as well as being a significant and visible contribution to the international sustainable exploration of the lunar surface.

The mission is designed to support both human and robotic exploration by providing a multipurpose lander known as the Lunar Descent Element (LDE):

•	Lunar Descent Element (LDE): 
o	A recurring lander, common to all ARGONAUT LDE missions. 
o	Designed to be compatible with different delivery missions without undergoing modifications; 
o	The LDE provides the functions of Payload transport to the Moon’s surface as well as the main mission functions common to all the different missions. 

The LDE is equipped to deliver various payloads through a mission-specific interface, typically referred to as the Cargo Platform Element (CPE). For the purpose of clarity the CPE and the related Payload are subject to a separate procurement under ESA’s responsibility. 
Thales Alenia Space Italy, have been Contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the Argonaut Lunar Descent Element (LDE) which will be used for the first mission in 2031. 
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the Argonaut LDE Quick passivation system design.

For safety reasons, the LDE shall provide quick passivation function of propellant tanks to avoid hypergolic explosion in case of accidental events. 
The passivation system shall work in all the mission phases, starting from launch through the spacecraft mission (once separated from the LV), until Lunar orbit insertion.

The main critical aspect is related to the timeframe and the reaction time needed, which is in the order of ms for the first mission phases, and seconds during third stage LV phase and space mission. 
The Contractor main tasks are :
• Perform trade-offs and analysis to evaluate and recommend the design solutions/architecture to ensure timely passivation of the Tanks.
• Highlight any aspect related to operational safety constraints.
• Prepare the documentation necessary to justify the test conditions, if any, established for development/qualification tests on Earth and correlation of the results with the corresponding environmental conditions seen by LDE in the realistic worst-case scenario.

The procurement of the Primary and Secondary Structures will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.
