title: ESPRIT WIT Launch Vehicle Adapter (LVA)
description:
The Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The Gateway – European System Providing Refueling Infrastructure and Telecommunication (ESPRIT) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with refueling, logistic and telecommunication functions (this latter function will be provided with a different element that will reach Gateway at a different time). The ESPRIT includes contributions from USA, and Canada. 
The ESPRIT WIT is the Windowed Infrastructure Tunnel devoted to the logistic and circular viewport functions, in addition to the Primary Structural function of the complete system.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the development and qualification of the window panes coatings in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2).

The Launch Vehicle Adapter (LVA) is a structural element, physically part of the ERM WIT Primary Structure, which shall ensure the fulfillment of the following main functions:

•	Provide the interface between the ERM WIT and the SLS adapter, adjusting the WIT diameter to the one of the Launcher adapter.
•	Provide the interface between the ERM WIT and the ERM UMAXT.

The LVA is a roll-forged truncated cone made of Titanium (Ti6Al4V), that shall be designed in order to guarantee both mechanical and thermal performances to meet the above functions.
Moreover its structure presents several holes in order to provide the piping and harness routing from the active IBDM to other services.

Further information concerning the ESPRIT campaign can be found on the Agency’s website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon. 
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

title: Replacement of CSG telemetry antennas 2026 to 2031
description:
The downrange stations are an essential element during the launcher mission as they ensure the launcher-to-ground communication links capability. Ever since the beginning, the CSG Range has been implementing a network of downrange telemetry stations to support Ariane and then Vega launches.
This project consists in the replacement of aged large antennas in a gradual approach, beginning with the SNA Stella 35 and then continuing with others (eg. Galliot’s or Bermuda’s ones). This replacement is now essential to maintain CSG Range availability. To optimize costs, the approach consists in proposing a set of identical and smaller antennas (diameter about 4m), allowing a predictive maintenance policy to come.

This project consists in the replacement of aged large antennas in a gradual approach, beginning with the SNA Stella 35 and then continuing with others (eg. Galliot’s or Bermuda’s ones). This replacement is now essential to maintain CSG Range availability. To optimize costs, the approach consists in proposing a set of identical and smaller antennas (diameter about 4m), allowing a predictive maintenance policy to come.

title: Bermuda station evolution toward permanent configuration - power supply equipment
description:
Since 2011, CSG range has been operating the transportable station in Bermuda for launches featuring northward trajectory which steadily increased since. The evolution of the Bermuda station towards a permanent configuration is an essential element to ensure its availability and reliability for launches as well as an optimized maintenance.
Beside the use of an area dedicated to ESA/CNES in the Bermudian building, the installation in the latter of the telemetry system racks and the approaching of the antenna, this development will require the renewal of the entire energy configuration (power supply generator, inverter units, transformer etc..)
This activity does not include the replacement of the antenna which is covered by another Tender Action.

title: Renewal of the work request orders
description:
CNES-CSG intends to renew the system called FASO whose purpose is to edit work request orders for people who have to work on the CSG Space base.
Those work orders are generated from the scheduling and planning tool.

Currently, the system is physically disconnected from the planning tool. This enforce manual exports to specific physical ‘stations’ located at some specific places where each person who is supposed to work on the Space base will retrieve its work order.
When the job is finished, the reporting has to be manually done within the planning tool.

The purpose of the project is to :
•	Automate both import of the work orders and export when the job is completed
•	Allow all industrial partners or temporary workers to access those workorders despite the fact that they are not known on the CNES active directory
•	Allow access to those work orders from mobile devices to facilitate the on site interventions

Delivery will consist in the new FASO system

title: Services provider tool for spacecraft campaign
description:
The aim is to set a tool for digitalizing and centralizing all the requests produced during a campaign. The tool will materialize CSG services through a digital catalogue for launch operators and satellite customers. Customers will be able to submit their requests directly via an ergonomic interface, so that they can be automatically redirected to the right internal contact.

At the Guiana Space Centre, there is currently no tool for creating, tracking or tracing a service request during launch campaign. Requests are made orally, by email or by message, resulting in a lack of follow-up and traceability. Satellite customers have no visibility of CSG's internal organization to direct their requests to the various responsible of activity.

The tool will save time at all levels and improve operational efficiency and user experience.

title: Vigil - Simulator Front End (SimFE)
description:
Vigil (formerly known as Lagrange), is an ESA Space Safety Programme (S2P) mission dedicated to position a satellite at the Lagrangian point L5 with the objective to perform continuous observations of the Sun and in particular, the space between the Earth and the Sun thereby providing measurement data for operational space weather services.
The current satellites which monitor Space Weather are nearing the end of their life and need to be replaced to ensure continuity of solar observations. These current satellites primarily operate from a science perspective, with the focus on studying the Sun for scientific purposes. However, an operational monitoring capability is now required to ensure accurate and timely forecasts are consistently available to provide advanced warnings of solar activity which threatens Earth, so that appropriate mitigation actions can be taken.
The ESA Vigil Mission will provide operational forecasting from the L5 Lagrange point, whilst a complimentary mission performed by the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration will provide operational forecasting from the L1 Lagrange point.
This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement of the Vigil Simulator Front End (SimFE) Airbus Defence and Space Ltd as Prime contractor of the Vigil project. The supplier selection will be made in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The scope of this procurement covers the full development, manufacturing, test and delivery of the SimFE equipment, which when added to Real Time Simulator (RTS) shall form the Real Time Simulation Environment (RTE) used for the Vigil space system development and verification including On-Board Software verification and validation.
The SimFE itself shall provide electrical interfacing between the RTS and real hardware that form the Electrical Functional Model (EFM) or Proto-Flight Model (PFM) of the Vigil spacecraft system and is capable of providing front-end analogue, digital, data power and command interfaces, to either Payload instruments, communications module and on-board computer, and further AOCS subsystem, Antenna Pointing Mechanisms Electronics and Data Handling subsystem.
The Invitation To Tender will be addressed to economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose registered office is established in such Member and Associated States which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating State in the ESA Vigil project.

title: 5G data Network ( D11 )
description:
Context

CNES-CSG wants to digitalize its activities in order to :
•	Reduce reconfiguration delay in between two launches
•	Maintenance and Operation reduction costs
•	Turn the CSG into an attractive spot for new space operators
•	Improve space base availability
•	Daily life improvement and simplification

Description

CNES is responsible for networks of the Space Center. So he has to improve current facilities to ensure a connectivity:
-	High rate for most of the users
-	Covering the whole Space Center (600 km²), with various data rates, allowing no dead area
-	With other CNES network: ground transport: network, WiFi,….

This new radio data network will have to be compliant with new 5G standard
It will be possible to use in place infrastructure (pylons)

Inputs will consist in:
-	a requirement specification or a technical specification
-	the results of a POC (proof of concept) to be done in S1 2023 in order to validate the technology and the functionalities that will be delivered on the space base, if available.
The current request will be to generalize the principles that will be validated during the Proof of concept to deploy the 5G all over the Space center

The expected performance will consist in deploying on the overall space base the 5G technology and assist the CNES CSG teams so that the system could be locally administrate during the run phase

title: Lunar i-hab –  Test Facility ITT
description:
The Cislunar Gateway – International Habitat (Lunar I-HAB) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2028. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the Contractor for the Test Facility Services, to be supplied in the framework of the I-Hab environmental test campaign, and for the procurement of the Mechanical Test Adapter.
During this test campaign, I-Hab will undergo two main environmental tests, sinusoidal and acoustic vibrations, and several other mechanical, fluidic and functional verifications. The Contractor is requested to provide all support services, facilities, equipment, material, personnel and documentation needed to perform or support the activities specified in ITT data package 
Moreover, the Contractor is responsible for the procurement of the Mechanical Test Adapter (MTA), the GSE used as interface between I-Hab and relevant test machines and facilities.

Further information concerning the Cislunar Gateway and the ESA contributions can be found on the Agency’s website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

title: Propellant Tank
description: The Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft. The Gateway – European System Providing Refueling Infrastructure and Telecommunication (ESPRIT) is ESA’s c ontribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with refueling, logistic and telecommunication functions (this latter function will be provided with a different element that will reach Gateway at a different time). The ESPRIT includes contributions from USA, and Canada. Thales Alenia Space UK as a core team member, and Thales Alenia Space France, prime contractor for the programme, have been contracted by the European Space Agency (ESA) for the realization of the ESPRIT module for the new Lunar Orbital Platform Gateway. Under a subcontract, Thales Alenia Space UK is responsible for the Bi-Propellant Transfer system (BTS), a system refuelling the chemical propulsion system of the Lunar Gateway. The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the subcontractor for the Propellant Tank in the subsystem in propellant transfer, pressurisation and venting operations. The procurement of the Propellant Tank will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65, rev.2). Further information concerning the ESPRIT campaign can be found on the Agency´s website here: https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon. title: TRUTHS PHASE B2 - Invitation to tender: OPTICS SLIT
description:
TRUTHS (Traceable Radiometry Underpinning Terrestrial- and Helio- Studies) is an Element of the European Earth Watch Programme approved at 178th PB-EO (ESA/PB-EO(2019)31) for submission at CM19+ as a new Element, called “TRUTHS”. 
TRUTHS (Traceable Radiometry Underpinning Terrestrial- and Helio- Studies – is an operational climate mission, aiming to enhance by an order-of-magnitude our ability to estimate the Earth radiation budget through direct measurements and to establish a ‘metrology laboratory in space’ to create a fiducial (International System of units - SI traceable) reference data set to cross-calibrate other sensors and improve the quality of their measurements.
·The TRUTHS Mission aims at measuring the incoming & outgoing energy from the climate system, including the spectral fingerprint needed to observationally attribute climate processes, with an accuracy needed to detect climate trends in the shortest possible time.

Airbus Defence and Space has been selected by ESA as the Prime Contractor for Phase B2 with a mandatory option for Advance C.
In this framework, Airbus Defence and Space Ltd will release an Invitation To Tender for the procurement of the Slit for the TRUTHS Phase B2. 
Supplier to confirm manufacturability of a high precision slit of 18micron width and 36 mm length to be machined into a foil material (0.5-1.0mm). The slit is to be used in a satellite optical instrument. Then to characterize the edge roughness and shape, flatness of the edges (to ensure all edges within a single plane), 2D shape accuracy achievable (straightness) and ability to control coating and finishing techniques for straylight reduction.

title: TRUTHS PHASE B2 - OPTICS ARC (Anti reflective coating)
description:
TRUTHS (Traceable Radiometry Underpinning Terrestrial- and Helio- Studies) is an Element of the European Earth Watch Programme approved at 178th PB-EO (ESA/PB-EO(2019)31) for submission at CM19+ as a new Element, called “TRUTHS”. 
TRUTHS (Traceable Radiometry Underpinning Terrestrial- and Helio- Studies – is an operational climate mission, aiming to enhance by an order-of-magnitude our ability to estimate the Earth radiation budget through direct measurements and to establish a ‘metrology laboratory in space’ to create a fiducial (International System of units - SI traceable) reference data set to cross-calibrate other sensors and improve the quality of their measurements.
The TRUTHS Mission aims at measuring the incoming & outgoing energy from the climate system, including the spectral fingerprint needed to observationally attribute climate processes, with an accuracy needed to detect climate trends in the shortest possible time.
The TRUTHS Mission has been authorised as part of the European Earth Watch Programme [ESA/PB-EO(2022)18 rev1] to start its Phase B2/Advance C implementation while authorisation to implement Phase C/D/E1 is subject to the availability of funding and authorisation at C-MiN 2025. 
Airbus Defence and Space has been selected by ESA as the Prime Contractor for Phase B2 with a mandatory option for Advance C.
In this framework, Airbus Defence and Space Ltd will release an Invitation To Tender for the procurement of an optical anti-reflective coating for the TRUTHS Phase B2.
The scope of work is to perform a study of multi layered ARC coating operating between 320 nm and 2400 nm and deposited on curved glass substrates to minimise reflectivity considering provided angular ranges, to reduce polarisation sensitivity and to minimise scatter losses. 
Based on the successful results of this study, it will be requested to coat and test some flat samples using the preferred ARC coating, before and after the operational space environment (i.e. thermo-mechanical and radiation), to achieve TRL 6. Should the results be unsuccessful the work will cease at the end of the study. 
The Invitation To Tender will be addressed to economic operators (including those deemed to act as Subcontractors) whose registered office is established in such Member and Associated States which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating State in the ESA TRUTHS Mission. 
To date, these are: Czech Republic, Greece, Romania, Spain, Switzerland, United Kingdom.

title: Construction of a awning adjacent to the S5C Transit Hall
description:
For few years, there has been a lack of space for Payload containers, Payload and Launchers equipment, as well as Payload Facilities mobile equipment. 
In order to respond to the need of flexibility, we must increase the storage space available protected from bad weather. That’s why we would like to have an awning adjacent to the S5C Transit Hall.
The objective is to cover an sufficiently large space so that various equipment could be stored, protected and handled. The project would require prerequisites regarding earthworks and foundations for the addition of a metal frame superstructure with cladding cover.

title: Towards Flexible Payload Processing Facilities at the European Spaceport
description:
in the framework of the satellites preparation activities at the Guiana Space Center (CSG), CNES must be able to adapt its payload processing facilities in order to support the preparation of a wide range of satellites (from cubesat to telecommunication satellites of several tons).

This project includes several perimeters, such as:

Power distribution
- Adapt the power supply installations in the clean halls and the checkout rooms to provide uninterrupted power supply through multiple types of sockets.

Mechanical means
- Provide the Payload Facilities with dedicated mobile cranes used inside the clean halls for small satellites.

- Partitioning of the clean halls : supply the clean halls with movable walls

- Working stations : worktables and dedicated means for smallsat projects

Telecommunication
- Connection to the CSG network from the Payload Facility

- Direct communication between the clean halls and the checkout rooms

- Provide the clean halls and the checkout rooms with screens able to display the relevant information for the teams working inside

Offices and infrastructures
- Storage area with A/C system (> 150 m²)

- Break rooms for satellite teams

Competencies :

Telecommunications and network
Power distribution
Mechanics
Infrastructure works
Miscellaneous :

- 4 to 6 different clean rooms (3 buildings) and associated facilities are targeted

- Estimated schedule : 2025 to 2027

- Contracts attribution distributed by WP

title: S3B cloakrooms upgrades
description:
The S3B location accomodates payloads in ISO 8 cleanroom. In order to preserve this environment, cleanliness specifications require that accesses [cloakrooms + material airlock] S3B HR and HN cleanrooms are upgraded to best meet the ISO 8 access standard.

The objective of this work is to upgrade the access areas (cloakrooms and material airlock) of the S3B to allow passage of equipment and all persons authorized to access it in accordance with the ISO 8 standard. title: Modification of the EPCU S1A airlock
description:
The EPCU S1A is a High Bay that can accommodate payloads in compliance with the ISO 8 cleanliness standard.
In order to access the High Bay without compromising the ISO 8 cleanliness standard, it is composed of two airlocks, one allowing transfers of payloads/equipment and the other dedicated exclusively to materials. 
Given the diversity of payload sizes, we need to adapt our facilities and optimise operational processes to accommodate different types of payload.
The aim of this work is to modify the airlock dedicated to materials into an airlock that meets the defined requirements to enable the arrival and transfer of payloads and equipment.

title: Refurbishment and improvement of the S5E location
description:
The S5E is a location dedicated to the maintenance of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) such as textile clothing, Personal Breathing Apparatus, scape operator, hoses or air bottles. All of this equipment is available to satellite customers and all users of the launch base. Today, the building no longer meets the ergonomic requirements and is not adapted to the cleanliness requirements that must be met by the revalidation flows of equipment used in clean rooms.
The objective of the proposed work is to refurbish the entire S5E location to improve the ergonomics and working conditions of operators, optimize revalidation times and create a flow of traffic where 'clean and revalidated' PPE do not use the same circuit as 'used-dirty' PPE.

title: ExoMars - Rosalind Franklin Mission (EXM-RFM): Invitation to Tender for Isolation Valves
description: The Rosalind Franklin Mission represents the continuation of ESA’s ExoMars programme following the breakup of the inter-Agency agreement with Roscosmos. As such, it replaces the previous Rover & Surface Platform Mission. The main objectives of the Rosalind Franklin Mission are to safely land on the Mars surface, collect and analyse in situ a range of Martian surface and subsurface soil samples, and to demonstrate technologies for planetary exploration. The key elements of the ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover are its advanced drilling system, coupled with a sophisticated on-board science laboratory, and its capability to move autonomously on a variety of terrains on Mars’ surface for at least 218 sols (8 months). Sampling down to a depth of 2 metres significantly increases the probability to detect preserved signs of past or even present life. The analysis of soil geo-chemistry will provide a detailed characterisation of the environment and geological history, and possibly provide evidence for the presence of organic compounds. The ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover will be placed on the surface of Mars by an Entry, Descent and Landing Module (EDLM). This module is the main new developmental element of the ExoMars-Rosalind Franklin mission and will require key contributions from European suppliers. The so-called “braking engines” will be provided by NASA as Customer Furnished Items (CFIs). The Rover System comprises the ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover Module and the Rover Operations Control Centre (ROCC), the latter developed by and located at ALTEC in Torino (Italy), where the ground operations of the Rover surface mission will be performed. The Rover and its payload will require maintenance and some upgrades to manage obsolescence and ensure compliance with the new mission requirements associated with the 2028 launch scenario. The ‘Rosalind Franklin’ Rover will benefit from the provision by NASA of Radio-Isotope Heating Units (RHUs). These RHUs are required to support the thermal control system of the Rover, replacing similar units previously provided by Roscosmos. The new flight system also requires the maintenance of the existing Carrier Module and of the Descent Module equipment and subsystems already developed by ESA. The launch services (launcher and launch site facilities) will also be provided by NASA. Airbus Defence and Space Ltd is the Lead Contractor for the Landing Platform Mechanical Thermal and Propulsion System (“MTPS”). As part of their scope of work, Airbus will release an Invitation to Tender (ITT) looking for a supplier of the Propulsion Isolation Valves. The Landing Platform will require at least 6 Propulsion Isolation Valves which will be used on the propulsion system.

title: Automatic Number-Plate Recognition (E9)
description:
Context:
The visual verification of vehicle badges at CSG does not provide a sufficiently high level of security for access control. An automated license plate check should be set up at access points.
Description:
When approaching the barrier, the system must automatically recognize a vehicle's license plate and check whether it is authorized to enter the site. Controls must be automatic and instantaneous, with no need for the security guard to intervene, thus ensuring greater fluidity and efficiency.
In conjunction with the digital access control system, which efficiently verifies the identity of those on board, access can be authorized and the access barrier lifted.

description:
In the context of CSG’s Digitalization process whose goal is to :
•	Reduce re configuration delay in between two launches
•	Operation reduction costs
•	Maintenance reduction costs
•	Turn the CSG into an attractive spot for new space operators
•	Improve space base availability
•	Daily life improvement and simplification
•	Ensure Space base industrial partners workflow transversality
•	Rejuvenate and modernize the CSG’s image

The CSG will capitalize on the basis that were set by the ‘Socle Numérique Transverse (SNT)’ project in order to bring a brand new Information System.

The digitalization will use this pedestal so that a major part of the projects that will contribute to reach this target could be in line with what had been fulfilled by the CSG-NG. All those projects will be designed, thought, manufactured and deployed in order to reach those objectives

title: CSG’s Digitalization - Radar and Launcher Simulation topic
description:
In the context of CSG’s Digitalization process whose goal is to :
•	Reduce re configuration delay in between two launches
•	Maintenance and Operation reduction costs
•	Turn the CSG into an attractive spot for new space operators
•	Improve space base availability
•	Daily life improvement and simplification
The CSG will capitalize on the basis that was set by the ‘Socle Numérique Transverse (SNT)’ project in order to bring a brand new Information System.
The global scope that the digitalization services must address are:
•	Satellites’ and launch campaigns operations
•	Maintenance and sustainability (in line with the SNT project)
•	CSG’s space base Infrastructures (physical, software or virtual) (mainly for networks and informatics)
•	Security, Safety and protection 
•	Daily life improvement and simplification
•	Communication
•	Datacenters
•	Projects valorization and marketability
•	Process improvements and optimization
•	Radars and Simulations
In order to match those needs, the project teams will be organized according to the following topics:
•	IT Networks
•	Planification and Task/Operation management
•	Maintenance management
•	Technical fact management
•	Data management
•	IT Hardware
•	Right profile and access management
•	Safety and Security
•	Information Broadcast
•	Radar and Launcher Simulation
Two transversal teams will be in charge of the global consistency of the projects for planning and architectural/urbanization purposes
 This publication concerns the Radar and Launcher Simulation topic
The expected services provision for each of those items are:
•	Architecture and urbanization of the systems, taken into account Maintenance and optimizations 
•	Project Management officer. Projects will have to be managed through a project’s portfolio. Team guidance for steps definition and planning formalization, accurate indicators follow up.
•	Requirements analysis and formalization of the projects that will be designed to meet those requirements.
•	Project owner support for specification redaction for each identified project, document redaction and accurate technical descriptions 
•	Market surveys and state of art
•	Analysis reports of studied solutions
•	Proof of concept based on the solution identified and validation
•	Project management for design, development, implementation and deployment of the identified projects
•	Providing the solutions and implements them (could be external solutions of specialized editors and vendors)
•	Support and coaching for information security analysis 
•	On-site installation (when necessary) and global system technical validation. The holder of the contract will be responsible of the supplies that will be plugged with CNES CSG’s equipment.
•	Training of the staff that will be in charge of the exploitation of the systems to ensure its autonomy
•	Users and administrators training.
•	Ensure the maintainability and the sustainability of the systems and projects 
•	Ensure knowledge transfer and reversibility to the CNES teams in order to ensure the ability to keep going with Project management, urbanization and mastering the new deployed tools 
These services therefore provide the entire life cycle of the projects that will arise from each of the topic.
All items will have to be compliant with CNES CSG's context and constraints
Although this publication is specific to a given topic, the tenderer must ensure the mutual consistency of the projects. He will have to coordinate with the teams in charge of planning and the overall architecture of the systems.

title: Replace the video wall of its Safety Coordination Office (BCS), of its Crisis Room and its Security PC
description:
The Guiana Space Center, Europe’s Spaceport - CNES, located in Kourou in French Guiana, wishes to replace the video wall of its Safety Coordination Office (BCS), of its Crisis Room and its Security PC. 
- With regards to the BCS: The objective of this replacement is to have a system similar to the current one but with screens adopting current technology and with the availability of long-term spare parts stocks. This wall, made up of one or more elements will have a size of 3mx5m.
- With regards to the crisis room: the objective of this replacement is to have a system similar in terms of equipment to that of the BCS. The wall will be smaller in size 2mx3m, will be able to receive preselected images from the BCS image wall. It will be able to display at least 6 to 8 images from different sources.
- With regards to the PC Security video wall: The objective of this replacement is to have a system similar to the current one. The wall will be smaller in size 2mx3m, will be able to receive preselected images from the BCS image wall and/or the crisis room. It will be able to display at least 6 to 8 images from different sources.

title: Renewal of Infrared cameras for rocket launch imaging
description:
CNES-CSG intends to renew its infrared cameras that follows the rockets after launching during a few minutes.

Currently, we are using MWIR cameras that are now obsolete and don't fulfill all requirements.
Recent tests have shown that LWIR cameras are more suitable.

The camera system must include image recording.

The purpose of the project is to:
•	Supply the cameras
•	Interface them with our turrets, and with the operational displays
•	Define the right parameters to optimize images

title: CSC Data Processors Re-engineering - Level-1 and Level-2 Sentinel-3 SRAL and MWR Processors
description:
Best practices Intended Announcement 

Open competition 

 

 

The CSC Data Processors Re-engineering Service aims at the implementation of a new Earth Observation Processor Framework (EOPF) and the re-engineering of the data processors currently used to operationally generate the Copernicus Sentinel-1/2/3(land) Level-0, Level-1, Level-2 data with the aim to harmonise and modernise the operational processing framework, to benefit from the capabilities of cloud-based environments such as the elasticity of computing resources and to efficiently support both the systematic production operations as well as the needs of a more flexible on-demand production context. 

 

CS GROUP has been selected by ESA as Prime Contractor for the Sentinels Data Processors Re-engineering Service. As part of this Service, CS GROUP will procure the implementation of the Sentinels processors re-engineering via open competitive tenders according to the ESA Best Practices procedure. 

Three open competitive tenders have already been issued: 

The first one on the 03/02/2023, covering the re-engineering of the Level -1 and Level-2 data processors for Sentinel-2 and the re-engineering of the Level-1 and Level-2 data processors for Sentinel-3 OLCI, SLSTR and Synergy. 

A second one on the 07/04/2023, covering the re-engineering of the Sentinel-1/2/3 Level-0 data processors 

A third one on the 01/06/2023, covering the re-engineering of the Level –1 and Level –2 data processors for Sentinel 1 

 

The fourth and last open competitive tender covering the following activities is planned to be published at the beginning of August 2023: 

The re-engineering of Sentinel 3 SRAL and MWR Level-1 and Level-2 data processors. 

 

Attention is drawn to the fact that the CSC Data Processors Re-engineering Service is funded by the Copernicus Programme under the MFF 2014-2021 and will therefore be open exclusively to economic operators which have their registered office in a EU Member State or a Country participating to the EU Copernicus Programme in the frame of such MFF. 

 

The Best Practices invitations to tender (each consisting of a Cover Letter, Statement of Work, Special Conditions of Tender and Draft Contract) will be available on esa-star Publication, a dedicated module of ESA’s tendering website esa-star (https://esastar-publication-ext.sso.esa.int)

title: Renewal of the Numerical computing means  of Ground safety Department.
description:
The current limitation of computing means does not make it possible to answer the increasing needs of calculations Environment and safeguard Ground. The models are modernized, more powerful while the means do not follow.
The implementation of new computing resources will have to allow numerical modelling of fluids requiring parallel computing power and storage.
The system characteristics must at least meet the following requirements
- 12 parallel connections 
- 2 operating systems used Windows and Linux
- 1 data server allowing archiving, backup and restoration of data (hot)
- 3 networks, two of which interface with the CSG systems
The portage between the old and the new means must be integrated

title: I-HAB –  External Work Package for AIT Activities
description:
The Cislunar Gateway – International Habitat (I-HAB) is 
ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting
the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization 
requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions 
from USA, Japan and Canada. 
The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure 
designed to support both robotic and human exploration 
of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained 
lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than 
the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. 
It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four

title: Temperature controlled truck equipped with a column tailgate
description:
In the framework of its activities at the Guiana Space Center (CSG), CNES must be able to :
•	Transport telecom racks, small spacecrafts, crates, parcels, packages and various loads to and from CSG site and various locations in French Guiana,
•	Transport equipments of the Spacecraft Customer teams (telecoms racks, nanosatellites, secure crates, aircraft pallets)
•	Transport secure goods,
•	Transport dangerous goods

The truck, which is the subject of this pre-publication, must have the following equipments to perform its main functions:
•	a flatbed with "accordion" type side panels (3 panels per side): transported equipments (telecom racks, small spacecrafts, parcels, packages, various loads, etc.) could be loaded from the sides using a forklift truck. Transported equipments must be kept in perfect condition, protected from weather conditions during transport.
•	A horizontally elevated DHOLLANDIA column tailgate: goods could be loaded with a pallet truck, or on the ground or on a platform,
•	An air conditioning system: equipments could be transported at a temperature between 14°C and 22°C.
Moreover, knowing that the intervention zones extend beyond the private enclosure of the Guiana Space Center (CSG), this temperature controlled truck equipped with a column tailgate must be able to travel legally on public roads.

title: Tactical Panel – Crisis GIS (E3)
description:
Context:
At present, there are no interactive IT means available for efficient consultation of CSG infrastructures information.
In the event of an incident, response time is an essential factor in preserving people and installations. Effective sharing of information at all levels (field - emergency center - crisis room), coupled with a more relevant cross-referencing of data, would save operational time in decision-making, especially in the crisis room.
Description:
This project deals with the implementation of a GIS (Geographic Information System) on a tactical panel-type hardware support in order to provide:
- A cartographic representation of the CSG and its surroundings in real time.
- All the information required by the firemen for their operations.
- An instant consultation from the field and simultaneous monitoring of operations to the crisis room.
Setting up a GIS that can be consulted and interacted with on appropriate hardware will be a great help in decision-making and real-time information sharing between the field, the fire station located at the Technical Center and the crisis room.
Thus, adding a geographical visualization of the situation in real-time represents a major asset for improving communication between all actors, while enhancing crisis management and decision-making.

As part of its mission to protect people, property and the environment, CNES is renewing a water-foam-powder firefighting vehicle.

title: Automatic Number-Plate Recognition (E9)
description:
Context:
The visual verification of vehicle badges at CSG does not provide a sufficiently high level of security for access control. An automated license plate check should be set up at access points.
Description:
When approaching the barrier, the system must automatically recognize a vehicle's license plate and check whether it is authorized to enter the site. Controls must be automatic and instantaneous, with no need for the security guard to intervene, thus ensuring greater fluidity and efficiency.
In conjunction with the digital access control system, which efficiently verifies the identity of those on board, access can be authorized and the access barrier lifted.

title: Introducing Connected operator
description:
CNES-CSG intends to develop new facilities for its customers and partners. Among those new functionalities, the connected operator shall for instance allow a remote engineer to interact with a local technician to fulfill technical interventions on the rocket or on the payloads.
New functionalities are also expected to help applying technical procedures thanks to augmented reality of virtual environments

The purpose of the project is to develop new tools and functionalities compatible with the security constraints at the CNES and profitable for all industrial partners to allow remote specialist to help conducting specific repairs or technical maintenances.
This might lead to the usage of augmented reality, virtual environments , mixed or assisted reality

The purpose of the project is to :
•	Define the technical solution compatible with the security constraints
•	Deploy the solution
•	Being creative and possibly suggest other approaches in order to fulfill the business case consisting in being locally assisted by remote specialists.

Delivery will consist in the new infrastructure that will support remote assistance

title: Renouvellement du Système de Détection de la Foudre (THOR)
description:
Pre-publication for Lightning Detection System Renewal (THOR).

This project aims to renew the current lightning detection system of the Guiana Space Center (CSG) which is currently constitute of:
•	Three interferometric detection sensors. 
•	One processing system in charge of collecting lightning data measurements and treatments.
•	A software to localize cloud-to-ground or intra-cloud lightning flashes in real time.
•	Various real-time display terminals. 

The future system could propose another method than interferometry to detect lightning as well as considering other sensors locations among a list of sites given by CSG. 

Like the current system, the new one will have a network detection sensor, a digital processor to collect and compute the lightning data, and a software which displays detection and high-precision localization of lightning flashes. 
The project perimeter contains renewal of lightning detection sensors, lightning data processing system, and an operating and display software with associated real-time display terminals.

Pré publication Renouvellement du Système de Détection de la Foudre (THOR).

Ce projet concerne le renouvellement du système de détection de la foudre du Centre Spatial Guyanais (CSG) constitué actuellement : 
•	De trois capteurs de détection de type interférométrique.
•	D’un serveur central d’acquisition, de stockage et de traitement des données.

title: Radôme station télémesure des Bermudes
description:
The French Guyana Space Center telemetry station located on the Bermuda archipelago is often operated during the CSG launch campaigns. Installed in the Bermuda in 2011 this station is exposed to a hostile environment; high temperatures, tropical storms, high level of air salinity. These elements strongly affect the antenna mechanics and fluids. They lead to a premature drying and corrosion that can damage the system. The installation of a dome is necessary as a countermeasure to protect the whole antenna from its external environment. 
La station de télémesure du Centre Spatial Guyanais localisée aux Bermudes est régulièrement utilisée pour le suivi des campagnes de lancements depuis le site du Centre Spatial Guyanais. Installée aux Bermudes en 2011, l’antenne est soumise à l’environnement de l’archipel qui présente une climatologie éprouvante pour les éléments mécaniques et fluides par des températures élevées, des tempêtes tropicales, une salinité de l’air importante. Ces conditions impactent fortement les différents éléments de l’antenne et provoquent un assèchement et une corrosion prématurés de ces derniers. Afin de protéger l’ensemble de l’antenne de son environnement extérieur, la mise en place d’un radôme s’avère nécessaire.

title: Nitrogen and helium fluid networks modernization in Payload Facilities (EPCU)
description:
Within Payload Facilities (EPCU S1, S3B, S5), the fluid networks (nitrogen and helium) are used by payload customers for campaign activities and also by EPCU operators for maintenance and operational activities. 

From one facility to another and/or within the same building, the nitrogen and helium fluid networks are different. These differences are due to initial design of the network but also to changes made on some networks and not on others. 
The objective is to : 
•	Remove disparities between networks
•	Modernize the design of the fluid networks in order to improve control, maintenance and operability
•	Create an architecture allowing the monitoring of systems in real time
•	Improve the reliability of an aging network subject to numerous leaks (introduce new materials, new technologies…)

description:
Context

•	Reduce reconfiguration delay in between two launches
•	Maintenance and Operation reduction costs
•	Turn the CSG into an attractive spot for new space operators
•	Improve space base availability
•	Daily life improvement and simplification

Description
In this context, the CNES CSG aims to deliver a new data-sharing platform that could be used by all industrial partners over the Space Centre.
Currently the data sharing in between industrial is complicated. We need a platform that could ensure the security and the sharing of data set that will allow to cover specific use cases such as Supply chain, energy consumptions.
 
The follow up and getting the big picture on those functional needs required to get a unified vision of same data that are held either by on or the other industrial partner on the base.
Setting up a data-sharing platform will enable to easily send/get those data and re-use them either on the platform itself or by importing those data in each industrial partner Information system.
This platform will also have to deliver data mining and data intelligence services so that each partner could use those tools to follow up the actions and dashboards to allow decisions

The expected delivery will consist in deploying the new data sharing platform, train and explain how it works to all industrial partners on the CSG Space port.

Description: Context

CNES-CSG wants to digitalize its activities in order to :
•	Reduce reconfiguration delay in between two launches
•	Maintenance and Operation reduction costs
•	Turn the CSG into an attractive spot for new space operators
•	Improve space base availability
•	Daily life improvement and simplification

Description
In this context, the CNES CSG aims to deliver a new data-sharing platform that could be used by all industrial partners over the Space Centre.
Currently the data sharing in between industrial is complicated. We need a platform that could ensure the security and the sharing of data set that will allow to cover specific use cases such as Supply chain, energy consumptions.
 
The follow up and getting the big picture on those functional needs required to get a unified vision of same data that are held either by on or the other industrial partner on the base.
Setting up a data-sharing platform will enable to easily send/get those data and re-use them either on the platform itself or by importing those data in each industrial partner Information system.
This platform will also have to deliver data mining and data intelligence services so that each partner could use those tools to follow up the actions and dashboards to allow decisions

The expected delivery will consist in deploying the new data sharing platform, train and explain how it works to all industrial partners on the CSG Space port.

title: Renewal of "Video Cameras for customers" system ( INV )
description:
CNES-CSG intends to renew the system called CAMDEC (Video cameras for customers) that allows filming permanently a satellite during its preparation and integration phase, in clean rooms.

CNES has several video facilities that allow to its customers permanently filming their satellite when it is in the cleanroom during preparation phase before its integration in the launcher. This System, called CAMDEC (Camera for the customers) is made of cameras and monitors screens.

CNES wants to renew this system in the aim to:
-	Improve camera resolution
-	Make the system fully remote controlled
-	Add new functionalities : image recording, qualification for images with sensible data

Delivery will consist in the new Camdec system, qualified for operations and use of sensible data

title: RSVSP Project
description:
Renewal of the Guiana Space Center’s (CSG) CCTV equipment "RSVSP Project"
This project concerns the renewal of the Guiana Space Center’s (CSG) CCTV equipment : RSVSP project.
The scope of the case includes:
•	Renewal of obsolete CCTV equipment (analog technology) by digital equipment, compatible with the fleet already deployed and operational on the Ariane 6 Ground Segment : cameras, processing and acquisition units, storage and archiving units, etc.
•	Interconnection of this new generation equipment to the CSG’s shared Safety and Protection network via active network equipment.
•	Provision, installation and connection of new cameras to the existing CCTV supervision system (SVSP).
•	Provision, installation and connection to the existing CCTV supervision system (SVSP) of new operator stations.
•	Taking into account the impacts of the various changes identified above on the existing CCTV supervision system (SVSP).
•	Taking into account functional ergonomic changes to the existing CCTV supervision system (SVSP).

Ce projet concerne le renouvellement des équipements de Vidéosurveillance Sûreté Protection (SVSP) du Centre Spatial Guyanais (CSG) : projet RSVSP.
Le périmètre de l’affaire inclut : 
•	Le renouvellement des équipements de vidéosurveillance obsolètes (technologie analogique) par des équipements numériques, compatibles du parc déjà déployé et opérationnel sur l’Ensemble de Lancement N°4 Ariane 6 : caméras, unités de traitement et d’acquisition, unités de stockage et d’archivage, etc…
•	L’interconnexion de ces équipements nouvelle génération au réseau mutualisé Sûreté Protection existant du CSG via des équipements réseau actifs.
•	La fourniture, l’installation et le raccordement au système de supervision de vidéosurveillance existant (SVSP) de nouvelles caméras.
•	La fourniture, l’installation et le raccordement au système de supervision de vidéosurveillance existant (SVSP) de nouveaux postes opérateurs.
•	La prise en compte des impacts liés aux diverses modifications identifiées ci-dessus sur le système de supervision existant (SVSP).
•	La prise en compte de modifications ergonomiques fonctionnelles du système de supervision existant (SVSP).

title: CREO Project
description:
Projet CREO "Renouvellement des moyens de calcul des retombées éléments lanceurs en opérations du CSG"

Dans le cadre de la Loi sur les Opérations Spatiale, l’opérateur de lancement doit démontrer la maitrise des zones de retombée des fragments de lanceurs (Art 23 de [RT]). Le CNES doit, au titre de son activité de contrôle, s’assurer que ces zones, nominales ou accidentelles, sont conformes à la réglementation. Des moyens existent en interne CNES, opérés par les équipes de la Sauvegarde Vol du Centre Spatial Guyanais et de la DTN, mais aucun moyen unique ne répond à tous les besoins identifiés. 

Le projet CREO (Calcul des Retombées d’Eléments lanceur Opérationnel) est un projet informatique qui consiste à utiliser l’outil développé en interne CNES, nommé OREO, comme coeur de calcul pour estimer les zones de retombées d’éléments lanceur en soumission et en temps réel (cas nominal ou dégradé). CREO devra héberger une IHM permettant une utilisation opérationnelle. Cela revient globalement à intégrer en IHM et à interfacer avec le temps réel l’outil OREO, ainsi qu’à réaliser quelques traitements simples dont de la visualisation cartographique. 
L’objectif global est de disposer d’un outil flexible et configurable facilement en fonction de l’architecture du lanceur et des moyens.
La première version sera qualifiée et testée pour le lanceur Ariane 6, puis le logiciel sera étendu aux autres lanceurs au CSG.
Le contenu des interfaces devra globalement être cohérent des autres outils actuels utilisés par le CSG (principalement le SCTV (Système de Coordination, Traitement et Visualisation)) 

CREO Project "Renewal of the means of calculating the impact of launchers in operation at CSG"

From the French Spatial Act, launch operator has to prove falling launch area conformity following Art. 23 of Technical Reglementation. The CNES has, from his control activity, to ensure that these areas, nominal or hazardous, are conform with the french reglementation. Some ground-base segment does exist already, operated by the Guyanese Space Centre (CSG) Flight Safety teams, but need improvement and unicity. 
The CREO project is an IT project which consists in integrating into the GUI and interacting it with real time tools a multi-launcher flight safety diagnostic tool currently used by the CSG Flight Safety teams called ‘OREO’, and in executing some simple treatments, including cartographic visualization. 
This tool is based on a CNES mode OREO.
The overall objective is to have a flexible and configurable tool that is easily configurable according to the launcher’s architecture and dimensioning scenarios.
The first version will be qualified and tested for the Ariane 6 launcher, and will be extended then to the others launchers.
The content of the interfaces must be consistent overall with the other current tools used by the CSG (mainly the SCTV (Coordination, Processing and Visualization System)).

title: S5 Door seal remplacement
description:
The door seals of the EPCU S5 are over 20 years old.
Damage of an interior door seal has a direct impact on the ambient conditions inside the clean room (loss of overpressure). In addition, with a spacecraft inside a clean room, the loss of an exterior door seal, would no longer allow us to ensure the security of the room or dock the CCU3 for a transfer.
We have to change 4 exterior door seals first, and then the 6 interior door of the EPCU S5.

title: CSG Industrial contract renewal of ordinary maintenance and operations : Electronics, Electrotechnology, RF 2
description:
Dear Sir/Madam,
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months:

The "Electronic, Electrotechnology, RF, Sensors" activity is part of the operational and/or permanent functional tasks of the CNES/CSG.

The chosen Contractor will provide the CNES/CSG with maintenance (preventive, corrective and ongoing) and operational services within the scope of the following resources:

•	5 tracking RADARS installed in Kourou and St Jean du Maroni,
•	2 weather radars as well as meteorological parameter measurement facilities (weather stations, field mills, radiosonde stations) installed in Kourou,
•	2 remote launcher neutralisation stations including antennas - TSAR station (a directional antenna and omnidirectional antennas), one installed at the CSG and the other transportable and installed in St Jean du Maroni,
•	4 launcher tracking stations including one in French Guiana at the CSG (with 2 antennas/tracking systems/TeleMetryMT receiving systems); one in St Jean du Maroni or St Georges de l'Oyapock in French Guiana (with 1 antenna/tracking system/TeleMetryMT receiving system - transportable); one in Libreville, Gabon (with 1 antenna/tracking system/TeleMetryMT receiving system); and one in Bermuda (with one antenna/tracking system/MT receiving system),

description:

title: CSG Industrial contract renewal of ordinary maintenance and operations : Safety " Environment, Ground safety, Workplace safety"
description:
Dear Sir/Madam,
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months:

1) Activity Environment and Ground Safety
The "Security systems, Environment, Ground safety, Workplace safety" activity forms part of the operational and/or permanent functional tasks of the CNES/CSG.
The Contractor's mission is carried out mainly in the CNES facilities at the CSG.
The mission consists of providing services intended to ensure the protection of people, property and the environment, in the frame of the overall mission of protection of people, property and the environment of CNES / CSG relating to ground activities.
The main technical skills required are the following ones :
•	Risk analysis of complex systems : pyrotechnic systems, solid and liquid propellant systems, mechanic / electric systems…
•	Risk analysis of hazardous activities : propellant tank filling and pressurization, handling payloads/launcher stages, dangerous goods / payload / launcher transportation…
•	Labor and environmental regulations, CSG rules and regulations

2) Activity workplace safety : 
The incumbent entity will be able to carry out on site health and safety of work activities on site. The regulatory security controls will be carried out by an incumbent entity that has been approved by the Minister of labour or equivalent commissioned entity of the French Authority. It will have an expert knowledge of French regulations.
They will advise the customer in particular on the use of means and facilities.
The Contract holder will be able to carry out certain health and safety of work activities on site, upon expert reports related to Health Safety Working Conditions.
The Contract holder will lead Safety awareness sessions (in French/English) particularly for hoisting devices and for mini gas supply networks.

Description: Dear Sir/Madam, CNES informs you that a European consultation covering the activities detailed below will be published on ESA-STAR in the next few months: The "CNES-CSG Logistics" activity is part of a global support mission linked to the operating needs of the CSG, and to the technical and operational activities of the Launch Base. The successful Contractor(s) will provide these services for CNES/CSG in the following technical scope: 
 
Logistics and transport systems maintenance (including specific equipment for transporting payloads, corresponding handling equipment, and administrative and regulatory aspects); 
Centralized management of the General Warehouse and Reception, packaging, packing, internal CSG and inter-site delivery, handling, dispatch of conventional and secured freight (chargeur connu); 
Transports and logistics activities for running the launch base and satellite campaigns (specific tools, shared equipment and propellants, payloads and associated tools transports from airport or harbour to CSG). 
Management of "Base" furniture (as opposed to "Non-Base" furniture) and Procurement, removal, installation, coordination, management of handling operations; 
Reception, distribution of mail letter and small handling operations on the CSG; 
Preparation, realization and management of customs transit files on site in relation with the CNES forwarding companies (excluding the operational activities of the Transport and RETT assistants); 
Handling of all types of materials and equipment... 
Coordination of the public transport companies contracted by the CNES for the Launch Base Employee. 
Coordination/management of shuttles to and from Félix-Eboué airport for guests, schoolchildren and VIPs during one-off CNES/CSG visits (interfaces with coach transporters, etc.) and daily visits for the general public; 
Coordination/management of CNES VIP direct transport and the provision and cleaning of cars. 
Coordination of daily management of the Diesel supply for the Launch Base with the Petroleum Company contracted by the CNES. 
 
The NATIONAL and INTERNATIONAL TRANSIT services cover operations related to the general functioning of CNES/CSG and to launches and are carried out within the framework of the missions of the Launch Base. CNES/CSG entrusts the contractor (s) with the mission of organising and executing, or having executed, customs and multimodal transport operations in import and export between the various storage locations on the CNES/CSG site and the rest of the world (controlled and reactive transit network) via the maritime (Dégrad des Cannes, Pariacabo harbors in Kourou) and airport (Cayenne - Félix Éboué Airport) entry points in French Guiana. The contractor (s) shall carry out all import and export customs formalities at the place of departure or destination as indirect Representative of CNES/CSG for customs clearance operations by receiving its instructions from the CNES/CSG TRANSIT office and shall ensure the advance of funds linked to the fees and taxes on goods. In French Guiana, the contractor shall draw up monthly global declarations (DCG) integrating the calculation of duties, taxes and fees to be paid to the customs. It takes all steps with the competent authorities (port and airport authorities, DGTM, Prefecture, Gendarmerie, customs, etc.) to obtain the necessary authorisations for operations on public or private roads. As the CNES/CSG has the "Chargeur Connu" approval, the Contractor must hold the status of Authorised Agent in French Guiana, Toulouse and the Paris airports" and must be authorised by the DGAC as an Authorised Agent for "Cargo Security". All types of miscellaneous or general cargo must be able to be transported individually or in groups; dangerous goods of different classes imported or exported in residual proportions or not by qualified, trained and authorised personnel.

title: CSG Industrial contract renewal of ordinary maintenance and operations : " Operations Planning and Coordination"
description:
Dear Sir/Madam,

The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months:

The Operations Planning and Coordination activity is a permanent task which plays a central role in the functioning of the CNES/CSG.
This task, through the Operations Coordination Office (also referred to as BCO), manages the joint activities carried out on the Launch Site. It enables planning of all the activities on the Site and in particular harmonisation of the maintenance activities (MCO: Maintenance in Operational Condition of the technical systems) with the operational activities relating to launch campaigns.

The activities to be planned and coordinated concern all the sites under the responsibility of the CNES, the EPCUs (acronym referring to the Payload Preparation Facilities), the technical centre and the remote operational resources. The planning process also sets the pace for the maintenance or upgrading of "major networks" (eg. NRJ, CLIM, Water).
The planning of activities for which CNES/CSG is responsible must be harmonised and optimised, taking into account the activities of other industrial operators on the Base.
In order to carry out its tasks, the Contractor is required to use the PLANISWARE planning software provided by CNES.
The planning system is interfaced with the office resources via communication networks, allowing users to make planning requests for their activities. 
The technical management and system administration of the PLANISWARE software are not the responsibility of the contractor responsible for the Operations Planning and Coordination activity. They are provided on behalf of the CNES/CSG by the provider responsible for the corporate IT activity.

title: CSG Industrial contract renewal of ordinary maintenance and operations : "Engineering Services (also referred to as BET)"
description:
Dear Sir/Madam,

The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months:
:
The on-site Engineering Services activity (“Bureau d’Etudes” in French also referred to as BET) is one of the permanent operational activities of CNES at the Guiana Space Centre. 
It is responsible for global engineering support of the technical and operational activities of the launch base, linked to the operational needs of the CSG.

1.	Engineering Services task consisting in preparing the technical files necessary for upgrades to the technical installations entrusted to it;
2.	project management for the performance and coordination of the work necessary for the implementation and qualification of upgrades;
3.	topographical surveying and dimensional metrology;
4.	management, updating (internal and external) and dissemination on request of the plans of the installations configuration-managed by the CNES/CSG;
5.	archiving and making available on request the industrial files of projects whose operation is outsourced by the CNES
Note 1: the work carried out within the framework of the above-mentioned services concerns the following technical specialities: energy (high and low voltage and lightning), mechanical engineering, fluids, infrastructure, air-conditioning (including the controllers and/or PLCs of the corresponding systems).
Note 2: Engineering Services is the entry (delivery) point for descriptive technical documentation coming into the CSG (industrial plans and files).
The Contractor must have the necessary skills to integrate new projects in the form of a digital model (BIM/SIG design) and to move towards using this database as a digital repository for configuration management.

title: CSG Industrial contract for renewal of ordinary maintenance and operations:  Security - Protection
description:
1) Security and Protection Activity
Some of the operations and/or ongoing missions of CNES/CSG entail ensuring the security of the site and its facilities, and protecting people and property.
Controlled from an Alarm Centre, the main tasks of the future Contractor will entail surveillance, access control and interventions on various CSG facilities (checking in the event of incidents, door openings, etc.) and sites, most of which are classified as Protected Areas and located within the perimeter of the Guiana Space Centre.
The reception-programming-badges activity
The Contractor will also be responsible for welcoming visitors and handling telephone calls, as well as issuing and managing personnel and vehicle passes (delivery and collection ) and access rights (programming) for the whole of the Guiana Space Centre.
The contractor will operate the systems set up by CNES/CSG
2) Security systems activity
The “Security Systems” activity helps ensure the security and protection of CSG personnel and facilities, a mission for which CNES/CSG is entirely and solely responsible.
The Contractor selected shall provide CNES/CSG with preventive, corrective and upgrading maintenance services in addition to operating services for the security systems (access control and alarm management, perimeter protection, external and internal video surveillance, the fire detection system and the CNES evacuation and fallback system, etc.).
The Contractor selected shall be responsible for implementing these systems during launch operations as well as during qualification testing of system upgrades.

PS: The current Launch Range industrial landscape managed by the CNES/CSG can be found at:

title: CSG Industrial contract renewal of ordinary maintenance and operations : “Support for preparing payloads”
description:
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months: Customer Service is part of a global assignment to support the technical and operational activities of the launch base in order to guarantee their successful conclusion. This support mainly includes:

the technical and operational activities of the Payload Preparation Complex (EPCU) to be carried out in order to manage and coordinate operations and to configure resources that will be used to support teams that are preparing and conducting satellite campaigns.

 

The management systems and resources are:

 

Mechanical systems (for lifting, handling, access to buildings, etc.)

Operational and technical premises (clean rooms, air-conditioned storage areas, offices and control room for the customer teams, utility rooms, etc.) •

power supply management and distribution systems in the EPCUs.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) management systems and specific equipment for certain rooms and operational activities (fuelling personnel PPE, clean room clothing, filtered-air hoses, etc.)

Monitoring and supervision systems for critical EPCU systems

Fluid systems: production and implementation (air, mini network, etc.) (air production, mini network, etc.)

Liquid and gaseous effluent management systems (flushing columns, effluent treatment and associated monitoring facilities)

Physical expert appraisal systems and devices (particle counting, thermometry, hygrometry, accelerometry, etc.) • chemical analysis systems and devices (gas detection)

 

The management of preventive and corrective maintenance as well as the monitoring and management of technical and operational launch base upgrades for the following facilities and activities:

 

All the systems and activities involved in operating and managing the EPCUs.

The resources for managing PPE and specific protective equipment related to operational activities for all base activities.

Specific transport and logistics activities organization for running the satellite campaigns with the support of CNES transports subcontractor.

The fleet of first-aid, fire-fighting and pollution control vehicles.

The activities of the chemical analysis laboratory (cleanness of operational rooms and analysis equipment).

The activities of the physical expert appraisal laboratory (electromagnetism, radiofrequency, accelerometry, test benches and test equipment, etc.).

These activities are carried out in a demanding operational context in terms of both security/safety and working hours.

title: STAR45 Project
description:
In the frame of the Centre Spatial Guyanais (CSG) antenna network treatment of obsolescence’s, the CNES is considering the renewal or replacement of the Telemetry antenna STAR 45, located at the “Montagne des pères” in French Guiana.

This 11m tracking antenna, currently, provides service for telemetry tracking launchers taking off from the European Spaceport in Kourou.

Two types of tasks are envisaged: the renewal of the tracking and servo systems or the complete replacement with a brand new antenna of smaller diameter.

Dans le cadre du traitement des obsolescences du réseau d’antennes du Centre Spatial Guyanes (CSG), le CNES envisage le renouvellement ou le remplacement l’antenne de Télémesure STAR 45 qui se situe à la Montage des pères, en Guyane française.

Cette antenne de poursuite de 11m est actuellement utilisée pour la poursuite et réception de la télémesure des lanceurs décollant du CSG.

Deux types de prestations sont envisagées : le renouvellement de la partie poursuite et asservissement ou le remplacement par une antenne neuve moins grande.

title: MSR-ERO X band RF suitcase
description:
The Mars Sample Return ? Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL
led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2033.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2027.

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO X band RF Suitcase in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The X band RF suitcase shall be built around representative items from MSR-ERO spacecraft including On Board Computer, X band Deep Space Transponder, X band TWTA and representative Mission central software.

Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the

title: SAPRESS Project
description:
The role of the Guyanese Space Centre (CSG) Flight Safety teams is to ensure the protection of people, property, the environment and public health during a space operation (Launch Operation)

The Sapress project is an IT project which consists in integrating into the GUI a multi-launcher flight safety diagnostic tool currently used by the CSG Flight Safety teams called ‘Sedia Calisa generic’, and in executing some simple treatments. 
This tool is based on a CNES model, built on Sedia Calisa Ariane 5 code.
The overall objective is to have a flexible and configurable tool that is easily configurable according to the launcher’s architecture and dimensioning scenarios.
The first version will be qualified and tested for the new Ariane 6 launcher.
The content of the interfaces must be consistent overall with the other current tools used by the CSG (mainly the SCTV (Coordination, Processing and Visualization System)).

Les équipes Sauvegarde Vol du Centre Spatial Guyanais (CSG) ont pour rôle de s’assurer de la Protection des personnes, des biens, de l’environnement et de la santé publique lors d’une opération spatiale (Opération de lancement)

title: I-HAB Quick disconnects (for  IATCS EATCS and ECLSS)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025.
 The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada.
 The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration.
 The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly.
 It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Quick Disconnects for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Quick Disconnects are part of the Active Thermal Control System (ATCS) and of the Environmental and Life Support System (ECLSS) belonging to the I-HAB Gateway module.
 Quick Disconnects will be part of both internal and external ATCS loops and are also foreseen in circuits belonging to some ECLSS functions.
The Quick Disconnects shall provide a quick and easy way of connecting and disconnecting fluid system components to perform scheduled and nonscheduled maintenance, and to facilitate fluid system reconfiguration, avoiding loss of fluid.
 Further information concerning the I-HAB campaign can be found on the Agencys website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

title: OPEN COMPETITION covering the procurement of the CRISTAL Instrument RF SS EGSE
description:
The Copernicus programme is an evolution of the previous Global Monitoring for Environment and Security (GMES) Programme, an Earth monitoring initiative led by the European Union (EU) and carried out in partnership with the EU Member States and the European Space Agency (ESA) established to fulfil the growing need amongst European policy-makers to access accurate and timely information services to manage the environment, understand and mitigate the effects of climate change and ensure civil security.
ESA has awarded six contracts covering the implementation of the Phase B2,C/D,E1 for each of the six new Copernicus missions, encompassing the procurement of both the prototype (instrument(s) and spacecraft), funded by the ESA Member States under the CSC-4 Programme, and the recurrent satellites, funded by the EU under the future MFF 2021-2027, where the recurrent satellites are offered at the same time as the prototype and are implemented as contractual options in a single contract. 
One of these missions is the Copernicus Polar Ice and Snow Topography Altimeter Mission , hereinafter referred to as well as CRISTAL. The objective of the CRISTAL Mission, is to provide enhanced retrieval of sea ice thickness and freeboard, land ice sheet/glacier elevation and ocean surface elevation, wave-height and wind speed by measurements implementing improvement in spatial resolution and performance. The primary high-level objectives are to monitor critical climate signals including: variability of Arctic and Southern Ocean sea-ice and its snow loading, as well as ice sheet, ice cap melting and sea level. Other objectives are to support applications related to coastal and inland waters and contribute to the observation of ocean topography.
In that frame, TAS-F was awarded an Airbus Defense and Space contract for the Interferometric Radar altimeter for Ice & Snow (IRIS). TAS-F is responsible for procuring the CRISTAL RF Sub-system EGSE, using the ESA Best Practices (BP) procedures (ESA/IPC(2012)65,rev.2).
TAS will release an Invitation To Tender (ITT) for the procurement of the Ku band and Ka band front-end of the COPERNICUS Polar Ice and Snow Topography Altimeter instrument of the CRISTAL mission. The Ku band and Ka band front-end will be integrated in the CRISTAL EGSE. The Ku band and Ka band front-end are parts of the RF s/s module which interface between the Altimeter and the digital s/s
This procurement will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65,rev.2) as modified for the purpose of the Copernicus programme.
