title: LSTM Instrument OGSE for AOB EM-PFM / POB PFM test (AOB-POB-OGSE)
description:
The Copernicus programme is an evolution of the previous Global Monitoring for Environment and Security (GMES) Programme, an Earth monitoring initiative led by the European Union (EU) and carried out in partnership with the EU Member States and the European Space Agency (ESA) established to fulfil the growing need amongst European policy-makers to access accurate and timely information services to better manage the environment, understand and mitigate the effects of climate change and ensure civil security. 
While the deployment of the first generation of Sentinels is approaching its completion, the intense use and increased awareness for the potential of Copernicus have generated great expectations for an evolved Copernicus system (“CSC Expansion”). Emerging and urgent needs for new types of observations have been consolidated in a distinct set of requirements which are addressed by six new Copernicus Sentinel missions, formerly known as “High Priority Candidate Missions” (HPCM), one of which being the Copernicus High Spatio-Temporal Resolution Land Surface Temperature Monitoring Mission, hereinafter referred to as well as LSTM Mission.
ESA has awarded six contracts covering the implementation of the Phase B2, C/D,E1 for each of the six Copernicus missions, encompassing the procurement of both the prototype (instrument(s) and spacecraft), funded by the ESA Member States under the CSC-4 Programme, and the recurrent satellites, funded by the EU under the future MFF 2021-2027, where the recurrent satellites are offered at the same time as the prototype and are implemented as contractual options in a single contract.
LSTM Mission contract was awarded to Airbus Defence and Space SAU (ES), as prime contractor, for the procurement of the LSTM satellites including LSTM instrument procured by Airbus Defence and Space SAS (FR).
The main objective of the LSTM Mission is complement the existing family of Copernicus satellites observation capabilities with high spatio-temporal resolution Thermal Infrared observations over land and coastal regions in support of agriculture management services, and a range of additional services. The LSTM primary objective is to provide timely and accurate monitoring of land and coastal areas in the spectral range of TIR, SWIR and VNIR. These measurements will allow determination of evapotranspiration at spatial scales enabling the range of innovative agricultural applications capturing the field scale variability required for irrigation, crop growth modelling and reporting on crop water productivity.
In this framework, Airbus Defence and Space SAS, instrument prime contractor, will release an Invitation To Tender for the procurement of the instrument Optical Ground Support Equipment’s (OGSE) for AOB/POB FPA testing called AOB-POB OGSE.
This OGSE will be used to verify and test the LSTM sub-assemblies during the AIT phases of the project. In particular the AOB/POB (VNIR and SWIR focal planes assemblies) emulates the LTSM flight telescope, from the optical point of view, for the on-ground test of LSTM focal plane units (AOB&POB). It operates in the 400nm to 1700nm spectral range. It shall be noted that the telescope presents strong optical aberrations: one specific goal of the OGSE is to mimic these aberrations with the requested accuracy to be able to perform MTF measurements, coregistration, spectral measurements and straylight measurements on AOB-POB FPAs.
The procurement of the LSTM OGSE’s will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65,rev.2).

Description: The Copernicus programme is an evolution of the previous Global Monitoring for Environment and Security (GMES) Programme, an Earth monitoring initiative led by the European Union (EU) and carried out in partnership with the EU Member States and the European Space Agency (ESA) established to fulfil the growing need amongst European policy-makers to access accurate and timely information services to better manage the environment, understand and mitigate the effects of climate change and ensure civil security. 
While the deployment of the first generation of Sentinels is approaching its completion, the intense use and increased awareness for the potential of Copernicus have generated great expectations for an evolved Copernicus system (“CSC Expansion”). Emerging and urgent needs for new types of observations have been consolidated in a distinct set of requirements which are addressed by six new Copernicus Sentinel missions, formerly known as “High Priority Candidate Missions” (HPCM), one of which being the Copernicus High Spatio-Temporal Resolution Land Surface Temperature Monitoring Mission, hereinafter referred to as well as LSTM Mission.
ESA has awarded six contracts covering the implementation of the Phase B2, C/D,E1 for each of the six Copernicus missions, encompassing the procurement of both the prototype (instrument(s) and spacecraft), funded by the ESA Member States under the CSC-4 Programme, and the recurrent satellites, funded by the EU under the future MFF 2021-2027, where the recurrent satellites are offered at the same time as the prototype and are implemented as contractual options in a single contract.
LSTM Mission contract was awarded to Airbus Defence and Space SAU (ES), as prime contractor, for the procurement of the LSTM satellites including LSTM instrument procured by Airbus Defence and Space SAS (FR).
The main objective of the LSTM Mission is complement the existing family of Copernicus satellites observation capabilities with high spatio-temporal resolution Thermal Infrared observations over land and coastal regions in support of agriculture management services, and a range of additional services. The LSTM primary objective is to provide timely and accurate monitoring of land and coastal areas in the spectral range of TIR, SWIR and VNIR. These measurements will allow determination of evapotranspiration at spatial scales enabling the range of innovative agricultural applications capturing the field scale variability required for irrigation, crop growth modelling and reporting on crop water productivity.

In this framework, Airbus Defence and Space SAS, instrument prime contractor, will release an Invitation To Tender for the procurement of the instrument SPectral EQuipment Test Response for DBS1 Ground Support Equipment’s (SPEQTRE-OGSE).

This OGSE will be used to verify and test the LSTM sub-assemblies during the AIT phases of the project. In particular the DBS1 (Dichroic Beam Splitter and associated filters) encompasses the verification of spectral performances of the DBS1 for VNIR & SWIR spectral bands (400nm to 1.7µm) and TIR spectral bands (8µm to 13µm). 

The procurement of the LSTM OGSE’s will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65,rev.2).

title: CHIME Instrument WiRAL Fiber Mixing (Spectrometer Illumination) (OGSE)
description: The Copernicus programme is an evolution of the previous Global Monitoring for Environment and Security (GMES) Programme, an Earth monitoring initiative led by the European Union (EU) and carried out in partnership with the EU Member States and the European Space Agency (ESA) established to fulfil the growing need amongst European policy-makers to access accurate and timely information services to manage the environment, understand and mitigate the effects of climate change and ensure civil security. ESA has awarded six contracts covering the implementation of the Phase B2,C/D,E1 for each of the six new Copernicus missions, encompassing the procurement of both the prototype (instrument(s) and spacecraft), funded by the ESA Member States under the CSC-4 Programme, and the recurrent satellites, funded by the EU under the future MFF 2021-2027, where the recurrent satellites are offered at the same time as the prototype and are implemented as contractual options in a single contract. One of these missions is the Copernicus Hyperspectral Imaging Mission For the Environment, hereinafter referred to as well as CHIME. CHIME Mission contract was awarded to Thales Alenia Space France (FR), as prime contractor, for the procurement of the CHIME satellites including CHIME instrument under OHB (DE). The main objective of the CHIME Mission is to complement Sentinel observations with an imaging spectroscopy observational capability for services supporting the improved management of natural resources and related policies. The mission will provide routine hyperspectral observations through the Copernicus Programme in support of EU- and related policies for the management of natural resources. This unique visible-to-shortwave infrared spectroscopy based capability will be dedicated to raw material and sustainable agricultural management with a focus on soil properties, mineral resources and agricultural services, including food security and biodiversity. To enable accurate quantitative estimates of specific vegetation bio/geo-physical/chemical variables, as well as top-soil variables and mineral compositions CHIME encompasses as payload an imaging spectrometer. This imaging spectrometer allows monitoring of land and coastal/inland water bodies with contiguous spectral channels covering the spectral range from the VIS to the SWIR. In this framework, OHB, as instrument prime contractor, will release an Invitation To Tender for the procurement of the instrument Optical Ground Support Equipment (OGSE). The Wide Illumination Range Subsystem - WiRAL will be part of the OGSE assembly for alignment and alignment verification of the Chime instrument detectors to the respective spectrometer during the AIT phases of the project. This encompasses a bread board model as well as several flight models. The main unit will be placed in ISO8 environment and will be used as light source for another OGSE (called SpecSID). The light generated by the WiRAL will be guided by optical fibers to the further OGSE in ISO5 environment. Additionally, it will provide a software environment for command, monitoring and data logging. The software will allow commands in a local and a remote mode. The WiRAL will feature the following main building blocks: main unit (light generation, fibers and metrology), control unit and calibration system. The present ITT will be addressed to economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose registered office is established in the countries defined herewith. This procurement will be conducted in line with the “ESA Best Practices for the Selection of Subcontractors by Prime Contractors in the frame of ESA’s Major Procurements” (reference ESA BEST PRACTICES IPC(2012)65,rev.2) as modified for the purpose of the Copernicus programme.

title: MSR-ERO – Second Batch of Mechanical Ground Support Equipment (MGSE Batch 1)
description:
The Mars Sample Return – Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agency’s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement action is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO MGSE Batch 2 to be used for the Spacecraft integration and test activities, in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
In detail the hardware subject of this procurement selection will be:
•	The RM Avionics Module Integration Rig (ARIG) is a stand used to support a subassembly of the ERO Return Module structure (consisting of a C-shaped composition of three structural panels) and capable of rotating the test article 360o about the horizontal axis such that each of the panela can be set horizontal when needed by the activities to be performed.

title: Système d'acquisition des Mâts Météo
description:
This project aims to renew the current weather masts system of the Guiana Space Center (CSG). The weather masts system contains wind (direction, speed) and temperature sensors at specific levels on weather masts (typical mast height: 60 meters) all over the space center. A digital system is in charge of collecting data measurements from each weather mast to a central processing system at the weather station site. The project perimeter contains renewal of wind and temperature sensors as well as associated mechanical mast interfaces, local data concentrators on each mast site and the centralized processing system at the weather station site. 

Ce projet concerne le renouvellement du système d’acquisition des Mâts Météo du Centre Spatial Guyanais (CSG). Le nouveau système comprend des capteurs d’acquisition du Vent (force et direction) et de la température à différents niveaux du sol à partir de plusieurs mâts (hauteur typique 60 mètres) répartis sur l’ensemble de la base. Un système numérique permet la collecte des acquisitions sur les différents mâts et leur centralisation pour traitement à la station Météo du CSG. Le périmètre du projet concerne le renouvellement des capteurs d’acquisition comprenant les interfaces mécaniques avec les mâts, les centrales associées en pied de mât et le système de traitement centralisé situé à la station Météo.

title: MSR-SFR - Procurement of Central Checkout System (CCS)
description:
The Mars Sample Return Campaign is a response to the long-running scientific objective to better understand Mars. By acquiring and returning to Earth a rigorously documented set of Mars samples, scientists will have access to the full breadth and depth of analytical science instruments available in terrestrial laboratories. The investigations will be free of the mass, volume, and power constraints that limit in-situ instruments. The resulting investigations of these returned samples will enable breakthrough advances in:
•the search for ancient and/or extant life on Mars;
•understanding the origin and evolution of Mars as a geological system;
•understanding the processes and history of climate on Mars;
•preparing for human exploration.

The MSR architecture involves a total of five campaign elements: four flight elements and one ground
element. Each campaign element consists of one or more functional elements. The four flight elements are:
•a caching rover mission, developed by NASA-JPL (Mars 2020 project), currently operating on Mars,
•a first Sample Retrieval Lander (SRL-1) mission, consisting of a NASA/JPL developed lander with a
Mars Ascent Vehicle (MAV) as well as ESA provided Sample Transfer Arm (STA)
•a second Sample Retrieval Lander (SRL-2) mission, carrying a Sample Fetch Rover (SFR),
•and an ESA provided Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) mission.

The Sample Fetch Rover will be launched on-board a Sample Return Lander in 2028 and arriving on Mars surface in mid-2030. Following a successful landing, the rover will deploy and egress from the platform and traverse to the depot in which the Mars2020 rover will have stored the sample tubes containing soil and rock samples. With the capability for autonomous and fast surface mobility, the Sample Fetch Rover will traverse to the depot, collect and store on board the individual sample tubes, and safely transport them back to the Sample Return Lander. 

Airbus Defence and Space Ltd will be acting as Prime Contractor to the European Space Agency to perform the MSR-SFR Phase B2CDE1, together with its subcontractors. 

As part of this Contract (currently in Phase B2), Airbus Defence and Space Ltd will release an Invitation to Tender (ITT) looking for a Supplier of the Central Checkout System.

The scope of work of the Contractor includes the provision of the test and verification computers to the SFR Vehicle programme including the design, the development, qualification, production and verification of the systems and providing support to the programme during setup, commissioning and subsequent use of the systems. The CCS Contract includes the following computers and systems:
•	Servers hosting the Virtual Machines that will be used for the Numerical Software Validation Facilities (NSVF)
•	Guidance Navigation and Control (GNC) machines
•	Functional Validation Bench (FVB) machines 
•	Test Bench Central Check out Systems
•	Flight Rover Central Check out System
•	Central Check out System Laptops
The NSVF, GNC and FVB machines support the development and verification of the on-board software and Guidance Navigational Control system. The NSVF also supports FV and AIT test debugging and functional validation. The Central Check out System forms the central hub of the SFR Vehicle test environments, from which the majority of the on-board equipment and software testing is performed. 
The Central Check out System application will be based on the Airbus Open Center (OC) software product, hosted on several Linux servers and workstations. The OC software will be installed by Airbus Defence and Space post-delivery and acceptance of the computer hardware.

title: Museum - Work Package 9 - AudioVisual and MultiMedia
description:
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months:

Context:
The CNES wishes to renovate the Space Museum in Kourou, French Guiana, to make it a space adapted to the expectations of its target public. This renovation encompasses all the interior spaces (permanent exhibition, reception area, shop), as well as the building’s cladding and the addition of exterior facilities.
Reflection on the renovation of the Space Museum is part of the strategy to promote in French Guiana the image of space and of the Guiana Space Centre (CSG), Europe’s Spaceport.
The design of the project is global and focuses on attractiveness in order to enhance the visit experience for all visitors: families, school groups, customers, institutions, employees, service providers, and others.
In addition, the project is part of a broader context, in particular associated with:
-	The modernisation of the image of the Guiana Space Centre (CSG),
-	The improvement of a global tourism offer of the CSG and the expectations regarding the welcoming of visitors,
-	A strong demand for information about the CSG and space activity in French Guiana.
Purpose of the contract:
This information concerns the contracts for works related to museum displays, scenography and graphic aspects.
The work for the CNES/CSG, at the site of the Space Museum at the Guiana Space Centre in Kourou (French Guiana), falls within a demanding operational context (project integrating an architectural and a scenographic component, CSG environment, location), which the contractor will need to take into account in their bid.
Please note that the renovation project is also the subject of a BIM-GEM (Building Information Modelling - Management-Operation-Maintenance) strategy from the design stage through to the use of the structure.
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months. These activities are part of the renovation of the Space Museum.

Work to be carried out will include:
-	AV/MM design, production: design, production, development (in French and English), integration, adjustments and on-site testing (correct operation check as well as “VBF” in French, regular operational testing as well as “VSR” in French) of audiovisual and multimedia devices;
-	Supply and installation of AV/MM equipment: technical studies, supply, preparation, programming, integration (in-workshop and on-site), transport, on-site installation, testing and adjustments (correct operation check, regular operational testing) of audiovisual and multimedia equipment

title: Iris with IOC - AOC (Airline Operational Communication) Applications for the Electronic Flight Bag
description:
The ESA Iris Initial Operational Capability (IOC), in addition to Air Traffic Management (ATM) services, has the ambition to be the vehicle for Electronic Flight Bag (EFB) IP applications, thus facilitating the transition of airlines to the digital age. 

These IP-enabled applications are specific to the Airline Information Services Domain (AISD). The applications are utilised by airline crew on the Electronic Flight Bag (EFB) for flight operations, airline administrative and engine and maintenance purposes.

This Statement of Work (SoW) specifies the integration, end-to-end testing and demonstration of EFB applications in an operational-like environment in the Iris Test Facility. This activity will culminate in a demonstration to ESA in the Iris Test Facility.

title: Regional Resource On-boarding to the Network of Resources
description:
The scope of this procurement shall support integration of regional resources (inter alia data, algorithms, models) into the Network of Resources (NoR) portfolio and manage the interaction with the regional community. As fragmentation is a major obstacle to efficiently use the “bring the user to the data” approach, regional resources shall be integrated in a partnership approach as much as possible into existing NoR Exploitation Platforms. 

Exploitation Platforms are a central element of ESA's Earth Observation (EO) Innovation Europe concept, which aims at the integration of EO data and information for a much broader use, for scientific, social and economic purposes, as well as for the generation of new commercial applications and services. 

The EO NoR initiative promotes the use of European resource and platform services to facilitate a simplified and efficient exploitation of EO data in cloud environments. The initiative incentivizes providers to contribute to a common framework harmonising the access to their services and helping the user to work with the data. ESA conducted an ITT (AO/1-9217/18/I-LG-Procurement of Earth Observation Exploitation Platform Network Resource Services) in 2018. The tender awarded a contract in December 2018 to Cloudeo AG as prime to select under the supervision of ESA, and via ESA’s Best Practices Processes, the services of eligible Resource and Platform Tier Providers. A NoR portal (https://nor-discover.cloudeo.group) lists in an online directory all the onboarded providers together with their NoR service portfolio. 

ESA can sponsor or co-fund scientists and value adding users for eligible research, development and pre-commercial projects. The portal also provides users with links to each providers helpdesk and website.

title: I-HAB BATTERY ELECTRONIC UNIT (BEU)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway – International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Battery Electronic Unit (BEU)in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Battery Electronic Unit (BEU) are part of the power subsystem.
The IHAB Electrical Power Subsystem (IHAB EPS ) includes a set of batteries for energy storage and a set of power management, distribution and switch units that are responsible:
- to control and regulate the battery charging and discharging in sun or during the eclipse phase,
- to control the balancing of all the battery cells during the charging phase
- to connect each battery to the BCDR before the Launch or during the tests and disconnect it before the removal or during the test
- to connect, disconnect and distribute the primary power to other elements of the Gateway when requested.

Description: The Mars Sample Return Programme is a response to the long-running scientific objective to better understand the past history of Mars and characterize its current environment. By acquiring and returning to Earth a rigorously documented set of Mars soil samples, scientists will have the possibility to perform extensive and accurate analyses, having access to the full breadth and depth of scientific instruments available in terrestrial laboratories. The scientific analysis of these returned samples will enable breakthrough advances in: 
• the search for ancient and/or extant life on Mars; 
• the understanding the origin and evolution of Mars as a geological system; 
• the understanding the processes and history of climate on Mars 
• preparing for future human exploration of Mars. The MSR architecture involves four campaign elements: three flight elements and one ground element (Operation Control Centre). Each campaign element consists of one or more functional elements. The three flight elements are: 
• a sample caching rover mission, developed by NASA/JPL, and currently already successfully operating on Mars;
• a Sample Retrieval Lander (SRL) mission, consisting of a NASA/JPL developed lander including a Mars Ascent Vehicle (MAV) as well as the ESA provided Sample Transfer Arm (STA) and Sample Fetch Rover (SFR); 
• and the ESA provided Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) mission. SFR is scheduled to be launched on-board the NASA’s Sample Return Lander. Following a successful landing, the rover will deploy and egress from the platform and traverse to the depot in which the Mars2020 rover will have stored the sample tubes containing soil and rock samples. Leonardo S.p.A acting as Lead Contractor for the Arm and Gripper Subsystem (AGS), under contract with the MSR-SFR Prime Contractor Airbus Defense and Space Ltd to the European Space Agency. As part of this contract (Phase B2 ATP), Leonardo will release an Invitation to Tender (ITT) looking for a supplier of the EGSE for Arm and Gripper Subsystem.
The EGSE will include motor drivers, heater drivers and sensor acquisition drivers, in order to control all the AGS units, i.e. all 6 joints, Gripper, HDRMs, RRB, at the same time.
It also includes all cables from EGSE to the AGS electrical interfaces. The SW will be developed by Leonardo.

title: I-HAB PORTABLE EQUIPMENT PANELS (PEPs)
description: The Cislunar Gateway – International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Portable Equipment Panels (PEPs) in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.The PEPs are part of the power subsystem that includes a set of batteries for energy storage and a set of power management, distribution and switch units that are responsible to control and regulate the battery charging and discharging in sun or during the eclipse phase; to control the balancing of all the battery cells during the charging phase; to connect each battery to the BCDR before the Launch or during the tests and disconnect it before the removal or during the test; to connect, disconnect and distribute the primary power to other elements of the Gateway when requested; to convert the primary power into secondary power to supply the various internal loads and heaters by switchable and protected power lines.From functional point of view the IHAB EPS is composed by two main power chains. Each main power chain (PWR-CHA and PWR-CHB) is supplied by one isolated primary power domain: Primary Power Domain A1 & A2 supply the PWR-CHA; Primary Power Domain B1 & B2 supply the PWR-CHB.All the functional blocks at this level and as part of power chain A or power chain B are indicated respectively as PPDA-A (Primary Power Distribution Assembly ChA) and PPDA-B for ChB.All the functional blocks of IHAB EPS at Level 2 are indicated respectively as SPCD-A1 and SPCDA2 (Secondary Power Conversion & Distribution – ChA1 and ChA2) and SPCD-1B and SPCD-2B for ChB1 and ChB2. Each primary power domain A & B is constituted by two primary power isolated feeds named A1 & A2 for the domain A, and B1 & B2 for the domain B.The PEPs are designed to ensure common standard Gateway power and data interface for portable equipment at various locations for science and crew systems support. The PEPs will have physical, electrical and data interfaces to be accommodate in a single panel and accessible by crew. For this reason each PEP will provide one variable 3-28Vdc voltage output rated at 8 A and one fixed 120Vdc outputs voltage rated at 10 A to portable equipment via two standard power utility outlets accommodated into two identical standard circular connectors named “J1” and “J2” and one auxiliary at 120Vdc output voltage rated at 10 A to power crew support equipment (i.e. USB hubs, USB charger) accommodated into one blind-mate connector named “J3”. The PEP will also provide one data outlet for access to the Gateway Ethernet network (J4) and a set of switches, digital displays, trim resistors and LEDs. This is to provide a visual indication of the status of the power outlets and also to allow a control the power status as well as reset a faulted condition on each power outlets by crew. Each PEP communicate with the C&DH via 133 Mil bus interfaces. This is: to receive commands to control the power outlets (i.e. power ON/OFF and fault condition reset) and for setting the voltage levels of variable power outputs; to distribute periodically the internal HK data and for reporting of anomaly events and protection conditions.Further information concerning the I-HAB campaign can be found on the Agency’s website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

description:

title: EO Network of Resources - Best Practices ITT to procure services from resource and platform tier providers
description:
Exploitation Platforms are a central element of ESA's Earth Observation (EO) Innovation Europe concept, which aims at the integration of EO data and information for a much broader use, for scientific, social and economic purposes, as well as for the generation of new commercial applications and services. 

The EO Network of Resources (NoR) initiative promotes the use of European resource and platform services to facilitate a simplified and efficient exploitation of EO data in cloud environments. The initiative incentivizes providers to contribute to a common framework harmonising the access to their services and helping the user to work with the data.

ESA conducted an ITT (AO/1-9217/18/I-LG-Procurement of Earth Observation Exploitation Platform Network Resource Services) in 2018. The tender awarded a contract in December 2018 to Cloudeo AG as prime to select under the supervision of ESA, and via ESA’s Best Practices Processes, the services of eligible Resource and Platform Tier Providers.

A NoR portal (https://nor-discover.cloudeo.group) lists in an online directory all the onboarded providers together with their NoR service portfolio. ESA can sponsor or co-fund scientists and value adding users for eligible research, development and pre-commercial projects. The portal also provides users with links to each providers helpdesk and website.

This intended tender is for the selection of Resource Tier and Platform Tier providers using cloud services with collocated Sentinel and non-Sentinel data.

Resource Tier and Platform Tier providers wishing to contribute to the NoR service directory are invited to provide a proposal. The tender process is made as simple as possible for interested service providers to respond to.

title: MSR-ERO –  First Batch of Mechanical Ground Support Equipment (MGSE Batch 1)
description:
The Mars Sample Return – Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agency’s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement action is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO MGSE Batch 1 to be used for the Spacecraft integration and test activities, in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
In detail the hardware subject of this procurement selection will be:
•	Vertical Integration Stand (VIS) – used to support S/C Modules and S/C Composite during most of the integration and test phases. 
•	S/C Lifting Device – used for S/C Modules and S/C Composite hoisting operations, with CoG adjustment capabilities to cover different S/C configurations
•	Orbit Insertion Module (OIM) Handling Adapter – interfacing the OIM and the S/C Composite and the integration stands and trolleys (e.g. VIS) used during the assembly and test phases and during transport
•	OIM Clamp Band (Ø1666mm) - used to secure the OIM and the S/C Composite to the OIM Adapter during all AIT phases, and to a vibration adapter during Mechanical Dynamic Tests 
•	Return Module (RM) Handling Adapter – used to interface the RM of the Spacecraft to supporting MGSE (e.g. VIS) 
•	RM Clamp Band (Ø1194mm) – used to secure the RM to the Handling Adapter during Module Level activities
•	S/C Mass Dummy (requested as an option) – used to proof load MGSE and to validate test setups where the S/C Composite is suspended

title: I-HAB  Mechanical Ground Support Equipment batch 1 (MGSE1)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Mechanical Ground Support Equipment batch 1 (MGSE1) in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Mechanical Ground Support Equipment batch 1 (MGSE1) are part of the support equipment needed for the integration of the I-HAB Gateway module.
The Mechanical Ground Support Equipment batch 1 (MGSE1)and relevant aim under this ITT are: 
Handling adapter Ring (needed to interface with the module through the LVA I/F for the handling sustaining and lifting purposes interfacing with: the lifting devices, the Integration Rotating Stand and to the Transport Container )
Lifting brackets (needed to interface with the module through the front cone flange (the one with 180 bolts) I/F for the handling sustaining and lifting purposes interfacing with: the lifting devices, and to the Transport Container )
Handling/test clamp band (needed to constraint the Handling Ring to the the LVA I/F)
Integration & Rotating Stand (needed to set the module in horizontal position with the required angle position to facilitate the integration and test activities)
Axial & Radial Hatches opening kits (needed to set the hatch doors in open position in safe way)
Modular Working platform (needed to allow accessibility for the preparation. Integration and test of all components to be integrated in I-HAB)
Horizontal Lifting Device (needed to displace the module in various configuration from the IRS to the TSC, to the tilting trolley and vieversa with the module in horizontal configuration)
Vertical Lifting Device (needed to displace the module in various configuration from the Tilting trolley to the facility test RIG and to the launch transport trolley and viceversa with the module in vertical configuration)
The Mechanical Ground Support Equipment batch 1 (MGSE1) are expected to be compatible with Human Factors for Human Space Flight.
Further information concerning the I-HAB campaign can be found on the Agencys website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

title: I-HAB Fluidic Ground Support Equipment (FGSE)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. 
The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Fluidic Ground Support Equipment for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Fluidic Ground Support Equipment are part of the equipment belonging to the I-HAB Gateway module.
 The Fluidic Ground Support Equipment are the needed items to perform the fluidic checks on all fluidic components and systems of the I-HAB module.
They will allow the fluidic qualification and acceptance tests on all ducts, tubes, pumps, radiators, cold plates valves and circuit partial and complete that will be installed inside to the I-HAB module.
The Fluidic Ground Support Equipment will permit the following activities and tests:
	- Liquid filling HFE 7200, Water/Glycol mixture solution, Water etc.
-	Flushing with gas and liquids
-	Test support with the I-HAB thermal control system (providing fluids at required pressure, temperature and flow)
-	Proof pressure tests with gas and liquids
-	Leakage test with tracing gas (helium) or through the pressure decay methods, monitoring the internal pressure behavior
-	Gas filling, Nitrogen helium, Oxygen 
The Fluidic Ground Support Equipment is expected to be safe and in according to the European and USA rules for dedicated fluidic equipment and servicer Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.
Further information concerning the I-HAB can be found on the Agencys website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

title: I-HAB – GAS trap
description:
The Cislunar Gateway – International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for GAS trap for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The TCS GAS trap is part of the equipment belonging to the I-HAB Gateway module.
The Gas Trap Unit (GTU) will be part of the Active Thermal Control System (ATCS) internal loop (working fluid: propylene glycol/water mix)
It is composed by the degassing device, a gas chamber, a manual gas relief valve, a fluid inlet and outlet welded to ATCS loop. Its function is to separate the bubbles of non-condensable gas from the coolant liquid matrix. The GAS trap is expected to be compatible with Human Factors for Human Space Flight.
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

title: I-HAB Harness (HRNS)
description:

title: ECLS Valves - I-HAB Positive Pressure Relief Assembly (PPRA)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025.
 The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada.
 The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration.
 The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly.
 It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the Contractors for the ECLS Positive Pressure Relief Assembly for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Positive Pressure Relief Assy (PPRA) protects the module structure from catastrophic failure due to over-pressurization.
 The valve assembly consists of a mechanical relief valve (Positive Pressure Relief Valve or PPRV) and a motor driven valve (Shut Off Valve or SOV) mounted in series used to provide a second barrier toward vacuum when the valve is not operating.
 The relief valve opens automatically when the pressure difference reaches the cracking pressure and closes automatically when it falls below the reseat pressure.
 The pneumatic section (PPRA/PPRV) will be equipped with a non-propulsive vent mounted on the external side of the primary structure.
 Manual override and position indication are required.
 The ITT is primarily applicable for the complete PPRA but offers for PPRV or SOV will also be considered.
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

title: ECLS Valves - I-HAB  Manual Pressure Equalization Valve (MPEV)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration.

title: I-HAB - High Capacity Mass Memory (HCMM)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway – International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESA’s contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. 

The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ‘basecamp’ for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor High Capacity Mass Memory (HCMM for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The High Capacity Mass Memory will be part of the Avionics subsystem.
The HCMM corresponds to the user memory function of the GATEWAY hosting the data recorded during all the missions by the astronauts.
The High Capacity Mass Memory is expected to be compatible with Human Factors for Human Space Flight.

title: X-BAND RADIO FREQUENCY SCOE
description:
The Mars Sample Return – Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agency’s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the X-Band Radio Frequency SCOE (XRFS), to be used for the Spacecraft integration and test activities, in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The X-band Radio Frequency SCOE (also referred to as XRFS, RF SCOE or TT&C SCOE) is the EGSE element in charge for supporting measurements of the RF performance of the on-board Communication Subsystem and for implementing the RF TM/TC communication between the Ground Testing equipment (namely, the TMTC Front End) and the Spacecraft. 
The RF SCOE directly interfaces, on the Spacecraft side, with the on-board Communication Subsystem, either via Antenna test caps or with a direct RF connection to the waveguides of the RFDU through dedicated EGSE waveguide assembly. In addition to the RF interfaces, the RF SCOE directly interfaces via digital lines the on-board Communication Subsystem (TC inputs and TM outputs) for BER evaluation.

The Cislunar Gateway ? International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESA?s contribution of an infrastructure 
element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization 
requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and 
Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to 
support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a ?basecamp? for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller 
than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to 
be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two 
weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for 
the Deployable Radiator for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Deployable Radiator is part of the I-HAB External ATCS (Active Thermal Control System).
It is composed of 2 wings, folded at launch and capable to deploy on-orbit, to 
increase the available radiative area.
The radiator shall be capable to rotate its longitudinal axis in a definite number 
of positions, to exploit the heat rejection capability at the maximum extent, 
by avoiding the direct solar heat flux impingement.
Each wing is constituted 
of 4 honeycomb panels, equipped with OSR (Optical Solar Reflectors) or 
provided with a paint with equivalent thermo-optical properties. 
Each panel s
hall host, and protect from the external environment (e.g. MMOD), two independent 
coolant fluid loops. Adequate heat rejection capability shall be ensured in off-nominal 
conditions with only one loop active.

The Deployable Radiator is expected to be compatible with the Human Space Flight 
and Gateway Program Requirements.

title: CLRR - Missions Operations Centre - remote management capacity on existing systems
description:
At the European Spaceport, the new Missions Operations Centre aims at enhanced capabilities of the Launch Range for centralized supervision of operations, in particular by fostering the remote operability as well as new enhanced management capabilities.
This Missions Operations Centre will be interfaced with several equipments of the Launch Range systems such as for the Telemetry operating 2 on-site antenas, and for the Localisation operating a maximum of 4 radars....
This activity pertains to the implementation of these remote management capabilities carrying out the development of an hight level software layout and system interfacing the existing Launch Range equipment or anyway the enhancement of the latter.

title: CLRR - Operational Software evolution (CDO-BLA project)
description: In the frame of the Core Launch Range Renewal development aiming at enhanced capabilities, the measure system of the Launch Range encompasses systems that compute the Telemetry data delivered by antennas, the localisation data provided by the radars, the Telecommand system. The Localisation software, after calculating the launcher position and its speed, communicates in real time the information to several operational sytem users. The Telemetry system processes the CVI extraction data coming from the downrange stations and provides with the onboard launcher information to several operational systems, in particular to the localisation. The mission analysis system performs, at least twice during a launch campaign preparation, the customisation of the specific configuration of the sensors implemented during the launch. The purpose of this activity is to carry out the evolution / adaptation of all these above measure system operational software as well as the mission analysis software and the in-flight safety submission software. It foresees also the implementation of upgraded features fostering the operational flexibility with the possibility to set the configuration depending on the perfomed activity (maintenance, launch day, training..) or the operational system implemented.

title: CLRR - Missions Operations Centre - network
description: At the European Spaceport, the new Missions Operations Centre aims at enhanced capabilities of the Launch Range for centralized supervision of operations, in particular by fostering the remote operability as well as new enhanced management capabilities. The several operational systems and IT activities will lay on LAN networks such as the core and nodal operational network (e.g. ACDC), the operator station access network (e.g. R.A.P.), operational Launch Range network (e.g. R.O.C.K.), operational far remote links network (e.g. R.O.L.L.) including also the Administration and Management Network (e.g. R.E.M.). The purpose of this activity is to carry out the design of these secured LAN networks dedicated to the operational activities, which involves hardware interfaces such as network equipment (e.g. router and switch) and other physical layer equipment .

title: I-HAB  Independent Software Verification & Validation (ISVV)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025.
 The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada.
 The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space andact as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration.
 The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly.
 It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for I-HAB Independent Software Verification & Validation (ISVV) in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The I-HAB Independent Software Verification & Validation (ISVV) is part of the support equipment to integrate and test the I-HAB Gateway module.
The I-HAB Independent Software Verification & Validation (ISVV) function is a technicalactivity performed by a team independent of the developer, aimed to increase the reliability of the Software product and to improve the quality of the development process.

title: UHF-Band Low Gain Antennas (LGA) and Radio Frequency Distribution Unit (UHF LGA & RFDU)
description:
The Mars Sample Return – Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.

Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agency’s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO UHF- band Low Gain Antennas (UHF LGAs) and Radio Frequency Distribution Unit (UHF RFDU) it in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The UHF LGAs and RFDU (UHF band Low Gain Antennas and Radio Frequency Distribution Unit) shall comprise:
-	Two UHF Low Gain antennas (named “UHF ANT” or “UHF LGA”), one located on –X side (UHF ANT1) and one on +Y side (UHF ANT2) of the ERO S/C. 
-	A Radio Frequency distribution units (UHF RFDU) comprising two RF switches and a set of 8 coaxial cables 
-	Ancillaries (Dust caps, RF loads)
Note: UHF transceiver is not part of the LGA/RFDU procurement

The main function of the UHF LGAs:
•	Signal radiation, i.e. conversion from guided transmission (coaxial I/F) to radiated waveform in UHF band forward link frequency band (only for ANT1)
•	Signal reception, i.e. conversion from radiated waveform to guided transmission (coaxial I/F) in UHF band return link frequency band (for both antennas)

The main function of the UHF Radio Frequency Distribution is to ensure: 
•	the transmit routing of the high power RF signal from the UHF-band Transceivers to the UHF-band antennas 
•	the receive routing of the RF signal from the UHF-band antennas to the UHF-band Transceivers

The UHF LGAs and RFDU shall operate in the following bands:
• UHF-Band Forward Link (Orbiter to Mars Asset) : 428 MHz – 450 MHz
• UHF-Band Return Link (Mars Asset to Orbiter) : 387 MHz – 410 MHz

title: MSR-ERO OIM-RM Separation System
description:
The Mars Sample Return ? Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL
led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO Separation System between
Return Module and Orbit Insertion Module in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The RM-OIM Separation System is one of the platform equipment belonging to the MSR-ERO spacecraft (S/C).

title: I-HAB   External Secondary Structures (ESS)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway ? International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESA?s contribution 
of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability 
and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from 
USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure 
designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and 
act as a ?basecamp? for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller 
than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be 
occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to 
two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of 
the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for External Secondary 
Structures for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The External Secondary Structures is part of the equipment belonging to 
the I-HAB Gateway module.
The External Secondary Structures (ESS) are housed outside the pressurized 
volume of the module. They are basically structural assemblies made of AA 
and/or CFRP me
mbers mounted on I-HAB primary structure rings in order to have a structural d
ecoupling that allows a free pressure shell expansion induced by its internal pressure. 
ESS structures have the task of carrying external fixed or ORU equipment. 
These structures accommodate also Extra-Vehicular Robotics Interfaces
The External Secondary Structures are expected to be compatible with Human 
Factors for Human Space Flight and Gateway Program Standards.
Notwithstanding 
the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for 
visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set o
f geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.
Further 
information concerning the I-HAB can be found on the Agency?s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Ro

title: I-HAB Meteorite Protection Structures (MPS)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an 
infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and 
utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA,
Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed
to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp
for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will
require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew
of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise
operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Meteorite 
Protection Structures for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Meteorite Protection Structures are part of the equipment belonging to the I-HAB Gateway module.
The Meteorite Protection Structures are housed outside the pressurized volume 
of the module via dedicated brackets that will be sized by the MPS developer. 
It acts has protective shield against the on orbit micro-meteoroids. The main
component are thin metallic panels in Aluminum Alloy, spaced from the pressure shell
and external critical equipment, provide shielding from the MMOD environment during IHAB mission. 
MMOD performance will be guaranteed from the concept that is addressed by the MPS
specification. Whereas the developer will be responsible for the other technical
aspects such as the mechanical performance specified by the contract specification.
If necessary to meet MMOD requirements, ballistic fabric layers (eg. Kevlar) integrated 
in MLI can be implemented on top of the shell / equipment. These protection if needed 
will be under TASI perimeter. Thus they will be not part of the contract.
Docking ports are protected by MLI reinforced with Nextel and / or Kevlar, if acceptable
from outgassing and temperature exposure point of view. This solution is derived
from that of the Halo Hatch and is not part of the contract.

The Meteorite Protection Structures The internal secondary structure is expected
to be compatible with Human Factors for Human Space Flight 
and Gateway Program Standards and Environment.
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for
visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical
return requirements/targets to be considered.
Further information concerning the I-HAB can be found on the Agencys website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

title: MSR-ERO X-Band Radio Frequency Distribution Assembly (X-RFDA)
description:
The Mars Sample Return Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agencys website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO X- band Radio Frequency Distribution Assembly unit it in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The X-RFDA (X band Radio Frequency Distribution Assembly) shall ensure: 

	the transmit routing of the low power RF signal from the Transponder X-band transmitters output to the X-band TWTAs (amplifiers) input 
	the transmit routing of the high power RF signal from each X-band TWTAs output to any of the X-band antennas (LGA1, LGA2, MGA, HGA) 
	the receive routing of the RF signal from any of the X-band antennas (LGA1, LGA2, MGA, HGA) to the Transponder X-band receivers input 

The RFDA shall operate in the following bands:
	Uplink band: 7145 - 7190 MHz 
	Downlink band: 8400 - 8450 MHz

title: I-HAB  External AIT activities (EXA)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for I-HAB External AIT activities (EXA) in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The I-HAB External AIT activities (EXA) is part of the support equipment to integrate and test the I-HAB Gateway module.
The I-HAB External AIT activities (EXA) aim is to cover for the C/D slice 2 program phases with relevant AIT figures consistent of (at max support phase):
-	AIT Mechanical operator
-	AIT Fluidic/Alignment operator
-	AIT EGSE expert operator
-	AIT Functional Operator
-	AIT QA operator 

The foreseen activities to be developed are related to the operational execution of the following tasks:
-	Integration and test activities documentation examination
-	Documentation preparation and configuration control of hardware and tooling
-	Operative AIT tasks execution
-	Test conduction and participation
-	Test set-up preparation
-	Handling of the flight hardware and GSE 
-	Work could be performed in shift and in holidays time
-	While the standard place of tasks execution will be in Italy, Turin, some test activities shall be performed in external country (The Netherlands, Germany, or in France, as needed) 
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.
Further information concerning the I-HAB can be found on the Agencys website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

title: I-HAB Harness (HRNS)
description:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. 
 The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. 
It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Harness (HRNS) for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Harness (HRNS) are part of the equipment belonging to the I-HAB Gateway module.
The harness (HRNS) function is to provide distribution and separation of power, analogue and digital signal, commands and lines to the different unit and/or interface. 
The harness will include the following items:
	Cables and connectors required to perform the electrical links
	Shielding provisions for the wiring
	Over shielding provision for the bundles when deemed necessary by EMC engineering for fulfilling magnetic and electrical fields cleanliness requirements or to limit dielectric charging from high energy electrons surrounding the spacecraft.
	Connectors accessories and protective caps and savers, edge protections and grommets	Harness fixation devices and associated hardware required to install the cabling on the structure and the connectors bracket mountedThe Harness (HRNS) is expected to be compatible with Human Factors for Human Space Flight.Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.Further information concerning the I-HAB can be found on the Agencys website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

title: EL3 phase A-B1 - Implementation of EL3 GNC Critical Technology
description:
The purpose of the present Invitation to Tender (ITT) is to implement theprocurement of the European Large Logistic Lander (EL3) Guidance, Navigation and Control (GNC) critical technology in the frame of the EL3 Phase A/B1 study.
The European Large Logistic Lander (EL3) is a key capability, based on Ariane 64, to deliver a science or logistical payload to a location on the lunar surface. 
Its missions can be cargo delivery missions or a sample return mission or science and/or technology demonstration missions.
The Bidder selection will be performed in accordance with ESA Best Practices.
The activity which is the subject of the present Invitation to Tender is part of the European Exploration Envelope Programme Period 2. Therefore, recipients of the present ITT are requested to note that the Agency can only consider a tender from a company or organisation be it as Prime Contractor or as a Subcontractor residing in an ESA Member or Associated State.
Notification of interest and requests for clarification shall be sent in an official way to the address indicated on the Letter of Invitation (when published).

title: MSR-ERO ¡V Central Check-Out System (CCS)
description:
The Mars Sample Return ¡V Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agency¡¦s website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO Central Check-Out System (CCS), to be used for the Spacecraft integration and test activities, in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The CCS will be used both on the AVM and PFM spacecraft AIT campaigns and Launch Campaign, being in charge of providing supervisor control, test execution and simulation environments together at the same time. The CCS shall be the unique manager and supervisor of the overall EGSE activities during S/C testing, therefore it shall be able to provide reliable monitor and control facilities in order to assess the correct functioning of the on board unit during all test flow. The CCS will be in charge to control and monitor the operations of the other EGSE elements as well. 
In particular, the CCS is used for:
X	Generating, editing and debugging of automated test scripts and their execution and control in the frame of the S/C testing
X	Sending Telecommands to on-board units (via other EGSE elements with direct interfaces to the Spacecraft) 
X	Reception, de-commutation and monitoring of real-time S/C Telemetry
X	Recording and archiving the S/C Telemetry and other Test data from-to Spacecraft with proper time tagging 
X	Data presentation - including alpha-numeric and graphical synoptic displays - of both Telemetry and Telecommand packets/parameters in raw and engineering formats
X	SCOE communication and remote control
X	Archiving of raw Telemetry Frames 
It is a specific program requirement that CCS uses Terma¡¦s CCS5 software as Master Test Processor.

title: MSR-ERO Low Gain Antenna (LGA)
description:
The Mars Sample Return Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agencys website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO X Band LGA unit it in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Low Gain Antenna function is to provide simultaneously:
-	Signal radiation, i.e. conversion from guided transmission (waveguide I/F) to radiated waveform in X band downlink frequency band
-	Signal reception, i.e. conversion from radiated waveform to guided transmission to guided transmission (waveguide I/F) in X band uplink frequency band
The LGA shall operate in the following bands:
-	Uplink band: 7145 - 7190 MHz 
-	Downlink band: 8400 - 8450 MHz 

The LGA shall also provide a peak gain of between 6 and 8dBi and a coverage of +/-90° off-boresight.

title: Antenna Reflector Assembly Sub-System for ESPRIT HALO
description:
The HALO Lunar Communication Subsystem (HLCS) will serve as a data link on the LOP-G Cislunar mission, which is an international framework and stepped approach for lunar and further Deep Space exploration purposes. The communication system located on this module provide the link for the Lunar system. The currently planned launch date is in last Quarter 2023.
Within the HLCS there are two S&Ka-Band High Gain Reflectors where the ARA (Antenna Reflector Assembly) is located and it comprises a sub-system formed by the Main reflector, the sub reflector and the struts.
The ARASS baseline configuration as required by the HLCS Prime is the manufacturing of 2 Flight Model assemblies, together with 1 Structural Model, as well as the necessary GSEs such as Unit Check Out Equipment.
Thales Alenia Space France (TAS-F) has been selected by ESA to be the ESPRIT HALO Prime Contractor. In turn TAS-F has selected SENER Aeroespacial S.A. as responsible for HLCS design, development and verification activities during phases B, C/D and E1, amongst them, the ARA. The selection of subcontractors is conducted in line with the Code of Best Practices, as tailored to the specific programmatic frame of ESPRIT HALO HLCS. 
In this framework, SENER Aeroespacial S.A. will release an ITT for the procurement of the ARASS. Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.

description:
PLATO (PLAnetary Transits and Oscillations of stars) is the European Space Agency (ESA)
M3 (medium-class) astronomical science mission for the search of exo-planets. This is per-formed by detecting and characterizing transit signature of exo-planets in front of the parent

title: FLEX  ITT#12  FLEX PLM / Mechanical Ground Support Equipment
description:
The FLuORescence Imaging Spectrometer (FLORIS) is 
the Instrument of the FLuorescence Explorer Mission 
(FLEX) of Earth Explorer 8 (EE8) mission, 
4th ?Fast-Track? (formerly known as Opportunity) 
Mission of European Space Agency.
The FLEX (Fluorescence Explorer) mission objective is 
to perform quantitative measurements of the solar 
induced vegetation fluorescence in order to monitor 
vegetation photosynthetic activity.
The FLEX Space Segment consists of a single satellite 
carrying the FLuORescence Imaging Spectrometer (FLORIS) 
push-broom instrument. This high-resolution imaging 
spectrometer will have a 80mm diameter pupil, a ±5° 
Field-of-view and will acquire data in the 500? 780nm
 spectral range, with a sampling of 0.1 nm in the 
oxygen bands (759?769 nm and 686?697 nm) and 0.5?2.0nm 
in the red edge, chlorophyll absorption and 
Photochemical Reflectance Index bands. 
FLEX satellite is flying in tandem with 
Copernicus Sentinel-3. The FLEX mission 
will work in combination with Sentinel-3's 
Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (OLCI) and 
Sea and Land Surface Temperature Radiometer (
SLSTR) that will provide additional information 
about vegetation status (TOA reflectance 
and temperature) and accurate atmospheric correction, 
which are essential for quantitative interpretation 
of fluorescence signal.
Leonardo S. p. A. is the Instrument Prime 
of the FLORIS Instrument contract initially 
placed by ESA. Thales Alenia Space ? France, 
FLEX Satellite Prime has been 
selected at end of Instrument phase B2. At FLEX Prime 
Satellite contract award, the FLORIS Instrument Contract 
has been novated under the full responsibility of the 
Thales Alenia Space France.
In this framework, Leonardo S.p.A. will release an 
Invitation to Tender (ITT) so as to select a 
supplier for the activities relevant to design, 
development and realization of the Floris Instrument 
Mechanical Ground Support Equipment
- FLORIS Instrument Optical Mo

title: Iris with IOC - Header compression
description:
Inmarsat Navigation Ventures Limited is the Prime Contractor on the ESA activity ?Iris with Initial Operational Capability (IOC)"

The objective of this work is to extend the study undertaken by Iris consortium partners on header compression techniques in order to propose and develop a Proof of Concept (PoC) system with header compression implemented, to characterise the performance achieved for different compression technologies, to assess if there is sufficient performance benefit to include header compression within the Iris protocol stack, and to produce a Technology Transfer Package (TTP) that can be made available to Iris air and ground segment equipment developers to enable the selected compression technology to be integrated in/with their equipment.

title: Iris IOC - ATN-IPS Standards Support
description:
The objective of this SoW is to provide Technical Support to the Iris Programme and in support of ATN/IPS standardisation in WP 3.3.2 of the ATN/IPS Project.

Work will be conducted under standards Development and Coordination (WP3.3) which aims to provide a structured approach for ATN/IPS standardisation efforts in order to align and coordinate all standardisation activities aspects of the FOC Work Stream, as well as for the IOC wide programme. The aim is to cover project wide activities transversal to Iris IOC and Iris FOC and requiring continuity of action such as SESAR coordination, and International Standardisation.

The main objective are to produce ATN/IPS technical notes and update the existing technical working papers to serve as input into additional standards activities. Prepare recommendations and inputs into ATN/IPS standards working groups, including AEEC, EUROCAE/RTCA/ICAO and others as appropriate and ensure that the current standards are sufficient for implementation of ATN/IPS functionality within the Iris context

title: CLRR - Renewal of the air cooling system at Payload processing facility EPCU S5
description:
The air conditioning system for the Payload processing facility EPCU S5 (including the 3 1MW cooler units, the 45 air-handling units, the fan coil units as well as the centralised control and regulation system) has become obsolete.
The purpose of this activity is to renew the abovementioned ageing system with state-of-the-art technology in order to better ensure its future availability, reliability and maintainability for operational needs as well as to study the possibility to include new active carbon filtering systems necessary to guarantee the level of property of the clean rooms in particular for some specific missions as scientific ones.

title: MSR-ERO High & Medium Gain Antenna Pointing Assembly (HGA & MGA APA)
description:
The Mars Sample Return Earth Return Orbiter (ERO) is one of three European Space Agency (ESA) contributions to the NASA/JPL led Mars Sample Return Campaign, which aims to return soil and atmospheric samples from the Mars surface to Earth by 2031.
ERO is foreseen for launch in 2026.
Further information concerning the Mars Sample Return campaign and the Earth Return Orbiter mission can be found on the Agencys website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Exploration/Mars_sample_return

The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for the MSR-ERO High & Medium Gain Antenna Pointing Assembly (HGA & MGA APA) unit it in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

APA shall provide the capability to move and point two antenna types: a ca. 2m parabolic reflector for HGA and a 90° offset steerable 20 cm reflector for MGA. The APA is intended as the moving mechanisms plus the relevant electronics.
APA requirements:
-	Dual Axis APM in azimuth and elevation axis arrangement
-	Pointing capability of Azimuth: -180° + 180°, Elevation: 0° -90°
-	Max slew rate: ≥0,5°/s
-	Max Acceleration ≥ 0,01°/s2
-	Pointing accuracy: better than 0.05° for HGA and 0.1° for MGA
-	Position sensing in each axis (resolution 0.008°)
