title: I-HAB TCS Filters
description:
The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an
 infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and
 utilization requirements from 2025. The I-HAB includes contributions from 
USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed
 to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp
 for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will
 require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of
 up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise 
operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for TCS Filter 
for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The TCS Filter function is to protect the pump unit from incoming particles that might
 damage it and to maintain the fluid quality in terms of particulate matter and
 impurity at a desirable level. The action of the filter is carried out both 
in removing ( by capturing in the mesh) free bubbles dispersed in the coolant matrix due
 to marginal ATCS circuit filling procedure and in breaking and/or fragmenting of
 potential concentrated trains or plugs of entrained bubbles.
The filter is composed of a metal mesh contained in a case and it is constantly fluxed
 by the coolant main stream. The filter hydraulic interfaces and internal fluid path 
are selected to ensure the minimum hydraulic pressure drop localized in the device.
The metallic mesh is characterized by two fundamental parameters:
-	Filtration rating
-	Dirt holding capability
The TCS Filter is expected to be compatible with Human Factors for Human Space Flight.
Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for
 visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of 
geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.
Further information
 concerning the I-HAB can be found on the Agencys website here:
https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon

title: Space Rider: OBC/OBDH, MMU, GNSS
description:
The Space Rider Mission definition activities, are progressing and targeting a reusable space transportation system integrated with VEGA-C 
able to operate in-orbit, de-orbit, re-enter, land on ground and be re-launched after limited refurbishment for n.5 subsequent missions.

The Program is very challenging in terms of technology and schedule and will require a dedicated effort from Industry in matching the Agency objectives 
to conduct the Space Rider Program in such a way as to achieve the scientific and technological objectives set for the missions whilst minimizing the costs.

The Invitation to Tender (ITT) is devoted to the development, qualification, flight model implementation and delivery of the two 
On Board Computers/Data Handling (OBC-OBDH) for the AVUM Orbital Module (AOM-OBDH) and for the Reentry Module (RM-OBC) plus a Mass Memory Unit (MMU)
and the two GNSS receivers. 

The contracts will be managed by Industrial Co-Primes (TAS and AVIO) being ESA the final customer of Space Rider Vehicle.

EMITS access problems to documents of this ITT should be referred to: 
Mr. Gian M. Canaparo e-mail: GianMaria.Canaparo@thalesaleniaspace.com

title: Ariane 6 - ITT : Sequencer LLL
description:
Ariane Group intend to issue an ITT for a payload sequencer on December 20th, 2019.
The ITT will be restricted to the companies from Czech republic.
The perimeter of the ITT is to provide a validated preliminary design of a sequencer for the Ariane 6 launcher. 
The sequencer shall allow multiplying the number of separation orders to separate a higher number of payloads than currently possible. The sequencer shall address any type of separation systems.
In this preliminary phase, a preliminary design of the sequencer based on a technical requirement specification (TRS) document is required, confirmed by the functional validation of a breadboard. First a preliminary definition file shall be proposed along with the design of the breadboard. Then the readiness of the breadboard hardware, test bench and test plan will allow starting of the functional tests. Deliverables will include in addition to the test report, a justified matrix of compliance to the TRS and the statement of work, the updated sequencer preliminary file after test, the preliminary sequencer specification, the development plan, the recurrent cost of the sequencer and sizing requirement for design to cost. 
The foreseen duration of the activity is six months.

title: FLEX  ITT#11  FLEX Instrument Harness
description:
The FLuORescence Imaging Spectrometer (FLORIS) is the Instrument of the FLuorescence Explorer Mission (FLEX) of Earth Explorer 8 (EE8) mission, 
4th ?Fast-Track? (formerly known as Opportunity) Mission of European Space Agency.
The FLEX (Fluorescence Explorer) mission objective is to perform quantitative measurements of the solar induced vegetation fluorescence 
in order to monitor vegetation photosynthetic activity.
The FLEX Space Segment consists of a single satellite carrying the FLuORescence Imaging Spectrometer (FLORIS) push-broom instrument. 
This high-resolution imaging spectrometer will acquire data in the 500? 780 nm spectral range, with a sampling of 0.1 nm in the oxygen bands 
(759?769 nm and 686?697 nm) and 0.5?2.0 nm in the red edge, chlorophyll absorption and Photochemical Reflectance Index bands. 
FLEX satellite is flying in tandem with Copernicus Sentinel-3. The FLEX mission will work in combination with Sentinel-3's Ocean and Land 
Colour Instrument (OLCI) and Sea and Land Surface Temperature Radiometer (SLSTR) that will provide additional information about 
vegetation status (TOA reflectance and temperature) and accurate atmospheric correction, which are essential for quantitative interpretation of fluorescence signal.
Leonardo S. p. A. is the Instrument Prime of the FLORIS Instrument contract placed by ESA. Thales Alenia Space France is FLEX Satellite Prime.
In this framework, Leonardo S.p.A. will release an Invitation to Tender (ITT) so as to select a supplier for the activities
relevant to manufacturing and test of FLORIS Instrument Harness.
The FLORIS Instrument Harness (HRN) connects the Instrument Optical Module (IOM) with the Instrument Control Unit (ICU).

title: Iris IOC - Air Segment Design and Roadmap
description:
The objective of the Air Segment Roadmap and Design is for industry partners, to extend the work undertaken during air Segment Studies to produce a technology roadmap for the proposed work in Air Segment Studies. To accommodate this, the following tasks need to be carried out:
?	Take output from system studies (AES Design ? Trade-off Report and AES FOC ?Pre-development Plan) in WP2.1.1.3.1 and WP2.1.1.3.2 to finalise Air Segment Requirements 
?	Provide system design description and justification for proposed AES design output in WP2.1.1.3.1 and WP2.1.1.3.2
?	Provide Air Segment system and functional architecture for proposed AES design output in WP2.1.1.3.1 and WP2.1.1.3.2
?	Take Air Segment Design and roadmap from WP2.1.1.7.1 and WP2.1.1.7.2, prepared by Aircraft manufacturers to provide technical roadmap for proposed Air Segment designs
?	Review Inmarsat Pre-developments plan and provide comments prior to SAR.

The output of Air Segment Roadmap and design should be technology roadmap for each area of study in air Segment Studies WPs (WP2.1.1.3.1 and WP2.1.1.3.2), which is used as input into pre-development as part of Phase 2.

title: EO Network of Resources - Best Practices ITT to procure services from platform tier providers
description:
Exploitation Platforms are a central element of ESA's Earth Observation (EO) Innovation Europe concept, which aims at the integration of EO data and information for a much broader use, for scientific, social and economic purposes, as well as for the generation of new commercial applications and services. 

The EO Network of Resources (NoR) initiative promotes the use of European resource and platform services to facilitate a simplified and efficient exploitation of EO data in cloud environments. The initiative incentivizes providers to contribute to a common framework harmonising the access to their services and helping the user to work with the data.

ESA conducted an ITT (AO/1-9217/18/I-LG-Procurement of Earth Observation Exploitation Platform Network Resource Services) in 2018. The tender awarded a contract in December 2018 to Cloudeo AG, with RHEA and BHO Legal as subcontractors, to select under the supervision of ESA, and via ESA?s Best Practices Processes, the services of eligible Resource and Platform Tier Providers.

A NoR portal will list in its online directory all the selected providers together with their NoR service portfolio which can be procured via a shopping cart. ESA can sponsor scientists and value adding users for eligible research, development and pre-commercial projects to procure such services. A NoR helpdesk staffed with remote sensing and IT experts, working closely with the providers, will support users in the selection of the services, as well as in the application process for sponsoring.

This intended tender is for the selection of Platform Tier providers using cloud services with collocated Sentinel and non-Sentinel data.

Platform Tier providers wishing to contribute to the NoR service directory are invited to provide a proposal. The tender process is made as simple as possible for interested service providers to respond.

title: FLEX_ITT15_FLEX PLM/FIPS GPP
description:
The FLuORescence Imaging Spectrometer (FLORIS) is the Instrument of the FLuorescence Explorer Mission (FLEX) of Earth Explorer 8 (EE8) mission, 4th ?Fast-Track? 
(formerly known as Opportunity) Mission of European Space Agency.
The FLEX (Fluorescence Explorer) mission objective is to perform quantitative measurements of the solar induced vegetation fluorescence in order to 
monitor vegetation photosynthetic activity.
The FLEX Space Segment consists of a single satellite carrying the FLuORescence Imaging Spectrometer (FLORIS) push-broom instrument. This high-resolution imaging 
spectrometer will acquire data in the 500? 780 nm spectral range, with a 
sampling of 0.1 nm in the oxygen bands (759?769 nm and 686?697 nm) and 0.5?2.0 nm in the red edge, chlorophyll absorption and Photochemical Reflectance Index bands. 
The FLEX mission will work in combination with Sentinel-3's Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (OLCI) and Sea and Land Surface Temperature Radiometer (SLSTR) 
that will provide additional information about vegetation status (TOA reflectance and temperature) and accurate atmospheric correction, which are essential 
for quantitative interpretation of fluorescence signal.
Leonardo S. p. A. is the Instrument Prime of the FLORIS Instrument contract placed by ESA. The FLEX Satellite Prime will be selected in a second procurement step. 
At FLEX Prime Satellite contract award, the FLORIS Instrument Contract will be novated under the full responsibility of the FLEX Satellite Prime.
In this framework, Leonardo S.p.A. will release an Invitation to Tender (ITT) so as to select a supplier for the activities relevant to Flex Instrument Performance 
Simulator (FIPS) and Ground Processor Prototype (GPP).
The FIPS and GPP are software tools that will evolve and serve multiple purposes since they will be used:
to support the development and verification of the Space Segment

title: IRIS with Initial Operation Capability (IOC) - Work Stream 2 - Air Segment System Studies
description:
Inmarsat Navigation Ventures Limited is the Prime Contractor on the ESA activity ?Iris with Initial Operational Capability (IOC)"

The objective of the Air Segment Studies is to extend the work undertaken during Iris Service Evolution to determine how SBB Safety aircraft Satcom terminals should be enhanced to meet the following requirements:
?	Improved performance during aircraft banking
?	Support of RPAS
?	Improved latency performance 
?	Support of operation through HEO satellites
The output of Air Segment Studies in Phase 1 should be a report that summarises technical findings of the work including recommendations for pre-development as part of Phase 2. 

Air Segment suppliers are invited to tender for the provision of;

1.	AES Trade-off report
a.	Banding analysis and requirements for AES design.
b.	AES design
i.	Banking impact of AES design
ii.	AES banking impact for RPAS 
iii.	Delta AES design for performance improvement 
iv.	Impact of HEO on AES design 
c.	Pre-development plan
d.	Support to market consolidation through business model, business case and stakeholder engagement activities including budgetary cost, risk associated with development, definition of work for predevelopment programme, development, integration and test plan, expected TRL achieved and validation activities

title: Iris with IOC - Work Stream 1
description:
Inmarsat Navigation Ventures Limited is the Prime Contractor on the ESA activity ?Iris with Initial Operational Capability (IOC)"

Based on the Iris Precursor Ground and Air technology, IOC Pilot will be based on trials involving up to 20 aircraft in commercial passenger service. 

Air Navigation Service Providers are invited to tender for the provision of;

1.	Planning and management of IRIS with IOC Pilot Flight Trials Activities. Adaptation of their platform to support satcom datalink. Contribution to data collection and analysis. 
2.	Support to an IRIS Service Provider (ISP) towards an application to EASA ATM/ANS Organisation Approval (AOA).
3.	Support to market consolidation through business model, business case and stakeholder engagement activities including coordination with SESAR programme.

title: BIOMASS Instrument Bench
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of the Instrument Bench by Airbus Defence and Space GmbH as a Core team 
member of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The Contractor (i.e. the equipment Contractor) shall be responsible for the 
provisions of all materials, manpower, facilities, supplies, tools, unit, 
documentation and support services as may be required to design, 
manufacture, assemble, test and deliver to Airbus Defence and Space the 
Biomass Instrument Bench, which consists of the Instrument Trolley and the 
Instrument EQM Structure.

The instrument trolley shall be used to manipulate the Biomass Instrument 
during its assembling, integration and test (AIT) procedure.
The Instrument EQM structure shall be used as mechanical support of the 
Biomass Instrument EQM Subsystems during the Biomass Instrument EQM AIT 
campaign.

The concepts of both assemblies are provided as engineering solution in the 
specification as a guideline.

In this framework, the present Invitation to Tender is addressed to 
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose 
registered office is established in such Member and Participating States 
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating 
State in the ESA Earth Observation Envelope Programme 4.

title: BIOMASS Instrument RF SCOE
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of the Instrument RF SCOE by Airbus Defence and Space GmbH as a Core team 
member of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The Instrument RF SCOE is the Electrical Ground Support Equipment (EGSE) counterpart to the RF interfaces of the Instrument. 
It is connected to the Instrument via the RF ports of the different 
integration and test levels ( DCU, DCU + ASW, DCU + CDN, INES, Instrument
and Satellite level) and is used for the verification of the RF paths 
(in transmit and receive). 

The Instrument RF SCOE shall provide all functionalities and interfaces 
for testing on DCU, DCU + ASW, DCU + CDN, INES, Instrument and Satellite level. 
It includes all RF measurement equipment needed to analyse the Instrument 
signals as well as signal generators to stimulate and test the Instrument 
receive chains. 

The Biomass Instrument project comprises six hardware and software 
integration levels, further detailed in RF SCOE SSOW and Specification. 
On all levels, testing and verification of the Biomass Instrument will be 
performed.

title: BIOMASS SC Test Facilities
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in 
Spring 2013 in Graz, Austria. The overall objective of the mission is to 
reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide spatial distribution and dynamics 
of forest biomass in order to improve current assessments and future 
projections of the global carbon cycle.
 
The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission, 
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and 
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement 
of Biomass SC Test Facilities by Airbus Defence and Space Ltd as Prime 
contractor of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the services of a test house to 
perform certain tests required for the SC Test Facilities.

The SC Test Facilities are required to test and qualify the Biomass S/C for 
the mechanical launch environment and in-orbit environment through 
vibration, acoustic, shock, EMC, mass properties and thermal vacuum 
testing, and the instrument PFM for thermal vacuum, RF and EMC testing. The 
test campaigns required to run are Instrument PFM, SM test campaign and PFM 
campaign

In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be addressed to 
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose 
registered office is established in such Member and Associated States 
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating 
State in the ESA Biomass project. 

The following States are participating in the said Programme: Austria,
Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany,
Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, 
Romania, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and the United Kingdom.

title: BIOMASS GSE Test Cables
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in 
Spring 2013 in Graz, Austria. The overall objective of the mission is to 
reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide spatial distribution and dynamics 
of forest biomass in order to improve current assessments and future 
projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission, 
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and 
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement 
of Biomass GSE Test Cables by Airbus Defence and Space Ltd as Prime 
contractor of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development, production,
testing and delivery of the GSE Test Cables.

The Ground Support Equipment (GSE) Test Cables are required to connect the 
necessary Special Check Out Equipment (SCOEs) with the Biomass Spacecraft 
to allow testing and verification. The cables will interface between SCOEs? 
(e.g. Power SCOE, RF SCOE) non-flight harness, and provide a flight quality 
connection to the Spacecraft during cleanroom testing and during 
environmental tests within a chamber. The test cables will be used to 
deliver: Power, RF and data depending on the SCOE.

In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be addressed to 
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose 
registered office is established in such Member and Associated States 
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating 
State in the ESA Biomass project. 

The following States are participating in the said Programme: Austria,
Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany,
Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, 
Romania, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and the United Kingdom.

Tenderers are hereby informed that for this ITT, preference may be given to 
tenders containing a substantial involvement of economic operators 
registered in Austria, Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, 
Ireland, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania
, Sweden and Switzerland, provided that:

- the tenders will have been assessed of a good quality (weighted mark of 
at least 55);and

- as representing an acceptable combination between technical quality 
(including risk) and price.

title: Biomass ISVV
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 in Graz, Austria. The overall objective of the mission is to 
reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide spatial distribution and dynamics 
of forest biomass in order to improve current assessments and future 
projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of Biomass ISVV by Airbus Defence and Space Ltd as Prime
contractor of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development, production,
testing and delivery of the ISVV.

The ISVV is the independent software verification and validation of the 
Biomass mission software running on the on board computer and other flight 
hardware. ISVV is an engineering practice intended to improve quality and 
reduce costs of a software product. It is also intended to reduce 
development risks by having an organization independent of the software 
developer to perform verification and validation of the specifications and 
code of a software product.
Software verification and validation activities check the software
against its specifications. Every project must verify and validate the 
software it produces. This is done by:
· checking that each software item meets specified requirements
· checking each software item before it is used as an input to another
activity;
· ensuring that checks on each software item are done, as far as
possible, by someone other than the author
· ensuring that the amount of verification and validation effort is 
adequate
to show each software item is suitable for operational use.

title: PROSPECT IMAGING SYSTEM
description:
The subject ITT addresses part of the PROSPECT Drilling and Sample Analysis package
 development (managed by Leonardo as Prime), due for flight on board the Russian 
Luna-Resource (Luna-27) mission in 2022. As part of PROSPECT an Imaging System 
is foreseen which shall deliver images of drilling and sampling operations. 
This Imaging System is composed of 3 main elements: 
1) a Camera Unit (CU), 2) an Artificial Illumination Unit (AIU) and 
3) an Imaging Support and Interface Unit (ISIU). 

The Camera Unit has been subjected to ITT AO130114 and shall be considered 
as a CFI for the present ITT, whose subject is targeted specifically at Artificial 
Illumination Unit (AIU) and Imaging Support & Interface Unit (ISIU). 

The Camera Unit will acquire static images and video footage of drilling and sampling
operations under both artificial illumination and natural sunlight conditions. 
The AIU and ISIU shall support the Camera Unit providing with proper support, 
interface and artificial illumination.

This procurement aims to identify and / or develop hardware of high technical 
maturity which can fulfil the requirements and which is compatible with the 
cost and schedule constraints of the project. 

The Contractor is also required to support the Prime Contractor responsible by providing
 relevant data associated with the Imaging System HW, to support via HW testing the
 verification of the performance, and to supply Engineering Model HW which can be
 used in overall system tests. This work shall be carried out within the overall scope 
of the running PROSPECT Phase B+ activity.

 Mission (FLEX) of Earth Explorer 8 (EE8) mission, 4th ?Fast-Track? (formerly known as 
Opportunity) Mission of European Space Agency.
The FLEX (Fluorescence Explorer) mission objective is to perform quantitative measurements of the
 solar induced vegetation fluorescence in order to monitor vegetation photosynthetic activity.
The FLEX Space Segment consists of a single satellite carrying the FLuORescence Imaging
 Spectrometer (FLORIS) push-broom instrument. This high-resolution imaging spectrometer will
 acquire data in the 500? 780 nm spectral range, with a sampling of 0.1 nm in the oxygen bands

additional information about vegetation status (TOA reflectance and temperature) and accurate

title: BIOMASS Instrument SCOE
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of the Instrument Electronic System (INES) Satellite Checkout Equipment 
(SCOE) by Airbus Defence and Space GmbH as a Core team 
member of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The Instrument Electronics System (INES) comprises the following subsystems:
- Central Electronics Subsystem (CES) including a Digital Control Unit (DCU), 
 Calibration Distribution Network (CDN), 
 all supported by an Application Software (ASW)
- Power Amplifier Subsystem (PAS)
- Receive Amplifier Subsystem (RAS)

The Feed Array is part of the BIOMASS Antenna System and has the function 
of transmitting and receiving the RF signals to and from the LDR (Large 
Deployable Reflector) by the INES. The LDR is an element of the Platform 
and forms together with the Instrument the SAR Payload.

The primary function of the INES SCOE is to provide the Biomass satellite
platform interfaces to the Instrument before it is integrated onto the 
platform. Hence, the INES SCOE shall provide the same interface types, 
interface connectors and functionalities than the ones provided by the 
platform, allowing interface verification and functional testing on Biomass 
Instrument AIT level prior to delivery to Biomass Satellite system 
integration, where the INES SCOE will be fully replaced by the satellite 
platform.

title: BIOMASS Instrument Receive Amplifier Subsystem (RAS)
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of Receive Amplifier Subsystem (RAS) by Airbus DS GmbH as a Core team 
member of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development (including the
required qualification activities), manufacturing, testing and delivery of
the RAS.

The Receive Amplifier Subsystem (RAS) routes and amplifies the received 
radar echo from the PAS to the CES at low noise for one polarisation. The 
envisaged architecture 1 and architecture 2 for the RAS is shown in the 
Specific Statement of Work (SSOW). The RAS comprises protection for the 
instrument, even if the Instrument is powered off. Degradation of the RAS 
and data unavailability in case of Radio Frequency Interference (RFI) is 
minimized by bandpass filters before or after the LNA, depending on the 
supplier solution after thorough analysis of Scenario 1 and Scenario 2. 

For the two polarisations available, the Biomass Instrument contains two 
identical RAS, one for each polarisation. For the accommodation and 
mechanical envelope of the two RAS on the satellite, the SSOW provides 
the necessary details.

A thorough analysis on the RFI, especially with, but not limited to 
different levels of RFI, image rejection, noise figure, damage levels, 
linearity and dynamic range shall be performed by the Tenderer. 

The Tenderer is requested to provide a detailed proposal describing both 
architectures. The proposal shall also contain for each architecture, the 
corresponding price breakdown supported by PSS forms, a schedule and a 
development plan. The decision to implement architecture 1 or 2 will be 
taken by Airbus DS GmbH / Satellite Prime not later than 6 months after 
the KO based on the contractor phase B2 tasks as described in SSoW.

In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be addressed to
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose
registered office is established in such Member and Associated States
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating
State in the ESA Biomass project. 

The following States are participating in the said Programme: Austria,
Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany,
Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, The Netherlands, Norway, Poland,
Portugal, Romania, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and the United Kingdom.

title: BIOMASS Instrument Central Electronic Subsystem (CES)
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of Central Electronics Subsystem (CES) by Airbus DS GmbH as a Core team 
member of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development (including the
required qualification activities), manufacturing, testing and delivery of
the CES.

The Central Electronics Subsystem (CES) is the heart of the Biomass 
instrument. It is an assembly of several equipments, connected by internal 
harness up to and including a connector bracket and mounted on the MXPZ
panel wall of the Instrument/satellite.

The CES contains all units required to form a full, cold redundant radar 
core including all networks required for internal calibration, plus the 
Boot Software. 

One important EGSE of the CES procurement is the INES SCOE that shall be 
used both at CES level by the contractor and at instrument level by Airbus 
Defence and Space. 

The INES SCOE shall be used to operate, test, and checkout the CES. The 
INES SCOE will also need to offer all interfaces from the satellite 
avionics to the PAS, RAS-V and RAS-H in addition to the functions described 
for the operation of the INES SCOE on CES level. For this purpose, the INES 
SCOE shall provide the same interfaces types, interface connectors and 
functionalities as provided by the satellite avionics, allowing interface 
verification and functional testing on instrument level.

The INES SCOE is expected to be procured by the successful CES bidder under 
Best Practice Open competition and under the management of the CES bidder. 

In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be addressed to
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose
registered office is established in such Member and Associated States
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating
State in the ESA Biomass project.

Description: The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of Central Electronics Subsystem (CES) by Airbus DS GmbH as a Core team 
member of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in 
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development (including the
required qualification activities), manufacturing, testing and delivery of
the CES.

The Central Electronics Subsystem (CES) is the heart of the Biomass 
instrument. It is an assembly of several equipments, connected by internal 
harness up to and including a connector bracket and mounted on the MXPZ
panel wall of the Instrument/satellite.

The CES contains all units required to form a full, cold redundant radar 
core including all networks required for internal calibration, plus the 
Boot Software. 

One important EGSE of the CES procurement is the INES SCOE that shall be 
used both at CES level by the contractor and at instrument level by Airbus 
Defence and Space. 

The INES SCOE shall be used to operate, test, and checkout the CES. The 
INES SCOE will also need to offer all interfaces from the satellite 
avionics to the PAS, RAS-V and RAS-H in addition to the functions described 
for the operation of the INES SCOE on CES level. For this purpose, the INES 
SCOE shall provide the same interfaces types, interface connectors and 
functionalities as provided by the satellite avionics, allowing interface 
verification and functional testing on instrument level.

The INES SCOE is expected to be procured by the successful CES bidder under 
Best Practice Open competition and under the management of the CES bidder. 

In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be addressed to
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose
registered office is established in such Member and Associated States
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating
State in the ESA Biomass project.

title: Biomass Platform and On-Board Data Generation Module for End-to-End Performance Simulator
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in Spring 2013
 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall objective of the mission
 is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide spatial distribution and dynamics of
 forest biomass in order to improve current assessments and future projections of the
 global carbon cycle. For this, a P-band SAR sensor is currently been implemented,
 providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and growth.

With the objective of supporting the development and verification of both Space and
 Ground Segments of the BIOMASS mission, a complete end-to-end simulation chain,
 named Biomass End-to-End Performance Simulator (BEEPS), will be developed.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement of the
 platform and On-Board Data Generation Module (ODGM) to be incorporated into the
 Biomass End-to-End Performance Simulator (BEEPS) for Phases C/D/E1. The supplier
 selection will be made in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

In detail, the scope of this procurement covers the design, development, qualification,
 production and verification of the ODGM. In terms of functionality, the ODGM
 implements the simulation of any platform function needed directly by the instrument
 model or needed in order to generate the data in a format compliant to the space to
 ground interface Space Source Packet data (i.e. RAW data), e.g., by simulating GPS,
 AOCS, temperatures, timing and data formatting functions. This function will also
 generate any HKTM source packet (ANC) in the real satellite packet format that is
 produced on-board and that is needed on-ground to perform the processing.
 The ODGM performs also any eventual processing/modification that the platform
 might apply to the Instrument generated Source Packet (e.g. time stamping).

 In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be addressed to

economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose

registered office is established in such Member and Associated States

which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating

State in the ESA Biomass project.
 
The following States are participating in the said Programme: Austria, Belgium, Canada,
 Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Luxemburg, The
 Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland and the
 United Kingdom.

 named Biomass End-to-End Performance Simulator (BEEPS), will be developed.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement of
 IOnospheric Module (IOM) to be incorporated into the BEEPS software for Phases

title: Biomass MGSE Batch#3  S/C Container and Mulit-Purpose Trolley (MPT)
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of Biomass MGSE Batch#3 - Spacecraft Container and Mulit-Purpose Trolley 
(MPT) by Airbus Defence and Space Ltd as Prime contractor of the Biomass 
project. The supplier selection will be made in accordance with the 
principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development, production,
testing and delivery of the MGSE Batch#3 - Spacecraft Container and Mulit-
Purpose Trolley (MPT).

Due to the size of the Biomass S/C and general handling limitations a 
solution that combines the S/C container and Multi-Purpose Trolley is 
required. This solution will see the S/C, orientated horizontally on the 
MTP, manoeuvred into the S/C container without the use of a crane. The 
design solution shall minimise the floor space required for loading, 
including any door swept areas.

The container shall be compatible with road, rail, sea and air transport 
and shall be also used for S/C pressure testing and any long term storage 
of the S/C. To facilitate these activities a services area with feed-
throughs to the packed S/C and a door to the outside is envisaged. The 
external dimensions of the design solution shall be within standard ISO-
container limits, with hold-down and lifting interfaces also compatible.
The MPT shall interface to an intermediate customer supplied adaptor before 
the S/C. The MTP shall provide a tilt/turn function and support the general 
integration activities on the S/C. It is expected that any damping system 
for transport is incorporated on the container and not the MTP.

In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be addressed to
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose
registered office is established in such Member and Associated States
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating
State in the ESA Biomass project.

title: Biomass Solar Array
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of Biomass Solar Array by Airbus Defence and Space Ltd as Prime
contractor of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be made in
accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development, production,
testing and delivery of the Solar Array.

The fundamental function of the Solar Array are to provide sufficient power
to the spacecraft to support both the spacecraft power demand and battery
recharge requirements as needed during the mission phases.

The Solar Array is part of the Biomass Power Functional Chain and
comprises:
-Solar Cell Assemblies
-Solar Panel Assemblies
-Inter panel or panel to spacecraft body deployment mechanisms
-Hold Down and Release Mechanisms (HDRMs)
-Deployment Control Systems
-Solar Array Rotation Mechanism (SARM)

There shall be a maximum of 4 panels with the outermost panel in the stowed
stack able to generate power during early stages of ascent and early
operations post launch.
In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be addressed to
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose
registered office is established in such Member and Associated States
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating
State in the ESA Biomass project.

title: Biomass Ground Processor Prototype
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall 
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide 
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve 
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle. 

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and 
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement 
of Biomass Ground Processor Prototype (GPP) by Airbus Defence and Space Ltd 
as Prime contractor of the Biomass project. The supplier selection will be 
made in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development, production, 
testing and delivery of the GPP.

The GPP serves to process RAW and Level 0 Biomass mission data to Level 
1a/1b and to generate calibration data where necessary. It will be used by 
ESA to support the development and validation of the operational processor 
and by the Biomass prime contractor to support the assessment of the 
Instrument performance and to consolidate the processing algorithms during 
on-ground and in-orbit tests.

The GPP will operate as a component within the Biomass end-to-end 
performance simulator (BEEPS), as well as in a standalone operation. 

The GPP supplier will be required to design, code and test the algorithms 
necessary to process Biomass data.

In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be addressed to
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose
registered office is established in such Member and Associated States
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating
State in the ESA Biomass project.

title: Biomass Structure
description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer
mission in Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz,
Austria. The overall objective of the mission is to reduce the
uncertainty in the worldwide spatial distribution and dynamics
of forest biomass in order to improve current assessments and
future projections of the global carbon cycle. 

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR
mission, providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest
disturbance and growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the
procurement of Biomass Satellite Structure by Airbus Defence and
Space Ltd as Prime contractor of the Biomass project. The
supplier selection will be made in accordance with the
principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development
(including the required qualification activities),
manufacturing, testing and delivery of the Satellite Structure.

The structure subsystem function is to support all S/C units,
instruments and appendages from S/C integration to the end of
the mission.

It consists of the following major elements:
-	a core ?H? configuration primary structure, comprising
five shear walls, a lower floor and a number of top/intermediate
floors,
-	a set of external panels supporting the LDR, Feed Array
and associated Instrument Electronics and the Spacecraft Service
units,
-	a set of brackets supporting those spacecraft units and
instruments which require a specific orientation with respect to
the master reference frame,
-	unit / instrument fixtures (fasteners, inserts) as
required,
-	a set of MGSE required for spacecraft integration,
spacecraft lifting, panel handling, etc as specified in the
Statement of work.

One structure items shall be delivered. Initially delivered as
the Structural Model (SM) which will be used to perform the
Spacecraft mechanical qualification, which is then refurbished
as the Flight Model (FM) which will be used for flight.

The structure subsystem supplier shall be experienced in
advanced space structures provision.

The structure shall be qualified at structure level with static
testing performed on key interfaces, completed by SM test
campaign. The supplier is also expected to provide some support
to further spacecraft mechanical testing and qualification.

In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be
addressed to economic operators (including those deemed to act
as subcontractors) whose registered office is established in
such Member and Associated States which, by the time of the
Contract award decision, will be a participating State in the
ESA Biomass project.
 
The following States are participating in the said Programme:
Austria, Belgium, Canada, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland,
France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, The Netherlands,
Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland
and the United Kingdom.
